        // A mip can end partway through the last run. Check the other runs
        // once so each row can copy them as fixed-size chunks.
        let (body, last) = runs.split_at(runs.len().saturating_sub(1));
        let chunk_size = body.first().map(|run| run.2).filter(|&size| {
            body.iter()
                .all(|&(offset, _, len)| len == size && offset.is_multiple_of(size))
        });
        for z in 0..depth {
            let (s, inner) = self.split(first + z);
            let base = u64::from(s) * self.slice_size + m.offset;
            for y in 0..m.height {
                let linear_row = z as usize * depth_pitch + y as usize * row_pitch;
                if linear {
                    let tiled_row = base + u64::from(y) * u64::from(m.pitch) * n as u64;
                    copy_run::<DETILE>(src, dst, tiled_row as usize, linear_row, bytes);
                } else {
                    let tiled_row = (base + self.row(m, y, inner)) as usize;
                    match chunk_size {
                        Some(8) if tiled_row.is_multiple_of(8) => {
                            copy_runs::<8, DETILE>(src, dst, body, tiled_row, linear_row)
                        }
                        Some(16) if tiled_row.is_multiple_of(16) => {
                            copy_runs::<16, DETILE>(src, dst, body, tiled_row, linear_row)
                        }
                        Some(32) if tiled_row.is_multiple_of(32) => {
                            copy_runs::<32, DETILE>(src, dst, body, tiled_row, linear_row)
                        }
                        _ => copy_runs::<0, DETILE>(src, dst, body, tiled_row, linear_row),
                    }
                    copy_runs::<0, DETILE>(src, dst, last, tiled_row, linear_row);
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn copy_run<const DETILE: bool>(
    src: &[u8],
    dst: &mut [u8],
    tiled: usize,
    linear: usize,
    len: usize,
) {
    let (from, to) = if DETILE {
        (tiled, linear)
    } else {
        (linear, tiled)
    };
    dst[to..][..len].copy_from_slice(&src[from..][..len]);
}

/// A row of equal runs is contiguous in linear memory. Treat it as a
/// slice of arrays so only the tiled chunk needs a bounds check per copy.
/// Use the byte ranges for irregular runs and the last run of each row.
fn copy_runs<const N: usize, const DETILE: bool>(
    src: &[u8],
    dst: &mut [u8],
    runs: &[(usize, usize, usize)],
    tiled_row: usize,
    linear_row: usize,
) {
    if N == 0 {
        for &(tiled, linear, len) in runs {
            copy_run::<DETILE>(src, dst, tiled_row + tiled, linear_row + linear, len);
        }
    } else if DETILE {
        let tiled = src.as_chunks::<N>().0;
        let linear = dst[linear_row..][..runs.len() * N].as_chunks_mut::<N>().0;
        for (out, &(offset, ..)) in linear.iter_mut().zip(runs) {
            *out = tiled[(tiled_row + offset) / N];
        }
    } else {
        let tiled = dst.as_chunks_mut::<N>().0;
        let linear = src[linear_row..][..runs.len() * N].as_chunks::<N>().0;
        for (input, &(offset, ..)) in linear.iter().zip(runs) {
            tiled[(tiled_row + offset) / N] = *input;
        }
    }
}

/// What a DXGI format stores per element: bytes, texels per element side
/// (4 for block compression), and whether its stencil is a second plane
/// (the GPU keeps depth and stencil apart).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Format {
    pub bytes: u32,
    pub block: u32,
    pub stencil: bool,
}

/// By DXGI format number. `None` for 96-bit, 1-bit, packed 4:2:2 and video
/// formats.
///
/// shortcut: those formats have no layout here; add them when a title uses
/// one.
pub fn format(dxgi: u32) -> Option<Format> {
    let (bytes, block, stencil) = match dxgi {
        1..=4 => (16, 1, false),
        9..=18 => (8, 1, false),
        19..=22 | 44..=47 => (4, 1, true),
        23..=43 | 67 | 87..=93 | 116 | 117 => (4, 1, false),
        48..=59 | 85 | 86 | 115 => (2, 1, false),
        118..=120 => (2, 1, true),
        60..=65 => (1, 1, false),
        70..=72 | 79..=81 => (8, 4, false),
        73..=78 | 82..=84 | 94..=99 => (16, 4, false),
        _ => return None,
    };
    Some(Format {
        bytes,
        block,
        stencil,
    })
}

/// A texture as the console allocates it: a D3D12-style description with
/// a swizzle mode.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TextureDesc {
    pub dimension: Dimension,
    /// In texels.
    pub width: u32,
    pub height: u32,
    /// Depth of a 3D texture, else the array size.
    pub depth_or_array: u32,
    /// 0: the full chain.
    pub mips: u32,
    /// DXGI format number.
    pub format: u32,
    pub samples: u32,
    pub swizzle: Swizzle,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Plane {
    /// From the start of the texture.
    pub offset: u64,
    pub stencil: bool,
    pub layout: Layout,
}

/// Every data plane of a texture (depth, then stencil), placed one after
/// the other.
///
/// shortcut: no compression metadata planes (HTILE, CMASK, FMASK, DCC);
/// the console adds them to render targets and depth buffers unless the
/// description denies them, so those are smaller here than on the console.
/// The host GPU renders them, so nothing reads that memory; add the planes
/// if a title sizes a pool from console sizes and runs out.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Texture {
    pub planes: Vec<Plane>,
    pub size: u64,
    pub alignment: u64,
}

impl Texture {
    pub fn new(desc: &TextureDesc) -> Result<Texture, Error> {
        let f = format(desc.format).ok_or(Error::Invalid)?;
        let depth3d = if desc.dimension == Dimension::Tex3d {
            desc.depth_or_array
        } else {
            1
        };
        let mips = match desc.mips {
            0 => 32 - desc.width.max(desc.height).max(depth3d).max(1).leading_zeros(),
            n => n,
        };
        let plane = |bytes| Desc {
            dimension: desc.dimension,
            width: desc.width,
            height: desc.height,
            depth: desc.depth_or_array,
            mips,
            element_bytes: bytes,
            block: f.block,
            samples: desc.samples.max(1),
            swizzle: desc.swizzle,
        };
        let mut planes = vec![Plane {
            offset: 0,
            stencil: false,
            layout: Layout::new(&plane(f.bytes))?,
        }];
        if f.stencil {
            let layout = Layout::new(&plane(1))?;
            let offset = planes[0].layout.size.next_multiple_of(layout.alignment);
            planes.push(Plane {
                offset,
                stencil: true,
                layout,
            });
        }
        let last = &planes[planes.len() - 1];
        let size = last.offset + last.layout.size;
        let alignment = planes.iter().map(|p| p.layout.alignment).max().unwrap_or(1);
        Ok(Texture {
            planes,
            size,
            alignment,
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn desc(w: u32, h: u32, mips: u32, bpe: u32, swizzle: Swizzle) -> Desc {
        Desc {
            dimension: Dimension::Tex2d,
            width: w,
            height: h,
            depth: 1,
            mips,
            element_bytes: bpe,
            block: 1,
            samples: 1,
            swizzle,
        }
    }

    /// Sizes past the hardware's 16384 texels per side are refused instead
    /// of overflowing the size arithmetic (found by random-input testing).
    #[test]
    fn extents_past_the_hardware_limit_are_invalid() {
        for swizzle in [Swizzle::LINEAR, Swizzle::SW_64KB_D_X] {
            let largest = Layout::new(&desc(MAX_EXTENT, MAX_EXTENT, 15, 16, swizzle)).unwrap();
            assert!(largest.size >= u64::from(MAX_EXTENT) * u64::from(MAX_EXTENT) * 16);
            for (w, h) in [
                (MAX_EXTENT + 1, 1),
                (1, MAX_EXTENT + 1),
                (u32::MAX, u32::MAX),
            ] {
                let result = Layout::new(&desc(w, h, 1, 16, swizzle));
                assert_eq!(result, Err(Error::Invalid), "{w}x{h}");
            }
            let mut deep = desc(1, 1, 1, 16, swizzle);
            deep.depth = u32::MAX;
            assert_eq!(Layout::new(&deep), Err(Error::Invalid));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn blocks_hold_their_size_in_elements() {
        for log2 in [8u32, 12, 16] {
            let swizzle = match log2 {
                8 => Swizzle::SW_256B_S,
                12 => Swizzle::SW_4KB_S,
                _ => Swizzle::SW_64KB_D,
            };
            for e in 0..5 {
                let l = Layout::new(&desc(1, 1, 1, 1 << e, swizzle)).unwrap();
                let [w, h, d] = l.block;
                assert_eq!(u64::from(w * h * d) << e, 1 << log2, "{log2} {e}");
                // The pattern covers exactly the block's coordinates.
                assert_eq!(l.pattern[0].len() as u32, w);
                assert_eq!(l.pattern[1].len() as u32, h);
            }
        }
        // 64 KiB, 16-byte elements: 64x64 (a 256x256 BC7 texture).
        let l = Layout::new(&desc(64, 64, 1, 16, Swizzle::SW_64KB_D)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(l.block, [64, 64, 1]);
        assert_eq!((l.size, l.alignment), (65536, 65536));
    }

    /// Every element of every mip and slice lands on its own address, inside
    /// the texture, and tiling then detiling gives the rows back.
    #[test]
    fn addresses_are_a_bijection_and_copies_round_trip() {
        let cases = [
            desc(64, 64, 7, 16, Swizzle::SW_64KB_D),
            desc(100, 60, 7, 4, Swizzle::SW_64KB_D),
            desc(250, 175, 8, 8, Swizzle::SW_4KB_S),
            desc(33, 17, 6, 1, Swizzle::SW_4KB_D),
            desc(40, 9, 3, 2, Swizzle::SW_64KB_S),
            desc(30, 20, 5, 4, Swizzle::LINEAR),
            desc(83, 31, 6, 1, Swizzle::SW_256B_S),
            Desc {
                block: 4,
                ..desc(109, 71, 6, 16, Swizzle::SW_256B_D)
            },
            Desc {
                depth: 3,
                ..desc(70, 70, 4, 16, Swizzle::SW_4KB_S)
            },
            Desc {
                dimension: Dimension::Tex3d,
                depth: 16,
                ..desc(64, 32, 7, 4, Swizzle::SW_4KB_S)
            },
        ];
        for d in cases {
            let l = Layout::new(&d).unwrap();
            let mut seen = vec![false; l.size as usize];
            let mut tiled = vec![0u8; l.size as usize];
            let n = d.element_bytes as usize;
            let slices = if d.dimension == Dimension::Tex3d { 1 } else { d.depth };
            for slice in 0..slices {
                for mip in 0..d.mips {
                    let m = l.mips[mip as usize];
                    let active = m.width as usize * n;
                    let row = active + 13;
                    let plane = row * m.height as usize + 11;
                    let linear: Vec<u8> = (0..plane * m.depth as usize)
                        .map(|i| (i * 7 + mip as usize * 13 + slice as usize) as u8)
                        .collect();
                    l.tile(&mut tiled, mip, slice, &linear, row, plane).unwrap();
                    let mut back = vec![0xcc; linear.len()];
                    l.detile(&tiled, mip, slice, &mut back, row, plane).unwrap();
                    for z in 0..m.depth {
                        let base = z as usize * plane;
                        for y in 0..m.height {
                            let start = base + y as usize * row;
                            assert_eq!(back[start..start + active], linear[start..start + active]);
                            assert!(back[start + active..start + row].iter().all(|&b| b == 0xcc));
                            for x in 0..m.width {
                                let at = l.offset(mip, x, y, slice + z).unwrap() as usize;
                                let source = start + x as usize * n;
                                assert_eq!(tiled[at..at + n], linear[source..source + n]);
                                assert!(at + n <= seen.len(), "{d:?} mip {mip} outside");
                                assert!(at.is_multiple_of(n));
                                assert!(!seen[at], "{d:?} mip {mip} ({x},{y},{z}) twice");
                                seen[at] = true;
                            }
                        }
                        assert!(back[base + plane - 11..base + plane].iter().all(|&b| b == 0xcc));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn tiled_chunks_match_element_offsets_with_odd_row_pitches() {
        for swizzle in [
            Swizzle::SW_256B_S,
            Swizzle::SW_256B_D,
            Swizzle::SW_4KB_S,
            Swizzle::SW_4KB_D,
            Swizzle::SW_64KB_S,
            Swizzle::SW_64KB_D,
        ] {
            for n in [1, 2, 4, 8, 16] {
                let l = Layout::new(&Desc {
                    depth: 2,
                    ..desc(73, 39, 7, n, swizzle)
                })
                .unwrap();
                let n = n as usize;
                let tiled: Vec<_> = (0..l.size)
                    .map(|i| (i.wrapping_mul(0x9e37_79b9) >> 24) as u8)
                    .collect();
                let mut retiled = vec![0xbb; tiled.len()];
                let mut expected_tiled = retiled.clone();
                for slice in 0..l.slices {
                    for (mip, m) in l.mips.iter().enumerate() {
                        let mip = mip as u32;
                        let bytes = m.width as usize * n;
                        let pitch = bytes + 3;
                        // Keep padding between rows, with exactly the active
                        // bytes in the last row.
                        let len = (m.height as usize - 1) * pitch + bytes;
                        let mut linear = vec![0xcc; len];
                        let mut expected = linear.clone();
                        for y in 0..m.height {
                            for x in 0..m.width {
                                let src = l.offset(mip, x, y, slice).unwrap() as usize;
                                let dst = y as usize * pitch + x as usize * n;
                                expected[dst..][..n].copy_from_slice(&tiled[src..][..n]);
                                expected_tiled[src..][..n].copy_from_slice(&tiled[src..][..n]);
                            }
                        }
                        l.detile(&tiled, mip, slice, &mut linear, pitch, len)
                            .unwrap();
                        assert_eq!(linear, expected, "{swizzle:?} {n} mip {mip} slice {slice}");
                        l.tile(&mut retiled, mip, slice, &expected, pitch, len)
                            .unwrap();
                    }
                }
                assert_eq!(retiled, expected_tiled, "{swizzle:?} {n}");
            }
        }
    }

    /// Hand-checked: in a 64 KiB `D` block of 4-byte elements, x bits go to
    /// address bits 2, 3, 6, 9, 11, 13, 15 and y bits to 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12,
    /// 14; a 4 KiB `S` block of 16-byte elements is 16x16 with y first.
    #[test]
    fn hand_checked_addresses() {
        let l = Layout::new(&desc(128, 128, 1, 4, Swizzle::SW_64KB_D)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(l.offset(0, 1, 0, 0), Ok(1 << 2));
        assert_eq!(l.offset(0, 4, 0, 0), Ok(1 << 6));
        assert_eq!(l.offset(0, 0, 4, 0), Ok(1 << 7));
        assert_eq!(l.offset(0, 0, 8, 0), Ok(1 << 8));
        assert_eq!(l.offset(0, 64, 64, 0), Ok((1 << 15) | (1 << 14)));
        let l = Layout::new(&desc(32, 32, 1, 16, Swizzle::SW_4KB_S)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(l.block, [16, 16, 1]);
        assert_eq!(l.offset(0, 0, 1, 0), Ok(1 << 4));
        assert_eq!(l.offset(0, 1, 0, 0), Ok(1 << 6));
        // Blocks row by row: (16, 0) is the second block, (0, 16) the third.
        assert_eq!(l.offset(0, 16, 0, 0), Ok(4096));
        assert_eq!(l.offset(0, 0, 16, 0), Ok(8192));
    }

    /// A 256x256 BC7 chain in 64 KiB `D`: one tail block holding mips 1-8,
    /// then mip 0; mip 1 sits at x = 32 elements, 32 KiB into the tail.
    #[test]
    fn mip_tail_comes_first() {
        let l = Layout::new(&desc(64, 64, 9, 16, Swizzle::SW_64KB_D)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(l.first_tail_mip, 1);
        assert_eq!(l.size, 2 * 65536);
        assert_eq!(l.mips[0].offset, 65536);
        assert_eq!(
            l.mips[1].tail,
            Some(Tail {
                offset: 32768,
                x: 32,
                y: 0
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(l.offset(1, 0, 0, 0), Ok(32768));
        // 4 KiB blocks hold fewer tail mips: 16x16 BC7 mips stay outside.
        let l = Layout::new(&desc(64, 64, 9, 16, Swizzle::SW_4KB_S)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(l.first_tail_mip, 3);
        assert_eq!(l.mips[2].offset, 4096);
        assert_eq!(l.mips[1].offset, 8192);
        assert_eq!(l.mips[0].offset, 8192 + 16384);
    }

    #[test]
    fn depth_stencil_is_two_planes() {
        let t = Texture::new(&TextureDesc {
            dimension: Dimension::Tex2d,
            width: 1920,
            height: 1080,
            depth_or_array: 1,
            mips: 1,
            format: 20,
            samples: 1,
            swizzle: Swizzle::SW_64KB_Z_X,
        })
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(t.planes.len(), 2);
        // 4-byte depth in 128x128 blocks, 1-byte stencil in 256x256 blocks.
        assert_eq!(t.planes[0].layout.size, 1920 * 1152 * 4);
        assert_eq!(t.planes[1].offset, t.planes[0].layout.size);
        assert_eq!(t.planes[1].layout.size, 2048 * 1280);
        assert!(!t.planes[0].layout.addressable());
    }

    #[test]
    fn texture_copies_reject_overflowing_pitches() {
        let layout = Layout::new(&desc(4, 2, 1, 4, Swizzle::LINEAR)).unwrap();
        let mut tiled = vec![0; layout.size as usize];
        let mut linear = [0; 32];
        assert_eq!(
            layout.detile(&tiled, 0, 0, &mut linear, usize::MAX, 0),
            Err(Error::TooSmall)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.tile(&mut tiled, 0, 0, &linear, usize::MAX, 0),
            Err(Error::TooSmall)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn volume_copy_rejects_overflowing_depth_pitch() {
        let layout = Layout::new(&Desc {
            dimension: Dimension::Tex3d,
            depth: 3,
            ..desc(4, 2, 1, 4, Swizzle::LINEAR)
        })
        .unwrap();
        let tiled = vec![0; layout.size as usize];
        let mut linear = [0; 96];
        assert_eq!(
            layout.detile(&tiled, 0, 0, &mut linear, 16, usize::MAX),
            Err(Error::TooSmall)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn bad_descriptions_and_buffers_are_refused() {
        assert_eq!(
            Layout::new(&desc(0, 4, 1, 4, Swizzle::SW_4KB_S)),
            Err(Error::Invalid)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            Layout::new(&desc(4, 4, 1, 12, Swizzle::SW_4KB_S)),
            Err(Error::Invalid)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            Layout::new(&desc(4, 4, 1, 4, Swizzle(3))),
            Err(Error::Invalid)
        );
        let l = Layout::new(&desc(64, 64, 1, 4, Swizzle::SW_4KB_S)).unwrap();
        let mut out = vec![0; 64 * 64 * 4];
        assert_eq!(
            l.detile(&[0; 100], 0, 0, &mut out, 256, 0),
            Err(Error::TooSmall)
        );
        assert_eq!(l.offset(0, 64, 0, 0), Err(Error::Invalid));
    }
}

```

`crates/victory-formats/src/xma.rs`:

```rs
//! XMA2, the console's hardware audio codec: mono or stereo WMA Pro frames of
//! 512 samples per channel, packed into 2048-byte packets.
//!
//! A packet starts with a 32-bit header (MSB first): the number of frames
//! that begin in it (6 bits), the number of bits that finish the previous
//! frame before the first new one (15), metadata (3) and how many packets of
//! other streams follow before this stream's next packet (8). Every frame
//! starts with its length in bits (15) and ends with a "more frames" bit.
//!
//! The frame decoder follows FFmpeg's `wmaprodec.c` (LGPL-2.1-or-later, used
//! under GPL-3.0-or-later) restricted to what XMA needs: at most two
//! channels, four subframe sizes (512 down to 128), no LFE channel.

mod tables;

use std::sync::OnceLock;

use tables::*;

pub const PACKET_BYTES: usize = 2048;
const PACKET_BITS: usize = PACKET_BYTES * 8;
const HEADER_BITS: usize = 32;
/// Samples per channel in one frame.
pub const FRAME_SAMPLES: usize = 512;
/// Samples per channel in one subframe, the unit of skips and loop ends.
pub const SUBFRAME_SAMPLES: usize = 128;
const LENGTH_BITS: u32 = 15;
/// 512 >> 2: the smallest subframe.
const MIN_SUBFRAME: usize = SUBFRAME_SAMPLES;
const BLOCK_SIZES: usize = 3;
const MAX_BANDS: usize = 29;
const MAX_SUBFRAMES: usize = 32;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Error(pub &'static str);

impl std::fmt::Display for Error {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "XMA: {}", self.0)
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for Error {}

// Packets.

/// A packet's header fields.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Packet {
    pub frames: u32,
    pub first_frame_bit: u32,
    pub skip: u32,
}

pub fn packet(data: &[u8], index: usize) -> Option<Packet> {
    let start = index.checked_mul(PACKET_BYTES)?;
    let b = data.get(start..)?.get(..4)?;
    let h = u32::from_be_bytes([b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]]);
    Some(Packet {
        frames: h >> 26,
        first_frame_bit: (h >> 11) & 0x7fff,
        skip: h & 0xff,
    })
}

/// One frame's bits gathered out of its packets.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Frame {
    /// The frame from its length field on, MSB first.
    pub data: Vec<u8>,
    pub bits: usize,
    /// Bit offset in the buffer where it starts, and where the next frame
    /// starts (`None` when the buffer has no further frame).
    pub start: usize,
    pub next: Option<usize>,
}

/// Bit positions in a buffer of packets, skipping each packet's header and
/// the packets of other streams.
struct Cursor<'a> {
    data: &'a [u8],
    pos: usize,
}

impl Cursor<'_> {
    fn bit(&mut self) -> Option<u32> {
        if self.pos.is_multiple_of(PACKET_BITS) {
            // Leaving a packet: jump over the other streams' packets.
            let previous = self.pos / PACKET_BITS;
            if previous > 0 {
                let skip = packet(self.data, previous - 1)?.skip as usize;
                self.pos = (previous + skip) * PACKET_BITS;
            }
            self.pos += HEADER_BITS;
        }
        let byte = *self.data.get(self.pos / 8)?;
        let bit = (byte >> (7 - self.pos % 8)) & 1;
        self.pos += 1;
        Some(bit as u32)
    }

    fn bits(&mut self, n: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        (0..n).try_fold(0, |v, _| Some(v << 1 | self.bit()?))
    }
}

/// Reads the frame starting at bit `start` (a frame start inside a packet's
/// payload) of `data`, a buffer of whole packets of one stream.
pub fn read_frame(data: &[u8], start: usize) -> Option<Frame> {
    let mut cursor = Cursor { data, pos: start };
    let bits = cursor.bits(LENGTH_BITS)? as usize;
    if bits <= LENGTH_BITS as usize || bits == 0x7fff {
        return None;
    }
    let mut out = vec![0u8; bits.div_ceil(8)];
    let mut cursor = Cursor { data, pos: start };
    for i in 0..bits {
        out[i / 8] |= (cursor.bit()? as u8) << (7 - i % 8);
    }
    let end = cursor.pos;
    let next = next_frame(data, start, end);
    Some(Frame {
        data: out,
        bits,
        start,
        next,
    })
}

/// Where the frame after the one at `start`..`end` begins: right after it,
/// unless it was the last frame to begin in its packet and the rest of that
/// packet is padding.
fn next_frame(data: &[u8], start: usize, end: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    let index = start / PACKET_BITS;
    let header = packet(data, index)?;
    let mut at = index * PACKET_BITS + HEADER_BITS + header.first_frame_bit as usize;
    let mut number = 0;
    while at < start {
        let mut cursor = Cursor { data, pos: at };
        let bits = cursor.bits(LENGTH_BITS)? as usize;
        // The same rule as `read_frame`: a length that does not cover its own
        // field is not a frame. A zero length would never move `at`, so a
        // damaged packet would loop here for good.
        if bits <= LENGTH_BITS as usize {
            return None;
        }
        at += bits;
        number += 1;
    }
    let last = number + 1 >= header.frames;
    let mut end = end;
    if end.is_multiple_of(PACKET_BITS) || (last && end / PACKET_BITS == index) {
        // The next frame begins in the next packet of this stream.
        let next = (end - 1) / PACKET_BITS + 1 + packet(data, (end - 1) / PACKET_BITS)?.skip as usize;
        let header = packet(data, next)?;
        end = next * PACKET_BITS + HEADER_BITS + header.first_frame_bit as usize;
    }
    (end / 8 < data.len()).then_some(end)
}

// Bitstream reading inside a frame.

struct Bits<'a> {
    data: &'a [u8],
    pos: usize,
    end: usize,
}

impl Bits<'_> {
    fn peek32(&self) -> u32 {
        let mut v = 0u64;
        let byte = self.pos / 8;
        for i in 0..5 {
            v = v << 8 | *self.data.get(byte + i).unwrap_or(&0) as u64;
        }
        (v << (24 + self.pos % 8) >> 32) as u32
    }

    fn read(&mut self, n: u32) -> u32 {
        if n == 0 {
            return 0;
        }
        let v = self.peek32() >> (32 - n);
        self.pos += n as usize;
        v
    }

    fn bit(&mut self) -> bool {
        self.read(1) != 0
    }

    fn signed(&mut self, n: u32) -> i32 {
        ((self.read(n) << (32 - n)) as i32) >> (32 - n)
    }

    fn consumed(&self) -> usize {
        self.pos
    }

    fn overread(&self) -> bool {
        self.pos > self.end
    }
}

/// A prefix code built like FFmpeg's `ff_vlc_init_from_lengths`: codes are
/// handed out in table order, each the next free one of its length.
struct Vlc {
    /// Left-aligned code, length, symbol; sorted by code.
    codes: Vec<(u32, u8, i32)>,
}

impl Vlc {
    fn new(entries: impl Iterator<Item = (i32, u8)>) -> Vlc {
        let mut code = 0u64;
        let mut codes = Vec::new();
        for (symbol, len) in entries {
            codes.push((code as u32, len, symbol));
            code += 1 << (32 - len);
        }
        Vlc { codes }
    }

    fn read(&self, bits: &mut Bits) -> i32 {
        let v = bits.peek32();
        let i = self.codes.partition_point(|c| c.0 <= v) - 1;
        let (_, len, symbol) = self.codes[i];
        bits.pos += len as usize;
        symbol
    }
}

struct Codes {
    scale: Vlc,
    scale_rl: Vlc,
    coef: [Vlc; 2],
    vec4: Vlc,
    vec2: Vlc,
    vec1: Vlc,
}

fn codes() -> &'static Codes {
    static CODES: OnceLock<Codes> = OnceLock::new();
    CODES.get_or_init(|| {
        let pairs = |t: &'static [(u16, u8)], offset: i32| {
            Vlc::new(t.iter().map(move |&(s, l)| (s as i32 + offset, l)))
        };
        Codes {
            scale: pairs(&SCALE, -60),
            scale_rl: pairs(&SCALE_RL, 0),
            coef: [
                Vlc::new(COEF0_SYMS.iter().zip(COEF0_LENS).map(|(&s, l)| (s as i32, l))),
                pairs(&COEF1, 0),
            ],
            vec4: Vlc::new(VEC4_SYMS.iter().zip(VEC4_LENS).map(|(&s, l)| (s as i32 - 1, l))),
            vec2: pairs(&VEC2, -1),
            vec1: pairs(&VEC1, 0),
        }
    })
}

/// `ff_wma_get_large_val`.
fn large_value(bits: &mut Bits) -> u32 {
    let mut n = 8;
    if bits.bit() {
        n += 8;
        if bits.bit() {
            n += 8;
            if bits.bit() {
                n += 7;
            }
        }
    }
    bits.read(n)
}

fn log2(v: usize) -> u32 {
    usize::BITS - 1 - v.max(1).leading_zeros()
}

// The inverse transform.

/// Half-length inverse MDCT as FFmpeg defines it (`av_tx` MDCT, inverse):
/// `n` coefficients to the middle `n` samples of the 2n-sample window,
/// negated and scaled by `scale`. Computed as a DCT-IV through an
/// n/2-point complex FFT.
fn imdct_half(input: &[f32], out: &mut [f32], scale: f32) {
    let n = input.len();
    let m = n / 2;
    let mut re = vec![0f64; m];
    let mut im = vec![0f64; m];
    for k in 0..m {
        let (a, b) = (input[2 * k] as f64, input[n - 1 - 2 * k] as f64);
        let (s, c) = (-std::f64::consts::PI * k as f64 / n as f64).sin_cos();
        (re[k], im[k]) = (a * c - b * s, a * s + b * c);
    }
    fft(&mut re, &mut im);
    for k in 0..m {
        let (s, c) = (-std::f64::consts::PI * (4 * k + 1) as f64 / (4 * n) as f64).sin_cos();
        let (wr, wi) = (re[k] * c - im[k] * s, re[k] * s + im[k] * c);
        // DCT-IV: c[2k] = Re, c[n-1-2k] = -Im; output j is c[n-1-j].
        out[n - 1 - 2 * k] = (wr as f32) * scale;
        out[2 * k] = -(wi as f32) * scale;
    }
}

/// In-place radix-2 forward DFT (`exp(-2πi nk/N)`).
fn fft(re: &mut [f64], im: &mut [f64]) {
    let n = re.len();
    let mut j = 0;
    for i in 1..n {
        let mut bit = n >> 1;
        while j & bit != 0 {
            j ^= bit;
            bit >>= 1;
        }
        j |= bit;
        if i < j {
            re.swap(i, j);
            im.swap(i, j);
        }
    }
    let mut len = 2;
    while len <= n {
        let (ws, wc) = (-2.0 * std::f64::consts::PI / len as f64).sin_cos();
        for start in (0..n).step_by(len) {
            let (mut cr, mut ci) = (1.0, 0.0);
            for k in 0..len / 2 {
                let (a, b) = (start + k, start + k + len / 2);
                let (tr, ti) = (re[b] * cr - im[b] * ci, re[b] * ci + im[b] * cr);
                (re[b], im[b]) = (re[a] - tr, im[a] - ti);
                (re[a], im[a]) = (re[a] + tr, im[a] + ti);
                (cr, ci) = (cr * wc - ci * ws, cr * ws + ci * wc);
            }
        }
        len <<= 1;
    }
}

/// `ff_sine_windows`: the rising half of a sine window of length `n`.
fn sine_window(n: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    (0..n)
        .map(|i| ((i as f64 + 0.5) * std::f64::consts::PI / (2.0 * n as f64)).sin() as f32)
        .collect()
}

// The frame decoder.

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Channel {
    prev_block_len: usize,
    transmit_coefs: bool,
    num_subframes: usize,
    subframe_len: [usize; MAX_SUBFRAMES],
    cur_subframe: usize,
    decoded_samples: usize,
    quant_step: i32,
    reuse_sf: bool,
    scale_factor_step: i32,
    max_scale_factor: i32,
    saved_scale_factors: [[i32; MAX_BANDS]; 2],
    scale_factor_idx: usize,
    /// Which of the two saved sets is in use for this subframe.
    scale_factors: usize,
    table_idx: usize,
    num_vec_coeffs: usize,
    coeffs: [f32; FRAME_SAMPLES],
    /// The frame's output, then half a frame of overlap for the next one.
    out: [f32; FRAME_SAMPLES + FRAME_SAMPLES / 2],
}

impl Channel {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Channel {
            prev_block_len: FRAME_SAMPLES,
            transmit_coefs: false,
            num_subframes: 0,
            subframe_len: [0; MAX_SUBFRAMES],
            cur_subframe: 0,
            decoded_samples: 0,
            quant_step: 0,
            reuse_sf: false,
            scale_factor_step: 1,
            max_scale_factor: 0,
            saved_scale_factors: [[0; MAX_BANDS]; 2],
            scale_factor_idx: 0,
            scale_factors: 0,
            table_idx: 0,
            num_vec_coeffs: 0,
            coeffs: [0.0; FRAME_SAMPLES],
            out: [0.0; FRAME_SAMPLES + FRAME_SAMPLES / 2],
        }
    }
}

/// Decodes the frames of one mono or stereo stream.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Decoder {
    channels: usize,
    num_sfb: [usize; BLOCK_SIZES],
    sfb_offsets: [[usize; MAX_BANDS + 1]; BLOCK_SIZES],
    sf_offsets: [[[usize; MAX_BANDS]; BLOCK_SIZES]; BLOCK_SIZES],
    ch: [Channel; 2],
    // Per subframe.
    subframe_len: usize,
    channels_for_cur_subframe: usize,
    channel_indexes: [usize; 2],
    num_bands: usize,
    table_idx: usize,
    esc_len: u32,
    transmit_num_vec_coeffs: bool,
    transform: bool,
    transform_band: [bool; MAX_BANDS],
    parsed_all_subframes: bool,
}

/// What the decoder needs from the stream format: the channel count and
/// the sample rate, which sets the scale factor band layout.
impl Decoder {
    pub fn new(channels: usize, sample_rate: u32) -> Decoder {
        let channels = channels.clamp(1, 2);
        let rate = match sample_rate {
            r if r > 44_100 => 48_000,
            r if r > 32_000 => 44_100,
            r if r > 24_000 => 32_000,
            _ => 24_000,
        };
        let mut sfb_offsets = [[0usize; MAX_BANDS + 1]; BLOCK_SIZES];
        let mut num_sfb = [0usize; BLOCK_SIZES];
        for i in 0..BLOCK_SIZES {
            let subframe_len = FRAME_SAMPLES >> i;
            let offsets = &mut sfb_offsets[i];
            let mut band = 1;
            for &freq in CRITICAL_FREQ.iter().take(MAX_BANDS - 1) {
                if offsets[band - 1] >= subframe_len {
                    break;
                }
                let offset = ((subframe_len * 2 * freq as usize) / rate + 2) & !3;
                if offset > offsets[band - 1] {
                    offsets[band] = offset;
                    band += 1;
                }
                if offset >= subframe_len {
                    break;
                }
            }
            offsets[band - 1] = subframe_len;
            num_sfb[i] = band - 1;
        }
        let mut sf_offsets = [[[0usize; MAX_BANDS]; BLOCK_SIZES]; BLOCK_SIZES];
        for i in 0..BLOCK_SIZES {
            for b in 0..num_sfb[i] {
                let offset = ((sfb_offsets[i][b] + sfb_offsets[i][b + 1] - 1) << i) >> 1;
                for x in 0..BLOCK_SIZES {
                    let mut v = 0;
                    while v + 1 < MAX_BANDS && (sfb_offsets[x][v + 1] << x) < offset {
                        v += 1;
                    }
                    sf_offsets[i][x][b] = v;
                }
            }
        }
        Decoder {
            channels,
            num_sfb,
            sfb_offsets,
            sf_offsets,
            ch: [Channel::new(), Channel::new()],
            subframe_len: FRAME_SAMPLES,
            channels_for_cur_subframe: 0,
            channel_indexes: [0, 1],
            num_bands: 0,
            table_idx: 0,
            esc_len: 0,
            transmit_num_vec_coeffs: false,
            transform: false,
            transform_band: [false; MAX_BANDS],
            parsed_all_subframes: false,
        }
    }

    pub fn channels(&self) -> usize {
        self.channels
    }

    /// Forgets the overlap with earlier frames (a new stream or a seek).
    pub fn reset(&mut self) {
        self.ch = [Channel::new(), Channel::new()];
    }

    /// Decodes one frame (`frame.data`, `frame.bits`) and appends
    /// `FRAME_SAMPLES` interleaved samples per channel to `out`.
    pub fn decode(&mut self, data: &[u8], bits: usize, out: &mut Vec<i16>) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let mut b = Bits {
            data,
            pos: 0,
            end: bits,
        };
        let len = b.read(LENGTH_BITS) as usize;
        let result = self.frame(&mut b, len);
        if result.is_err() {
            // Whatever the frame held is lost; keep the stream's timing.
            for c in 0..self.channels {
                self.ch[c].out = [0.0; FRAME_SAMPLES + FRAME_SAMPLES / 2];
            }
        }
        for i in 0..FRAME_SAMPLES {
            for c in 0..self.channels {
                out.push(to_i16(self.ch[c].out[i]));
            }
        }
        for c in 0..self.channels {
            self.ch[c].out.copy_within(FRAME_SAMPLES.., 0);
        }
        result
    }

    /// The overlap left after the last frame, then silence: half a frame of
    /// samples per channel.
    pub fn flush(&mut self, out: &mut Vec<i16>) {
        for i in 0..FRAME_SAMPLES / 2 {
            for c in 0..self.channels {
                out.push(to_i16(self.ch[c].out[i]));
            }
        }
        self.reset();
    }

    fn frame(&mut self, b: &mut Bits, len: usize) -> Result<(), Error> {
        self.tile_header(b)?;
        // Post-processing transform.
        if self.channels > 1 && b.bit() && b.bit() {
            b.read((self.channels * self.channels * 4) as u32);
        }
        // Dynamic range compression gain, unused.
        b.read(8);
        if b.bit() {
            // Trim at start and end, which only WMA Pro files apply.
            if b.bit() {
                b.read(log2(FRAME_SAMPLES * 2));
            }
            if b.bit() {
                b.read(log2(FRAME_SAMPLES * 2));
            }
        }
        self.parsed_all_subframes = false;
        for c in 0..self.channels {
            let ch = &mut self.ch[c];
            ch.decoded_samples = 0;
            ch.cur_subframe = 0;
            ch.reuse_sf = false;
        }
        while !self.parsed_all_subframes {
            self.subframe(b)?;
        }
        // FFmpeg flags `len != consumed + 2` but keeps the samples; so do we.
        if b.overread() || b.consumed() > len {
            return Err(Error("frame overread"));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn subframe_length(&self, b: &mut Bits, offset: usize) -> Result<usize, Error> {
        if offset == FRAME_SAMPLES - MIN_SUBFRAME {
            return Ok(MIN_SUBFRAME);
        }
        // Four subframe sizes: a 1-bit "not maximal", then 1 bit of shift.
        let shift = if b.bit() { 1 + b.read(1) } else { 0 };
        let len = FRAME_SAMPLES >> shift;
        if len < MIN_SUBFRAME {
            return Err(Error("subframe length"));
        }
        Ok(len)
    }

    fn tile_header(&mut self, b: &mut Bits) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let mut num_samples = [0usize; 2];
        let mut contains = [false; 2];
        let mut channels_for_cur_subframe = self.channels;
        let mut min_channel_len = 0;
        for c in 0..self.channels {
            self.ch[c].num_subframes = 0;
        }
        let fixed = b.bit();
        loop {
            for c in 0..self.channels {
                contains[c] = num_samples[c] == min_channel_len
                    && (fixed
                        || channels_for_cur_subframe == 1
                        || min_channel_len == FRAME_SAMPLES - MIN_SUBFRAME
                        || b.bit());
            }
            let subframe_len = self.subframe_length(b, min_channel_len)?;
            min_channel_len += subframe_len;
            for c in 0..self.channels {
                let ch = &mut self.ch[c];
                if contains[c] {
                    if ch.num_subframes >= MAX_SUBFRAMES {
                        return Err(Error("too many subframes"));
                    }
                    ch.subframe_len[ch.num_subframes] = subframe_len;
                    num_samples[c] += subframe_len;
                    ch.num_subframes += 1;
                    if num_samples[c] > FRAME_SAMPLES {
                        return Err(Error("channel longer than a frame"));
                    }
                } else if num_samples[c] <= min_channel_len {
                    if num_samples[c] < min_channel_len {
                        channels_for_cur_subframe = 0;
                        min_channel_len = num_samples[c];
                    }
                    channels_for_cur_subframe += 1;
                }
            }
            if min_channel_len >= FRAME_SAMPLES || b.overread() {
                break;
            }
        }
        if b.overread() {
            return Err(Error("tile header"));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn channel_transform(&mut self, b: &mut Bits) -> Result<(), Error> {
        self.transform = false;
        if self.channels == 1 {
            return Ok(());
        }
        if b.bit() {
            return Err(Error("channel transform bit"));
        }
        // One group holding every channel of the subframe.
        if self.channels_for_cur_subframe == 2 {
            if b.bit() {
                if b.bit() {
                    return Err(Error("channel transform type"));
                }
            } else {
                self.transform = true;
            }
        }
        if self.transform {
            if !b.bit() {
                for i in 0..self.num_bands {
                    self.transform_band[i] = b.bit();
                }
            } else {
                self.transform_band = [true; MAX_BANDS];
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn coefficients(&mut self, b: &mut Bits, c: usize) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let codes = codes();
        let table = b.bit() as usize;
        let (run, level): (&[u16], &[f32]) = if table == 1 {
            (&COEF1_RUN, &COEF1_LEVEL)
        } else {
            (&COEF0_RUN, &COEF0_LEVEL)
        };
        let subframe_len = self.subframe_len;
        let ch = &mut self.ch[c];
        let mut rl_mode = false;
        let mut cur = 0;
        let mut num_zeros = 0;
        while (self.transmit_num_vec_coeffs || !rl_mode) && cur + 3 < ch.num_vec_coeffs {
            let mut vals = [0u32; 4];
            let idx = codes.vec4.read(b);
            if idx < 0 {
                for i in (0..4).step_by(2) {
                    let idx = codes.vec2.read(b);
                    if idx < 0 {
                        for v in &mut vals[i..i + 2] {
                            let mut x = codes.vec1.read(b) as u32;
                            if x as usize == VEC1.len() - 1 {
                                x += large_value(b);
                            }
                            *v = x;
                        }
                    } else {
                        vals[i] = (idx >> 4) as u32;
                        vals[i + 1] = (idx & 0xf) as u32;
                    }
                }
            } else {
                vals = [
                    (idx >> 12) as u32,
                    ((idx >> 8) & 0xf) as u32,
                    ((idx >> 4) & 0xf) as u32,
                    (idx & 0xf) as u32,
                ];
            }
            for v in vals {
                if v != 0 {
                    let negative = !b.bit();
                    ch.coeffs[cur] = if negative { -(v as f32) } else { v as f32 };
                    num_zeros = 0;
                } else {
                    ch.coeffs[cur] = 0.0;
                    num_zeros += 1;
                    rl_mode |= num_zeros > subframe_len >> 8;
                }
                cur += 1;
            }
            if b.overread() {
                return Err(Error("vector coefficients"));
            }
        }
        if cur < subframe_len {
            ch.coeffs[cur..subframe_len].fill(0.0);
            // `ff_wma_run_level_decode`, version 1.
            let mask = subframe_len - 1;
            let mut offset = cur;
            while offset < subframe_len {
                let code = codes.coef[table].read(b);
                if code > 1 {
                    offset += run[code as usize] as usize;
                    let negative = !b.bit();
                    let v = level[code as usize];
                    ch.coeffs[offset & mask] = if negative { -v } else { v };
                } else if code == 1 {
                    break;
                } else {
                    let value = large_value(b) as i32;
                    if b.bit() {
                        if b.bit() {
                            if b.bit() {
                                // A broken escape ends the channel's
                                // coefficients, as in FFmpeg.
                                break;
                            }
                            offset += b.read(self.esc_len) as usize + 4;
                        } else {
                            offset += b.read(2) as usize + 1;
                        }
                    }
                    let negative = !b.bit();
                    ch.coeffs[offset & mask] = if negative { -value } else { value } as f32;
                }
                if b.overread() {
                    return Err(Error("run level coefficients"));
                }
                offset += 1;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn scale_factors(&mut self, b: &mut Bits) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let codes = codes();
        for i in 0..self.channels_for_cur_subframe {
            let c = self.channel_indexes[i];
            let sf_offsets = self.sf_offsets[self.table_idx][self.ch[c].table_idx];
            let ch = &mut self.ch[c];
            let target = 1 - ch.scale_factor_idx;
            ch.scale_factors = target;
            if ch.reuse_sf {
                let from = ch.saved_scale_factors[ch.scale_factor_idx];
                for (sf, &offset) in ch.saved_scale_factors[target].iter_mut().zip(&sf_offsets).take(self.num_bands) {
                    *sf = from[offset];
                }
            }
            if ch.cur_subframe == 0 || b.bit() {
                if !ch.reuse_sf {
                    ch.scale_factor_step = b.read(2) as i32 + 1;
                    let mut val = 45 / ch.scale_factor_step;
                    for band in 0..self.num_bands {
                        val += codes.scale.read(b);
                        ch.saved_scale_factors[target][band] = val;
                    }
                } else {
                    let mut band = 0;
                    while band < self.num_bands {
                        let idx = codes.scale_rl.read(b);
                        let (skip, val, negative) = match idx {
                            0 => {
                                let code = b.read(14);
                                ((code & 0x3f) >> 1, (code >> 6) as i32, code & 1 == 0)
                            }
                            1 => break,
                            _ => (
                                SCALE_RL_RUN[idx as usize] as u32,
                                SCALE_RL_LEVEL[idx as usize] as i32,
                                !b.bit(),
                            ),
                        };
                        band += skip as usize;
                        if band >= self.num_bands {
                            return Err(Error("scale factor run"));
                        }
                        ch.saved_scale_factors[target][band] += if negative { -val } else { val };
                        band += 1;
                    }
                }
                ch.scale_factor_idx = target;
                ch.table_idx = self.table_idx;
                ch.reuse_sf = true;
            }
            let sf = &ch.saved_scale_factors[ch.scale_factors][..self.num_bands];
            ch.max_scale_factor = sf.iter().copied().max().unwrap_or(0);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn subframe(&mut self, b: &mut Bits) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let mut offset = FRAME_SAMPLES;
        let mut subframe_len = FRAME_SAMPLES;
        let mut total_samples = FRAME_SAMPLES * self.channels;
        for c in 0..self.channels {
            let ch = &self.ch[c];
            if offset > ch.decoded_samples {
                offset = ch.decoded_samples;
                subframe_len = ch.subframe_len[ch.cur_subframe.min(MAX_SUBFRAMES - 1)];
            }
        }
        self.channels_for_cur_subframe = 0;
        for c in 0..self.channels {
            let ch = &mut self.ch[c];
            total_samples -= ch.decoded_samples;
            if offset == ch.decoded_samples
                && ch.cur_subframe < ch.num_subframes
                && subframe_len == ch.subframe_len[ch.cur_subframe]
            {
                total_samples -= subframe_len;
                ch.decoded_samples += subframe_len;
                self.channel_indexes[self.channels_for_cur_subframe] = c;
                self.channels_for_cur_subframe += 1;
            }
        }
        if self.channels_for_cur_subframe == 0 {
            return Err(Error("no channel in subframe"));
        }
        if total_samples == 0 {
            self.parsed_all_subframes = true;
        }
        self.table_idx = log2(FRAME_SAMPLES / subframe_len) as usize;
        self.num_bands = self.num_sfb[self.table_idx];
        self.subframe_len = subframe_len;
        self.esc_len = log2(subframe_len - 1) + 1;

        // Extended header: fill bits.
        if b.bit() {
            let mut fill = b.read(2) as usize;
            if fill == 0 {
                let len = b.read(4);
                fill = b.read(len) as usize + 1;
            }
            b.pos += fill;
        }
        if b.bit() {
            return Err(Error("reserved bit"));
        }
        self.channel_transform(b)?;

        let mut transmit_coeffs = false;
        for i in 0..self.channels_for_cur_subframe {
            let c = self.channel_indexes[i];
            self.ch[c].transmit_coefs = b.bit();
            transmit_coeffs |= self.ch[c].transmit_coefs;
        }
        if transmit_coeffs {
            self.transmit_num_vec_coeffs = b.bit();
            if self.transmit_num_vec_coeffs {
                let num_bits = log2(subframe_len.div_ceil(4)) + 1;
                for i in 0..self.channels_for_cur_subframe {
                    let c = self.channel_indexes[i];
                    let n = (b.read(num_bits) << 2) as usize;
                    if n > subframe_len {
                        return Err(Error("vector coefficient count"));
                    }
                    self.ch[c].num_vec_coeffs = n;
                }
            } else {
                for i in 0..self.channels_for_cur_subframe {
                    self.ch[self.channel_indexes[i]].num_vec_coeffs = subframe_len;
                }
            }
            // Quantisation step (16-bit samples: 90 * 16 >> 4).
            let mut quant_step = 90;
            let mut step = b.signed(6);
            quant_step += step;
            if step == -32 || step == 31 {
                let negative = step == -32;
                let mut quant = 0;
                while b.pos + 5 < b.end {
                    step = b.read(5) as i32;
                    if step != 31 {
                        break;
                    }
                    quant += 31;
                }
                quant_step += if negative { -(quant + step) } else { quant + step };
            }
            if self.channels_for_cur_subframe == 1 {
                self.ch[self.channel_indexes[0]].quant_step = quant_step;
            } else {
                let modifier_len = b.read(3);
                for i in 0..self.channels_for_cur_subframe {
                    let c = self.channel_indexes[i];
                    self.ch[c].quant_step = quant_step;
                    if b.bit() {
                        self.ch[c].quant_step += if modifier_len > 0 {
                            b.read(modifier_len) as i32 + 1
                        } else {
                            1
                        };
                    }
                }
            }
            self.scale_factors(b)?;
        }

        for i in 0..self.channels_for_cur_subframe {
            let c = self.channel_indexes[i];
            if self.ch[c].transmit_coefs && b.pos < b.end {
                self.coefficients(b, c)?;
            } else {
                self.ch[c].coeffs[..subframe_len].fill(0.0);
            }
        }

        // Where this subframe's samples go in the channel output.
        let at = offset + FRAME_SAMPLES / 2;
        if transmit_coeffs {
            self.inverse_channel_transform();
            // Output in [-1, 1] for 16-bit streams.
            let scale = 2.0 / subframe_len as f32 / 32768.0;
            let sfb = self.sfb_offsets[self.table_idx];
            let mut tmp = [0f32; FRAME_SAMPLES];
            for i in 0..self.channels_for_cur_subframe {
                let ch = &mut self.ch[self.channel_indexes[i]];
                let sf = ch.saved_scale_factors[ch.scale_factors];
                for band in 0..self.num_bands {
                    let end = sfb[band + 1].min(subframe_len);
                    let exp = ch.quant_step - (ch.max_scale_factor - sf[band]) * ch.scale_factor_step;
                    let quant = 10f32.powf(exp as f32 / 20.0);
                    for (t, &c) in tmp[sfb[band]..end].iter_mut().zip(&ch.coeffs[sfb[band]..end]) {
                        *t = c * quant;
                    }
                }
                imdct_half(&tmp[..subframe_len], &mut ch.out[at..at + subframe_len], scale);
            }
        } else {
            for i in 0..self.channels_for_cur_subframe {
                self.ch[self.channel_indexes[i]].out[at..at + subframe_len].fill(0.0);
            }
        }

        // Window and overlap-add with the previous block.
        for i in 0..self.channels_for_cur_subframe {
            let ch = &mut self.ch[self.channel_indexes[i]];
            let mut winlen = ch.prev_block_len;
            let mut start = at - winlen / 2;
            if subframe_len < winlen {
                start += (winlen - subframe_len) / 2;
                winlen = subframe_len;
            }
            window_overlap(&mut ch.out[start..start + winlen], &windows()[log2(winlen) as usize - 7]);
            ch.prev_block_len = subframe_len;
        }

        for i in 0..self.channels_for_cur_subframe {
            let ch = &mut self.ch[self.channel_indexes[i]];
            if ch.cur_subframe >= ch.num_subframes {
                return Err(Error("subframe overrun"));
            }
            ch.cur_subframe += 1;
        }
        if b.overread() {
            return Err(Error("subframe overread"));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn inverse_channel_transform(&mut self) {
        if !self.transform || self.channels_for_cur_subframe != 2 {
            return;
        }
        let sfb = self.sfb_offsets[self.table_idx];
        let [a, b] = &mut self.ch;
        for band in 0..self.num_bands {
            let range = sfb[band]..sfb[band + 1].min(self.subframe_len);
            if self.transform_band[band] {
                for y in range {
                    let (l, r) = (a.coeffs[y], b.coeffs[y]);
                    (a.coeffs[y], b.coeffs[y]) = (l - r, l + r);
                }
            } else {
                for y in range {
                    a.coeffs[y] *= 181.0 / 128.0;
                    b.coeffs[y] *= 181.0 / 128.0;
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Sine windows for blocks of 128, 256 and 512 samples.
fn windows() -> &'static [Vec<f32>; 3] {
    static WINDOWS: OnceLock<[Vec<f32>; 3]> = OnceLock::new();
    WINDOWS.get_or_init(|| [sine_window(128), sine_window(256), sine_window(512)])
}

/// FFmpeg's `vector_fmul_window` in place: the first half of `block` holds
/// the previous block's tail, the second half the current block's head.
fn window_overlap(block: &mut [f32], window: &[f32]) {
    let len = block.len() / 2;
    for k in 0..len {
        let (i, j) = (k, 2 * len - 1 - k);
        let (s0, s1) = (block[i], block[2 * len - 1 - k]);
        let (wi, wj) = (window[i], window[j]);
        block[i] = s0 * wj - s1 * wi;
        block[j] = s0 * wi + s1 * wj;
    }
}

fn to_i16(v: f32) -> i16 {
    (v * 32768.0).round().clamp(-32768.0, 32767.0) as i16
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Writes `value` as `n` bits, MSB first, at bit `pos`.
    fn put_bits(data: &mut [u8], pos: usize, n: u32, value: u32) {
        for i in 0..n as usize {
            if value >> (n as usize - 1 - i) & 1 == 1 {
                data[(pos + i) / 8] |= 1 << (7 - (pos + i) % 8);
            }
        }
    }

    /// A damaged packet whose first frame says it is 0 bits long: finding
    /// the frame after a later one must give up, not walk in place forever
    /// (found by random-input testing).
    #[test]
    fn a_zero_length_frame_before_the_start_ends_the_search() {
        let mut data = vec![0u8; PACKET_BYTES];
        // Two frames, the first at payload bit 0; its 15-bit length stays 0.
        put_bits(&mut data, 0, 32, 2 << 26);
        let start = HEADER_BITS + 100;
        put_bits(&mut data, start, LENGTH_BITS, 200);
        let frame = read_frame(&data, start).expect("the frame at `start` is well formed");
        assert_eq!(frame.bits, 200);
        assert_eq!(frame.next, None);
    }

    /// The direct sum `imdct_half` stands for (FFmpeg's naive inverse MDCT:
    /// the standard formula, negated).
    fn imdct_reference(input: &[f32]) -> Vec<f32> {
        let n = input.len();
        (0..n)
            .map(|j| {
                let t = (j + n / 2) as f64 + 0.5 + n as f64 / 2.0;
                -(input
                    .iter()
                    .enumerate()
                    .map(|(k, &x)| x as f64 * (std::f64::consts::PI / n as f64 * t * (k as f64 + 0.5)).cos())
                    .sum::<f64>() as f32)
            })
            .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn fast_imdct_matches_the_direct_sum() {
        for n in [128usize, 256, 512] {
            let input: Vec<f32> = (0..n).map(|i| ((i * 7919) % 97) as f32 - 48.0).collect();
            let mut fast = vec![0f32; n];
            imdct_half(&input, &mut fast, 1.0);
            let reference = imdct_reference(&input);
            for (a, b) in fast.iter().zip(&reference) {
                assert!((a - b).abs() < 1e-2 * (1.0 + b.abs()), "n {n}: {a} vs {b}");
            }
        }
    }

    /// Windowed MDCT blocks of a signal, put back together the way the
    /// decoder does (half IMDCT, then window and overlap), give the signal.
    #[test]
    fn imdct_and_window_reconstruct_a_signal() {
        let n = 256;
        let signal: Vec<f32> = (0..n * 6).map(|i| (i as f32 * 0.05).sin() * 0.3).collect();
        // The 2n-sample sine window; its rising half is `sine_window(n)`.
        let window = |i: usize| ((i as f64 + 0.5) * std::f64::consts::PI / (2.0 * n as f64)).sin();
        let mut out = vec![0f32; n * 7];
        for block in 0..5 {
            let base = block * n;
            let coeffs: Vec<f32> = (0..n)
                .map(|k| {
                    (0..2 * n)
                        .map(|i| {
                            let t = i as f64 + 0.5 + n as f64 / 2.0;
                            // FFmpeg's forward MDCT pairs with its inverse
                            // by sign.
                            -signal[base + i] as f64
                                * window(i)
                                * (std::f64::consts::PI / n as f64 * t * (k as f64 + 0.5)).cos()
                        })
                        .sum::<f64>() as f32
                })
                .collect();
            // The half output is the middle of the 2n window.
            let at = base + n / 2;
            imdct_half(&coeffs, &mut out[at..at + n], 2.0 / n as f32);
            if block > 0 {
                window_overlap(&mut out[at - n / 2..at + n / 2], &sine_window(n));
            }
        }
        for i in n..5 * n {
            assert!((out[i] - signal[i]).abs() < 1e-3, "{i}: {} vs {}", out[i], signal[i]);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn packet_rejects_out_of_range_indices_and_partial_headers() {
        assert!(packet(&[0; 4], usize::MAX / PACKET_BYTES + 1).is_none());
        assert!(packet(&[0; 3], 0).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn packet_headers_and_frame_walk() {
        // Two packets: frame A (100 bits) and B (16300 bits, crossing into
        // packet 1 by 48 bits), then C (60 bits) in packet 1; the rest is
        // padding.
        let mut data = vec![0xffu8; 2 * PACKET_BYTES];
        let header = |frames: u32, first: u32| (frames << 26) | (first << 11);
        let bits = [(0, header(2, 0), 32), (PACKET_BITS, header(1, 48), 32)];
        let put = |data: &mut Vec<u8>, at: usize, value: u32, width: u32| {
            for i in 0..width as usize {
                let bit = (value >> (width as usize - 1 - i)) & 1;
                let p = at + i;
                data[p / 8] = (data[p / 8] & !(1 << (7 - p % 8))) | ((bit as u8) << (7 - p % 8));
            }
        };
        for &(at, v, w) in &bits {
            put(&mut data, at, v, w);
        }
        put(&mut data, 32, 100, 15);
        put(&mut data, 132, 16300, 15);
        let c_start = PACKET_BITS + 32 + 48;
        put(&mut data, c_start, 60, 15);
        let a = read_frame(&data, 32).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((a.bits, a.next), (100, Some(132)));
        let b = read_frame(&data, 132).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((b.bits, b.next), (16300, Some(c_start)));
        // Its last bits come from after packet 1's header.
        assert_eq!(b.data.len(), 16300usize.div_ceil(8));
        let c = read_frame(&data, c_start).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.bits, 60);
        // C was packet 1's only frame: the next would be in packet 2.
        assert_eq!(c.next, None);
    }

    /// Walks and decodes saved input buffers (`VICTORY_XMA_STREAMS=<dir>` of
    /// `*.xma` files with their `*.ctx` context words, made outside the
    /// repository): the frames walked from the first packet must be the
    /// frames the packet headers count, and every frame must decode.
    #[test]
    #[ignore = "needs streams outside the repository"]
    fn walks_saved_streams() {
        let dir = std::env::var("VICTORY_XMA_STREAMS").unwrap();
        let mut bad = 0;
        let mut streams = 0;
        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(dir).unwrap() {
            let path = entry.unwrap().path();
            if path.extension().is_none_or(|e| e != "xma") {
                continue;
            }
            streams += 1;
            let data = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
            let counted: u32 = (0..data.len() / PACKET_BYTES)
                .map(|i| packet(&data, i).unwrap().frames)
                .sum();
            // Context word 1: sample rate in bits 27-28, stereo in bit 29.
            let ctx = std::fs::read(path.with_extension("ctx")).unwrap();
            let word = u32::from_le_bytes(ctx[4..8].try_into().unwrap());
            let rate = [24_000, 32_000, 44_100, 48_000][(word >> 27 & 3) as usize];
            let mut decoder = Decoder::new(1 + (word >> 29 & 1) as usize, rate);
            let (mut walked, mut errors, mut peak, mut pcm) = (0, 0, 0i16, Vec::new());
            let mut at = Some(HEADER_BITS + packet(&data, 0).unwrap().first_frame_bit as usize);
            while let Some(frame) = at.and_then(|bit| read_frame(&data, bit)) {
                pcm.clear();
                errors += decoder.decode(&frame.data, frame.bits, &mut pcm).is_err() as u32;
                peak = pcm.iter().fold(peak, |p, s| p.max(s.saturating_abs()));
                walked += 1;
                at = frame.next;
            }
            println!(
                "{}: {} packets, {counted} frames counted, {walked} walked, {errors} bad, peak {peak}",
                path.display(),
                data.len() / PACKET_BYTES
            );
            bad += u32::from(walked != counted || errors > 0);
        }
        assert!(streams > 0, "VICTORY_XMA_STREAMS contains no .xma files");
        assert_eq!(bad, 0);
    }

    /// Decodes a stream's packets and compares with a reference decode of
    /// the same file (16-bit PCM): `VICTORY_XMA_REFERENCE=<dir>` holding
    /// `mono.xmadata`/`mono.ref` and `stereo.xmadata`/`stereo.ref` (made
    /// outside the repository).
    #[test]
    #[ignore = "needs reference files outside the repository"]
    fn matches_a_reference_decoder() {
        let dir = std::path::PathBuf::from(std::env::var("VICTORY_XMA_REFERENCE").unwrap());
        for (name, channels) in [("mono", 1), ("stereo", 2)] {
            let data = std::fs::read(dir.join(format!("{name}.xmadata"))).unwrap();
            let reference: Vec<i16> = std::fs::read(dir.join(format!("{name}.ref")))
                .unwrap()
                .as_chunks::<2>()
                .0
                .iter()
                .map(|&b| i16::from_le_bytes(b))
                .collect();
            let mut decoder = Decoder::new(channels, 48_000);
            let mut pcm = Vec::new();
            let mut at = Some(HEADER_BITS + packet(&data, 0).unwrap().first_frame_bit as usize);
            let mut errors = 0;
            while let Some(frame) = at.and_then(|bit| read_frame(&data, bit)) {
                errors += decoder.decode(&frame.data, frame.bits, &mut pcm).is_err() as usize;
                at = frame.next;
            }
            // Find the decoder delay, then measure the error.
            let best = (0..2048 / channels)
                .map(|d| {
                    let n = reference.len().min(pcm.len() - d * channels);
                    let e: f64 = (0..n)
                        .map(|i| (pcm[d * channels + i] as f64 - reference[i] as f64).powi(2))
                        .sum();
                    (e, d, n)
                })
                .min_by(|a, b| a.0.total_cmp(&b.0))
                .unwrap();
            let signal: f64 = reference.iter().map(|&s| (s as f64).powi(2)).sum();
            let snr = 10.0 * (signal / best.0.max(1.0)).log10();
            println!(
                "{name}: {} samples, {errors} bad frames, delay {} samples, SNR {snr:.1} dB",
                pcm.len() / channels,
                best.1
            );
            assert!(errors == 0 && snr > 40.0);
        }
    }
}

`crates/victory-formats/src/xma/tables.rs`:

```rs
//! Huffman and level tables of the WMA Pro bitstream that XMA2 frames use,
//! converted from FFmpeg's `libavcodec/wmaprodata.h` (LGPL-2.1-or-later,
//! used here under GPL-3.0-or-later as that licence allows). Pairs are
//! (symbol, code length) in canonical code order.

pub(super) const CRITICAL_FREQ: [u16; 28] = [
    100, 200, 300, 400, 510, 630, 770, 920,
    1080, 1270, 1480, 1720, 2000, 2320, 2700, 3150,
    3700, 4400, 5300, 6400, 7700, 9500, 12000, 15500,
    20675, 28575, 41375, 63875,
];

pub(super) const SCALE: [(u16, u8); 121] = [
    (58, 5), (64, 6), (66, 7), (65, 7), (62, 5), (63, 6), (68, 9), (69, 10),

//! Everything specific to the title: its container formats, build
//! identities, and the hooks we place in its code (located by per-build
//! offsets or byte-pattern signatures). What may and may not be stored here
//! is defined in docs/asset-policy.md.

pub mod sgd5;

/// A specific build of the title executable we know how to run.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct KnownBuild {
    /// Our own label, e.g. "1.0.0 retail".
    pub label: &'static str,
    /// BLAKE3 of the original executable, hex.
    pub blake3: &'static str,
}

/// Builds we support. Empty until the executable is available.
pub const KNOWN_BUILDS: &[KnownBuild] = &[];

/// Looks up a build by the BLAKE3 hash of its executable.
pub fn identify(blake3_hex: &str) -> Option<&'static KnownBuild> {
    KNOWN_BUILDS
        .iter()
        .find(|b| b.blake3.eq_ignore_ascii_case(blake3_hex))
}

`crates/victory-game/src/sgd5.rs`:

```rs
//! `SGD5`: the engine's shader file. Each record holds one shader container,
//! deflate-packed. The header tables are not decoded yet, so records are
//! found by their marker and cross-checked by their sizes:
//!
//! ```text
//! u8 name length (with NUL), name, NUL, u8 kind,
//! u32 n, u32 0x000DDCE7, u32 n, u32 unpacked size, raw deflate (n - 12 bytes)
//! ```

pub const MAGIC: &[u8; 4] = b"SGD5";
const MARKER: [u8; 4] = 0x000D_DCE7_u32.to_le_bytes();
/// Containers are at most a few MiB; refuse to allocate for absurd sizes.
const MAX_UNPACKED: usize = 64 << 20;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Record<'a> {
    /// Offset of the marker in the file.
    pub offset: usize,
    /// Like `PS_<name>_<hash>_Wrapped`; `None` if the bytes before the
    /// record do not read as one.
    pub name: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Record type, meaning unknown (0x32 most shaders, 0x41 mesh shaders
    /// and some material families, 0x3c compute, 0x40, 0x42).
    pub kind: u8,
    packed: &'a [u8],
    unpacked_size: usize,
}

impl Record<'_> {
    /// The container, or `None` if the stream is corrupt.
    pub fn unpack(&self) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        let mut state = zlib_rs::Inflate::new(false, 15);
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let (mut in_pos, mut out_pos) = (0usize, 0usize);
        loop {
            if out_pos == self.unpacked_size {
                let mut extra = [0u8; 1];
                let status = state
                    .decompress(
                        &self.packed[in_pos..],
                        &mut extra,
                        zlib_rs::InflateFlush::NoFlush,
                    )
                    .ok()?;
                return (status == zlib_rs::Status::StreamEnd
                    && state.total_out() as usize == self.unpacked_size)
                    .then_some(out);
            }
            if out_pos == out.len() {
                let next_len = if out.is_empty() {
                    self.unpacked_size
                        .min(self.packed.len().saturating_mul(4).max(4096))
                } else {
                    out.len().saturating_mul(2).min(self.unpacked_size)
                };
                out.resize(next_len, 0);
            }
            let status = state
                .decompress(
                    &self.packed[in_pos..],
                    &mut out[out_pos..],
                    zlib_rs::InflateFlush::NoFlush,
                )
                .ok()?;
            let next_in = state.total_in() as usize;
            let next_out = state.total_out() as usize;
            match status {
                zlib_rs::Status::StreamEnd => {
                    out.truncate(next_out);
                    return (next_out == self.unpacked_size).then_some(out);
                }
                zlib_rs::Status::Ok if next_in != in_pos || next_out != out_pos => {
                    in_pos = next_in;
                    out_pos = next_out;
                }
                zlib_rs::Status::Ok | zlib_rs::Status::BufError => return None,
            }
        }
    }
}

/// An SGD5 file, or a file holding one (an archive: records are found by
/// their marker, so no index is needed).
pub fn is_sgd5(file: &[u8]) -> bool {
    memchr::memmem::find(file, MAGIC).is_some()
}

/// Every record in an SGD5 file, in file order.
pub fn records(file: &[u8]) -> impl Iterator<Item = Record<'_>> {
    memchr::memmem::find_iter(file, &MARKER).filter_map(|at| record(file, at))
}

fn record(file: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<Record<'_>> {
    let u32_at = |o: usize| {
        file.get(o..o + 4)
            .map(|b| u32::from_le_bytes(b.try_into().expect("4 bytes")) as usize)
    };
    let n = u32_at(at.checked_sub(4)?)?;
    let unpacked_size = u32_at(at + 8)?;
    if u32_at(at + 4)? != n || n < 12 || unpacked_size > MAX_UNPACKED {
        return None;
    }
    let nul = at.checked_sub(6)?;
    Some(Record {
        offset: at,
        name: (file[nul] == 0).then(|| name_before(file, nul)).flatten(),
        kind: file[at - 5],
        packed: file.get(at + 12..at + n)?,
        unpacked_size,
    })
}

/// The printable name that ends at `nul` and follows its length byte.
fn name_before(file: &[u8], nul: usize) -> Option<&str> {
    let run = file[..nul]
        .iter()
        .rposition(|b| !b.is_ascii_graphic())
        .map_or(0, |p| p + 1);
    // From 32 characters on, the length byte is printable too.
    (run.saturating_sub(1)..nul)
        .find(|&l| usize::from(file[l]) == nul - l)
        .and_then(|l| std::str::from_utf8(&file[l + 1..nul]).ok())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn record_bytes(name: &str, kind: u8, payload: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut buf = vec![0u8; zlib_rs::compress_bound(payload.len())];
        let config = zlib_rs::DeflateConfig {
            window_bits: -15,
            ..zlib_rs::DeflateConfig::new(6)
        };
        let (packed, rc) = zlib_rs::compress_slice(&mut buf, payload, config);
        assert_eq!(rc, zlib_rs::ReturnCode::Ok);
        let n = (packed.len() + 12) as u32;
        let mut out = vec![0xF4, 0x01, 0, 0, name.len() as u8 + 1];
        out.extend_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&[0, kind]);
        for v in [n, 0x000D_DCE7, n, payload.len() as u32] {
            out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
        }
        out.extend_from_slice(packed);
        out
    }

    #[test]
    fn reads_records() {
        let long = format!("PS_{}_Wrapped", "x".repeat(40));
        let mut file = MAGIC.to_vec();
        file.extend_from_slice(&[1, 2, 3, 4]);
        file.extend(record_bytes(
            "VS_Blit_0011aabb_Wrapped",
            0x32,
            b"first container",
        ));
        // A marker whose sizes disagree is not a record.
        file.extend_from_slice(&[9, 0, 0, 0, 0xE7, 0xDC, 0x0D, 0, 8, 0, 0, 0]);
        file.extend(record_bytes(&long, 0x41, &[7; 300]));

        assert!(is_sgd5(&file));
        let found: Vec<_> = records(&file).collect();
        assert_eq!(found.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(found[0].name, Some("VS_Blit_0011aabb_Wrapped"));
        assert_eq!(found[0].kind, 0x32);
        assert_eq!(found[0].unpack().as_deref(), Some(&b"first container"[..]));
        assert_eq!(found[1].name, Some(long.as_str()));
        assert_eq!(found[1].unpack(), Some(vec![7; 300]));

        // The same file inside an archive.
        let mut archive = vec![0x5A; 0x1000];
        archive.extend_from_slice(&file);
        assert!(is_sgd5(&archive));
        assert_eq!(records(&archive).count(), 2);
        assert!(!is_sgd5(&archive[..0x1000]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn corrupt_stream_does_not_unpack() {
        let mut file = record_bytes("CS_x", 0x3c, &[1; 64]);
        file[27] = 0xFF; // first packed byte: reserved block type
        let r = records(&file).next().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.unpack(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn handles_empty_and_rejects_mismatched_or_truncated_streams() {
        let empty = record_bytes("CS_empty", 0x3c, &[]);
        assert_eq!(records(&empty).next().unwrap().unpack(), Some(Vec::new()));

        let payload: Vec<u8> = (0..16_384u32)
            .map(|i| (i.wrapping_mul(31) ^ (i >> 5)) as u8)
            .collect();
        let good = record_bytes("PS_big", 0x32, &payload);
        let r = records(&good).next().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.unpack(), Some(payload.clone()));

        // Oversized stream (declared unpacked_size smaller than actual output).
        let mut smaller = good.clone();
        smaller[r.offset + 8..r.offset + 12]
            .copy_from_slice(&((payload.len() - 1) as u32).to_le_bytes());
        assert_eq!(records(&smaller).next().unwrap().unpack(), None);

        // Under-filled stream (declared unpacked_size larger than actual output).
        let mut larger = good.clone();
        larger[r.offset + 8..r.offset + 12]
            .copy_from_slice(&((payload.len() + 1) as u32).to_le_bytes());
        assert_eq!(records(&larger).next().unwrap().unpack(), None);

        // Truncated raw deflate stream.
        let mut truncated = good[..good.len() - 1].to_vec();
        let new_n = (truncated.len() - r.offset) as u32;
        truncated[r.offset - 4..r.offset].copy_from_slice(&new_n.to_le_bytes());
        truncated[r.offset + 4..r.offset + 8].copy_from_slice(&new_n.to_le_bytes());
        assert_eq!(records(&truncated).next().unwrap().unpack(), None);
    }
}
