```rs
    u64::from(generation & GENERATIONS) << 32 | u64::from(i)
}

/// The record words that name the constant buffer view of `size` bytes at
/// `address` whole; `None` if they cannot: an address past 47 bits, or a
/// size of 16 KiB or more that is no multiple of 256 or reaches 4 MiB (the
/// size has 15 bits: bytes below 16 KiB, else units of 256 bytes). Such a
/// view is a table entry.
fn constant_words(address: u64, size: u32) -> Option<[u32; 2]> {
    if address >> CONSTANT_ADDRESS_BITS != 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let code = if size < 1 << 14 {
        u64::from(size)
    } else if size.is_multiple_of(256) && size >> 8 < 1 << 14 {
        1 << 14 | u64::from(size >> 8)
    } else {
        return None;
    };
    Some(kind_words(CONSTANT, code << CONSTANT_ADDRESS_BITS | address))
}

/// The constant buffer view [`constant_words`] named.
fn constant_of(i: u32, generation: u32) -> View {
    let payload = payload(i, generation);
    let code = (payload >> CONSTANT_ADDRESS_BITS) as u32;
    let size = if code >> 14 == 0 { code } else { (code & 0x3fff) << 8 };
    View::Constant(payload & ((1 << CONSTANT_ADDRESS_BITS) - 1), size)
}

/// A placed view's shape and its address.
fn shape_of(unordered: bool, resource: &[u32; 14], desc: &[u32; 16]) -> (Shape, u64) {
    let mut rest = [0u32; 14];
    rest[..10].copy_from_slice(&desc[..10]);
    rest[10..].copy_from_slice(&desc[12..]);
    (
        (unordered, *resource, rest),
        u64::from(desc[10]) | u64::from(desc[11]) << 32,
    )
}

/// The record words that name the view of placed memory at `address` with
/// shape number `shape`.
fn placed_words(shape: u32, address: u64) -> [u32; 2] {
    kind_words(PLACED, u64::from(shape) << PLACED_ADDRESS_BITS | address)
}

impl Views {
    /// The number of `shape`, a new one if it is not there yet; `None` when
    /// the shapes are full (the view is then a table entry).
    fn shape(&mut self, shape: Shape) -> Option<u32> {
        if let Some(&at) = self.shape_index.get(&shape) {
            return Some(at);
        }
        if self.shapes.len() >= SHAPES {
            return None;
        }
        let at = self.shapes.len() as u32;
        self.shapes.push(shape);
        self.shape_index.insert(shape, at);
        Some(at)
    }

    /// The view of placed memory [`placed_words`] named.
    fn placed_of(&self, i: u32, generation: u32) -> Option<View> {
        let payload = payload(i, generation);
        let address = payload & ((1 << PLACED_ADDRESS_BITS) - 1);
        let &(unordered, resource, rest) = self.shapes.get((payload >> PLACED_ADDRESS_BITS) as usize)?;
        let mut desc = [0u32; 16];
        desc[..10].copy_from_slice(&rest[..10]);
        (desc[10], desc[11]) = (address as u32, (address >> 32) as u32);
        desc[12..].copy_from_slice(&rest[10..]);
        Some(View::Placed(unordered, resource, desc))
    }

    /// The record words of `view` as a table entry, if it has one.
    fn entry_of(&self, view: &View) -> Option<[u32; 2]> {
        let &i = self.index.get(view)?;
        Some([i, self.list[i as usize].1])
    }

    /// The record words of `view` as a table entry: its entry (a new or a
    /// freed one if the view is not there yet) and that entry's generation.
    fn entry(&mut self, view: View) -> [u32; 2] {
        let i = match self.index.get(&view) {
            Some(&i) => i,
            None => {
                let i = match self.free.pop() {
                    Some(i) => {
                        self.list[i as usize].0 = view.clone();
                        i
                    }
                    None => {
                        self.list.push((view.clone(), 1));
                        self.list.len() as u32 - 1
                    }
                };
                for r in view.resources().into_iter().filter(|&r| r != 0) {
                    self.by_resource.entry(r).or_default().push(i);
                }
                self.index.insert(view, i);
                i
            }
        };
        [i, self.list[i as usize].1]
    }
}

/// The two words that name `view` in a record: the view itself where its
/// kind allows ([`Views`]), else its table entry.
fn words_for(view: View) -> [u32; 2] {
    use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
    if inline() {
        match &view {
            View::Constant(address, size) => {
                if let Some(words) = constant_words(*address, *size) {
                    NAMED_WHOLE[0].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
                    return words;
                }
            }
            View::Placed(unordered, resource, desc) => {
                let (shape, address) = shape_of(*unordered, resource, desc);
                if address >> PLACED_ADDRESS_BITS == 0 {
                    // Nearly every placed view has a shape seen before.
                    let known = views_read().shape_index.get(&shape).copied();
                    let shape = known.or_else(|| views_write().shape(shape));
                    if let Some(shape) = shape {
                        NAMED_WHOLE[1].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
                        return placed_words(shape, address);
                    }
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    // A view written before keeps its entry and generation.
    if let Some(words) = views_read().entry_of(&view) {
        return words;
    }
    views_write().entry(view)
}

fn views_read() -> std::sync::RwLockReadGuard<'static, Views> {
    VIEWS.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

fn views_write() -> std::sync::RwLockWriteGuard<'static, Views> {
    VIEWS.write().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

/// For the memory line: the distinct views kept ([`Views`]), those of them
/// free for reuse, and the bytes the table and its index hold for them (an
/// estimate: an entry of the table, and one of the index with its share of
/// a tree node; the shapes likewise); then the entries that are constant
/// buffer views and views of placed memory (those that did not fit a
/// record, or all of them with `VICTORY_VIEW_INLINE=0`), the shapes of
/// placed views kept, and the views named whole in their records since the
/// start: constant buffer views, views of placed memory.
#[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]
pub(crate) fn views_kept() -> [u64; 8] {
    use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
    let views = views_read();
    let each = size_of::<(View, u32)>() as u64;
    let shape = size_of::<Shape>() as u64;
    let (mut constants, mut placed) = (0, 0);
    for (view, _) in &views.list {
        match view {
            View::Constant(..) => constants += 1,
            View::Placed(..) => placed += 1,
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    [
        views.list.len() as u64,
        views.free.len() as u64,
        views.list.capacity() as u64 * each
            + views.index.len() as u64 * each * 3 / 2
            + views.shapes.capacity() as u64 * shape
            + views.shape_index.len() as u64 * shape * 3 / 2,
        constants,
        placed,
        views.shapes.len() as u64,
        NAMED_WHOLE[0].load(Relaxed),
        NAMED_WHOLE[1].load(Relaxed),
    ]
}

impl View {
    /// The resource objects the view names.
    fn resources(&self) -> [usize; 2] {
        match *self {
            View::Shader(r, _) => [r, 0],
            View::Unordered(r, counter, _) => [r, counter],
            _ => [0, 0],
        }
    }

    /// The texture object the view is of, if that texture has no host copy
    /// yet (`crate::resource::host_waits`): a slot written with such a
    /// view is left null until the texture is first used.
    #[cfg(windows)]
    fn waiting_texture(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        match *self {
            View::Shader(r, _) | View::Unordered(r, _, _)
                if crate::resource::host_waits(r as This) =>
            {
                Some(r)
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Title slots (their handles) written with a view of a texture object
/// that had no host copy then, by texture. A title texture gets its host
/// copy on first use (`resource.rs` `Hosted`), and the title
/// writes each texture's views into its view heap when it creates the
/// texture: making those host slots would make every host copy at once.
/// They are made when the texture is: translated shaders index the heap
/// directly, so a slot is not always made again by the draw that reads it.
#[cfg(windows)]
static WAITING: std::sync::Mutex<std::collections::BTreeMap<usize, Vec<u64>>> =
    std::sync::Mutex::new(std::collections::BTreeMap::new());

/// Textures given their host copy since [`make_waiting`] last ran.
#[cfg(windows)]
static MADE_LATE: std::sync::Mutex<Vec<usize>> = std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new());

/// Title texture `resource` was given its host copy (called under that
/// texture's own lock: nothing else is locked here).
#[cfg(windows)]
pub(crate) fn texture_made(resource: usize) {
    MADE_LATE
        .lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
        .push(resource);
}

/// The slot at `handle` was written with a view of texture `resource`,
/// which has no host copy: it waits for one.
#[cfg(windows)]
fn wait_for(resource: usize, handle: u64) {
    /// A texture with more slots waiting than this is in use for all we
    /// know (its views are being copied about): its host copy is made.
    const MOST: usize = 64;
    let many = {
        let mut waiting = WAITING.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        let slots = waiting.entry(resource).or_default();
        if !slots.contains(&handle) {
            slots.push(handle);
        }
        slots.len() > MOST
    };
    if many {
        // Makes it, and notes it made.
        let _ = crate::resource::host_copy(resource as This);
    } else if !crate::resource::host_waits(resource as This) {
        // Made by another thread since the slot was looked at: that making
        // may have been taken by `make_waiting` before this slot was noted.
        texture_made(resource);
    }
}

/// Makes the host slots that waited for a texture's host copy, for the
/// textures made since the last call. Called before a submission runs, by
/// the thread that submits: a slot is read when a list runs.
#[cfg(windows)]
pub(crate) fn make_waiting() {
    let made = std::mem::take(&mut *MADE_LATE.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()));
    for resource in made {
        let handles = WAITING
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .remove(&resource);
        for handle in handles.into_iter().flatten() {
            // Only if the slot still holds a view of that texture: the
            // title may have written it since (and a view of another
            // texture without a host copy must go on waiting).
            // (Looked up first: the handle is read only while its heap is
            // there.)
            let Some((heap, index)) = shader_slot(handle) else {
                continue;
            };
            let same = match view(handle) {
                Some(View::Shader(r, _) | View::Unordered(r, _, _)) => r == resource,
                _ => false,
            };
            if same && let Some(Some(host)) = heap.host.get() {
                host.mirror(index, handle, true);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn record(handle: u64, view: View) {
    if handle == 0 {
        return;
    }
    let [i, generation] = words_for(view);
    // SAFETY: the handle is a descriptor slot, at least 16 bytes.
    unsafe { (handle as *mut [u32; 3]).write_unaligned([VIEW_TAG, i, generation]) };
    #[cfg(windows)]
    mirror(handle);
}

/// The title released `resource`: the views naming it go stale.
pub(crate) fn forget(resource: usize) {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    WAITING
        .lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
        .remove(&resource);
    let mut views = views_write();
    let Some(entries) = views.by_resource.remove(&resource) else {
        return;
    };
    for i in entries {
        let (view, generation) = views.list[i as usize].clone();
        // Entries freed through a view's other resource may hold another
        // view by now.
        if views.index.get(&view) != Some(&i) || !view.resources().contains(&resource) {
            continue;
        }
        views.index.remove(&view);
        // (Below the bits that say a record is no table entry.)
        views.list[i as usize].1 = ((generation + 1) & GENERATIONS).max(1);
        // The view's other resource (a counter) keeps a stale entry, which
        // `forget` of that resource skips.
        views.free.push(i);
    }
}

/// The view the record words `i` and `generation` name: the one they hold
/// whole, or the view of entry `i` if `generation` is still its own.
fn view_at(i: u32, generation: u32) -> Option<View> {
    match generation >> KIND_SHIFT {
        0 => {
            let views = views_read();
            let (view, current) = views.list.get(i as usize)?;
            (*current == generation).then(|| view.clone())
        }
        CONSTANT => Some(constant_of(i, generation)),
        PLACED => views_read().placed_of(i, generation),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// The view recorded at `handle`, if one is (and its resource is alive).
pub(crate) fn view(handle: u64) -> Option<View> {
    if handle == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    // SAFETY: the handle is a descriptor slot the title passes back.
    let [tag, i, generation] = unsafe { (handle as *const [u32; 3]).read_unaligned() };
    if tag != VIEW_TAG {
        return None;
    }
    view_at(i, generation)
}

/// A description of `N` words, if the title passes one.
fn words<const N: usize>(desc: *const [u32; N]) -> Option<[u32; N]> {
    // SAFETY: the title passes a description or null.
    (!desc.is_null()).then(|| unsafe { desc.read_unaligned() })
}

/// Device method.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn create_cbv(_: This, desc: *const [u32; 4], handle: u64) {
    if let Some([lo, hi, size, _]) = words(desc) {
        let address = u64::from(lo) | u64::from(hi) << 32;
        record(handle, View::Constant(address, size));
    }
}

/// Device method.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn create_srv(
    _: This,
    resource: This,
    desc: *const [u32; 10],
    handle: u64,
) {
    record(handle, View::Shader(resource as usize, words(desc)));
}

/// Device method.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn create_uav(
    _: This,
    resource: This,
    counter: This,
    desc: *const [u32; 10],
    handle: u64,
) {
    let view = View::Unordered(resource as usize, counter as usize, words(desc));
    record(handle, view);
}

/// Device methods 0x230 and 0x238: shader resource and unordered access
/// views of memory the title placed itself, `(resource desc, view desc,
/// handle)`.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn create_placed_srv(
    _: This,
    resource: *const [u32; 14],
    desc: *const [u32; 16],
    handle: u64,
) {
    if let (Some(resource), Some(desc)) = (words(resource), words(desc)) {
        record(handle, View::Placed(false, resource, desc));
    }
}

pub(crate) extern "system" fn create_placed_uav(
    _: This,
    resource: *const [u32; 14],
    desc: *const [u32; 16],
    handle: u64,
) {
    if let (Some(resource), Some(desc)) = (words(resource), words(desc)) {
        record(handle, View::Placed(true, resource, desc));
    }
}

/// Device method.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn create_sampler(_: This, desc: *const [u32; 13], handle: u64) {
    if let Some(desc) = words(desc) {
        record(handle, View::Sampler(desc));
    }
}

/// Device method 0x1e8.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn create_sampler_x(_: This, desc: *const [u32; 27], handle: u64) {
    if let Some(desc) = words(desc) {
        record(handle, View::ConsoleSampler(desc));
    }
}

/// Device method: `count` descriptors of `kind` from `src` to `dst`.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn copy_simple(_: This, count: u32, dst: u64, src: u64, kind: u32) {
    let step = u64::from(increment(kind).unwrap_or(0));
    let len = u64::from(count) * step;
    if dst != 0 && src != 0 {
        // SAFETY: both ranges are descriptor slots the title owns.
        unsafe { std::ptr::copy(src as *const u8, dst as *mut u8, len as usize) };
        #[cfg(windows)]
        for i in 0..u64::from(count) {
            mirror(dst + i * step);
        }
    }
}

/// Device method: ranges of descriptors (start and count each) gathered
/// from the sources and scattered to the destinations, in order.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] // the method's own arguments
pub(crate) extern "system" fn copy(
    _: This,
    dst_ranges: u32,
    dst_starts: *const u64,
    dst_sizes: *const u32,
    src_ranges: u32,
    src_starts: *const u64,
    src_sizes: *const u32,
    kind: u32,
) {
    let Some(step) = increment(kind) else {
        return;
    };
    // Each range as (start, count); a null size array means one descriptor
    // per range.
    let ranges = |n: u32, starts: *const u64, sizes: *const u32| -> Vec<(u64, u32)> {
        (0..n as usize)
            .map(|i| {
                // SAFETY: the title passes `n` starts and sizes (or null sizes).
                unsafe {
                    (
                        *starts.add(i),
                        if sizes.is_null() { 1 } else { *sizes.add(i) },
                    )
                }
            })
            .collect()
    };
    if dst_starts.is_null() || src_starts.is_null() {
        return;
    }
    let src = ranges(src_ranges, src_starts, src_sizes);
    let mut dst = ranges(dst_ranges, dst_starts, dst_sizes).into_iter();
    let (mut to, mut room) = dst.next().unwrap_or((0, 0));
    for (mut from, mut left) in src {
        while left > 0 {
            while room == 0 {
                let Some(next) = dst.next() else { return };
                (to, room) = next;
            }
            let n = left.min(room);
            copy_simple(std::ptr::null(), n, to, from, kind);
            let bytes = u64::from(n) * u64::from(step);
            (to, from, room, left) = (to + bytes, from + bytes, room - n, left - n);
        }
    }
}

/// The view recorded at `handle`, if one is.
pub(crate) fn rtv_record(handle: u64) -> Option<RtvRecord> {
    tagged_record(handle, RTV_TAG)
}

/// The depth view recorded at `handle`, if one is.
pub(crate) fn dsv_record(handle: u64) -> Option<RtvRecord> {
    tagged_record(handle, DSV_TAG)
}

fn tagged_record(handle: u64, tag: u32) -> Option<RtvRecord> {
    if handle == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    // SAFETY: the handle is a descriptor slot the title passes back.
    let record = unsafe { (handle as *const RtvRecord).read_unaligned() };
    (record.tag == tag).then_some(record)
}

/// Device method.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn create_heap(
    _: This,
    desc_ptr: *const HeapDesc,
    iid: *const Iid,
    out: *mut This,
) -> HRESULT {
    // SAFETY: the title passes a description (null is tolerated).
    let Some(&desc) = (unsafe { desc_ptr.as_ref() }) else {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    };
    let Some(size) = increment(desc.kind).map(|i| u64::from(i) * u64::from(desc.count.max(1)))
    else {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    };
    // SAFETY: read only as a hint: a title that passes the plain
    // description has its own stack or data after it.
    let placement = unsafe { desc_ptr.add(1).cast::<Placement>().read_unaligned() };
    // shortcut: a placement is recognised by its size matching the count,
    // since the plain and extended descriptions share the slot and the
    // interface version; find the flag that tells them apart if a title
    // trips over this.
    let placed = placement.address != 0 && placement.size == size;
    tracing::debug!(?desc, placed, "descriptor heap");
    let (start, memory) = if placed {
        (placement.address, None)
    } else {
        match Memory::zeroed(size, 64) {
            Ok(memory) => (memory.address(), Some(memory)),
            Err(hr) => return hr,
        }
    };
    let visible = desc.flags & SHADER_VISIBLE != 0 && matches!(desc.kind, VIEWS_KIND | SAMPLERS);
    let heap = Box::new(Heap {
        object: Object::new(&FUNCTIONS),
        desc,
        start,
        memory,
        #[cfg(windows)]
        host: std::sync::OnceLock::new(),
        #[cfg(windows)]
        pending: Default::default(),
        #[cfg(windows)]
        written: (placed && visible)
            .then(|| crate::watch::track(start as usize, size as usize, true))
            .flatten(),
    });
    #[cfg(windows)]
    if visible {
        let at = std::ptr::from_ref::<Heap>(&heap) as usize;
        let mut heaps = SHADER_HEAPS.write().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        heaps.push((start, start + size, at));
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    let _ = visible;
    object::hand_out(DESCRIPTOR_HEAP, heap, iid, &HEAP_IIDS, out)
}

extern "system" fn query(this: This, iid: *const Iid, out: *mut This) -> HRESULT {
    let found = object::is(iid, &HEAP_IIDS).then_some(this);
    object::answer(DESCRIPTOR_HEAP, iid, found, out)
}
extern "system" fn release(this: This) -> u32 {
    object::release_boxed::<Heap>(this)
}
extern "system" fn desc(this: This, out: *mut HeapDesc) {
    if !out.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: checked non-null; the title passes room for a description.
        unsafe { out.write(heap(this).desc) };
    }
}
/// The same address for the CPU and the GPU start.
extern "system" fn start(this: This) -> u64 {
    heap(this).start
}

/// IUnknown 3, object 4, device child 1, heap 3.
static FUNCTIONS: Table<24> = {
    let mut f = object::d3d12_object(object::missing_table::<DESCRIPTOR_HEAP, 24>());
    f[0] = query as *const ();
    f[2] = release as *const ();
    f[7] = object::parent_device as *const (); // 0x38
    f[8] = desc as *const (); // 0x40
    f[9] = start as *const (); // 0x48 CPU
    f[10] = start as *const (); // 0x50 GPU
    Table(f)
};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::object::{S_OK, slot};

    /// What newer titles pass; tests use it throughout, so that reading the
    /// placement stays inside the value.
    #[repr(C)]
    struct Extended(HeapDesc, Placement);

    fn create(desc: HeapDesc, placement: Placement, out: &mut This) -> HRESULT {
        let extended = Extended(desc, placement);
        create_heap(std::ptr::null(), &extended.0, &HEAP_IIDS[0], out)
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn raw_heap_sync_stops_before_dynamic_host_slots() {
        let start = 0x1000usize;
        let step = 32;
        let capped = 5;
        assert_eq!(
            changed_slots(
                start + 3 * step + 4,
                start + 4 * step + 8,
                start,
                step as u64,
                capped
            ),
            3..5
        );
        assert_eq!(
            changed_slots(
                start + 6 * step,
                start + 9 * step,
                start,
                step as u64,
                capped
            ),
            5..5
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn heaps_hold_count_descriptors_from_their_start() {
        let null = std::ptr::null();
        let desc = HeapDesc {
            kind: 0,
            count: 1000,
            flags: 1,
            nodes: 0,
        };
        let none = Placement {
            address: 0,
            size: 0,
        };
        let mut h = null;
        assert_eq!(create(desc, none, &mut h), S_OK);
        let cpu = slot::<extern "system" fn(This) -> u64>(h, 0x48)(h);
        assert_eq!(cpu % 64, 0);
        assert_eq!(slot::<extern "system" fn(This) -> u64>(h, 0x50)(h), cpu);
        assert_eq!(increment_size(null, 0), 32);
        // SAFETY: the heap holds 1000 descriptors of 32 bytes.
        unsafe { (cpu as *mut u8).add(999 * 32 + 31).write(1) };
        assert_eq!(increment_size(null, 9), 0);
        let bad = HeapDesc { kind: 9, ..desc };
        assert_eq!(create(bad, none, &mut h), E_INVALIDARG);
    }

    /// A descriptor copied into a placed heap as bytes is mirrored before
    /// the next submission, even though no descriptor method saw the copy.
    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn records_copied_as_bytes_are_made_at_the_next_sync() {
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
            MEM_COMMIT, MEM_RELEASE, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE, VirtualAlloc, VirtualFree,
        };
        const MEM_WRITE_WATCH: u32 = 0x20_0000;
        let memory = unsafe {
            VirtualAlloc(
                std::ptr::null(),
                crate::watch::PAGE,
                MEM_RESERVE | MEM_COMMIT | MEM_WRITE_WATCH,
                PAGE_READWRITE,
            )
        };
        assert!(!memory.is_null());
        let desc = HeapDesc {
            kind: SAMPLERS,
            count: 64,
            flags: SHADER_VISIBLE,
            nodes: 1,
        };
        let placement = Placement {
            address: memory as u64,
            size: 64 * 16,
        };
        let mut h: This = std::ptr::null();
        assert_eq!(create(desc, placement, &mut h), S_OK);
        if let Some(host) = heap(h).host() {
            let mut elsewhere = [0u64; 2];
            let source = elsewhere.as_mut_ptr() as u64;
            let sampler = [21, 3, 3, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x7f7f_ffff, 0];
            create_sampler(std::ptr::null(), &sampler, source);
            // SAFETY: the heap slot and source both hold 16 descriptor bytes.
            unsafe {
                std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(
                    source as *const u8,
                    memory.cast::<u8>().add(5 * 16),
                    16,
                )
            };
            assert!(!host.made(5));
            sync_heaps();
            assert!(host.made(5));
        }
        slot::<extern "system" fn(This) -> u32>(h, 0x10)(h);
        // SAFETY: this allocation belongs to the test.
        unsafe { VirtualFree(memory, 0, MEM_RELEASE) };
    }

    #[test]
    fn views_survive_copies() {
        let null = std::ptr::null();
        let mut heap = vec![0u64; 4 * 8]; // four 32-byte slots
        let at = |i: usize| heap.as_ptr() as u64 + 32 * i as u64;
        let (s0, s1, s2, s3) = (at(0), at(1), at(2), at(3));
        create_cbv(null, &[0x1000, 1, 256, 0], s0);
        assert_eq!(view(s0), Some(View::Constant(0x1_0000_1000, 256)));
        create_srv(null, null, std::ptr::null(), s1);
        assert_eq!(view(s1), Some(View::Shader(0, None)));
        // The same view twice is one entry.
        create_srv(null, null, std::ptr::null(), s2);
        // SAFETY: both slots are in `heap`.
        assert_eq!(unsafe { *(s1 as *const [u32; 3]) }, unsafe {
            *(s2 as *const [u32; 3])
        });
        // Two ranges of one into one range of two.
        let (dst, dst_n, src, src_n) = ([s2], [2u32], [s0, s1], [1u32, 1]);
        copy(
            null,
            1,
            dst.as_ptr(),
            dst_n.as_ptr(),
            2,
            src.as_ptr(),
            src_n.as_ptr(),
            0,
        );
        assert_eq!(view(s2), view(s0));
        assert_eq!(view(s3), view(s1));
        assert_eq!(view(at(0) + 8), None);
        heap[0] = 0;
    }

    /// Constant buffer views are named whole in their records: any address
    /// a program can have, any size below 16 KiB, multiples of 256 bytes
    /// up to 4 MiB; what does not fit says so.
    #[test]
    fn constant_views_fit_their_records() {
        let top = (1u64 << CONSTANT_ADDRESS_BITS) - 1;
        for address in [0u64, 0x100, 0x2602_0000, 0xd_6b60_0000, 0x7ffd_a34f_0000, top] {
            for size in [0u32, 1, 255, 256, 4000, (1 << 14) - 1, 1 << 14, 65536, (1 << 22) - 256] {
                let [i, generation] = constant_words(address, size).expect("fits");
                assert_eq!(generation >> KIND_SHIFT, CONSTANT);
                assert_eq!(view_at(i, generation), Some(View::Constant(address, size)), "{address:#x} {size}");
            }
        }
        assert_eq!(constant_words(top + 1, 256), None, "an address past 47 bits");
        assert_eq!(constant_words(0x1000, (1 << 14) + 1), None, "16 KiB or more, no multiple of 256");
        assert_eq!(constant_words(0x1000, 1 << 22), None, "4 MiB");
        // Different views never share their words.
        assert_ne!(constant_words(0x1000, 256), constant_words(0x1000, 512));
        assert_ne!(constant_words(0x1000, 256), constant_words(0x1100, 256));
        assert_ne!(constant_words(0x1000, 1 << 14), constant_words(0x1000, 64));
    }

    /// The leak of run 65: a title that writes constant buffer views and
    /// views of placed memory at ever new addresses adds nothing to the
    /// table; one shape stands for all the placed views alike.
    #[test]
    fn views_at_new_addresses_add_no_entries() {
        if !inline() {
            return;
        }
        let null = std::ptr::null();
        let slots = [0u64; 4];
        let at = slots.as_ptr() as u64;
        // A resource description and a view no other test uses.
        let resource: [u32; 14] = std::array::from_fn(|k| 0x5ee0_0000 + k as u32);
        let mut desc: [u32; 16] = std::array::from_fn(|k| 0x7a70_0000 + k as u32);
        let mine = |v: &View| match v {
            View::Constant(address, _) => (0x6_0000_0000..0x6_1000_0000).contains(address),
            View::Placed(_, r, _) => *r == resource,
            _ => false,
        };
        let entries = || VIEWS.read().unwrap().list.iter().filter(|(v, _)| mine(v)).count();
        let shapes = || VIEWS.read().unwrap().shapes.iter().filter(|s| s.1 == resource).count();
        for n in 0..20_000u64 {
            let address = 0x6_0000_0000 + n * 0x100;
            create_cbv(null, &[address as u32, (address >> 32) as u32, 512, 0], at);
            assert_eq!(view(at), Some(View::Constant(address, 512)));
            let placed = 0xd_4940_0000 + n * 0x1_0000;
            (desc[10], desc[11]) = (placed as u32, (placed >> 32) as u32);
            create_placed_srv(null, &resource, &desc, at);
            assert_eq!(view(at), Some(View::Placed(false, resource, desc)));
        }
        assert_eq!(entries(), 0, "no table entries");
        assert_eq!(shapes(), 1, "one shape for 20,000 placed views");
        // The same shape, unordered: another shape.
        create_placed_uav(null, &resource, &desc, at);
        assert_eq!(view(at), Some(View::Placed(true, resource, desc)));
        assert_eq!(shapes(), 2);
        // Placed memory past 1 TiB (not title memory) is a table entry.
        (desc[10], desc[11]) = (0, 0x100);
        create_placed_srv(null, &resource, &desc, at);
        assert_eq!(view(at), Some(View::Placed(false, resource, desc)));
        assert_eq!(entries(), 1);
        // A record's words are the same for the same view (the host knows
        // a slot's view by them), and differ with the address.
        // SAFETY: both handles are slots of 32 bytes above.
        let words = |handle: u64| unsafe { *(handle as *const [u32; 3]) };
        let other = [0u64; 4];
        create_cbv(null, &[0x40, 6, 512, 0], at);
        create_cbv(null, &[0x40, 6, 512, 0], other.as_ptr() as u64);
        assert_eq!(words(at), words(other.as_ptr() as u64));
        create_cbv(null, &[0x140, 6, 512, 0], other.as_ptr() as u64);
        assert_ne!(words(at), words(other.as_ptr() as u64));
    }

    /// A released resource's views go stale; the same view of a new
    /// resource at the same address is a new record.
    #[test]
    fn views_die_with_their_resource() {
        let null = std::ptr::null();
        let slots = [0u64; 2 * 4];
        let (a, b) = (slots.as_ptr() as u64, slots.as_ptr() as u64 + 32);
        let resource = 0x7777_0000usize as This;
        create_srv(null, resource, std::ptr::null(), a);
        assert_eq!(view(a), Some(View::Shader(0x7777_0000, None)));
        forget(0x7777_0000);
        assert_eq!(view(a), None, "stale after release");
        create_srv(null, resource, std::ptr::null(), b);
        assert_eq!(view(b), Some(View::Shader(0x7777_0000, None)));
        // SAFETY: both slots are in `slots`.
        let (old, new) = unsafe { (*(a as *const [u32; 3]), *(b as *const [u32; 3])) };
        assert_ne!(old, new, "a new generation");
    }

    /// The title places its shader-visible heap in its own memory
    /// and checks that the heap starts there.
    #[test]
    fn placed_heaps_start_at_the_title_memory() {
        let mut memory = vec![0u8; 64 * 32];
        let address = memory.as_mut_ptr() as u64;
        let desc = HeapDesc {
            kind: 0,
            count: 64,
            flags: 1,
            nodes: 1,
        };
        let mut h = std::ptr::null();
        assert_eq!(
            create(
                desc,
                Placement {
                    address,
                    size: 64 * 32
                },
                &mut h
            ),
            S_OK
        );
        assert_eq!(slot::<extern "system" fn(This) -> u64>(h, 0x48)(h), address);
        assert_eq!(slot::<extern "system" fn(This) -> u64>(h, 0x50)(h), address);
        // A size that does not match the count is not a placement.
        assert_eq!(create(desc, Placement { address, size: 7 }, &mut h), S_OK);
        assert_ne!(slot::<extern "system" fn(This) -> u64>(h, 0x48)(h), address);
    }
}

```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/descriptor/host.rs`:

```rs
//! Host descriptor heaps behind the title's shader-visible heaps (decision
//! 0007, step 3). Translated shaders index the heaps directly at the
//! title's descriptor positions, so each host heap keeps the title heap's
//! order: slot `i` is made from what the title wrote at slot `i`, when it
//! writes it (view creation and descriptor copies) and again when a draw
//! reads it through a table and finds the slot changed.

use std::sync::Mutex;

use windows::Win32::Graphics::Direct3D12::*;
use windows::Win32::Graphics::Dxgi::Common::*;

use super::{VIEW_TAG, View, view_at};
use crate::host::host;

pub(crate) struct HostHeap {
    pub(crate) heap: ID3D12DescriptorHeap,
    cpu: usize,
    step: u32,
    /// Slots mirroring the title's; view heaps have `dynamic` more.
    count: u32,
    /// Dynamic slots past `count`: [`DYNAMIC`] in view heaps, none in
    /// sampler heaps. (Upstream falls back to 2^16 on a capped host heap;
    /// ours keeps 2^18 there: 2^16 and 2^17 both ran out in this title.)
    dynamic: u32,
    sampler: bool,
    /// The record (view index and generation) each slot was last made from.
    made: Mutex<Vec<u64>>,
    /// A fingerprint of the record each slot held when the pass over
    /// records copied in as bytes last looked at it
    /// ([`HostHeap::mirror_copied`]; 0: never looked at). Made on first use.
    copied: Mutex<Vec<u64>>,
    /// The host resource each slot views, held while the slot does: shaders
    /// index heaps directly, so a slot the title has not rewritten since it
    /// released the resource may still be read, and a freed host resource
    /// read there is a GPU page fault (the console reads stale memory).
    kept: Mutex<Vec<Option<ID3D12Resource>>>,
    /// Where the search for free dynamic slots starts, and which are taken
    /// (by lists not yet reset).
    next: Mutex<(u32, Vec<bool>)>,
    /// How many dynamic slots are free (changed under `next`'s lock): with
    /// fewer than a table needs, the search is not made. Once the world
    /// had taken them all, every later table of the frame searched every
    /// slot before it was refused.
    free: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32,
    /// The shortest table that found no run of free slots since slots were
    /// last given back (changed under `next`'s lock; `u32::MAX`: none).
    /// Until something is given back the free runs only shrink, so a table
    /// of that length or longer is refused without the search. Enough
    /// slots were free, but in pieces, and every such table walked the
    /// whole ring before it was refused: 0.33 ms each with 131,072 slots,
    /// 1.0 s of the recording threads in a frame that refused 3,143 (run
    /// 45), under the lock all of them need. (A free run that lies across
    /// the place the search starts from is seen by neither.)
    too_long: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32,
    /// View heaps: the bytes per element of the buffer view at each title
    /// slot, for shaders that pick a buffer by an index they compute
    /// (`victory_shader::emit::SLOT_STRIDES`): an upload buffer of
    /// `SLOT_STRIDES_COUNT` dwords, its GPU address and its mapping.
    strides: Option<(ID3D12Resource, u64, usize)>,
    /// Title slots holding buffer views. Such a view gets its host slot
    /// (and its memory a host copy) only when something reads it: a draw
    /// through a table, or [`HostHeap::buffer_slots`] for shaders that pick
    /// buffers from the whole heap.
    buffers: Mutex<std::collections::BTreeSet<u32>>,
    /// Of those and of the slots that left the set: the ones written since
    /// [`HostHeap::buffer_changes`] last took them.
    changed: Mutex<std::collections::HashSet<u32>>,
    /// Title slots holding a view of a texture the title may fill itself (a
    /// placed texture, a texture object), with the frame from which they
    /// are due: such a texture is uploaded when a draw reads it through a
    /// table; one a shader picks by a computed index is brought up to date
    /// from here ([`HostHeap::texture_slots_due`]).
    textures: Mutex<TextureQueue>,
    /// Per title slot, the frame (plus one; 0: never) in which a draw last
    /// read it through a table, or made a table it lies in (with
    /// [`TABLED_READ`] set if the draw read it). The draw that
    /// reads such a slot brings its texture up to date itself and the slot
    /// then leaves `textures`; a write of a slot that was a table's within
    /// the last [`TABLED_FRAMES`] frames is due only [`TABLED_GRACE`]
    /// frames later, by when its draw has read it. A title that builds a
    /// table per draw writes thousands of texture views a frame into slots
    /// only tables read (the title: some 2,500 a frame in its
    /// opening cutscene, a few hundred textures over and over), and every
    /// one of them stood in the queue of textures picked by index, ahead
    /// of or behind the ones shaders do pick by index.
    tabled: Vec<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32>,
    /// The title memory each placed texture view of this heap describes,
    /// by slot and by address ([`Spans`]): which slots a newer view of
    /// other memory there makes stale, and which to look at again when the
    /// runtime maps, unmaps or writes memory ([`remapped`]).
    placed: std::sync::Arc<Mutex<Spans>>,
}

/// The spans of every view heap made ([`HostHeap::placed`]), for the
/// texture code, which has no heap at hand ([`next_start`],
/// [`first_viewed`]).
static PLACED_SPANS: Mutex<Vec<std::sync::Weak<Mutex<Spans>>>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());

/// Where the next texture placed inside `[start, end)` starts, past the
/// first bytes of the one at `start` ([`HEAD`]): what is there of the
/// texture at `start` ends there, whatever its full size. `None`: no view
/// in a slot shaders pick by index describes memory in that range.
pub(crate) fn next_start(start: u64, end: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    let heaps = PLACED_SPANS.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    heaps
        .iter()
        .filter_map(std::sync::Weak::upgrade)
        .filter_map(|spans| spans.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).next_start(start, end))
        .min()
}

/// The lowest level that a view of the placed texture at `start` shows,
/// over the slots shaders pick by index that hold one now. The title
/// views a texture from the first level it holds. `None`: no such slot.
pub(crate) fn first_viewed(start: u64) -> Option<u32> {
    let heaps = PLACED_SPANS.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    heaps
        .iter()
        .filter_map(std::sync::Weak::upgrade)
        .filter_map(|spans| spans.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).first_viewed(start))
        .min()
}

/// Levels on demand (`crate::tiles`): where the placed textures start
/// whose first level with memory changed since a texture pass last took
/// them ([`HostHeap::texture_views_remade`]).
static RESHOWN: Mutex<Vec<u64>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());

/// The first level with memory of the placed texture at `start` changed:
/// its slots are made again at the next texture pass.
pub(crate) fn levels_changed(start: u64) {
    RESHOWN.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push(start);
}

/// Levels on demand (`crate::tiles`): where the placed textures start
/// whose last upload left a held level without tiles (the card had no
/// room, or no heap could be had), and when (`crate::host::moment`). A
/// texture pass makes their slots due again once the card has room
/// ([`HostHeap::texture_slots_waiting`]).
static WAITING: Mutex<std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, u64>> = Mutex::new(std::collections::BTreeMap::new());

/// The last upload of the placed texture at `start` left a held level
/// without tiles. A texture picked by index is uploaded once and then
/// only when its memory is found changed, and its staging buffer goes
/// with the upload: without this the level stayed empty (the texture
/// blurred, or black if no level had tiles) for as long as the title left
/// its memory alone, where a texture refused for want of room is tried
/// again.
pub(crate) fn levels_waiting(start: u64) {
    WAITING.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).insert(start, crate::host::moment());
}

/// Title memory by the placed texture views that describe it: per span of
/// memory (its start, its end at full size) the title slots holding a
/// view of a texture that takes exactly that span. A console title need
/// not clear a descriptor when it streams a texture out, so a newer view
/// that cannot be there together with an older one is all that says the
/// older one is stale ([`Rule`] says when that is). Views of one span with
/// different descriptions (the formats of one family, say) are one
/// texture's.
///
/// Spans may overlap: a texture's smallest levels lie at the start of its
/// memory, and a title that holds only those puts the next texture where
/// the larger ones would be (the title: three 512x256 textures
/// of 0x2c000 bytes each whose starts are 0x2000 and 0x4000 apart, all
/// three read by the same frame's draws, run 188). What is there of a
/// texture ends where the next one starts.
/// No host heap is needed, so it is tested without one.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Spans {
    /// When a newer view makes an older one stale.
    rule: Rule,
    by_start: std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, (u64, std::collections::BTreeSet<u32>)>,
    by_slot: std::collections::HashMap<u32, u64>,
    /// The level each slot's view starts at ([`Spans::shows`]).
    first: std::collections::HashMap<u32, u32>,
    /// The bytes a placed texture takes, by resource description: worked
    /// out once for each (a title writes the views of a few thousand
    /// descriptions, thousands of times a frame).
    sizes: std::collections::HashMap<[u32; 14], Option<u64>>,
}

/// When a view the title writes makes an older view of other memory stale.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Rule {
    /// When it starts where the older one starts: at the same address
    /// with another length, or within the older one's first [`HEAD`]
    /// bytes (or the older within its own). No two textures share the
    /// block of their smallest levels. A view that only reaches into the
    /// address range of an older texture's larger levels says nothing.
    #[default]
    Start,
    /// Whenever their spans at full size overlap (the rule until run
    /// 188, where it made null the slots of textures packed as above:
    /// each view written took its neighbours out of the queue and off the
    /// card, for good). `VICTORY_STALE_TEXTURES=overlap`.
    Overlap,
    /// Never; a view that would be stale under [`Rule::Overlap`] is left
    /// out of the spans instead. `VICTORY_STALE_TEXTURES=0`, as before.
    Never,
}

/// The first bytes of a placed texture that are its own under
/// [`Rule::Start`]: the 4 KiB block its smallest levels share. (Of 129
/// pairs of overlapping neighbours in the listings of runs 188 and 189,
/// none starts closer than 0x2000 to the one before it.)
const HEAD: u64 = 4096;

impl Spans {
    /// The bytes of title memory a placed texture with the resource
    /// description `desc` takes (`crate::resource::placed_bytes`).
    fn bytes(&mut self, desc: &[u32; 14]) -> Option<u64> {
        if let Some(&known) = self.sizes.get(desc) {
            return known;
        }
        let bytes = crate::resource::placed_bytes(desc);
        self.sizes.insert(*desc, bytes);
        bytes
    }

    /// The starts of the spans that overlap `[start, end)`, each taken to
    /// end where the next one starts: the last span that starts before
    /// `start`, if it reaches past it at full size, and every span that
    /// starts inside.
    fn overlapping(&self, start: u64, end: u64) -> Vec<u64> {
        let before = self
            .by_start
            .range(..start)
            .next_back()
            .filter(|(_, span)| span.0 > start)
            .map(|(at, _)| *at);
        before.into_iter().chain(self.by_start.range(start..end).map(|(at, _)| *at)).collect()
    }

    /// Slot `index` holds a view of a texture in `[start, end)`. `newer`:
    /// the title wrote it now, so the slots whose views cannot be there
    /// with it ([`Rule`]) are stale: they are returned, and forgotten.
    /// Otherwise (a draw made the slot from what it held), and under
    /// [`Rule::Never`], a view that clashes with other spans is left out.
    fn note(&mut self, index: u32, start: u64, end: u64, newer: bool) -> Vec<u32> {
        let same = |span: Option<&(u64, std::collections::BTreeSet<u32>)>| span.is_some_and(|s| s.0 == end);
        if self.by_slot.get(&index) == Some(&start) && same(self.by_start.get(&start)) {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        self.forget(index);
        if end <= start {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let rule = self.rule;
        // The spans the view cannot be there with.
        let clashing: Vec<u64> = match rule {
            Rule::Start => self
                .by_start
                .range(start.saturating_sub(HEAD - 1)..start.saturating_add(HEAD))
                .map(|(at, _)| *at)
                .collect(),
            Rule::Overlap | Rule::Never => self.overlapping(start, end),
        };
        let mut stale = Vec::new();
        for at in clashing {
            if at == start && same(self.by_start.get(&at)) {
                continue;
            }
            if !newer || rule == Rule::Never {
                return stale;
            }
            if let Some((old_end, slots)) = self.by_start.remove(&at) {
                // The first of them are said with both spans, to tell a
                // replacement from a neighbour in one launch's log.
                static SAID: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0);
                if SAID.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) < 48 {
                    tracing::info!(
                        slot = index,
                        start = format_args!("{start:#x}"),
                        end = format_args!("{end:#x}"),
                        stale_start = format_args!("{at:#x}"),
                        stale_end = format_args!("{old_end:#x}"),
                        stale_slots = slots.len(),
                        rule = ?rule,
                        "a placed texture view makes older views of other memory stale"
                    );
                }
                for slot in slots {
                    self.by_slot.remove(&slot);
                    stale.push(slot);
                }
            }
        }
        self.by_start.entry(start).or_insert_with(|| (end, Default::default())).1.insert(index);
        self.by_slot.insert(index, start);
        stale
    }

    /// The view in slot `index` starts at level `first` of its texture.
    fn shows(&mut self, index: u32, first: u32) {
        self.first.insert(index, first);
    }

    /// The lowest level a view of the texture at `start` starts at.
    fn first_viewed(&self, start: u64) -> Option<u32> {
        self.by_start.get(&start)?.1.iter().filter_map(|slot| self.first.get(slot)).min().copied()
    }

    /// The first span that starts inside `[start, end)` past the first
    /// [`HEAD`] bytes of it.
    fn next_start(&self, start: u64, end: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        self.by_start.range(start.saturating_add(HEAD)..end).next().map(|(at, _)| *at)
    }

    /// The slots that hold a view of the texture at `start`.
    fn slots_at(&self, start: u64) -> Vec<u32> {
        self.by_start.get(&start).map(|span| span.1.iter().copied().collect()).unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// Slot `index` holds no placed texture view any more.
    fn forget(&mut self, index: u32) {
        self.first.remove(&index);
        let Some(start) = self.by_slot.remove(&index) else {
            return;
        };
        if let Some(span) = self.by_start.get_mut(&start) {
            span.1.remove(&index);
            if span.1.is_empty() {
                self.by_start.remove(&start);
            }
        }
    }

    /// The slots whose texture's memory overlaps `[start, end)`.
    fn slots_in(&self, start: u64, end: u64) -> Vec<u32> {
        self.overlapping(start, end)
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|at| self.by_start.get(at))
            .flat_map(|span| span.1.iter().copied())
            .collect()
    }

    /// The slots of the textures that hold bytes of `[start, end)`, for a
    /// write there: as [`Spans::slots_in`], but when a texture starts at
    /// `start` itself the one before it is left out (it ends where that
    /// one starts, and a request that fills a texture begins at its first
    /// byte: `slots_in` would name its neighbour with every such write).
    fn slots_holding(&self, start: u64, end: u64) -> Vec<u32> {
        if end <= start {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let before = if self.by_start.contains_key(&start) {
            None
        } else {
            self.by_start.range(..start).next_back().filter(|(_, span)| span.0 > start).map(|(_, span)| span)
        };
        before
            .into_iter()
            .chain(self.by_start.range(start..end).map(|(_, span)| span))
            .flat_map(|span| span.1.iter().copied())
            .collect()
    }
}

/// Title memory written behind the guards' back whose bytes are there
/// (DirectStorage's reads into physical pages, at the addresses the title
/// has them mapped; `crate::watch::title_memory_written`), since a texture
/// pass last took the ranges ([`page_written`]). Kept apart from
/// [`REMAPPED`] so that what such writes do is counted by itself.
static PAGE_WRITTEN: Mutex<Vec<(u64, u64)>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());

/// Since the start: such ranges kept for a pass; ranges dropped because no
/// pass took them; slots of placed textures that held bytes of them when a
/// pass took them; of those, the slots whose texture had been uploaded
/// before the write (out of the queue, or in it after an upload): they are
/// the ones that kept the bytes from before, and the ones made due when
/// `VICTORY_PAGE_WRITES` asks for it.
pub(crate) static PAGE_WRITES: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64; 4] =
    [const { std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0) }; 4];

/// Frames from the pass that takes a written range to the look at its
/// slots: the levels of one texture arrive in a few requests, and a look
/// two frames on takes those of the next frame with it.
const PAGE_WRITE_AFTER: u64 = 2;

/// The bytes of a write the guards do not see are in title memory `[at,
/// at + len)`: the placed textures there changed with no descriptor
/// written and nothing mapped. Kept for the next texture pass
/// ([`HostHeap::texture_slots_page_written`]), as [`remapped`] keeps its
/// ranges; locks one mutex and calls nothing.
pub(crate) fn page_written(at: usize, len: usize) {
    use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
    /// Ranges kept until a pass takes them.
    const MOST: usize = 1 << 15;
    let (start, end) = (at as u64, at.saturating_add(len) as u64);
    if end <= SPANNED[0].load(Relaxed) || start >= SPANNED[1].load(Relaxed) {
        return;
    }
    let mut ranges = PAGE_WRITTEN.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    PAGE_WRITES[0].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
    if let Some(last) = ranges.last_mut()
        && last.1 == start
    {
        last.1 = end;
        return;
    }
    if ranges.len() >= MOST {
        PAGE_WRITES[1].fetch_add(ranges.len() as u64, Relaxed);
        ranges.clear();
    }
    ranges.push((start, end));
}

/// Title memory the runtime mapped, unmapped or is about to write since a
/// texture pass last took the ranges ([`remapped`]).
static REMAPPED: Mutex<Vec<(u64, u64)>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());

/// The lowest start and the highest end of any span of [`Spans`] so far
/// (the start is `u64::MAX` until there is one): what the runtime does to
/// memory outside is none of the texture pass's business.
static SPANNED: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64; 2] = [
    std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(u64::MAX),
    std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0),
];

/// Since the start: slots whose view a newer view of other memory there
/// made stale; ranges of memory noted as mapped, unmapped or written;
/// ranges dropped because no pass took them; slots made due by such
/// ranges; and made slots whose memory was found unmapped (made null).
pub(crate) static STALE: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64; 5] =
    [const { std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0) }; 5];

/// When a view the title writes makes older views of other memory stale
/// ([`Rule`]): where it starts in the block of their smallest levels, by
/// default; `VICTORY_STALE_TEXTURES=0`: never, as before;
/// `VICTORY_STALE_TEXTURES=overlap`: wherever their spans overlap, the rule
/// until run 188.
fn stale_rule() -> Rule {
    static RULE: std::sync::OnceLock<Rule> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *RULE.get_or_init(|| match std::env::var("VICTORY_STALE_TEXTURES").as_deref() {
        Ok("0") => Rule::Never,
        Ok("overlap") => Rule::Overlap,
        _ => Rule::Start,
    })
}

/// The runtime mapped or unmapped title memory `[at, at + len)`, or is
/// about to write it through the kernel (`crate::watch`): the placed
/// textures there may have arrived, gone, or changed with no descriptor
/// written. The range is kept for the next texture pass
/// ([`HostHeap::texture_slots_remapped`]). Called with the runtime's own
/// locks held: this locks one mutex of its own and calls nothing.
pub(crate) fn remapped(at: usize, len: usize) {
    use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
    /// Ranges kept until a pass takes them.
    const MOST: usize = 1 << 15;
    let (start, end) = (at as u64, at.saturating_add(len) as u64);
    if end <= SPANNED[0].load(Relaxed) || start >= SPANNED[1].load(Relaxed) {
        return;
    }
    let mut ranges = REMAPPED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    STALE[1].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
    // Pages are mapped one after the other.
    if let Some(last) = ranges.last_mut()
        && last.1 == start
    {
        last.1 = end;
        return;
    }
    if ranges.len() >= MOST {
        // No pass runs (no shader that picks textures by index is bound):
        // the slots there are looked at when they are due, as before.
        STALE[2].fetch_add(ranges.len() as u64, Relaxed);
        ranges.clear();
    }
    ranges.push((start, end));
}

/// Frames for which a slot a draw read through a table counts as a table's
/// slot ([`HostHeap::tabled`]).
const TABLED_FRAMES: u64 = 240;

/// Frames a write of a table's slot waits in the queue for the draw that
/// reads it, before the slot is taken for one shaders pick by index.
/// Frames as `crate::frame::current` counts them: in its opening cutscene
/// The title begins two or three of them per frame it presents
/// (435 begun in the 353 s of run 52's, for some 140 presented).
const TABLED_GRACE: u64 = 8;

/// In [`HostHeap::tabled`]: a draw read the slot in that frame.
const TABLED_READ: u32 = 1 << 31;

/// Since the start: writes of texture views into slots that count as a
/// table's (due later), and slots that left the queue because a draw read
/// them through a table.
pub(crate) static TABLED_WRITES: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64; 2] =
    [const { std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0) }; 2];

/// Whether slots draws read through tables leave the queue of textures
/// picked by index; `VICTORY_TABLED_TEXTURES=1` keeps them in it as
/// before.
fn tabled_out() -> bool {
    static ON: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_TABLED_TEXTURES").is_none_or(|v| v != "1"))
}

/// What the queue of textures picked by index knows of a title slot.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Waiting {
    /// The frame from which the slot is due.
    due: u64,
    /// The frame it was written in.
    written: u64,
    /// Which write of the queue put it here: the pass hands it back with
    /// what it did, so a slot written again meanwhile stays as written.
    write: u64,
    /// Looks in a row that found nothing to upload (its memory not mapped,
    /// or no more of it than at the last upload).
    looks: u8,
    /// Bytes of its memory that were mapped when it was last uploaded
    /// without all of it there; 0: not uploaded yet.
    mapped: u64,
    /// For a slot uploaded whole and looked at again
    /// ([`TextureQueue::recheck`]): where its memory is (address, bytes),
    /// the fingerprint it had at the upload, how many looks found it
    /// unchanged, and the frame of the upload. A fingerprint of 0: none.
    checked: (u64, u64, u64, u8, u64),
}

/// The queue of title slots whose texture view waits to be brought up to
/// date for shaders that pick textures by index: which are due, and in
/// which order (no host heap needed, so it is tested without one).
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct TextureQueue {
    slots: std::collections::BTreeMap<u32, Waiting>,
    writes: u64,
    /// Slots held back because the card had no room for the host copy
    /// they need ([`TextureQueue::hold`]), each with the write it was
    /// held as.
    held: std::collections::BTreeMap<u32, u64>,
}

impl TextureQueue {
    /// A texture view was written into slot `index` in `frame`, due from
    /// frame `due`. `seen`: it was not written, a draw or the pass made
    /// the host slot from a view the queue may hold already, which then
    /// stays as it is.
    fn written(&mut self, index: u32, frame: u64, due: u64, seen: bool) {
        if seen && self.slots.contains_key(&index) {
            return;
        }
        self.writes += 1;
        let write = self.writes;
        self.slots.insert(index, Waiting { due, written: frame, write, looks: 0, mapped: 0, checked: (0, 0, 0, 0, 0) });
    }

    fn remove(&mut self, index: u32) {
        self.slots.remove(&index);
    }

    /// Up to `max` slots due at `frame`, each with its write number, in
    /// the order to serve them:
    /// - first the ones looked at before (their memory was not mapped, or
    ///   only part of it): the look is a query, and memory that has
    ///   arrived since is what the title streamed in last;
    /// - then the others, the newest write first and the oldest next, in
    ///   turns: slot order served the low slots of a backlog of
    ///   25,000-40,000 while the textures of the shot on screen waited
    ///   (run 52: 98% of the drawn pixels had no colour texture in the
    ///   first 3D frames).
    fn due(&self, frame: u64, max: usize) -> Vec<(u32, u64)> {
        let mut again: Vec<(u64, u32, u64)> = Vec::new();
        let mut fresh: Vec<(u64, u32, u64)> = Vec::new();
        for (&index, w) in self.slots.iter().filter(|(_, w)| w.due <= frame) {
            let class = if w.looks > 0 || w.mapped > 0 { &mut again } else { &mut fresh };
            class.push((w.written, index, w.write));
        }
        // By the number of the write, counted over the run.
        let newest_first = |a: &(u64, u32, u64), b: &(u64, u32, u64)| b.2.cmp(&a.2);
        again.sort_unstable_by(newest_first);
        fresh.sort_unstable_by(newest_first);
        let mut order: Vec<(u32, u64)> = again.iter().map(|&(_, index, write)| (index, write)).collect();
        let (mut new, mut old) = (0, fresh.len());
        while new < old && order.len() < max {
            order.push((fresh[new].1, fresh[new].2));
            new += 1;
            if new < old && order.len() < max {
                old -= 1;
                order.push((fresh[old].1, fresh[old].2));
            }
        }
        order.truncate(max);
        order
    }

    /// The entry of `index` if it is still the write the pass was handed.
    fn same(&mut self, index: u32, write: u64) -> Option<&mut Waiting> {
        self.slots.get_mut(&index).filter(|w| w.write == write)
    }

    /// Slot `index` is up to date: out of the queue until written again.
    fn done(&mut self, index: u32, write: u64) {
        if self.same(index, write).is_some() {
            self.slots.remove(&index);
        }
    }

    /// Nothing to upload at slot `index` now: looked at again after 1, 2,
    /// 4, ... frames, at most `most`.
    fn later(&mut self, index: u32, write: u64, frame: u64, most: u64) {
        if let Some(w) = self.same(index, write) {
            w.due = frame + (1u64 << w.looks.min(16)).min(most.max(1));
            w.looks = w.looks.saturating_add(1);
        }
    }

    /// The card has no room for the host copy slot `index` needs: it is
    /// not handed out again before frame `due`, or before the card has
    /// room again ([`TextureQueue::room`]). Nothing else of it changes: it
    /// is not a slot "waiting for its memory", and when it is due it has
    /// its old place among the slots never looked at. (It stayed due, so
    /// every pass on a full card looked at the same few hundred slots
    /// again and stopped there, and the slots behind them were never
    /// reached: the ones whose host copy exists and only wants bringing up
    /// to date, and the ones whose memory went, which is what lets host
    /// copies go and makes room.)
    fn hold(&mut self, index: u32, write: u64, due: u64) {
        if let Some(w) = self.same(index, write) {
            w.due = w.due.max(due);
            self.held.insert(index, write);
        }
    }

    /// The card has room again at `frame`: the slots held back for lack of
    /// it are due now, as if they had never been held. Returns how many.
    fn room(&mut self, frame: u64) -> usize {
        let held = std::mem::take(&mut self.held);
        let mut back = 0;
        for (index, write) in held {
            if let Some(w) = self.same(index, write) {
                w.due = w.due.min(frame);
                back += 1;
            }
        }
        back
    }

    /// Slot `index` was uploaded with `mapped` bytes of its memory there,
    /// not all of it: looked at again from frame `due`.
    fn partly(&mut self, index: u32, write: u64, due: u64, mapped: u64) {
        if let Some(w) = self.same(index, write) {
            (w.due, w.looks, w.mapped) = (due, 0, mapped.max(1));
        }
    }

    /// Slot `index` was uploaded whole from memory `at` (address, bytes)
    /// with fingerprint `print`: looked at again from frame `due`, for a
    /// title that fills a texture's memory after it wrote the view (the
    /// `looks`-th such look; `uploaded` is the upload's frame).
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    fn recheck(&mut self, index: u32, write: u64, due: u64, at: (u64, u64), print: u64, looks: u8, uploaded: u64) {
        if let Some(w) = self.same(index, write) {
            (w.due, w.looks, w.mapped) = (due, 1, 0);
            w.checked = (at.0, at.1, print, looks, uploaded);
        }
    }

    /// What [`TextureQueue::recheck`] noted of slot `index`, if it is
    /// waiting for such a look.
    fn checked(&self, index: u32) -> Option<(u64, u64, u64, u8, u64)> {
        self.slots.get(&index).map(|w| w.checked).filter(|c| c.2 != 0)
    }

    /// The memory slot `index`'s texture lies in was mapped, unmapped or
    /// written in `frame`: the slot is looked at from frame `due` as one
    /// written now, whatever was known of it (a pass at work on it does
    /// not take it out).
    fn changed(&mut self, index: u32, frame: u64, due: u64) {
        self.writes += 1;
        let write = self.writes;
        let due = self.slots.get(&index).map_or(due, |w| w.due.min(due));
        self.slots.insert(index, Waiting { due, written: frame, write, looks: 0, mapped: 0, checked: (0, 0, 0, 0, 0) });
    }

    /// Bytes of slot `index`'s memory that were mapped at its last upload
    /// (0: not uploaded, or all of it was).
    fn mapped(&self, index: u32) -> u64 {
        self.slots.get(&index).map_or(0, |w| w.mapped)
    }

    /// For the frame line: slots in the queue; of them due at `frame`;
    /// waiting for their memory (looked at, never uploaded); uploaded in
    /// part; and the frames the oldest due one has waited since its write.
    fn census(&self, frame: u64) -> [u64; 5] {
        let mut c = [self.slots.len() as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0];
        for w in self.slots.values() {
            if w.mapped > 0 {
                c[3] += 1;
            } else if w.looks > 0 {
                c[2] += 1;
            }
            if w.due <= frame {
                c[1] += 1;
                c[4] = c[4].max(frame.saturating_sub(w.written));
            }
        }
        c
    }
}

/// Whether `view` is of a texture the title may fill itself: a texture it
/// placed in memory, or a texture object.
pub(crate) fn is_texture_view(view: &View) -> bool {
    match view {
        View::Placed(false, resource, _) => resource[0] != 1,
        View::Shader(r, _) => crate::resource::buffer_bytes(*r as crate::object::This).is_none(),
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// Buffer views left null because the host would refuse them
/// ([`buffer_view_ok`]), since the start.
pub(crate) static REFUSED_VIEWS: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);

/// Whether the host device is gone, and why (the first time it is asked
/// after that): for passes that make many views, to name the one that did
/// it.
pub(crate) fn device_removed() -> Option<String> {
    let host = host()?;
    // SAFETY: a plain query.
    let reason = unsafe { host.device.GetDeviceRemovedReason() };
    reason.err().map(|e| e.to_string())
}

/// Writes of title view-heap slots with a placed texture view and with a
/// view of a texture object, since the start (diagnostic counts).
pub(crate) static PLACED_TEXTURE_SLOTS: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);
pub(crate) static OBJECT_TEXTURE_SLOTS: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);

/// Bytes per element of a buffer view, as the console's descriptor holds
/// them for indexed reads (structured: the stride; raw: 1, the index is the
/// byte; typed: the format's); `None` if `view` is not a buffer view.
fn view_stride(view: &View) -> Option<u32> {
    const BUFFER: u32 = 1;
    let (words, unordered): (&[u32; 10], bool) = match view {
        View::Shader(_, Some(d)) if d[1] == BUFFER => (d, false),
        View::Unordered(_, _, Some(d)) if d[1] == BUFFER => (d, true),
        View::Placed(unordered, resource, d) if resource[0] == BUFFER => {
            (d[..10].try_into().ok()?, *unordered)
        }
        _ => return None,
    };
    // SAFETY: buffer views' union members.
    let (stride, raw, format) = unsafe {
        if unordered {
            let d = uav_desc(words);
            let b = d.Anonymous.Buffer;
            (b.StructureByteStride, b.Flags.0 & D3D12_BUFFER_UAV_FLAG_RAW.0 != 0, d.Format)
        } else {
            let d = srv_desc(words);
            let b = d.Anonymous.Buffer;
            (b.StructureByteStride, b.Flags.0 & D3D12_BUFFER_SRV_FLAG_RAW.0 != 0, d.Format)
        }
    };
    Some(if stride > 0 {
        stride
    } else if raw {
        1
    } else {
        crate::resource::element(format.0 as u32).map_or(0, |(bytes, _)| bytes as u32)
    })
}

/// Host heaps' GPU ranges (start, bytes, bytes per slot, sampler), for
/// device-removed reports: a shader indexing a heap past its end faults.
static GPU_RANGES: Mutex<Vec<(u64, u64, u64, bool)>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());

/// For device-removed reports: where host GPU address `va` lies against
/// the host descriptor heaps.
pub(crate) fn near_heaps(va: u64) -> String {
    let ranges = GPU_RANGES.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    let mut text = String::new();
    for &(start, bytes, step, sampler) in ranges.iter() {
        let kind = if sampler { "sampler" } else { "view" };
        let place = if va < start {
            format!("{:#x} below", start - va)
        } else if va < start + bytes {
            format!("inside, slot {}", (va - start) / step)
        } else {
            format!("{:#x} past its end (slot {})", va - start - bytes, (va - start) / step)
        };
        text.push_str(&format!("; {kind} heap {start:#x}+{bytes:#x}: {place}"));
    }
    text
}

/// The host's limit for shader-visible view heaps on resource binding
/// tiers 1 and 2; tier 3 hardware may take more.
const PORTABLE_VIEWS: u32 = 1_000_000;

/// The size of every host view heap on a host that takes more than
/// [`PORTABLE_VIEWS`] (AMD): the title's heap (a little over 1,000,000
/// views in the retail game) plus [`DYNAMIC`] fits with room to spare, and
/// the last slot is the null slot every view index at or past it reads.
const UNCAPPED_VIEWS: u32 = 1 << 21;

/// Picks, once, the null slot at the end of every host view heap and tells
/// the translator now (`set_view_heap_limit`) instead of when the title's
/// heap is made: a shader keeps the limit it was translated with, and the
/// title makes 25 pipelines (their shaders translated at once) before it
/// makes its view heap. Called before a shader is translated and before a
/// view heap is made.
///
/// Every host clamps. A host that caps view heaps at [`PORTABLE_VIEWS`]
/// (NVIDIA) hung on a view index past the heap; one that does not (AMD
/// RDNA3, RX 7900 XT) took a page fault and removed the device on entering
/// the world: a compute program read view slot 16,777,088 (0xffff80) of a
/// heap of 1,507,328, past its end. Unclamped, that index is undefined on
/// any host.
pub(crate) fn probe_view_limit() {
    static ONCE: std::sync::Once = std::sync::Once::new();
    ONCE.call_once(|| {
        let Some(host) = host() else { return };
        let fits = |count: u32| {
            // SAFETY: plain heap creation; the heap is released at once.
            let made: windows::core::Result<ID3D12DescriptorHeap> = unsafe {
                host.device
                    .CreateDescriptorHeap(&D3D12_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_DESC {
                        Type: D3D12_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_TYPE_CBV_SRV_UAV,
                        NumDescriptors: count,
                        Flags: D3D12_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_FLAG_SHADER_VISIBLE,
                        NodeMask: 0,
                    })
            };
            made.is_ok()
        };
        let views = if fits(UNCAPPED_VIEWS) {
            UNCAPPED_VIEWS
        } else {
            PORTABLE_VIEWS
        };
        tracing::info!(
            views,
            "host view heaps hold {views} views; view indices are clamped to the null slot at the end from the first shader on"
        );
        victory_shader::emit::set_view_heap_limit(views - 1);
    });
}

/// Slots past the title's in a view heap, for tables a draw needs made
/// afresh (constant buffers copied per draw). A list holds the slots it
/// took until it is reset (its submissions have run) or released.
/// 2^16 ran out in the world ("no free dynamic descriptor slots", run 11;
/// upstream PR #336 takes 2^18). On a host heap capped at 1,000,000 views
/// (NVIDIA) these come out of the title's slots, whose highest seen is
/// about 720,000: 2^17 left 868,000 of them, and ran out in the opening
/// cutscene (a frame asks for up to 16,000 tables while the frame before
/// still holds its own; a draw refused its table read slots never made
/// for it, and the card stopped within frames). 2^18 leaves 737,000; a
/// table past them is made afresh in these slots like any other.
pub(crate) const DYNAMIC: u32 = 1 << 18;

impl HostHeap {
    pub(crate) fn new(sampler: bool, count: u32) -> Option<Self> {
        let host = host()?;
        let kind = if sampler {
            D3D12_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_TYPE_SAMPLER
        } else {
            D3D12_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_TYPE_CBV_SRV_UAV
        };
        let make = |count: u32| -> windows::core::Result<ID3D12DescriptorHeap> {
            // SAFETY: plain heap creation.
            unsafe {
                host.device
                    .CreateDescriptorHeap(&D3D12_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_DESC {
                        Type: kind,
                        NumDescriptors: count,
                        Flags: D3D12_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_FLAG_SHADER_VISIBLE,
                        NodeMask: 0,
                    })
            }
        };
        let extra = if sampler { 0 } else { DYNAMIC };
        // A view heap ends at the null slot shaders clamp view indices to
        // (`probe_view_limit`), whatever the title's own count: the title's
        // slots, then the dynamic ones, then null up to and with that slot.
        if !sampler {
            probe_view_limit();
        }
        let null = if sampler {
            0
        } else {
            victory_shader::emit::view_heap_limit()
        };
        let (heap, count, size) = if null == 0 {
            match make(count + extra) {
                Ok(heap) => (heap, count, count + extra),
                Err(e) => {
                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, count, sampler, "no host descriptor heap");
                    return None;
                }
            }
        } else {
            let size = null + 1;
            let fitted = if count + extra <= null {
                count
            } else {
                // shortcut: descriptors past the host's limit are left out; a title that reaches
                // them needs remapping. They read the null slot instead.
                tracing::warn!(count, "host view heap capped at {size}; views past it read a null slot");
                null - extra
            };
            match make(size) {
                Ok(heap) => (heap, fitted, size),
                Err(e) => {
                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, count, size, "no host view heap");
                    return None;
                }
            }
        };
        // SAFETY: a live heap.
        let (cpu, step) = unsafe {
            (
                heap.GetCPUDescriptorHandleForHeapStart().ptr,
                host.device.GetDescriptorHandleIncrementSize(kind),
            )
        };
        tracing::debug!(count, sampler, "host descriptor heap");
        // SAFETY: a live shader-visible heap.
        let gpu = unsafe { heap.GetGPUDescriptorHandleForHeapStart().ptr };
        GPU_RANGES.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push((
            gpu,
            u64::from(size) * u64::from(step),
            u64::from(step),
            sampler,
        ));
        let strides = (!sampler)
            .then(|| {
                let bytes = u64::from(victory_shader::emit::SLOT_STRIDES_COUNT) * 4;
                let (buffer, data) = host.upload_buffer(bytes)?;
                // SAFETY: the buffer's whole mapping; a live buffer.
                let gpu = unsafe {
                    std::ptr::write_bytes(data, 0, bytes as usize);
                    buffer.GetGPUVirtualAddress()
                };
                crate::host::name(&buffer, || "element strides by view heap slot".to_owned());
                Some((buffer, gpu, data as usize))
            })
            .flatten();
        let h = HostHeap {
            heap,
            cpu,
            step,
            count,
            dynamic: extra,
            sampler,
            made: Mutex::new(vec![0; count as usize]),
            copied: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
            kept: Mutex::new(vec![None; (count + extra) as usize]),
            next: Mutex::new((0, vec![false; DYNAMIC as usize])),
            free: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(DYNAMIC),
            too_long: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(u32::MAX),
            strides,
            buffers: Mutex::default(),
            changed: Mutex::default(),
            textures: Mutex::default(),
            tabled: (0..if sampler { 0 } else { count })
                .map(|_| std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0))
                .collect(),
            placed: {
                let spans = std::sync::Arc::<Mutex<Spans>>::default();
                if !sampler {
                    PLACED_SPANS
                        .lock()
                        .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                        .push(std::sync::Arc::downgrade(&spans));
                }
                spans
            },
        };
        // A slot never written is undefined: shaders reading one (a slot
        // the title wrote in a way we do not know, or a table entry no
        // used-resource entry names) read a wild address. Every slot starts
        // null instead.
        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
        if let Err(e) = h.fill_null(kind, size) {
            tracing::warn!(error = %e, "host descriptor heap not made null");
        }
        tracing::debug!(ms = started.elapsed().as_millis(), "host descriptor heap made null");
        Some(h)
    }

    /// Makes the first `total` slots null: one null slot in a CPU-side heap,
    /// doubled by copies to a block, the block copied over the heap.
    fn fill_null(&self, kind: D3D12_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_TYPE, total: u32) -> windows::core::Result<()> {
        const BLOCK: u32 = 1 << 16;
        let Some(host) = host() else { return Ok(()) };
        // SAFETY: plain heap creation and copies inside live heaps.
        unsafe {
            let block: ID3D12DescriptorHeap =
                host.device.CreateDescriptorHeap(&D3D12_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_DESC {
                    Type: kind,
                    NumDescriptors: BLOCK,
                    ..Default::default()
                })?;
            let start = block.GetCPUDescriptorHandleForHeapStart();
            let at = |i: u32| D3D12_CPU_DESCRIPTOR_HANDLE {
                ptr: start.ptr + (i * self.step) as usize,
            };
            if self.sampler {
                null_sampler(start);
            } else {
                null_view(start);
            }
            let mut filled = 1;
            while filled < BLOCK {
                let n = filled.min(BLOCK - filled);
                host.device.CopyDescriptorsSimple(n, at(filled), start, kind);
                filled += n;
            }
            let mut done = 0;
            while done < total {
                let n = BLOCK.min(total - done);
                host.device.CopyDescriptorsSimple(n, self.cpu(done), start, kind);
                done += n;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// A plain point sampler at slot `index`, for sampler slots without a
    /// view.
    fn null_sampler(&self, index: u32) {
        null_sampler(self.cpu(index));
    }
}

/// A plain point sampler at `at`.
fn null_sampler(at: D3D12_CPU_DESCRIPTOR_HANDLE) {
```
