```rs
/// A display mode as the console lists it: size, refresh rate (numerator,
/// denominator), format, scanline order, scaling, flags.
#[repr(C)]
struct Mode {
    width: u32,
    height: u32,
    refresh: [u32; 2],
    format: u32,
    scanlines: u32,
    scaling: u32,
    flags: u32,
}
const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Mode>() == 32);

/// The size of the display the console reports: `VICTORY_DISPLAY_MODE=WxH`
/// if set (as a console reports the television it is plugged into: a
/// Series X on a 1080p set lists a 1080p mode), else 3840x2160.
/// shortcut: not yet the host display's own size by default; make it so
/// once a title is seen to render for the mode it is given.
fn display_size() -> (u32, u32) {
    static SIZE: std::sync::OnceLock<(u32, u32)> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *SIZE.get_or_init(|| {
        let asked = std::env::var("VICTORY_DISPLAY_MODE").ok().and_then(|v| {
            let (w, h) = v.trim().split_once(['x', 'X'])?;
            Some((w.trim().parse::<u32>().ok()?, h.trim().parse::<u32>().ok()?))
        });
        let size = match asked {
            Some((w, h)) if (640..=7680).contains(&w) && (360..=4320).contains(&h) => (w, h),
            _ => (3840, 2160),
        };
        tracing::info!(width = size.0, height = size.1, "display mode reported to the title");
        size
    })
}

/// The console's mode list: one 4K mode at 60 Hz (the title looks
/// for a 120 Hz one to allow 120 Hz frame intervals).
/// shortcut: fixed mode, not the host display's; report the host's rates if
/// a title paces by them.
extern "system" fn modes(
    _: This,
    _format: u32,
    _flags: u32,
    count: *mut u32,
    out: *mut Mode,
) -> HRESULT {
    // SAFETY: the title passes its count (null is tolerated).
    let Some(count) = (unsafe { count.as_mut() }) else {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    };
    if out.is_null() {
        *count = 1;
        return S_OK;
    }
    if *count < 1 {
        return MORE_DATA;
    }
    *count = 1;
    let (width, height) = display_size();
    let mode = Mode {
        width,
        height,
        refresh: [60, 1],
        format: 0,
        scanlines: 1, // progressive
        scaling: 0,
        flags: 0,
    };
    // SAFETY: checked non-null; room for `count` >= 1 modes.
    unsafe { out.write(mode) };
    S_OK
}

/// IUnknown 3, object 4, output 15 (12 as on PC, then 3 console ones).
static OUTPUT_FUNCTIONS: Table<32> = {
    let mut f = object::missing_table::<OUTPUT, 32>();
    f[0] = output_query as *const ();
    f[6] = output_parent as *const (); // 0x30
    f[21] = modes as *const (); // 0xa8
    Table(f)
};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::object::{E_NOINTERFACE, slot};

    type Query = extern "system" fn(This, *const Iid, *mut This) -> HRESULT;
    type Get = extern "system" fn(This, *mut This) -> HRESULT;
    type Indexed = extern "system" fn(This, u32, *mut This) -> HRESULT;
    type Describe = extern "system" fn(This, *mut AdapterDescription) -> HRESULT;

    /// Minecraft's startup: device → DXGI device (newest first) → adapter →
    /// description, factory, first output.
    #[test]
    fn startup_walks_from_device_to_output() {
        let d3d = crate::device::device();
        let newest_pc = guid(
            0x6007896c,
            0x3244,
            0x4afd,
            [0xbf, 0x18, 0xa6, 0xd3, 0xbe, 0xda, 0x50, 0x23],
        );
        let mut dxgi = std::ptr::null();
        let qi = slot::<Query>(d3d, 0);
        assert_eq!(qi(d3d, &newest_pc, &mut dxgi), E_NOINTERFACE);
        assert!(dxgi.is_null());
        assert_eq!(qi(d3d, &DEVICE_IIDS[2], &mut dxgi), S_OK);
        assert_eq!(dxgi, device());

        let mut adapter = std::ptr::null();
        assert_eq!(slot::<Get>(dxgi, 0x38)(dxgi, &mut adapter), S_OK);
        let mut description = std::mem::MaybeUninit::<AdapterDescription>::uninit();
        assert_eq!(
            slot::<Describe>(adapter, 0x40)(adapter, description.as_mut_ptr()),
            S_OK
        );
        // SAFETY: written above.
        assert_eq!(unsafe { description.assume_init() }.vendor, AMD);

        let mut factory = std::ptr::null();
        let parent = slot::<Query>(adapter, 0x30);
        assert_eq!(parent(adapter, &FACTORY_IIDS[2], &mut factory), S_OK);
        let mut again = std::ptr::null();
        assert_eq!(slot::<Indexed>(factory, 0x38)(factory, 0, &mut again), S_OK);
        assert_eq!(again, adapter);

        let mut output = std::ptr::null();
        let outputs = slot::<Indexed>(adapter, 0x38);
        assert_eq!(outputs(adapter, 0, &mut output), S_OK);
        assert!(!output.is_null());
        assert_eq!(outputs(adapter, 1, &mut output), NOT_FOUND);
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/fence.rs`:

```rs
//! Fences: a 64-bit value and the events waiting for it. Nothing runs on a
//! GPU yet, so only signals (the title's, later our queues') move one.
#![allow(clippy::not_unsafe_ptr_arg_deref)]

use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

use crate::object::{self, E_NOTIMPL, FENCE, HRESULT, Iid, Object, S_OK, Table, This, guid};
use crate::resource::PAGEABLE_IIDS;

pub(crate) const FENCE_IIDS: [Iid; 4] = [
    guid(
        0x0a753dcf,
        0xc4d8,
        0x4b91,
        [0xad, 0xf6, 0xbe, 0x5a, 0x60, 0xd9, 0x5a, 0x76],
    ),
    PAGEABLE_IIDS[0],
    PAGEABLE_IIDS[1],
    PAGEABLE_IIDS[2],
];

#[repr(C)]
struct Fence {
    object: Object,
    /// Titles also read it straight from memory, at the fence's GPU
    /// address.
    value: AtomicU64,
    flags: u32,
    /// Events to set once the value reaches theirs (handles as integers).
    waiters: Mutex<Vec<(u64, usize)>>,
    /// For [`pace`]: when each wait above was asked for.
    #[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]
    asked: Mutex<Vec<pace::Asked>>,
}

fn fence<'a>(this: This) -> &'a Fence {
    // SAFETY: called from fence methods only.
    unsafe { &*this.cast::<Fence>() }
}

pub(crate) extern "system" fn create(
    _: This,
    initial: u64,
    flags: u32,
    iid: *const Iid,
    out: *mut This,
) -> HRESULT {
    tracing::debug!(initial, flags, "fence");
    let fence = Box::new(Fence {
        object: Object::new(&FUNCTIONS),
        value: AtomicU64::new(initial),
        flags,
        waiters: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
        #[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]
        asked: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
    });
    object::hand_out(FENCE, fence, iid, &FENCE_IIDS, out)
}

fn set_event(event: usize) {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    // SAFETY: the title passed an event handle.
    unsafe {
        windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::SetEvent(event as *mut c_void)
    };
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    let _ = event;
}

extern "system" fn query(this: This, iid: *const Iid, out: *mut This) -> HRESULT {
    object::answer(
        FENCE,
        iid,
        object::is(iid, &FENCE_IIDS).then_some(this),
        out,
    )
}
extern "system" fn release(this: This) -> u32 {
    object::release_boxed::<Fence>(this)
}
pub(crate) extern "system" fn completed(this: This) -> u64 {
    fence(this).value.load(Ordering::Acquire)
}
extern "system" fn set_event_on_completion(this: This, value: u64, event: *mut c_void) -> HRESULT {
    let fence = fence(this);
    let mut waiters = fence.waiters.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    if fence.value.load(Ordering::Acquire) >= value {
        if !event.is_null() {
            set_event(event as usize);
        }
        #[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]
        pace::ready();
        return S_OK;
    }
    #[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]
    pace::waits(this, &fence.asked, value, fence.value.load(Ordering::Acquire));
    if event.is_null() {
        // With submissions sent to the card and not waited for
        // (`crate::host::late`) the signal may be behind them: they are
        // settled, which sets it.
        #[cfg(windows)]
        if crate::host::late() {
            drop(waiters);
            crate::host::settle_for_fence();
            if fence.value.load(Ordering::Acquire) >= value {
                return S_OK;
            }
            tracing::warn!(value, "blocking fence wait not implemented");
            return E_NOTIMPL;
        }
        // shortcut: a null event means "block until reached"; nothing can
        // reach it while no GPU work runs, so fail instead of hanging.
        tracing::warn!(value, "blocking fence wait not implemented");
        return E_NOTIMPL;
    }
    waiters.push((value, event as usize));
    S_OK
}
/// Moves the fence to `value` and sets the events that waited for it.
pub(crate) fn set(this: This, value: u64) {
    let fence = fence(this);
    let mut waiters = fence.waiters.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    fence.value.store(value, Ordering::Release);
    #[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]
    pace::reached(this, &fence.asked, value);
    waiters.retain(|&(wanted, event)| {
        let reached = wanted <= value;
        if reached {
            set_event(event);
        }
        !reached
    });
}
pub(crate) extern "system" fn signal(this: This, value: u64) -> HRESULT {
    set(this, value);
    // A queue may have waited for it: what it held runs now.
    #[cfg(windows)]
    crate::queue::release_held(false);
    S_OK
}

extern "system" fn creation_flags(this: This) -> u32 {
    fence(this).flags
}
/// Where the value lives (GPU addresses are CPU addresses).
extern "system" fn gpu_address(this: This) -> u64 {
    (&raw const fence(this).value) as u64
}

/// How the title paces itself on its fences, measured (diagnostics
/// builds): which value it waits for, how long until our line gets the
/// fence there, and how many frames lie between the title's `Signal` on
/// its queue and the fence being set. Run 233 put presents behind the
/// line and the frame did not get shorter: the title waited somewhere
/// else, and this says for what.
#[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]
pub(crate) mod pace {
    use std::sync::Mutex;
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, AtomicU64, Ordering};
    use std::time::Instant;

    use crate::object::This;

    pub(crate) struct Asked {
        value: u64,
        at: Instant,
        frame: u64,
        thread: u32,
    }

    /// The title's `Signal` calls on a queue not yet at the fence:
    /// fence, value, when, frame.
    static QUEUED: Mutex<Vec<(usize, u64, Instant, u64)>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());
    /// The thread that presents.
    static RENDER: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
    /// Since the last line: waits already met; waits not met; of those,
    /// the render thread's; reached waits, their microseconds, their
    /// frames between; the render thread's reached waits and microseconds;
    /// signals set, their microseconds since the title's call, their
    /// frames between.
    static N: [AtomicU64; 11] = [const { AtomicU64::new(0) }; 11];
    static SAID: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
    static LINE_AT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);

    /// Whether events are said one by one now: four seconds of every two
    /// minutes of the wall clock, the same seconds in which the loader says
    /// the title's `mwaitx` waits (`console_insn`), to lay the two side by side.
    fn detail_now() -> bool {
        std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).is_ok_and(|d| d.as_secs() % 120 < 4)
    }

    fn thread() -> u32 {
        // SAFETY: a plain query.
        unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentThreadId() }
    }

    pub(super) fn ready() {
        N[0].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    pub(super) fn waits(fence: This, asked: &Mutex<Vec<Asked>>, value: u64, now: u64) {
        let thread = thread();
        let render = thread == RENDER.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        N[1].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        if render {
            N[2].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
        let frame = crate::queue::presented();
        if detail_now() || SAID.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) < 48 {
            tracing::info!(
                "pace: the title waits for fence {fence:?} value {value} (it is at {now}) in frame {frame}, on {}",
                if render { "the render thread".to_string() } else { format!("thread {thread}") }
            );
        }
        let mut asked = asked.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if asked.len() < 4096 {
            asked.push(Asked { value, at: Instant::now(), frame, thread });
        }
    }

    /// The title called `Signal` for `fence` on a queue.
    pub(crate) fn signal_called(fence: usize, value: u64) {
        let mut queued = QUEUED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if queued.len() < 4096 {
            queued.push((fence, value, Instant::now(), crate::queue::presented()));
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn reached(fence: This, asked: &Mutex<Vec<Asked>>, value: u64) {
        let frame = crate::queue::presented();
        let render = RENDER.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        {
            let mut queued = QUEUED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
            queued.retain(|&(f, v, at, called)| {
                let done = f == fence as usize && v <= value;
                if done {
                    N[8].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                    N[9].fetch_add(at.elapsed().as_micros() as u64, Ordering::Relaxed);
                    N[10].fetch_add(frame.saturating_sub(called), Ordering::Relaxed);
                    if detail_now() || SAID.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) < 48 {
                        tracing::info!(
                            "pace: fence {fence:?} is set to {v}, {:.1} ms after the title's Signal for it (called in frame {called}, set in frame {frame})",
                            at.elapsed().as_micros() as f64 / 1e3
                        );
                    }
                }
                !done
            });
        }
        let mut asked = asked.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        asked.retain(|a| {
            let done = a.value <= value;
            if done {
                let us = a.at.elapsed().as_micros() as u64;
                N[3].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                N[4].fetch_add(us, Ordering::Relaxed);
                N[5].fetch_add(frame.saturating_sub(a.frame), Ordering::Relaxed);
                if a.thread == render {
                    N[6].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                    N[7].fetch_add(us, Ordering::Relaxed);
                }
                if detail_now() || SAID.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) < 48 {
                    tracing::info!(
                        "pace: fence {fence:?} reached {} {:.1} ms after the wait for it (asked in frame {}, reached in frame {frame})",
                        a.value,
                        us as f64 / 1e3,
                        a.frame
                    );
                }
            }
            !done
        });
    }

    /// Once a frame, on the thread that presents: a line every 256 frames.
    pub(crate) fn frame() {
        RENDER.store(thread(), Ordering::Relaxed);
        let frame = crate::queue::presented();
        let last = LINE_AT.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        if frame < last + 256 {
            return;
        }
        LINE_AT.store(frame, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let n: Vec<f64> = N.iter().map(|n| n.swap(0, Ordering::Relaxed) as f64).collect();
        let frames = (frame - last).max(1) as f64;
        let per = |a: f64, b: f64| if b > 0.0 { a / b } else { 0.0 };
        tracing::info!(
            "pace, per frame: fence waits already met {:.2}, not met {:.2} (the render thread's {:.2}); a wait is met {:.1} ms and {:.2} frames after it was asked \
             (the render thread's: {:.1} ms, {:.1} ms a frame); the title's queue signals: {:.2} a frame, a fence is set {:.1} ms and {:.2} frames after the title's Signal call",
            n[0] / frames,
            n[1] / frames,
            n[2] / frames,
            per(n[4], n[3]) / 1e3,
            per(n[5], n[3]),
            per(n[7], n[6]) / 1e3,
            n[7] / frames / 1e3,
            n[8] / frames,
            per(n[9], n[8]) / 1e3,
            per(n[10], n[8]),
        );
    }
}

/// IUnknown 3, object 4, device child 1, fence 3, fence 1 (2, a console
/// one among them).
static FUNCTIONS: Table<24> = {
    let mut f = object::d3d12_object(object::missing_table::<FENCE, 24>());
    f[0] = query as *const ();
    f[2] = release as *const ();
    f[7] = object::parent_device as *const (); // 0x38
    f[8] = completed as *const (); // 0x40
    f[9] = set_event_on_completion as *const (); // 0x48
    f[10] = signal as *const (); // 0x50
    f[11] = creation_flags as *const (); // 0x58
    f[12] = gpu_address as *const (); // 0x60
    Table(f)
};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::object::slot;

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn signals_set_waiting_events() {
        use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{CloseHandle, WAIT_OBJECT_0};
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{CreateEventW, WaitForSingleObject};

        let mut f = std::ptr::null();
        assert_eq!(create(std::ptr::null(), 1, 0, &FENCE_IIDS[0], &mut f), S_OK);
        assert_eq!(slot::<extern "system" fn(This) -> u64>(f, 0x40)(f), 1);
        // SAFETY: plain auto-reset event.
        let event = unsafe { CreateEventW(std::ptr::null(), 0, 0, std::ptr::null()) };
        assert!(!event.is_null());
        let wait = slot::<extern "system" fn(This, u64, *mut c_void) -> HRESULT>(f, 0x48);
        let signal = slot::<extern "system" fn(This, u64) -> HRESULT>(f, 0x50);
        assert_eq!(wait(f, 5, event), S_OK);
        // SAFETY: a valid event.
        assert_ne!(unsafe { WaitForSingleObject(event, 0) }, WAIT_OBJECT_0);
        assert_eq!(signal(f, 5), S_OK);
        // SAFETY: as above.
        assert_eq!(unsafe { WaitForSingleObject(event, 0) }, WAIT_OBJECT_0);
        assert_eq!(wait(f, 5, event), S_OK, "already reached");
        // SAFETY: as above.
        assert_eq!(unsafe { WaitForSingleObject(event, 0) }, WAIT_OBJECT_0);
        assert_eq!(wait(f, 9, std::ptr::null_mut()), E_NOTIMPL);
        // The title reads the value at the fence's address.
        let at = slot::<extern "system" fn(This) -> u64>(f, 0x60)(f);
        // SAFETY: the fence's value.
        assert_eq!(unsafe { *(at as *const u64) }, 5);
        // SAFETY: ours.
        unsafe { CloseHandle(event) };
        assert_eq!(slot::<extern "system" fn(This) -> u32>(f, 0x10)(f), 0);
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/fpsbox.rs`:

```rs
//! The frame rate, drawn into the top left corner of every frame shown.
//!
//! The window's caption has the frame rate, but a capture of the window's
//! picture (a stream) does not carry the caption. Here the number is part
//! of the picture: a small box of text copied onto the swap chain's back
//! buffer right after the title's frame, before it is presented. The
//! title's own frame is not touched, so saved frames and everything read
//! back from it are as before.
//!
//! The text is drawn on the CPU with a font of its own (5 by 7 dots a
//! glyph) into a buffer the card copies from; a buffer is made once for a
//! text and never written again, so a present still in the air reads what
//! it was recorded with. On by default; `VICTORY_FPS_COUNTER=0` leaves the
//! frame as the title drew it.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};

use windows::Win32::Graphics::Direct3D12::*;
use windows::Win32::Graphics::Dxgi::Common::*;

/// The frame rate in tenths of a frame a second, as last measured (once a
/// second, by the presenter's meter); `u32::MAX` before the first.
static TENTHS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(u32::MAX);

/// Whether the counter is drawn.
fn on() -> bool {
    static ON: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_FPS_COUNTER").is_none_or(|v| v != "0"))
}

/// The frame rate just measured.
pub(crate) fn set(fps: f64) {
    if fps.is_finite() && fps >= 0.0 {
        TENTHS.store((fps * 10.0).round().min(99_999.0) as u32, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
}

/// A glyph's seven rows, five dots each (bit 4 is the left one).
fn glyph(c: char) -> [u8; 7] {
    match c {
        '0' => [0b01110, 0b10001, 0b10011, 0b10101, 0b11001, 0b10001, 0b01110],
        '1' => [0b00100, 0b01100, 0b00100, 0b00100, 0b00100, 0b00100, 0b01110],
        '2' => [0b01110, 0b10001, 0b00001, 0b00010, 0b00100, 0b01000, 0b11111],
        '3' => [0b11110, 0b00001, 0b00001, 0b01110, 0b00001, 0b00001, 0b11110],
        '4' => [0b00010, 0b00110, 0b01010, 0b10010, 0b11111, 0b00010, 0b00010],
        '5' => [0b11111, 0b10000, 0b11110, 0b00001, 0b00001, 0b10001, 0b01110],
        '6' => [0b00110, 0b01000, 0b10000, 0b11110, 0b10001, 0b10001, 0b01110],
        '7' => [0b11111, 0b00001, 0b00010, 0b00100, 0b01000, 0b01000, 0b01000],
        '8' => [0b01110, 0b10001, 0b10001, 0b01110, 0b10001, 0b10001, 0b01110],
        '9' => [0b01110, 0b10001, 0b10001, 0b01111, 0b00001, 0b00010, 0b01100],
        '.' => [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0b01100, 0b01100],
        'F' => [0b11111, 0b10000, 0b10000, 0b11110, 0b10000, 0b10000, 0b10000],
        'P' => [0b11110, 0b10001, 0b10001, 0b11110, 0b10000, 0b10000, 0b10000],
        'S' => [0b01111, 0b10000, 0b10000, 0b01110, 0b00001, 0b00001, 0b11110],
        _ => [0; 7],
    }
}

/// The text for a frame rate in tenths.
fn text(tenths: u32) -> String {
    format!("{}.{} FPS", tenths / 10, tenths % 10)
}

/// Bytes a pixel of a swap chain format this layer presents in, or none.
fn pixel_bytes(format: DXGI_FORMAT) -> Option<usize> {
    match format {
        DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM | DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM | DXGI_FORMAT_R10G10B10A2_UNORM => Some(4),
        DXGI_FORMAT_R16G16B16A16_FLOAT => Some(8),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// One pixel of `format`: of the text (`lit`) or of the box behind it.
fn pixel(format: DXGI_FORMAT, lit: bool, out: &mut [u8]) {
    // The text: a bright yellow. The box: nearly black.
    let (r, g, b): (f32, f32, f32) = if lit { (1.0, 0.92, 0.16) } else { (0.03, 0.03, 0.03) };
    let byte = |v: f32| (v * 255.0).round() as u8;
    match format {
        DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM => out.copy_from_slice(&[byte(r), byte(g), byte(b), 255]),
        DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM => out.copy_from_slice(&[byte(b), byte(g), byte(r), 255]),
        DXGI_FORMAT_R10G10B10A2_UNORM => {
            let ten = |v: f32| (v * 1023.0).round() as u32;
            out.copy_from_slice(&(ten(r) | ten(g) << 10 | ten(b) << 20 | 3 << 30).to_le_bytes());
        }
        _ => {
            for (i, v) in [r, g, b, 1.0].into_iter().enumerate() {
                out[i * 2..i * 2 + 2].copy_from_slice(&half(v).to_le_bytes());
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A value from 0 to 1 as a 16-bit float.
fn half(v: f32) -> u16 {
    let bits = v.clamp(0.0, 1.0).to_bits();
    if v <= 0.0 {
        return 0;
    }
    // Sign 0; the exponent moves from a bias of 127 to one of 15; the top
    // ten bits of the fraction stay. Values under 2^-14 (none of ours) are 0.
    let exponent = ((bits >> 23) & 0xFF) as i32 - 127 + 15;
    if exponent <= 0 {
        return 0;
    }
    ((exponent as u32) << 10 | (bits >> 13) & 0x3FF) as u16
}

/// The box for `text` at `scale` dots a pixel: its width and height in
/// pixels and, row by row from the top, whether each pixel is text.
fn bitmap(text: &str, scale: u32) -> (u32, u32, Vec<bool>) {
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    let pad = 2 * scale;
    let width = 2 * pad + chars.len() as u32 * 6 * scale - scale;
    let height = 2 * pad + 7 * scale;
    let mut lit = vec![false; (width * height) as usize];
    for (i, &c) in chars.iter().enumerate() {
        let rows = glyph(c);
        for (row, bits) in rows.into_iter().enumerate() {
            for column in 0..5u32 {
                if bits >> (4 - column) & 1 == 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                let (x0, y0) = (pad + (i as u32 * 6 + column) * scale, pad + row as u32 * scale);
                for y in y0..y0 + scale {
                    for x in x0..x0 + scale {
                        lit[(y * width + x) as usize] = true;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    (width, height, lit)
}

/// A buffer the card copies a text's box from, with its footprint.
struct Made {
    buffer: ID3D12Resource,
    width: u32,
    height: u32,
    pitch: u32,
}

// SAFETY: a free-threaded D3D12 object and plain numbers.
unsafe impl Send for Made {}

/// The boxes made so far, by text, format and scale.
static MADE: Mutex<Option<HashMap<(u32, i32, u32), Made>>> = Mutex::new(None);

/// Copies the frame rate's box onto `back`, a back buffer of `width` by
/// `height` pixels of `format` that `list` holds as a copy's destination.
/// Nothing if the counter is off, no rate was measured yet, the format is
/// not one of ours or the frame is too small for the box.
pub(crate) fn draw(host: &crate::host::Host, list: &ID3D12GraphicsCommandList, back: &ID3D12Resource, (width, height, format): (u32, u32, DXGI_FORMAT)) {
    if !on() {
        return;
    }
    let tenths = TENTHS.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
    let Some(bytes) = pixel_bytes(format).filter(|_| tenths != u32::MAX) else {
        return;
    };
    // About a fortieth of the frame's height a glyph: 6 dots a pixel at
    // 2160 lines, 3 at 1080.
    let scale = (height / 360).clamp(2, 12);
    let mut made = MADE.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    let made = made.get_or_insert_with(HashMap::new);
    if made.len() > 2048 {
        // (Every text is a buffer of a few hundred KiB; a rate that wanders
        // over thousands of values is not expected.)
        made.clear();
    }
    let key = (tenths, format.0, scale);
    if !made.contains_key(&key) {
        let (w, h, lit) = bitmap(&text(tenths), scale);
        let pitch = (w as usize * bytes).next_multiple_of(D3D12_TEXTURE_DATA_PITCH_ALIGNMENT as usize);
        let Some((buffer, data)) = host.shared_buffer((pitch * h as usize) as u64) else {
            return;
        };
        // SAFETY: the buffer's own mapped bytes, `pitch * h` of them.
        let out = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(data, pitch * h as usize) };
        for y in 0..h as usize {
            for x in 0..w as usize {
                let at = y * pitch + x * bytes;
                pixel(format, lit[y * w as usize + x], &mut out[at..at + bytes]);
            }
        }
        made.insert(key, Made { buffer, width: w, height: h, pitch: pitch as u32 });
    }
    let Some(m) = made.get(&key) else {
        return;
    };
    let margin = 4 * scale;
    if m.width + 2 * margin > width || m.height + 2 * margin > height {
        return;
    }
    // SAFETY: an open list; the back buffer is a copy's destination in it
    // and the box lies inside it; our buffer holds `pitch * height` bytes
    // and is kept for as long as the process runs.
    unsafe {
        let from = D3D12_TEXTURE_COPY_LOCATION {
            pResource: std::mem::transmute_copy(&m.buffer),
            Type: D3D12_TEXTURE_COPY_TYPE_PLACED_FOOTPRINT,
            Anonymous: D3D12_TEXTURE_COPY_LOCATION_0 {
                PlacedFootprint: D3D12_PLACED_SUBRESOURCE_FOOTPRINT {
                    Offset: 0,
                    Footprint: D3D12_SUBRESOURCE_FOOTPRINT { Format: format, Width: m.width, Height: m.height, Depth: 1, RowPitch: m.pitch },
                },
            },
        };
        let to = D3D12_TEXTURE_COPY_LOCATION {
            pResource: std::mem::transmute_copy(back),
            Type: D3D12_TEXTURE_COPY_TYPE_SUBRESOURCE_INDEX,
            Anonymous: D3D12_TEXTURE_COPY_LOCATION_0 { SubresourceIndex: 0 },
        };
        list.CopyTextureRegion(&to, margin, margin, 0, &from, None);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn the_text_is_the_rate_to_a_tenth() {
        assert_eq!(text(103), "10.3 FPS");
        assert_eq!(text(7), "0.7 FPS");
        assert_eq!(text(300), "30.0 FPS");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_box_holds_every_glyph_with_a_margin() {
        let (w, h, lit) = bitmap("10.3 FPS", 3);
        // Eight glyphs of five dots and seven gaps of one, a pad of two dots all round.
        assert_eq!((w, h), ((8 * 5 + 7 + 4) * 3, (7 + 4) * 3));
        assert_eq!(lit.len(), (w * h) as usize);
        // The pad is box, not text; the "1" has its stem lit.
        assert!(lit[..(w * 6) as usize].iter().all(|&l| !l), "the top pad");
        assert!((0..h).all(|y| !lit[(y * w) as usize] && !lit[(y * w + w - 1) as usize]), "the side pads");
        let at = |x: u32, y: u32| lit[(y * w + x) as usize];
        // Glyph 0 ("1"): dot column 2 of row 0 is lit, column 0 is not.
        assert!(at(6 + 2 * 3, 6) && !at(6, 6));
        // A space lights nothing: glyph 4.
        assert!((0..7 * 3).all(|y| (0..5 * 3).all(|x| !at(6 + 4 * 18 + x, 6 + y))));
        // Every glyph used has at least one dot, but the space.
        for c in "0123456789.FPS".chars() {
            assert!(glyph(c).iter().any(|&r| r != 0), "{c}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn pixels_are_in_the_formats_the_layer_presents_in() {
        let mut four = [0u8; 4];
        pixel(DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM, true, &mut four);
        assert_eq!(four, [255, 235, 41, 255]);
        pixel(DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM, true, &mut four);
        assert_eq!(four, [41, 235, 255, 255]);
        pixel(DXGI_FORMAT_R10G10B10A2_UNORM, true, &mut four);
        let v = u32::from_le_bytes(four);
        assert_eq!((v & 1023, v >> 10 & 1023, v >> 20 & 1023, v >> 30), (1023, 941, 164, 3));
        let mut eight = [0u8; 8];
        pixel(DXGI_FORMAT_R16G16B16A16_FLOAT, true, &mut eight);
        assert_eq!(u16::from_le_bytes([eight[0], eight[1]]), 0x3C00, "1.0 as a half");
        assert_eq!(u16::from_le_bytes([eight[6], eight[7]]), 0x3C00);
        assert_eq!(half(0.5), 0x3800);
        assert_eq!(half(0.0), 0);
        assert_eq!(pixel_bytes(DXGI_FORMAT_R16G16B16A16_FLOAT), Some(8));
        assert_eq!(pixel_bytes(DXGI_FORMAT_D32_FLOAT), None);
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/frame.rs`:

```rs
//! Frame pacing: the title sets a frame interval and waits for each frame
//! to begin. Ours is a clock started by the first interval set, ticking
//! once per interval; the token is the frame number. Each event kind
//! (origin, vblank, flip) happens once per tick, so two waits for the same
//! kind never end on the same tick: the title polls the origin
//! with "token on time-out" (starting its next frame at once) and is paced
//! by a blocking wait for the flip before each present.
//!
//! shortcut: event offsets are ignored (every event is at the tick); tie
//! the clock to presentation if a title paces by them.
#![allow(clippy::not_unsafe_ptr_arg_deref)]

use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use crate::object::{HRESULT, S_FALSE, S_OK, This};

/// What a wait returns when its time is up first.
const TIMEOUT: HRESULT = S_FALSE;
/// The frame-origin event: the one that starts frames and makes tokens.
const ORIGIN: u32 = 0;
/// Make the frame's token even if the wait times out (the title starts the
/// frame early).
const TOKEN_ON_TIMEOUT: u32 = 2;
const SIXTIETH: Duration = Duration::from_micros(16_667);

struct Clock {
    start: Instant,
    interval: Duration,
    /// The tick number at `start` (ticks go on across interval changes).
    first: u64,
}

static CLOCK: Mutex<Option<Clock>> = Mutex::new(None);
static FRAME: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);

fn clock() -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'static, Option<Clock>> {
    CLOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

/// Device method: a frame every `length` microseconds. The period is how
/// many intervals a frame may take to reach the display (pipeline depth),
/// not part of the rate.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn set_interval(
    _: This,
    _output: This,
    length: u32,
    _period: u32,
    _flags: u32,
) -> HRESULT {
    let interval = match length {
        0 => SIXTIETH,
        us => Duration::from_micros(u64::from(us)),
    };
    tracing::info!(?interval, "frame interval");
    // A new interval starts from now, after the last tick handed out.
    let first = LAST
        .iter()
        .map(|t| t.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
        .max()
        .unwrap_or(0);
    *clock() = Some(Clock {
        start: Instant::now(),
        interval,
        first,
    });
    S_OK
}

/// Device method: events are scheduled at every tick.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn schedule(
    _: This,
    _kind: u32,
    _offset: u32,
    _list: *const u8,
    _flags: u32,
) -> HRESULT {
    S_OK
}

/// Frames begun so far (frame waits that ended).
pub(crate) fn current() -> u64 {
    FRAME.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

/// Per event kind (origin, vblank, flip and later kinds): the last tick a
/// wait for it ended on.
static LAST: [AtomicU64; 3] = [const { AtomicU64::new(0) }; 3];

fn last(kind: u32) -> &'static AtomicU64 {
    &LAST[(kind as usize).min(LAST.len() - 1)]
}

/// The next tick after now and after the last one a wait for `kind` ended
/// on (an event happens once per tick: a wait woken a little early must not
/// let the next one end on the same tick), and how long until it.
fn next_tick(kind: u32) -> (u64, Duration) {
    let mut clock = clock();
    let c = clock.get_or_insert_with(|| Clock {
        start: Instant::now(),
        interval: SIXTIETH,
        first: 0,
    });
    let elapsed = c.start.elapsed().as_nanos();
    let interval = c.interval.as_nanos().max(1);
    let tick =
        (c.first + (elapsed / interval + 1) as u64).max(last(kind).load(Ordering::Relaxed) + 1);
    let at = u128::from(tick - c.first) * interval;
    (
        tick,
        Duration::from_nanos(at.saturating_sub(elapsed) as u64),
    )
}

/// Device method: blocks until the next tick (or the time-out); an origin
/// wait then hands out the new frame's token. Other events keep the token
/// the title passes. Ticks are absolute (start plus whole intervals), so
/// lateness never accumulates.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn wait(
    _: This,
    kind: u32,
    timeout_ms: u32,
    _list: *const u8,
    flags: u32,
    token: *mut u64,
) -> HRESULT {
    let origin = kind == ORIGIN;
    let (mut tick, mut wait) = next_tick(kind);
    let limit = Duration::from_millis(u64::from(timeout_ms));
    // A blocking wait for an event that has happened since the last wait
    // for it ended (a frame took longer than a tick) ends at once, on the
    // tick that passed: sleeping on to the next one cost 17 ms of every
    // 730 ms frame (run 58: "2.0 frame waits sleeping 16.8 ms"). Polls (a
    // time-out shorter than a tick) answer as before.
    // `VICTORY_LATE_WAITS=1` sleeps to the next tick, as before.
    static SLEEP: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    if !*SLEEP.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_LATE_WAITS").is_some_and(|v| v == "1"))
        && limit >= wait
        && tick > last(kind).load(Ordering::Relaxed) + 1
    {
        tick -= 1;
        wait = Duration::ZERO;
    }
    let hr = if wait > limit {
        std::thread::sleep(limit);
        TIMEOUT
    } else {
        std::thread::sleep(wait);
        last(kind).fetch_max(tick, Ordering::Relaxed);
        S_OK
    };
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        let us = wait.min(limit).as_micros() as u64;
        crate::framelog::add(crate::framelog::T::PaceUs, us);
        crate::framelog::here(crate::framelog::H::PaceUs, us);
    }
    #[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]
    {
        use crate::copystat::{C, add};
        add(C::PaceWaits, 1);
        add(C::PaceUs, wait.min(limit).as_micros() as u64);
    }
    // A frame begun on a time-out takes no tick: its flip still does.
    if origin && (hr == S_OK || flags & TOKEN_ON_TIMEOUT != 0) {
        // Tokens count frames (consecutive), not ticks.
        let frame = FRAME.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) + 1;
        if !token.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: checked non-null; the title passes its token.
            unsafe { token.write(frame) };
        }
    }
    #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
    tracing::debug!(
        kind,
        timeout_ms,
        flags,
        hr,
        tick,
        wait_us = wait.as_micros() as u64,
        frame = current(),
        "frame wait"
    );
    hr
}

/// Device method: no statistics are kept, so none are returned.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn statistics(
    _: This,
    _token: u64,
    _kinds: u32,
    count: *mut u32,
    _out: *mut u8,
) -> HRESULT {
    if !count.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: checked non-null.
        unsafe { count.write(0) };
    }
    S_OK
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn waits_end_on_ticks_and_count_frames() {
        let null = std::ptr::null();
        assert_eq!(set_interval(null, null, 2_000, 1, 0), S_OK);
        let mut first = 0;
        assert_eq!(wait(null, 0, 1_000, std::ptr::null(), 0, &mut first), S_OK);
        let before = Instant::now();
        let mut second = 0;
        assert_eq!(wait(null, 0, 1_000, std::ptr::null(), 0, &mut second), S_OK);
        assert!(second > first);
        assert!(before.elapsed() <= Duration::from_millis(50));
        assert_eq!(wait(null, 0, 0, std::ptr::null(), 0, &mut second), TIMEOUT);
        // Tokens count frames, a frame started early on a time-out too.
        let mut early = 0;
        let flags = TOKEN_ON_TIMEOUT;
        assert_eq!(
            wait(null, 0, 0, std::ptr::null(), flags, &mut early),
            TIMEOUT
        );
        let mut next = 0;
        assert_eq!(wait(null, 0, 1_000, std::ptr::null(), 0, &mut next), S_OK);
        assert!(early == second + 1 && next == early + 1);
        assert!(LAST[0].load(Ordering::Relaxed) >= 2);

        // The title's loop (the clock is global, so in the same test): an
        // origin poll that times out (and starts the frame), then a
        // blocking flip wait. Each flip takes its own tick.
        const FLIP: u32 = 2;
        assert_eq!(set_interval(null, null, 5_000, 3, 0), S_OK);
        let mut token = 0;
        let flips: Vec<u64> = (0..4)
            .map(|_| {
                let _ = wait(null, 0, 0, std::ptr::null(), TOKEN_ON_TIMEOUT, &mut token);
                assert_eq!(
                    wait(null, FLIP, u32::MAX, std::ptr::null(), 0, &mut token),
                    S_OK
                );
                LAST[2].load(Ordering::Relaxed)
            })
            .collect();
        assert!(flips.windows(2).all(|w| w[1] == w[0] + 1), "{flips:?}");
        // Even when a flip wait begins on the tick another just ended on.
        let (tick, _) = next_tick(FLIP);
        assert!(tick > flips[3]);
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/framelog.rs`:

```rs
//! Every frame's length, and what the long ones were made of.
//!
//! The frame-rate line averages over a second or more, and its counters
//! are reset at each line: a single long frame is lost in it, and so is
//! what that frame was made of. Run 222's dips (150 ms frames with some of
//! 250 to 500 ms among them) could not be placed from those lines.
//!
//! Here every counter runs from the start and is never reset. At the end
//! of each present call the totals are read, and their differences since
//! the present before are that frame's. Every five seconds one line gives
//! the frame times (each one, the shortest, the median, the longest), one
//! gives the usual frame's make-up (the mean of the frames that were not
//! long), and each long frame gets a line of its own in the same form, so
//! a long frame is read against a usual one column by column.
//!
//! On by default in diagnostics builds, off in others;
//! `VICTORY_FRAME_LOG=1` or `0` says otherwise. The counters themselves
//! are plain atomic adds in every build.

use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering::Relaxed};

/// Totals since the start (microseconds unless said otherwise).
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(usize)]
pub enum T {
    /// The title's present call, all of it; of it, running the queues'
    /// lines and settling submissions before our copy; and our copy to the
    /// window with the host's present.
    PresentUs,
    PresentLineUs,
    PresentShowUs,
    /// The title's submit calls (`queue::execute`), on every thread.
    ExecuteUs,
    /// The submit thread of ours (`VICTORY_ASYNC_SUBMIT=1`) at work: wall
    /// time running the queues' lines, and its processor time doing so.
    WorkerUs,
    WorkerUserUs,
    WorkerKernelUs,
    /// Submissions sent; preparing them and waiting for the card, on
    /// whichever thread (the frame-rate line's "preparing" and "on the
    /// GPU").
    Submissions,
    PrepareUs,
    CardWaitUs,
    /// The card with nothing of ours queued, and how much of that while
    /// the submitting thread was working.
    CardIdleUs,
    CardIdleBehindUs,
    /// Copies of title memory for submissions (time, bytes), and what
    /// shaders wrote copied back (time, bytes).
    CopyUs,
    CopyBytes,
    CopyBackUs,
    CopyBackBytes,
    /// List calls that record into host lists, on every thread
    /// (nanoseconds, calls). Diagnostics builds only.
    RecordNs,
    RecordCalls,
    /// The runtime changing what title memory shows: calls, the time from
    /// asking for the lock to letting it go, and of that the wait for
    /// readers.
    Remaps,
    RemapUs,
    RemapWaitUs,
    /// Texture refreshes on every thread, and of them the wait for title
    /// memory to hold still; uploads recorded.
    RefreshUs,
    RefreshStillUs,
    Uploads,
    /// Waiting for host pipelines being made.
    PipelineWaitUs,
    /// Writes taken by the guards on view memory.
    GuardFaults,
    /// The title's frame waits: time slept, on every thread.
    PaceUs,
    /// DirectStorage requests finished, their destination bytes, and the
    /// workers' time in them.
    DiskReads,
    DiskBytes,
    DiskUs,
    /// The card's time by kind of list (`crate::cardmeter`), as read a
    /// second and a half after the lists were recorded: our lists that
    /// bring copies in the card's memory up to date and hash their pieces,
    /// our compare lists, and every other list; and how many of each.
    CardSyncUs,
    CardSyncLists,
    CardCheckUs,
    CardCheckLists,
    CardListsUs,
    CardLists,
    /// Looks at which processor a thread is on ([`on_slow_core`]), and how
    /// many found a slow one (an efficiency core of a hybrid processor):
    /// the thread that presents (one look a present), our submit thread
    /// (one a turn), and the recording threads (one every couple of
    /// milliseconds of list calls).
    RenderLooks,
    RenderSlow,
    WorkerLooks,
    WorkerSlow,
    RecordLooks,
    RecordSlow,
    Count,
}

const N: usize = T::Count as usize;
static TOTAL: [AtomicU64; N] = [const { AtomicU64::new(0) }; N];

/// Adds to a total.
pub fn add(t: T, n: u64) {
    TOTAL[t as usize].fetch_add(n, Relaxed);
}

/// Takes from a total (a time that was summed over threads is corrected
/// to the time it took).
pub fn sub(t: T, n: u64) {
    TOTAL[t as usize].fetch_sub(n, Relaxed);
}

/// What a thread did inside our calls since its last present: for the
/// thread that presents (the title's render thread).
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(usize)]
pub enum H {
    /// List calls, nanoseconds.
    RecordNs,
    /// Submit calls, microseconds.
    ExecuteUs,
    /// Frame waits, microseconds slept.
    PaceUs,
    Count,
}

const HN: usize = H::Count as usize;

thread_local! {
    static HERE: std::cell::Cell<[u64; HN]> = const { std::cell::Cell::new([0; HN]) };
}

/// Adds to this thread's own count.
pub fn here(h: H, n: u64) {
    HERE.with(|c| {
        let mut v = c.get();
        v[h as usize] += n;
        c.set(v);
    });
}

/// Whether the processor this thread runs on right now is a slow one: on a
/// processor with two kinds of cores (the console has eight alike; an Intel
/// hybrid has fast cores and efficiency cores at about half their speed),
/// one of a lower efficiency class than the best. Always false where all
/// cores are alike.
pub fn on_slow_core() -> bool {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcessorNumber;
    /// By logical processor (of group 0): whether it is slow.
    static SLOW: std::sync::OnceLock<Vec<bool>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    let slow = SLOW.get_or_init(|| {
        let sets = cpu_sets();
        let best = sets.iter().map(|c| c.2).max().unwrap_or(0);
        let mut slow = vec![false; sets.iter().map(|c| c.1 as usize + 1).max().unwrap_or(0)];
        for (_, processor, class) in &sets {
            slow[*processor as usize] = *class < best;
        }
        tracing::info!(
            "processors: {} logical, {} of them slow ones (a lower efficiency class than the best); the frame log counts how \
             often the render, submit and recording threads are found on a slow one",
            slow.len(),
            slow.iter().filter(|&&s| s).count()
        );
        slow
    });
    // SAFETY: a plain query.
    let processor = unsafe { GetCurrentProcessorNumber() } as usize;
    slow.get(processor).copied().unwrap_or(false)
}

/// The system's processor sets of group 0: each one's id, its logical
/// processor and its efficiency class (higher is faster).
fn cpu_sets() -> Vec<(u32, u8, u8)> {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::SystemInformation::{GetSystemCpuSetInformation, SYSTEM_CPU_SET_INFORMATION};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcess;
    let mut bytes = 0u32;
    // SAFETY: a size query, then the call into a buffer of that size.
    unsafe { GetSystemCpuSetInformation(std::ptr::null_mut(), 0, &mut bytes, GetCurrentProcess(), 0) };
    let mut buffer = vec![0u64; (bytes as usize).div_ceil(8).max(1)];
    // SAFETY: as above; the buffer holds `bytes` bytes, aligned for the records.
    let ok = unsafe { GetSystemCpuSetInformation(buffer.as_mut_ptr().cast(), bytes, &mut bytes, GetCurrentProcess(), 0) };
    let mut sets = Vec::new();
    let mut at = 0usize;
    while ok != 0 && at + size_of::<SYSTEM_CPU_SET_INFORMATION>() <= bytes as usize {
        // SAFETY: a record inside the buffer; each says its own size.
        let info = unsafe { &*(buffer.as_ptr().cast::<u8>().add(at).cast::<SYSTEM_CPU_SET_INFORMATION>()) };
        if info.Size == 0 {
            break;
        }
        // SAFETY: the record's type is CpuSet (the only one there is).
        let set = unsafe { &info.Anonymous.CpuSet };
        if set.Group == 0 {
            sets.push((set.Id, set.LogicalProcessorIndex, set.EfficiencyClass));
        }
        at += info.Size as usize;
    }
    sets
}

/// The slow logical processors of group 0 as a mask (a lower efficiency
/// class than the best): 0 where all cores are alike.
pub fn slow_processors() -> usize {
    let sets = cpu_sets();
    let best = sets.iter().map(|c| c.2).max().unwrap_or(0);
    sets.iter().filter(|c| c.2 < best && c.1 < usize::BITS as u8).fold(0, |mask, c| mask | 1usize << c.1)
}

/// Asks the system to run the calling thread on the fast cores only, where
/// the processor has two kinds (`VICTORY_FAST_CORES=0`: not asked).
///
/// The title keeps its own threads on fast cores (run 229: its render
/// thread in 3,484 looks of 3,484, its recording threads in 104,254 of
/// 104,254), as on the console, whose eight cores are alike. The layer's
/// submit thread was found on a slow one in 1,529 looks of 24,021, and the
/// frame waits for that thread. A set of processors selected for a thread
/// is a preference the scheduler keeps unless nothing of it is free.
pub fn keep_on_fast_cores(what: &str) {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{GetCurrentThread, SetThreadSelectedCpuSets};
    static ON: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    if !*ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_FAST_CORES").is_none_or(|v| v != "0")) {
        return;
    }
    let sets = cpu_sets();
    let best = sets.iter().map(|c| c.2).max().unwrap_or(0);
    let fast: Vec<u32> = sets.iter().filter(|c| c.2 == best).map(|c| c.0).collect();
    // All alike (or nothing known): nothing to ask for.
    if fast.is_empty() || fast.len() == sets.len() {
        return;
    }
    // SAFETY: our own thread and a list of the system's own set ids.
    let ok = unsafe { SetThreadSelectedCpuSets(GetCurrentThread(), fast.as_ptr(), fast.len() as u32) };
    if ok == 0 {
        tracing::warn!(what, error = %std::io::Error::last_os_error(), "the thread could not be kept on the fast cores");
    } else {
        tracing::info!(what, fast = fast.len(), of = sets.len(), "the thread is kept on the fast cores (VICTORY_FAST_CORES=0: not)");
    }
}

/// Asks the system to run the calling thread on the slow cores only, where
/// the processor has two kinds and at least eight slow logical processors
/// (a helper that must not take a fast core from the title's threads).
/// True if it was asked.
///
/// The title pins its threads as on the console, where disk decompression
/// is the hardware's: measured on a 14700KF, 31 of its threads are tied to
/// logical processors 0-13, the fast cores. The layer decompresses on as
/// many worker threads as there are logical processors (28), free to run
/// anywhere: in the opening cutscene's streaming stretch about ten of them
/// were busy while the title's recording calls took three times as long.
pub fn keep_on_slow_cores(what: &str) -> bool {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{GetCurrentThread, SetThreadSelectedCpuSets};
    let sets = cpu_sets();
    let best = sets.iter().map(|c| c.2).max().unwrap_or(0);
    let slow: Vec<u32> = sets.iter().filter(|c| c.2 < best).map(|c| c.0).collect();
    if slow.len() < 8 {
        return false;
    }
    // SAFETY: our own thread and a list of the system's own set ids.
    let ok = unsafe { SetThreadSelectedCpuSets(GetCurrentThread(), slow.as_ptr(), slow.len() as u32) } != 0;
    static ONCE: std::sync::Once = std::sync::Once::new();
    ONCE.call_once(|| {
        tracing::info!(what, slow = slow.len(), of = sets.len(), ok, "helper threads are kept on the slow cores: the first one");
    });
    ok
}

/// Whether frames are logged.
pub fn on() -> bool {
    static ON: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| match std::env::var_os("VICTORY_FRAME_LOG") {
        Some(v) => v != "0",
        None => cfg!(feature = "diagnostics"),
    })
}

fn micros(t: windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::FILETIME) -> u64 {
    (u64::from(t.dwHighDateTime) << 32 | u64::from(t.dwLowDateTime)) / 10
}

/// This thread's processor time so far (user, kernel), in microseconds.
pub fn thread_times() -> (u64, u64) {
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::FILETIME;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{GetCurrentThread, GetThreadTimes};
    let zero = FILETIME { dwLowDateTime: 0, dwHighDateTime: 0 };
    let (mut created, mut exited, mut kernel, mut user) = (zero, zero, zero, zero);
    // SAFETY: our own thread and four valid out pointers.
    unsafe { GetThreadTimes(GetCurrentThread(), &mut created, &mut exited, &mut kernel, &mut user) };
    (micros(user), micros(kernel))
}

/// The process's processor time so far (user, kernel), in microseconds.
fn process_times() -> (u64, u64) {
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::FILETIME;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{GetCurrentProcess, GetProcessTimes};
    let zero = FILETIME { dwLowDateTime: 0, dwHighDateTime: 0 };
    let (mut created, mut exited, mut kernel, mut user) = (zero, zero, zero, zero);
    // SAFETY: our own process and four valid out pointers.
    unsafe { GetProcessTimes(GetCurrentProcess(), &mut created, &mut exited, &mut kernel, &mut user) };
    (micros(user), micros(kernel))
}

/// The process's page faults so far (soft and hard).
fn page_faults() -> u64 {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::ProcessStatus::{K32GetProcessMemoryInfo, PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcess;
    // SAFETY: plain data the call fills in.
    let mut c: PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    c.cb = size_of::<PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS>() as u32;
    // SAFETY: our own process and a sized structure.
    unsafe { K32GetProcessMemoryInfo(GetCurrentProcess(), &mut c, c.cb) };
    u64::from(c.PageFaultCount)
}

/// The PC's free physical memory, in MiB.
pub(crate) fn free_mb() -> u64 {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::SystemInformation::{GlobalMemoryStatusEx, MEMORYSTATUSEX};
    // SAFETY: plain data the call fills in.
    let mut m: MEMORYSTATUSEX = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    m.dwLength = size_of::<MEMORYSTATUSEX>() as u32;
    // SAFETY: a sized structure.
    unsafe { GlobalMemoryStatusEx(&mut m) };
    m.ullAvailPhys >> 20
}

/// Values read when a frame ends, all running totals but the last.
const S: usize = 11;
const S_THREAD_USER: usize = 0;
const S_THREAD_KERNEL: usize = 1;
const S_PROCESS_USER: usize = 2;
const S_PROCESS_KERNEL: usize = 3;
const S_PAGE_FAULTS: usize = 4;
const S_DRAWS: usize = 5;
const S_PIPELINES_MADE: usize = 6;
const S_PIPELINES_LOADED: usize = 7;
const S_STAGING_REUSED: usize = 8;
const S_STAGING_MADE: usize = 9;
/// Not a total: the free memory then.
const S_FREE_MB: usize = 10;

fn sample() -> [u64; S] {
    let (tu, tk) = thread_times();
    let (pu, pk) = process_times();
    [
        tu,
        tk,
        pu,
        pk,
        page_faults(),
        crate::draw::drawn(),
        crate::pipeline::frame_log_counts().0,
        crate::pipeline::frame_log_counts().1,
        crate::texture::SPARE_STATS[0].load(Relaxed),
        crate::texture::SPARE_STATS[1].load(Relaxed),
        free_mb(),
    ]
}

/// One frame: its number, when it ended (seconds since the first), its
/// length in microseconds, and the differences of the totals, the sampled
/// values and the presenting thread's own counts over it.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Frame {
    number: u64,
    at: f64,
    us: f64,
    t: [f64; N],
    s: [f64; S],
    h: [f64; HN],
}

struct State {
    first: std::time::Instant,
    /// The last frame's end: when, the totals and samples then, and the
    /// thread that presented.
    last: Option<(std::time::Instant, [u64; N], [u64; S], u32)>,
    number: u64,
    frames: Vec<Frame>,
    since: std::time::Instant,
    /// The lengths of the last frames (microseconds), for the usual one.
    recent: std::collections::VecDeque<f64>,
}

static STATE: Mutex<Option<State>> = Mutex::new(None);

fn median(values: impl Iterator<Item = f64>) -> f64 {
    let mut v: Vec<f64> = values.collect();
    if v.is_empty() {
        return 0.0;
    }
    v.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);
    v[v.len() / 2]
}

/// A frame's make-up as text (`f` may be a mean of frames).
fn text(f: &Frame) -> String {
    let t = |x: T| f.t[x as usize];
    let ms = |x: T| f.t[x as usize] / 1e3;
    let s = |i: usize| f.s[i];
    let h = |x: H| f.h[x as usize];
    format!(
        "{:.0} ms | render thread: ran {:.0} ms (user {:.0}, kernel {:.0}); in the present call {:.1} (lines and settling \
         {:.1}, copy and show {:.1}), in submit calls {:.1}, in list calls {:.1}, paced {:.1} | submit thread: at work \
         {:.1} ms (user {:.1}, kernel {:.1}); {:.0} submissions, preparing {:.1}, waiting for the card {:.1}; copies {:.1} \
         ms {:.1} MB; copy-back {:.1} ms {:.2} MB | card: idle {:.1} ms ({:.1} behind us); by its own clock, of the lists of a moment ago: our \
         send-and-hash lists {:.1} ms in {:.0}, our compare lists {:.1} ms in {:.0}, all other lists {:.1} ms in {:.0} | \
         recording, all threads: {:.1} ms in {:.0} calls; all submit calls {:.1} ms | textures: refresh {:.1} ms ({:.1} waiting for memory to hold \
         still), {:.0} uploads, staging {:.0} made {:.0} reused | remapping: {:.0} calls {:.1} ms ({:.1} waiting for \
         readers) | pipelines: {:.0} made, {:.0} loaded, {:.1} ms waited | disk: {:.0} reads {:.1} MB {:.1} worker ms | \
         faults: {:.0} page, {:.0} guard | process: {:.0} user {:.0} kernel ms | pacing, all threads {:.1} ms | {:.0} \
         draws | {:.0} MB free | found on a slow core: the render thread {:.0} of {:.0} looks, the submit thread {:.0} of {:.0}, recording threads {:.0} of {:.0}",
        f.us / 1e3,
        (s(S_THREAD_USER) + s(S_THREAD_KERNEL)) / 1e3,
        s(S_THREAD_USER) / 1e3,
        s(S_THREAD_KERNEL) / 1e3,
        ms(T::PresentUs),
        ms(T::PresentLineUs),
        ms(T::PresentShowUs),
        h(H::ExecuteUs) / 1e3,
        h(H::RecordNs) / 1e6,
        h(H::PaceUs) / 1e3,
        ms(T::WorkerUs),
        ms(T::WorkerUserUs),
        ms(T::WorkerKernelUs),
        t(T::Submissions),
        ms(T::PrepareUs),
        ms(T::CardWaitUs),
        ms(T::CopyUs),
        t(T::CopyBytes) / 1e6,
        ms(T::CopyBackUs),
        t(T::CopyBackBytes) / 1e6,
        ms(T::CardIdleUs),
        ms(T::CardIdleBehindUs),
        ms(T::CardSyncUs),
        t(T::CardSyncLists),
        ms(T::CardCheckUs),
        t(T::CardCheckLists),
        ms(T::CardListsUs),
        t(T::CardLists),
        t(T::RecordNs) / 1e6,
        t(T::RecordCalls),
        ms(T::ExecuteUs),
        ms(T::RefreshUs),
        ms(T::RefreshStillUs),
        t(T::Uploads),
        s(S_STAGING_MADE),
        s(S_STAGING_REUSED),
        t(T::Remaps),
        ms(T::RemapUs),
        ms(T::RemapWaitUs),
        s(S_PIPELINES_MADE),
        s(S_PIPELINES_LOADED),
        ms(T::PipelineWaitUs),
        t(T::DiskReads),
        t(T::DiskBytes) / 1e6,
        ms(T::DiskUs),
        s(S_PAGE_FAULTS),
        t(T::GuardFaults),
        s(S_PROCESS_USER) / 1e3,
        s(S_PROCESS_KERNEL) / 1e3,
        ms(T::PaceUs),
        s(S_DRAWS),
        s(S_FREE_MB),
        t(T::RenderSlow),
        t(T::RenderLooks),
        t(T::WorkerSlow),
        t(T::WorkerLooks),
        t(T::RecordSlow),
        t(T::RecordLooks),
    )
}

/// The mean of `frames` (not empty).
fn mean(frames: &[&Frame]) -> Frame {
    let n = frames.len() as f64;
    let mut out = Frame { number: 0, at: 0.0, us: 0.0, t: [0.0; N], s: [0.0; S], h: [0.0; HN] };
    for f in frames {
        out.us += f.us / n;
        for i in 0..N {
            out.t[i] += f.t[i] / n;
        }
        for i in 0..S {
            out.s[i] += f.s[i] / n;
        }
        for i in 0..HN {
            out.h[i] += f.h[i] / n;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Over how many microseconds a frame is long, the usual one being
/// `usual`: half as long again, and at least 40 ms more.
fn long_over(usual: f64) -> f64 {
    (usual * 1.5).max(usual + 40_000.0)
}

/// The lines of a reading: the frame times, the usual frame, the long ones.
fn lines(frames: &[Frame], usual: f64, seconds: f64) -> Vec<String> {
    let over = long_over(usual);
    let (long, plain): (Vec<&Frame>, Vec<&Frame>) = frames.iter().partition(|f| f.us > over);
    let each: Vec<String> = frames.iter().map(|f| format!("{:.0}", f.us / 1e3)).collect();
    let shortest = frames.iter().map(|f| f.us).fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min);
    let longest = frames.iter().map(|f| f.us).fold(0.0, f64::max);
    let mut out = vec![format!(
        "frame times: {} frames in {seconds:.1} s: shortest {:.0} ms, median {:.0}, longest {:.0}; {} long (over {:.0} ms, \
         the usual frame of the last {RECENT} being {:.0}); each: {}",
        frames.len(),
        shortest / 1e3,
        median(frames.iter().map(|f| f.us)) / 1e3,
        longest / 1e3,
        long.len(),
        over / 1e3,
        usual / 1e3,
        each.join(" ")
    )];
    if !plain.is_empty() {
        out.push(format!("usual frame (the mean of {} not long): {}", plain.len(), text(&mean(&plain))));
    }
    for f in long.iter().take(LONG_MOST) {
        out.push(format!("long frame {} at {:.1} s: {}", f.number, f.at, text(f)));
    }
    if long.len() > LONG_MOST {
        out.push(format!("long frames: {} more in this reading are not listed", long.len() - LONG_MOST));
    }
    out
}

/// Frames whose lengths give the usual one, and the long frames listed in
/// a reading at most.
const RECENT: usize = 64;
const LONG_MOST: usize = 8;

/// A frame ends: called at the end of the title's present call, on the
/// thread that made it.
pub fn frame() {
    if !on() {
        return;
    }
    crate::cardmeter::collect();
    add(T::RenderLooks, 1);
    if on_slow_core() {
        add(T::RenderSlow, 1);
    }
    let now = std::time::Instant::now();
    let totals: [u64; N] = std::array::from_fn(|i| TOTAL[i].load(Relaxed));
    let sampled = sample();
    let here = HERE.with(|c| c.replace([0; HN]));
    // SAFETY: a plain query.
    let thread = unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentThreadId() };
    let mut state = STATE.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    let state = state.get_or_insert_with(|| State {
        first: now,
        last: None,
        number: 0,
        frames: Vec::new(),
        since: now,
        recent: std::collections::VecDeque::new(),
    });
    state.number += 1;
    if let Some((then, t0, s0, thread0)) = state.last.replace((now, totals, sampled, thread)) {
        let mut f = Frame {
            number: state.number,
            at: (now - state.first).as_secs_f64(),
            us: (now - then).as_micros() as f64,
            t: std::array::from_fn(|i| totals[i].wrapping_sub(t0[i]) as i64 as f64),
            s: std::array::from_fn(|i| sampled[i].wrapping_sub(s0[i]) as i64 as f64),
            h: here.map(|v| v as f64),
        };
        f.s[S_FREE_MB] = sampled[S_FREE_MB] as f64;
        if thread != thread0 {
            // Another thread presented: its processor time is not this frame's.
            (f.s[S_THREAD_USER], f.s[S_THREAD_KERNEL]) = (0.0, 0.0);
        }
        state.frames.push(f);
    }
    let elapsed = state.since.elapsed();
    if elapsed < std::time::Duration::from_secs(5) || state.frames.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let frames = std::mem::take(&mut state.frames);
    state.since = now;
    // The usual frame: the median of the last frames, this reading's with
    // those before it.
    for f in &frames {
        if state.recent.len() == RECENT {
            state.recent.pop_front();
        }
        state.recent.push_back(f.us);
    }
    let usual = median(state.recent.iter().copied());
    for line in lines(&frames, usual, elapsed.as_secs_f64()) {
        tracing::info!("{line}");
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn frame(number: u64, ms: f64) -> Frame {
        let mut f = Frame { number, at: number as f64, us: ms * 1e3, t: [0.0; N], s: [0.0; S], h: [0.0; HN] };
        f.t[T::PresentUs as usize] = ms * 100.0;
        f.t[T::Uploads as usize] = ms;
        f
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_long_frame_is_listed_beside_the_usual_one() {
        let frames: Vec<Frame> = [150.0, 160.0, 140.0, 400.0, 150.0].iter().enumerate().map(|(i, &ms)| frame(i as u64, ms)).collect();
        let out = lines(&frames, 150_000.0, 1.0);
        assert_eq!(out.len(), 3, "{out:#?}");
        assert!(out[0].starts_with("frame times: 5 frames in 1.0 s: shortest 140 ms, median 150, longest 400; 1 long (over 225 ms"), "{}", out[0]);
        assert!(out[0].ends_with("each: 150 160 140 400 150"), "{}", out[0]);
        // The usual frame is the mean of the four that are not long.
        assert!(out[1].starts_with("usual frame (the mean of 4 not long): 150 ms |"), "{}", out[1]);
        assert!(out[1].contains("in the present call 15.0 "), "{}", out[1]);
        assert!(out[1].contains(" 150 uploads"), "{}", out[1]);
        assert!(out[2].starts_with("long frame 3 at 3.0 s: 400 ms |"), "{}", out[2]);
        assert!(out[2].contains("in the present call 40.0 "), "{}", out[2]);
        assert!(out[2].contains(" 400 uploads"), "{}", out[2]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn long_is_half_as_long_again_and_at_least_40_ms_more() {
        assert_eq!(long_over(150_000.0), 225_000.0);
        assert_eq!(long_over(30_000.0), 70_000.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn more_long_frames_than_are_listed_are_counted() {
        let mut frames: Vec<Frame> = (0..12).map(|i| frame(i, 500.0)).collect();
        frames.push(frame(12, 100.0));
        let out = lines(&frames, 100_000.0, 5.0);
        assert_eq!(out.iter().filter(|l| l.starts_with("long frame ")).count(), LONG_MOST);
        assert!(out.last().unwrap().starts_with("long frames: 4 more"), "{out:#?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn totals_and_a_threads_own_counts_add_up() {
        let before = TOTAL[T::DiskReads as usize].load(Relaxed);
        add(T::DiskReads, 3);
        sub(T::DiskReads, 1);
        assert_eq!(TOTAL[T::DiskReads as usize].load(Relaxed) - before, 2);
        here(H::PaceUs, 5);
        here(H::PaceUs, 6);
        assert_eq!(HERE.with(|c| c.get())[H::PaceUs as usize], 11);
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/host.rs`:

```rs
//! The host GPU: one D3D12 device and direct queue (decision 0007), and a
//! window to present on.
//!
//! shortcut: every submission is waited for, so CPU and GPU never overlap
//! (unless `VICTORY_LATE_WAIT=1`, see [`late`]);
//! overlap them with per-submission fences once more than clears run.

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Mutex, OnceLock};

use windows::Win32::Foundation::{HANDLE, HWND, LPARAM, LRESULT, RECT, WPARAM};
use windows::Win32::Graphics::Direct3D::D3D_FEATURE_LEVEL_12_0;
use windows::Win32::Graphics::Direct3D12::*;
use windows::Win32::Graphics::Dxgi::Common::*;
use windows::Win32::Graphics::Dxgi::*;
use windows::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::GetModuleHandleW;
use windows::Win32::System::Threading::{CreateEventW, INFINITE, WaitForSingleObject};
use windows::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::*;
use windows::core::{Interface, PCWSTR, w};

/// Resource states without the console's own bits (compression hints from
/// bit 25 up), which the host rejects.
pub(crate) fn pc_state(state: u32) -> u32 {
    state & 0x01ff_ffff
}

/// A console state as a host texture state: PC bits only, and none of the
/// buffer-only ones the console allows on textures (vertex, constant and
/// index buffer, stream out, indirect arguments, as in "generic read").
pub(crate) fn texture_state(state: u32) -> u32 {
    const BUFFER_ONLY: u32 = 0x1 | 0x2 | 0x100 | 0x200;
    pc_state(state) & !BUFFER_ONLY
}

/// Render target views live only until their command is recorded, so a
/// ring of host descriptors is enough.
const RTV_RING: u32 = 1024;

/// Whether the host device has GPU upload heaps (asked when it is made).
static GPU_UPLOAD: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool = std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);

pub(crate) struct Host {
    pub(crate) device: ID3D12Device,
    queue: ID3D12CommandQueue,
    fence: ID3D12Fence,
    /// The last value signalled on `fence`, behind the submission lock.
    submitted: Mutex<u64>,
    event: HANDLE,
    rtvs: ID3D12DescriptorHeap,
    rtv_size: u32,
    /// A ring of depth views, used as `rtvs`.
    dsvs: ID3D12DescriptorHeap,
    dsv_size: u32,
    next_dsv: AtomicU32,
    /// With `VICTORY_D3D12_DEBUG` set (diagnostics builds): the debug
    /// layer's messages.
    messages: Option<ID3D12InfoQueue>,
    next_rtv: AtomicU32,
    presenter: Mutex<Option<Presenter>>,
    /// The adapter the device is on, for its memory budget
    /// ([`Host::video_memory`]); `None` if the system does not name it.
    adapter: Option<IDXGIAdapter3>,
}

// SAFETY: D3D12 devices, queues, fences and descriptor heaps are
// free-threaded; the event handle is only waited on under `submitted`.
unsafe impl Send for Host {}
// SAFETY: as above.
unsafe impl Sync for Host {}

/// Host objects the title let go of while a submission may still use them
/// (a texture its descriptors name, a descriptor slot's old resource), by
/// the submission count they wait for. The title's descriptor writes and
/// releases reach the host at once, from its own threads, while the host
/// runs a submission: freeing there is a GPU page fault on the freed
/// texture (a device hang).
static RETIRED: Mutex<Vec<(u64, Retired)>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());
/// Submissions started and finished (waited for).
static STARTED: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);
static FINISHED: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);

/// A retired object, dropped on whatever thread finishes the submission.
struct Retired(#[allow(dead_code)] Box<dyn std::any::Any>);
// SAFETY: what is retired is D3D12 objects (free-threaded) and the
// reference-counted wrappers holding them, dropped once.
unsafe impl Send for Retired {}

/// Milliseconds since the first call.
pub(crate) fn now_ms() -> u64 {
    static EPOCH: OnceLock<std::time::Instant> = OnceLock::new();
    EPOCH.get_or_init(std::time::Instant::now).elapsed().as_millis() as u64
}

/// This moment, for telling later how long ago it was ([`long_ago`]): the
/// frames begun so far (high half, `crate::frame::current`) and tenths of a
/// second since the start. Host copies of title memory, staging buffers and
/// host textures note when they were last used with it.
pub(crate) fn moment() -> u64 {
    (crate::frame::current() << 32) | ((now_ms() / 100) & 0xffff_ffff)
}

/// Whether `moment` lies at least `ms` milliseconds and `frames` frames
/// back. Both: at seconds per frame, what every frame uses is not touched
/// for seconds, and at many frames per second not for many frames. (A title
/// that never waits for frames has no frame count: nothing is then idle.)
pub(crate) fn long_ago(moment: u64, ms: u64, frames: u64) -> bool {
    let now = self::moment();
    let tenths = (now & 0xffff_ffff).saturating_sub(moment & 0xffff_ffff);
    (now >> 32).saturating_sub(moment >> 32) >= frames && tenths * 100 >= ms
}

/// Available physical RAM on the host in bytes, from `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`.
pub(crate) fn available_physical_ram() -> Option<u64> {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::SystemInformation::{GlobalMemoryStatusEx, MEMORYSTATUSEX};
    // SAFETY: plain data the call fills in.
    let mut m: MEMORYSTATUSEX = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    m.dwLength = std::mem::size_of::<MEMORYSTATUSEX>() as u32;
    // SAFETY: a sized structure.
    let ok = unsafe { GlobalMemoryStatusEx(&mut m) } != 0;
    ok.then_some(m.ullAvailPhys)
}

/// Effective idle timeout (in milliseconds) for VRAM-backed host textures,
/// scaled down under VRAM pressure. Never returns less than 1,000 ms so
/// handles not yet recorded into a list or slot remain protected.
pub(crate) fn vram_idle_ms(video_memory: Option<[u64; 4]>) -> u64 {
    const NORMAL_MS: u64 = 5_000;
    const MODERATE_MS: u64 = 2_500;
    const HIGH_MS: u64 = 1_000;
    let Some([budget, used, ..]) = video_memory else {
        return NORMAL_MS;
    };
    if budget == 0 {
        return NORMAL_MS;
    }
    let used_pct = (u128::from(used) * 100) / u128::from(budget);
    if used_pct >= 85 {
        HIGH_MS
    } else if used_pct >= 75 {
        MODERATE_MS
    } else {
        NORMAL_MS
    }
}

/// Effective idle timeout (in milliseconds) for system-RAM caches (staging
/// buffers, loose shadows, and the mapped pipeline library), scaled down
/// when free physical RAM is low. Never returns less than 2,000 ms.
pub(crate) fn ram_idle_ms(avail_phys: Option<u64>) -> u64 {
    const GIB: u64 = 1024 * 1024 * 1024;
    const NORMAL_MS: u64 = 10_000;
    const MODERATE_MS: u64 = 5_000;
    const HIGH_MS: u64 = 2_000;
    let Some(avail) = avail_phys else {
        return NORMAL_MS;
    };
    if avail < 2 * GIB {
        HIGH_MS
    } else if avail < 4 * GIB {
        MODERATE_MS
    } else {
        NORMAL_MS
    }
}

/// How many references are held on a host object (its COM count): ours
/// all, since the host's views and commands hold none. A buffer or texture
/// with one is held by its owner alone: no descriptor slot keeps it
/// (`HostHeap::kept`) and no list (`HostList::keep`).
pub(crate) fn references(object: &impl Interface) -> u32 {
    type Method = unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut std::ffi::c_void) -> u32;
    let raw = object.as_raw();
    // SAFETY: a live COM object, whose first three methods are those of
    // `IUnknown` (query, add a reference, release one); the pair leaves the
    // count as it was, and the release returns it. The first is not called.
    unsafe {
        let methods = *raw.cast::<*const [Method; 3]>();
        ((*methods)[1])(raw);
        ((*methods)[2])(raw)
    }
}

/// Once a second, before a submission starts: lets go of what nothing
/// names any more (copies of windows of title memory, staging buffers,
/// host copies of textures the title fills).
/// `VICTORY_SWEEP=0` keeps everything, as before.
fn sweep() {
    // The in-place probe and census, if asked for (`VICTORY_INPLACE_PROBE`).
    crate::inplace::tick();
    static ON: OnceLock<bool> = OnceLock::new();
    if !*ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_SWEEP").is_none_or(|v| v != "0")) {
        return;
    }
    static LAST: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);
    let now = now_ms();
    let last = LAST.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
    if now < last + 1000
        || LAST
            .compare_exchange(last, now, Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed)
            .is_err()
    {
        return;
    }
    crate::pipeline::trim_library();
    crate::shadow::let_go_idle();
    crate::texture::let_go_idle();
    crate::resource::let_go_idle();
}

/// Drops `object` once every submission running now has finished: at once
/// if none is.
pub(crate) fn retire<T: 'static>(object: T) {
    let started = STARTED.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if started <= FINISHED.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
        RETIREMENTS[0].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        drop(object);
        return;
    }
    RETIREMENTS[1].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    RETIRED
        .lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
        .push((started, Retired(Box::new(object))));
}

/// Drops what waited for submissions up to `finished`.
fn bury(finished: u64) {
    let done: Vec<(u64, Retired)> = {
        let mut retired = RETIRED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if retired.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let (done, keep) = std::mem::take(&mut *retired)
            .into_iter()
            .partition(|(at, _)| *at <= finished);
        *retired = keep;
        done
    };
    drop(done);
}

/// Objects [`retire`] dropped at once (no submission was running) and
/// kept until a running submission finished, since the start.
static RETIREMENTS: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64; 2] = [const { std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0) }; 2];

/// What the layer did to the host's objects lately, newest last (sweeps
/// that let host copies go, pipeline library calls, saves and trims): said
/// once when the host device is removed ([`log_removal_context`]), with
/// what the submitting thread and the pipeline workers were doing at that
/// moment. A device the driver removes "internally" names no command, and
/// the pass that happens to notice first names only the view it was at:
/// the three such losses of runs 72, 73 and 82 each came within 5 ms of a
/// pipeline library call that no line of the log tied to them.
/// `VICTORY_TRAIL=0`: nothing is kept and nothing is said.
static TRAIL: Mutex<std::collections::VecDeque<(u64, u32, String)>> = Mutex::new(std::collections::VecDeque::new());
/// The entries kept.
const TRAIL_MOST: usize = 96;

fn trail_on() -> bool {
    static ON: OnceLock<bool> = OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_TRAIL").is_none_or(|v| v != "0"))
}

/// Microseconds since the first call.
pub(crate) fn now_us() -> u64 {
    static EPOCH: OnceLock<std::time::Instant> = OnceLock::new();
    EPOCH.get_or_init(std::time::Instant::now).elapsed().as_micros() as u64
}

/// The calling thread, as the log's other lines name threads.
pub(crate) fn thread_id() -> u32 {
    // SAFETY: a plain query.
    unsafe { windows::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentThreadId() }
}

/// Notes something done to the host's objects ([`TRAIL`]); `what` is only
/// run when the trail is kept.
pub(crate) fn trail(what: impl FnOnce() -> String) {
    if !trail_on() {
        return;
    }
    let entry = (now_us(), thread_id(), what());
    // Sweeps also go to the log as they happen: the trail is only said at
    // a loss, and the driver's errors in the system's event log (run 224's
    // first fell inside a sweep of 4,711 host textures) need the sweeps of
    // clean runs beside them.
    if entry.2.starts_with("sweep:") {
        tracing::info!("{}", entry.2);
    }
    let mut trail = TRAIL.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    if trail.len() >= TRAIL_MOST {
        trail.pop_front();
    }
    trail.push_back(entry);
}

/// What the submitting thread is doing (0 nothing: between submissions,
/// 1 preparing one, 2 waiting for the card to run it, 3 copying back what
/// it wrote), the lists of that submission, and since when ([`now_us`]).
static SUBMITTING: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64; 3] = [const { std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0) }; 3];

fn submitting(phase: u64, lists: usize) {
    SUBMITTING[1].store(lists as u64, Ordering::Relaxed);
    SUBMITTING[2].store(now_us(), Ordering::Relaxed);
    SUBMITTING[0].store(phase, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

/// What was going on when the host device went: whether a submission was
/// on the card, the pipeline library's state and the calls running in it,
/// and the trail.
pub(crate) fn removal_context() -> String {
    use std::fmt::Write;
    let now = now_us();
    let ms = |at: u64| now.saturating_sub(at) as f64 / 1000.0;
    let phase = match SUBMITTING[0].load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
        0 => "between submissions (nothing of ours was running on the card)",
        1 => "preparing a submission (nothing of ours was running on the card)",
        2 => "waiting for the card to run a submission",
        _ => "copying back what a submission wrote (nothing of ours was running on the card)",
    };
    let mut text = format!(
        "the submitting thread was {phase}, of {} lists, for {:.1} ms; {}; objects let go at once {} and after a running submission {}; submissions started {} finished {}",
        SUBMITTING[1].load(Ordering::Relaxed),
        ms(SUBMITTING[2].load(Ordering::Relaxed)),
        crate::pipeline::library_removal_note(),
        RETIREMENTS[0].load(Ordering::Relaxed),
        RETIREMENTS[1].load(Ordering::Relaxed),
        STARTED.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
        FINISHED.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
    );
    let trail = TRAIL.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    let _ = write!(text, "; the last {} things done, newest last:", trail.len());
    for (at, thread, what) in trail.iter() {
        let _ = write!(text, "\n  {:.1} ms before, thread {thread}: {what}", ms(*at));
    }
    text
}

/// Says [`removal_context`] in the log, once: called by whoever finds the
/// host device removed.
pub(crate) fn log_removal_context() {
    static SAID: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool = std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);
    if !trail_on() || SAID.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed) {
        return;
    }
    tracing::error!("when the host device went: {}", removal_context());
}

/// Time spent in submissions since the last frame-rate line, in
/// microseconds: preparing them on the CPU (title memory copies, texture
/// detiling), then waiting for the GPU.
static SUBMISSION_US: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64; 2] =
    [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0), std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0)];

/// Adds to [`SUBMISSION_US`] and to the frame log's totals.
fn submission_us(i: usize, us: u64) {
```
