`crates/victory-gpu/src/pipeline/library.rs`:

```rs
//! Compiled host pipelines kept on disk, and the title pipelines worth
//! starting early (decision 0007, "Pipeline cache").
//!
//! 1. Every host pipeline goes into the host's pipeline library, named by
//!    a hash of all that its host description holds (the translated
//!    shaders' code, which changes when a translation does, our root
//!    signature, the graphics state). The library is saved under the cache
//!    folder; the host refuses a library of another adapter or driver, and
//!    an entry whose description differs, so neither is ever used.
//! 2. The title pipelines a run drew or dispatched with are listed by a key
//!    known when the title creates them (their shader containers and
//!    graphics state); the next run hands those to the workers at
//!    creation, during loading.
//!
//! Library calls overlap: the host documents the library as safe to use
//! from several threads ("The pipeline library is thread-safe to use, and
//! will internally synchronize as necessary", `CreatePipelineLibrary`,
//! Thread Safety), with one exception kept here: two loads of the same
//! pipeline are made one after the other ([`same_name`]). Under one lock of
//! ours for every call, the eight workers made pipelines one at a time:
//! 87 to 96 of 110 looks at each worker found it waiting for that lock
//! (run 49), and an earlier run's 2,300 pipelines, all in the library, were
//! still being loaded 46 s into the opening cutscene.
//! `VICTORY_LIBRARY_LOCK=1`: one call at a time, as before.
//!
//! The library's file is mapped, not read into memory ([`Blob`]): the host
//! keeps pointing into the bytes it was made from for as long as it lives,
//! and read into a buffer they were 1,352 MB of the process's own memory
//! for the whole run (run 60), all of it in physical memory. Mapped, the
//! pages are the file's: only those the host reads are in memory, and the
//! system can drop them without writing them anywhere. A save writes the
//! new library through a mapping of the new file in the same way (a buffer
//! of the library's size was made, filled and written out at each save).
//! `VICTORY_LIBRARY_MAP=0`: read and written through buffers, as before.
//!
//! The mapped file's handle stays open for as long as the mapping lives
//! ([`holds`]). A save renames the new library over the file this run has
//! mapped, and with the handle closed Windows then gives up the old file's
//! contents: every page of the mapping that is not in memory at that
//! moment, or leaves memory later (the trim below, or Windows taking pages
//! back), reads as zeros from then on. The host's library reads such pages
//! as stored pipelines; the driver, handed a pipeline of zeros, removes the
//! device with DXGI_ERROR_DRIVER_INTERNAL_ERROR (runs 72, 73 and 82, each
//! within 5 ms of the first library call after a save and a trim; and the
//! library run 77 saved from such pages was refused by run 78). Measured
//! with a 64 MB file written past the system's cache, mapped and replaced:
//! 16,352 of 16,384 pages read zeros with the handle closed, none with it
//! open (the test below). `VICTORY_LIBRARY_HANDLE=0`: closed, as before.

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard, OnceLock, RwLock};

use windows::Win32::Graphics::Direct3D12::*;
use windows::core::{HSTRING, Interface, PCWSTR};

static DIR: OnceLock<PathBuf> = OnceLock::new();

/// Keeps the pipeline library and the early list in `dir` from now on.
pub fn use_pipeline_cache(dir: PathBuf) {
    let _ = DIR.set(dir);
}

/// Host pipelines created, loaded from the library, and title pipelines
/// started at creation, since the start.
pub(crate) static MADE: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
pub(crate) static LOADED: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
pub(crate) static EARLY: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
/// For the memory lines: the bytes of the library's file, kept in memory
/// while the library lives, and the bytes the last save wrote (a buffer of
/// that size is made, filled and written every time pipelines were added,
/// at most every 20 s).
pub(crate) static BLOB: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
pub(crate) static SAVED: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);

/// Whether the library's file is mapped ([`Blob`]) and saved through a
/// mapping. On by default; `VICTORY_LIBRARY_MAP=0` uses buffers, as before.
fn mapped() -> bool {
    static ON: OnceLock<bool> = OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_LIBRARY_MAP").is_none_or(|v| v != "0"))
}

/// Whether the mapped library file's handle is kept open while it is
/// mapped (see the module's notes: without it a save in the same run turns
/// the mapping's pages into zeros as they leave memory). On by default;
/// `VICTORY_LIBRARY_HANDLE=0` closes it after mapping, as before.
fn holds() -> bool {
    static ON: OnceLock<bool> = OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_LIBRARY_HANDLE").is_none_or(|v| v != "0"))
}

/// A whole file mapped into memory: read-only (the library's file) or
/// writable (the file a save fills). Unmapped when dropped.
struct Mapped {
    at: windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::MEMORY_MAPPED_VIEW_ADDRESS,
    len: usize,
    /// The file, for a mapping made by [`Mapped::open`] ([`holds`]): open
    /// until after the view is unmapped, so that the file a rename took
    /// the name from keeps its contents for the view.
    _file: Option<std::fs::File>,
}

impl Mapped {
    /// Maps `file` (`len` bytes, not zero) for reading, or for reading and
    /// writing.
    fn map(file: &std::fs::File, len: usize, write: bool) -> Option<Mapped> {
        use std::os::windows::io::AsRawHandle;
        use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle;
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
            CreateFileMappingW, FILE_MAP_READ, FILE_MAP_WRITE, MapViewOfFile, PAGE_READONLY, PAGE_READWRITE,
        };
        if len == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        // SAFETY: a file we hold open; the view keeps the file's pages
        // after the mapping object and the file are closed.
        let at = unsafe {
            let mapping = CreateFileMappingW(
                file.as_raw_handle(),
                std::ptr::null(),
                if write { PAGE_READWRITE } else { PAGE_READONLY },
                0,
                0,
                std::ptr::null(),
            );
            if mapping.is_null() {
                return None;
            }
            let at = MapViewOfFile(mapping, if write { FILE_MAP_WRITE } else { FILE_MAP_READ }, 0, 0, 0);
            CloseHandle(mapping);
            at
        };
        (!at.Value.is_null()).then_some(Mapped { at, len, _file: None })
    }

    /// The file at `path`, mapped for reading; `None` if it is not there,
    /// is empty or cannot be mapped.
    fn open(path: &std::path::Path) -> Option<Mapped> {
        Mapped::open_holding(path, holds())
    }

    /// As [`Mapped::open`]; `hold` says whether the file stays open with
    /// the mapping.
    fn open_holding(path: &std::path::Path, hold: bool) -> Option<Mapped> {
        // Opened as the standard library opens a file to read: others may
        // read, write, rename and delete it meanwhile, so a save still
        // renames the new library over this one.
        let file = std::fs::File::open(path).ok()?;
        let len = usize::try_from(file.metadata().ok()?.len()).ok()?;
        let mut mapped = Mapped::map(&file, len, false)?;
        if hold {
            mapped._file = Some(file);
        }
        Some(mapped)
    }

    /// A new file of `len` bytes at `path` (replacing what is there),
    /// mapped for writing.
    fn create(path: &std::path::Path, len: usize) -> Option<Mapped> {
        let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
            .read(true)
            .write(true)
            .create(true)
            .truncate(true)
            .open(path)
            .ok()?;
        file.set_len(len as u64).ok()?;
        Mapped::map(&file, len, true)
    }

    fn bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        // SAFETY: the view holds `len` readable bytes until dropped.
        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(self.at.Value.cast(), self.len) }
    }

    /// Only for a view made by [`Mapped::create`].
    fn bytes_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [u8] {
        // SAFETY: a writable view of `len` bytes, ours alone.
        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(self.at.Value.cast(), self.len) }
    }
}

impl Drop for Mapped {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: our view.
        unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::UnmapViewOfFile(self.at) };
    }
}

/// The bytes a library is made from: the host reads them for as long as
/// the library lives, so they are kept beside it.
enum Blob {
    /// No file (an empty library).
    None,
    /// The file read into memory (`VICTORY_LIBRARY_MAP=0`, tests, or a file
    /// that could not be mapped).
    Held(Vec<u8>),
    /// The file itself, mapped.
    Mapped(Mapped),
}

impl Blob {
    /// The library file in `dir`: a library a save left beside it
    /// ([`NEXT_FILE`]) takes its place first.
    fn of(dir: &std::path::Path) -> Blob {
        let path = dir.join(LIBRARY_FILE);
        let next = dir.join(NEXT_FILE);
        if next.exists() && std::fs::rename(&next, &path).is_err() {
            tracing::warn!("the host pipeline library saved last could not take the old one's place");
        }
        if mapped()
            && let Some(file) = Mapped::open(&path)
        {
            return Blob::Mapped(file);
        }
        match std::fs::read(&path) {
            Ok(bytes) if !bytes.is_empty() => Blob::Held(bytes),
            _ => Blob::None,
        }
    }

    fn bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        match self {
            Blob::None => &[],
            Blob::Held(bytes) => bytes,
            Blob::Mapped(file) => file.bytes(),
        }
    }
}

/// The mapped library file's view (address, bytes; 0: not mapped), when a
/// pipeline was last loaded from the library (`crate::host::now_ms`), and
/// whether the view's pages were let go since ([`trim`]).
static VIEW: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize; 2] = [const { std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0) }; 2];
static LOADED_AT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
static TRIMMED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
/// The bytes of the view let go so far, for the memory line.
pub(crate) static TRIMMED_BYTES: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
/// When the view's pages were last let go (`crate::host::now_ms`), and how
/// often and when a save of this run last renamed a new library over the
/// mapped file: for [`removal_note`].
static TRIMMED_AT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
static REPLACED: [AtomicU64; 2] = [const { AtomicU64::new(0) }; 2];

/// The library calls running now: thread, what (load, make, store,
/// serialise), the pipeline, and since when (`crate::host::now_us`).
static CALLS: Mutex<Vec<(u32, &'static str, String, u64)>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());

thread_local! {
    /// The pipeline this thread is making (its shaders), for [`CALLS`].
    static LABEL: std::cell::RefCell<String> = const { std::cell::RefCell::new(String::new()) };
}

/// Names the pipeline this thread makes next.
pub(crate) fn label(text: String) {
    LABEL.with(|l| *l.borrow_mut() = text);
}

/// A library call of this thread, listed in [`CALLS`] until dropped.
struct Call(u32, u64);

fn call(what: &'static str, name: &str) -> Call {
    let (thread, since) = (crate::host::thread_id(), crate::host::now_us());
    let label = LABEL.with(|l| l.borrow().clone());
    CALLS
        .lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
        .push((thread, what, format!("{name} {label}"), since));
    Call(thread, since)
}

impl Drop for Call {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        CALLS
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .retain(|c| (c.0, c.3) != (self.0, self.1));
    }
}

/// For the report when the host device is removed: the library calls
/// running at that moment, whether this run replaced the mapped file and
/// let its pages go, and how many pages of the mapping read as zeros now.
/// A library holds no page of zeros (the 259 MB one of run 83 has no run of
/// 2,048 zero bytes): each such page is one whose contents were lost (see
/// the module's notes), and a pipeline stored there is what the driver was
/// handed.
pub(crate) fn removal_note() -> String {
    use std::fmt::Write;
    let now = crate::host::now_us();
    let mut text = String::from("pipeline library: ");
    {
        let calls = CALLS.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if calls.is_empty() {
            text.push_str("no call running");
        }
        for (i, (thread, what, name, since)) in calls.iter().enumerate() {
            let _ = write!(
                text,
                "{}{what} of {name} running for {:.1} ms on thread {thread}",
                if i == 0 { "" } else { ", " },
                now.saturating_sub(*since) as f64 / 1000.0
            );
        }
    }
    let (at, len) = (VIEW[0].load(Ordering::Relaxed), VIEW[1].load(Ordering::Relaxed));
    if at == 0 {
        text.push_str("; its file is not mapped");
        return text;
    }
    let ago = |ms: u64| crate::host::now_ms().saturating_sub(ms) as f64 / 1000.0;
    let _ = write!(
        text,
        "; its file is mapped ({len} bytes), the handle {}",
        if holds() { "kept open" } else { "closed (VICTORY_LIBRARY_HANDLE=0)" }
    );
    match REPLACED[0].load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
        0 => text.push_str("; this run has not replaced the file"),
        n => {
            let _ = write!(
                text,
                "; this run replaced the file under the mapping {n} times, last {:.1} s ago",
                ago(REPLACED[1].load(Ordering::Relaxed))
            );
        }
    }
    if TRIMMED_BYTES.load(Ordering::Relaxed) > 0 {
        let _ = write!(text, "; its pages were last let go {:.1} s ago", ago(TRIMMED_AT.load(Ordering::Relaxed)));
    }
    // Within two seconds: pages not in memory come from the disk.
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
    // SAFETY: the view lives as long as the library, which is never dropped.
    let bytes = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(at as *const u8, len) };
    let (mut zero, mut looked, mut first) = (0u64, 0u64, None);
    for (n, page) in bytes.chunks(4096).enumerate() {
        if n % 4096 == 0 && started.elapsed() > std::time::Duration::from_secs(2) {
            break;
        }
        looked += 1;
        if page.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
            zero += 1;
            if first.is_none() {
                first = Some(n);
            }
        }
    }
    let _ = write!(text, "; {zero} of the {looked} pages looked at read as zeros now");
    if let Some(first) = first {
        let _ = write!(text, " (the first is page {first}): the library's contents were lost there");
    }
    text
}

/// Lets the mapped library file's pages go from the process's memory once
/// no pipeline has been loaded for ten seconds. The host reads nearly the
/// whole file while the early pipelines load (run 65: all 1,490 MB of it
/// were in the process's memory a minute in, and 1,300 MB still at the
/// end, on a PC with 2 GB free); after that it reads the file again only
/// when a new pipeline loads. Pages let go stay in Windows' file cache
/// while nothing else wants the memory, and come back on the next read.
/// Called once a second by the sweep; does its work on a thread of its own
/// (hundreds of thousands of pages), once after each burst of loads.
/// `VICTORY_LIBRARY_TRIM=0`: the pages stay until Windows takes them.
pub(crate) fn trim() {
    static ON: OnceLock<bool> = OnceLock::new();
    let (at, len) = (VIEW[0].load(Ordering::Relaxed), VIEW[1].load(Ordering::Relaxed));
    if at == 0
        || TRIMMED.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
        || !*ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_LIBRARY_TRIM").is_none_or(|v| v != "0"))
    {
        return;
    }
    let quiet_ms = crate::host::ram_idle_ms(crate::host::available_physical_ram());
    if crate::host::now_ms() < LOADED_AT.load(Ordering::Relaxed) + quiet_ms
        || TRIMMED.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed)
    {
        return;
    }
    let work = move || {
        // SAFETY: the view lives as long as the library, which is never
        // dropped. Unlocking pages that are not locked fails, as expected,
        // and takes them out of the working set: the documented way to let
        // pages of a mapped file go.
        unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::VirtualUnlock(at as *const _, len) };
        TRIMMED_BYTES.fetch_add(len as u64, Ordering::Relaxed);
        TRIMMED_AT.store(crate::host::now_ms(), Ordering::Relaxed);
        crate::host::trail(|| format!("pipeline library: the mapped file's pages let go from memory ({len} bytes)"));
    };
    if std::thread::Builder::new().name("victory-library-trim".into()).spawn(work).is_err() {
        TRIMMED.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
}

struct Library {
    library: ID3D12PipelineLibrary1,
    /// The blob the library was made from: it must outlive the library.
    _blob: Blob,
    /// Pipelines stored since the last save.
    added: AtomicU64,
    /// Stores share it and a save takes it alone: the size the library
    /// asks for must still be its size when it is written out.
    saving: RwLock<()>,
}

// SAFETY: D3D12 objects are free-threaded, and the library synchronises
// its own calls (see the module's notes); what it does not, two loads of
// one name, is serialised by `same_name`.
unsafe impl Send for Library {}
// SAFETY: as above; the other fields are an atomic and a lock.
unsafe impl Sync for Library {}

/// Held by a load of the pipeline named `name`: loads of the same name
/// wait for each other (the host's one exception to the library's thread
/// safety: such a load may change that pipeline's entry). Names share 64
/// locks, so two different names seldom wait.
fn same_name(name: &str) -> MutexGuard<'static, ()> {
    static LOADING: [Mutex<()>; 64] = [const { Mutex::new(()) }; 64];
    let at = name.bytes().fold(0usize, |h, b| h.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(usize::from(b)));
    LOADING[at % LOADING.len()].lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

/// With `VICTORY_LIBRARY_LOCK=1`: held by every library call, as before.
fn one_call() -> Option<MutexGuard<'static, ()>> {
    static ON: OnceLock<bool> = OnceLock::new();
    static CALLING: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());
    ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_LIBRARY_LOCK").is_some_and(|v| v == "1"))
        .then(|| CALLING.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()))
}

const LIBRARY_FILE: &str = "host-pipelines.bin";
/// A library the driver refused, kept as it was ([`open`]).
const REJECTED_FILE: &str = "host-pipelines.rejected.bin";
/// A saved library that could not replace [`LIBRARY_FILE`] while this run
/// had it mapped (a system that refuses to replace a mapped file): the next
/// start renames it over the library first ([`Blob::of`]).
const NEXT_FILE: &str = "host-pipelines.next";
const EARLY_FILE: &str = "early-pipelines.txt";
/// Title pipelines listed for an early start, at most.
const EARLY_MAX: usize = 8192;

fn library() -> Option<&'static Library> {
    static LIBRARY: OnceLock<Option<Library>> = OnceLock::new();
    LIBRARY
        .get_or_init(|| {
            // With RenderDoc loaded the device is RenderDoc's: the card's
            // library is not for it, and what it would save is not for
            // the card. Neither read nor written in such a run.
            #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
            if crate::renderdoc::loaded() {
                tracing::info!("RenderDoc is loaded: the host pipeline library is neither read nor saved in this run");
                return None;
            }
            let device = crate::host::host()?.device.cast::<ID3D12Device1>().ok()?;
            let blob = DIR.get().map_or(Blob::None, |d| Blob::of(d));
            let library = open(&device, blob);
            if library.is_none() {
                tracing::warn!("no host pipeline library: pipelines are not kept");
            }
            library
        })
        .as_ref()
}

/// The library in `blob`, or an empty one if the host rejects the blob (an
/// adapter or driver change, damage).
fn open(device: &ID3D12Device1, blob: Blob) -> Option<Library> {
    let make = |bytes: &[u8]| -> windows::core::Result<ID3D12PipelineLibrary1> {
        // SAFETY: the bytes outlive the library (kept beside it).
        unsafe {
            device.CreatePipelineLibrary::<ID3D12PipelineLibrary>(bytes)?.cast()
        }
    };
    let mut rejected = false;
    if !blob.bytes().is_empty() {
        match make(blob.bytes()) {
            Ok(library) => {
                let bytes = blob.bytes().len();
                BLOB.store(bytes as u64, Ordering::Relaxed);
                tracing::info!(bytes, mapped = matches!(blob, Blob::Mapped(_)), "host pipeline library loaded");
                if let Blob::Mapped(file) = &blob {
                    VIEW[1].store(file.len, Ordering::Relaxed);
                    VIEW[0].store(file.at.Value as usize, Ordering::Relaxed);
                    LOADED_AT.store(crate::host::now_ms(), Ordering::Relaxed);
                }
                return Some(Library {
                    library,
                    _blob: blob,
                    added: AtomicU64::new(0),
                    saving: RwLock::new(()),
                });
            }
            Err(e) => {
                rejected = true;
                tracing::warn!(error = %e, "host pipeline library rejected; starting an empty one (the rejected file is kept as {REJECTED_FILE})");
            }
        }
    } else {
        tracing::info!("no host pipeline library yet; starting an empty one");
    }
    // The rejected bytes are let go (a mapped file is unmapped) before the
    // empty library is made: nothing reads them any more.
    drop(blob);
    // And the file is kept under another name, not written over by this
    // run's first save: a refusal may be this device's alone (run 263:
    // RenderDoc's device refused the card's library, an empty one was
    // saved over 366 MB of built pipelines, and the next run drew black
    // until they were built again).
    if rejected && let Some(dir) = DIR.get() {
        if let Err(e) = std::fs::rename(dir.join(LIBRARY_FILE), dir.join(REJECTED_FILE)) {
            tracing::warn!(error = %e, "the rejected host pipeline library could not be kept under its other name");
        }
    }
    let library = make(&[]).ok()?;
    Some(Library {
        library,
        _blob: Blob::None,
        added: AtomicU64::new(0),
        saving: RwLock::new(()),
    })
}

/// A pipeline's name in the library: the hash of what its host
/// description holds.
pub(crate) fn name(kind: &str, root: &[u8], code: &[&[u8]], state: &str) -> String {
    let mut h = blake3::Hasher::new();
    for part in [kind.as_bytes(), root].into_iter().chain(code.iter().copied()).chain([state.as_bytes()]) {
        h.update(&(part.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
        h.update(part);
    }
    h.finalize().to_hex()[..32].to_owned()
}

/// The pipeline named `name`: loaded from the library by `load` if it is
/// there with the same description, else made by `create` and stored.
pub(crate) fn pipeline(
    name: &str,
    load: impl FnOnce(&ID3D12PipelineLibrary1, PCWSTR) -> windows::core::Result<ID3D12PipelineState>,
    create: impl FnOnce() -> windows::core::Result<ID3D12PipelineState>,
) -> windows::core::Result<ID3D12PipelineState> {
    let wide = HSTRING::from(name);
    let Some(library) = library() else {
        MADE.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        return create();
    };
    let began = std::time::Instant::now();
    let loaded = {
        let _all = one_call();
        let _one = same_name(name);
        let _call = call("load", name);
        load(&library.library, PCWSTR(wide.as_ptr()))
    };
    // The load read the library's file (see `trim`).
    LOADED_AT.store(crate::host::now_ms(), Ordering::Relaxed);
    TRIMMED.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
    let refused = match loaded {
        Ok(pso) => {
            LOADED.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
            crate::host::trail(|| {
                let label = LABEL.with(|l| l.borrow().clone());
                format!("pipeline library: loaded {label} in {:.1} ms", began.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 1e3)
            });
            return Ok(pso);
        }
        Err(e) => e,
    };
    // Compiled outside any lock: compiles take up to seconds.
    let pso = {
        let _call = call("make", name);
        create()?
    };
    MADE.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    crate::host::trail(|| {
        let label = LABEL.with(|l| l.borrow().clone());
        format!(
            "pipeline library: made {label} in {:.1} ms (the library did not load it: {refused})",
            began.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 1e3
        )
    });
    let _all = one_call();
    let _stores = library.saving.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    let _call = call("store", name);
    // SAFETY: a live pipeline; a name already stored (a description that
    // differs) is refused, which leaves the library as it was.
    if unsafe { library.library.StorePipeline(PCWSTR(wide.as_ptr()), &pso) }.is_ok() {
        library.added.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
    Ok(pso)
}

/// Writes the library and the early list if pipelines were added since the
/// last save and `SAVE_EVERY` has passed (or `now`).
pub(crate) fn save(now: bool) {
    static LAST: Mutex<Option<std::time::Instant>> = Mutex::new(None);
    const SAVE_EVERY: std::time::Duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(20);
    let (Some(dir), Some(library)) = (DIR.get(), library()) else { return };
    {
        let mut last = LAST.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if !now && last.is_some_and(|t| t.elapsed() < SAVE_EVERY) {
            return;
        }
        *last = Some(std::time::Instant::now());
    }
    if let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(dir) {
        tracing::warn!(error = %e, "host pipeline library not saved");
        return;
    }
    let tmp = dir.join(LIBRARY_FILE).with_extension("tmp");
    // The bytes of the library written to `tmp`; 0 when no pipeline was
    // added: the library on disk is then what it was, and only the early
    // list is written (a title pipeline first drawn with wrote all 1,352 MB
    // of the library again: run 60's second save).
    let bytes = {
        let _all = one_call();
        // No store between asking the size and writing; loads go on.
        let _alone = library.saving.write().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        let added = library.added.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        if !USED_CHANGED.swap(false, Ordering::Relaxed) && added == 0 {
            return;
        }
        if added == 0 {
            0
        } else {
            // SAFETY: a plain query.
            let size = unsafe { library.library.GetSerializedSize() };
            let _call = call("serialise", "the whole library");
            if let Err(e) = serialise(&library.library, &tmp, size) {
                tracing::warn!(error = %e, "host pipeline library not serialised");
                let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);
                return;
            }
            library.added.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
            SAVED.store(size as u64, Ordering::Relaxed);
            size
        }
    };
    let used: Vec<String> = USED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).iter().flatten().cloned().collect();
    let library_written = if bytes > 0 { replace_library(dir, &tmp) } else { Ok(()) };
    if bytes > 0 && library_written.is_ok() {
        // In place unless the system refused and the new one waits beside it.
        let in_place = !dir.join(NEXT_FILE).exists();
        if in_place && VIEW[0].load(Ordering::Relaxed) != 0 {
            REPLACED[1].store(crate::host::now_ms(), Ordering::Relaxed);
            REPLACED[0].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
        crate::host::trail(|| {
            format!(
                "pipeline library: saved {bytes} bytes, {}",
                if in_place { "renamed over the library's file" } else { "left beside the library's file for the next start" }
            )
        });
    }
    let written = library_written
        .and_then(|()| write_atomically(&dir.join(EARLY_FILE), used.join("\n").as_bytes()));
    match written {
        Ok(()) => tracing::info!(
            bytes,
            early = used.len(),
            made = MADE.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            loaded = LOADED.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            started_early = EARLY.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            "host pipeline library saved"
        ),
        Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, "host pipeline library not saved"),
    }
}

/// Writes the library's `size` serialised bytes to the file `tmp`: through
/// a mapping of that file, so that the bytes are the file's pages and not
/// 1.3 GB more of the process's own memory for the seconds a save takes;
/// through a buffer where the file cannot be mapped (and with
/// `VICTORY_LIBRARY_MAP=0`).
fn serialise(library: &ID3D12PipelineLibrary1, tmp: &std::path::Path, size: usize) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let failed = |e: windows::core::Error| std::io::Error::other(e.to_string());
    if mapped()
        && let Some(mut file) = Mapped::create(tmp, size)
    {
        // SAFETY: a buffer of the size the library asks for.
        return unsafe { library.Serialize(file.bytes_mut()) }.map_err(failed);
    }
    let mut bytes = vec![0u8; size];
    // SAFETY: a buffer of the size the library asks for.
    unsafe { library.Serialize(&mut bytes) }.map_err(failed)?;
    std::fs::write(tmp, &bytes)
}

/// Renames the written library `tmp` over the library's file in `dir`. This
/// run may have that file mapped: Windows 11 replaces a mapped file, and
/// the mapping goes on reading the old one for as long as a handle on it
/// is open ([`holds`]; with none, only the pages in memory at that moment
/// stay: the rest read as zeros). Where a system refuses, the new library
/// is left beside it as [`NEXT_FILE`] for the next start.
fn replace_library(dir: &std::path::Path, tmp: &std::path::Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    std::fs::rename(tmp, dir.join(LIBRARY_FILE)).or_else(|_| std::fs::rename(tmp, dir.join(NEXT_FILE)))
}

/// Writes `bytes` to a temporary file beside `path`, then renames it over
/// `path`: a reader never sees a part.
fn write_atomically(path: &std::path::Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let tmp = path.with_extension("tmp");
    std::fs::write(&tmp, bytes)?;
    std::fs::rename(&tmp, path)
}

/// Title pipeline keys requested by draws or dispatches (this run and the last).
static USED: Mutex<Option<HashSet<String>>> = Mutex::new(None);
static USED_CHANGED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

fn used() -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'static, Option<HashSet<String>>> {
    let mut used = USED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    if used.is_none() {
        let listed = DIR
            .get()
            .and_then(|d| std::fs::read_to_string(d.join(EARLY_FILE)).ok())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let set: HashSet<String> = listed.lines().filter(|l| !l.is_empty()).map(str::to_owned).collect();
        tracing::info!(pipelines = set.len(), "title pipelines to start early");
        *used = Some(set);
    }
    used
}

/// Whether the title pipeline with `key` was requested in this or an earlier run.
pub(crate) fn wanted_early(key: &str) -> bool {
    used().as_ref().is_some_and(|s| s.contains(key))
}

/// A draw or dispatch requested the title pipeline with `key`.
pub(crate) fn note_used(key: &str) {
    let mut used = used();
    let set = used.get_or_insert_with(HashSet::new);
    if set.len() < EARLY_MAX && set.insert(key.to_owned()) {
        USED_CHANGED.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn names_change_with_what_goes_into_the_pipeline() {
        let a = name("graphics", b"root", &[b"vs", b"ps"], "state");
        assert_eq!(a, name("graphics", b"root", &[b"vs", b"ps"], "state"));
        assert_ne!(a, name("graphics", b"root", &[b"vs", b"ps2"], "state"));
        assert_ne!(a, name("graphics", b"root", &[b"vs", b"ps"], "state2"));
        assert_ne!(a, name("graphics", b"root2", &[b"vs", b"ps"], "state"));
        assert_ne!(a, name("mesh", b"root", &[b"vs", b"ps"], "state"));
        // Parts do not run into each other.
        assert_ne!(a, name("graphics", b"root", &[b"vsp", b"s"], "state"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_rejected_blob_gives_an_empty_library() {
        let Some(device) = crate::host::host().and_then(|h| h.device.cast::<ID3D12Device1>().ok()) else {
            return; // no host GPU here
        };
        let library = open(&device, Blob::Held(b"not a pipeline library".repeat(16))).expect("an empty library");
        // SAFETY: a plain query on a live library.
        assert!(unsafe { library.library.GetSerializedSize() } > 0);
        assert!(matches!(library._blob, Blob::None));
    }

    /// A mapped file reads as the file's bytes, a file written through a
    /// mapping holds what was written, and the library's file can be
    /// replaced while it is mapped (or the new one waits as the next).
    #[test]
    fn the_library_file_is_mapped_and_replaced() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = dir.path().join(LIBRARY_FILE);
        assert!(matches!(Blob::of(dir.path()), Blob::None), "no file yet");
        std::fs::write(&path, b"").unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(Blob::of(dir.path()), Blob::None), "an empty file");
        let old: Vec<u8> = (0..200_000u32).map(|i| i as u8).collect();
        std::fs::write(&path, &old).unwrap();
        let blob = Blob::of(dir.path());
        assert!(matches!(blob, Blob::Mapped(_)) || !mapped());
        assert_eq!(blob.bytes(), &old[..]);
        // A save while the old file is mapped.
        let tmp = path.with_extension("tmp");
        let new: Vec<u8> = (0..300_000u32).map(|i| (i * 7) as u8).collect();
        {
            let mut file = Mapped::create(&tmp, new.len()).expect("a new file, mapped");
            file.bytes_mut().copy_from_slice(&new);
        }
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&tmp).unwrap(), new);
        replace_library(dir.path(), &tmp).unwrap();
        assert!(!tmp.exists());
        // The mapping still reads the old library.
        assert_eq!(blob.bytes(), &old[..]);
        drop(blob);
        // The next start reads the new one, wherever the save left it.
        assert_eq!(Blob::of(dir.path()).bytes(), &new[..]);
        assert!(!dir.path().join(NEXT_FILE).exists());
    }

    /// The bytes at `at` of the pattern the test below writes.
    fn pattern(at: usize, out: &mut [u8]) {
        for (i, word) in out.chunks_exact_mut(4).enumerate() {
            let v = ((at / 4 + i) as u32).wrapping_mul(2_654_435_761).wrapping_add(1);
            word.copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
        }
    }

    /// A file of `len` bytes (whole MiB) of [`pattern`], written past the
    /// system's cache: none of its pages is in memory afterwards. False
    /// where the folder's file system does not take such writes.
    fn write_uncached(path: &std::path::Path, len: usize) -> bool {
        use std::io::Write;
        use std::os::windows::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
        // FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING | FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH
        const UNCACHED: u32 = 0x2000_0000 | 0x8000_0000;
        const CHUNK: usize = 1 << 20;
        let Ok(mut file) = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
            .write(true)
            .create(true)
            .truncate(true)
            .custom_flags(UNCACHED)
            .open(path)
        else {
            return false;
        };
        // Such writes want a buffer on a sector boundary.
        let mut store = vec![0u8; CHUNK + 4096];
        let start = store.as_ptr().align_offset(4096);
        for at in (0..len).step_by(CHUNK) {
            let chunk = &mut store[start..start + CHUNK];
            pattern(at, chunk);
            if file.write_all(chunk).is_err() {
                return false;
            }
        }
        true
    }

    /// The device loss of runs 72, 73 and 82: the library's file is
    /// replaced while it is mapped, and pages of the mapping that were not
    /// in memory then are read afterwards (in the runs: pages the trim let
    /// go and Windows gave to something else). With the file's handle kept
    /// open they still read as the old file. (With it closed, as before,
    /// all but the first few read as zeros on the PC this was found on.)
    #[test]
    fn a_replaced_library_file_still_reads_from_the_disk() {
        const LEN: usize = 8 << 20;
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = dir.path().join(LIBRARY_FILE);
        if !write_uncached(&path, LEN) {
            return; // no uncached writes here: nothing to show
        }
        let mapped = Mapped::open_holding(&path, true).expect("the file, mapped");
        // A save: the new library, renamed over the mapped one.
        let tmp = path.with_extension("tmp");
        {
            let mut file = Mapped::create(&tmp, LEN).expect("a new file, mapped");
            file.bytes_mut().fill(0xEE);
        }
        replace_library(dir.path(), &tmp).unwrap();
        // Every page of the old mapping, read for the first time now.
        let mut expected = vec![0u8; 4096];
        for (page, bytes) in mapped.bytes().chunks(4096).enumerate() {
            pattern(page * 4096, &mut expected);
            assert!(bytes == &expected[..], "page {page} of the replaced library no longer reads as the old file");
        }
    }
}

```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/pipeline/make.rs`:

```rs
//! Host pipelines are made by workers, not by the title thread that first
//! records a draw with them. Translating a shader and the host driver's
//! compile take from milliseconds to seconds each (structurisation of the
//! biggest compute programs ~0.4 s, some driver compiles 3.4 s), and
//! the title's first world frame wants over 1,200 new pipelines: made
//! on its recording threads, that frame took more than 30 s and the
//! title's GPU watchdog ended the run (decision 0007, "Pipelines made off
//! the title's threads").
//!
//! A first use queues the pipeline and waits for it within a budget per
//! frame, so the cheap ones (menus, one-off passes such as a colour-grading
//! bake) are there at once as before; past the budget a draw or dispatch
//! whose pipeline is not ready is dropped, as an untranslated one is.
//!
//! The default budget is half a second per title frame. A pass the title
//! runs only once and whose pipeline takes longer is lost.

use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU8, AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Condvar, Mutex, OnceLock};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use super::Shader;
use super::host::{GraphicsState, HostPipeline};

/// What a host pipeline is made from, and the host pipeline once made.
pub(crate) struct Pending {
    shaders: Vec<Arc<Shader>>,
    pub(crate) graphics: Option<Box<GraphicsState>>,
    queue_state: AtomicU8,
    made: OnceLock<Option<HostPipeline>>,
    /// What identifies it across runs (shader containers and state), and
    /// whether a draw or dispatch has requested it yet.
    key: String,
    used: AtomicBool,
}

// SAFETY: D3D12 objects are free-threaded; the graphics state (whose input
// elements point into its own names) is only read after creation.
unsafe impl Send for Pending {}
// SAFETY: as above.
unsafe impl Sync for Pending {}

impl Pending {
    pub(crate) fn new(shaders: Vec<Arc<Shader>>, graphics: Option<Box<GraphicsState>>) -> Pending {
        let mut key = blake3::Hasher::new();
        for s in &shaders {
            key.update(s.stage.as_bytes());
            key.update(s.hash.as_bytes());
        }
        key.update(graphics.as_ref().map(|g| g.describe()).unwrap_or_default().as_bytes());
        Pending {
            shaders,
            graphics,
            queue_state: AtomicU8::new(NOT_QUEUED),
            made: OnceLock::new(),
            key: key.finalize().to_hex()[..32].to_owned(),
            used: AtomicBool::new(false),
        }
    }

    fn make(&self) {
        self.made
            .get_or_init(|| HostPipeline::new(&self.shaders, self.graphics.as_deref()));
        let (lock, done) = &DONE;
        let _held = lock.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        done.notify_all();
    }
}

/// Why a pipeline has no host pipeline (diagnostics): its shaders that do
/// not translate, else "refused" or "being made"; `None` if it has one.
#[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
pub(crate) fn missing(p: &Pending) -> Option<String> {
    match p.made.get() {
        Some(Some(_)) => None,
        None => Some("being made".into()),
        Some(None) => {
            let failed: Vec<String> = p
                .shaders
                .iter()
                .filter(|s| matches!(s.translated.get(), Some(None)))
                .map(|s| format!("{} {}", s.stage, s.hash))
                .collect();
            Some(if failed.is_empty() {
                format!("refused {:?}", p.shaders)
            } else {
                failed.join(" + ")
            })
        }
    }
}

/// Signalled whenever a worker has made a pipeline.
static DONE: (Mutex<()>, Condvar) = (Mutex::new(()), Condvar::new());

/// Waiting allowed per title frame, over all threads.
fn wait_budget() -> Duration {
    static BUDGET: OnceLock<Duration> = OnceLock::new();
    *BUDGET.get_or_init(|| {
        let millis = std::env::var("VICTORY_PIPELINE_WAIT_MS")
            .ok()
            .and_then(|value| value.trim().parse::<u64>().ok())
            .unwrap_or(500);
        tracing::info!(millis, "host pipeline wait budget per frame");
        Duration::from_millis(millis)
    })
}

/// Pipelines queued and not made yet.
static WAITING: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);

/// Pipelines queued and not made yet (for the frame line).
pub(crate) fn waiting() -> u64 {
    WAITING.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

/// The host pipeline if it is made (or is made within the frame's budget);
/// queues it on first use.
pub(crate) fn ready(p: &Arc<Pending>) -> Option<&HostPipeline> {
    // A still-pending pipeline was requested by the title too. Prewarm it
    // on the next launch, even if this run never got to use it.
    if !p.used.load(Ordering::Relaxed) && !p.used.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed) {
        super::library::note_used(&p.key);
    }
    if p.made.get().is_none() {
        start(p, REQUESTED);
        wait(p, crate::frame::current());
    }
    p.made.get()?.as_ref()
}

/// Makes `p` on this thread if it is not made yet (waiting for a worker
/// that is making it); whether it has a host pipeline.
pub(crate) fn now(p: &Arc<Pending>) -> bool {
    p.make();
    p.made.get().is_some_and(|made| made.is_some())
}

/// At the title's creation of a pipeline: starts it at once if an earlier
/// run drew with it (during loading, so the world's first frames find it).
pub(crate) fn early(p: &Arc<Pending>) {
    if !p.shaders.is_empty() && super::library::wanted_early(&p.key) {
        super::library::EARLY.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        start(p, EARLY);
    }
}

/// Whether the frame's budget is one for all threads together: a thread
/// that waits takes what is left of it and gives back what it did not
/// use. Counted only when a wait had ended, the budget was one per thread:
/// each of the title's five recording threads began its first wait of a
/// frame with nothing counted yet and waited the whole half second, 2.5 s
/// of waiting in every frame in which pipelines were being made (runs
/// 34-49: "2504 ms waiting for pipelines" in each such frame).
/// On by default; `VICTORY_PIPELINE_WAIT_SHARED=0` counts as before.
fn shared_budget() -> bool {
    static ON: OnceLock<bool> = OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_PIPELINE_WAIT_SHARED").is_none_or(|v| v != "0"))
}

/// Waits for `p` while frame `frame` has budget left.
fn wait(p: &Pending, frame: u64) {
    let budget = wait_budget();
    if budget.is_zero() {
        return;
    }
    // The frame the budget belongs to, and what was waited of it (or is
    // taken by a thread waiting now).
    static SPENT: Mutex<(u64, Duration)> = Mutex::new((u64::MAX, Duration::ZERO));
    let shared = shared_budget();
    let left = {
        let mut spent = SPENT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if spent.0 != frame {
            *spent = (frame, Duration::ZERO);
        }
        let left = budget.saturating_sub(spent.1);
        if shared {
            spent.1 += left;
        }
        left
    };
    if left.is_zero() {
        return;
    }
    let started = Instant::now();
    let (lock, done) = &DONE;
    let mut held = lock.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    while p.made.get().is_none() {
        let rest = left.saturating_sub(started.elapsed());
        if rest.is_zero() {
            break;
        }
        held = done.wait_timeout(held, rest).unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).0;
    }
    drop(held);
    let waited = started.elapsed().min(left);
    {
        let mut spent = SPENT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        // A frame that began meanwhile has its own budget.
        if spent.0 == frame {
            if shared {
                spent.1 = spent.1.saturating_sub(left - waited);
            } else {
                spent.1 += waited;
            }
        }
    }
    crate::framelog::add(crate::framelog::T::PipelineWaitUs, started.elapsed().as_micros() as u64);
    #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
    crate::copystat::add(
        crate::copystat::C::PipelineWaitUs,
        started.elapsed().as_micros() as u64,
    );
}

const NOT_QUEUED: u8 = 0;
const EARLY: u8 = 1;
const REQUESTED: u8 = 2;
const MAKING: u8 = 3;

struct Queue {
    early: VecDeque<Arc<Pending>>,
    requested: VecDeque<Arc<Pending>>,
}

impl Queue {
    const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            early: VecDeque::new(),
            requested: VecDeque::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Queues an unrequested pipeline or promotes one queued at creation.
    /// Returns whether it is new to the queue, or `None` if nothing changed.
    fn push(&mut self, p: &Arc<Pending>, priority: u8) -> Option<bool> {
        let prev = p.queue_state.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        if prev >= priority {
            return None;
        }
        p.queue_state.store(priority, Ordering::Relaxed);
        if priority == REQUESTED {
            self.requested.push_back(p.clone());
        } else {
            self.early.push_back(p.clone());
        }
        Some(prev == NOT_QUEUED)
    }

    fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<Arc<Pending>> {
        let p = self.requested.pop_front().or_else(|| {
            // An early entry can have been promoted and claimed already.
            std::iter::from_fn(|| self.early.pop_front())
                .find(|p| p.queue_state.load(Ordering::Relaxed) == EARLY)
        })?;
        p.queue_state.store(MAKING, Ordering::Relaxed);
        Some(p)
    }
}

static QUEUE: Mutex<Queue> = Mutex::new(Queue::new());
static AVAILABLE: Condvar = Condvar::new();

/// Start or promote work for a draw without waiting behind the entire early
/// list. Queue changes and worker claims happen under the same lock.
fn start(p: &Arc<Pending>, priority: u8) {
    if p.queue_state.load(Ordering::Relaxed) >= priority {
        return;
    }
    if !workers() {
        if p.queue_state.swap(MAKING, Ordering::Relaxed) == NOT_QUEUED {
            p.make();
        }
        return;
    }
    let mut queue = QUEUE.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    if let Some(new) = queue.push(p, priority) {
        if new {
            PEAK.fetch_max(WAITING.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) + 1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
        AVAILABLE.notify_one();
    }
}

fn next() -> Arc<Pending> {
    let mut queue = QUEUE.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    loop {
        if let Some(p) = queue.pop() {
            return p;
        }
        queue = AVAILABLE.wait(queue).unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    }
}

/// Starts the workers (half the logical processors, 2 to 8) on first use.
fn workers() -> bool {
    static RUNNING: OnceLock<bool> = OnceLock::new();
    *RUNNING.get_or_init(|| {
        let mut running = false;
        let workers = std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(2, |n| (n.get() / 2).clamp(2, 8));
        for i in 0..workers {
            let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
                .name(format!("victory-pipelines-{i}"))
                .spawn(|| {
                    // Below the title's own threads (loading, recording).
                    // SAFETY: a plain call on our own thread.
                    unsafe {
                        use windows::Win32::System::Threading::*;
                        let _ = SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(), THREAD_PRIORITY_BELOW_NORMAL);
                    }
                    loop {
                        next().make();
                        if WAITING.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed) == 1 {
                            drained();
                        } else {
                            super::library::save(false);
                        }
                    }
                });
            if let Err(e) = spawned {
                tracing::warn!(error = %e, "no pipeline worker");
            } else {
                running = true;
            }
        }
        running
    })
}

/// The most pipelines waiting at once since the workers last ran out.
static PEAK: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);

/// The workers ran out of work: logged after a batch of 10 or more, and
/// the cache saved (at most every 20 s).
fn drained() {
    use super::library::{EARLY, LOADED, MADE};
    if PEAK.swap(0, Ordering::Relaxed) >= 10 {
        tracing::info!(
            made = MADE.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            loaded = LOADED.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            started_early = EARLY.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            "host pipelines all made"
        );
    }
    super::library::save(false);
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A first use queues the pipeline and, within the budget, gets the
    /// worker's answer (here: no host pipeline for no shaders).
    #[test]
    fn first_use_is_made_by_a_worker() {
        let p = Arc::new(Pending::new(Vec::new(), None));
        assert!(ready(&p).is_none());
        assert_ne!(p.queue_state.load(Ordering::Relaxed), NOT_QUEUED);
        let started = Instant::now();
        while p.made.get().is_none() && started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(10) {
            std::thread::yield_now();
        }
        assert!(matches!(p.made.get(), Some(None)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn pending_pipeline_is_recorded_for_the_next_launch() {
        let mut p = Pending::new(Vec::new(), None);
        p.key = "pending-pipeline-test".to_owned();
        // Simulate a worker that has taken the job but cannot finish it yet.
        p.queue_state.store(MAKING, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let p = Arc::new(p);

        assert!(!super::super::library::wanted_early(&p.key));
        assert!(ready(&p).is_none());
        assert!(p.made.get().is_none());
        assert!(super::super::library::wanted_early(&p.key));
    }

    #[test]
    fn draws_promote_early_pipelines_without_claiming_them_twice() {
        let earlier = Arc::new(Pending::new(Vec::new(), None));
        let promoted = Arc::new(Pending::new(Vec::new(), None));
        let requested = Arc::new(Pending::new(Vec::new(), None));
        let mut queue = Queue::new();

        assert_eq!(queue.push(&earlier, EARLY), Some(true));
        assert_eq!(queue.push(&promoted, EARLY), Some(true));
        assert_eq!(queue.push(&requested, REQUESTED), Some(true));
        assert_eq!(queue.push(&promoted, REQUESTED), Some(false));
        assert_eq!(queue.push(&promoted, REQUESTED), None);

        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(&queue.pop().unwrap(), &requested));
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(&queue.pop().unwrap(), &promoted));
        assert_eq!(queue.push(&promoted, REQUESTED), None);
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(&queue.pop().unwrap(), &earlier));
        assert!(queue.pop().is_none());
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/plaincopy.rs`:

```rs
//! Copies of title memory made in place, by this process, with a way back
//! when a page is not there (`VICTORY_COPY_PLAIN=1`; off by default).
//!
//! Every copy of title memory into a host buffer goes through the kernel
//! (`ReadProcessMemory` on our own process, `crate::host::copy_mapped`):
//! the title unmaps and remaps its memory while we read it, a read in
//! place of a page that is gone is an access violation, and the kernel's
//! copy fails instead. It costs what a system call that locks and probes
//! every page costs: run 225's profile has the submitting thread 35 ms a
//! frame inside `ZwReadVirtualMemory` for about 100 MB (3 GB a second),
//! where the processor's own copy moves that much in a third of the time.
//!
//! Here the copy is one `rep movsb` in a function of ours that uses no
//! stack. An exception handler, first in the line, looks at every access
//! violation: one that is a READ and happened at exactly that instruction
//! continues at the function's other exit, which returns 0, and the
//! caller falls back to the kernel's copy as before (it says which page
//! is gone and fills in zeros). A write that faults is not ours to take:
//! the destination is host memory, which is always there; such a fault
//! goes on to the handlers after this one.

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering::Relaxed};

#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".globl victory_copy_guarded",
    ".globl victory_copy_guarded_at",
    ".globl victory_copy_guarded_fault",
    "victory_copy_guarded:",
    // rcx: to, rdx: from, r8: bytes. rsi and rdi are the caller's: kept in
    // r9 and r10, which are ours to use, so nothing is on the stack.
    "    mov r9, rsi",
    "    mov r10, rdi",
    "    mov rdi, rcx",
    "    mov rsi, rdx",
    "    mov rcx, r8",
    "victory_copy_guarded_at:",
    "    rep movsb",
    "    mov rsi, r9",
    "    mov rdi, r10",
    "    mov eax, 1",
    "    ret",
    "victory_copy_guarded_fault:",
    "    mov rsi, r9",
    "    mov rdi, r10",
    "    xor eax, eax",
    "    ret",
);

#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
unsafe extern "C" {
    fn victory_copy_guarded(to: *mut u8, from: *const u8, len: usize) -> u32;
    static victory_copy_guarded_at: u8;
    static victory_copy_guarded_fault: u8;
}

/// Whether copies of title memory into host memory are made in place
/// (`VICTORY_COPY_PLAIN=1`).
pub(crate) fn on() -> bool {
    static ON: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| {
        let on = cfg!(target_arch = "x86_64") && std::env::var_os("VICTORY_COPY_PLAIN").is_some_and(|v| v == "1");
        if on {
            install();
            tracing::info!(
                "copies of title memory into host buffers are made in place, with the kernel's copy behind them for a \
                 page that is not there (VICTORY_COPY_PLAIN=1)"
            );
        }
        on
    })
}

/// Copies made in place, their bytes, the copies that met a page that was
/// not there (and went to the kernel's copy), and the copies not tried in
/// place because their source faulted lately ([`RECENT`]) or they were
/// under [`LEAST`] bytes, since the last line.
static COUNT: [AtomicU64; 5] = [const { AtomicU64::new(0) }; 5];

/// The fewest bytes copied in place. A read of a byte or a word is how the
/// layer ASKS whether a page is there (a texture's first page, a record):
/// it is expected to fail, and a failed kernel read costs a microsecond
/// where a fault and its handler cost tens (run 230: 1,000 to 1,300 faults
/// a frame, nearly all of them such askings, took back most of what the
/// copies in place had won).
const LEAST: usize = 256;

/// The 64 KiB blocks of title memory a copy in place faulted in lately:
/// their copies go straight to the kernel's, which reads round the hole.
/// By the block's number, in the place its low bits name (a later block
/// with the same low bits takes the place). Forgotten every two seconds:
/// the title maps the memory in the end.
static RECENT: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize; 1024] = [const { std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0) }; 1024];
/// When [`RECENT`] was last emptied (milliseconds of [`now_ms`]).
static EMPTIED: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);

fn now_ms() -> u64 {
    static START: std::sync::OnceLock<std::time::Instant> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    START.get_or_init(std::time::Instant::now).elapsed().as_millis() as u64
}

/// The numbers of the first and last 64 KiB block of `[from, from + len)`,
/// never 0 (0 is an empty place).
fn blocks(from: usize, len: usize) -> (usize, usize) {
    ((from >> 16) | 1 << 63, ((from + len.max(1) - 1) >> 16) | 1 << 63)
}

/// Whether a copy from there faulted lately.
fn faulted_lately(from: usize, len: usize) -> bool {
    let now = now_ms();
    let emptied = EMPTIED.load(Relaxed);
    if now.saturating_sub(emptied) >= 2_000 && EMPTIED.compare_exchange(emptied, now, Relaxed, Relaxed).is_ok() {
        for place in &RECENT {
            place.store(0, Relaxed);
        }
        return false;
    }
    let (first, last) = blocks(from, len);
    RECENT[first & 1023].load(Relaxed) == first || RECENT[last & 1023].load(Relaxed) == last
}

/// A copy from there faulted.
fn note_fault(from: usize, len: usize) {
    let (first, last) = blocks(from, len);
    RECENT[first & 1023].store(first, Relaxed);
    RECENT[last & 1023].store(last, Relaxed);
}

/// The handler that turns a read fault inside [`guarded`] into its return
/// of false; put first in the line, once.
#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
fn install() {
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{
        EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION, EXCEPTION_GUARD_PAGE, EXCEPTION_IN_PAGE_ERROR,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::{
        AddVectoredExceptionHandler, EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION, EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH, EXCEPTION_POINTERS,
    };
    unsafe extern "system" fn on_fault(info: *mut EXCEPTION_POINTERS) -> i32 {
        // SAFETY: the system passes the exception being dispatched and the
        // context it will continue with.
        let (r, context) = unsafe { (&*(*info).ExceptionRecord, &mut *(*info).ContextRecord) };
        // Only at the copy's own instruction.
        if context.Rip != (&raw const victory_copy_guarded_at) as u64 {
            return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
        }
        const READ: usize = 0;
        let read = r.NumberParameters >= 1 && r.ExceptionInformation[0] == READ;
        let gone = (r.ExceptionCode == EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION || r.ExceptionCode == EXCEPTION_IN_PAGE_ERROR) && read;
        if gone || r.ExceptionCode == EXCEPTION_GUARD_PAGE {
            context.Rip = (&raw const victory_copy_guarded_fault) as u64;
            return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION;
        }
        EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH
    }
    static ONCE: std::sync::Once = std::sync::Once::new();
    // SAFETY: a handler that reads the record it is given and nothing else.
    ONCE.call_once(|| unsafe {
        AddVectoredExceptionHandler(1, Some(on_fault));
    });
}

#[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
fn install() {}

/// Copies `len` bytes from `from` to `to` in place; false if a page of the
/// source was not there (then some of `to` may have been written).
///
/// `to` must be writable memory of `len` bytes that is ours (host memory);
/// `from` may be anything.
#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
fn guarded(to: *mut u8, from: *const u8, len: usize) -> bool {
    install();
    // SAFETY: the destination is the caller's to write; a source page that
    // is not there ends the copy with 0 instead of a fault ([`install`]).
    unsafe { victory_copy_guarded(to, from, len) != 0 }
}

#[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
fn guarded(_: *mut u8, _: *const u8, _: usize) -> bool {
    false
}

/// With [`on`]: copies title memory at `from` into host memory at `to`;
/// false if it is off or a source page was not there (the caller then
/// copies through the kernel, as before).
pub(crate) fn copy(to: *mut u8, from: *const u8, len: usize) -> bool {
    if !on() {
        return false;
    }
    if len < LEAST {
        COUNT[4].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
        return false;
    }
    if faulted_lately(from as usize, len) {
        COUNT[3].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
        return false;
    }
    let whole = guarded(to, from, len);
    if whole {
        COUNT[0].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
        COUNT[1].fetch_add(len as u64, Relaxed);
    } else {
        COUNT[2].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
        note_fault(from as usize, len);
    }
    whole
}

/// With the frame line: what [`copy`] did per frame over `frames`.
pub(crate) fn line(frames: f64) {
    if !on() {
        return;
    }
    let [copies, bytes, gone, lately, small] = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4].map(|i| COUNT[i].swap(0, Relaxed) as f64 / frames);
    tracing::info!(
        "copies of title memory made in place per frame (VICTORY_COPY_PLAIN=1): {copies:.0}, {:.1} MB; {gone:.1} met a page \
         that was not there and went through the kernel's copy; left to the kernel's copy untried: {lately:.0} whose source \
         faulted in the last two seconds, {small:.0} of under {LEAST} bytes",
        bytes / 1e6
    );
}

#[cfg(all(test, target_arch = "x86_64"))]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
        MEM_COMMIT, MEM_RELEASE, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_NOACCESS, PAGE_READWRITE, VirtualAlloc, VirtualFree,
    };

    const PAGE: usize = 4096;

    #[test]
    fn memory_that_is_there_is_copied() {
        let from: Vec<u8> = (0..100_000u32).map(|i| (i * 7 + 3) as u8).collect();
        let mut to = vec![0u8; from.len()];
        assert!(guarded(to.as_mut_ptr(), from.as_ptr(), from.len()));
        assert_eq!(to, from);
        // Nothing to copy is a copy.
        assert!(guarded(to.as_mut_ptr(), from.as_ptr(), 0));
    }

    /// Three pages reserved, the first committed: a copy that stays in the
    /// first page is whole; one that runs into the second ends with false,
    /// the bytes before the hole copied, and the thread goes on.
    #[test]
    fn a_page_that_is_not_there_ends_the_copy_without_a_fault() {
        // SAFETY: memory of the test's own.
        let base = unsafe { VirtualAlloc(std::ptr::null(), 3 * PAGE, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_NOACCESS) } as *mut u8;
        assert!(!base.is_null());
        // SAFETY: the first page of that reservation.
        assert!(!unsafe { VirtualAlloc(base.cast(), PAGE, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE) }.is_null());
        // SAFETY: committed and writable.
        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(base, PAGE) }.fill(0xAB);
        let mut to = vec![0u8; 2 * PAGE];
        assert!(guarded(to.as_mut_ptr(), base, PAGE));
        assert!(to[..PAGE].iter().all(|&b| b == 0xAB));
        to.fill(0);
        assert!(!guarded(to.as_mut_ptr(), base.wrapping_add(PAGE / 2), PAGE));
        assert!(to[..PAGE / 2].iter().all(|&b| b == 0xAB), "the bytes before the hole");
        assert!(to[PAGE / 2..].iter().all(|&b| b == 0), "nothing after it");
        // A source that is not there at all.
        assert!(!guarded(to.as_mut_ptr(), base.wrapping_add(PAGE), PAGE));
        // Committed but closed to reads.
        // SAFETY: the third page of the reservation.
        assert!(!unsafe { VirtualAlloc(base.wrapping_add(2 * PAGE).cast(), PAGE, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_NOACCESS) }.is_null());
        assert!(!guarded(to.as_mut_ptr(), base.wrapping_add(2 * PAGE), 16));
        // And the registers the caller owns came back: this still works.
        assert!(guarded(to.as_mut_ptr(), base, PAGE));
        assert!(to[..PAGE].iter().all(|&b| b == 0xAB));
        // SAFETY: the test's reservation.
        unsafe { VirtualFree(base.cast(), 0, MEM_RELEASE) };
    }

    /// A source that faulted is remembered by its 64 KiB blocks, and only
    /// those.
    #[test]
    fn a_source_that_faulted_is_remembered_by_its_blocks() {
        // (Addresses no other test uses; the table is shared.)
        let at = 0x7654_3210_0000usize;
        assert!(!faulted_lately(at, 4096));
        note_fault(at + 100, 4096);
        assert!(faulted_lately(at, 16));
        assert!(faulted_lately(at + 0xffff, 1));
        // A copy that ends in the block, and one that begins in it.
        assert!(faulted_lately(at - 4096, 8192));
        // The blocks beside it are not remembered.
        assert!(!faulted_lately(at + 0x10000, 4096));
        assert!(!faulted_lately(at - 0x10000, 4096));
        assert_eq!(blocks(0, 0), (1 << 63, 1 << 63));
    }

    /// Many threads at once, half of them faulting: each gets its own answer.
    #[test]
    fn threads_fault_and_copy_side_by_side() {
        // SAFETY: memory of the test's own.
        let base = unsafe { VirtualAlloc(std::ptr::null(), 2 * PAGE, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_NOACCESS) } as usize;
        assert_ne!(base, 0);
        // SAFETY: the first page of that reservation.
        assert!(!unsafe { VirtualAlloc(base as *const _, PAGE, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE) }.is_null());
        let threads: Vec<_> = (0..8)
            .map(|t| {
                std::thread::spawn(move || {
                    let mut to = vec![0u8; PAGE];
                    for _ in 0..2_000 {
                        let from = (base + if t % 2 == 0 { 0 } else { PAGE }) as *const u8;
                        assert_eq!(guarded(to.as_mut_ptr(), from, PAGE), t % 2 == 0);
                    }
                })
            })
            .collect();
        for t in threads {
            t.join().unwrap();
        }
        // SAFETY: the test's reservation.
        unsafe { VirtualFree(base as *mut _, 0, MEM_RELEASE) };
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/primitive.rs`:

```rs
//! Console primitive types the host lacks. A rectangle list gives three
//! corners per rectangle, the second the one between the other two, and
//! the hardware adds the fourth at `v0 + v2 - v1` (the title's
//! full-screen rectangles come as top left, bottom left, bottom right); on
//! the host each rectangle becomes two triangles, with the fourth vertex
//! made from the other three on the CPU.
//!
//! shortcut: the fourth vertex is computed from vertex inputs, not from
//! vertex shader outputs as the hardware does; that is the same for vertex
//! shaders linear in their inputs (blits, 2D quads). Inputs in formats
//! [`components`] does not know keep the first vertex's value, and so do
//! components past the end of the vertex (an element that reaches into the
//! next one, which the layout allows).
//!
//! A pipeline the title makes for rectangles completes them on the GPU
//! instead, in a geometry stage (`victory_shader::emit::rect_list_gs`):
//! from the vertex shader's outputs, whichever vertex the corner is, for
//! direct, indexed and indirect draws alike. This expansion is what is
//! left for a pipeline that could not get that stage.

/// Expands `rects` rectangles of `stride`-byte vertices from `src` into six
/// vertices each in `dst`: `(v0, v1, v2)` and `(v0, v2, v3)`, so both
/// triangles turn the same way. `elements` are (byte offset, format).
pub(crate) fn expand_rects(src: &[u8], dst: &mut [u8], stride: usize, elements: &[(u32, u32)]) {
    for (rect, out) in src
        .chunks_exact(3 * stride)
        .zip(dst.chunks_exact_mut(6 * stride))
    {
        let v = |i: usize| &rect[i * stride..(i + 1) * stride];
        for (slot, i) in [0, 1, 2, 0, 2].into_iter().enumerate() {
            out[slot * stride..(slot + 1) * stride].copy_from_slice(v(i));
        }
        let fourth = &mut out[5 * stride..];
        fourth.copy_from_slice(v(0));
        for &(offset, format) in elements {
            let at = offset as usize;
            let Some((n, kind)) = components(format) else {
                continue;
            };
            // Only the components inside the vertex: the rest belong to the
            // next one.
            let inside = stride.saturating_sub(at) / kind.bytes();
            for c in 0..n.min(inside) {
                let get = |i: usize| kind.read(&v(i)[at..], c);
                let value = get(0) + get(2) - get(1);
                kind.write(&mut fourth[at..], c, value);
            }
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Kind {
    F32,
    F16,
    Unorm8,
    Unorm16,
}

/// Component count and kind of the vertex formats rectangles use.
fn components(format: u32) -> Option<(usize, Kind)> {
    Some(match format {
        2 => (4, Kind::F32),
        6 => (3, Kind::F32),
        16 => (2, Kind::F32),
        41 => (1, Kind::F32),
        10 => (4, Kind::F16),
        34 => (2, Kind::F16),
        54 => (1, Kind::F16),
        11 => (4, Kind::Unorm16),
        35 => (2, Kind::Unorm16),
        28 | 29 | 87 | 91 => (4, Kind::Unorm8),
        _ => return None,
    })
}

impl Kind {
    fn bytes(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Kind::F32 => 4,
            Kind::F16 | Kind::Unorm16 => 2,
            Kind::Unorm8 => 1,
        }
    }

    fn read(self, at: &[u8], c: usize) -> f32 {
        let b = &at[c * self.bytes()..];
        match self {
            Kind::F32 => f32::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]]),
            Kind::F16 => half_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1]])),
            Kind::Unorm16 => f32::from(u16::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1]])) / 65535.0,
            Kind::Unorm8 => f32::from(b[0]) / 255.0,
        }
    }

    fn write(self, at: &mut [u8], c: usize, v: f32) {
        let n = self.bytes();
        let b = &mut at[c * n..(c + 1) * n];
        match self {
            Kind::F32 => b.copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes()),
            Kind::F16 => b.copy_from_slice(&f32_to_half(v).to_le_bytes()),
            Kind::Unorm16 => {
                b.copy_from_slice(&((v.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 65535.0).round() as u16).to_le_bytes())
            }
            Kind::Unorm8 => b[0] = (v.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 255.0).round() as u8,
        }
    }
}

fn half_to_f32(h: u16) -> f32 {
    let sign = u32::from(h >> 15) << 31;
    let exp = u32::from((h >> 10) & 0x1f);
    let man = u32::from(h & 0x3ff);
    let bits = match (exp, man) {
        (0, 0) => sign,
        // Subnormal: scale the mantissa.
        (0, m) => {
            let v = m as f32 * 2f32.powi(-24);
            return if sign != 0 { -v } else { v };
        }
        (31, m) => sign | 0x7f80_0000 | m << 13,
        (e, m) => sign | (e + 112) << 23 | m << 13,
    };
    f32::from_bits(bits)
}

fn f32_to_half(v: f32) -> u16 {
    let bits = v.to_bits();
    let sign = ((bits >> 16) & 0x8000) as u16;
    let exp = ((bits >> 23) & 0xff) as i32 - 127 + 15;
    let man = bits & 0x7f_ffff;
    if exp >= 31 {
        return sign | 0x7c00; // too large: infinity
    }
    if exp <= 0 {
        if exp < -10 {
            return sign; // below half the smallest subnormal: zero
        }
        // Half subnormals are `m * 2^-24`. An f32 in this range is still
        // normal (exponent field >= 1), so its significand has the implicit
        // leading 1; shift it into the half mantissa, rounding to even.
        let sig = (1u32 << 23) | man;
        let shift = (14 - exp) as u32;
        let halfway = 1u32 << (shift - 1);
        let q = sig >> shift;
        let r = sig & ((1u32 << shift) - 1);
        let m = q + u32::from(r > halfway || (r == halfway && (q & 1) != 0));
        return sign | m as u16;
    }
    // Rounded to nearest: a carry out of the mantissa is added into the
    // exponent (`2 - 2^-12` is 2.0); at most it reaches infinity, 0x7c00.
    let half = (exp as u32) << 10;
    sign | (half + ((man + 0x1000) >> 13)) as u16
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A rectangle of float2 positions and RGBA8 colors, given as top
    /// left, bottom left, bottom right: the fourth corner completes the
    /// parallelogram at the top right.
    #[test]
    fn rectangles_get_their_fourth_corner() {
        let vertex = |x: f32, y: f32, r: u8| {
            let mut v = Vec::new();
            v.extend(x.to_le_bytes());
            v.extend(y.to_le_bytes());
            v.extend([r, 0, 0, 255]);
            v
        };
        let src: Vec<u8> = [
            vertex(-1.0, 1.0, 0),
            vertex(-1.0, -1.0, 100),
            vertex(1.0, -1.0, 150),
        ]
        .concat();
        let mut dst = vec![0u8; 6 * 12];
        expand_rects(&src, &mut dst, 12, &[(0, 16), (8, 28)]);
        assert_eq!(dst[..36], src[..]);
        assert_eq!(dst[36..48], src[..12]);
        assert_eq!(dst[48..60], src[24..36]);
        assert_eq!(dst[60..], vertex(1.0, 1.0, 50)[..]);
        assert_eq!(f32_to_half(1.5), 0x3e00);
        assert_eq!(half_to_f32(0x3e00), 1.5);
        assert_eq!(half_to_f32(0xc000), -2.0);
    }

    /// A rounding that carries out of the mantissa raises the exponent
    /// (the carry used to be or-ed into an odd exponent, halving the value).
    #[test]
    fn halves_round_up_into_the_next_power_of_two() {
        assert_eq!(f32_to_half(2.0 - 2f32.powi(-12)), 0x4000);
        assert_eq!(f32_to_half(0.5 - 2f32.powi(-13)), 0x3800);
        assert_eq!(f32_to_half(65520.0), 0x7c00, "past the largest half");
        // An R16_FLOAT element at 1.0, 2^-12 and 1.0: the fourth corner is
        // 2 - 2^-12, which rounds to 2.0.
        let src: Vec<u8> = [0x3c00_u16, 0x0c00, 0x3c00]
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|h| h.to_le_bytes())
            .collect();
        let mut dst = vec![0u8; 6 * 2];
        expand_rects(&src, &mut dst, 2, &[(0, 54)]);
        assert_eq!(dst[10..], 0x4000_u16.to_le_bytes());
    }

    /// An element that reaches past the stride (float4 at 4 in 8-byte
    /// vertices, RGBA8 at the stride itself): the components inside get
    /// the fourth corner, the rest keep the first vertex's bytes. The old
    /// code indexed past the vertex and panicked.
    #[test]
    fn elements_past_the_stride_are_left_alone() {
        let vertex = |x: f32, y: f32| [x.to_le_bytes(), y.to_le_bytes()].concat();
        let src = [vertex(0.0, 2.0), vertex(1.0, 3.0), vertex(5.0, 7.0)].concat();
        let mut dst = vec![0u8; 6 * 8];
        expand_rects(&src, &mut dst, 8, &[(0, 16), (4, 2), (8, 28)]);
        assert_eq!(dst[..40], [&src[..], &src[..8], &src[16..]].concat()[..]);
        assert_eq!(dst[40..], vertex(4.0, 6.0)[..]);
    }

    /// `half_to_f32` reads subnormals, so an f16 rectangle output must be
    /// able to write them back instead of flushing every one to zero.
    #[test]
    fn half_subnormals_convert_in_both_directions() {
        assert_eq!(f32_to_half(2f32.powi(-24)), 0x0001);
        assert_eq!(f32_to_half(-2f32.powi(-24)), 0x8001);
        assert_eq!(f32_to_half(2f32.powi(-23)), 0x0002);
        assert_eq!(f32_to_half(1023.0 * 2f32.powi(-24)), 0x03ff);
        // Ties go to an even mantissa: 0/1 and 1/2.
        assert_eq!(f32_to_half(2f32.powi(-25)), 0x0000);
        assert_eq!(f32_to_half(3.0 * 2f32.powi(-25)), 0x0002);
        // Below half the smallest subnormal, and normal values, are unchanged.
        assert_eq!(f32_to_half(2f32.powi(-26)), 0x0000);
        assert_eq!(f32_to_half(1.5), 0x3e00);
        assert_eq!(half_to_f32(0x0001), 2f32.powi(-24));
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/profile.rs`:

```rs
//! Where the layer's threads spend their time: a sampling profiler
//! (`VICTORY_PROFILE=1`, diagnostics builds; off otherwise).
//!
//! The log's own counters say how long the phases of a frame take, not
//! what a thread does inside them: in the graphics driver, in a kernel
//! call, waiting for a lock. A thread of ours ([`run`]) looks, a thousand
//! times a second (`VICTORY_PROFILE_HZ`), at the threads that matter:
//!
//! * the submitting thread and the recording threads, which name
//!   themselves by what they call ([`seen`]: [`crate::host::Host`]'s
//!   submissions, the list calls);
//! * our workers, by the names we start them with (`victory-pipelines-N`,
//!   `victory-wide-N`, `victory-late-wait`) and the title's main thread;
//! * the busiest of the other threads (the title's own).
//!
//! A look ([`Sampler::capture`]) suspends the thread, reads its registers
//! and copies the used part of its stack with the kernel's own read, and
//! lets it go: between the two nothing of ours takes a lock, allocates or
//! reads memory that may be gone. The stack is walked afterwards, in the
//! copy ([`Sampler::walk`]), by each image's unwind data (the Windows
//! loader registered it for title images too), every read checked to stay
//! inside the copy. A thread that has used no processor cycles since the
//! last look is where it was: it is not suspended again.
//!
//! Names are found when the report is written, not when a sample is
//! taken ([`Symbols`]): our executable through its PDB (inlined calls
//! too), system and driver code by export or `module+offset`, title code
//! as `title+offset` of the function's start.
//!
//! The report is written every `VICTORY_PROFILE_EVERY` seconds (30) and at
//! exit to `VICTORY_PROFILE_OUT` (`%TEMP%\victory_profile_<pid>.txt`), the
//! stacks for a flame graph beside it (`.folded`). Per kind of thread:
//! time by module, by function (own and with what it calls), where it
//! waited and for which of our functions, the hottest lines of ours. Times
//! are milliseconds per presented frame ([`frame`]).

use std::cell::Cell;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::fmt::Write as _;
use std::hash::{BuildHasherDefault, Hasher};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::ptr::{null, null_mut};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU8, AtomicU32, AtomicU64, Ordering::Relaxed};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{
    CloseHandle, DUPLICATE_SAME_ACCESS, DuplicateHandle, HANDLE, HMODULE, LocalFree,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::{
    CONTEXT, CONTEXT_CONTROL_AMD64, CONTEXT_INTEGER_AMD64, GetThreadContext, IMAGEHLP_LINEW64,
    IMAGEHLP_MODULEW64, ReadProcessMemory, RtlLookupFunctionEntry, RtlVirtualUnwind, SYMBOL_INFOW,
    UNW_FLAG_NHANDLER,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::{
    GetModuleFileNameW, GetModuleHandleW, GetProcAddress, LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32,
    LoadLibraryExA,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{MEM_COMMIT, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE, VirtualAlloc};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::ProcessStatus::{
    K32EnumProcessModules, K32GetModuleInformation, MODULEINFO,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
    GetCurrentProcess, GetCurrentThread, GetCurrentThreadId, GetThreadDescription, GetThreadId,
    GetThreadTimes, OpenThread, ResumeThread, SetThreadPriority, SuspendThread, THREAD_GET_CONTEXT,
    THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL, THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION, THREAD_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION,
    THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME, WaitForSingleObject,
};

#[link(name = "kernel32", kind = "raw-dylib")]
unsafe extern "system" {
    /// The processor cycles a thread has used so far.
    fn QueryThreadCycleTime(thread: HANDLE, cycles: *mut u64) -> i32;
}

#[link(name = "ntdll", kind = "raw-dylib")]

    /// with `access`; an NTSTATUS, not zero after the last.
    fn NtGetNextThread(
        process: HANDLE,
        thread: HANDLE,

    fn NtQueryInformationThread(
        thread: HANDLE,
        class: i32,
```
