`crates/victory-gpu/src/shot.rs`:

```rs
//! Diagnostics: one frame taken apart, by the layer itself ("frame shot").
//!
//! A frame debugger from outside (RenderDoc) wraps the host device and
//! hooks the process: run 263 ended ten seconds in, inside the hook of a
//! streaming program's game capture on that wrapped device, and the driver
//! refused the pipeline library made for the real one. Nothing of that
//! kind happens here: no library is loaded, the device is the one every run
//! uses, and the only commands added are the two kinds the layer records in
//! every run already (a copy of a texture into a read-back buffer, as the
//! saved pictures are made, and a timestamp, as the card meter's).
//!
//! `VICTORY_SHOT=<folder>` switches it on. A shot is taken of the frame
//! after a present at which
//!  * the file `take` is found in that folder (it is removed; the script
//!    `shot.ps1` makes it), or
//!  * the frame is one of `VICTORY_SHOT_AT` (comma-separated, counted from
//!    the first frame of 500 draws or more, as `VICTORY_RENDERDOC_AT`).
//!
//! Of that frame the shot keeps, in `<folder>\shot-<frame>-<hhmmss>` (the
//! time of day it began, UTC):
//!  * `events.txt`: every draw, dispatch, copy, submission and drop in the
//!    order recorded, with the list it was recorded into, the thread, and
//!    the place of its timestamp (the lines of `capture::op`: shaders,
//!    targets, states, what is read);
//!  * `stamps.txt`: the card's clock before each of those commands, so the
//!    time to the next one in the same list is that command's;
//!  * `snap-*.png`: what a texture held where it left a state shaders
//!    write in (render target, depth write, unordered access): the picture
//!    a pass left. The title gives its textures' states in a form without
//!    states (enhanced barriers), so the layer moves every texture itself,
//!    and that is where the copies are made: inside a list
//!    (`HostList::transition`) and between lists, in the list that runs
//!    before each one (`HostList::prelude`). `snaps.txt` lists them;
//!  * `info.txt`, and `done` when everything is written.
//!
//! **Pictures come in parts.** With the title running the PC has one to
//! four gigabytes free (run 269: 3.6 GB in the opening cutscene, 0.9 GB in
//! the first room), and a frame's targets are more than that. A place
//! where a picture can be taken is named by its texture and how many
//! times the texture left a written state before in the frame: the same
//! name in every frame that is built the same way. The shot's own frame
//! takes as many as fit in half of the memory that is free above 0.7 GB
//! (`VICTORY_SHOT_MB` at most, 1024 unless said); when they are written and
//! their buffers gone, a later frame takes the ones still missing, and so
//! on until none is, or a frame gets none. The lines and times are all of
//! the first frame, and are taken even when there is no room for any
//! picture; a picture says which frame it is of.
//!
//! The pictures are read two seconds and eight frames after their frame
//! (every list of it has long run) and written by a thread of their own on
//! the slow cores. Multisampled textures and volumes are not copied; of an
//! array the first six slices' first level; a texture at most eight times
//! a frame; at most `VICTORY_SHOT_MAX` (12) shots a run.

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU8, AtomicU32, AtomicU64, Ordering::Relaxed};
use std::sync::{Mutex, OnceLock};

use windows::Win32::Graphics::Direct3D12::*;
use windows::Win32::Graphics::Dxgi::Common::DXGI_SAMPLE_DESC;

const IDLE: u8 = 0;
const RECORDING: u8 = 1;
const PENDING: u8 = 2;
const SAVING: u8 = 3;
static PHASE: AtomicU8 = AtomicU8::new(IDLE);
/// Whether the frame being recorded keeps its lines and times (a shot's
/// first frame; the later ones only take pictures).
static LINES: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

/// Which frame of which shot is being taken (1, 2, ...): what a list holds
/// for a shot belongs to one.
static SHOT_ID: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);

/// Timestamps of a shot, and how many a list takes at a time.
const SLOTS: u32 = 131_072;
const BLOCK: u32 = 128;
/// The next free timestamp of the shot being taken.
static NEXT: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);

/// Lines a shot holds at most.
const MAX_EVENTS: usize = 400_000;
/// Copies of one texture in a frame.
const REPEATS: u32 = 8;
/// Frames a shot takes its pictures in, at most.
const MAX_PARTS: u32 = 48;
/// When this many lists recorded for a shot's frame have been submitted,
/// the frame is the title's to finish: lists begun from then on are the
/// next frame's (the title records it while the layer still runs this
/// one: run 269's first shot held frame 0x781 and, behind its submissions,
/// all of 0x782), and the present that follows ends the shot's frame. A
/// present before that is of a frame recorded before the shot began, and
/// the shot goes on through it, three presents at most.
const FRAME_LISTS: u32 = 20;
/// Lists of the frame being recorded that the title has submitted.
static SUBMITTED: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);

/// Whether the title has begun to submit the frame being recorded.
fn closing() -> bool {
    SUBMITTED.load(Relaxed) >= FRAME_LISTS
}

/// The title submits `list`, while a shot records.
pub(crate) fn submitted(list: &crate::host::HostList) {
    let mark = *list.shot_mark.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    if mark.0 != 0 && mark.0 == SHOT_ID.load(Relaxed) {
        SUBMITTED.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
    }
}
/// Memory left alone (MB), and the least a frame's pictures need.
const RESERVE_MB: u64 = 700;
const LEAST_MB: u64 = 48;
/// The host state copies are read in.
const COPY_SOURCE: u32 = 0x800;

/// The folder shots go to, if the tool is on.
fn folder() -> Option<&'static PathBuf> {
    static FOLDER: OnceLock<Option<PathBuf>> = OnceLock::new();
    FOLDER
        .get_or_init(|| {
            let folder = PathBuf::from(std::env::var_os("VICTORY_SHOT")?);
            if !folder.is_absolute() {
                tracing::warn!(folder = %folder.display(), "VICTORY_SHOT is not a full path: no frame shots");
                return None;
            }
            if let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(&folder) {
                tracing::warn!(error = %e, folder = %folder.display(), "the folder for frame shots could not be made: none are taken");
                return None;
            }
            tracing::info!(
                folder = %folder.display(),
                at = ?at(),
                "frame shots are on (VICTORY_SHOT): one is taken when the file `take` appears in the folder, and at the frames of VICTORY_SHOT_AT"
            );
            Some(folder)
        })
        .as_ref()
}

fn number(name: &str, default: u64) -> u64 {
    std::env::var(name).ok().and_then(|v| v.trim().parse().ok()).unwrap_or(default)
}

/// `VICTORY_SHOT_AT`: frames counted from the first one of 500 draws.
fn at() -> &'static [u64] {
    static AT: OnceLock<Vec<u64>> = OnceLock::new();
    AT.get_or_init(|| {
        std::env::var("VICTORY_SHOT_AT").unwrap_or_default().split(',').filter_map(|f| f.trim().parse().ok()).collect()
    })
}

/// The read-back memory (MB) a frame of a shot may take now.
fn room_mb() -> u64 {
    (crate::framelog::free_mb().saturating_sub(RESERVE_MB) / 2).min(number("VICTORY_SHOT_MB", 1024))
}

/// A line of the shot.
struct Event {
    list: usize,
    thread: u32,
    /// The place of the timestamp recorded before the command, or none.
    stamp: u32,
    text: String,
}

/// A picture of the shot, still in its read-back buffer.
struct Snap {
    /// How many times its texture left a written state before in the
    /// frame.
    occurrence: u32,
    name: String,
    buffer: ID3D12Resource,
    footprint: D3D12_SUBRESOURCE_FOOTPRINT,
    bytes: u64,
    /// The title's texture (or, unknown, the host copy), its own size and
    /// format, the slice copied, and the states it left and went to.
    texture: usize,
    width: u64,
    height: u32,
    format: i32,
    slice: u32,
    before: u32,
    after: u32,
}

/// What a shot carries from one of its frames to the next.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct Carry {
    /// The shot's first frame (its folder's name) and why it was taken.
    first: u64,
    why: String,
    /// The time of day (UTC, `hhmmss`) the shot began: the rest of its
    /// folder's name. (Two runs' shots of the same frame number went into
    /// one folder: runs 270 and 273, `shot-1864`.)
    began: u32,
    /// Frames taken so far; pictures saved and failed in them.
    parts: u32,
    saved: u32,
    failed: u32,
    /// The places done: host copy, occurrence, slice.
    done: std::collections::HashSet<(usize, u32, u32)>,
    /// Of the first frame: lines, draws and dispatches, presents, places.
    lines: usize,
    work: u32,
    presents: u32,
    places: u32,
    not_taken: u32,
    read_back_mb: u64,
}

impl Carry {
    /// `shot-<first frame>-<hhmmss>`.
    fn folder_name(&self) -> String {
        format!("shot-{}-{:06}", self.first, self.began)
    }
}

/// The time of day now, UTC, as the number `hhmmss`.
fn hhmmss() -> u32 {
    let s = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map_or(0, |d| d.as_secs() % 86_400) as u32;
    (s / 3600) * 10_000 + (s / 60 % 60) * 100 + s % 60
}

struct Shot {
    id: u32,
    /// The frame this part is of.
    frame: u64,
    carry: Carry,
    presents: u32,
    /// Draws and dispatches among its lines.
    work: u32,
    events: Vec<Event>,
    snaps: Vec<Snap>,
    /// Read-back bytes so far, and the most allowed.
    bytes: u64,
    budget: u64,
    /// Places met so far in this frame; how many are left for a later
    /// frame; the ones never taken (repeats, too large).
    places: u32,
    later: u32,
    not_taken: u32,
    /// Times a texture (host copy) left a written state so far.
    per_texture: std::collections::HashMap<usize, u32>,
    /// The title's texture by host copy.
    titles: std::collections::HashMap<usize, usize>,
    /// The ranges of timestamps lists resolved: first place and count.
    resolved: Vec<(u32, u32)>,
    /// When recording ended, and the frame's number.
    stopped: Option<(std::time::Instant, u64)>,
}

// SAFETY: host objects (free-threaded), handed from the recording threads
// to the one that writes the shot out, behind a lock.
unsafe impl Send for Shot {}

static SHOT: Mutex<Option<Shot>> = Mutex::new(None);
/// A shot between two of its frames.
static WAITING: Mutex<Option<Carry>> = Mutex::new(None);

/// The timestamps' heap and where they are read back.
struct Clock {
    heap: ID3D12QueryHeap,
    back: ID3D12Resource,
    /// The read-back buffer's bytes, mapped for good.
    mapped: usize,
    frequency: u64,
}

// SAFETY: host objects (free-threaded) and a mapping that is only read.
unsafe impl Send for Clock {}
// SAFETY: as above.
unsafe impl Sync for Clock {}

static CLOCK: OnceLock<Option<Clock>> = OnceLock::new();

fn make_clock() -> Option<Clock> {
    if std::env::var_os("VICTORY_SHOT_TIMES").is_some_and(|v| v == "0") {
        return None;
    }
    let host = crate::host::host()?;
    let device = host.device();
    let mut heap: Option<ID3D12QueryHeap> = None;
    let mut back: Option<ID3D12Resource> = None;
    let readback = D3D12_HEAP_PROPERTIES { Type: D3D12_HEAP_TYPE_READBACK, ..Default::default() };
    let desc = D3D12_RESOURCE_DESC {
        Dimension: D3D12_RESOURCE_DIMENSION_BUFFER,
        Width: u64::from(SLOTS) * 8,
        Height: 1,
        DepthOrArraySize: 1,
        MipLevels: 1,
        SampleDesc: DXGI_SAMPLE_DESC { Count: 1, Quality: 0 },
        Layout: D3D12_TEXTURE_LAYOUT_ROW_MAJOR,
        ..Default::default()
    };
    // SAFETY: plain object creation; the buffer is mapped once and stays so
    // (the card meter's heap and buffer, made the same way).
    unsafe {
        device
            .CreateQueryHeap(&D3D12_QUERY_HEAP_DESC { Type: D3D12_QUERY_HEAP_TYPE_TIMESTAMP, Count: SLOTS, NodeMask: 0 }, &mut heap)
            .ok()?;
        device
            .CreateCommittedResource(&readback, D3D12_HEAP_FLAG_NONE, &desc, D3D12_RESOURCE_STATE_COPY_DEST, None, &mut back)
            .ok()?;
        let (heap, back) = (heap?, back?);
        let mut mapped = std::ptr::null_mut();
        back.Map(0, None, Some(&mut mapped)).ok()?;
        let frequency = host.timestamp_frequency();
        if mapped.is_null() || frequency == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        Some(Clock { heap, back, mapped: mapped as usize, frequency })
    }
}

/// Whether a frame is being recorded for a shot. One load: asked at every
/// state change of a texture in every diagnostics run.
pub(crate) fn recording() -> bool {
    PHASE.load(Relaxed) == RECORDING
}

/// Whether the frame being recorded keeps its lines ([`line`]). Asked at
/// every noted command of every diagnostics run.
pub(crate) fn keeping_lines() -> bool {
    recording() && LINES.load(Relaxed)
}

thread_local! {
    /// The timestamp [`stamp`] recorded for the line this thread is about
    /// to give to [`line`].
    static STAMP: std::cell::Cell<u32> = const { std::cell::Cell::new(u32::MAX) };
    /// The line this thread is about to give to [`line`] is of a list of
    /// the next frame ([`stamp`]): not kept.
    static NEXT_FRAME: std::cell::Cell<bool> = const { std::cell::Cell::new(false) };
}

/// A fresh block of timestamps, if any are left.
fn take_block() -> Option<u32> {
    let base = NEXT.fetch_add(BLOCK, Relaxed);
    (base <= SLOTS - BLOCK).then_some(base)
}

/// Resolves `count` timestamps from `base` in `list` and notes the range.
fn resolve(list: &ID3D12GraphicsCommandList, clock: &Clock, id: u32, base: u32, count: u32) {
    // SAFETY: an open list, our heap and our read-back buffer; the places
    // are the block's own, and each was ended in this list before.
    unsafe { list.ResolveQueryData(&clock.heap, D3D12_QUERY_TYPE_TIMESTAMP, base, count, &clock.back, u64::from(base) * 8) };
    let mut shot = SHOT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    if let Some(s) = shot.as_mut().filter(|s| s.id == id) {
        s.resolved.push((base, count));
    }
}

/// Before a command of the title is recorded into `list`, while a shot
/// records: the list is marked as one of the shot's frame, and in a frame
/// that keeps its lines the card's clock goes into the list here, for the
/// line that follows ([`line`]).
pub(crate) fn stamp(list: &crate::host::HostList) {
    if !recording() {
        return;
    }
    let id = SHOT_ID.load(Relaxed);
    {
        let mut mark = list.shot_mark.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if mark.0 != id {
            // A list begun after the frame's lists were submitted is the
            // next frame's.
            if closing() {
                NEXT_FRAME.set(true);
                return;
            }
            let lines = SHOT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).as_ref().map_or(0, |s| s.events.len());
            *mark = (id, lines as u32);
        }
    }
    if !LINES.load(Relaxed) {
        return;
    }
    let Some(Some(clock)) = CLOCK.get() else {
        return;
    };
    let mut block = list.shot_block.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    let (base, used, of) = *block;
    let end = |slot: u32| {
        // SAFETY: an open list and a place of our heap.
        unsafe { list.list.EndQuery(&clock.heap, D3D12_QUERY_TYPE_TIMESTAMP, slot) };
    };
    let slot = if used == 0 || of != id {
        let Some(base) = take_block() else { return };
        *block = (base, 1, id);
        base
    } else if used == BLOCK - 1 {
        // The block's last place ends it; the command opens the next.
        end(base + used);
        resolve(&list.list, clock, id, base, BLOCK);
        let Some(next) = take_block() else {
            *block = (0, 0, 0);
            return;
        };
        *block = (next, 1, id);
        next
    } else {
        *block = (base, used + 1, id);
        base + used
    };
    end(slot);
    STAMP.set(slot);
}

/// `list` is about to be closed: the block of timestamps it holds is ended
/// and resolved.
pub(crate) fn close(list: &crate::host::HostList) {
    let mut block = list.shot_block.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    let (base, used, of) = std::mem::take(&mut *block);
    if used == 0 || of != SHOT_ID.load(Relaxed) {
        return;
    }
    let Some(Some(clock)) = CLOCK.get() else {
        return;
    };
    // SAFETY: an open list and a place of our heap (a block always keeps
    // its last place for this).
    unsafe { list.list.EndQuery(&clock.heap, D3D12_QUERY_TYPE_TIMESTAMP, base + used) };
    resolve(&list.list, clock, of, base, used + 1);
}

/// A list of the layer's own (the one that runs before a title list, the
/// one that sends changed bytes to the card and hashes them, the one that
/// compares) begins in `cmd`, while a shot's first frame records: the
/// card's clock, for [`span_end`]. The title's commands are a part of the
/// card's frame; these are the rest of it.
pub(crate) fn span_begin(cmd: &ID3D12GraphicsCommandList) -> u32 {
    if !keeping_lines() {
        return u32::MAX;
    }
    let Some(Some(clock)) = CLOCK.get() else {
        return u32::MAX;
    };
    let slot = NEXT.fetch_add(2, Relaxed);
    if slot > SLOTS - 2 {
        return u32::MAX;
    }
    // SAFETY: an open list and a place of our heap.
    unsafe { cmd.EndQuery(&clock.heap, D3D12_QUERY_TYPE_TIMESTAMP, slot) };
    slot
}

/// The list [`span_begin`] timed ends here; `what` is its line, for the
/// title list `list` or none.
pub(crate) fn span_end(cmd: &ID3D12GraphicsCommandList, slot: u32, list: usize, what: impl FnOnce() -> String) {
    if slot == u32::MAX {
        return;
    }
    let Some(Some(clock)) = CLOCK.get() else {
        return;
    };
    // SAFETY: an open list, our heap and read-back buffer, the two places
    // `span_begin` took.
    unsafe {
        cmd.EndQuery(&clock.heap, D3D12_QUERY_TYPE_TIMESTAMP, slot + 1);
        cmd.ResolveQueryData(&clock.heap, D3D12_QUERY_TYPE_TIMESTAMP, slot, 2, &clock.back, u64::from(slot) * 8);
    }
    let mut shot = SHOT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    let Some(s) = shot.as_mut() else { return };
    if s.carry.parts != 0 || s.events.len() >= MAX_EVENTS {
        return;
    }
    s.resolved.push((slot, 2));
    // SAFETY: a plain query.
    let thread = unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentThreadId() };
    s.events.push(Event { list, thread, stamp: slot, text: what() });
}

/// A line of `capture::op`, while a shot's first frame records.
pub(crate) fn line(list: usize, text: &str) {
    let stamp = STAMP.replace(u32::MAX);
    if NEXT_FRAME.replace(false) {
        return;
    }
    let mut shot = SHOT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    let Some(s) = shot.as_mut() else { return };
    if s.stopped.is_some() || s.carry.parts != 0 || s.events.len() >= MAX_EVENTS {
        return;
    }
    if ["draw ", "indexed ", "mesh ", "indirect ", "dispatch "].iter().any(|k| text.starts_with(k)) {
        s.work += 1;
    }
    // SAFETY: a plain query.
    let thread = unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentThreadId() };
    s.events.push(Event { list, thread, stamp, text: text.to_owned() });
}

/// Whether pictures of host format `format` can be shown
/// (`capture::to_rgba`'s formats, by the texture's own format).
fn shows(format: i32) -> bool {
    matches!(format, 1..=2 | 9..=16 | 19..=65 | 87..=93)
}

/// `list` says which title texture a host copy is of, while a shot
/// records (pictures are named after the title's texture, as the lines
/// name targets).
pub(crate) fn known(copy: usize, title: usize) {
    let mut shot = SHOT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    if let Some(s) = shot.as_mut() {
        s.titles.insert(copy, title);
    }
}

/// Whether `list` was recorded in the frame of the shot being taken, and
/// if so the line its recording began at: for the list that runs before it
/// at submission ([`leaves`] there), which may be made after the frame's
/// present.
pub(crate) fn of_the_frame(list: &crate::host::HostList) -> Option<u32> {
    if !matches!(PHASE.load(Relaxed), RECORDING | PENDING) {
        return None;
    }
    let mark = *list.shot_mark.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    (mark.0 != 0 && mark.0 == SHOT_ID.load(Relaxed)).then_some(mark.1)
}

/// Whether a move from host state `before` to `after` takes a texture out
/// of a state shaders write in (render target, unordered access, depth
/// write): a place for a picture.
pub(crate) fn might_leave(before: u32, after: u32) -> bool {
    const WRITES: u32 = 0x4 | 0x8 | 0x10;
    before & WRITES != 0 && before != after && before != COPY_SOURCE
}

/// Host texture `copy` is about to be moved from state `before` to `after`
/// by commands recorded into `cmd`: either the title's list `recording`
/// itself, or (`begins`: the line that list's recording began at) the list
/// that runs before it at submission. If the texture leaves a state
/// shaders write in, this is a place for a picture: where one is taken,
/// the texture is moved to the copy-source state, copied, and moved back
/// to `before` here, so the caller's own move is recorded as in any
/// other frame (a caller may read "no change of state" as "not used
/// since": the alias copies of `crate::texture` do).
pub(crate) fn leaves(
    cmd: &ID3D12GraphicsCommandList,
    list: usize,
    recording: Option<&crate::host::HostList>,
    begins: Option<u32>,
    copy: &std::sync::Arc<crate::resource::HostTexture>,
    before: u32,
    after: u32,
) {
    if !might_leave(before, after) {
        return;
    }
    let texture = &copy.texture;
    // SAFETY: a live resource.
    let d = unsafe { texture.GetDesc() };
    if d.Dimension != D3D12_RESOURCE_DIMENSION_TEXTURE2D || d.SampleDesc.Count > 1 || !shows(d.Format.0) {
        return;
    }
    let Some(host) = crate::host::host() else { return };
    let key = std::sync::Arc::as_ptr(copy) as usize;
    let slices = if d.DepthOrArraySize <= 6 { u32::from(d.DepthOrArraySize) } else { 1 };
    // In the title's own list the copy gets a timestamp of its own, so
    // its time is not the command's before it. (A list of the next frame
    // has no places.)
    if let Some(recording) = recording {
        stamp(recording);
        if NEXT_FRAME.replace(false) {
            return;
        }
    }
    let stamp = STAMP.replace(u32::MAX);
    // SAFETY: a plain query.
    let thread = unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentThreadId() };
    // Which place this is: the texture's n-th in the frame.
    let (occurrence, title) = {
        let mut shot = SHOT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        let Some(s) = shot.as_mut() else { return };
        let met = s.per_texture.entry(key).or_default();
        *met += 1;
        (*met - 1, s.titles.get(&key).copied().unwrap_or(key))
    };
    let most = number("VICTORY_SHOT_MB", 1024) << 20;
    let mut moved = false;
    for slice in 0..slices {
        let sub = slice * u32::from(d.MipLevels);
        let mut total = 0u64;
        // SAFETY: a live device; outputs for one subresource.
        unsafe { host.device().GetCopyableFootprints(&d, sub, 1, 0, None, None, None, Some(&mut total)) };
        // Whether the place's picture is taken in this frame; the line of
        // a frame that keeps lines says which.
        {
            let mut shot = SHOT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
            let Some(s) = shot.as_mut() else { break };
            let first = s.carry.parts == 0;
            if first {
                s.places += 1;
            }
            let what = format!(
                "texture {title:#x} n {occurrence} slice {slice} {}x{} f{} leaves state {before:#x} for {after:#x}{}",
                d.Width,
                d.Height,
                d.Format.0,
                begins.map_or(String::new(), |b| format!(" at the start of the recording that begins at line {b}"))
            );
            let say = |s: &mut Shot, word: &str, why: &str| {
                if first && s.events.len() < MAX_EVENTS {
                    s.events.push(Event { list, thread, stamp: if slice == 0 { stamp } else { u32::MAX }, text: format!("{word} {what}{why}") });
                }
            };
            // The same in every frame: a texture's ninth place on, and a
            // picture larger than a frame may ever take.
            if occurrence >= REPEATS {
                if first {
                    s.not_taken += 1;
                }
                say(s, "SNAP-NOT", " (the texture's ninth place or later)");
                continue;
            }
            if total == 0 || total > most {
                if first {
                    s.not_taken += 1;
                }
                say(s, "SNAP-NOT", " (too large)");
                continue;
            }
            if s.carry.done.contains(&(key, occurrence, slice)) {
                // Taken by an earlier frame of the shot.
                continue;
            }
            if s.bytes + total > s.budget {
                s.later += 1;
                say(s, "SNAP-LATER", "");
                continue;
            }
            s.bytes += total;
            s.carry.done.insert((key, occurrence, slice));
            say(s, "SNAP", "");
        }
        if !moved {
            // SAFETY: an open list and a live texture in state `before`.
            unsafe {
                cmd.ResourceBarrier(&[crate::host::transition(
                    texture,
                    D3D12_RESOURCE_STATES(before as i32),
                    D3D12_RESOURCE_STATES(COPY_SOURCE as i32),
                )]);
            }
            moved = true;
        }
        let Some((buffer, footprint)) = crate::capture::read_back_of(host.device(), cmd, texture, sub) else {
            continue;
        };
        let name = format!("snap-{title:x}-n{occurrence}-s{slice}-{}x{}-f{}", d.Width, d.Height, d.Format.0);
        let mut shot = SHOT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        let Some(s) = shot.as_mut() else { break };
        s.snaps.push(Snap {
            occurrence,
            name,
            buffer,
            footprint: footprint.Footprint,
            bytes: total,
            texture: title,
            width: d.Width,
            height: d.Height,
            format: d.Format.0,
            slice,
            before,
            after,
        });
    }
    if moved {
        // SAFETY: an open list and a live texture in the copy-source state.
        unsafe {
            cmd.ResourceBarrier(&[crate::host::transition(
                texture,
                D3D12_RESOURCE_STATES(COPY_SOURCE as i32),
                D3D12_RESOURCE_STATES(before as i32),
            )]);
        }
    }
}

/// The first frame of 500 draws or more, for `VICTORY_SHOT_AT`.
static WORLD: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(u64::MAX);

/// Why a shot is taken of the frame after `frame`, if one is.
fn trigger(folder: &std::path::Path, frame: u64) -> Option<String> {
    let world = WORLD.load(Relaxed);
    if world != u64::MAX && at().contains(&(frame + 1 - world)) {
        return Some(format!("frame {} after the first one of 500 draws (VICTORY_SHOT_AT)", frame + 1 - world));
    }
    // The file is looked for at every fourth present.
    if frame.is_multiple_of(4) {
        let take = folder.join("take");
        if take.exists() {
            // A file that cannot be removed would ask again at once.
            return match std::fs::remove_file(&take) {
                Ok(()) => Some("asked for (the file `take`)".to_string()),
                Err(e) => {
                    static ONCE: std::sync::Once = std::sync::Once::new();
                    ONCE.call_once(|| tracing::warn!(error = %e, "the file `take` could not be removed: no frame shot for it"));
                    None
                }
            };
        }
    }
    None
}

/// At the present of `frame`, on the thread that presents; `drawn` is the
/// number of draws run on the host so far.
pub(crate) fn present(frame: u64, drawn: u64) {
    let Some(folder) = folder() else { return };
    static LAST: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
    if drawn.saturating_sub(LAST.swap(drawn, Relaxed)) >= 500 {
        let _ = WORLD.compare_exchange(u64::MAX, frame, Relaxed, Relaxed);
    }
    match PHASE.load(Relaxed) {
        IDLE => {
            let waiting = WAITING.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone();
            if let Some(carry) = waiting {
                // The next frame of a shot: one built like its first (the
                // title's frames come in pairs: an even number of frames on).
                if (frame + 1 - carry.first).is_multiple_of(2) {
                    *WAITING.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = None;
                    arm(frame + 1, carry, folder);
                }
            } else if let Some(why) = trigger(folder, frame) {
                static TAKEN: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
                let most = number("VICTORY_SHOT_MAX", 12);
                if u64::from(TAKEN.fetch_add(1, Relaxed)) >= most {
                    tracing::warn!(most, "frame shot not taken: the run has its most already (VICTORY_SHOT_MAX)");
                } else {
                    arm(frame + 1, Carry { first: frame + 1, why, began: hhmmss(), ..Default::default() }, folder);
                }
            }
        }
        RECORDING => {
            let mut shot = SHOT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
            let Some(s) = shot.as_mut() else {
                PHASE.store(IDLE, Relaxed);
                return;
            };
            s.presents += 1;
            // The frame's own present is the one after its lists were
            // submitted.
            let goes_on = !closing() && s.presents < 3;
            if s.carry.parts == 0 {
                let text = format!(
                    "PRESENT frame {frame}: {} draws and dispatches recorded since the shot began{}",
                    s.work,
                    if goes_on { "; the shot goes on through the next frame" } else { "" }
                );
                s.events.push(Event { list: 0, thread: 0, stamp: u32::MAX, text });
            }
            if !goes_on {
                s.stopped = Some((std::time::Instant::now(), frame));
                PHASE.store(PENDING, Relaxed);
                tracing::info!(
                    frame,
                    part = s.carry.parts,
                    lines = s.events.len(),
                    places = s.places,
                    pictures = s.snaps.len(),
                    for_later = s.later,
                    read_back_mb = s.bytes >> 20,
                    "frame shot: a frame is recorded; its pictures are read in two seconds"
                );
            }
        }
        PENDING => {
            let mut shot = SHOT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
            let ready = shot
                .as_ref()
                .and_then(|s| s.stopped)
                .is_some_and(|(when, of)| when.elapsed() >= std::time::Duration::from_secs(2) && frame >= of + 8);
            if ready && let Some(s) = shot.take() {
                PHASE.store(SAVING, Relaxed);
                let to = folder.join(s.carry.folder_name());
                let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new().name("victory-shot".into()).spawn(move || {
                    crate::framelog::keep_on_slow_cores("frame shot");
                    let next = save(s, &to);
                    *WAITING.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = next;
                    PHASE.store(IDLE, Relaxed);
                });
                if let Err(e) = spawned {
                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, "frame shot: no thread to write it out; dropped");
                    PHASE.store(IDLE, Relaxed);
                }
            }
        }
        _ => {}
    }
}

/// Starts a frame of a shot: frame `frame`, the shot's first or (`carry`
/// says) a later one.
fn arm(frame: u64, carry: Carry, folder: &std::path::Path) {
    let mut room = room_mb();
    if room < LEAST_MB {
        if carry.parts != 0 {
            tracing::warn!(
                free_mb = crate::framelog::free_mb(),
                part = carry.parts,
                "frame shot ends here: too little memory free for more of its pictures"
            );
            finish(&carry, &folder.join(carry.folder_name()), "ended early: too little memory free for more pictures", 0);
            return;
        }
        // The lines and times need none of it.
        room = 0;
    }
    let lines = carry.parts == 0;
    let clock = lines && CLOCK.get_or_init(make_clock).is_some();
    NEXT.store(0, Relaxed);
    SUBMITTED.store(0, Relaxed);
    let id = SHOT_ID.fetch_add(1, Relaxed) + 1;
    tracing::info!(
        frame,
        part = carry.parts,
        pictures_so_far = carry.done.len(),
        why = carry.why,
        room_mb = room,
        free_mb = crate::framelog::free_mb(),
        timestamps = clock,
        "frame shot: recording the next frame"
    );
    *SHOT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = Some(Shot {
        id,
        frame,
        carry,
        presents: 0,
        work: 0,
        events: Vec::with_capacity(if lines { 32768 } else { 0 }),
        snaps: Vec::new(),
        bytes: 0,
        budget: room << 20,
        places: 0,
        later: 0,
        not_taken: 0,
        per_texture: Default::default(),
        titles: Default::default(),
        resolved: Vec::new(),
        stopped: None,
    });
    LINES.store(lines, Relaxed);
    PHASE.store(RECORDING, Relaxed);
}

/// Writes one frame of a shot out and lets its buffers go. What the shot
/// carries on, if pictures are left for a later frame.
fn save(shot: Shot, to: &std::path::Path) -> Option<Carry> {
    use std::fmt::Write;
    use std::io::Write as _;
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
    if let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(to) {
        tracing::warn!(error = %e, folder = %to.display(), "frame shot not saved: no folder");
        return None;
    }
    let mut carry = shot.carry.clone();
    let part = carry.parts;
    if part == 0 {
        // Lines: place, list, thread, timestamp's place (-1: none), text.
        let mut events = String::with_capacity(shot.events.iter().map(|e| e.text.len() + 40).sum());
        for (seq, e) in shot.events.iter().enumerate() {
            let stamp = if e.stamp == u32::MAX { -1 } else { i64::from(e.stamp) };
            let _ = writeln!(events, "{seq}\t{:#x}\t{}\t{stamp}\t{}", e.list, e.thread, e.text.replace(['\n', '\r', '\t'], " "));
        }
        if let Err(e) = std::fs::write(to.join("events.txt"), events) {
            tracing::warn!(error = %e, folder = %to.display(), "frame shot: its lines could not be written");
        }
        // Timestamps: the places lists resolved, as the card wrote them.
        let mut stamps = String::new();
        if let Some(Some(clock)) = CLOCK.get() {
            let _ = writeln!(stamps, "frequency\t{}", clock.frequency);
            for &(base, count) in &shot.resolved {
                for slot in base..(base + count).min(SLOTS) {
                    // SAFETY: a place inside the mapped read-back buffer,
                    // which the card wrote long ago (or never: then what
                    // it held).
                    let ticks = unsafe { std::ptr::read_volatile((clock.mapped as *const u64).add(slot as usize)) };
                    let _ = writeln!(stamps, "{slot}\t{ticks}");
                }
            }
        }
        let _ = std::fs::write(to.join("stamps.txt"), stamps);
        let _ = std::fs::write(
            to.join("snaps.txt"),
            "texture\tn\tslice\tfile\tpart\tframe\twidth\theight\tformat\tbefore\tafter\tnot_black_percent\tmean_rgb\n",
        );
        carry.lines = shot.events.len();
        carry.work = shot.work;
        carry.presents = shot.presents;
        carry.places = shot.places;
        carry.not_taken = shot.not_taken;
    }
    // Pictures.
    let full = std::env::var_os("VICTORY_SHOT_FULL").is_some_and(|v| v == "1");
    let mut list = String::new();
    let (mut saved, mut failed) = (0u32, 0u32);
    for snap in shot.snaps {
        let f = snap.footprint;
        let mut data = std::ptr::null_mut();
        // SAFETY: the copy finished long ago; the mapping spans the bytes
        // the footprint was sized for.
        let rgba = unsafe {
            if snap.buffer.Map(0, None, Some(&mut data)).is_err() || data.is_null() {
                None
            } else {
                let rows = std::slice::from_raw_parts(data.cast::<u8>(), snap.bytes as usize);
                let rgba = crate::capture::to_rgba(f.Format.0 as u32, f.Width as usize, f.Height as usize, f.RowPitch as usize, rows);
                snap.buffer.Unmap(0, None);
                rgba
            }
        };
        let Some(rgba) = rgba else {
            failed += 1;
            continue;
        };
        // Every `step`th pixel each way: 1280 across at most, unless asked.
        let step = if full { 1 } else { (f.Width.max(f.Height) as usize).div_ceil(1280).max(1) };
        let (w, h) = ((f.Width as usize).div_ceil(step), (f.Height as usize).div_ceil(step));
        let mut raw = Vec::with_capacity((w * 3 + 1) * h);
        let (mut lit, mut sum) = (0u64, [0u64; 3]);
        for y in 0..h {
            raw.push(0);
            for x in 0..w {
                let p = &rgba[((y * step) * f.Width as usize + x * step) * 4..][..3];
                raw.extend_from_slice(p);
                lit += u64::from(p.iter().any(|&c| c > 8));
                for (s, &c) in sum.iter_mut().zip(p) {
                    *s += u64::from(c);
                }
            }
        }
        let n = (w * h).max(1) as u64;
        match std::fs::write(to.join(format!("{}.png", snap.name)), crate::capture::png_rgb(w as u32, h as u32, &raw)) {
            Ok(()) => saved += 1,
            Err(_) => {
                failed += 1;
                continue;
            }
        }
        let _ = writeln!(
            list,
            "{:#x}\t{}\t{}\t{}.png\t{part}\t{}\t{}\t{}\t{}\t{:#x}\t{:#x}\t{:.1}\t{},{},{}",
            snap.texture,
            snap.occurrence,
            snap.slice,
            snap.name,
            shot.frame,
            snap.width,
            snap.height,
            snap.format,
            snap.before,
            snap.after,
            lit as f64 * 100.0 / n as f64,
            sum[0] / n,
            sum[1] / n,
            sum[2] / n
        );
    }
    if let Ok(mut file) = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).create(true).open(to.join("snaps.txt")) {
        let _ = file.write_all(list.as_bytes());
    }
    carry.parts += 1;
    carry.saved += saved;
    carry.failed += failed;
    carry.read_back_mb += shot.bytes >> 20;
    tracing::info!(
        folder = %to.display(),
        part,
        frame = shot.frame,
        pictures = saved,
        failed,
        for_later = shot.later,
        seconds = started.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
        "frame shot: a frame's part is saved"
    );
    // More pictures in a later frame, while frames still get some.
    if shot.later == 0 {
        finish(&carry, to, "complete", 0);
        None
    } else if (saved == 0 && part != 0) || carry.parts >= MAX_PARTS {
        finish(&carry, to, "ended early: a frame got no further picture", shot.later);
        None
    } else {
        Some(carry)
    }
}

/// A shot's last files: `info.txt` and `done`.
fn finish(carry: &Carry, to: &std::path::Path, how: &str, missing: u32) {
    let info = format!(
        "frame\t{}\nwhy\t{}\nended\t{how}\npresents\t{}\ndraws_and_dispatches\t{}\nlines\t{}\nplaces_for_pictures\t{}\nplaces_never_taken\t{}\n\
         frames_taken_in\t{}\npictures_saved\t{}\npictures_failed\t{}\npictures_missing\t{missing}\nread_back_mb\t{}\n",
        carry.first,
        carry.why,
        carry.presents,
        carry.work,
        carry.lines,
        carry.places,
        carry.not_taken,
        carry.parts,
        carry.saved,
        carry.failed,
        carry.read_back_mb
    );
    let _ = std::fs::write(to.join("info.txt"), info);
    let _ = std::fs::write(to.join("done"), "");
    tracing::info!(
        folder = %to.display(),
        how,
        frames = carry.parts,
        lines = carry.lines,
        places = carry.places,
        pictures = carry.saved,
        failed = carry.failed,
        missing,
        "frame shot saved"
    );
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    #[test]
    fn the_formats_shown_are_the_ones_the_pictures_decode() {
        // Every format `shows` names decodes, and one it does not name
        // does not (a block-compressed one: never a target).
        for format in (1..=2).chain(9..=16).chain(19..=65).chain(87..=93) {
            assert!(super::shows(format));
            let pixel = [0u8; 16];
            assert!(crate::capture::to_rgba(format as u32, 1, 1, 16, &pixel).is_some(), "format {format}");
        }
        assert!(!super::shows(71));
        assert!(crate::capture::to_rgba(71, 1, 1, 16, &[0u8; 16]).is_none());
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Command signatures: the record layout of indirect execution. Kept for
//! translating it later.
#![allow(clippy::not_unsafe_ptr_arg_deref)]

use crate::object::{
    self, COMMAND_SIGNATURE, E_INVALIDARG, HRESULT, Iid, Object, Table, This, guid,
};
use crate::resource::PAGEABLE_IIDS;

const SIGNATURE_IIDS: [Iid; 4] = [
    guid(
        0xc36a797c,
        0xec80,
        0x4f0a,
        [0x89, 0x85, 0xa7, 0xb2, 0x47, 0x50, 0x82, 0xd1],
    ),
    PAGEABLE_IIDS[0],
    PAGEABLE_IIDS[1],
    PAGEABLE_IIDS[2],
];

#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct Desc {
    stride: u32,
    count: u32,
    /// Each a type and up to three 32-bit fields.
    arguments: *const [u32; 4],
    nodes: u32,
}

#[repr(C)]
struct Signature {
    object: Object,
    stride: u32,
    arguments: Vec<[u32; 4]>,
}

/// Device method.
pub(crate) extern "system" fn create(
    _: This,
    desc: *const Desc,
    _root: This,
    iid: *const Iid,
    out: *mut This,
) -> HRESULT {
    // SAFETY: the title passes a description (null is tolerated).
    let Some(desc) = (unsafe { desc.as_ref() }) else {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    };
    if desc.arguments.is_null() && desc.count > 0 {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    let arguments = if desc.count == 0 {
        Vec::new()
    } else {
        // SAFETY: the title passes `count` argument descriptions.
        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(desc.arguments, desc.count as usize) }.to_vec()
    };
    tracing::debug!(stride = desc.stride, ?arguments, "command signature");
    let signature = Box::new(Signature {
        object: Object::new(&FUNCTIONS),
        stride: desc.stride,
        arguments,
    });
    object::hand_out(COMMAND_SIGNATURE, signature, iid, &SIGNATURE_IIDS, out)
}

/// A signature's record stride and arguments (type, then up to three
/// fields each).
pub(crate) fn layout<'a>(this: This) -> Option<(u32, &'a [[u32; 4]])> {
    if this.is_null() {
        return None;
    }
    // SAFETY: the title passes one of our signatures.
    let s = unsafe { &*this.cast::<Signature>() };
    Some((s.stride, &s.arguments))
}

extern "system" fn query(this: This, iid: *const Iid, out: *mut This) -> HRESULT {
    let found = object::is(iid, &SIGNATURE_IIDS).then_some(this);
    object::answer(COMMAND_SIGNATURE, iid, found, out)
}
extern "system" fn release(this: This) -> u32 {
    object::release_boxed::<Signature>(this)
}

/// IUnknown 3, object 4, device child 1.
static FUNCTIONS: Table<24> = {
    let mut f = object::d3d12_object(object::missing_table::<COMMAND_SIGNATURE, 24>());
    f[0] = query as *const ();
    f[2] = release as *const ();
    f[7] = object::parent_device as *const (); // 0x38
    Table(f)
};
```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/spread.rs`:

```rs
//! The title's crowded thread groups get more processors to run on.
//!
//! The title pins its threads as on the console: sixteen logical
//! processors of eight like cores. Measured on a 14700KF (eight fast cores
//! as logical processors 0-15, twelve efficiency cores as 16-27): eleven
//! of its threads, the ones that record lists and run its jobs, share
//! logical processors 8-12, which are two and a half fast cores; a
//! two-second sample found those five 70 to 107 % busy while fast core 7
//! and the efficiency cores carried no pinned thread at all. The profile
//! of run 236 shows what that costs: code of the recording threads that
//! cannot wait for anything (a load of an atomic, a step in a tree) was
//! on a processor in only 58 to 72 of 100 looks, where the same kind of
//! code on the layer's unpinned submit thread was in 90 to 97. The frame
//! waits about 50 ms for those threads before the submit thread's 80.
//!
//! With `VICTORY_SPREAD=1` a group with more threads than processors may
//! also run on the processors no pinned thread of the title uses: the
//! slow cores by default (`VICTORY_SPREAD_SPARE=<hex mask>`: those
//! instead). The title cannot tell which processor a thread is on (it
//! imports neither `GetCurrentProcessorNumber` nor uses `rdpid`), and a
//! wider set is a place to run, not an order: the scheduler still prefers
//! the fast cores. `VICTORY_SPREAD=alt`: twenty seconds with, twenty
//! without, in turn, each change said in the log, to measure it in one
//! scene. Off by default.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{CloseHandle, HANDLE, INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::ToolHelp::{CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, THREADENTRY32, Thread32First, Thread32Next};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::SystemInformation::GROUP_AFFINITY;
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
    GetCurrentProcess, GetCurrentProcessId, GetProcessAffinityMask, GetThreadGroupAffinity, OpenThread, SetThreadGroupAffinity, THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION,
    THREAD_SET_INFORMATION,
};

/// 0 off, 1 on, 2 in turn.
fn mode() -> u8 {
    static MODE: std::sync::OnceLock<u8> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *MODE.get_or_init(|| match std::env::var("VICTORY_SPREAD").as_deref() {
        Ok("1") => 1,
        Ok("alt") => 2,
        _ => 0,
    })
}

/// A pinned thread of the title: the mask the title gave it and the one it
/// has from us.
struct Pinned {
    original: usize,
    wide: usize,
}

/// The mask for a group of `threads` threads the title pinned to `mask`:
/// with `spare` added if they are more than its processors.
fn widened(mask: usize, threads: usize, spare: usize) -> usize {
    if threads > mask.count_ones() as usize { mask | spare } else { mask }
}

/// Whether `mask` is a pinning of the title's: some of the console's
/// sixteen logical processors, not all the processors there are.
fn console_pinning(mask: usize, all: usize) -> bool {
    mask != 0 && mask != all && mask & !0xFFFF == 0
}

/// The ids of this process's threads.
fn threads() -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut ids = Vec::new();
    // SAFETY: a snapshot handle, closed below; the entry says its own size.
    unsafe {
        let snapshot = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, 0);
        if snapshot == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE {
            return ids;
        }
        let process = GetCurrentProcessId();
        let mut entry: THREADENTRY32 = std::mem::zeroed();
        entry.dwSize = size_of::<THREADENTRY32>() as u32;
        let mut more = Thread32First(snapshot, &mut entry) != 0;
        while more {
            if entry.th32OwnerProcessID == process {
                ids.push(entry.th32ThreadID);
            }
            more = Thread32Next(snapshot, &mut entry) != 0;
        }
        CloseHandle(snapshot);
    }
    ids
}

/// A thread's mask in processor group 0, if it can be asked.
fn mask_of(thread: HANDLE) -> Option<usize> {
    // SAFETY: plain data filled in by the query.
    let mut affinity: GROUP_AFFINITY = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    // SAFETY: an open thread handle and a valid out pointer.
    (unsafe { GetThreadGroupAffinity(thread, &mut affinity) } != 0 && affinity.Group == 0).then_some(affinity.Mask)
}

/// One look at all threads: the title's pinned ones are noted, and each
/// gets its wide mask (`wide`) or the title's own back.
fn pass(pinned: &mut HashMap<u32, Pinned>, all: usize, spare: usize, wide: bool, said: &mut String) {
    let ids = threads();
    pinned.retain(|id, _| ids.contains(id));
    let mut open: Vec<(u32, HANDLE, usize)> = Vec::new();
    for id in ids {
        // SAFETY: a thread id of this process; the handle is closed below.
        let handle = unsafe { OpenThread(THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION | THREAD_SET_INFORMATION, 0, id) };
        if handle.is_null() {
            continue;
        }
        match mask_of(handle) {
            Some(mask) => {
                let ours = pinned.get(&id).is_some_and(|p| mask == p.wide || mask == p.original);
                if !ours {
                    if console_pinning(mask, all) {
                        // New, or the title pinned it again.
                        pinned.insert(id, Pinned { original: mask, wide: mask });
                    } else {
                        // Not pinned (an id used again by another thread).
                        pinned.remove(&id);
                    }
                }
                open.push((id, handle, mask));
            }
            // SAFETY: the handle opened above.
            None => unsafe {
                CloseHandle(handle);
            },
        }
    }
    let mut groups: HashMap<usize, usize> = HashMap::new();
    for p in pinned.values() {
        *groups.entry(p.original).or_default() += 1;
    }
    for p in pinned.values_mut() {
        p.wide = widened(p.original, groups[&p.original], spare);
    }
    for (id, handle, mask) in open {
        if let Some(p) = pinned.get(&id) {
            let want = if wide { p.wide } else { p.original };
            if mask != want {
                let affinity = GROUP_AFFINITY { Mask: want, Group: 0, Reserved: [0; 3] };
                // SAFETY: an open thread handle and a mask of this system's processors.
                if unsafe { SetThreadGroupAffinity(handle, &affinity, std::ptr::null_mut()) } == 0 {
                    tracing::debug!(id, want, error = %std::io::Error::last_os_error(), "a thread's processors could not be set");
                }
            }
        }
        // SAFETY: the handle opened above.
        unsafe { CloseHandle(handle) };
    }
    let mut table: Vec<(usize, usize)> = groups.into_iter().collect();
    table.sort();
    let text = table
        .iter()
        .map(|&(mask, threads)| {
            let to = widened(mask, threads, spare);
            if to == mask {
                format!("{threads} on {mask:#x} ({} processors)", mask.count_ones())
            } else {
                format!("{threads} on {mask:#x} ({} processors) -> {to:#x} ({})", mask.count_ones(), to.count_ones())
            }
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join("; ");
    if text != *said {
        tracing::info!("spread: the title's pinned threads by its mask: {text}");
        *said = text;
    }
}

/// Starts the thread that widens the title's crowded groups, if asked for.
pub(crate) fn start() {
    static ONCE: std::sync::Once = std::sync::Once::new();
    if mode() == 0 {
        return;
    }
    ONCE.call_once(|| {
        let made = std::thread::Builder::new().name("victory-spread".into()).spawn(|| {
            let (mut all, mut system) = (0usize, 0usize);
            // SAFETY: our own process and valid out pointers.
            if unsafe { GetProcessAffinityMask(GetCurrentProcess(), &mut all, &mut system) } == 0 || all == 0 {
                tracing::warn!("spread: the process's processors could not be asked; nothing is widened");
                return;
            }
            let spare = match std::env::var("VICTORY_SPREAD_SPARE").ok().and_then(|v| usize::from_str_radix(v.trim_start_matches("0x"), 16).ok()) {
                Some(mask) => mask & all,
                None => crate::framelog::slow_processors() & all,
            };
            if spare == 0 {
                tracing::info!("spread: no spare processors (all cores are alike and VICTORY_SPREAD_SPARE names none); nothing is widened");
                return;
            }
            tracing::info!(
                "spread: the title's thread groups with more threads than processors may also run on processors {spare:#x} (VICTORY_SPREAD=1; alt: in turn)"
            );
            let epoch = std::time::Instant::now();
            let mut pinned = HashMap::new();
            let mut said = String::new();
            let mut last = None;
            loop {
                let wide = mode() == 1 || (epoch.elapsed().as_secs() / 20) % 2 == 1;
                if mode() == 2 && last != Some(wide) {
                    tracing::info!(
                        "the title's crowded thread groups run on more processors from now (VICTORY_SPREAD=alt): {}",
                        if wide { "ON" } else { "off, as usual" }
                    );
                }
                last = Some(wide);
                pass(&mut pinned, all, spare, wide, &mut said);
                // Often enough to catch threads the title starts and to turn with the
                // twenty-second phases; a pass is a snapshot and a query a thread.
                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(500));
            }
        });
        if let Err(error) = made {
            tracing::warn!(%error, "the spread thread could not be started");
        }
    });
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn only_crowded_groups_are_widened() {
        let spare = 0x0FFF_0000;
        // eleven threads on five processors: crowded
        assert_eq!(widened(0x1F00, 11, spare), 0x0FFF_1F00);
        // eight on eight, three on six, one on one: left alone
        assert_eq!(widened(0xFF, 8, spare), 0xFF);
        assert_eq!(widened(0x3F00, 3, spare), 0x3F00);
        assert_eq!(widened(0x2000, 1, spare), 0x2000);
        assert_eq!(widened(0x3FFF, 11, spare), 0x3FFF);
        assert_eq!(widened(0x3FFF, 15, spare), 0x0FFF_3FFF);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_pinning_of_the_title_is_within_the_console_s_sixteen() {
        let all = 0x0FFF_FFFF;
        assert!(console_pinning(0x1F00, all));
        assert!(console_pinning(0xFFFF, all));
        assert!(!console_pinning(all, all), "not pinned");
        assert!(!console_pinning(0x0FFF_1F00, all), "already wide: not the title's");
        assert!(!console_pinning(0, all));
        // a PC with sixteen processors: all of them is not a pinning
        assert!(!console_pinning(0xFFFF, 0xFFFF));
    }

    #[test]
    fn this_process_has_threads_and_they_have_masks() {
        let ids = threads();
        assert!(!ids.is_empty());
        // SAFETY: a thread id of this process.
        let handle = unsafe { OpenThread(THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION | THREAD_SET_INFORMATION, 0, ids[0]) };
        assert!(!handle.is_null());
        assert!(mask_of(handle).is_some_and(|m| m != 0));
        // SAFETY: the handle opened above.
        unsafe { CloseHandle(handle) };
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/texback.rs`:

```rs
//! Textures shaders write that the title's own code then reads on the CPU.
//! On the console the CPU and the GPU share memory, so what a compute pass
//! stores into a texture is in title memory for the CPU to read. Here it stays
//! in the texture's host copy. The title's ocean is one: its wave passes write
//! a 256x256 height map (R32_FLOAT) and a displacement map (R32G32_FLOAT), and
//! its CPU code samples both, which is what boats float on; it read memory
//! nothing had written (run rw1, `VICTORY_READ_WATCH=1`: about 30 places in
//! the title read those two kinds), and boats sank.
//!
//! For textures of the kinds in `VICTORY_TEXTURE_BACK` (comma-separated
//! `<width>x<height>f<format>`; `1` for the four water formats found by
//! the upstream trace), a list in which shaders write one copies it
//! into a read-back buffer of ours when it closes, and once the list has run
//! the texels are tiled into the texture's title memory in the console's
//! layout, as the console's GPU would have left them.
//!
//! shortcut: by kind, not by texture: textures of those kinds the title never
//! reads are copied back too (about a megabyte per such list). The copy shows
//! what the list's last write left; a title read in between sees the frame
//! before, as it would before the console's GPU has run.

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, OnceLock, Weak};

use windows::Win32::Graphics::Direct3D12::*;

use crate::object::This;

/// The kinds copied back: (width, height, format).
fn kinds() -> &'static [(u64, u32, u32)] {
    static KINDS: OnceLock<Vec<(u64, u32, u32)>> = OnceLock::new();
    KINDS.get_or_init(|| {
        const DEFAULT: &str = "256x256f41,256x256f16,64x64f16,128x128f36";
        let list = match std::env::var("VICTORY_TEXTURE_BACK").as_deref() {
            Ok("1") => DEFAULT.to_owned(),
            Ok(spec) => spec.to_owned(),
            Err(_) => String::new(),
        };
        let kinds: Vec<(u64, u32, u32)> = list
            .split(',')
            .filter_map(|k| {
                let (size, format) = k.trim().split_once('f')?;
                let (w, h) = size.split_once('x')?;
                Some((w.parse().ok()?, h.parse().ok()?, format.parse().ok()?))
            })
            .collect();
        if !kinds.is_empty() {
            tracing::info!(?kinds, "textures of these kinds that shaders write are copied back into title memory (VICTORY_TEXTURE_BACK)");
        }
        kinds
    })
}

/// Whether title texture `resource` is of a kind copied back.
pub(crate) fn wanted(resource: This) -> bool {
    let kinds = kinds();
    !kinds.is_empty()
        && crate::resource::texture_kind(resource).is_some_and(|k| kinds.contains(&k))
}

/// An outstanding write to a specific allocation. Mapping and resource
/// changes invalidate only the writes that could touch the replaced memory.
struct Ticket {
    owner: usize,
    at: usize,
    end: usize,
    valid: AtomicBool,
}

static TICKETS: Mutex<Vec<Weak<Ticket>>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());
static TRACKING: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

fn track(owner: usize, at: usize, end: usize) -> Arc<Ticket> {
    let ticket = Arc::new(Ticket { owner, at, end, valid: AtomicBool::new(true) });
    let mut tickets = TICKETS.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    tickets.retain(|weak| weak.strong_count() != 0);
    tickets.push(Arc::downgrade(&ticket));
    TRACKING.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    ticket
}

fn invalidate(matches: impl Fn(&Ticket) -> bool) {
    if !TRACKING.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
        return;
    }
    TICKETS.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).retain(|weak| {
        let Some(ticket) = weak.upgrade() else { return false };
        if matches(&ticket) {
            ticket.valid.store(false, Ordering::Release);
        }
        true
    });
}

pub(crate) fn released(owner: usize) {
    invalidate(|ticket| ticket.owner == owner);
}

pub(crate) fn replaced(at: usize) {
    invalidate(|ticket| ticket.at == at);
}

pub(crate) fn remapped(at: usize, len: usize) {
    let end = at.saturating_add(len);
    invalidate(|ticket| at < ticket.end && ticket.at < end);
}

pub(crate) struct Target {
    pub(crate) copy: Arc<crate::resource::HostTexture>,
    layout: victory_formats::texture::Layout,
    ticket: Arc<Ticket>,
}

impl Target {
    pub(crate) fn new(resource: This) -> Option<Self> {
        // Keep the host copy independently of the title's resource lifetime.
        let copy = crate::resource::host_copy(resource)?;
        let _mapping = crate::watch::title_memory_reading();
        let (layout, at, size) = crate::resource::title_texture(resource)?;
        let end = at.checked_add(size).filter(|&end| at != 0 && end > at)?;
        let ticket = track(resource as usize, at, end);
        Some(Self { copy, layout, ticket })
    }

    pub(crate) fn owner(&self) -> usize { self.ticket.owner }
}

/// The readback resources and the allocation the pixels belong to.
pub(crate) struct Back {
    buffer: ID3D12Resource,
    footprints: Vec<D3D12_PLACED_SUBRESOURCE_FOOTPRINT>,
    rows: Vec<u32>,
    mips: u32,
    layout: victory_formats::texture::Layout,
    ticket: Arc<Ticket>,
}

impl Back {
    pub(crate) fn range(&self) -> (usize, usize) {
        (self.ticket.at, self.ticket.end)
    }
}

/// Records a host copy from a texture already in COPY_SOURCE.
pub(crate) fn record(list: &ID3D12GraphicsCommandList, target: Target) -> Option<Back> {
    if !target.ticket.valid.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
        return None;
    }
    let host = crate::host::host()?;
    let texture = &target.copy.texture;
    // SAFETY: a live texture kept through the command list's state tracking.
    let desc = unsafe { texture.GetDesc() };
    let mips = u32::from(desc.MipLevels.max(1));
    let subresources = mips * u32::from(desc.DepthOrArraySize.max(1));
    let n = subresources as usize;
    let mut footprints = vec![D3D12_PLACED_SUBRESOURCE_FOOTPRINT::default(); n];
    let mut rows = vec![0u32; n];
    let mut total = 0u64;
    // SAFETY: out arrays of `n` entries.
    unsafe {
        host.device.GetCopyableFootprints(
            &desc,
            0,
            subresources,
            0,
            Some(footprints.as_mut_ptr()),
            Some(rows.as_mut_ptr()),
            None,
            Some(&mut total),
        )
    };
    // The last footprint's advertised extent can omit row-end padding.
    // The tiler reads a pitched slice, so the mapped buffer must include it.
    for (footprint, &rows) in footprints.iter().zip(&rows) {
        let format = footprint.Footprint;
        let pitched = u64::from(format.RowPitch)
            .checked_mul(u64::from(rows))?
            .checked_mul(u64::from(format.Depth))?;
        total = total.max(footprint.Offset.checked_add(pitched)?);
    }
    let buffer = host.read_back_buffer(total)?;
    for (i, footprint) in footprints.iter().enumerate() {
        let to = D3D12_TEXTURE_COPY_LOCATION {
            // SAFETY: a borrowed pointer the location never releases.
            pResource: unsafe { std::mem::transmute_copy(&buffer) },
            Type: D3D12_TEXTURE_COPY_TYPE_PLACED_FOOTPRINT,
            Anonymous: D3D12_TEXTURE_COPY_LOCATION_0 { PlacedFootprint: *footprint },
        };
        let from = D3D12_TEXTURE_COPY_LOCATION {
            // SAFETY: as above.
            pResource: unsafe { std::mem::transmute_copy(texture) },
            Type: D3D12_TEXTURE_COPY_TYPE_SUBRESOURCE_INDEX,
            Anonymous: D3D12_TEXTURE_COPY_LOCATION_0 { SubresourceIndex: i as u32 },
        };
        // SAFETY: an open list; the texture is in the copy-source state.
        unsafe { list.CopyTextureRegion(&to, 0, 0, 0, &from, None) };
    }
    Some(Back { buffer, footprints, rows, mips, layout: target.layout, ticket: target.ticket })
}

/// Once the list has run, tile its texels back into the same title allocation.
pub(crate) fn land(back: &Back) {
    static COPIED: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
    static STALE: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
    let _mapping = crate::watch::title_memory_reading();
    let _ticket_guard = TICKETS.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    if !back.ticket.valid.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
        let skipped = STALE.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) + 1;
        if skipped.is_power_of_two() {
            tracing::info!(skipped, "skipping texture readbacks whose title allocation changed");
        }
        return;
    }
    let (at, end) = back.range();
    let size = end - at;
    let mut tiled = vec![0u8; size];
    // Keep title bytes the subresources do not cover.
    if !crate::host::read_into(at as *const u8, &mut tiled) {
        return;
    }
    let mut data = std::ptr::null_mut();
    // SAFETY: our read-back buffer, written by the list that has run.
    unsafe {
        if back.buffer.Map(0, None, Some(&mut data)).is_err() || data.is_null() {
            return;
        }
    }
    for (i, (footprint, &rows)) in back.footprints.iter().zip(&back.rows).enumerate() {
        let (mip, slice) = (i as u32 % back.mips, i as u32 / back.mips);
        let f = footprint.Footprint;
        let pitch = f.RowPitch as usize;
        let len = pitch * rows as usize * f.Depth as usize;
        // SAFETY: the subresource's part of the mapped buffer.
        let linear = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(data.cast::<u8>().add(footprint.Offset as usize), len) };
        if let Err(e) = back.layout.tile(&mut tiled, mip, slice, linear, pitch, pitch * rows as usize) {
            static ONCE: std::sync::Once = std::sync::Once::new();
            ONCE.call_once(|| tracing::warn!(?e, mip, slice, "a texture copied back could not be tiled"));
            // SAFETY: mapped above.
            unsafe { back.buffer.Unmap(0, None) };
            return;
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: mapped above.
    unsafe { back.buffer.Unmap(0, None) };
    crate::host::copy_mapped(at as *mut u8, tiled.as_ptr(), size, true);
    let copied = COPIED.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) + 1;
    if copied == 1 || copied.is_multiple_of(128) {
        tracing::info!(copied, bytes = size, "texture readback landed");
    }
}


#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn only_readbacks_for_changed_allocations_are_invalidated() {
        let first = track(91, 0x1000, 0x2000);
        let next = track(92, 0x2000, 0x3000);
        let far = track(93, 0x4000, 0x5000);

        remapped(0x0f00, 0x200);
        assert!(!first.valid.load(Ordering::Acquire));
        assert!(next.valid.load(Ordering::Acquire));
        replaced(0x2000);
        assert!(!next.valid.load(Ordering::Acquire));
        assert!(far.valid.load(Ordering::Acquire));

        released(93);
        assert!(!far.valid.load(Ordering::Acquire));
        assert!(track(94, 0x2000, 0x3000).valid.load(Ordering::Acquire));
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-gpu/src/texture.rs`:

```rs
//! Texture contents the title writes itself (decision 0007, "Texture
//! memory"): streamed pages, layout-library copies, movie frames, glyph
//! atlases. Such a texture lives in console memory in its tiled layout;
//! before a submission samples its host copy, the memory is detiled into a
//! staging buffer when its content changed, and the staging buffer is
//! copied into the host texture.
//!
//! "Changed" means a page of the memory was written since the last detiling
//! ([`crate::watch`]), in write-watched memory; in physical-page views,
//! which cannot be watched, a content hash of the whole memory at every
//! submission that samples it.
//!
//! shortcut: a change detiles the whole texture, not the pages written.
//! Only textures read through descriptor tables are brought up to date
//! (directly indexed views are not known per draw); plane 0 is uploaded
//! (every mip and array slice), depth and stencil planes are not.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use windows::Win32::Graphics::Direct3D12::*;

use crate::host::{HostList, host};
use crate::object::This;

macro_rules! once {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => {{
        static ONCE: std::sync::Once = std::sync::Once::new();
        ONCE.call_once(|| tracing::warn!($($arg)*));
    }};
}

/// A texture's upload state: the staging buffer laid out as the host
/// texture's subresources, and what was last detiled.
pub(crate) struct Staging {
    buffer: ID3D12Resource,
    /// Its bytes.
    #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
    size: u64,
    data: *mut u8,
    footprints: Vec<D3D12_PLACED_SUBRESOURCE_FOOTPRINT>,
    rows: Vec<u32>,
    layout: victory_formats::texture::Layout,
    /// Mips per array slice.
    mips: u32,
    /// The staging buffer's bytes (counted in `STAGED` while it lives).
    bytes: u64,
    memory: *const u8,
    last: Mutex<Last>,
    /// Whether the staging buffer was detiled since a submitted list last
    /// uploaded it, and whether one has uploaded it at all: a list records
    /// the upload only then. (Every list that sampled a title texture
    /// uploaded all of it again, changed or not: 5,411 subresource copies
    /// of 1,120 textures in one frame of run 18.)
    dirty: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
    uploaded: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
    /// When a list last recorded a use of it (`crate::host::moment`).
    used: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64,
    /// Levels on demand (`crate::tiles`): the texture's host copy was made
    /// without memory of its own when the staging buffer was made.
    on_demand: bool,
    /// For such a texture: the levels that were the title's at the last
    /// detiling (a bit a level; the staging buffer holds zeros for the
    /// others), and what that was judged by ([`Staging::judgement`]).
    detiled: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32,
    judged: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64; 2],
    /// For such a texture: when an upload last left a held level without
    /// tiles (`crate::host::moment`, never 0; 0: none did). The upload is
    /// recorded again about a second later if the card has room by then
    /// ([`upload`]).
    waiting: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64,
    /// The size of the buffer if it came from the pool of spare staging
    /// buffers and goes back to it ([`staging_buffer`]); 0: a buffer of its
    /// own, released when this is dropped.
    pooled: u64,
}

/// A staging buffer nothing holds: the buffer and where it is mapped.
struct Spare(ID3D12Resource, usize);

// SAFETY: a D3D12 buffer and its mapping, touched by nobody while it is
// spare.
unsafe impl Send for Spare {}

/// Spare staging buffers by size (a power of two), and their bytes in all.
static SPARE: Mutex<(std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, Vec<Spare>>, u64)> =
    Mutex::new((std::collections::BTreeMap::new(), 0));
/// The most bytes kept spare, and the largest buffer that is pooled.
const SPARE_MOST: (u64, u64) = (256 << 20, 8 << 20);
/// Staging buffers taken from the spare ones, and made, since the start.
pub(crate) static SPARE_STATS: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64; 2] = [const { std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0) }; 2];

/// A mapped upload buffer of `total` bytes for a texture's staging, all
/// zeros, and its pool size (0: not pooled).
///
/// Every texture the title streams in got a buffer of its own from the
/// host and gave it back when its staging went: about a quarter of a
/// millisecond to make (run 213's profile: 25 ms a frame on the recording
/// threads for some 100 uploads, most of it the graphics kernel waiting)
/// and more to free on the thread that submits. A streaming burst is 200
/// to 500 uploads in a frame (run 222), and those are the frames that
/// dip. Buffers of up to 8 MiB are now kept by size and used again,
/// zeroed as a new one is (levels not there yet must read as zeros).
/// `VICTORY_STAGING_POOL=0`: made and freed each time, as before.
/// `VICTORY_STAGING_POOL=alt`: twenty seconds with the pool, twenty
/// without, in turn, each change said in the log: a buffer made without
/// is freed as before, and the spare ones wait for the next turn.
/// `VICTORY_STAGING_POOL_MB`: the most kept spare (256 unless said).
fn staging_buffer(host: &crate::host::Host, total: u64) -> Option<(ID3D12Resource, *mut u8, u64)> {
    let size = total.max(64 << 10).next_power_of_two();
    if size > SPARE_MOST.1 || !staging_pool() {
        // (Counted as made: the frame log's "staging N made" is then the
        // buffers of a run without the pool too.)
        SPARE_STATS[1].fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        return host.upload_buffer(total).map(|(buffer, data)| (buffer, data, 0));
    }
    let spare = {
        let mut all = SPARE.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        let taken = all.0.get_mut(&size).and_then(Vec::pop);
        if taken.is_some() {
            all.1 -= size;
        }
        taken
    };
    if let Some(Spare(buffer, data)) = spare {
        SPARE_STATS[0].fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        // SAFETY: the buffer's own mapping, `size` bytes, which nothing
        // else holds.
        unsafe { std::ptr::write_bytes(data as *mut u8, 0, total as usize) };
        return Some((buffer, data as *mut u8, size));
    }
    SPARE_STATS[1].fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
    host.upload_buffer(size).map(|(buffer, data)| (buffer, data, size))
}

/// Whether staging buffers are taken from and returned to the spare ones
/// now (`VICTORY_STAGING_POOL`).
fn staging_pool() -> bool {
    /// 0 off, 1 on, 2 in turn.
    static MODE: std::sync::OnceLock<u8> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    match *MODE.get_or_init(|| match std::env::var("VICTORY_STAGING_POOL").as_deref() {
        Ok("0") => 0,
        Ok("alt") => 2,
        _ => 1,
    }) {
        0 => false,
        1 => true,
        _ => {
            static EPOCH: std::sync::OnceLock<std::time::Instant> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
            let on = (EPOCH.get_or_init(std::time::Instant::now).elapsed().as_secs() / 20) % 2 == 1;
            static LAST: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU8 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU8::new(2);
            if LAST.swap(u8::from(on), std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) != u8::from(on) {
                tracing::info!(
                    "texture staging buffers are taken from the spare ones from now (VICTORY_STAGING_POOL=alt): {}",
                    if on { "ON" } else { "off, made and freed each time" }
                );
            }
            on
        }
    }
}

/// The most bytes of staging buffers kept spare (`VICTORY_STAGING_POOL_MB`).
fn spare_most() -> u64 {
    static MOST: std::sync::OnceLock<u64> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *MOST.get_or_init(|| {
        std::env::var("VICTORY_STAGING_POOL_MB").ok().and_then(|v| v.trim().parse::<u64>().ok()).map_or(SPARE_MOST.0, |mb| mb << 20)
    })
}

/// What a texture's staging buffer holds: the hash of the memory detiled
/// (memory not watched), or the write-watch asking it was detiled after.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Last {
    hash: Option<blake3::Hash>,
    asked: u64,
    /// The frame a partly mapped texture was last read in.
    partial: Option<u64>,
}

// SAFETY: the staging mapping is written only at submission, under
// `last`'s lock; the title memory is only read.
unsafe impl Send for Staging {}
// SAFETY: as above.
unsafe impl Sync for Staging {}

static STAGING: Mutex<Option<HashMap<usize, Arc<Staging>>>> = Mutex::new(None);

/// The buffer a texture the host writes is copied through into the texture
/// of a view the title placed in its memory in another format
/// ([`alias`]): every level of every layer as each of the two formats lays
/// it out for a copy (the same bytes: the texels are as wide), the written
/// texture's layout first.
struct Through {
    buffer: ID3D12Resource,
    parts: Vec<(
        D3D12_PLACED_SUBRESOURCE_FOOTPRINT,
        D3D12_PLACED_SUBRESOURCE_FOOTPRINT,
    )>,
}

/// The most levels times layers [`alias`] copies (a cube of nine levels).
const ALIAS_PARTS: u32 = 54;

// SAFETY: a device-local buffer only lists record copies with.
unsafe impl Send for Through {}
// SAFETY: as above.
unsafe impl Sync for Through {}

/// The copy buffers of [`alias`], by the placed view's texture.
static THROUGH: Mutex<Option<HashMap<usize, Arc<Through>>>> = Mutex::new(None);

/// Brings `placed`, the texture of a view the title placed in the memory
/// of `source` in another format (`crate::resource::alias_of`), up to date
/// with what the host wrote to `source`: the texels of every level and
/// layer are copied as they are, through a buffer (the host copies between
/// two formats of one texel width in no other way). Recorded the first time
/// the list reads the view
/// and again whenever the list used `source` in another way since (wrote
/// it, or read it itself). Leaves `placed` in the copy destination state,
/// as [`upload`] does. False if the copy cannot be made: the caller fills
/// the texture from title memory, as before.
pub(crate) fn alias(list: &HostList, placed: This, source: This) -> bool {
    const TARGET_OR_UNORDERED: u32 = 0x4 | 0x8;
    const COPY_DEST: u32 = 0x400;
    const COPY_SOURCE: u32 = 0x800;
    let (Some(to), Some(from)) = (
        crate::resource::host_resource(placed),
        crate::resource::host_resource(source),
    ) else {
        return false;
    };
    let Some(host) = host() else { return false };
    let through = {
        let mut map = THROUGH.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        let map = map.get_or_insert_with(HashMap::new);
        match map.get(&(placed as usize)) {
            Some(through) => through.clone(),
            None => {
                // SAFETY: live textures.
                let (of_from, of_to) = unsafe { (from.GetDesc(), to.GetDesc()) };
                // Levels times layers (a volume's slices are one part).
                let count = |d: &D3D12_RESOURCE_DESC| {
                    let layers = if d.Dimension == D3D12_RESOURCE_DIMENSION_TEXTURE3D {
                        1
                    } else {
                        u32::from(d.DepthOrArraySize)
                    };
                    u32::from(d.MipLevels) * layers
                };
                let parts = count(&of_from);
                if parts == 0 || parts > ALIAS_PARTS || parts != count(&of_to) {
                    return false;
                }
                let mut rows = [(); 2]
                    .map(|()| vec![D3D12_PLACED_SUBRESOURCE_FOOTPRINT::default(); parts as usize]);
                let mut bytes = [0u64; 2];
                // SAFETY: plain queries; the out pointers are ours and
                // hold `parts` layouts each.
                unsafe {
                    host.device.GetCopyableFootprints(
                        &of_from,
                        0,
                        parts,
                        0,
                        Some(rows[0].as_mut_ptr()),
                        None,
                        None,
                        Some(&mut bytes[0]),
                    );
                    host.device.GetCopyableFootprints(
                        &of_to,
                        0,
                        parts,
                        0,
                        Some(rows[1].as_mut_ptr()),
                        None,
                        None,
                        Some(&mut bytes[1]),
                    );
                }
                let alike = rows[0].iter().zip(&rows[1]).all(|(a, b)| {
                    let (fa, fb) = (a.Footprint, b.Footprint);
                    a.Offset == b.Offset
                        && (fa.Width, fa.Height, fa.Depth, fa.RowPitch)
                            == (fb.Width, fb.Height, fb.Depth, fb.RowPitch)
                });
                if bytes[0] == 0 || bytes[0] != bytes[1] || !alike {
                    return false;
                }
                let Some(buffer) = host.uav_buffer(bytes[0]) else {
                    return false;
                };
                crate::host::name(&buffer, || {
                    format!(
                        "alias copy {}x{} f{} to f{}",
                        of_from.Width, of_from.Height, of_from.Format.0, of_to.Format.0
                    )
                });
                tracing::info!(
                    view = ?placed,
                    texture = ?source,
```
