```rs
            let on = (EPOCH.get_or_init(std::time::Instant::now).elapsed().as_secs() / 20) % 2 == 1;
            static LAST: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU8 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU8::new(2);
            if LAST.swap(u8::from(on), std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) != u8::from(on) {
                tracing::info!(
                    "view memory stays known while its guard is open from now (VICTORY_VIEW_KNOWN=alt): {}",
                    if on { "ON" } else { "off, as usual" }
                );
            }
            on
        }
    }
}

static GUARDS: Mutex<Guards> = Mutex::new(Guards {
    protected: BTreeSet::new(),
    clean: BTreeSet::new(),
    absent: BTreeSet::new(),
    aliased: BTreeSet::new(),
    viewed: BTreeSet::new(),
});

fn guards() -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'static, Guards> {
    GUARDS.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

/// Whether the block `page` is read-only by our hand and unwritten since a
/// copy took it (diagnostics of `VICTORY_BACK_OWN_CHECK`).
pub(crate) fn clean(page: usize) -> bool {
    guards().clean.contains(&page)
}

/// For view memory: the pages of `[start, end)`'s blocks written since
/// they were last guarded (all of a block's pages), guarding them again
/// before the caller copies them. `None` if the memory is not a view.
fn guard(start: usize, end: usize) -> Option<Vec<usize>> {
    // A range whose first block the guards hold already (read-only by our
    // hand, or noted absent) is a view: no question to Windows. The
    // question walks the page tables to the end of the pages that share the
    // first one's state, and a guarded view is one long run of read-only
    // pages: 0.6 ms for the title's 174 MB heap, 16 times a frame, and most
    // of the 68 ms a frame of "guards" (run 58).
    // `VICTORY_GUARD_ASK=1` asks every time, as before.
    static ASK: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    let known = !*ASK.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_GUARD_ASK").is_some_and(|v| v == "1")) && {
        let g = guards();
        let first = start / BLOCK;
        g.protected.contains(&first) || g.absent.contains(&first) || (view_known() && g.viewed.contains(&first))
    };
    if !known && !is_view(start, end) {
        return None;
    }
    install();
    let mut g = guards();
    let mut written = Vec::new();
    let mut run: Option<usize> = None;
    let (first, last) = (start / BLOCK, end.div_ceil(BLOCK));
    // The range's clean blocks, in order: read off the set in one pass,
    // not looked up one block at a time. A frame asks about some 10 GB of
    // view memory, 150,000 blocks, nearly all clean: the lookups were most
    // of the 60-90 ms a frame of "guards" (run 54). What the loop adds to
    // the set meanwhile is the block it stands at or ones before it.
    let clean: Vec<usize> = g.clean.range(first..last).copied().collect();
    if clean.len() == last - first {
        // Nothing written, mapped or new since the range was last taken.
        return Some(written);
    }
    let mut next_clean = 0;
    let mut uncommitted_until = first;
    for block in first..=last {
        while next_clean < clean.len() && clean[next_clean] < block {
            next_clean += 1;
        }
        let is_clean = next_clean < clean.len() && clean[next_clean] == block;
        let mut open = block < last && !is_clean;
        if open && g.absent.contains(&block) {
            // Ordinary commits need no runtime mapping notification. Reuse
            // this asking's query for the following blocks in the same region.
            if block >= uncommitted_until {
                uncommitted_until = uncommitted_end(block);
            }
            open = block >= uncommitted_until;
            if open {
                g.absent.remove(&block);
            }
        }
        if open {
            written.extend(block * BLOCK / PAGE..(block + 1) * BLOCK / PAGE);
            if g.protected.contains(&block) {
                // Written through the runtime, still read-only.
                g.clean.insert(block);
            } else {
                run.get_or_insert(block);
                continue;
            }
        }
        if let Some(from) = run.take() {
            protect(&mut g, from, block);
        }
    }
    Some(written)
}

/// Whether `[start, end)` is view memory. The title's views lie in
/// placeholders, mapped and unmapped block by block as it streams, so a
/// range can begin in a block that is not mapped right now: the first
/// pages of the range that are there decide. A range with nothing there
/// counts as a view (its blocks are noted absent, and looked at again when
/// the runtime maps them).
///
/// Looking at the first address only took such a range for "not a view":
/// its copy was marked not watched for good and copied whole at every
/// refresh, around its unmapped pages (run 54: 300 such ranges, 570 MB
/// copied a frame for them, 255 copies a frame reading around holes).
/// `VICTORY_GUARD_HOLES=0` looks at the first address only, as before.
fn is_view(start: usize, end: usize) -> bool {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
        MEM_COMMIT, MEM_MAPPED, MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION, VirtualQuery,
    };
    static HOLES: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    let holes = *HOLES.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_GUARD_HOLES").is_none_or(|v| v != "0"));
    let mut at = start;
    loop {
        // SAFETY: plain data filled in by the query.
        let mut info: MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        // SAFETY: a valid out pointer of the right size.
        let n = unsafe { VirtualQuery(at as *const _, &mut info, size_of_val(&info)) };
        if n == 0 {
            return false;
        }
        if info.Type == MEM_MAPPED {
            return true;
        }
        // Committed memory that is no view (the title's heaps, ours), or
        // the answer as it was before.
        if info.State == MEM_COMMIT || !holes {
            return false;
        }
        // A hole (a placeholder, or free): on to what follows it.
        let next = (info.BaseAddress as usize).saturating_add(info.RegionSize);
        if next <= at || next >= end {
            return true;
        }
        at = next;
    }
}

/// Makes blocks `[from, to)` read-only and notes them guarded and clean;
/// block by block if they span views, leaving out any that fail, and
/// noting those not committed (unmapped) absent. The same physical pages
/// at every other view of them are made read-only too: a write through
/// one of those is this memory written, and only a fault can say so.
/// `VICTORY_VIEW_GUARD=0` leaves the other views as they are, as before.
fn protect(g: &mut Guards, from: usize, to: usize) {
    protect_here(g, from, to);
    if !view_guard() {
        return;
    }
    for (base, bytes) in crate::inplace::views_between(from.saturating_mul(BLOCK), to.saturating_mul(BLOCK)) {
        let first = (base / BLOCK).max(from);
        let last = (base.saturating_add(bytes).div_ceil(BLOCK)).min(to);
        for block in first..last {
            let shown = crate::inplace::pages_of(block * BLOCK);
            // One view (nothing else to guard), or the page the title shows
            // wherever it has nothing (thousands of views): each view of
            // that one is guarded by itself.
            if shown.len() < 2 || shown.len() > MANY_VIEWS {
                continue;
            }
            #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
            ALIASES[0].fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
            for alias in shown {
                let alias = alias / BLOCK;
                g.aliased.insert(alias);
                if alias != block {
                    protect_alias(g, alias);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Views of one page past which its views are not guarded together.
pub(crate) const MANY_VIEWS: usize = 64;

/// Whether all the views of a guarded page are guarded together
/// (`VICTORY_VIEW_GUARD`).
fn view_guard() -> bool {
    static ON: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_VIEW_GUARD").is_none_or(|v| v != "0"))
}

/// Diagnostics: blocks guarded together with their other views, blocks
/// opened because another view of theirs was written, and blocks opened
/// because a view of theirs was mapped; since the start.
#[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
pub(crate) static ALIASES: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64; 3] = [const { std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0) }; 3];

/// Makes `block` read-only: another view of pages a copy has just taken
/// through its own view, so that a write through this one faults too. It is
/// not noted clean. The copies of title memory at this view have not taken
/// the pages: noted clean, the block would not be reported written at their
/// next check and they would keep the bytes from before the write (`guard`
/// reports a block that is read-only and not clean as written, then notes it
/// clean). A block that is clean stays so: had the pages been written since
/// its copies took them, `open` would have opened it.
fn protect_alias(g: &mut Guards, block: usize) {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{PAGE_READONLY, VirtualProtect};
    if g.protected.contains(&block) {
        return;
    }
    let mut old = 0;
    // SAFETY: title view memory; only its protection changes.
    if unsafe { VirtualProtect((block * BLOCK) as *const _, BLOCK, PAGE_READONLY, &mut old) } != 0 {
        g.protected.insert(block);
        if view_known() {
            g.viewed.insert(block);
        }
    }
}

/// [`protect`] for one range, without the other views of its pages.
fn protect_here(g: &mut Guards, from: usize, to: usize) {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{PAGE_READONLY, VirtualProtect};
    let set = |from: usize, to: usize| {
        let mut old = 0;
        // SAFETY: title view memory; only its protection changes.
        unsafe {
            VirtualProtect(
                (from * BLOCK) as *const _,
                (to - from) * BLOCK,
                PAGE_READONLY,
                &mut old,
            ) != 0
        }
    };
    let note = |g: &mut Guards, from: usize, to: usize| {
        g.protected.extend(from..to);
        g.clean.extend(from..to);
        if view_known() {
            g.viewed.extend(from..to);
        }
    };
    if set(from, to) {
        note(g, from, to);
        return;
    }
    for block in from..to {
        if set(block, block + 1) {
            note(g, block, block + 1);
        } else {
            #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
            let error = std::io::Error::last_os_error();
            if block < uncommitted_end(block) {
                g.absent.insert(block);
            } else {
                // Diagnostics: a committed block that will not be made
                // read-only is reported written at every asking and never
                // known to the guards (one in 1,024 said).
                #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
                {
                    static N: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);
                    if N.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) % 1024 == 0 {
                        tracing::info!("a block of title memory could not be made read-only (one in 1024): {:#x}: {error}", block * BLOCK);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The end (exclusive) of the whole uncommitted blocks starting at `block`.
fn uncommitted_end(block: usize) -> usize {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
        MEM_FREE, MEM_RESERVE, MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION, VirtualQuery,
    };
    // SAFETY: plain data filled in by the query.
    let mut info: MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    // SAFETY: a valid out pointer of the right size.
    let n = unsafe { VirtualQuery((block * BLOCK) as *const _, &mut info, size_of_val(&info)) };
    if n != 0 && matches!(info.State, MEM_RESERVE | MEM_FREE) {
        (info.BaseAddress as usize).saturating_add(info.RegionSize) / BLOCK
    } else {
        block
    }
}

/// Gives write access back to the guarded blocks of `[start, end)` and
/// notes them written; true if any was guarded. The same physical pages at
/// every other view of them are opened too: the write that faulted (or is
/// ours, `crate::host::copy_mapped`) goes through one view, and every
/// guard over the pages must copy them again.
fn open(g: &mut Guards, start: usize, end: usize) -> bool {
    let any = open_here(g, start, end);
    if start >= end || g.aliased.is_empty() {
        return any;
    }
    let aliased: Vec<usize> = g.aliased.range(start / BLOCK..end.div_ceil(BLOCK)).copied().collect();
    for block in aliased {
        g.aliased.remove(&block);
        for alias in crate::inplace::pages_of(block * BLOCK) {
            if alias / BLOCK != block && open_here(g, alias, alias.saturating_add(BLOCK)) {
                #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
                ALIASES[1].fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
            }
            g.aliased.remove(&(alias / BLOCK));
        }
    }
    any
}

/// [`open`] for one range, without the other views of its pages.
fn open_here(g: &mut Guards, start: usize, end: usize) -> bool {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{PAGE_READWRITE, VirtualProtect};
    let blocks: Vec<usize> = g
        .protected
        .range(start / BLOCK..end.div_ceil(BLOCK))
        .copied()
        .collect();
    for &block in &blocks {
        g.protected.remove(&block);
        g.clean.remove(&block);
        let mut old = 0;
        // SAFETY: a block we made read-only.
        unsafe { VirtualProtect((block * BLOCK) as *const _, BLOCK, PAGE_READWRITE, &mut old) };
    }
    !blocks.is_empty()
}

/// Before our own write into title memory `[at, at + len)` through the
/// kernel (which does not fault into our handler): opens its guarded blocks.
/// The runtime calls it (as `kernel_will_write`) before the title's kernel
/// reads into its own memory.
pub fn writing(at: usize, len: usize) {
    // The length is the title's (`fread`'s size times count, saturated).
    open(&mut guards(), at, at.saturating_add(len));
    // A placed texture there changes with no descriptor written.
    crate::descriptor::host::remapped(at, len);
}

/// What `VICTORY_PAGE_WRITES` asks to be done with a write the guards do
/// not see once its bytes are there ([`title_memory_written`]), as bits:
/// 1, the guarded blocks under it are opened and count as written (host
/// copies of buffers and textures read through tables take them again);
/// 2, the placed textures picked by index that lie under it are due again;
/// 4, both also for reads to plain addresses when they have finished.
/// Unset or `guards`: bit 1 alone. `0`: nothing, counted only (the default
/// until run 199). `1`: bits 1 and 2. `slots`: bit 2 alone. `all`:
/// everything.
/// (Bit 1 by default: in every run 10,000 to 50,000 guarded blocks of host
/// copies lay under such writes and kept the bytes from before; runs 197
/// and 198 opened them, 9,766 and 10,796 blocks, with nothing worse for
/// it. Bit 2 makes texture slots due and is the one that flooded the
/// queue in an earlier form: still asked for by name.)
pub(crate) fn page_writes() -> u8 {
    static MODE: std::sync::OnceLock<u8> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *MODE.get_or_init(|| match std::env::var("VICTORY_PAGE_WRITES").as_deref().map(str::trim) {
        Ok("0") => 0,
        Ok("1") => 3,
        Ok("slots") => 2,
        Ok("all") => 7,
        _ => 1,
    })
}

/// Since the start: writes into physical pages through the runtime's own
/// views that landed at addresses the title has mapped (one for each run
/// of addresses); their bytes; guarded blocks that lay under them (host
/// copies that would otherwise keep the bytes from before); reads to
/// plain addresses that finished.
pub(crate) static WRITTEN: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64; 4] = [const { std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0) }; 4];

/// The bytes of a write the guards do not see are there: title memory
/// `[at, at + len)`. `pages`: DirectStorage wrote them into physical pages
/// through a view of the runtime's own, and this is an address where the
/// title has those pages mapped (no title address faulted, nothing was
/// mapped or unmapped; the shortcut this file's header names). Otherwise a
/// read to a plain address has finished, of which [`writing`] was told
/// before it began.
///
/// Upstream's c75fdba does the same for its trackers (its `Writing` marks
/// the pages once more when dropped; page destinations are reported at
/// each address showing them). Here it is counted always and acted on as
/// [`page_writes`] says. Called without the runtime's page-table lock;
/// takes the guards' lock, then, alone, the lock of the ranges kept for
/// the texture pass.
pub fn title_memory_written(at: usize, len: usize, pages: bool) {
    use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
    if len == 0 {
        return;
    }
    let mode = page_writes();
    let end = at.saturating_add(len);
    if pages {
        WRITTEN[0].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
        WRITTEN[1].fetch_add(len as u64, Relaxed);
    } else {
        WRITTEN[3].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
        if mode & 4 == 0 {
            return;
        }
    }
    {
        let mut g = guards();
        let guarded = g.protected.range(at / BLOCK..end.div_ceil(BLOCK)).count() as u64;
        if pages {
            WRITTEN[2].fetch_add(guarded, Relaxed);
        }
        if mode & 1 != 0 && guarded != 0 {
            open(&mut g, at, end);
        }
    }
    // A placed texture there changed with no descriptor written.
    crate::descriptor::host::page_written(at, len);
}

/// The runtime mapped a view of the physical bytes `[offset, offset + len)`
/// of `section` (`crate::inplace::title_memory_view`): the view is
/// writable, so the same bytes guarded at another view must be checked
/// again — and are, the pages noted written, which also has the next check
/// guard the new view (`protect`).
pub(crate) fn views_mapped(section: usize, offset: u64, len: usize) {
    if !view_guard() {
        return;
    }
    let ranges = crate::inplace::views_of_section(section, offset, len);
    if ranges.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let mut g = guards();
    for &(at, n) in &ranges {
        if open_here(&mut g, at, at.saturating_add(n)) {
            #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
            ALIASES[2].fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
    }
}

/// Held shared by a read of title memory in place, and alone by the runtime
/// while it changes what title memory shows.
///
/// The runtime does not change a mapping in one step. To unmap one page of
/// a view it unmaps the whole view and maps what stays again
/// (`xmem.rs` `unmap`), and a view it maps is a reservation until the next
/// call commits it (`map`, then `commit`). For that moment pages the title
/// never gave up are "reserved, never committed", and a thread reading
/// them in place takes an access violation: run 71 in `Layout::detile`,
/// run 74 in the hash before it, both under `Staging::refresh_now`, which
/// had asked whether the texture was all mapped and been told yes. Asking
/// cannot help; not changing the mapping while such a read is under way
/// does.
static MAPPING: std::sync::RwLock<()> = std::sync::RwLock::new(());

/// What the runtime holds while it changes what title memory shows
/// ([`title_memory_remapping`]).
pub struct Remapping(#[allow(dead_code)] std::sync::RwLockWriteGuard<'static, ()>, std::time::Instant);

impl Drop for Remapping {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // From asking for the lock until it is let go (the frame log).
        crate::framelog::add(crate::framelog::T::RemapUs, self.1.elapsed().as_micros() as u64);
    }
}

/// The runtime is about to map, unmap or move physical pages of title
/// memory: until what it returns is dropped, no read of title memory in
/// place is under way and none begins ([`title_memory_reading`]). Taken
/// around the whole change, the unmapping and the mapping again.
pub fn title_memory_remapping() -> Remapping {
    let asked = std::time::Instant::now();
    let held = MAPPING.write().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    crate::framelog::add(crate::framelog::T::Remaps, 1);
    crate::framelog::add(crate::framelog::T::RemapWaitUs, asked.elapsed().as_micros() as u64);
    Remapping(held, asked)
}

/// What a read of title memory in place holds ([`title_memory_reading`]).
pub struct Reading(#[allow(dead_code)] std::sync::RwLockReadGuard<'static, ()>);

/// For reading title memory in place: until what it returns is dropped,
/// the runtime changes no mapping, so memory found mapped stays mapped.
/// Not to be taken twice by one thread, nor held across anything that
/// maps title memory.
pub fn title_memory_reading() -> Reading {
    Reading(MAPPING.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()))
}

/// [`title_memory_reading`] if it can be had at once: `None` while the
/// runtime changes a mapping (or waits to), for a caller that has another
/// way to read and would rather not wait.
pub fn title_memory_reading_now() -> Option<Reading> {
    match MAPPING.try_read() {
        Ok(guard) => Some(Reading(guard)),
        Err(std::sync::TryLockError::Poisoned(e)) => Some(Reading(e.into_inner())),
        Err(std::sync::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => None,
    }
}

/// The runtime mapped or unmapped title memory `[at, at + len)`: what it
/// shows is new and read-write, so it is no longer guarded (nor known
/// unmapped).
pub fn title_memory_remapped(at: usize, len: usize) {
    // Stored pages followed there end (`VICTORY_BACK_READS`): counted only.
    #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
    crate::backreads::remapped(at, len);
    crate::texback::remapped(at, len);
    // A placed texture there arrives, goes or changes with no descriptor
    // written.
    crate::descriptor::host::remapped(at, len);
    // The views the runtime told us of there are no longer what it shows.
    crate::inplace::views_gone(at, len);
    // And nothing stays in place over it.
    crate::inplace::title_memory_freeing(at, len);
    let mut g = guards();
    let range = at / BLOCK..at.saturating_add(len).div_ceil(BLOCK);
    let absent: Vec<usize> = g.absent.range(range.clone()).copied().collect();
    for block in absent {
        g.absent.remove(&block);
    }
    let blocks: Vec<usize> = g.protected.range(range).copied().collect();
    for block in blocks {
        g.protected.remove(&block);
        g.clean.remove(&block);
    }
    let aliased: Vec<usize> = g.aliased.range(at / BLOCK..at.saturating_add(len).div_ceil(BLOCK)).copied().collect();
    for block in aliased {
        g.aliased.remove(&block);
    }
    if view_known() {
        // The runtime calls this for two things only (`xmem`: `map` and
        // `unmap`): a range it has just mapped a section's pages into,
        // and a view it is about to make a placeholder again. Either way
        // what stands there is view memory or a hole in it, which is what
        // `is_view` would answer for a range that begins there; and the
        // write watch's asking can only fail there. The title remaps some
        // 83 times a frame, and each time the blocks were forgotten, so
        // that the next asking about each range went to the kernel twice
        // (run 235: 266 to 565 failed askings a frame with the blocks
        // remembered from their guards alone, no fewer than without).
        g.viewed.extend(at / BLOCK..at.saturating_add(len).div_ceil(BLOCK));
        return;
    }
    // What the range shows is new: no longer known to be a view.
    let viewed: Vec<usize> = g.viewed.range(at / BLOCK..at.saturating_add(len).div_ceil(BLOCK)).copied().collect();
    for block in viewed {
        g.viewed.remove(&block);
    }
}

/// Registers the handler that takes writes to guarded blocks, once, ahead
/// of the crash reporter's.
fn install() {
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION, NTSTATUS};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::{
        AddVectoredExceptionHandler, EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION, EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH,
        EXCEPTION_POINTERS,
    };
    unsafe extern "system" fn on_write(info: *mut EXCEPTION_POINTERS) -> i32 {
        // SAFETY: the system passes the exception being dispatched.
        let r = unsafe { &*(*info).ExceptionRecord };
        const WRITE: usize = 1;
        if r.ExceptionCode != EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION as NTSTATUS
            || r.NumberParameters < 2
            || r.ExceptionInformation[0] != WRITE
        {
            return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
        }
        let at = r.ExceptionInformation[1];
        // Held across both checks: another thread may have opened the block
        // since this one faulted, and a copy may have guarded it again since
        // (then it is ours again, not read-only for some other reason).
        let mut g = guards();
        if open(&mut g, at, at + 1) {
            #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
            crate::copystat::add(crate::copystat::C::GuardFaults, 1);
            crate::framelog::add(crate::framelog::T::GuardFaults, 1);
            return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION;
        }
        if writable(at) {
            EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION
        } else {
            EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH
        }
    }
    static ONCE: std::sync::Once = std::sync::Once::new();
    // SAFETY: the handler only touches our guard state and protections.
    ONCE.call_once(|| unsafe {
        AddVectoredExceptionHandler(1, Some(on_write));
    });
}

/// Whether `at` is committed read-write memory now.
fn writable(at: usize) -> bool {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
        MEM_COMMIT, MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION, PAGE_READWRITE, VirtualQuery,
    };
    // SAFETY: plain data filled in by the query.
    let mut info: MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    // SAFETY: a valid out pointer of the right size.
    let n = unsafe { VirtualQuery(at as *const _, &mut info, size_of_val(&info)) };
    n != 0 && info.State == MEM_COMMIT && info.Protect == PAGE_READWRITE
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
        MEM_COMMIT, MEM_RELEASE, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE, VirtualAlloc, VirtualFree,
    };
    const MEM_WRITE_WATCH: u32 = 0x20_0000;

    #[test]
    fn written_pages_are_reported_to_every_asker() {
        // SAFETY: a fresh write-watched allocation, freed at the end.
        let p = unsafe {
            VirtualAlloc(
                std::ptr::null(),
                4 * PAGE,
                MEM_RESERVE | MEM_COMMIT | MEM_WRITE_WATCH,
                PAGE_READWRITE,
            )
        } as usize;
        assert_ne!(p, 0);
        let (start, end) = (p, p + 4 * PAGE);
        let (_, before) = writes(start, end, false).expect("watched");
        assert!(before.is_empty());
        // SAFETY: committed pages of ours.
        unsafe { ((p + PAGE + 8) as *mut u8).write(1) };
        let (now, after) = writes(start, end, false).expect("watched");
        assert_eq!(after, [(p / PAGE + 1, now)]);
        // Another asker after the kernel's bit was cleared still sees it.
        let (later, again) = writes(p + PAGE, p + 2 * PAGE, false).expect("watched");
        assert!(later > now);
        assert_eq!(again, [(p / PAGE + 1, now)]);
        let mut plain = vec![0u8; PAGE];
        assert!(
            writes(
                plain.as_mut_ptr() as usize,
                plain.as_ptr() as usize + PAGE,
                true
            )
            .is_none()
        );
        // SAFETY: our allocation.
        unsafe { VirtualFree(p as *mut _, 0, MEM_RELEASE) };
    }

    /// A kernel read into a guarded view block fails; opened first, it
    /// lands and the block counts as written.
    #[test]
    fn kernel_reads_into_guarded_blocks_after_opening() {
        use std::io::{Read, Seek, Write};
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
            CreateFileMappingW, FILE_MAP_WRITE, MapViewOfFile, UnmapViewOfFile,
        };
        // SAFETY: a pagefile section of two blocks, mapped read-write.
        let view = unsafe {
            let section = CreateFileMappingW(
                -1isize as _,
                std::ptr::null(),
                PAGE_READWRITE,
                0,
                (2 * BLOCK) as u32,
                std::ptr::null(),
            );
            assert!(!section.is_null());
            MapViewOfFile(section, FILE_MAP_WRITE, 0, 0, 2 * BLOCK).Value as usize
        };
        assert_ne!(view, 0);
        assert!(guard(view, view + 2 * BLOCK).is_some()); // now read-only
        let mut file = tempfile::tempfile().unwrap();
        file.write_all(b"from the disk").unwrap();
        // `ReadFile` inside: the kernel writes the view.
        let read = |file: &mut std::fs::File| {
            file.rewind().unwrap();
            // SAFETY: 13 bytes of our view, nothing else refers to them.
            let into = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut((view + 100) as *mut u8, 13) };
            file.read(into).is_ok_and(|n| n == 13)
        };
        assert!(
            !read(&mut file),
            "the kernel does not fault into our handler"
        );
        writing(view + 100, 13);
        assert!(read(&mut file));
        // SAFETY: the bytes just read.
        let landed = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts((view + 100) as *const u8, 13) };
        assert_eq!(landed, b"from the disk");
        assert_eq!(
            guard(view, view + 2 * BLOCK),
            Some((view / PAGE..view / PAGE + 1).collect())
        );
        // SAFETY: our view.
        unsafe {
            UnmapViewOfFile(
                windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::MEMORY_MAPPED_VIEW_ADDRESS {
                    Value: view as *mut _,
                },
            )
        };
        title_memory_remapped(view, 2 * BLOCK);
    }

    #[test]
    fn writes_in_partly_committed_view_blocks_are_reported() {
        use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{CloseHandle, INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE};
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
            CreateFileMappingW, FILE_MAP_WRITE, MEMORY_MAPPED_VIEW_ADDRESS, MapViewOfFile,
            SEC_RESERVE, UnmapViewOfFile,
        };

        const SIZE: usize = 3 * BLOCK;
        struct View(MEMORY_MAPPED_VIEW_ADDRESS);
        impl Drop for View {
            fn drop(&mut self) {
                title_memory_remapped(self.0.Value as usize, SIZE);
                // SAFETY: our view is still mapped.
                unsafe { UnmapViewOfFile(self.0) };
            }
        }
        // SAFETY: a new reserved pagefile section. The view holds its own
        // reference after we close the handle, including on assertion failure.
        let view = unsafe {
            let section = CreateFileMappingW(
                INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE,
                std::ptr::null(),
                PAGE_READWRITE | SEC_RESERVE,
                0,
                SIZE as u32,
                std::ptr::null(),
            );
            assert!(!section.is_null());
            let view = MapViewOfFile(section, FILE_MAP_WRITE, 0, 0, SIZE);
            CloseHandle(section);
            assert!(!view.Value.is_null());
            View(view)
        };
        let start = view.0.Value as usize;
        let commit = |at: usize, len| {
            // SAFETY: these pages belong to our reserved view.
            let committed = unsafe { VirtualAlloc(at as _, len, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE) };
            assert_eq!(committed as usize, at);
        };
        let early = start + BLOCK + 3 * KERNEL_PAGE;
        let late = start + 2 * BLOCK + 3 * KERNEL_PAGE;
        commit(start, BLOCK);
        commit(early, KERNEL_PAGE);
        let refresh = || guard(start, start + SIZE).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(refresh(), [start / PAGE, early / PAGE, late / PAGE]);
        // The last block is still entirely reserved.
        assert!(!refresh().contains(&(late / PAGE)));

        commit(late, KERNEL_PAGE); // Ordinary commit, without a runtime mapping notification.
        for at in [early, late] {
            assert!(writable(at));
            // SAFETY: each address is inside its committed read-write page.
            unsafe { (at as *mut u8).write_volatile(1) };
        }
        assert_eq!(refresh(), [early / PAGE, late / PAGE]);
    }

    /// A range of view memory whose first block is not mapped is a view
    /// all the same: its blocks are reported once, then the ones written
    /// or mapped since.
    #[test]
    fn a_range_that_begins_in_an_unmapped_block_is_guarded() {
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
            CreateFileMappingW, MEM_PRESERVE_PLACEHOLDER, MEM_REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER,
            MEM_RESERVE_PLACEHOLDER, MapViewOfFile3, PAGE_NOACCESS, UnmapViewOfFile2,
            VirtualAlloc2,
        };
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcess;
        // SAFETY: a fresh placeholder of three blocks and a pagefile
        // section of three; the middle block is mapped first.
        let (p, section) = unsafe {
            let p = VirtualAlloc2(
                GetCurrentProcess(),
                std::ptr::null(),
                3 * BLOCK,
                MEM_RESERVE | MEM_RESERVE_PLACEHOLDER,
                PAGE_NOACCESS,
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                0,
            ) as usize;
            assert_ne!(p, 0);
            let section = CreateFileMappingW(
                -1isize as _,
                std::ptr::null(),
                PAGE_READWRITE,
                0,
                (3 * BLOCK) as u32,
                std::ptr::null(),
            );
            assert!(!section.is_null());
            (p, section)
        };
        let map = |block: usize| {
            // SAFETY: splits the placeholder at the block and maps the
            // section's block there.
            let view = unsafe {
                VirtualFree(
                    (p + block * BLOCK) as *mut _,
                    BLOCK,
                    MEM_RELEASE | MEM_PRESERVE_PLACEHOLDER,
                );
                MapViewOfFile3(
                    section,
                    GetCurrentProcess(),
                    (p + block * BLOCK) as *const _,
                    (block * BLOCK) as u64,
                    BLOCK,
                    MEM_REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER,
                    PAGE_READWRITE,
                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
                    0,
                )
            };
            assert_eq!(view.Value as usize, p + block * BLOCK);
            view
        };
        let pages = |block: usize| (p + block * BLOCK) / PAGE..(p + (block + 1) * BLOCK) / PAGE;
        let all: Vec<usize> = (0..3).flat_map(pages).collect();
        // Nothing mapped at all: a view with every block absent.
        assert!(is_view(p, p + 3 * BLOCK));
        let middle = map(1);
        title_memory_remapped(p + BLOCK, BLOCK);
        // The range begins in the placeholder, its middle block is a view.
        assert!(is_view(p, p + 3 * BLOCK));
        assert_eq!(guard(p, p + 3 * BLOCK), Some(all));
        assert_eq!(guard(p, p + 3 * BLOCK), Some(Vec::new()), "nothing written since");
        // SAFETY: inside the mapped middle block.
        unsafe { ((p + BLOCK + 8) as *mut u8).write_volatile(1) };
        assert_eq!(guard(p, p + 3 * BLOCK), Some(pages(1).collect()));
        let first = map(0);
        title_memory_remapped(p, BLOCK);
        assert_eq!(guard(p, p + 3 * BLOCK), Some(pages(0).collect()));
        assert_eq!(guard(p, p + 3 * BLOCK), Some(Vec::new()));
        // Memory of ours that is no view stays none.
        let mut local = [0u8; 16];
        let at = local.as_mut_ptr() as usize;
        assert!(!is_view(at, at + local.len()));
        // SAFETY: our views and placeholder.
        unsafe {
            UnmapViewOfFile2(GetCurrentProcess(), first, MEM_PRESERVE_PLACEHOLDER);
            UnmapViewOfFile2(GetCurrentProcess(), middle, MEM_PRESERVE_PLACEHOLDER);
            for block in 0..3 {
                VirtualFree((p + block * BLOCK) as *mut _, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
            }
            windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle(section);
        }
        title_memory_remapped(p, 3 * BLOCK);
    }

    /// Blocks of a placeholder between views are reported once, then not
    /// again (they cannot be guarded) until the runtime maps them.
    #[test]
    fn unmapped_blocks_are_reported_once_until_mapped() {
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
            CreateFileMappingW, MEM_PRESERVE_PLACEHOLDER, MEM_REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER,
            MEM_RESERVE_PLACEHOLDER, MapViewOfFile3, PAGE_NOACCESS, UnmapViewOfFile2,
            VirtualAlloc2,
        };
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcess;
        // SAFETY: a fresh placeholder of three blocks and a pagefile
        // section of two; block 0 shows the section's first block, as the
        // runtime maps physical pages.
        let (p, section) = unsafe {
            let p = VirtualAlloc2(
                GetCurrentProcess(),
                std::ptr::null(),
                3 * BLOCK,
                MEM_RESERVE | MEM_RESERVE_PLACEHOLDER,
                PAGE_NOACCESS,
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                0,
            ) as usize;
            assert_ne!(p, 0);
            let section = CreateFileMappingW(
                -1isize as _,
                std::ptr::null(),
                PAGE_READWRITE,
                0,
                (2 * BLOCK) as u32,
                std::ptr::null(),
            );
            assert!(!section.is_null());
            (p, section)
        };
        let map = |block: usize| {
            // SAFETY: splits the placeholder at the block and maps the
            // section's block there.
            let view = unsafe {
                VirtualFree(
                    (p + block * BLOCK) as *mut _,
                    BLOCK,
                    MEM_RELEASE | MEM_PRESERVE_PLACEHOLDER,
                );
                MapViewOfFile3(
                    section,
                    GetCurrentProcess(),
                    (p + block * BLOCK) as *const _,
                    (block * BLOCK) as u64,
                    BLOCK,
                    MEM_REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER,
                    PAGE_READWRITE,
                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
                    0,
                )
            };
            assert_eq!(view.Value as usize, p + block * BLOCK);
            view
        };
        let first = map(0);
        let pages = |block: usize| (p + block * BLOCK) / PAGE..(p + (block + 1) * BLOCK) / PAGE;
        let all: Vec<usize> = (0..3).flat_map(pages).collect();
        assert_eq!(guard(p, p + 3 * BLOCK), Some(all));
        assert_eq!(
            guard(p, p + 3 * BLOCK),
            Some(Vec::new()),
            "nothing written since"
        );
        let second = map(1);
        title_memory_remapped(p + BLOCK, BLOCK);
        assert_eq!(guard(p, p + 3 * BLOCK), Some(pages(1).collect()));
        assert_eq!(guard(p, p + 3 * BLOCK), Some(Vec::new()));
        // SAFETY: our views and placeholder.
        unsafe {
            UnmapViewOfFile2(GetCurrentProcess(), first, MEM_PRESERVE_PLACEHOLDER);
            UnmapViewOfFile2(GetCurrentProcess(), second, MEM_PRESERVE_PLACEHOLDER);
            for block in 0..3 {
                VirtualFree((p + block * BLOCK) as *mut _, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
            }
            windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle(section);
        }
        title_memory_remapped(p, 3 * BLOCK);
    }

    /// A pagefile section mapped twice: two views of the same physical
    /// pages, the second left for the test; the section handle, the two
    /// addresses.
    fn two_views(bytes: usize) -> (usize, usize, usize) {
        use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
            CreateFileMappingW, FILE_MAP_WRITE, MapViewOfFile,
        };
        // SAFETY: a fresh pagefile section, mapped twice; the views keep
        // the section alive and the handle is closed by the caller.
        unsafe {
            let section = CreateFileMappingW(
                INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE,
                std::ptr::null(),
                PAGE_READWRITE,
                0,
                bytes as u32,
                std::ptr::null(),
            );
            assert!(!section.is_null());
            let one = MapViewOfFile(section, FILE_MAP_WRITE, 0, 0, bytes).Value as usize;
            let two = MapViewOfFile(section, FILE_MAP_WRITE, 0, 0, bytes).Value as usize;
            assert_ne!(one, 0);
            assert_ne!(two, 0);
            crate::inplace::title_memory_view(one, bytes, section as usize, 0);
            crate::inplace::title_memory_view(two, bytes, section as usize, 0);
            (section as usize, one, two)
        }
    }

    /// The section of [`two_views`] is closed and its views unmapped; the
    /// guard is told they are gone first.
    fn drop_views(section: usize, views: &[usize], bytes: usize) {
        use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle;
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{MEMORY_MAPPED_VIEW_ADDRESS, UnmapViewOfFile};
        for &view in views {
            title_memory_remapped(view, bytes);
            // SAFETY: a view of the section mapped by `two_views`.
            unsafe {
                UnmapViewOfFile(MEMORY_MAPPED_VIEW_ADDRESS {
                    Value: view as *mut _,
                })
            };
        }
        // SAFETY: the section's last reference.
        unsafe { CloseHandle(section as *mut std::ffi::c_void) };
    }

    /// The title wrote the pages of a guarded texture through another view
    /// of them: the fault at that view is the guard's to see, and the
    /// guarded view's next check reports the pages written.
    #[test]
    fn a_write_through_another_view_is_reported_at_the_guarded_one() {
        const SIZE: usize = 2 * BLOCK;
        let (section, guarded, other) = two_views(SIZE);
        let pages = |block: usize| (guarded + block * BLOCK) / PAGE;
        // The first check takes it in (and every view of its pages).
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(0), pages(1)]));
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(Vec::new()), "nothing written yet");
        // Writing through the other view faults into the handler, which
        // opens that view and the guarded one: the next check sees it.
        // SAFETY: the second view, read-write once the handler has opened it.
        unsafe { ((other + BLOCK + 8) as *mut u8).write(1) };
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(1)]));
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(Vec::new()));
        drop_views(section, &[guarded, other], SIZE);
    }

    /// A view of guarded pages is mapped anew: it is writable, so the
    /// guarded view checks its pages again (and guards the new view).
    #[test]
    fn a_view_mapped_beside_a_guarded_one_makes_it_check_again() {
        const SIZE: usize = 2 * BLOCK;
        let (section, guarded, other) = two_views(SIZE);
        let pages = |block: usize| (guarded + block * BLOCK) / PAGE;
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(0), pages(1)]));
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(Vec::new()), "nothing written yet");
        title_memory_remapped(other, SIZE);
        crate::inplace::title_memory_view(other, SIZE, section, 0);
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(0), pages(1)]));
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(Vec::new()));
        drop_views(section, &[guarded, other], SIZE);
    }

    /// A write of the runtime's own, told at one view of the pages
    /// (`writing`): the other views' next checks report the pages written.
    #[test]
    fn a_write_told_at_one_view_is_reported_at_the_others() {
        const SIZE: usize = 2 * BLOCK;
        let (section, guarded, other) = two_views(SIZE);
        let pages = |block: usize| (guarded + block * BLOCK) / PAGE;
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(0), pages(1)]));
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(Vec::new()), "nothing written yet");
        writing(other + BLOCK, BLOCK);
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(1)]));
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(Vec::new()));
        // Half a page and the next: both blocks, not just the first's.
        writing(other + BLOCK / 2, BLOCK);
        assert_eq!(guard(guarded, guarded + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(0), pages(1)]));
        drop_views(section, &[guarded, other], SIZE);
    }

    /// Both views of the pages are checked, each for a copy of its own
    /// (the title shows one physical page at several addresses, and each
    /// address has its host copy): a write through either is reported at
    /// both, whichever is checked first. Guarding the pages for the first
    /// view's check must not note the second view clean, or its copy would
    /// keep the bytes from before the write.
    #[test]
    fn a_write_is_reported_at_every_checked_view() {
        const SIZE: usize = 2 * BLOCK;
        let (section, one, two) = two_views(SIZE);
        let pages = |view: usize, block: usize| (view + block * BLOCK) / PAGE;
        assert_eq!(guard(one, one + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(one, 0), pages(one, 1)]));
        assert_eq!(guard(two, two + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(two, 0), pages(two, 1)]), "the second view's first check");
        assert_eq!(guard(one, one + SIZE), Some(Vec::new()), "nothing written yet");
        assert_eq!(guard(two, two + SIZE), Some(Vec::new()), "nothing written yet");
        // SAFETY: the second view, read-write once the handler has opened it.
        unsafe { ((two + BLOCK + 8) as *mut u8).write(1) };
        assert_eq!(guard(one, one + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(one, 1)]));
        assert_eq!(guard(two, two + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(two, 1)]), "written through this view, checked second");
        // SAFETY: the first view, as above.
        unsafe { ((one + 8) as *mut u8).write(1) };
        assert_eq!(guard(two, two + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(two, 0)]));
        assert_eq!(guard(one, one + SIZE), Some(vec![pages(one, 0)]), "written through this view, checked second");
        assert_eq!(guard(one, one + SIZE), Some(Vec::new()));
        assert_eq!(guard(two, two + SIZE), Some(Vec::new()));
        drop_views(section, &[one, two], SIZE);
    }

    /// A page shown in more than `MANY_VIEWS` views is guarded at each by
    /// itself: the others stay writable, and nothing looks through them all.
    #[test]
    fn a_page_of_many_views_is_guarded_one_view_at_a_time() {
        let (section, one, two) = two_views(BLOCK);
        let filler = one + (1 << 45);
        for n in 0..MANY_VIEWS {
            crate::inplace::title_memory_view(filler + n * BLOCK, BLOCK, section, 0);
        }
        assert_eq!(guard(one, one + BLOCK), Some(vec![one / PAGE]));
        assert!(writable(two), "another view of it is left alone");
        // SAFETY: the guarded view, opened by the handler.
        unsafe { ((one + 8) as *mut u8).write(1) };
        assert_eq!(guard(one, one + BLOCK), Some(vec![one / PAGE]));
        title_memory_remapped(filler, MANY_VIEWS * BLOCK);
        drop_views(section, &[one, two], BLOCK);
    }

    /// A write or mapping that runs past the end of the address space (a
    /// title's `fread` with a huge count) covers up to the end; the sum used
    /// to overflow. Up there no test has guarded blocks.
    #[test]
    fn ranges_past_the_address_space_end_do_not_overflow() {
        let top = usize::MAX - 16;
        writing(top, PAGE);
        title_memory_remapped(top, usize::MAX);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod mapping_tests {
    use super::{title_memory_reading, title_memory_remapping};
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
    use std::sync::{Arc, mpsc};
    use std::time::Duration;

    /// A change of mapping waits for a read in place that is under way, and
    /// a read in place waits for a change of mapping.
    #[test]
    fn reads_in_place_and_remappings_wait_for_each_other() {
        // A reader holds; the change does not begin until it lets go.
        let changed = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let reading = title_memory_reading();
        let (began, wait) = mpsc::channel();
        let change = {
            let changed = changed.clone();
            std::thread::spawn(move || {
                began.send(()).unwrap();
                let _changing = title_memory_remapping();
                changed.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
            })
        };
        wait.recv().unwrap();
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
        assert!(!changed.load(Ordering::SeqCst), "the mapping changed under a read in place");
        drop(reading);
        change.join().unwrap();
        assert!(changed.load(Ordering::SeqCst));
        // A change holds; the read does not begin until it is done.
        let read = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let changing = title_memory_remapping();
        let (began, wait) = mpsc::channel();
        let reader = {
            let read = read.clone();
            std::thread::spawn(move || {
                began.send(()).unwrap();
                let _reading = title_memory_reading();
                read.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
            })
        };
        wait.recv().unwrap();
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
        assert!(!read.load(Ordering::SeqCst), "a read in place began during a change of mapping");
        drop(changing);
        reader.join().unwrap();
        assert!(read.load(Ordering::SeqCst));
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-hle/src/host.rs`:

```rs
//! Pass-through to the host's own implementation of shared APIs.

use victory_pe::ImportSymbol;

/// Which DLLs may be satisfied by the host's own implementation.
///
/// Console titles link mostly against Windows API sets that behave the same
/// on PC. Passing those through lets bring-up focus on what really differs.
/// Anything whose semantics differ on console (memory, files, threads) is
/// overridden in `modules`, which always wins over the host.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct HostPolicy {
    /// Lower-case patterns; a trailing `*` matches a prefix.
    pub allow: Vec<String>,
}

impl Default for HostPolicy {
    fn default() -> Self {
        let allow = [
            "api-ms-win-core-*",
            "api-ms-win-eventing-*",
            "api-ms-win-security-*",
            "api-ms-win-crt-*",
            "kernel32.dll",
            "kernelbase.dll",
            "ntdll.dll",
            "ucrtbase.dll",
            "vcruntime140*",
            "msvcp140*",
            // Off-machine traffic is refused in `modules::net`.
            "ws2_32.dll",
            "bcrypt.dll",
            "crypt32.dll",
            "ncrypt.dll",
            "winhttp.dll",
            "sspicli.dll",
            "cabinet.dll",
            "avrt.dll",
            // Window, message and shell APIs: the host's desktop window
            // stands in for the console's single core window.
            "ext-ms-win-rtcore-ntuser-*",
            "api-ms-win-shcore-*",
            "msvcp_win.dll",
            "ole32.dll",
            "advapi32.dll",
            "iphlpapi.dll",
            // The title's crash handler writes minidumps with it (loaded by name).
            "dbghelp.dll",
            // Same APIs as the console's (XAudio2 ordinal 1 is XAudio2Create
            // on both); Media Foundation reads local media files.
            "xaudio2_9.dll",
            "mfplat.dll",
            "mfreadwrite.dll",
        ];
        HostPolicy {
            allow: allow.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),
        }
    }
}

impl HostPolicy {
    /// No pass-through at all: shows the full surface a title needs.
    pub fn none() -> Self {
        HostPolicy { allow: Vec::new() }
    }

    pub fn allows(&self, dll: &str) -> bool {
        let dll = dll.to_ascii_lowercase();
        self.allow
            .iter()
            .any(|pattern| match pattern.strip_suffix('*') {
                Some(prefix) => dll.starts_with(prefix),
                None => dll == *pattern,
            })
    }

    pub(crate) fn resolve(&self, dll: &str, symbol: &ImportSymbol) -> Option<usize> {
        if !self.allows(dll) {
            return None;
        }
        imp::resolve(dll, symbol)
    }
}

/// The host's own `name` from the System32 DLL `dll`: what a title import
/// of it is bound to when we do not override it.
pub(crate) fn function(dll: &str, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    let name = ImportSymbol::Name {
        hint: 0,
        name: name.into(),
    };
    imp::resolve(dll, &name)
}

#[cfg(windows)]
mod imp {
    use std::collections::HashMap;
    use std::ffi::CString;
    use std::sync::{LazyLock, Mutex};

    use victory_pe::ImportSymbol;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::{
        GetProcAddress, LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32, LoadLibraryExA,
    };

    /// Module handles by lower-case DLL name (stored as usize: Send + Sync).
    static MODULES: LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<String, usize>>> = LazyLock::new(Default::default);

    pub(super) fn resolve(dll: &str, symbol: &ImportSymbol) -> Option<usize> {
        let module = module(dll)?;
        let proc = match symbol {
            ImportSymbol::Name { name, .. } => {
                let name = CString::new(name.as_str()).ok()?;
                // SAFETY: valid module handle, NUL-terminated name.
                unsafe { GetProcAddress(module as _, name.as_ptr().cast()) }
            }
            // SAFETY: MAKEINTRESOURCE-style ordinal lookup on a valid module.
            ImportSymbol::Ordinal(o) => unsafe { GetProcAddress(module as _, *o as usize as _) },
        };
        proc.map(|f| f as *const () as usize)
    }

    fn module(dll: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        let key = dll.to_ascii_lowercase();
        let mut cache = MODULES.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if let Some(&m) = cache.get(&key) {
            return Some(m);
        }
        let name = CString::new(key.as_str()).ok()?;
        // System32 only: never pick up a same-named DLL from the current folder or PATH.
        // SAFETY: NUL-terminated DLL name; only allow-listed system DLLs get here.
        let handle = unsafe {
            LoadLibraryExA(
                name.as_ptr().cast(),
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32,
            )
        } as usize;
        (handle != 0).then(|| *cache.entry(key).or_insert(handle))
    }
}

#[cfg(not(windows))]
mod imp {
    pub(super) fn resolve(_dll: &str, _symbol: &victory_pe::ImportSymbol) -> Option<usize> {
        None
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-hle/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Our implementation of the Xbox system API surface.
//!
//! A title imports from three kinds of DLLs, and each gets its own policy:
//!
//! | kind | examples | handled by |
//! |------|----------|------------|
//! | Windows API sets the console shares with PC | `api-ms-win-core-synch-*`, `ws2_32.dll` | host pass-through, overridden here where console behaviour differs (paths, memory) |
//! | console-only system APIs | `xgameruntime.dll`, `xmem.dll`, `d3d12_xs.dll` | implemented here, in [`modules`] |
//! | anything else | | an unimplemented-import stub from the loader |
//!
//! Resolution order for every import: an implementation in [`modules`],
//! then the host if [`HostPolicy`] allows that DLL, then `Missing`.

mod host;
pub mod modules;
mod registry;
pub mod runtime;

pub use host::HostPolicy;
pub use registry::{HleExport, HleModule, registry};
pub use victory_gpu::console;

use victory_loader::{ImportResolver, Provenance, Resolution};
use victory_pe::ImportSymbol;

/// Resolves a title's imports against our runtime and the host.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct HleResolver {
    pub host: HostPolicy,
}

impl HleResolver {
    pub fn new(host: HostPolicy) -> Self {
        HleResolver { host }
    }

    /// Where an import would come from, without binding anything.
    pub fn classify(&self, dll: &str, symbol: &ImportSymbol) -> Option<Provenance> {
        match self.resolve(dll, symbol) {
            Resolution::Found { provenance, .. } => Some(provenance),
            Resolution::Missing => None,
        }
    }
}

impl ImportResolver for HleResolver {
    fn resolve(&self, dll: &str, symbol: &ImportSymbol) -> Resolution {
        // Ordinal imports look up `#n`.
        if let Some(address) = registry::lookup(dll, &symbol.to_string()) {
            return Resolution::Found {
                address,
                provenance: Provenance::Hle,
            };
        }
        match self.host.resolve(dll, symbol) {
            Some(address) => Resolution::Found {
                address,
                provenance: Provenance::Host,
            },
            None => Resolution::Missing,
        }
    }
}

// The registry is code-only, so the "Missing" outcome can be checked on any
// host; host pass-through itself needs Windows.
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn name(n: &str) -> ImportSymbol {
        ImportSymbol::Name {
            hint: 0,
            name: n.into(),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn console_api_resolves_to_hle() {
        let r = HleResolver::new(HostPolicy::none());
        assert_eq!(
            r.classify("XGameRuntime.dll", &name("XGameRuntimeInitialize")),
            Some(Provenance::Hle)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn strict_policy_reports_missing() {
        let r = HleResolver::new(HostPolicy::none());
        assert_eq!(
            r.classify("api-ms-win-core-synch-l1-1-0.dll", &name("Sleep")),
            None
        );
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn shared_api_sets_pass_through_to_host() {
        let r = HleResolver::default();
        assert_eq!(
            r.classify("api-ms-win-core-synch-l1-2-0.dll", &name("Sleep")),
            Some(Provenance::Host)
        );
        // Console-only DLLs never pass through.
        assert_eq!(
            r.classify("xmem.dll", &name("XMemSetAllocationHooks")),
            None
        );
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn overrides_win_over_host() {
        let r = HleResolver::default();
        assert_eq!(
            r.classify(
                "api-ms-win-core-libraryloader-l1-2-0.dll",
                &name("GetModuleHandleW")
            ),
            Some(Provenance::Hle)
        );
    }
}
```
