`crates/victory-hle/src/modules/apu.rs`:

```rs
//! The console's audio decoder (`xapu.dll`): Opus packets in, float PCM out.
//!
//! A title connects once for one kind of processing, gets a block of memory
//! for its packets and output, and then queues per-stream commands
//! (activate, process, reset, deactivate) and dequeues one result per
//! command. We decode each command when it is queued, so its result is ready
//! at once; the order of results is the order of commands.
#![allow(non_snake_case)]
#![allow(clippy::not_unsafe_ptr_arg_deref)]

use std::alloc::Layout;
use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::sync::Mutex;

use opus_pure::OpusDecoder;
use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{CloseHandle, HANDLE};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{CreateEventW, SetEvent};

use super::xasync::E_INVALIDARG;
use super::xgameruntime::{HRESULT, S_OK};
use crate::{HleModule, hle_export};

const E_NOTIMPL: HRESULT = 0x8000_4001_u32 as i32;
const E_OUTOFMEMORY: HRESULT = 0x8007_000E_u32 as i32;
const QUEUE_FULL: HRESULT = 0x8AC8_1000_u32 as i32;
/// No result yet, which titles poll for.
pub(crate) const PENDING_RESULTS: HRESULT = 0x8AC8_1001_u32 as i32;
const INVALID_COMMAND: HRESULT = 0x8AC8_1002_u32 as i32;
const INVALID_STREAM: HRESULT = 0x8AC8_1003_u32 as i32;
const ALREADY_ACTIVE: HRESULT = 0x8AC8_1005_u32 as i32;
const BAD_PACKET: HRESULT = 0x8AC8_1008_u32 as i32;

/// Processing kinds; only plain decoding is implemented.
const DECODE_OPUS: u32 = 1;

const ACTIVATE: u32 = 1;
const DEACTIVATE: u32 = 2;
const PROCESS: u32 = 3;
const NOTIFY: u32 = 4;
const RESET: u32 = 5;

/// Command option: signal the connection's event when the result is ready.
const SIGNAL: u32 = 1;
/// Connect options.
const DEINTERLEAVED_OUTPUT: u32 = 4;
const RESULT_EVENT: u32 = 8;

/// The longest Opus packet duration at 48 kHz (120 ms).
const MAX_FRAMES: usize = 5760;

#[repr(C)]
pub struct ConnectInput {
    process: u32,
    streams: u32,
    commands_per_stream: u32,
    memory: u32,
    frames_per_output: u32,
    options: u32,
}

#[repr(C)]
pub struct ConnectOutput {
    memory: *mut c_void,
    result_event: HANDLE,
}

/// What every command starts with, and what its result echoes.
#[repr(C, packed)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct CommandId {
    kind: u32,
    stream: u32,
    sequence: u32,
    options: u32,
    context: u64,
}

#[repr(C, packed)]
struct Activate {
    id: CommandId,
    channels: u32,
    init_length: u32,
    init: *const c_void,
    start_pitch: f32,
    processing_length: u32,
    processing: *mut c_void,
}

#[repr(C, packed)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Process {
    id: CommandId,
    pitch_ramp: f32,
    target_pitch: f32,
    first_frame: u32,
    frame_count: u32,
    input_length: u32,
    input: *const u8,
    output_length: u32,
    output: *mut u8,
}

#[repr(C, packed)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct ApuResult {
    id: CommandId,
    state: u32,
    state_data: u64,
    usec: u64,
    error: HRESULT,
    frames: u32,
    output_length: u32,
    output: *mut u8,
    pitch: f32,
    input_length: u32,
    input: *const u8,
}

// SAFETY: the raw pointers are title addresses carried through, never
// dereferenced after the result is made.
unsafe impl Send for ApuResult {}

pub struct Connection {
    memory: *mut u8,
    layout: Layout,
    event: HANDLE,
    options: u32,
    per_stream: u32,
    state: Mutex<State>,
}

struct State {
    streams: Vec<Option<OpusDecoder>>,
    /// Results not yet dequeued, per stream.
    queued: Vec<u32>,
    results: VecDeque<ApuResult>,
    commands: u32,
    dequeued: u32,
}

fn lock(c: &Connection) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, State> {
    c.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

pub extern "system" fn XApuConnect(
    input: *const ConnectInput,
    output: *mut ConnectOutput,
    handle: *mut *mut Connection,
) -> HRESULT {
    if input.is_null() || output.is_null() || handle.is_null() {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    // SAFETY: checked non-null.
    let input = unsafe { &*input };
    if !(1..=500).contains(&input.streams)
        || !(1..=16).contains(&input.commands_per_stream)
        || input.memory == 0
    {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    if input.process != DECODE_OPUS {
        // shortcut: rate conversion (decode-convert, PCM convert) is not
        // implemented; add a resampler if a title connects for it.
        tracing::warn!(
            process = input.process,
            "audio decoder: processing kind not implemented"
        );
        return E_NOTIMPL;
    }
    if input.frames_per_output != 0 {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    let Ok(layout) = Layout::from_size_align(input.memory as usize, 16) else {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    };
    // SAFETY: non-zero size.
    let memory = unsafe { std::alloc::alloc_zeroed(layout) };
    if memory.is_null() {
        return E_OUTOFMEMORY;
    }
    let event = if input.options & RESULT_EVENT != 0 {
        // SAFETY: plain auto-reset event, no name.
        unsafe { CreateEventW(std::ptr::null(), 0, 0, std::ptr::null()) }
    } else {
        std::ptr::null_mut()
    };
    let streams = input.streams as usize;
    tracing::info!(
        streams,
        memory = input.memory,
        options = input.options,
        "audio decoder connected"
    );
    let connection = Box::new(Connection {
        memory,
        layout,
        event,
        options: input.options,
        per_stream: input.commands_per_stream,
        state: Mutex::new(State {
            streams: (0..streams).map(|_| None).collect(),
            queued: vec![0; streams],
            results: VecDeque::new(),
            commands: 0,
            dequeued: 0,
        }),
    });
    // SAFETY: checked non-null.
    unsafe {
        output.write(ConnectOutput {
            memory: memory.cast(),
            result_event: event,
        });
        handle.write(Box::into_raw(connection));
    }
    S_OK
}

pub extern "system" fn XApuDisconnect(handle: *mut Connection) -> HRESULT {
    if handle.is_null() {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    // SAFETY: made by `XApuConnect`; disconnected once.
    let connection = unsafe { Box::from_raw(handle) };
    if !connection.event.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: our event.
        unsafe { CloseHandle(connection.event) };
    }
    // SAFETY: allocated in `XApuConnect` with this layout.
    unsafe { std::alloc::dealloc(connection.memory, connection.layout) };
    S_OK
}

pub extern "system" fn XApuEnqueueCommand(
    handle: *mut Connection,
    command: *const CommandId,
    total: *mut u32,
) -> HRESULT {
    if handle.is_null() || command.is_null() {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    // SAFETY: a connection from `XApuConnect`; every command starts with an id.
    let (connection, id) = unsafe { (&*handle, command.read_unaligned()) };
    let mut state = lock(connection);
    let stream = id.stream as usize;
    if stream >= state.streams.len() {
        return INVALID_STREAM;
    }
    if state.queued[stream] >= connection.per_stream {
        return QUEUE_FULL;
    }
    let mut result = ApuResult {
        id,
        state: 0,
        state_data: 0,
        usec: 0,
        error: S_OK,
        frames: 0,
        output_length: 0,
        output: std::ptr::null_mut(),
        pitch: 1.0,
        input_length: 0,
        input: std::ptr::null(),
    };
    let decoder = &mut state.streams[stream];
    match id.kind {
        ACTIVATE => {
            // SAFETY: an activate command is this struct.
            let channels = unsafe { command.cast::<Activate>().read_unaligned() }.channels;
            tracing::debug!(stream, channels, "Opus stream activated");
            result.error = if decoder.is_some() {
                ALREADY_ACTIVE
            } else {
                match OpusDecoder::new(48_000, channels as usize) {
                    Ok(d) if (1..=2).contains(&channels) => {
                        *decoder = Some(d);
                        S_OK
                    }
                    _ => E_INVALIDARG,
                }
            };
        }
        DEACTIVATE => *decoder = None,
        RESET => {
            if let Some(d) = decoder {
                let _ = d.reset_state();
            }
        }
        NOTIFY => {}
        PROCESS => {
            // SAFETY: a process command is this struct.
            let command = unsafe { command.cast::<Process>().read_unaligned() };
            match decoder {
                Some(d) => process(d, connection.options, &command, &mut result),
                None => result.error = INVALID_STREAM,
            }
        }
        _ => return INVALID_COMMAND,
    }
    state.queued[stream] += 1;
    state.commands = state.commands.wrapping_add(1);
    state.results.push_back(result);
    if !total.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: optional out parameter.
        unsafe { total.write(state.commands) };
    }
    if id.options & SIGNAL != 0 && !connection.event.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: our event.
        unsafe { SetEvent(connection.event) };
    }
    S_OK
}

/// Decodes one packet into the command's output buffer, keeping the frames
/// from `first_frame` on, at most `frame_count` of them.
fn process(decoder: &mut OpusDecoder, options: u32, command: &Process, result: &mut ApuResult) {
    let channels = decoder.channels();
    let (input, input_length) = (command.input, command.input_length);
    let (output, output_length) = (command.output, command.output_length);
    result.input = input;
    result.input_length = input_length;
    result.output = output;
    if input.is_null() || output.is_null() || input_length == 0 {
        result.error = E_INVALIDARG;
        return;
    }
    // SAFETY: the title's packet in its connection memory.
    let packet = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(input, input_length as usize) };
    let mut pcm = vec![0f32; MAX_FRAMES * channels];
    let decoded = match decoder.decode(packet, MAX_FRAMES, &mut pcm) {
        Ok(n) => n,
        Err(_) => {
            result.error = BAD_PACKET;
            return;
        }
    };
    let first = (command.first_frame as usize).min(decoded);
    let frames = (decoded - first)
        .min(command.frame_count as usize)
        .min(output_length as usize / (4 * channels));
    let kept = &pcm[first * channels..(first + frames) * channels];
    // SAFETY: the title's output buffer holds `output_length` bytes.
    let out = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(output.cast::<f32>(), frames * channels) };
    if options & DEINTERLEAVED_OUTPUT != 0 && channels == 2 {
        for (i, frame) in kept.as_chunks::<2>().0.iter().enumerate() {
            (out[i], out[frames + i]) = (frame[0], frame[1]);
        }
    } else {
        out.copy_from_slice(kept);
    }
    result.frames = frames as u32;
    result.output_length = (frames * channels * 4) as u32;
}

pub extern "system" fn XApuDequeueResult(handle: *mut Connection, out: *mut ApuResult) -> HRESULT {
    if handle.is_null() || out.is_null() {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    // SAFETY: a connection from `XApuConnect`.
    let mut state = lock(unsafe { &*handle });
    let Some(result) = state.results.pop_front() else {
        return PENDING_RESULTS;
    };
    let stream = result.id.stream as usize;
    state.queued[stream] -= 1;
    state.dequeued = state.dequeued.wrapping_add(1);
    // SAFETY: the title passes room for one result.
    unsafe { out.write_unaligned(result) };
    S_OK
}

pub extern "system" fn XApuGetResultCount(handle: *mut Connection, total: *mut u32) -> u32 {
    if handle.is_null() {
        return 0;
    }
    // SAFETY: a connection from `XApuConnect`.
    let state = lock(unsafe { &*handle });
    if !total.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: optional out parameter.
        unsafe { total.write(state.dequeued) };
    }
    state.results.len() as u32
}

pub(crate) fn module() -> HleModule {
    HleModule {
        name: "apu",
        dlls: &["xapu.dll"],
        exports: vec![
            hle_export!(XApuConnect),
            hle_export!(XApuDisconnect),
            hle_export!(XApuEnqueueCommand),
            hle_export!(XApuDequeueResult),
            hle_export!(XApuGetResultCount),
        ],
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use opus_pure::{Application, OpusEncoder};

    fn id(kind: u32, stream: u32) -> CommandId {
        CommandId {
            kind,
            stream,
            sequence: 7,
            options: 0,
            context: 0x1234,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_opus_as_the_title_drives_it() {
        assert_eq!(size_of::<ApuResult>(), 0x50);
        // 256 mono/stereo streams, two commands each, as the title connects.
        let input = ConnectInput {
            process: DECODE_OPUS,
            streams: 256,
            commands_per_stream: 2,
            memory: 0x10_4000,
            frames_per_output: 0,
            options: 1,
        };
        let mut output = ConnectOutput {
            memory: std::ptr::null_mut(),
            result_event: std::ptr::null_mut(),
        };
        let mut handle = std::ptr::null_mut();
        assert_eq!(XApuConnect(&input, &mut output, &mut handle), S_OK);
        let base = output.memory.cast::<u8>();

        let activate = Activate {
            id: id(ACTIVATE, 3),
            channels: 2,
            init_length: 0,
            init: std::ptr::null(),
            start_pitch: 1.0,
            processing_length: 0,
            processing: std::ptr::null_mut(),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            XApuEnqueueCommand(handle, (&raw const activate).cast(), std::ptr::null_mut()),
            S_OK
        );

        // A 20 ms stereo packet of a 440 Hz tone.
        let tone: Vec<f32> = (0..960 * 2)
            .map(|i| ((i / 2) as f32 * 440.0 * std::f32::consts::TAU / 48_000.0).sin() * 0.5)
            .collect();
        let mut encoder = OpusEncoder::new(48_000, 2, Application::Audio).unwrap();
        let mut packet = [0u8; 1500];
        let n = encoder.encode(&tone, 960, &mut packet).unwrap();
        // SAFETY: inside the connection memory.
        unsafe { std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(packet.as_ptr(), base, n) };
        let process = Process {
            id: id(PROCESS, 3),
            pitch_ramp: 0.0,
            target_pitch: 1.0,
            first_frame: 0,
            frame_count: 960,
            input_length: n as u32,
            input: base,
            output_length: 0xf00 * 2,
            output: base.wrapping_add(0x14000),
        };
        let mut total = 0;
        assert_eq!(
            XApuEnqueueCommand(handle, (&raw const process).cast(), &mut total),
            S_OK
        );
        assert_eq!(total, 2);
        // Two results queued for stream 3: its queue is full.
        assert_eq!(
            XApuEnqueueCommand(handle, (&raw const process).cast(), &mut total),
            QUEUE_FULL
        );
        assert_eq!(XApuGetResultCount(handle, std::ptr::null_mut()), 2);

        let mut result = std::mem::MaybeUninit::<ApuResult>::zeroed();
        assert_eq!(XApuDequeueResult(handle, result.as_mut_ptr()), S_OK);
        // SAFETY: written above.
        let first = unsafe { result.assume_init() };
        let (kind, error, context) = (first.id.kind, first.error, first.id.context);
        assert_eq!((kind, error, context), (ACTIVATE, S_OK, 0x1234));
        assert_eq!(XApuDequeueResult(handle, result.as_mut_ptr()), S_OK);
        // SAFETY: written above.
        let decoded = unsafe { result.assume_init() };
        let (kind, error, frames, length) = (
            decoded.id.kind,
            decoded.error,
            decoded.frames,
            decoded.output_length,
        );
        assert_eq!((kind, error, frames, length), (PROCESS, S_OK, 960, 960 * 8));
        // SAFETY: the decoder wrote 960 stereo frames there.
        let pcm =
            unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(base.wrapping_add(0x14000).cast::<f32>(), 1920) };
        let energy: f32 = pcm.iter().map(|s| s * s).sum::<f32>() / 1920.0;
        assert!(energy > 0.01, "decoded a tone, energy {energy}");
        assert_eq!(
            XApuDequeueResult(handle, result.as_mut_ptr()),
            PENDING_RESULTS
        );
        let mut dequeued = 0;
        assert_eq!(XApuGetResultCount(handle, &mut dequeued), 0);
        assert_eq!(dequeued, 2);

        // A process on a stream that was never activated fails in its result.
        let mut stray = process;
        stray.id.stream = 4;
        assert_eq!(
            XApuEnqueueCommand(handle, (&raw const stray).cast(), &mut total),
            S_OK
        );
        assert_eq!(XApuDequeueResult(handle, result.as_mut_ptr()), S_OK);
        // SAFETY: written above.
        let error = unsafe { result.assume_init() }.error;
        assert_eq!(error, INVALID_STREAM);
        assert_eq!(XApuDisconnect(handle), S_OK);
    }
}

```

`crates/victory-hle/src/modules/audio.rs`:

```rs
//! The console's audio hardware (`AcpHal.dll`):
//!
//! * the APU heap: host memory with 32-bit device addresses;
//! * SHAPE context arrays allocated from it;
//! * the audio coprocessor's command and message queues, where every
//!   command completes at once and is acknowledged as the hardware would;
//! * the XMA decoder: enabled XMA contexts are decoded on a thread of ours
//!   into their output rings, like the hardware does.
//!
//! SHAPE's other units (rate conversion, EQ, filters, mixing through
//! flowgraphs) are not emulated, so voices that need them stay silent.
//! Mixed audio leaves through the host's WASAPI, which titles and
//! middleware reach through COM like on PC. fmod's console build sets up
//! the coprocessor inside `System_Create` and waits there for its first
//! command to be acknowledged; the title uses only XMA contexts.
#![allow(non_snake_case)]
#![allow(clippy::not_unsafe_ptr_arg_deref)]

use std::alloc::Layout;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, VecDeque};
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard, OnceLock, RwLock, RwLockReadGuard};
use std::time::Instant;

use super::xasync::E_INVALIDARG;
use super::xgameruntime::{HRESULT, S_OK};
use crate::{HleModule, hle_export};

#[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]
pub mod capture;

const E_FAIL: HRESULT = 0x8000_4005_u32 as i32;
const E_OUTOFMEMORY: HRESULT = 0x8007_000E_u32 as i32;

fn lock<T>(m: &Mutex<T>) -> MutexGuard<'_, T> {
    m.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

// The APU heap.

struct Block {
    size: usize,
    apu: u32,
    layout: Layout,
}

struct Heap {
    /// By host address.
    blocks: BTreeMap<usize, Block>,
    /// Host address by device address.
    by_apu: BTreeMap<u32, usize>,
    /// Free device address ranges, start to end, merged with neighbours.
    free: BTreeMap<u32, u32>,
    /// Set by `ApuCreateHeap` or the first allocation: the heap exists.
    created: bool,
}

static HEAP: Mutex<Heap> = Mutex::new(Heap {
    blocks: BTreeMap::new(),
    by_apu: BTreeMap::new(),
    free: BTreeMap::new(),
    created: false,
});

/// Device addresses start above 0, which means "none" to titles.
const APU_BASE: u32 = 0x0001_0000;

impl Heap {
    /// First fit in the free ranges.
    fn take(&mut self, size: u32, align: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        if self.free.is_empty() && !self.created {
            self.free.insert(APU_BASE, u32::MAX);
        }
        self.created = true;
        let (start, end, apu) = self.free.iter().find_map(|(&start, &end)| {
            let apu = start.checked_next_multiple_of(align)?;
            (apu.checked_add(size)? <= end).then_some((start, end, apu))
        })?;
        self.free.remove(&start);
        if start < apu {
            self.free.insert(start, apu);
        }
        if apu + size < end {
            self.free.insert(apu + size, end);
        }
        Some(apu)
    }

    fn give_back(&mut self, mut start: u32, mut end: u32) {
        if let Some((&before, &before_end)) = self.free.range(..start).next_back()
            && before_end == start
        {
            self.free.remove(&before);
            start = before;
        }
        if let Some(after_end) = self.free.remove(&end) {
            end = after_end;
        }
        self.free.insert(start, end);
    }
}

/// Zeroed host memory and its device address.
fn heap_alloc(size: usize, align: usize) -> Option<(*mut u8, u32)> {
    let layout = Layout::from_size_align(size.max(1), align.max(16)).ok()?;
    let mut heap = lock(&HEAP);
    let apu = heap.take(u32::try_from(layout.size()).ok()?, align as u32)?;
    // SAFETY: non-zero size.
    let ptr = unsafe { std::alloc::alloc_zeroed(layout) };
    if ptr.is_null() {
        heap.give_back(apu, apu + layout.size() as u32);
        return None;
    }
    heap.blocks
        .insert(ptr as usize, Block { size, apu, layout });
    heap.by_apu.insert(apu, ptr as usize);
    // The big ones are named in the log: they are the title's audio memory
    // given out of our allocator, which the memory line counts as ours.
    if size >= 32 << 20 {
        tracing::info!(mb = size >> 20, at = ?ptr, "audio memory for the title from our allocator");
    }
    Some((ptr, apu))
}

fn heap_free(ptr: *mut u8) {
    let mut heap = lock(&HEAP);
    let Some(block) = heap.blocks.remove(&(ptr as usize)) else {
        return;
    };
    heap.by_apu.remove(&block.apu);
    heap.give_back(block.apu, block.apu + block.layout.size() as u32);
    drop(heap);
    // SAFETY: allocated by `heap_alloc` with this layout.
    unsafe { std::alloc::dealloc(ptr, block.layout) };
}

/// Sizes the heap once, before anything is allocated from it. The console
/// reserves both parts up front; we allocate per block, so the sizes only
/// decide whether the call is valid.
// shortcut: the cached and non-cached sizes are not enforced as limits;
// enforce them if a title relies on running out.
pub extern "system" fn ApuCreateHeap(cached: u32, _non_cached: u32) -> HRESULT {
    const ALREADY_ALLOCATED: HRESULT = 0x8ACA_0001_u32 as i32;
    if cached == 0 {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    let mut heap = lock(&HEAP);
    if heap.created {
        return ALREADY_ALLOCATED;
    }
    heap.created = true;
    heap.free.insert(APU_BASE, u32::MAX);
    S_OK
}

/// The host address of a device address, null outside the heap.
pub extern "system" fn ApuMapApuAddress(apu: u32) -> *mut c_void {
    heap_unmap(apu).map_or(std::ptr::null_mut(), |p| p.cast())
}

/// The device address of any byte of a heap block, 0 elsewhere.
fn heap_map(ptr: usize) -> u32 {
    let heap = lock(&HEAP);
    match heap.blocks.range(..=ptr).next_back() {
        Some((&start, block)) if ptr < start + block.size.max(1) => {
            block.apu + (ptr - start) as u32
        }
        _ => 0,
    }
}

/// The host address of a device address, if a heap block holds it.
fn heap_unmap(apu: u32) -> Option<*mut u8> {
    let heap = lock(&HEAP);
    let (&start, &host) = heap.by_apu.range(..=apu).next_back()?;
    let block = &heap.blocks[&host];
    (apu < start.saturating_add(block.size.max(1) as u32))
        .then(|| (host + (apu - start) as usize) as *mut u8)
}

/// `len` bytes of title memory at a device address, if one heap block holds
/// them all.
fn heap_bytes<'a>(apu: u32, len: usize) -> Option<&'a mut [u8]> {
    let heap = lock(&HEAP);
    let (&start, &host) = heap.by_apu.range(..=apu).next_back()?;
    let offset = (apu - start) as usize;
    (offset + len <= heap.blocks[&host].size)
        // SAFETY: inside a live heap block, which the title and the audio
        // hardware share like on the console.
        .then(|| unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut((host + offset) as *mut u8, len) })
}

pub extern "system" fn ApuAlloc(
    out: *mut *mut c_void,
    apu: *mut u32,
    size: u32,
    align: u32,
    _flags: u32,
) -> HRESULT {
    if out.is_null() || size == 0 || align < 4 || !align.is_power_of_two() {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    let Some((ptr, address)) = heap_alloc(size as usize, align as usize) else {
        return E_OUTOFMEMORY;
    };
    // SAFETY: checked non-null; optional out parameter checked below.
    unsafe {
        out.write(ptr.cast());
        if !apu.is_null() {
            apu.write(address);
        }
    }
    S_OK
}

pub extern "system" fn ApuFree(ptr: *mut c_void) {
    heap_free(ptr.cast());
}

pub extern "system" fn ApuMapVirtualAddress(ptr: *const c_void) -> u32 {
    heap_map(ptr as usize)
}

pub extern "system" fn ApuIsVirtualAddressValid(ptr: *const c_void, align: u32) -> bool {
    let apu = heap_map(ptr as usize);
    apu != 0 && (align == 0 || apu.is_multiple_of(align))
}

// SHAPE context arrays.

/// Six counts (rate conversion, EQ/compression, filter/volume, DMA, XMA,
/// PCM), then the six arrays and their device addresses.
#[repr(C, packed)]
pub struct ShapeContexts {
    counts: [u32; 6],
    arrays: [*mut c_void; 6],
    apu: [u32; 6],
}

/// Bytes per context: rate conversion, DMA and XMA as fmod clears them;
/// the others (not seen yet) get a generous upper bound.
const CONTEXT_BYTES: [usize; 6] = [32, 256, 256, 16, 64, 256];

static CONTEXTS: Mutex<Option<[usize; 6]>> = Mutex::new(None);

pub extern "system" fn AcpHalAllocateShapeContexts(contexts: *mut ShapeContexts) -> HRESULT {
    if contexts.is_null() {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    let mut allocated = lock(&CONTEXTS);
    if allocated.is_some() {
        return E_FAIL;
    }
    // SAFETY: the title passes its request; packed fields are copied out.
    let counts = unsafe { std::ptr::addr_of!((*contexts).counts).read_unaligned() };
    let mut arrays: [*mut c_void; 6] = [std::ptr::null_mut(); 6];
    let mut addresses = [0u32; 6];
    for i in 0..6 {
        if counts[i] == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        let Some((ptr, apu)) = heap_alloc(counts[i] as usize * CONTEXT_BYTES[i], 256) else {
            arrays.iter().for_each(|&p| heap_free(p.cast()));
            return E_OUTOFMEMORY;
        };
        (arrays[i], addresses[i]) = (ptr.cast(), apu);
    }
    // SAFETY: as above.
    unsafe {
        std::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*contexts).arrays).write_unaligned(arrays);
        std::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*contexts).apu).write_unaligned(addresses);
    }
    *allocated = Some(arrays.map(|p| p as usize));
    let mut xma = XMA.write().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    xma.array = arrays[4] as usize;
    xma.voices = (0..counts[4]).map(|_| Mutex::new(None)).collect();
    S_OK
}

pub extern "system" fn AcpHalReleaseShapeContexts() -> HRESULT {
    match lock(&CONTEXTS).take() {
        Some(arrays) => {
            *XMA.write().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = Xma::EMPTY;
            arrays.iter().for_each(|&p| heap_free(p as *mut u8));
            S_OK
        }
        None => E_FAIL,
    }
}

// The XMA decoder.
//
// An XMA context (16 words in the shared context array) names up to two
// input buffers of 2 KiB packets, a ring of 256-byte output blocks the
// hardware fills with 16-bit PCM, and the read offset the title advances
// by command. Words and bit fields, as titles write them:
// 0: input 0 size in packets (0-11), loop count (12-19, 255 forever),
//    valid inputs (20-21), output size in blocks (22-26), write block
//    (27-31, hardware);
// 1: input 1 size (0-11), loop end subframe (12-13), loop start subframes
//    to skip (17-19), subframes to skip at the start (24-26), sample rate
//    (27-28: 24, 32, 44.1, 48 kHz), stereo (29), output writable (31);
// 2: read position in bits (0-25), error status (26-30), error (31);
// 3: loop start in bits (0-25); 4: loop end in bits (0-25), current input
//    (31); 5, 6: input addresses; 7: output address; 8: overlap buffer;
//    9: read block (0-4).
// Titles read back only the write block, "writable" and the read block,
// and take whatever lies between read and write.
// shortcut: each enabled context decodes from a cold state and the overlap
// buffer is ignored (titles copy it between consecutive contexts of one
// voice); keep decoder state there if a title's seams turn out audible.

use victory_formats::xma;

const ENABLE_XMA: u32 = 5;
const ENABLE_XMAS: u32 = 6;
const DISABLE_XMA: u32 = 7;
const DISABLE_XMAS: u32 = 8;
const ADVANCE_XMA_READ: u32 = 18;

const BLOCK_BYTES: usize = 256;
const SAMPLES_PER_BLOCK: usize = BLOCK_BYTES / 2;
/// Error status: the input ran out.
const INPUT_INVALID: u32 = 4;

struct Voice {
    decoder: Option<xma::Decoder>,
    pcm: VecDeque<i16>,
    /// Samples per channel still to drop (start or loop subframe skips).
    skip: usize,
    ended: bool,
    trace: Trace,
}

/// What a voice did, for the debug log when it is disabled.
struct Trace {
    since: Instant,
    /// Samples per channel written to the ring.
    produced: usize,
    /// Blocks the title took (command 18), how often, and how often it
    /// found the ring less than full.
    taken: usize,
    takes: u32,
    partial_takes: u32,
    frames: u32,
    bad_frames: u32,
    /// The loudest sample written.
    peak: i16,
    /// Milliseconds after enabling when the input ran out.
    ended_ms: Option<u128>,
}

struct Xma {
    /// Host address of the context array.
    array: usize,
    /// One entry per context, `Some` while enabled. Each has its own lock,
    /// so a command for one voice never waits for others to decode (the
    /// title sends them from its time-critical mixer thread).
    voices: Vec<Mutex<Option<Voice>>>,
}

impl Xma {
    const EMPTY: Xma = Xma {
        array: 0,
        voices: Vec::new(),
    };
}

/// Written only when the context arrays are allocated or released.
static XMA: RwLock<Xma> = RwLock::new(Xma::EMPTY);

fn xma() -> RwLockReadGuard<'static, Xma> {
    XMA.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

/// A context's words in title memory.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Context(*mut u32);

impl Context {
    fn get(self, word: usize) -> u32 {
        // SAFETY: inside the context array; the title reads and writes it
        // concurrently, like the hardware's.
        unsafe { self.0.add(word).read_volatile() }
    }

    fn set(self, word: usize, value: u32) {
        // SAFETY: as above.
        unsafe { self.0.add(word).write_volatile(value) }
    }

    fn field(self, word: usize, shift: u32, bits: u32) -> u32 {
        (self.get(word) >> shift) & ((1 << bits) - 1)
    }

    fn set_field(self, word: usize, shift: u32, bits: u32, value: u32) {
        let mask = ((1u32 << bits) - 1) << shift;
        self.set(word, (self.get(word) & !mask) | ((value << shift) & mask));
    }

    fn channels(self) -> usize {
        1 + self.field(1, 29, 1) as usize
    }
}

impl Xma {
    fn context(&self, index: u32) -> Option<Context> {
        ((index as usize) < self.voices.len() && self.array != 0)
            .then(|| Context((self.array + index as usize * 64) as *mut u32))
    }

    fn enable(&self, index: u32) {
        let Some(context) = self.context(index) else {
            return;
        };
        let mut slot = lock(&self.voices[index as usize]);
        context.set_field(2, 26, 6, 0);
        tracing::debug!(
            index,
            words = ?(0..10).map(|w| format!("{:08x}", context.get(w))).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            "XMA voice enabled"
        );
        #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
        dump_input(index, context);
        *slot = Some(Voice {
            decoder: None,
            pcm: VecDeque::new(),
            skip: context.field(1, 24, 3) as usize * xma::SUBFRAME_SAMPLES,
            ended: false,
            trace: Trace {
                since: Instant::now(),
                produced: 0,
                taken: 0,
                takes: 0,
                partial_takes: 0,
                frames: 0,
                bad_frames: 0,
                peak: 0,
                ended_ms: None,
            },
        });
        drop(slot);
        wake_decoder();
    }

    fn disable(&self, index: u32) {
        let Some(context) = self.context(index) else {
            return;
        };
        let Some(voice) = lock(&self.voices[index as usize]).take() else {
            return;
        };
        let t = &voice.trace;
        tracing::debug!(
            index,
            ms = t.since.elapsed().as_millis(),
            produced = t.produced,
            taken = t.taken * SAMPLES_PER_BLOCK / context.channels(),
            takes = t.takes,
            partial_takes = t.partial_takes,
            frames = t.frames,
            bad_frames = t.bad_frames,
            peak = t.peak,
            input_ended_ms = ?t.ended_ms,
            read_bit = context.field(2, 0, 26),
            input_bits = context.field(0, 0, 12) * xma::PACKET_BYTES as u32 * 8,
            "XMA voice disabled"
        );
    }

    /// Moves the title's read block on, which frees output space.
    fn advance_read(&self, index: u32, blocks: u32) {
        let Some(context) = self.context(index) else {
            return;
        };
        // The decoder writes the same words.
        let mut slot = lock(&self.voices[index as usize]);
        let size = context.field(0, 22, 5).max(1);
        // The count is the title's: reduced first, so the sum stays small.
        let read = (context.field(9, 0, 5) + blocks % size) % size;
        context.set_field(9, 0, 5, read);
        if blocks > 0 {
            context.set_field(1, 31, 1, 1);
        }
        if let Some(voice) = &mut *slot {
            let t = &mut voice.trace;
            t.taken += blocks as usize;
            t.takes += 1;
            t.partial_takes += u32::from(blocks < size);
        }
        drop(slot);
        wake_decoder();
    }

    /// Fills every enabled context's output as far as it has room.
    fn pump(&self) {
        let start = Instant::now();
        let mut active = 0;
        for index in 0..self.voices.len() as u32 {
            if let (Some(context), Some(voice)) =
                (self.context(index), &mut *lock(&self.voices[index as usize]))
            {
                pump(context, voice);
                active += 1;
            }
        }
        let took = start.elapsed();
        if took.as_millis() >= 4 {
            tracing::debug!(active, ms = took.as_millis(), "slow XMA decoding pass");
        }
    }
}

fn pump(context: Context, voice: &mut Voice) {
    let size = context.field(0, 22, 5);
    if size == 0 {
        return;
    }
    while context.field(1, 31, 1) == 1 {
        if voice.pcm.len() < SAMPLES_PER_BLOCK && !decode(context, voice) {
            return;
        }
        let write = context.field(0, 27, 5);
        let address = context.get(7) as usize + write as usize * BLOCK_BYTES;
        let Some(out) = heap_bytes(address as u32, BLOCK_BYTES) else {
            return;
        };
        for pair in out.as_chunks_mut::<2>().0 {
            let sample = voice.pcm.pop_front().unwrap_or(0);
            voice.trace.peak = voice.trace.peak.max(sample.saturating_abs());
            pair.copy_from_slice(&sample.to_le_bytes());
        }
        voice.trace.produced += SAMPLES_PER_BLOCK / context.channels();
        let write = (write + 1) % size;
        context.set_field(0, 27, 5, write);
        if write == context.field(9, 0, 5) {
            // Full: nothing more until the title advances its read block.
            context.set_field(1, 31, 1, 0);
        }
    }
}

/// Decodes the next frame of the current input into `voice.pcm`; false
/// when there is nothing left to decode.
fn decode(context: Context, voice: &mut Voice) -> bool {
    if voice.ended {
        return false;
    }
    let channels = context.channels();
    let mut current = context.field(4, 31, 1);
    let valid = context.field(0, 20, 2);
    if valid & (1 << current) == 0 {
        if valid & (1 << (1 - current)) == 0 {
            // Out of input: the overlap tail, then nothing.
            if let Some(decoder) = &mut voice.decoder {
                let mut tail = Vec::new();
                decoder.flush(&mut tail);
                voice.pcm.extend(tail);
            }
            voice.ended = true;
            voice.trace.ended_ms = Some(voice.trace.since.elapsed().as_millis());
            context.set_field(2, 26, 5, INPUT_INVALID);
            context.set_field(2, 31, 1, 1);
            return !voice.pcm.is_empty();
        }
        current = 1 - current;
        context.set_field(4, 31, 1, current);
        context.set_field(2, 0, 26, 0);
    }
    let (address, packets) = match current {
        0 => (context.get(5), context.field(0, 0, 12)),
        _ => (context.get(6), context.field(1, 0, 12)),
    };
    let Some(data) = heap_bytes(address & !0x7ff, packets as usize * xma::PACKET_BYTES) else {
        context.set_field(0, 20 + current, 1, 0);
        return true;
    };
    let mut at = context.field(2, 0, 26) as usize;
    if at < 32 {
        at = 32 + xma::packet(data, 0).map_or(0, |p| p.first_frame_bit as usize);
    }
    let Some(frame) = xma::read_frame(data, at) else {
        // This input is used up.
        context.set_field(0, 20 + current, 1, 0);
        return true;
    };
    let decoder = voice.decoder.get_or_insert_with(|| {
        const RATES: [u32; 4] = [24_000, 32_000, 44_100, 48_000];
        xma::Decoder::new(channels, RATES[context.field(1, 27, 2) as usize])
    });
    let mut pcm = Vec::with_capacity(xma::FRAME_SAMPLES * channels);
    voice.trace.frames += 1;
    if let Err(e) = decoder.decode(&frame.data, frame.bits, &mut pcm) {
        voice.trace.bad_frames += 1;
        if voice.trace.bad_frames <= 2 {
            tracing::debug!(
                at,
                bits = frame.bits,
                head = ?&frame.data[..frame.data.len().min(8)],
                %e,
                "XMA frame did not decode"
            );
        }
    }
    let mut next = frame.next.unwrap_or(0);
    let loops = context.field(0, 12, 8);
    let loop_end = context.field(4, 0, 26) as usize;
    let ends_loop = loop_end != 0
        && (frame.start == loop_end
            || (frame.start < loop_end && frame.next.is_none_or(|n| loop_end < n)));
    if loops > 0 && ends_loop {
        let keep = (context.field(1, 12, 2) as usize + 1) * xma::SUBFRAME_SAMPLES * channels;
        pcm.truncate(keep);
        next = context.field(3, 0, 26) as usize;
        voice.skip = context.field(1, 17, 3) as usize * xma::SUBFRAME_SAMPLES;
        if loops != 255 {
            context.set_field(0, 12, 8, loops - 1);
        }
    }
    let skip = (voice.skip * channels).min(pcm.len());
    voice.skip -= skip / channels;
    voice.pcm.extend(&pcm[skip..]);
    if next == 0 {
        context.set_field(0, 20 + current, 1, 0);
    }
    context.set_field(2, 0, 26, next as u32);
    true
}

/// `VICTORY_XMA_DUMP=<dir>`: saves the context words (`<n>-<index>.ctx`)
/// and input buffer 0 (`.xma`) of the first 32 voices enabled, to test
/// the decoder on a title's streams outside the title.
#[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
fn dump_input(index: u32, context: Context) {
    static COUNT: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0);
    let Some(dir) = std::env::var_os("VICTORY_XMA_DUMP") else {
        return;
    };
    let n = COUNT.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
    if n >= 32 {
        return;
    }
    let dir = std::path::PathBuf::from(dir);
    let words: Vec<u8> = (0..16).flat_map(|w| context.get(w).to_le_bytes()).collect();
    let input = heap_bytes(
        context.get(5) & !0x7ff,
        context.field(0, 0, 12) as usize * xma::PACKET_BYTES,
    );
    let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir);
    let _ = std::fs::write(dir.join(format!("{n:02}-{index}.ctx")), words);
    let _ = std::fs::write(dir.join(format!("{n:02}-{index}.xma")), input.unwrap_or_default());
}

/// Starts the decoding thread on the first enabled voice, and has it fill
/// rings now: a voice just enabled or read from.
fn wake_decoder() {
    static DECODER: OnceLock<std::thread::Thread> = OnceLock::new();
    DECODER
        .get_or_init(|| {
            std::thread::Builder::new()
                .name("victory XMA decoder".into())
                .spawn(|| {
                    loop {
                        xma().pump();
                        // A 256-byte output block lasts 2.7 ms at 48 kHz mono.
                        std::thread::park_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_millis(2));
                    }
                })
                .map_or_else(|_| std::thread::current(), |h| h.thread().clone())
        })
        .unpark();
}

/// Runs an XMA command; false for one this does not know.
fn xma_command(command: u32, word: impl Fn(usize) -> Option<u32>) -> bool {
    let xma = xma();
    match command {
        ENABLE_XMA => xma.enable(word(0).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)),
        DISABLE_XMA => xma.disable(word(0).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)),
        ENABLE_XMAS | DISABLE_XMAS => {
            for i in 0..xma.voices.len() as u32 {
                if word(i as usize / 32).unwrap_or(0) & (1 << (i % 32)) != 0 {
                    match command {
                        ENABLE_XMAS => xma.enable(i),
                        _ => xma.disable(i),
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        ADVANCE_XMA_READ => xma.advance_read(word(0).unwrap_or(u32::MAX), word(1).unwrap_or(0)),
        _ => return false,
    }
    true
}

// The audio coprocessor.

const LOAD_FLOWGRAPH: u32 = 1;
const REGISTER_MESSAGES: u32 = 2;
const UNREGISTER_MESSAGES: u32 = 3;

const FLOWGRAPH_COMPLETED: u32 = 0x02;
const COMMAND_COMPLETED: u32 = 0x10;
const DISCONNECTED: u32 = 0x80;

/// Audio frames of 128 samples at 48 kHz.
const FRAMES_PER_SECOND: u64 = 375;

#[repr(C, packed)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Message {
    kind: u32,
    dropped: u32,
    usec: u32,
    data: [u8; 16],
}

struct State {
    connected: bool,
    /// Message kinds the title registered for.
    mask: u32,
    messages: VecDeque<Message>,
    /// Queue size given to `connect`.
    capacity: usize,
    /// Messages lost to a full queue since the last one queued.
    dropped: u32,
    since: Instant,
}

impl State {
    fn usec(&self) -> u64 {
        self.since.elapsed().as_micros() as u64
    }

    fn frame(&self) -> u32 {
        (self.usec() * FRAMES_PER_SECOND / 1_000_000) as u32
    }

    /// Queues a registered message; a full queue drops it and counts it in
    /// the next one that fits.
    fn post(&mut self, kind: u32, data: &[u8]) {
        if self.mask & kind == 0 {
            return;
        }
        if self.messages.len() >= self.capacity {
            self.dropped = self.dropped.saturating_add(1);
            tracing::debug!(kind, dropped = self.dropped, "coprocessor message dropped");
            return;
        }
        let mut message = Message {
            kind,
            dropped: std::mem::take(&mut self.dropped),
            usec: self.usec() as u32,
            data: [0; 16],
        };
        message.data[..data.len()].copy_from_slice(data);
        self.messages.push_back(message);
    }
}

/// The interface object: its method table, then our state.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Acp {
    vtable: &'static AcpMethods,
    state: Mutex<State>,
}

#[repr(C)]
struct AcpMethods {
    connect: extern "system" fn(*mut Acp, u32, u32) -> HRESULT,
    disconnect: extern "system" fn(*mut Acp) -> HRESULT,
    submit: extern "system" fn(*mut Acp, u32, u64, u32, *const c_void, u32) -> HRESULT,
    pop_message: extern "system" fn(*mut Acp, *mut Message) -> bool,
    message_count: extern "system" fn(*mut Acp) -> u32,
    release: extern "system" fn(*mut Acp),
}

static ACP_METHODS: AcpMethods = AcpMethods {
    connect,
    disconnect,
    submit,
    pop_message,
    message_count,
    release,
};

fn state(this: *mut Acp) -> MutexGuard<'static, State> {
    // SAFETY: title code calls methods on the object `AcpHalCreate` made,
    // which lives until `release`.
    lock(unsafe { &(*this).state })
}

extern "system" fn connect(this: *mut Acp, commands: u32, messages: u32) -> HRESULT {
    if commands == 0 {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    let mut state = state(this);
    state.connected = true;
    state.capacity = messages as usize;
    S_OK
}

extern "system" fn disconnect(this: *mut Acp) -> HRESULT {
    let mut state = state(this);
    if !state.connected {
        return E_FAIL;
    }
    state.post(DISCONNECTED, &[]);
    state.connected = false;
    S_OK
}

/// Done at once: message registrations take effect, a flowgraph completes
/// unprocessed, a command with an id is acknowledged, and its notification
/// word is set.
extern "system" fn submit(
    this: *mut Acp,
    command: u32,
    id: u64,
    _frame: u32,
    data: *const c_void,
    notification: u32,
) -> HRESULT {
    static SEEN: Mutex<u64> = Mutex::new(0);
    if command < 64 && *lock(&SEEN) & 1 << command == 0 {
        *lock(&SEEN) |= 1 << command;
        tracing::info!(command, "first coprocessor command of this kind");
    }
    let mut state = state(this);
    let word = |at: usize| -> Option<u32> {
        // SAFETY: the command's data starts with these u32 fields.
        (!data.is_null()).then(|| unsafe { data.cast::<u32>().add(at).read_unaligned() })
    };
    match command {
        REGISTER_MESSAGES => state.mask |= word(0).unwrap_or(0),
        UNREGISTER_MESSAGES => state.mask &= !word(0).unwrap_or(0),
        LOAD_FLOWGRAPH => {
            let flowgraph = word(1).unwrap_or(0);
            state.post(FLOWGRAPH_COMPLETED, &flowgraph.to_le_bytes());
        }
        _ if xma_command(command, word) => {}
        // shortcut: context updates and the other SHAPE units' commands are
        // acknowledged but not carried out; add them when a title sends
        // them (each kind is logged once above).
        _ => {}
    }
    if id != 0 {
        let mut done = [0u8; 16];
        done[..4].copy_from_slice(&command.to_le_bytes());
        done[4..12].copy_from_slice(&id.to_le_bytes());
        done[12..].copy_from_slice(&state.frame().to_le_bytes());
        state.post(COMMAND_COMPLETED, &done);
    }
    if notification != 0
        && let Some(word) = heap_unmap(notification)
    {
        // SAFETY: a u32 in a heap block, which the title reads as volatile.
        unsafe { word.cast::<u32>().write_volatile(1) };
    }
    S_OK
}

extern "system" fn pop_message(this: *mut Acp, out: *mut Message) -> bool {
    let Some(message) = state(this).messages.pop_front() else {
        return false;
    };
    if !out.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: the title passes room for one message.
        unsafe { out.write_unaligned(message) };
    }
    true
}

extern "system" fn message_count(this: *mut Acp) -> u32 {
    state(this).messages.len() as u32
}

extern "system" fn release(this: *mut Acp) {
    // SAFETY: made by `AcpHalCreate` with `Box::into_raw`; released once.
    drop(unsafe { Box::from_raw(this) });
}

pub extern "system" fn AcpHalCreate(out: *mut *mut Acp) -> HRESULT {
    if out.is_null() {
        return E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    let acp = Box::new(Acp {
        vtable: &ACP_METHODS,
        state: Mutex::new(State {
            connected: false,
            mask: 0,
            messages: VecDeque::new(),
            capacity: 0,
            dropped: 0,
            since: Instant::now(),
        }),
    });
    // SAFETY: checked non-null.
    unsafe { out.write(Box::into_raw(acp)) };
    S_OK
}

pub(crate) fn module() -> HleModule {
    HleModule {
        name: "audio",
        dlls: &["acphal.dll"],
        exports: vec![
            hle_export!(AcpHalAllocateShapeContexts),
            hle_export!(AcpHalReleaseShapeContexts),
            hle_export!(AcpHalCreate),
            hle_export!(ApuAlloc),
            hle_export!(ApuCreateHeap),
            hle_export!(ApuFree),
            hle_export!(ApuIsVirtualAddressValid),
            hle_export!(ApuMapApuAddress),
            hle_export!(ApuMapVirtualAddress),
        ],
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn heap_maps_every_byte_of_a_block() {
        let _serial = lock(&CONTEXT_TESTS);
        let (mut ptr, mut apu) = (std::ptr::null_mut(), 0);
        assert_eq!(ApuAlloc(&mut ptr, &mut apu, 0x100, 128, 1), S_OK);
        assert!(apu != 0 && apu.is_multiple_of(128));
        let inner = ptr.cast::<u8>().wrapping_add(0x40).cast_const().cast();
        assert_eq!(ApuMapVirtualAddress(inner), apu + 0x40);
        assert!(ApuIsVirtualAddressValid(ptr, 128));
        assert_eq!(heap_unmap(apu + 4), Some(ptr.cast::<u8>().wrapping_add(4)));
        ApuFree(ptr);
        assert_eq!(ApuMapVirtualAddress(ptr), 0);
        assert_eq!(ApuAlloc(&mut ptr, &mut apu, 0x100, 6, 1), E_INVALIDARG);
    }

    /// The context arrays and the heap exist once per process: tests that
    /// allocate from them run one at a time (a concurrent allocation could
    /// take a freed range a test expects back).
    static CONTEXT_TESTS: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());

    #[test]
    fn heap_reuses_freed_addresses() {
        let _serial = lock(&CONTEXT_TESTS);
        let (mut a, mut b, mut c) = (
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
        );
        let (mut apu_a, mut apu_b, mut apu_c) = (0, 0, 0);
        assert_eq!(ApuAlloc(&mut a, &mut apu_a, 0x1000, 0x1000, 1), S_OK);
        assert_eq!(ApuAlloc(&mut b, &mut apu_b, 0x1000, 0x1000, 1), S_OK);
        ApuFree(a);
        assert_eq!(ApuAlloc(&mut c, &mut apu_c, 0x800, 0x800, 1), S_OK);
        // The freed range is free again, whichever part `c` took.
        assert!(
            lock(&HEAP)
                .free
                .iter()
                .any(|(&s, &e)| s <= apu_a + 0x800 && apu_a + 0x1000 <= e)
                || apu_c == apu_a
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ApuMapApuAddress(apu_b + 8),
            b.cast::<u8>().wrapping_add(8).cast()
        );
        assert!(ApuMapApuAddress(0).is_null());
        assert_eq!(
            ApuCreateHeap(64 << 20, 0),
            0x8ACA_0001_u32 as i32,
            "too late"
        );
        ApuFree(b);
        ApuFree(c);
    }

    /// Two packets of three silent mono frames each: a fixed one-subframe
    /// layout, no transmitted coefficients.
    fn silent_stream() -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut data = vec![0xffu8; 2 * xma::PACKET_BYTES];
        let mut put = |at: usize, value: u32, width: usize| {
            for i in 0..width {
                let (p, bit) = (at + i, (value >> (width - 1 - i)) & 1);
                data[p / 8] = (data[p / 8] & !(0x80 >> (p % 8))) | ((bit as u8) << (7 - p % 8));
            }
        };
        for packet in 0..2 {
            let base = packet * xma::PACKET_BYTES * 8;
            put(base, 3 << 26, 32);
            for frame in 0..3 {
                let at = base + 32 + frame * 31;
                put(at, 31, 15); // length
                put(at + 15, 0b10, 2); // fixed layout, one 512-sample subframe
                put(at + 17, 0, 8 + 1 + 3 + 2); // gain, no trim, empty subframe
            }
        }
        data
    }

    #[test]
    fn xma_contexts_decode_into_their_output_rings() {
        let _serial = lock(&CONTEXT_TESTS);
        let mut request = ShapeContexts {
            counts: [0, 0, 0, 0, 4, 0],
            arrays: [std::ptr::null_mut(); 6],
            apu: [0; 6],
        };
        assert_eq!(AcpHalAllocateShapeContexts(&mut request), S_OK);
        let context = Context(request.arrays[4].cast::<u32>().wrapping_add(16));

        let (mut input, mut input_apu) = (std::ptr::null_mut(), 0);
        assert_eq!(ApuAlloc(&mut input, &mut input_apu, 0x1000, 0x800, 1), S_OK);
        let stream = silent_stream();
        // SAFETY: two packets were allocated.
        unsafe { std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(stream.as_ptr(), input.cast(), stream.len()) };
        let (mut output, mut output_apu) = (std::ptr::null_mut(), 0);
        assert_eq!(
            ApuAlloc(&mut output, &mut output_apu, 0x400, 0x100, 2),
            S_OK
        );
        // SAFETY: the ring was just allocated.
        unsafe { output.cast::<u8>().write_bytes(0x55, 0x400) };

        // As the title sets one up: two packets, input 0 valid, a ring of
        // four blocks, writable, 48 kHz mono, reading from the first frame.
        context.set(0, 2 | 1 << 20 | 4 << 22);
        context.set(1, 1 << 31 | 3 << 27);
        context.set(2, 32);
        context.set(5, input_apu);
        context.set(7, output_apu);

        let mut acp = std::ptr::null_mut();
        assert_eq!(AcpHalCreate(&mut acp), S_OK);
        // SAFETY: just created.
        let m = unsafe { (*acp).vtable };
        assert_eq!((m.connect)(acp, 0x1000, 0x1000), S_OK);
        let submit = |command: u32, words: &[u32]| {
            assert_eq!(
                (m.submit)(acp, command, 0xf1, u32::MAX, words.as_ptr().cast(), 0),
                S_OK
            );
        };
        submit(ENABLE_XMA, &[1]);
        xma().pump();
        // Full: all four blocks written (silence), the write block wrapped
        // onto the read block, and the ring no longer writable.
        assert_eq!(context.field(0, 27, 5), 0);
        assert_eq!(context.field(1, 31, 1), 0);
        // SAFETY: the ring.
        let ring = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(output.cast::<u8>(), 0x400) };
        assert!(ring.iter().all(|&b| b == 0));

        // Read four blocks at a time until the input has run out and the
        // ring keeps room (the decoding thread may fill it too).
        for _ in 0..20 {
            submit(ADVANCE_XMA_READ, &[1, 4]);
            xma().pump();
            if context.field(2, 31, 1) == 1 && context.field(1, 31, 1) == 1 {
                break;
            }
        }
        // Six frames and the flushed tail: 3,328 samples, 26 blocks.
        let produced = |x: &Xma| lock(&x.voices[1]).as_ref().map(|v| v.trace.produced);
        assert_eq!(produced(&xma()), Some(26 * SAMPLES_PER_BLOCK));
        assert_eq!(context.field(0, 20, 2), 0, "input used up");
        assert_eq!(context.field(2, 26, 5), INPUT_INVALID);

        // A count near `u32::MAX` wraps the read block like any other
        // (3 + 0xffff_ffff blocks on a ring of four is block 2); the sum
        // used to overflow.
        context.set_field(9, 0, 5, 3);
        submit(ADVANCE_XMA_READ, &[1, u32::MAX]);
        assert_eq!(context.field(9, 0, 5), 2);

        submit(DISABLE_XMA, &[1]);
        assert_eq!(produced(&xma()), None);
        (m.release)(acp);
        ApuFree(input);
        ApuFree(output);
        assert_eq!(AcpHalReleaseShapeContexts(), S_OK);
    }

    #[test]
    fn full_message_queues_count_drops() {
        let mut acp = std::ptr::null_mut();
        assert_eq!(AcpHalCreate(&mut acp), S_OK);
        // SAFETY: just created.
        let m = unsafe { (*acp).vtable };
        assert_eq!((m.connect)(acp, 16, 2), S_OK);
        let mask = COMMAND_COMPLETED;
        assert_eq!(
            (m.submit)(
                acp,
                REGISTER_MESSAGES,
                0,
                u32::MAX,
                (&raw const mask).cast(),
                0
            ),
            S_OK
        );
        for id in 1..=4 {
            assert_eq!((m.submit)(acp, 12, id, u32::MAX, std::ptr::null(), 0), S_OK);
        }
        assert_eq!((m.message_count)(acp), 2);
        let mut message = Message {
            kind: 0,
            dropped: 0,
            usec: 0,
            data: [0; 16],
        };
        assert!((m.pop_message)(acp, &mut message) && (m.pop_message)(acp, &mut message));
        assert_eq!((m.submit)(acp, 12, 5, u32::MAX, std::ptr::null(), 0), S_OK);
        assert!((m.pop_message)(acp, &mut message));
        let dropped = message.dropped;
        assert_eq!(dropped, 2);
        (m.release)(acp);
    }

    #[test]
    fn startup_as_fmod_does_it() {
        let _serial = lock(&CONTEXT_TESTS);
        // Context arrays: rate conversion, DMA and XMA.
        let mut request = ShapeContexts {
            counts: [0x200, 0, 0, 0x400, 0x200, 0],
            arrays: [std::ptr::null_mut(); 6],
            apu: [0; 6],
        };
        assert_eq!(size_of::<ShapeContexts>(), 0x60);
        assert_eq!(AcpHalAllocateShapeContexts(&mut request), S_OK);
        let arrays = request.arrays;
        assert!(!arrays[0].is_null() && !arrays[3].is_null() && !arrays[4].is_null());
        assert!(arrays[1].is_null());
        // SAFETY: 0x200 rate-conversion contexts of 32 bytes were allocated.
        unsafe { arrays[0].cast::<u8>().write_bytes(0, 0x200 << 5) };

        // Connect, register every message but frame starts, then wait for
        // the registration to be acknowledged.
        let mut acp = std::ptr::null_mut();
        assert_eq!(AcpHalCreate(&mut acp), S_OK);
        // SAFETY: just created.
        let m = unsafe { (*acp).vtable };
        assert_eq!((m.connect)(acp, 0x804, 0x804), S_OK);
        let mask = 0xfe_u32;
        let data = (&raw const mask).cast();
        assert_eq!(
            (m.submit)(acp, REGISTER_MESSAGES, 1, u32::MAX, data, 0),
            S_OK
        );
        let mut message = Message {
            kind: 0,
            dropped: 0,
            usec: 0,
            data: [0; 16],
        };
        assert!((m.pop_message)(acp, &mut message));
        let (kind, dropped) = (message.kind, message.dropped);
        assert_eq!((kind, dropped), (COMMAND_COMPLETED, 0));
        assert_eq!(
            u64::from_le_bytes(message.data[4..12].try_into().unwrap()),
            1
        );
        assert!(!(m.pop_message)(acp, &mut message));
        assert_eq!((m.disconnect)(acp), S_OK);
        assert_eq!((m.message_count)(acp), 1, "disconnected");
        (m.release)(acp);
        assert_eq!(AcpHalReleaseShapeContexts(), S_OK);
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-hle/src/modules/audio/capture.rs`:

```rs
//! Debugging aid: `VICTORY_AUDIO_CAPTURE=<file.wav>` records what the title
//! plays, 48 kHz stereo 16-bit, through process loopback: our own process
//! tree only, never the rest of the host's mix. Stretches where nothing was
//! played are written as silence, so the file keeps real time.
//!
//! The recorder runs in a child copy of this executable: an audio client
//! in the title's process raises that process's timer resolution, which
//! changes how the title's own waits behave.

use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{Seek, SeekFrom, Write};
use std::path::Path;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use windows::Win32::Media::Audio::{
    AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_DATA_DISCONTINUITY, AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_SILENT, AUDCLNT_SHAREMODE_SHARED,
    AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_AUTOCONVERTPCM, AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_LOOPBACK,
    AUDIOCLIENT_ACTIVATION_PARAMS, AUDIOCLIENT_ACTIVATION_PARAMS_0,
    AUDIOCLIENT_ACTIVATION_TYPE_PROCESS_LOOPBACK, AUDIOCLIENT_PROCESS_LOOPBACK_PARAMS,
    ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync, IActivateAudioInterfaceAsyncOperation,
    IActivateAudioInterfaceCompletionHandler, IActivateAudioInterfaceCompletionHandler_Impl,
    IAudioCaptureClient, IAudioClient, PROCESS_LOOPBACK_MODE_INCLUDE_TARGET_PROCESS_TREE,
    VIRTUAL_AUDIO_DEVICE_PROCESS_LOOPBACK, WAVE_FORMAT_PCM, WAVEFORMATEX,
};
use windows::Win32::System::Com::{COINIT_MULTITHREADED, CoInitializeEx};
use windows::Win32::Foundation::WAIT_OBJECT_0;
use windows::Win32::System::Threading::{
    OpenProcess, PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE, Sleep, WaitForSingleObject,
};
use windows::core::{HRESULT, IUnknown, Interface, Ref, implement};

const RATE: u32 = 48_000;
const FRAME_BYTES: usize = 4;

/// Activation completes asynchronously; the recording thread polls for it.
#[implement(IActivateAudioInterfaceCompletionHandler)]
struct Activated;

impl IActivateAudioInterfaceCompletionHandler_Impl for Activated_Impl {
    fn ActivateCompleted(
        &self,
        _: Ref<IActivateAudioInterfaceAsyncOperation>,
    ) -> windows::core::Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Names the process to record, in the recorder's environment.
const TARGET: &str = "VICTORY_AUDIO_CAPTURE_OF";

/// Starts the recorder if `VICTORY_AUDIO_CAPTURE` names a file. With this
/// module's debug log, also logs once a second what a `Sleep(1)` takes in
/// this process (the title's millisecond waits get the same).
pub fn start() {
    if tracing::enabled!(tracing::Level::DEBUG) {
        let _ = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("victory timing probe".into())
            .spawn(|| {
                loop {
                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1));
                    let at = Instant::now();
                    // SAFETY: plain wait.
                    unsafe { Sleep(1) };
                    let ms = at.elapsed().as_secs_f32() * 1000.0;
                    tracing::debug!(ms, "Sleep(1) took");
                }
            });
    }
    if std::env::var_os("VICTORY_AUDIO_CAPTURE").is_some()
        && let Err(e) = std::env::current_exe().and_then(|exe| {
            std::process::Command::new(exe)
                .env(TARGET, std::process::id().to_string())
                .spawn()
        })
    {
        tracing::warn!("audio capture not started: {e}");
    }
}

/// In the recorder (a child started by [`start`]): records until the
/// target exits and returns true; false in any other process.
pub fn child() -> bool {
    let (Some(pid), Some(path)) = (
        std::env::var(TARGET).ok().and_then(|p| p.parse().ok()),
        std::env::var_os("VICTORY_AUDIO_CAPTURE"),
    ) else {
        return false;
    };
    if let Err(e) = record(pid, Path::new(&path)) {
        tracing::warn!("audio capture stopped: {e}");
    }
    true
}

fn header(frames: u64) -> [u8; 44] {
    let data = u32::try_from(frames * FRAME_BYTES as u64).unwrap_or(u32::MAX - 36);
    let mut h = [0u8; 44];
    let fields: [(&[u8], usize); 11] = [
        (b"RIFF", 0),
        (&(36 + data).to_le_bytes(), 4),
        (b"WAVEfmt ", 8),
        (&16u32.to_le_bytes(), 16),
        (&1u16.to_le_bytes(), 20),
        (&2u16.to_le_bytes(), 22),
        (&RATE.to_le_bytes(), 24),
        (&(RATE * FRAME_BYTES as u32).to_le_bytes(), 28),
        (&(FRAME_BYTES as u16).to_le_bytes(), 32),
        (&16u16.to_le_bytes(), 34),
        (b"data", 36),
    ];
    for (bytes, at) in fields {
        h[at..at + bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(bytes);
    }
    h[40..].copy_from_slice(&data.to_le_bytes());
    h
}

fn record(pid: u32, path: &Path) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // SAFETY: COM calls with parameters built here; buffers are used only
    // between `GetBuffer` and `ReleaseBuffer`.
    unsafe {
        CoInitializeEx(None, COINIT_MULTITHREADED).ok()?;
        let target = OpenProcess(PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE, false, pid)?;
        let params = AUDIOCLIENT_ACTIVATION_PARAMS {
            ActivationType: AUDIOCLIENT_ACTIVATION_TYPE_PROCESS_LOOPBACK,
            Anonymous: AUDIOCLIENT_ACTIVATION_PARAMS_0 {
                ProcessLoopbackParams: AUDIOCLIENT_PROCESS_LOOPBACK_PARAMS {
                    TargetProcessId: pid,
                    ProcessLoopbackMode: PROCESS_LOOPBACK_MODE_INCLUDE_TARGET_PROCESS_TREE,
                },
            },
        };
        /// A `PROPVARIANT` holding a blob (`VT_BLOB`).
        #[repr(C)]
        struct Blob {
            vt: u16,
            reserved: [u16; 3],
            size: u32,
            data: *const AUDIOCLIENT_ACTIVATION_PARAMS,
        }
        let blob = Blob {
            vt: 0x41,
            reserved: [0; 3],
            size: size_of_val(&params) as u32,
            data: &params,
        };
        let handler: IActivateAudioInterfaceCompletionHandler = Activated.into();
        let operation = ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync(
            VIRTUAL_AUDIO_DEVICE_PROCESS_LOOPBACK,
            &IAudioClient::IID,
            Some((&raw const blob).cast()),
            &handler,
        )?;
        let client = loop {
            let (mut hr, mut client) = (HRESULT(0), None::<IUnknown>);
            // Fails (`E_ILLEGAL_METHOD_CALL`) until activation completes.
            if operation.GetActivateResult(&mut hr, &mut client).is_ok() {
                hr.ok()?;
                break client.ok_or("no audio client")?.cast::<IAudioClient>()?;
            }
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));
        };
        let format = WAVEFORMATEX {
            wFormatTag: WAVE_FORMAT_PCM as u16,
            nChannels: 2,
            nSamplesPerSec: RATE,
            nAvgBytesPerSec: RATE * FRAME_BYTES as u32,
            nBlockAlign: FRAME_BYTES as u16,
            wBitsPerSample: 16,
            cbSize: 0,
        };
        client.Initialize(
            AUDCLNT_SHAREMODE_SHARED,
            AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_LOOPBACK | AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_AUTOCONVERTPCM,
            10_000_000,
            0,
            &format,
            None,
        )?;
        let capture: IAudioCaptureClient = client.GetService()?;
        let mut file = File::create(path)?;
        file.write_all(&header(0))?;
        client.Start()?;
        tracing::info!(path = %path.display(), "recording the title's audio");

        let (mut written, mut first) = (0u64, None);
        let mut patched = Instant::now();
        loop {
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));
            let ended = WaitForSingleObject(target, 0) == WAIT_OBJECT_0;
            while capture.GetNextPacketSize()? > 0 {
                let (mut data, mut frames, mut flags, mut qpc) = (std::ptr::null_mut(), 0, 0, 0);
                capture.GetBuffer(&mut data, &mut frames, &mut flags, None, Some(&mut qpc))?;
                // Where this packet belongs, from its time stamp (100 ns).
                let at = (qpc - *first.get_or_insert(qpc)) * u64::from(RATE) / 10_000_000;
                if at > written + u64::from(RATE / 500) {
                    tracing::debug!(
                        ms = (at - written) * 1000 / u64::from(RATE),
                        "audio capture: nothing played"
                    );
                    let silence = vec![0u8; (at - written) as usize * FRAME_BYTES];
                    file.write_all(&silence)?;
                    written = at;
                }
                let bytes = frames as usize * FRAME_BYTES;
                if flags & AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_SILENT.0 as u32 != 0 {
                    file.write_all(&vec![0u8; bytes])?;
                } else {
                    file.write_all(std::slice::from_raw_parts(data, bytes))?;
                }
                if flags & AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_DATA_DISCONTINUITY.0 as u32 != 0 && written > 0 {
                    tracing::debug!("audio capture: discontinuity");
                }
                written += u64::from(frames);
                capture.ReleaseBuffer(frames)?;
            }
            if ended || patched.elapsed() >= Duration::from_secs(1) {
                // Valid sizes at any time: runs end by being killed.
                file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0))?;
                file.write_all(&header(written))?;
                file.seek(SeekFrom::End(0))?;
                patched = Instant::now();
            }
            if ended {
                return Ok(());
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```rs
//! `d3d12_xs.dll`: virtual memory setup, device creation, root signature
//! serialization. The device and everything it creates live in
//! `victory-gpu`.

use std::ffi::c_void;

use victory_gpu::device;
use victory_gpu::object::{HRESULT, Iid, Object};

use crate::{HleExport, HleModule};

/// Device creation; first hands the device the title's general allocator
/// (`XMemAlloc`, which honours the title's hooks) for resource memory.
extern "system" fn create_device(
    adapter: *const c_void,
    parameters: *const u32,
    iid: *const Iid,
    out: *mut *const Object,
) -> HRESULT {
    victory_gpu::resource::use_allocator(super::xmem::XMemAlloc, super::xmem::XMemFree);
    victory_gpu::resource::use_page_mapper(super::xmem::map_alias);
    #[cfg(windows)]
    victory_gpu::on_failure(host_gpu_failed);
    device::create(adapter, parameters, iid, out)
}

/// A host GPU failure ends the run like a crash: reported to the crash log,
/// then the process ends as the console ends a title.
#[cfg(windows)]
fn host_gpu_failed(what: &str) -> ! {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{GetCurrentProcess, TerminateProcess};
    victory_loader::log_crash(&format!("VIctory: host GPU failure: {what}"));
    const DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED: u32 = 0x887A_0005;
    // SAFETY: ends our own process.
    unsafe { TerminateProcess(GetCurrentProcess(), DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED) };
    unreachable!("the process has ended")
}

/// The offline warm-up: see `victory_gpu::shader_cache::warm`.
pub fn warm_shader(container: &[u8]) -> Result<bool, String> {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        victory_gpu::shader_cache::warm(container)
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        let _ = container;
        Err("no shader cache on this host".into())
    }
}

/// Keeps the host's translations of the title's shaders in `dir` (a
/// folder of the cache) across runs, and its compiled pipelines beside it
/// (`pipelines`).
pub fn use_shader_cache(dir: std::path::PathBuf) {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        victory_gpu::pipeline::use_pipeline_cache(dir.with_file_name("pipelines"));
        victory_gpu::shader_cache::use_shader_cache(dir);
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    let _ = dir;
}

pub(crate) fn module() -> HleModule {
    HleModule {
        name: "d3d12x",
        dlls: &["d3d12_xs.dll"],
        exports: vec![
            HleExport {
                name: "D3D12ConfigureVirtualMemoryX",
                address: device::configure_virtual_memory as *const () as usize,
            },
            HleExport {
                name: "D3D12XboxCreateDevice",
                address: create_device as *const () as usize,
            },
            HleExport {
                name: "D3D12SerializeRootSignature",
                address: victory_gpu::root::serialize as *const () as usize,
            },
            HleExport {
                name: "D3D12SerializeVersionedRootSignature",
                address: victory_gpu::root::serialize_versioned as *const () as usize,
            },
            // The AMD upscaler's (Series S).
            HleExport {
                name: "D3D12CreateRootSignatureDeserializer",
                address: victory_gpu::root::create_deserializer as *const () as usize,
            },
            // A data import: the title reads the id at this address.
            HleExport {
                name: "IID_ID3D12Device",
                address: (&raw const device::IID) as usize,
            },
        ],
    }
}
```

```rs
/// 2: disabled. We present in SDR, so the title must render SDR.
// shortcut: HDR output is not done (see the presentation items in
// `TODO.md`); report enabled, with the host display's luminance, once the
// swap chain can present HDR.
extern "system" fn try_enable_hdr(_: This, preference: u32, _info: *mut c_void) -> u32 {
    tracing::info!(preference, "HDR mode: disabled (SDR presentation)");
    2
}

/// Nothing launches URIs for the title: no store, browser or console app
/// exists here, and the console's are online services.
extern "system" fn launch_uri(_: This, _user: *const c_void, uri: *const c_char) -> HRESULT {
    tracing::info!(uri = text(uri).unwrap_or_default(), "URI not launched");
    NOT_SUPPORTED
}

/// A deferral keeps the host display on, as on the console, through a
/// power request; the handle is that request.
#[cfg(windows)]
extern "system" fn acquire_deferral(_: This, out: *mut *mut c_void) -> HRESULT {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Power::{
        PowerCreateRequest, PowerRequestDisplayRequired, PowerSetRequest,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
        POWER_REQUEST_CONTEXT_SIMPLE_STRING, REASON_CONTEXT,
    };
    if out.is_null() {
        return super::xasync::E_INVALIDARG;
    }
    let mut reason: Vec<u16> = "Title display deferral\0".encode_utf16().collect();
    let mut context = REASON_CONTEXT {
        Flags: POWER_REQUEST_CONTEXT_SIMPLE_STRING,
        ..Default::default()
    };
    context.Reason.SimpleReasonString = reason.as_mut_ptr();
    // SAFETY: a valid context; the string is copied by the call.
    let request = unsafe { PowerCreateRequest(&context) };
    if request as isize == -1 {
        return last_error();
    }
    // SAFETY: the request we just created.
    if unsafe { PowerSetRequest(request, PowerRequestDisplayRequired) } == 0 {
        let hr = last_error();
        // SAFETY: as above; not handed out.
        unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle(request) };
        return hr;
    }
    put(out, request)
}

#[cfg(windows)]
extern "system" fn close_deferral(_: This, handle: *mut c_void) {
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Power::{PowerClearRequest, PowerRequestDisplayRequired};
    if !handle.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: a request from `acquire_deferral`.
        unsafe {
            PowerClearRequest(handle, PowerRequestDisplayRequired);
            CloseHandle(handle);
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn last_error() -> HRESULT {
    // SAFETY: no preconditions.
    let code = unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::GetLastError() };
    (0x8007_0000 | (code & 0xffff)) as i32
}

// row pitch, bytes) on request, e.g. `victory_gpu::last_frame() ->
// Option<Frame>`, copied from the back buffer after `PresentX`.
extern "system" fn take_screenshot(_: This, _user: *const c_void, _result: *mut c_void) -> HRESULT {
    tracing::info!("screenshot not taken");
    NOT_SUPPORTED
}

#[cfg(all(test, windows))]

    #[test]

        type Hdr = extern "system" fn(This, u32, *mut c_void) -> u32;
        assert_eq!(
```
