```rs
/// The device type is not a runtime call: code linked into the title reads
/// `ConsoleMode` from this key (`RegOpenKeyW`, `RegQueryValueExW`) and
/// takes a missing value for a PC.
#[cfg(windows)]
mod device_type {
    #![allow(non_snake_case)]

    use std::ffi::c_void;

    use victory_gpu::console::{self, Console};

    use crate::modules::files::host;
    use crate::{HleModule, hle_export};

    type Key = *mut c_void;
    const LOCAL_MACHINE: Key = 0xffff_ffff_8000_0002_u64 as Key;
    const KEY: &str = r"Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\OEM";
    const VALUE: &str = "ConsoleMode";
    const SUCCESS: u32 = 0;
    const FILE_NOT_FOUND: u32 = 2;
    const INVALID_PARAMETER: u32 = 87;
    const MORE_DATA: u32 = 234;
    const DWORD: u32 = 4;

    /// Stands for the key; never a host handle value.
    static OEM: u8 = 0;
    fn oem() -> Key {
        (&raw const OEM).cast_mut().cast()
    }

    /// What the title's code maps to each model's device type.
    pub(super) fn console_mode(console: Console) -> u32 {
        match console {
            Console::SeriesX => 0x64,
            Console::SeriesS => 0x60,
        }
    }

    fn is(text: *const u16, expected: &str) -> bool {
        if text.is_null() {
            return false;
        }
        // SAFETY: the title passes a NUL-terminated string.
        let text = unsafe {
            let len = (0..).take_while(|&i| *text.add(i) != 0).count();
            String::from_utf16_lossy(std::slice::from_raw_parts(text, len))
        };
        text.eq_ignore_ascii_case(expected)
    }

    /// Opens our key for its path; the key has no subkeys. `None`: not
    /// ours, ask the host.
    fn open(root: Key, sub: *const u16, out: *mut Key) -> Option<u32> {
        if root == oem() {
            return Some(FILE_NOT_FOUND);
        }
        if root == LOCAL_MACHINE && is(sub, KEY) && !out.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: checked non-null; the title passes room for a key.
            unsafe { out.write(oem()) };
            return Some(SUCCESS);
        }
        None
    }

    // Our titles import only these registry functions (and `RegOpenKeyExW`
    // below), so no other call can reach the host with our key.
    pub extern "system" fn RegOpenKeyW(root: Key, sub: *const u16, out: *mut Key) -> u32 {
        open(root, sub, out).unwrap_or_else(|| {
            host!("advapi32.dll", "RegOpenKeyW": extern "system" fn(Key, *const u16, *mut Key) -> u32)(
                root, sub, out,
            )
        })
    }

    pub extern "system" fn RegOpenKeyExW(
        root: Key,
        sub: *const u16,
        options: u32,
        access: u32,
        out: *mut Key,
    ) -> u32 {
        open(root, sub, out).unwrap_or_else(|| {
            host!("advapi32.dll", "RegOpenKeyExW": extern "system" fn(
                Key, *const u16, u32, u32, *mut Key,
            ) -> u32)(root, sub, options, access, out)
        })
    }

    pub extern "system" fn RegQueryValueExW(
        key: Key,
        name: *const u16,
        reserved: *mut u32,
        kind: *mut u32,
        data: *mut u8,
        size: *mut u32,
    ) -> u32 {
        if key != oem() {
            return host!("advapi32.dll", "RegQueryValueExW": extern "system" fn(
                Key, *const u16, *mut u32, *mut u32, *mut u8, *mut u32,
            ) -> u32)(key, name, reserved, kind, data, size);
        }
        if !is(name, VALUE) {
            return FILE_NOT_FOUND;
        }
        if !data.is_null() && size.is_null() {
            return INVALID_PARAMETER;
        }
        // SAFETY: the title passes valid or null pointers, sized by `size`.
        unsafe {
            if !kind.is_null() {
                kind.write(DWORD);
            }
            if size.is_null() {
                return SUCCESS;
            }
            let room = size.read();
            size.write(4);
            if data.is_null() {
                return SUCCESS;
            }
            if room < 4 {
                return MORE_DATA;
            }
            data.cast::<u32>()
                .write_unaligned(console_mode(console::current()));
        }
        tracing::debug!(console = console::current().name(), "device type read");
        SUCCESS
    }

    pub extern "system" fn RegCloseKey(key: Key) -> u32 {
        if key == oem() {
            return SUCCESS;
        }
        host!("advapi32.dll", "RegCloseKey": extern "system" fn(Key) -> u32)(key)
    }

    pub(crate) fn module() -> HleModule {
        HleModule {
            name: "device type",
            dlls: &["advapi32.dll", "api-ms-win-core-registry-*"],
            exports: vec![
                hle_export!(RegOpenKeyW),
                hle_export!(RegOpenKeyExW),
                hle_export!(RegQueryValueExW),
                hle_export!(RegCloseKey),
            ],
        }
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::*;

        fn w(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
            s.encode_utf16().chain([0]).collect()
        }

        #[test]
        fn titles_read_the_chosen_model() {
            assert_eq!(console_mode(Console::SeriesX), 0x64);
            assert_eq!(console_mode(Console::SeriesS), 0x60);
            let mut key = std::ptr::null_mut();
            let path = w(&KEY.to_ascii_lowercase());
            assert_eq!(RegOpenKeyW(LOCAL_MACHINE, path.as_ptr(), &mut key), SUCCESS);
            let (mut kind, mut value, mut size) = (0, 0u32, 4);
            let name = w(VALUE);
            let query = |data: *mut u32, size: *mut u32, kind: *mut u32| {
                RegQueryValueExW(
                    key,
                    name.as_ptr(),
                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
                    kind,
                    data.cast(),
                    size,
                )
            };
            assert_eq!(query(&mut value, &mut size, &mut kind), SUCCESS);
            assert_eq!((kind, size), (DWORD, 4));
            assert_eq!(value, console_mode(console::current()));
            let mut small = 2;
            assert_eq!(query(&mut value, &mut small, &mut kind), MORE_DATA);
            assert_eq!(small, 4);
            let other = w("Other");
            assert_eq!(
                RegQueryValueExW(
                    key,
                    other.as_ptr(),
                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
                    &mut kind,
                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
                    &mut size
                ),
                FILE_NOT_FOUND
            );
            let mut sub = std::ptr::null_mut();
            assert_eq!(
                RegOpenKeyExW(key, other.as_ptr(), 0, 1, &mut sub),
                FILE_NOT_FOUND
            );
            assert_eq!(RegCloseKey(key), SUCCESS);
            let mut again = std::ptr::null_mut();
            assert_eq!(
                RegOpenKeyExW(LOCAL_MACHINE, path.as_ptr(), 0, 1, &mut again),
                SUCCESS
            );
            assert_eq!(again, oem());
        }

        #[test]
        fn other_keys_reach_the_host() {
            let mut key = std::ptr::null_mut();
            let path = w(r"Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion");
            assert_eq!(RegOpenKeyW(LOCAL_MACHINE, path.as_ptr(), &mut key), SUCCESS);
            assert_ne!(key, oem());
            let (mut size, name) = (0, w("ProductName"));
            assert_eq!(
                RegQueryValueExW(
                    key,
                    name.as_ptr(),
                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
                    &mut size
                ),
                SUCCESS
            );
            assert!(size > 0);
            assert_eq!(RegCloseKey(key), SUCCESS);
        }
    }
}
```

```rs
//! XUser: one offline local user, signed in, never a guest, with every
//! privilege. Served as the user provider's objects from `QueryApiImpl`;
//! adding a user completes through `xasync` like any other async call. No
//! input device is associated with the user (there are none, `gameinput`).
#![allow(clippy::not_unsafe_ptr_arg_deref)]

use std::ffi::{c_char, c_void};

use super::xasync::{self, AsyncBlock, ProviderData};
use super::xgameruntime::{

/// The documented "no such user" error.
pub const USER_NOT_FOUND: HRESULT = 0x8924_5104_u32 as i32;

pub const XUID: u64 = 0x0009_0000_0000_0001;
pub const LOCAL_ID: u64 = 1;
const GAMERTAG: &str = "Player";

/// The only user; a handle is its address, duplicating and closing are free.
pub struct User;
static USER: User = User;
type Handle = *const User;

fn user() -> Handle {
    &USER
}

fn found(found: bool, out: *mut Handle) -> HRESULT {
    if found {
        put(out, user())
    } else {
        USER_NOT_FOUND
    }
}

pub static OBJECT: Object = Object::new("user", &VTABLE);
pub static GAMERTAG_OBJECT: Object = Object::new("user gamertag", &GAMERTAG_VTABLE);
pub static DEVICE_OBJECT: Object = Object::new("user devices", &DEVICE_VTABLE);

pub const INTERFACES: &[Interface] = &[
    (PROVIDER, IID, &OBJECT),
    // The title (2026) asks with the provider's id; its thunks call
    // the same slots with the same arguments (0x108/0x110 change events).
    (PROVIDER, PROVIDER, &OBJECT),
    (PROVIDER, GAMERTAG_IID, &GAMERTAG_OBJECT),
    (DEVICE_PROVIDER, DEVICE_IID, &DEVICE_OBJECT),
];

type This = *const Object;
extern "system" fn duplicate(_: This, _: Handle, out: *mut Handle) -> HRESULT {
    put(out, user())
}
extern "system" fn close(_: This, _: Handle) {}
extern "system" fn compare(_: This, a: Handle, b: Handle) -> i32 {
    i32::from(a != b)
}

/// The async provider for adding a user: done at once, the result is a
/// handle.
extern "system" fn add_provider(op: u32, data: *const ProviderData) -> HRESULT {
    const BEGIN: u32 = 0;
    const GET_RESULT: u32 = 2;
    // SAFETY: the async runtime passes valid provider data.
    let data = unsafe { &*data };
    match op {
        BEGIN => xasync::XAsyncComplete(data.block, S_OK, size_of::<Handle>()),
        GET_RESULT => return put(data.buffer.cast::<Handle>(), user()),
        _ => {}
    }
    S_OK
}

/// Tells our add calls apart from other async calls on the same block.
static ADD: u8 = 0;

/// Any options add the one user, silently.
extern "system" fn add_async(_: This, options: u32, block: *mut AsyncBlock) -> HRESULT {
    tracing::info!(options, "XUserAddAsync: the offline local user");
    xasync::XAsyncBegin(
        block,
        std::ptr::null_mut(),
        (&raw const ADD).cast(),
        std::ptr::null(),
        Some(add_provider),
    )
}
extern "system" fn add_result(_: This, block: *mut AsyncBlock, out: *mut Handle) -> HRESULT {
    xasync::XAsyncGetResult(
        block,
        (&raw const ADD).cast(),
        size_of::<Handle>(),
        out.cast(),
        std::ptr::null_mut(),
    )
}
extern "system" fn get_local_id(_: This, _: Handle, out: *mut u64) -> HRESULT {
    put(out, LOCAL_ID)
}
extern "system" fn find_by_local_id(_: This, id: u64, out: *mut Handle) -> HRESULT {
    found(id == LOCAL_ID, out)
}
extern "system" fn get_id(_: This, _: Handle, out: *mut u64) -> HRESULT {
    put(out, XUID)
}
extern "system" fn find_by_id(_: This, id: u64, out: *mut Handle) -> HRESULT {
    found(id == XUID, out)
}
extern "system" fn get_is_guest(_: This, _: Handle, out: *mut bool) -> HRESULT {
    put(out, false)
}
/// 0: signed in.
extern "system" fn get_state(_: This, _: Handle, out: *mut u32) -> HRESULT {
    put(out, 0)
}
/// The user's gamertag as the component asked for (`XUserGamertagComponent`):
/// it has no suffix, so the modern suffix is empty and every other component
/// (classic, modern, unique modern) is the name itself.
extern "system" fn get_gamertag(
    _: This,
    _: Handle,
    component: u32,
    size: usize,
    buffer: *mut u8,
    used: *mut usize,
) -> HRESULT {
    const MODERN_SUFFIX: u32 = 2;
    let text = match component {
        MODERN_SUFFIX => "",
        _ => GAMERTAG,
    };
    put_string(text, size, buffer, used)
}
/// Granted; deny reason 0 (none).
extern "system" fn check_privilege(
    _: This,
    _: Handle,
    _options: u32,
    _privilege: u32,
    has: *mut bool,
    reason: *mut u32,
) -> HRESULT {
    if !reason.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: checked non-null.
        unsafe { reason.write(0) };
    }
    put(has, true)
}

/// 3: adult.
extern "system" fn get_age_group(_: This, _: Handle, out: *mut u32) -> HRESULT {
    put(out, 3)
}

static RESOLVE: u8 = 0;
static TOKEN: u8 = 0;

/// Every privilege is granted, so there is nothing to resolve.
extern "system" fn resolve_privilege_async(
    _: This,
    _: Handle,
    _options: u32,
    _privilege: u32,
    block: *mut AsyncBlock,
) -> HRESULT {
    xasync::finished(block, (&raw const RESOLVE).cast(), S_OK)
}
extern "system" fn resolve_privilege_result(_: This, block: *mut AsyncBlock) -> HRESULT {
    let none = std::ptr::null_mut();
    xasync::XAsyncGetResult(block, (&raw const RESOLVE).cast(), 0, none, none.cast())
}

/// The documented "failed to get token": tokens come from the service.
pub const FAILED_TO_GET_TOKEN: HRESULT = 0x8924_5111_u32 as i32;

#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
extern "system" fn token_async(
    _: This,
    _: Handle,
    _options: u32,
    _method: *const c_char,
    url: *const c_char,
    _header_count: usize,
    _headers: *const c_void,
    _body_size: usize,
    _body: *const c_void,
    block: *mut AsyncBlock,
) -> HRESULT {
    tracing::info!(
        url = text(url).unwrap_or_default(),
        "token and signature: offline"
    );
    xasync::finished(block, (&raw const TOKEN).cast(), FAILED_TO_GET_TOKEN)
}
extern "system" fn token_size(_: This, block: *mut AsyncBlock, out: *mut usize) -> HRESULT {
    xasync::XAsyncGetResultSize(block, out)
}
extern "system" fn token_result(
    _: This,
    block: *mut AsyncBlock,
    size: usize,
    buffer: *mut c_void,
    _data: *mut *const c_void,
    used: *mut usize,
) -> HRESULT {
    xasync::XAsyncGetResult(block, (&raw const TOKEN).cast(), size, buffer, used)
}

/// The user never changes and no device is ever associated, so these
/// callbacks are never called.
extern "system" fn register(
    _: This,
    _queue: *const c_void,
    _context: *mut c_void,
    _callback: *const c_void,
    out: *mut u64,
) -> HRESULT {
    put(out, token())
}
extern "system" fn unregister(_: This, _token: u64, _wait: bool) -> bool {
    true
}

/// No input device belongs to a user.
extern "system" fn find_for_device(_: This, _device: *const c_void, _: *mut Handle) -> HRESULT {
    USER_NOT_FOUND
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::modules::xasync::E_NOT_SUFFICIENT_BUFFER;
    use crate::modules::xgameruntime::method as slot;

    #[test]
    fn a_gamertag_without_a_suffix_has_an_empty_modern_suffix() {
        type Gamertag =
            extern "system" fn(This, Handle, u32, usize, *mut u8, *mut usize) -> HRESULT;
        let this: This = &OBJECT;
        let user = std::ptr::null();
        // Classic, modern, modern suffix, unique modern; through both slots.
        let expected: [&[u8]; 4] = [b"Player\0", b"Player\0", b"\0", b"Player\0"];
        for (object, at) in [(&GAMERTAG_OBJECT, 0x18), (&OBJECT, 0x78)] {
            let get = slot::<Gamertag>(object, at);
            for (component, expected) in (0..).zip(expected) {
                let (mut name, mut used) = ([0xff_u8; 16], 0);
                let hr = get(this, user, component, 16, name.as_mut_ptr(), &mut used);
                assert_eq!(hr, S_OK);
                assert_eq!(&name[..used], expected, "component {component}");
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn startup_adds_the_user_and_reads_its_id() {
        type Add = extern "system" fn(This, u32, *mut AsyncBlock) -> HRESULT;
        type AddResult = extern "system" fn(This, *mut AsyncBlock, *mut Handle) -> HRESULT;
        type GetId = extern "system" fn(This, Handle, *mut u64) -> HRESULT;
        type Gamertag =
            extern "system" fn(This, Handle, u32, usize, *mut u8, *mut usize) -> HRESULT;
        let this: This = &OBJECT;
        let mut block = AsyncBlock {
            queue: std::ptr::null(),
            context: std::ptr::null_mut(),
            callback: None,
            internal: [0; 4],
        };
        assert_eq!(slot::<Add>(&OBJECT, 0x38)(this, 1, &mut block), S_OK);
        assert_eq!(xasync::XAsyncGetStatus(&mut block, true), S_OK);
        let mut handle = std::ptr::null();
        assert_eq!(
            slot::<AddResult>(&OBJECT, 0x40)(this, &mut block, &mut handle),
            S_OK
        );
        assert!(!handle.is_null());
        let mut xuid = 0;
        assert_eq!(slot::<GetId>(&OBJECT, 0x58)(this, handle, &mut xuid), S_OK);
        assert_eq!(xuid, XUID);

        let mut name = [0u8; 16];
        let mut used = 0;
        let get = slot::<Gamertag>(&GAMERTAG_OBJECT, 0x18);
        assert_eq!(get(this, handle, 0, 16, name.as_mut_ptr(), &mut used), S_OK);
        assert_eq!(&name[..used], b"Player\0");
        assert_eq!(
            get(this, handle, 0, 2, name.as_mut_ptr(), &mut used),
            E_NOT_SUFFICIENT_BUFFER
        );

        type Age = extern "system" fn(This, Handle, *mut u32) -> HRESULT;
        let mut age = 0;
        assert_eq!(slot::<Age>(&OBJECT, 0x98)(this, handle, &mut age), S_OK);
        assert_eq!(age, 3, "adult");
        type Token = extern "system" fn(
            This,
            Handle,
            u32,
            *const c_char,
            *const c_char,
            usize,
            *const c_void,
            usize,
            *const c_void,
            *mut AsyncBlock,
        ) -> HRESULT;
        let (null, url) = (std::ptr::null(), c"https://example.invalid/");
        let token = slot::<Token>(&OBJECT, 0xb8);
        assert_eq!(
            token(
                this,
                handle,
                0,
                c"GET".as_ptr(),
                url.as_ptr(),
                0,
                null,
                0,
                null,
                &mut block
            ),
            S_OK
        );
        assert_eq!(
            xasync::XAsyncGetStatus(&mut block, true),
            FAILED_TO_GET_TOKEN
        );
    }
}
```

```rs
//! The table of everything we implement.

use std::sync::LazyLock;

use crate::modules;

/// One function we implement, under the name the title imports (`#n` for an
/// ordinal).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct HleExport {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub address: usize,
}

/// A group of implementations and the DLL names they answer for.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct HleModule {
    /// Human-readable name, e.g. "kernel".
    pub name: &'static str,
    /// Lower-case DLL names served. A trailing `*` matches a prefix, which
    /// covers versioned API sets (`api-ms-win-core-libraryloader-l1-2-0.dll`).
    pub dlls: &'static [&'static str],
    pub exports: Vec<HleExport>,
}

impl HleModule {
    pub fn serves(&self, dll: &str) -> bool {
        let dll = dll.to_ascii_lowercase();
        self.dlls
            .iter()
            .any(|pattern| match pattern.strip_suffix('*') {
                Some(prefix) => dll.starts_with(prefix),
                None => dll == *pattern,
            })
    }
}

/// Declares an export whose Rust name equals the imported name.
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! hle_export {
    ($f:ident) => {
        $crate::HleExport {
            name: stringify!($f),
            address: $f as *const () as usize,
        }
    };
}

static REGISTRY: LazyLock<Vec<HleModule>> = LazyLock::new(modules::all);

/// All modules we implement.
pub fn registry() -> &'static [HleModule] {
    &REGISTRY
}

pub(crate) fn lookup(dll: &str, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    registry()
        .iter()
        .filter(|m| m.serves(dll))
        .flat_map(|m| m.exports.iter())
        .find(|e| e.name == name)
        .map(|e| e.address)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn export_names_are_unique_per_dll_pattern() {
        for module in registry() {
            let mut names: Vec<_> = module.exports.iter().map(|e| e.name).collect();
            names.sort_unstable();
            let before = names.len();
            names.dedup();
            assert_eq!(
                before,
                names.len(),
                "duplicate export in module {}",
                module.name
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn api_set_prefix_matching() {
        let m = HleModule {
            name: "t",
            dlls: &["api-ms-win-core-libraryloader-*"],
            exports: vec![],
        };
        assert!(m.serves("API-MS-WIN-CORE-LIBRARYLOADER-L1-2-0.dll"));
        assert!(!m.serves("api-ms-win-core-file-l1-1-0.dll"));
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Process-wide state the implementations need.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};

static MAIN_IMAGE_BASE: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);

/// Records where the title's main image is mapped. The title expects
/// `GetModuleHandle(NULL)` and friends to return this, not our own exe.
pub fn set_main_image(base: usize) {
    MAIN_IMAGE_BASE.store(base, Ordering::Release);
}

pub fn main_image() -> Option<usize> {
    match MAIN_IMAGE_BASE.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
        0 => None,
        base => Some(base),
    }
}

/// Original file of each title image we mapped, by base address.
static IMAGE_PATHS: Mutex<Vec<(usize, PathBuf)>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());

/// Records the file a title image was mapped from: the title asks for its
/// own path (`GetModuleFileName`) to find its data, and must not get our
/// cache copy.
pub fn set_image_path(base: usize, path: &Path) {
    let path = std::path::absolute(path).unwrap_or_else(|_| path.to_owned());
    let mut paths = IMAGE_PATHS.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    paths.retain(|(b, _)| *b != base);
    paths.push((base, path));
}

/// Forgets a title image that was unmapped again.
pub fn forget_image(base: usize) {
    let mut paths = IMAGE_PATHS.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    paths.retain(|(b, _)| *b != base);
}

pub fn image_path(base: usize) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let paths = IMAGE_PATHS.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    paths
        .iter()
        .find(|(b, _)| *b == base)
        .map(|(_, p)| p.clone())
}

/// The title image whose original file is called `file` (any case).
pub fn image_named(file: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    let paths = IMAGE_PATHS.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    paths
        .iter()
        .find(|(_, p)| p.file_name().is_some_and(|n| n.eq_ignore_ascii_case(file)))
        .map(|(b, _)| *b)
}

/// Maps a title DLL the title loads itself (`LoadLibrary`) and returns its
/// base; `Ok(None)` if `file` is not one of the title's DLLs.
pub type TitleDllLoader = Box<dyn Fn(&str) -> Result<Option<usize>, String> + Send + Sync>;

static TITLE_DLL_LOADER: std::sync::OnceLock<TitleDllLoader> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();

/// Set once, by whoever mapped the title (it knows the folders and the
/// resolver); later calls are ignored.
pub fn set_title_dll_loader(loader: TitleDllLoader) {
    let _ = TITLE_DLL_LOADER.set(loader);
}

pub fn load_title_dll(file: &str) -> Result<Option<usize>, String> {
    TITLE_DLL_LOADER.get().map_or(Ok(None), |load| load(file))
}

/// What the title's manifest (`MicrosoftGame.config` beside its executable)
/// says about it, and where its persistent local storage lives.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Title {
    pub id: u32,
    /// The store's product id (empty if the manifest has none).
    pub store_id: String,
    /// Persistent local storage: our folder for it and the title's quota.
    /// Game saves live beside it ([`Title::saves`]).
    pub storage: PathBuf,
    pub storage_bytes: u64,
}

impl Title {
    /// Id, store id and storage quota from the manifest (zero or empty
    /// where it has none); the storage folder is left for the caller.
    pub fn from_manifest(text: &str) -> Title {
        let elements = elements(text);
        let get = |path: &str| {
            elements
                .iter()
                .find(|(p, _)| p == path)
                .map(|(_, text)| text.as_str())
        };
        let id = get("Game/TitleId").and_then(|v| u32::from_str_radix(v, 16).ok());
        let storage_mb = get("Game/PersistentLocalStorage/SizeMB").and_then(|v| v.parse().ok());
        Title {
            id: id.unwrap_or(0),
            store_id: get("Game/StoreId").unwrap_or_default().to_owned(),
            storage: PathBuf::new(),
            storage_bytes: storage_mb.unwrap_or(0) << 20,
        }
    }

    /// Where game saves live: next to persistent local storage, under the
    /// data directory, never the cache.
    pub fn saves(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.storage.with_file_name("saves")
    }
}

/// Each element of an XML text as its path from the root (`Game/TitleId`)
/// and its trimmed text up to the first child, the predefined entities
/// decoded; comments, CDATA sections, declarations and attributes are
/// skipped.
fn elements(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut path: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
    let mut rest = text;
    while let Some(open) = rest.find('<') {
        rest = &rest[open..];
        let end = if rest.starts_with("<!--") {
            rest.find("-->").map(|e| e + 3)
        } else if rest.starts_with("<![CDATA[") {
            rest.find("]]>").map(|e| e + 3)
        } else {
            rest.find('>').map(|e| e + 1)
        };
        let Some(end) = end else { break };
        let tag = &rest[1..end - 1];
        rest = &rest[end..];
        if tag.starts_with(['!', '?']) {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(name) = tag.strip_prefix('/') {
            if let Some(at) = path.iter().rposition(|n| *n == name.trim()) {
                path.truncate(at);
            }
            continue;
        }
        let closed = tag.ends_with('/');
        let name = tag
            .trim_end_matches('/')
            .split_whitespace()
            .next()
            .unwrap_or("");
        path.push(name);
        let body = rest[..rest.find('<').unwrap_or(rest.len())].trim();
        let body = [("&lt;", "<"), ("&gt;", ">"), ("&quot;", "\""), ("&apos;", "'"), ("&amp;", "&")]
            .iter()
            .fold(body.to_owned(), |b, (entity, c)| b.replace(entity, c));
        out.push((path.join("/"), body));
        if closed {
            path.pop();
        }
    }
    out
}

static TITLE: Mutex<Option<Title>> = Mutex::new(None);

pub fn set_title(title: Title) {
    *TITLE.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = Some(title);
}

/// The running title; the default (id 0, no storage) until set.
pub fn title() -> Title {
    TITLE
        .lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
        .clone()
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Gives the process the console's millisecond timers. Titles pace
/// themselves with short waits (the title's audio mixer sleeps
/// about 4 ms per 5.3 ms block) and cannot tune the timer on the console;
/// a desktop process waits in 15.6 ms ticks unless it asks for finer ones,
/// and Windows 11 drops that request while the window is hidden unless the
/// process opts out. Process-wide, for the whole run.
#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn use_console_timers() {
    use windows_sys::Win32::Media::timeBeginPeriod;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
        GetCurrentProcess, PROCESS_POWER_THROTTLING_CURRENT_VERSION, PROCESS_POWER_THROTTLING_EXECUTION_SPEED,
        PROCESS_POWER_THROTTLING_IGNORE_TIMER_RESOLUTION, PROCESS_POWER_THROTTLING_STATE,
        ProcessPowerThrottling, SetProcessInformation,
    };
    // Also: the system does not run this process at reduced speed (its
    // "efficiency mode": lower clock, the slow cores of a hybrid processor)
    // when its window is not the one in front, as while its owner works in
    // another window or streams. The console has eight cores alike and no
    // such mode. `VICTORY_EFFICIENCY_MODE=1` leaves the system its choice.
    let execution = if std::env::var_os("VICTORY_EFFICIENCY_MODE").is_some_and(|v| v == "1") {
        0
    } else {
        PROCESS_POWER_THROTTLING_EXECUTION_SPEED
    };
    let keep = PROCESS_POWER_THROTTLING_STATE {
        Version: PROCESS_POWER_THROTTLING_CURRENT_VERSION,
        ControlMask: PROCESS_POWER_THROTTLING_IGNORE_TIMER_RESOLUTION | execution,
        StateMask: 0,
    };
    // SAFETY: plain process settings; `keep` outlives the call.
    unsafe {
        SetProcessInformation(
            GetCurrentProcess(),
            ProcessPowerThrottling,
            (&raw const keep).cast(),
            size_of_val(&keep) as u32,
        );
        timeBeginPeriod(1);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn reads_title_id_store_id_and_storage_quota() {
        let text = "\u{feff}<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>\n<Game configVersion=\"1\">\
                    <!-- <TitleId>00000000</TitleId> -->\
                    <Identity Name=\"x\"/>\n  <TitleId>639AA8DD</TitleId>\n\
                    <![CDATA[ <TitleId>1</TitleId> ]]>                    <StoreId>9&amp;C</StoreId><Other><SizeMB>7</SizeMB></Other>\
                    <PersistentLocalStorage>\n  <SizeMB>1024</SizeMB> <!-- c -->\n\
                    </PersistentLocalStorage></Game>";
        let t = Title::from_manifest(text);
        assert_eq!((t.id, t.storage_bytes), (0x639A_A8DD, 1024 << 20));
        assert_eq!(t.store_id, "9&C");
        assert_eq!(Title::from_manifest("").storage_bytes, 0);
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-hle/tests/no_dll_planting.rs`:

```rs
//! Host pass-through must only load DLLs from System32, never from the
//! current folder (e.g. a title's folder shipping its own `msvcp140_*.dll`).
#![cfg(windows)]

use victory_hle::{HleResolver, HostPolicy};
use victory_pe::ImportSymbol;

#[test]
fn ignores_dlls_in_current_folder() {
    let name = "msvcp140_victorytest.dll";
    assert!(
        HostPolicy::default().allows(name),
        "test needs an allow-listed name"
    );
    assert!(HostPolicy::default().allows("vcruntime140_1.dll"));

    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    // Any loadable DLL will do.
    std::fs::copy(r"C:\Windows\System32\version.dll", dir.path().join(name)).unwrap();
    std::env::set_current_dir(dir.path()).unwrap();

    let symbol = ImportSymbol::Name {
        hint: 0,
        name: "GetFileVersionInfoSizeW".into(),
    };
    let found = HleResolver::default().classify(name, &symbol);
    std::env::set_current_dir(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(found, None, "DLL was loaded from the current folder");
}
```

`crates/victory-loader/src/console_insn.rs`:

```rs
//! Instructions the console's CPU (Zen 2) has and an Intel PC's lacks, emulated: the title's
//! code raises STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION on them (the title zeroes memory with a `clzero` loop at
//! its first frames), and the vectored handler steps over them here.
//!
//! Ported from XCL (github.com/ivall/xcl, GPL-2.0-only): `insn.rs` (decoder, as
//! `console_insn_decode.rs`, unchanged) and `eh.rs` `emulate_console_only`.

#[path = "console_insn_decode.rs"]
mod decode;

use decode::ConsoleOnly;
use std::cell::Cell;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering::Relaxed};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::CONTEXT;

const CONTINUE_EXECUTION: i32 = -1;

/// Whether what Windows said about memory is remembered per thread (the regions it found
/// writable, the code bytes it found readable) and not asked again at every emulated
/// instruction. A query walks the pages of the region it answers for: asked from outside, it
/// took 2-9 ms in the title's heaps of 0.6-2.2 GB and 89 ms in its 6.2 GB page pool (run 30),
/// and the title zeroes blocks of them with `clzero` loops all through a frame: six of its
/// threads spent 25-78 % of their time inside that query (runs 29 and 30), about 27 s of
/// processor time in Windows per 9 s frame. On by default; `VICTORY_CLZERO_ASK=1` asks every
/// time, as before.
fn remembers() -> bool {
    static ON: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_CLZERO_ASK").is_none_or(|v| v != "1"))
}

/// Answers a remembered region gives before Windows is asked about it again: one freed or
/// protected meanwhile is forgotten then.
const ANSWERS: u32 = 4096;

thread_local! {
    /// The regions Windows last said are committed and writable (start, end), newest first,
    /// and the answers they gave since they were emptied.
    static WRITABLE: Cell<([(usize, usize); 4], u32)> = const { Cell::new(([(0, 0); 4], 0)) };
    /// Faulting addresses and the code bytes found readable there, newest first.
    static CODE: Cell<[(usize, usize); 8]> = const { Cell::new([(0, 0); 8]) };
}

/// Instructions emulated, the times Windows was asked about memory for them, and the bytes
/// `clzero` loops zeroed, since the start.
static EMULATED: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
static ASKED: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
static ZEROED: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);

/// Exceptions taken by kind since the last line: a lone `clzero`, the 12-byte loop, the
/// 15-byte loop taken whole, `monitorx`, `mwaitx`, everything else; and the 64-byte lines the
/// 15-byte loops zeroed (each was an exception of its own before they were taken whole).
static KINDS: [AtomicU64; 7] = [const { AtomicU64::new(0) }; 7];
const K_CLZERO: usize = 0;
const K_LOOP12: usize = 1;
const K_LOOP15: usize = 2;
const K_MONITORX: usize = 3;
const K_MWAITX: usize = 4;
const K_OTHER: usize = 5;
const K_LOOP15_LINES: usize = 6;

/// Waits the title made with `monitorx` / `mwaitx` (it waits for a fence that way, reading
/// the fence's value in memory: its +0x4fb0ad0) that have ended since the last line: how
/// many, their microseconds, and both again for those of 1 ms and more, 5 ms and more,
/// 20 ms and more.
static WAITS: [AtomicU64; 8] = [const { AtomicU64::new(0) }; 8];
/// Waits said in the log one by one.
static WAITS_SAID: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
/// When the last line was written, in milliseconds of [`clock_us`].
static LINE_AT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);

thread_local! {
    /// The address and the value this thread last armed a monitor for (`monitorx`: rax, and
    /// the title's wanted value in rsi).
    static MONITOR: Cell<(usize, u64)> = const { Cell::new((0, 0)) };
    /// This thread's wait under way: when it began and when its last `mwaitx` was, in
    /// microseconds, what it waits for, and its `mwaitx` count.
    static WAIT: Cell<(u64, u64, usize, u64, u32)> = const { Cell::new((0, 0, 0, 0, 0)) };
}

/// Microseconds on the performance counter.
fn clock_us() -> u64 {
    static PER_SECOND: std::sync::OnceLock<i64> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    let per_second = *PER_SECOND.get_or_init(|| {
        let mut f = 0i64;
        // SAFETY: a valid out pointer.
        unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Performance::QueryPerformanceFrequency(&mut f) };
        f.max(1)
    });
    let mut now = 0i64;
    // SAFETY: a valid out pointer.
    unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Performance::QueryPerformanceCounter(&mut now) };
    (now as u128 * 1_000_000 / per_second as u128) as u64
}

/// Whether events are said one by one now: four seconds of every two minutes of the wall
/// clock, the same seconds in which the fence meter of the graphics side says its own
/// (`victory_gpu::fence::pace`), so that the two can be laid side by side.
fn detail_now() -> bool {
    std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).is_ok_and(|d| d.as_secs() % 120 < 4)
}

/// Whether the 15-byte `clzero` loop is taken whole (`VICTORY_CLZERO_LOOP15=0`: line by
/// line, as before).
fn loop15() -> bool {
    static ON: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_CLZERO_LOOP15").is_none_or(|v| v != "0"))
}

/// A wait of this thread has ended: counted, and said if it is one to say.
fn wait_ended(begin: u64, last: u64, address: usize, wanted: u64, spins: u32) {
    let us = last.saturating_sub(begin);
    for (i, least) in [0u64, 1_000, 5_000, 20_000].into_iter().enumerate() {
        if us >= least {
            WAITS[2 * i].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
            WAITS[2 * i + 1].fetch_add(us, Relaxed);
        }
    }
    if us >= 500 && (detail_now() || WAITS_SAID.fetch_add(1, Relaxed) < 40) {
        // SAFETY: no preconditions.
        let thread = unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentThreadId() };
        tracing::info!(
            "mwait: thread {thread} waited {:.1} ms for the value at {address:#x} to reach {wanted} ({spins} mwaitx)",
            us as f64 / 1e3
        );
    }
}

/// A `mwaitx` of this thread: part of the wait under way, or the first of a new one.
fn wait_step() {
    let now = clock_us();
    let (address, wanted) = MONITOR.with(Cell::get);
    let (begin, last, was_at, was_for, spins) = WAIT.with(Cell::get);
    if begin != 0 && was_at == address && was_for == wanted && now.saturating_sub(last) < 2_000 {
        WAIT.with(|w| w.set((begin, now, address, wanted, spins + 1)));
        return;
    }
    if begin != 0 {
        wait_ended(begin, last, was_at, was_for, spins);
    }
    WAIT.with(|w| w.set((now, now, address, wanted, 1)));
}

/// A line every five seconds: exceptions a second by kind, and the waits that ended.
fn line() {
    let now = clock_us() / 1000;
    let last = LINE_AT.load(Relaxed);
    if now < last + 5_000 || LINE_AT.compare_exchange(last, now, Relaxed, Relaxed).is_err() {
        return;
    }
    if last == 0 {
        return;
    }
    let seconds = (now - last) as f64 / 1e3;
    let k: Vec<f64> = KINDS.iter().map(|k| k.swap(0, Relaxed) as f64 / seconds).collect();
    let w: Vec<f64> = WAITS.iter().map(|w| w.swap(0, Relaxed) as f64).collect();
    tracing::info!(
        "console CPU instructions, exceptions a second: clzero alone {:.0}, its 12-byte loop {:.0}, its 15-byte loop taken whole {:.0} ({:.0} lines a second, each an exception \
         before; VICTORY_CLZERO_LOOP15=0: again), monitorx {:.0}, mwaitx {:.0}, others {:.0} | mwaitx waits ended a second: {:.0}, {:.1} ms of thread time a second; of 1 ms and \
         more {:.1} ({:.1} ms), of 5 ms and more {:.1} ({:.1} ms), of 20 ms and more {:.1} ({:.1} ms)",
        k[K_CLZERO],
        k[K_LOOP12],
        k[K_LOOP15],
        k[K_LOOP15_LINES],
        k[K_MONITORX],
        k[K_MWAITX],
        k[K_OTHER],
        w[0] / seconds,
        w[1] / seconds / 1e3,
        w[2] / seconds,
        w[3] / seconds / 1e3,
        w[4] / seconds,
        w[5] / seconds / 1e3,
        w[6] / seconds,
        w[7] / seconds / 1e3,
    );
}

fn readable(va: usize, bytes: usize) -> bool {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{MEM_COMMIT, MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION, PAGE_GUARD, PAGE_NOACCESS, VirtualQuery};
    // SAFETY: plain data filled in by the query.
    let mut m: MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    // SAFETY: a valid out pointer of the right size.
    let found = unsafe { VirtualQuery(va as *const _, &mut m, size_of_val(&m)) } != 0;
    ASKED.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
    found && m.State == MEM_COMMIT && m.Protect & (PAGE_NOACCESS | PAGE_GUARD) == 0 && m.BaseAddress as usize + m.RegionSize >= va + bytes
}

fn writable(va: usize, bytes: usize) -> bool {
    writable_to(va, va + bytes) == Some(va + bytes)
}

/// Where the committed, writable memory that `va` lies in ends, at most `end`; None if `va`
/// is not in such memory. A region found is remembered ([`remembers`]).
/// shortcut: a remembered region that was freed or protected since is written all the same
/// for up to [`ANSWERS`] answers: the write then faults inside the handler, which the guard
/// on view memory opens as it does any write, and which is a crash otherwise (as the
/// unchecked single-line emulation behind this one already is).
fn writable_to(va: usize, end: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{MEM_COMMIT, MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, PAGE_READWRITE, VirtualQuery};
    let remember = remembers();
    if remember {
        let (regions, answers) = WRITABLE.with(Cell::get);
        if let Some(&(_, to)) = regions.iter().find(|&&(from, to)| from <= va && va < to) {
            let next = if answers >= ANSWERS { ([(0, 0); 4], 0) } else { (regions, answers + 1) };
            WRITABLE.with(|w| w.set(next));
            return Some(to.min(end));
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: plain data filled in by the query.
    let mut m: MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    // SAFETY: a valid out pointer of the right size.
    let found = unsafe { VirtualQuery(va as *const _, &mut m, size_of_val(&m)) } != 0;
    ASKED.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
    if !found || m.State != MEM_COMMIT || m.Protect & (PAGE_READWRITE | PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE) == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let (from, to) = (m.BaseAddress as usize, m.BaseAddress as usize + m.RegionSize);
    if remember {
        WRITABLE.with(|w| {
            let (mut regions, answers) = w.get();
            regions.rotate_right(1);
            regions[0] = (from, to);
            w.set((regions, answers));
        });
    }
    Some(to.min(end))
}

/// The register `r` of `ctx` (CONTEXT order: rax, rcx, rdx, rbx, rsp, rbp, rsi, rdi, r8..r15).
fn register(ctx: &mut CONTEXT, r: u8) -> &mut u64 {
    match r & 15 {
        0 => &mut ctx.Rax,
        1 => &mut ctx.Rcx,
        2 => &mut ctx.Rdx,
        3 => &mut ctx.Rbx,
        4 => &mut ctx.Rsp,
        5 => &mut ctx.Rbp,
        6 => &mut ctx.Rsi,
        7 => &mut ctx.Rdi,
        8 => &mut ctx.R8,
        9 => &mut ctx.R9,
        10 => &mut ctx.R10,
        11 => &mut ctx.R11,
        12 => &mut ctx.R12,
        13 => &mut ctx.R13,
        14 => &mut ctx.R14,
        _ => &mut ctx.R15,
    }
}

/// Where the lines of the loop `mov rax, ptr; add ptr, 0x40; clzero; cmp ptr, end; jb` end,
/// from the state the loop has at its `clzero`: the line at `rax` is zeroed now, and one
/// more at `ptr` for every pass the `cmp` sends back. None if this is not the plain case
/// the loop makes (the line at `rax` on a 64-byte boundary, `ptr` the next line, under
/// 2 GiB in all): then every line is taken alone, as the instruction itself does it.
fn loop15_end(rax: usize, ptr: usize, end: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    if rax & 63 != 0 || ptr != rax.wrapping_add(64) || ptr < rax {
        return None;
    }
    let more = if ptr < end { (end - ptr).div_ceil(64) } else { 0 };
    let last = ptr.checked_add(more.checked_mul(64)?)?;
    (last - rax < 2 << 30).then_some(last)
}

/// The `clzero` at `rip` in the loop `mov rax, ptr; add ptr, 0x40; clzero; cmp ptr, end; jb`,
/// with all the lines the loop would still zero: `Some(true)` when they are zeroed and the
/// registers stand as the loop leaves them at its last `clzero` (the caller steps over the
/// instruction; the title's own `cmp` and `jb` then leave the loop), `Some(false)` when the
/// first line is not writable (the real instruction faults there too), and when only a
/// first part was writable the registers stand at the line after it, where the instruction
/// runs again. None if it is not that loop: the lone instruction is emulated.
///
/// # Safety
/// `rip` is the faulting instruction of `ctx`, whose bytes were read.
unsafe fn clzero_loop15(ctx: &mut CONTEXT, rip: usize, ptr_reg: u8, end_reg: u8) -> Option<bool> {
    // The seven bytes in front of it: in the same page as the instruction, which ran.
    if rip & 0xFFF < 7 && !readable(rip - 7, 7) {
        return None;
    }
    // SAFETY: readable, as checked or as the instruction's own page.
    let before = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts((rip - 7) as *const u8, 7) };
    if !decode::loop15_head(before, ptr_reg) || end_reg == 0 || end_reg == ptr_reg {
        return None;
    }
    let rax = ctx.Rax as usize;
    let ptr = *register(ctx, ptr_reg) as usize;
    let end = *register(ctx, end_reg) as usize;
    let last = loop15_end(rax, ptr, end)?;
    // Region by region, as the 12-byte loop: a block may lie across several views.
    let mut at = rax;
    while at < last {
        let Some(to) = writable_to(at, last) else { break };
        // A region ends on a page boundary, so `to` is on a line boundary as `at` is.
        // SAFETY: committed and writable from `at` to `to`.
        unsafe { std::ptr::write_bytes(at as *mut u8, 0, to - at) };
        at = to;
    }
    if at == rax {
        return Some(false);
    }
    ZEROED.fetch_add((at - rax) as u64, Relaxed);
    KINDS[K_LOOP15_LINES].fetch_add(((at - rax) / 64) as u64, Relaxed);
    if at < last {
        // What follows is not writable: the loop stands at that line's `clzero` now, where
        // the real one faults too. The instruction runs again (the caller must not step).
        ctx.Rax = at as u64;
        *register(ctx, ptr_reg) = (at + 64) as u64;
        ctx.Rip = (rip as u64).wrapping_sub(3);
        return Some(true);
    }
    ctx.Rax = (last - 64) as u64;
    *register(ctx, ptr_reg) = last as u64;
    Some(true)
}

/// An illegal instruction at `ctx.Rip`: a console-only one is emulated and stepped over
/// (`CONTINUE_EXECUTION`); anything else returns 0 (the crash report and the title's handlers
/// see it).
///
/// # Safety
/// `ctx` is the faulting thread's context, from the exception being dispatched.
pub(crate) unsafe fn emulate(ctx: &mut CONTEXT) -> i32 {
    let rip = ctx.Rip as usize;
    // The same few instructions fault again and again: their bytes are asked about once.
    let known = if remembers() { CODE.with(Cell::get) } else { [(0, 0); 8] };
    let n = match known.iter().find(|&&(at, n)| at == rip && n > 0) {
        Some(&(_, n)) => n,
        None => {
            if !readable(rip, 1) {
                return 0;
            }
            let n = (1..=16).rev().find(|&n| readable(rip, n)).unwrap_or(0);
            if remembers() {
                let mut known = known;
                known.rotate_right(1);
                known[0] = (rip, n);
                CODE.with(|c| c.set(known));
            }
            n
        }
    };
    // SAFETY: `n` bytes at `rip` are readable.
    let code = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(rip as *const u8, n) };
    let Some((what, len)) = decode::decode(code) else { return 0 };
    static SEEN: std::sync::Mutex<Vec<std::mem::Discriminant<ConsoleOnly>>> = std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new());
    if let Ok(mut seen) = SEEN.lock()
        && !seen.contains(&std::mem::discriminant(&what))
    {
        seen.push(std::mem::discriminant(&what));
        if what != ConsoleOnly::Ud2 {
            tracing::warn!(instruction = ?what, at = format_args!("{rip:#x}"), "a console CPU instruction this CPU lacks: emulated (logged once)");
        }
    }
    match what {
        ConsoleOnly::Ud2 => return 0,
        ConsoleOnly::Clwb => {
            // nothing to write back on the PC: patched to NOPs, no exception next time
            use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, VirtualProtect};
            let mut old = 0u32;
            // SAFETY: the instruction's own bytes, made writable for the patch and restored.
            unsafe {
                if VirtualProtect(rip as *const _, len, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, &mut old) != 0 {
                    std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(rip as *mut u8, len).fill(0x90);
                    VirtualProtect(rip as *const _, len, old, &mut old);
                }
            }
        }
        ConsoleOnly::Monitorx => {
            KINDS[K_MONITORX].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
            MONITOR.with(|m| m.set((ctx.Rax as usize, ctx.Rsi)));
        }
        ConsoleOnly::Mwaitx => {
            KINDS[K_MWAITX].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
            wait_step();
            std::hint::spin_loop()
        }
        ConsoleOnly::Clzero | ConsoleOnly::ClzeroStep { .. } => {
            // The loop `mov rax, ptr; add ptr, 0x40; clzero; cmp ptr, end; jb` (the title's
            // +0x4e8ab4c and three more like it zero 896 to 7,040 bytes each, a line an
            // exception) is taken whole from the line it stands at.
            if let ConsoleOnly::ClzeroStep { ptr_reg, end_reg } = what
                && loop15()
                && let Some(done) = unsafe { clzero_loop15(ctx, rip, ptr_reg, end_reg) }
            {
                if !done {
                    return 0;
                }
                ctx.Rip += len as u64;
                EMULATED.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
                KINDS[K_LOOP15].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
                line();
                return CONTINUE_EXECUTION;
            }
            KINDS[K_CLZERO].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
            // with an address-size prefix (0x67) the line is at EAX, zero-extended
            let a32 = code[..len - 3].contains(&0x67);
            let line = (if a32 { ctx.Rax & 0xFFFF_FFFF } else { ctx.Rax } as usize) & !63;
            if !writable(line, 64) {
                return 0; // the real instruction faults there too
            }
            // SAFETY: the 64-byte line is committed and writable.
            unsafe { std::ptr::write_bytes(line as *mut u8, 0, 64) };
        }
        ConsoleOnly::ClzeroLoop { end_reg } => {
            KINDS[K_LOOP12].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
            // the whole `clzero; add rax,40h; cmp rax,end; jb` loop at once
            let regs: [u64; 16] = [
                ctx.Rax, ctx.Rcx, ctx.Rdx, ctx.Rbx, ctx.Rsp, ctx.Rbp, ctx.Rsi, ctx.Rdi, ctx.R8, ctx.R9, ctx.R10, ctx.R11, ctx.R12, ctx.R13, ctx.R14, ctx.R15,
            ];
            let end = regs[end_reg as usize & 15] as usize;
            let start = ctx.Rax as usize;
            if end > start && end - start < 2 << 30 {
                // Region by region: a block may lie across several (the title's pages are
                // mapped one view each), and one answer for all of it was a refusal, after
                // which every 64-byte line took an exception of its own.
                let mut at = start;
                while at < end {
                    let Some(to) = writable_to(at, end) else { break };
                    // SAFETY: committed and writable from `at` to `to`.
                    unsafe { std::ptr::write_bytes(at as *mut u8, 0, to - at) };
                    at = to;
                }
                if at == start {
                    return 0;
                }
                ZEROED.fetch_add((at - start) as u64, Relaxed);
                if at < end {
                    // What follows is not writable: the loop goes on there (the same
                    // instruction again), where the real one faults too.
                    ctx.Rax = at as u64;
                    return CONTINUE_EXECUTION;
                }
            }
            ctx.Rax = end as u64;
        }
        ConsoleOnly::Rdpru => {
            let mut v = 0i64;
            // SAFETY: a valid out pointer.
            unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Performance::QueryPerformanceCounter(&mut v) };
            let v = if ctx.Rcx as u32 <= 1 { v as u64 } else { 0 };
            ctx.Rax = v & 0xFFFF_FFFF;
            ctx.Rdx = v >> 32;
        }
        ConsoleOnly::Rdpid(r) => {
            // SAFETY: no preconditions.
            let cpu = unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcessorNumber() } as u64;
            let regs: [&mut u64; 16] = [
                &mut ctx.Rax, &mut ctx.Rcx, &mut ctx.Rdx, &mut ctx.Rbx, &mut ctx.Rsp, &mut ctx.Rbp, &mut ctx.Rsi, &mut ctx.Rdi, &mut ctx.R8, &mut ctx.R9, &mut ctx.R10, &mut ctx.R11, &mut ctx.R12, &mut ctx.R13,
                &mut ctx.R14, &mut ctx.R15,
            ];
            *regs[r as usize & 15] = cpu;
        }
        // the low quadword changes; the high one is zeroed, as a Zen 5 does
        ConsoleOnly::Extrq { dst, src, len, idx } => {
            // SAFETY: the context's XMM registers (CONTEXT_FLOATING_POINT is captured for exceptions).
            let x = unsafe { &mut ctx.Anonymous.FltSave.XmmRegisters };
            let (len, idx) = match src {
                Some(s) => {
                    let c = x[s as usize & 15].Low;
                    (c as u8, (c >> 8) as u8)
                }
                None => (len, idx),
            };
            let d = &mut x[dst as usize & 15];
            d.Low = decode::extrq(d.Low, len, idx);
            d.High = 0;
        }
        ConsoleOnly::Insertq { dst, src, reg, len, idx } => {
            // SAFETY: as above.
            let x = unsafe { &mut ctx.Anonymous.FltSave.XmmRegisters };
            let s = x[src as usize & 15];
            let (len, idx) = if reg { (s.High as u8, (s.High >> 8) as u8) } else { (len, idx) };
            let d = &mut x[dst as usize & 15];
            d.Low = decode::insertq(d.Low, s.Low, len, idx);
            d.High = 0;
        }
    }
    if !matches!(
        what,
        ConsoleOnly::Monitorx | ConsoleOnly::Mwaitx | ConsoleOnly::Clzero | ConsoleOnly::ClzeroStep { .. } | ConsoleOnly::ClzeroLoop { .. }
    ) {
        KINDS[K_OTHER].fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
    }
    line();
    ctx.Rip += len as u64;
    // How often this runs at all (each one is an exception: a trip into Windows and back).
    let emulated = EMULATED.fetch_add(1, Relaxed) + 1;
    if emulated >= 1 << 16 && emulated.is_power_of_two() {
        tracing::info!(
            emulated,
            asked = ASKED.load(Relaxed),
            zeroed_mb = ZEROED.load(Relaxed) >> 20,
            "console CPU instructions emulated so far, the times Windows was asked about memory for them, and what clzero loops zeroed"
        );
    }
    CONTINUE_EXECUTION
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// What the title's loop leaves, run line by line as the processor would: the lines it
    /// zeroed and the registers (rax, ptr) at the end, from the state at its first `clzero`.
    fn by_hand(mut rax: usize, mut ptr: usize, end: usize) -> (Vec<usize>, usize, usize) {
        let mut lines = vec![rax & !63];
        while ptr < end {
            rax = ptr;
            ptr += 0x40;
            lines.push(rax & !63);
        }
        (lines, rax, ptr)
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_15_byte_loop_ends_where_the_processor_would_end_it() {
        for (rax, len) in [(0x1000usize, 7040usize), (0x1000, 3264), (0x1000, 3776), (0x1000, 896), (0x4000, 64), (0x4000, 65), (0x4000, 100), (0x4000, 1), (0x4000, 0), (0x8000, 128)] {
            let (ptr, end) = (rax + 64, rax + len);
            let (lines, last_rax, last_ptr) = by_hand(rax, ptr, end);
            let last = loop15_end(rax, ptr, end).expect("the plain case");
            assert_eq!(last, last_ptr, "rax {rax:#x} len {len}");
            assert_eq!(last - 64, last_rax, "rax {rax:#x} len {len}");
            assert_eq!((last - rax) / 64, lines.len(), "rax {rax:#x} len {len}");
            assert_eq!(*lines.last().unwrap(), last - 64);
        }
        // an end before the pointer: the line at rax alone
        assert_eq!(loop15_end(0x1000, 0x1040, 0x800), Some(0x1040));
        // not the plain case: a line not on a boundary, a pointer that is not the next line
        assert_eq!(loop15_end(0x1008, 0x1048, 0x2000), None);
        assert_eq!(loop15_end(0x1000, 0x1080, 0x2000), None);
        assert_eq!(loop15_end(0x1000, 0x1040, 0x1000 + (3 << 30)), None, "over 2 GiB");
    }

    /// The loop as the title has it at +0x4e8ab4c, for the given registers.
    fn code(ptr_reg: u8, end_reg: u8) -> Vec<u8> {
        let (ph, pl, eh, el) = (ptr_reg >> 3, ptr_reg & 7, end_reg >> 3, end_reg & 7);
        vec![
            0x48 | ph << 2, 0x89, 0xC0 | pl << 3, // mov rax, ptr
            0x48 | ph, 0x83, 0xC0 | pl, 0x40, // add ptr, 0x40
            0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC, // clzero
            0x48 | eh << 2 | ph, 0x39, 0xC0 | el << 3 | pl, // cmp ptr, end
            0x72, 0xF1, // jb -15
            0x90,
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_15_byte_loop_is_zeroed_whole_and_leaves_the_loop_s_registers() {
        for (ptr_reg, end_reg, len) in [(10u8, 11u8, 7040usize), (9, 10, 3264), (8, 9, 3776), (2, 8, 896), (10, 11, 64), (10, 11, 100)] {
            let code = code(ptr_reg, end_reg);
            // a block of 0xAA with room on both sides, its start on a line boundary
            let mut block = vec![0xAAu8; 16384];
            let base = (block.as_mut_ptr() as usize + 4096 + 63) & !63;
            // SAFETY: plain data.
            let mut ctx: CONTEXT = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
            ctx.Rip = code.as_ptr() as u64 + 7;
            ctx.Rax = base as u64;
            *register(&mut ctx, ptr_reg) = base as u64 + 64;
            *register(&mut ctx, end_reg) = (base + len) as u64;
            // SAFETY: the context points at the code above.
            assert_eq!(unsafe { emulate(&mut ctx) }, CONTINUE_EXECUTION);
            let (lines, last_rax, last_ptr) = by_hand(base, base + 64, base + len);
            assert_eq!(ctx.Rip, code.as_ptr() as u64 + 10, "at the loop's own cmp");
            assert_eq!(ctx.Rax as usize, last_rax);
            assert_eq!(*register(&mut ctx, ptr_reg) as usize, last_ptr);
            assert_eq!(*register(&mut ctx, end_reg) as usize, base + len, "the end is left alone");
            let zeroed = lines.len() * 64;
            let at = base - block.as_ptr() as usize;
            assert!(block[at..at + zeroed].iter().all(|&b| b == 0), "{zeroed} bytes zeroed");
            assert!(block[..at].iter().all(|&b| b == 0xAA), "nothing before the block");
            assert!(block[at + zeroed..].iter().all(|&b| b == 0xAA), "nothing after its last line");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_clzero_that_only_looks_like_the_loop_is_one_line() {
        // the same bytes behind it, another head in front (add ptr, 0x80): one line, one step
        let mut code = code(10, 11);
        code[6] = 0x80;
        let mut block = vec![0xAAu8; 8192];
        let base = (block.as_mut_ptr() as usize + 2048 + 63) & !63;
        // SAFETY: plain data.
        let mut ctx: CONTEXT = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        ctx.Rip = code.as_ptr() as u64 + 7;
        ctx.Rax = base as u64;
        ctx.R10 = base as u64 + 64;
        ctx.R11 = base as u64 + 640;
        // SAFETY: the context points at the code above.
        assert_eq!(unsafe { emulate(&mut ctx) }, CONTINUE_EXECUTION);
        assert_eq!(ctx.Rip, code.as_ptr() as u64 + 10);
        assert_eq!((ctx.Rax, ctx.R10), (base as u64, base as u64 + 64), "registers untouched");
        let at = base - block.as_ptr() as usize;
        assert!(block[at..at + 64].iter().all(|&b| b == 0));
        assert!(block[at + 64..].iter().all(|&b| b == 0xAA), "one line only");
    }
}
```
