`crates/victory-loader/src/console_insn_decode.rs`:

```rs
//! Instructions the console's CPU (Zen 2) has and a PC's may lack – a title raises
//! STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION on them on an Intel CPU before Ice Lake / Alder Lake (CLWB,
//! SHA) or on any Intel CPU (CLZERO, RDPRU, MONITORX / MWAITX and SSE4a's EXTRQ / INSERTQ,
//! which are AMD's). The exception handler (`eh`) emulates the ones decoded here and steps over
//! them.

/// A console-only instruction at the faulting address.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ConsoleOnly {
    /// `clwb m8`: write a cache line back – nothing to do, the PC's memory is coherent
    Clwb,
    /// `clzero`: zero the 64-byte cache line at rAX
    Clzero,
    /// `clzero` loop: `clzero; add rax, 0x40; cmp rax, <reg>; jb -12` – zero `[rax..reg)`
    ClzeroLoop { end_reg: u8 },
    /// `clzero` in the loop `mov rax, <ptr>; add <ptr>, 0x40; clzero; cmp <ptr>, <end>; jb -15`
    /// (the seven bytes before it are the caller's to check, [`loop15_head`]): the length is
    /// the `clzero`'s own
    ClzeroStep { ptr_reg: u8, end_reg: u8 },
    /// `rdpru`: ecx = 0 MPERF / 1 APERF → edx:eax (a counter)
    Rdpru,
    /// `monitorx` / `mwaitx`: a wait the emulation skips
    Monitorx,
    Mwaitx,
    /// `rdpid r64`: TSC_AUX (the processor number) into the register (CONTEXT order: rax, rcx,
    /// rdx, rbx, rsp, rbp, rsi, rdi, r8..r15)
    Rdpid(u8),
    /// SSE4a `extrq xmm, imm8 (length), imm8 (index)` / `extrq xmm1, xmm2` (`src` Some: the
    /// length and index in xmm2's bits 5:0 and 13:8): a bit field of the low quadword, moved
    /// down and zero-extended (the high quadword zeroed). Registers are XMM numbers 0..15.
    Extrq { dst: u8, src: Option<u8>, len: u8, idx: u8 },
    /// SSE4a `insertq xmm1, xmm2, imm8 (length), imm8 (index)` / `insertq xmm1, xmm2` (`reg`:
    /// the length and index in xmm2's bits 69:64 and 77:72): the low bits of xmm2 put into a
    /// bit field of xmm1's low quadword.
    Insertq { dst: u8, src: u8, reg: bool, len: u8, idx: u8 },
    /// `ud2`: the title's own trap (not emulated)
    Ud2,
}

/// A field length of SSE4a's six bits: 0 is 64.
fn field_len(len: u8) -> u32 {
    match len & 63 {
        0 => 64,
        n => n as u32,
    }
}

/// EXTRQ on a low quadword: `len` bits from bit `idx`, zero-extended (a field past bit 63 is
/// undefined on the console; here it is what a shift gives).
pub fn extrq(v: u64, len: u8, idx: u8) -> u64 {
    let (len, idx) = (field_len(len), (idx & 63) as u32);
    let field = v.checked_shr(idx).unwrap_or(0);
    if len >= 64 {
        field
    } else {
        field & ((1u64 << len) - 1)
    }
}

/// INSERTQ on a low quadword: the low `len` bits of `src` put at bit `idx` of `dst`.
pub fn insertq(dst: u64, src: u64, len: u8, idx: u8) -> u64 {
    let (len, idx) = (field_len(len), (idx & 63) as u32);
    let ones = if len >= 64 { u64::MAX } else { (1u64 << len) - 1 };
    let mask = ones.checked_shl(idx).unwrap_or(0);
    (dst & !mask) | ((src & ones).checked_shl(idx).unwrap_or(0) & mask)
}

/// The length of a ModRM-encoded operand (ModRM, SIB and displacement) at `b[0]`, None when the
/// bytes run out.
fn modrm_len(b: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    let modrm = *b.first()?;
    let (md, rm) = (modrm >> 6, modrm & 7);
    if md == 3 {
        return Some(1);
    }
    let mut len = 1;
    let mut base = rm;
    if rm == 4 {
        base = *b.get(1)? & 7;
        len += 1;
    }
    len += match md {
        0 if base == 5 => 4, // disp32 (rip-relative, or a SIB without a base)
        0 => 0,
        1 => 1,
        _ => 4,
    };
    (b.len() >= len).then_some(len)
}

/// Whether `before`, the seven bytes in front of a [`ConsoleOnly::ClzeroStep`], are
/// `mov rax, <ptr>; add <ptr>, 0x40` for that pointer register (neither rax nor rsp).
pub fn loop15_head(before: &[u8], ptr_reg: u8) -> bool {
    let (hi, lo) = (ptr_reg >> 3 & 1, ptr_reg & 7);
    ptr_reg != 0
        && ptr_reg != 4
        && before.len() == 7
        // mov rax, ptr: REX.W (+R for r8..r15) 89 /r with rm = rax
        && before[0] == 0x48 | hi << 2
        && before[1] == 0x89
        && before[2] == 0xC0 | lo << 3
        // add ptr, 0x40: REX.W (+B) 83 /0 ib
        && before[3] == 0x48 | hi
        && before[4] == 0x83
        && before[5] == 0xC0 | lo
        && before[6] == 0x40
}

/// The console-only instruction at the start of `code` and its length.
pub fn decode(code: &[u8]) -> Option<(ConsoleOnly, usize)> {
    let mut i = 0;
    // `rep`: the last of F2 / F3, which decides between them (and over 66) for SSE4a
    let (mut p66, mut pf3, mut rep, mut rex) = (false, false, 0u8, 0u8);
    while let Some(&b) = code.get(i) {
        match b {
            0x66 => p66 = true,
            0xF2 => rep = 0xF2,
            0xF3 => {
                pf3 = true;
                rep = 0xF3;
            }
            0x2E | 0x3E | 0x26 | 0x36 | 0x64 | 0x65 | 0x67 => {}
            // REX counts only right before the opcode: one before a legacy prefix is ignored
            0x40..=0x4F => {
                rex = b;
                i += 1;
                continue;
            }
            _ => break,
        }
        rex = 0;
        i += 1;
    }
    if *code.get(i)? != 0x0F {
        return None;
    }
    match (*code.get(i + 1)?, code.get(i + 2).copied()) {
        (0x01, Some(0xFC)) => {
            // clzero (0F 01 FC); add rax, 0x40 (48 83 C0 40); cmp rax, <reg> ([48|4C] 39 modrm); jb -12 (72 F4)
            // (not after an 0x67: that CLZERO is at EAX, and the jb goes back to the 0F, past the
            // prefix – it is stepped alone, the loop is taken from the next one)
            if code.len() >= i + 12
                && !code[..i].contains(&0x67)
                && code[i + 3..i + 7] == [0x48, 0x83, 0xC0, 0x40]
                && (code[i + 7] == 0x48 || code[i + 7] == 0x4C)
                && code[i + 8] == 0x39
                && code[i + 10..i + 12] == [0x72, 0xF4]
            {
                let rex_r = code[i + 7] == 0x4C;
                let modrm = code[i + 9];
                let reg_idx = ((modrm >> 3) & 7) | if rex_r { 8 } else { 0 };
                Some((ConsoleOnly::ClzeroLoop { end_reg: reg_idx }, i + 12))
            } else if i == 0
                && code.len() >= 8
                && code[3] & 0xF8 == 0x48
                && code[3] & 0x02 == 0
                && code[4] == 0x39
                && code[5] >> 6 == 3
                && code[6..8] == [0x72, 0xF1]
            {
                // clzero; cmp <ptr>, <end> (REX.W 39 /r, register form); jb -15
                let (rex, modrm) = (code[3], code[5]);
                let end_reg = ((modrm >> 3) & 7) | (rex & 4) << 1;
                let ptr_reg = (modrm & 7) | (rex & 1) << 3;
                Some((ConsoleOnly::ClzeroStep { ptr_reg, end_reg }, 3))
            } else {
                Some((ConsoleOnly::Clzero, i + 3))
            }
        }
        (0x01, Some(0xFD)) => Some((ConsoleOnly::Rdpru, i + 3)),
        (0x01, Some(0xFA)) => Some((ConsoleOnly::Monitorx, i + 3)),
        (0x01, Some(0xFB)) => Some((ConsoleOnly::Mwaitx, i + 3)),
        (0x0B, _) => Some((ConsoleOnly::Ud2, i + 2)),
        // SSE4a: register operands only (ModRM mod 3); REX.R extends reg, REX.B rm
        // (the last of F2 / F3 decides: F2 INSERTQ, F3 #UD; neither with 66: EXTRQ)
        (0x78 | 0x79, Some(m)) if (rep == 0xF2 || (rep == 0 && p66)) && m >> 6 == 3 => {
            let reg = ((m >> 3) & 7) | (rex & 4) << 1;
            let rm = (m & 7) | (rex & 1) << 3;
            let imm = |k: usize| code.get(i + 3 + k).copied();
            match (code[i + 1], rep == 0xF2) {
                // extrq xmm(rm), imm8, imm8 – the ModRM reg field is /0
                (0x78, false) if (m >> 3) & 7 == 0 => Some((ConsoleOnly::Extrq { dst: rm, src: None, len: imm(0)?, idx: imm(1)? }, i + 5)),
                (0x79, false) => Some((ConsoleOnly::Extrq { dst: reg, src: Some(rm), len: 0, idx: 0 }, i + 3)),
                (0x78, true) => Some((ConsoleOnly::Insertq { dst: reg, src: rm, reg: false, len: imm(0)?, idx: imm(1)? }, i + 5)),
                (0x79, true) => Some((ConsoleOnly::Insertq { dst: reg, src: rm, reg: true, len: 0, idx: 0 }, i + 3)),
                _ => None,
            }
        }
        // 66 0F AE /6 with a memory operand (without 66 it is xsaveopt)
        (0xAE, Some(m)) if p66 && (m >> 3) & 7 == 6 && m >> 6 != 3 => Some((ConsoleOnly::Clwb, i + 2 + modrm_len(&code[i + 2..])?)),
        // F3 0F C7 /7 with a register operand
        (0xC7, Some(m)) if pf3 && (m >> 3) & 7 == 7 && m >> 6 == 3 => Some((ConsoleOnly::Rdpid((m & 7) | (rex & 1) << 3), i + 3)),
        _ => None,
    }
}


#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// EXTRQ / INSERTQ as AMD's manual gives them: a length of 0 is 64.
    #[test]
    fn sse4a_bit_fields() {
        assert_eq!(extrq(0x1234_5678_9ABC_DEF0, 8, 16), 0xBC);
        assert_eq!(extrq(0x1234_5678_9ABC_DEF0, 0, 0), 0x1234_5678_9ABC_DEF0);
        assert_eq!(extrq(0x8000_0000_0000_0000, 1, 63), 1);
        assert_eq!(insertq(0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF, 0xAB, 8, 8), 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_ABFF);
        assert_eq!(insertq(0, 0x1FF, 4, 60), 0xF000_0000_0000_0000);
        assert_eq!(insertq(0x1111, 0xDEAD_BEEF_0000_0000, 0, 0), 0xDEAD_BEEF_0000_0000);
        for (v, len, idx) in [(0x0123_4567_89AB_CDEFu64, 12u8, 20u8), (u64::MAX, 63, 1), (0x55, 3, 0)] {
            assert_eq!(extrq(insertq(0, v, len, idx), len, idx), extrq(v, len, 0));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_the_console_only_instructions() {
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Clzero, 3)));
        // clzero loop against r10 (4C 39 D0 = cmp rax, r10)
        assert_eq!(
            decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC, 0x48, 0x83, 0xC0, 0x40, 0x4C, 0x39, 0xD0, 0x72, 0xF4]),
            Some((ConsoleOnly::ClzeroLoop { end_reg: 10 }, 12))
        );
        // clzero loop against rdx (48 39 D0 = cmp rax, rdx)
        assert_eq!(
            decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC, 0x48, 0x83, 0xC0, 0x40, 0x48, 0x39, 0xD0, 0x72, 0xF4]),
            Some((ConsoleOnly::ClzeroLoop { end_reg: 2 }, 12))
        );
        // the same loop after an address-size prefix: that one CLZERO alone
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x67, 0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC, 0x48, 0x83, 0xC0, 0x40, 0x48, 0x39, 0xD0, 0x72, 0xF4]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Clzero, 4)));
        // the title's other loop, as at its +0x4e8ab4c: mov rax, r10; add r10, 0x40; clzero;
        // cmp r10, r11; jb -15 (and against r9/r10, r8/r9, rdx/r8)
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC, 0x4D, 0x39, 0xDA, 0x72, 0xF1]), Some((ConsoleOnly::ClzeroStep { ptr_reg: 10, end_reg: 11 }, 3)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC, 0x4D, 0x39, 0xD1, 0x72, 0xF1]), Some((ConsoleOnly::ClzeroStep { ptr_reg: 9, end_reg: 10 }, 3)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC, 0x4D, 0x39, 0xC8, 0x72, 0xF1]), Some((ConsoleOnly::ClzeroStep { ptr_reg: 8, end_reg: 9 }, 3)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC, 0x4C, 0x39, 0xC2, 0x72, 0xF1]), Some((ConsoleOnly::ClzeroStep { ptr_reg: 2, end_reg: 8 }, 3)));
        assert!(loop15_head(&[0x4C, 0x89, 0xD0, 0x49, 0x83, 0xC2, 0x40], 10));
        assert!(loop15_head(&[0x4C, 0x89, 0xC8, 0x49, 0x83, 0xC1, 0x40], 9));
        assert!(loop15_head(&[0x4C, 0x89, 0xC0, 0x49, 0x83, 0xC0, 0x40], 8));
        assert!(loop15_head(&[0x48, 0x89, 0xD0, 0x48, 0x83, 0xC2, 0x40], 2));
        assert!(!loop15_head(&[0x4C, 0x89, 0xD0, 0x49, 0x83, 0xC2, 0x40], 9), "another register");
        assert!(!loop15_head(&[0x4C, 0x89, 0xD0, 0x49, 0x83, 0xC2, 0x80], 10), "another step");
        // not that loop: another jump back, a memory operand, a 32-bit compare
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC, 0x4D, 0x39, 0xDA, 0x72, 0xF4]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Clzero, 3)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC, 0x4D, 0x39, 0x1A, 0x72, 0xF1]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Clzero, 3)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC, 0x45, 0x39, 0xDA, 0x72, 0xF1]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Clzero, 3)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFD]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Rdpru, 3)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFA]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Monitorx, 3)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x01, 0xFB]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Mwaitx, 3)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x0B]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Ud2, 2)));
        // clwb [rax]; clwb [rcx+0x40]; clwb [rsp+8]; clwb [rip+disp32]; clwb [r8]
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x66, 0x0F, 0xAE, 0x30]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Clwb, 4)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x66, 0x0F, 0xAE, 0x71, 0x40]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Clwb, 5)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x66, 0x0F, 0xAE, 0x74, 0x24, 0x08]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Clwb, 6)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x66, 0x0F, 0xAE, 0x35, 1, 2, 3, 4]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Clwb, 8)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x66, 0x41, 0x0F, 0xAE, 0x30]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Clwb, 5)));
        // rdpid rax; rdpid r9
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0xF3, 0x0F, 0xC7, 0xF8]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Rdpid(0), 4)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0xF3, 0x41, 0x0F, 0xC7, 0xF9]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Rdpid(9), 5)));
        // not console-only: clflushopt (/7), xsaveopt (no 66), a plain mov, truncated bytes
        // SSE4a, as a retail game has it (#216: insertq xmm0, xmm1 with length / index bytes)
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0xF2, 0x0F, 0x78, 0xC1, 0x08, 0x10]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Insertq { dst: 0, src: 1, reg: false, len: 8, idx: 16 }, 6)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0xF2, 0x45, 0x0F, 0x79, 0xC1]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Insertq { dst: 8, src: 9, reg: true, len: 0, idx: 0 }, 5)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x66, 0x0F, 0x78, 0xC2, 0x04, 0x08]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Extrq { dst: 2, src: None, len: 4, idx: 8 }, 6)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x66, 0x0F, 0x79, 0xCA]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Extrq { dst: 1, src: Some(2), len: 0, idx: 0 }, 4)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0xF2, 0x0F, 0x78, 0xC1, 0x08]), None, "an immediate missing");
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0x78, 0xC1, 0x08, 0x10]), None, "VMREAD without a prefix is not SSE4a");
        // prefixes as a Zen 5 runs them (Kalmarv on #209): the last of F2 / F3 decides, 66 next
        // to them does not; 0x67 and a REX before a legacy prefix are ignored
        let insertq = Some((ConsoleOnly::Insertq { dst: 0, src: 1, reg: false, len: 16, idx: 16 }, 7));
        for code in [[0x66, 0xF2, 0x0F, 0x78, 0xC1, 0x10, 0x10], [0xF2, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x78, 0xC1, 0x10, 0x10], [0xF3, 0xF2, 0x0F, 0x78, 0xC1, 0x10, 0x10], [0x67, 0xF2, 0x0F, 0x78, 0xC1, 0x10, 0x10], [0x41, 0xF2, 0x0F, 0x78, 0xC1, 0x10, 0x10]] {
            assert_eq!(decode(&code), insertq, "{code:02x?}");
        }
        for code in [[0xF2, 0xF3, 0x0F, 0x78, 0xC1, 0x10, 0x10], [0xF3, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x78, 0xC1, 0x10, 0x10], [0x66, 0xF3, 0x0F, 0x78, 0xC0, 0x10, 0x10]] {
            assert_eq!(decode(&code), None, "#UD on the CPU: {code:02x?}");
        }
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x67, 0x0F, 0x01, 0xFC]), Some((ConsoleOnly::Clzero, 4)));
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x66, 0x0F, 0xAE, 0x38]), None);
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F, 0xAE, 0x30]), None);
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x48, 0x8B, 0x01]), None);
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x66, 0x0F, 0xAE, 0x74, 0x24]), None);
        assert_eq!(decode(&[0x0F]), None);
    }
}

```

`crates/victory-loader/src/crash.rs`:

```rs
//! Names the faulting code when title code crashes.
//!
//! A vectored handler sees every exception first, so it only prints the
//! kinds that end a process (access violations and the like, and
//! breakpoints: titles assert with `int3`, fatal without a debugger) as
//! first-chance, since a handler may still take them (ntdll's loader does
//! with its own probes). What nobody handles, of any kind (an uncaught C++
//! exception too), is reported from the unhandled-exception filter
//! (`report_unhandled`, which the runtime calls ahead of the title's own)
//! and appended to the crash log, with the title's last debug output, which
//! often states the reason. Panics of ours go to the crash log too.

use std::ptr::null_mut;
use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{
    EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION, EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT, EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION,
    EXCEPTION_INT_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO, EXCEPTION_PRIV_INSTRUCTION, EXCEPTION_STACK_OVERFLOW, HMODULE,
};

use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::{
    AddVectoredExceptionHandler, CONTEXT, EXCEPTION_POINTERS, M128A, RtlLookupFunctionEntry,
    RtlVirtualUnwind, SetUnhandledExceptionFilter, UNW_FLAG_NHANDLER,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::{
    GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS, GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT,
    GetModuleFileNameW, GetModuleHandleExW,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentThreadStackLimits;

const EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH: i32 = 0;
/// Frames listed per report.
pub(crate) const MAX_FRAMES: usize = 40;

/// Memory saved to files when a crash is reported: (address, length, file).
#[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
static SAVE: std::sync::OnceLock<Vec<(usize, usize, std::path::PathBuf)>> =
    std::sync::OnceLock::new();

/// Debugging aid: on a reported crash, also write each `[address, address
/// + len)` (readable title memory, e.g. an engine table) to its file.
#[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
pub fn save_on_crash(ranges: Vec<(usize, usize, std::path::PathBuf)>) {
    let _ = SAVE.set(ranges);
}

/// The file crash reports are appended to, besides being printed.
static LOG: std::sync::OnceLock<std::path::PathBuf> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();

/// Also appends every unhandled-exception report and panic to `file`, so a
/// crash can be read after the console is gone.
pub fn log_crashes_to(file: std::path::PathBuf) {
    if LOG.set(file).is_ok() {
        let print = std::panic::take_hook();
        std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(move |info| {
            print(info);
            append_to_log(&format!(
                "VIctory: panic on thread {:?}: {info}\n{}",
                std::thread::current().name().unwrap_or("?"),
                title_output()
            ));
        }));
    }
}

/// Appends a failure that is not an exception (the host GPU's) to the crash
/// log, with the title's last debug output, and prints it.
pub fn log_crash(text: &str) {
    let text = format!("{text}
{}", title_output());
    eprint!("{text}");
    append_to_log(&text);
}

fn append_to_log(text: &str) {
    use std::io::Write;
    let Some(file) = LOG.get() else { return };
    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map_or(0, |d| d.as_secs());
    let opened = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(file);
    if let Ok(mut f) = opened {
        let _ = write!(f, "unix time {now}, process {}\n{text}\n", std::process::id());
    }
}

/// The title's last lines of debug output, kept for crash reports.
static SAID: std::sync::Mutex<std::collections::VecDeque<String>> =
    std::sync::Mutex::new(std::collections::VecDeque::new());
const SAID_LINES: usize = 8;

/// Keeps a line of the title's debug output for the next crash report.
pub fn note_title_output(line: &str) {
    if line.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let mut said = SAID.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    if said.len() == SAID_LINES {
        said.pop_front();
    }
    said.push_back(line.to_owned());
}

/// The kept lines, one per report line; nothing if another thread holds
/// them (it may be the one that faulted).
fn title_output() -> String {
    let Ok(said) = SAID.try_lock() else {
        return String::new();
    };
    said.iter().map(|l| format!("  title said: {l}\n")).collect()
}

/// Installs the handlers; call once before running title code.
pub fn report_crashes() {
    unsafe extern "system" fn filter(info: *const EXCEPTION_POINTERS) -> i32 {
        // SAFETY: the system passes the exception being dispatched.
        unsafe { report_unhandled(info) };
        EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH
    }
    // SAFETY: registers handlers that only read the exception they are
    // given; the title's own filter, once it sets one, takes the place of
    // ours and calls `report_unhandled` first.
    unsafe {
        AddVectoredExceptionHandler(0, Some(handler));
        SetUnhandledExceptionFilter(Some(filter));
    }
}

/// What the vectored handler reports as it happens.
const FATAL: [i32; 6] = [
    EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION,
    EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION,
    EXCEPTION_PRIV_INSTRUCTION,
    EXCEPTION_INT_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO,
    EXCEPTION_STACK_OVERFLOW,
    EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT,
];

/// Console CPUs are Zen 2: titles use AMD-only instructions Intel CPUs
/// lack. Does their job instead: `clzero` (`0f 01 fc`) zeroes the 64-byte
/// line at `rax`; `monitorx`/`mwaitx` (`0f 01 fa`/`fb`) are wait hints, so
/// a spin loop around them works with mwaitx as a yield.
unsafe fn emulate_amd_only(info: *mut EXCEPTION_POINTERS) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: the system passes valid exception pointers; the faulting
    // instruction's bytes are readable, as the CPU just fetched them.
    unsafe {
        let record = &*(*info).ExceptionRecord;
        let context = &mut *(*info).ContextRecord;
        if record.ExceptionCode != EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION {
            return false;
        }
        let code = context.Rip as *const u8;
        match code.cast::<[u8; 3]>().read_unaligned() {
            [0x0f, 0x01, 0xfc] => ((context.Rax & !63) as *mut u8).write_bytes(0, 64),
            [0x0f, 0x01, 0xfa] => {}
            [0x0f, 0x01, 0xfb] => std::thread::yield_now(),
            _ => {
                // Only bytes inside the faulting instruction's page are read: the next page may
                // not be mapped.
                let room = 0x1000 - (context.Rip as usize & 0xfff);
                let mut bytes = [0u8; 32];
                let n = room.min(bytes.len());
                std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(code, bytes.as_mut_ptr(), n);
                if let Some(pass) = clwb_loop(&bytes[..n]) {
                    // A whole write-back loop in one exception (see `clwb_loop`).
                    let limit = *gpr(context, pass.limit);
                    let base = gpr(context, pass.base);
                    *base = if *base <= limit {
                        base.wrapping_add(((limit - *base) / 64 + 1) * 64)
                    } else {
                        base.wrapping_add(64)
                    };
                    let flags = cmp_flags(*base, limit);
                    context.EFlags = context.EFlags & !CMP_FLAGS | flags;
                    context.Rip += pass.len as u64;
                    return true;
                }
                if n >= 15
                    && let Some(len) = clwb_len(bytes[..15].try_into().unwrap_or([0; 15]))
                {
                    // A write-back hint: the PC's memory is coherent, so it has nothing to do.
                    context.Rip += len as u64;
                    return true;
                }
                let Some(len) = sse4a(code, &mut context.Anonymous.FltSave.XmmRegisters) else {
                    return false;
                };
                context.Rip += len as u64;
                return true;
            }
        }
        context.Rip += 3;
    }
    true
}

/// `clwb m8` (`66 [rex] 0f ae /6`, a memory operand), which Intel CPUs before
/// Ice Lake lack: its length, or `None` for any other instruction.
fn clwb_len(code: [u8; 15]) -> Option<usize> {
    let at = if code[1] & 0xf0 == 0x40 { 2 } else { 1 };
    if code[0] != 0x66 || code[at] != 0x0f || code[at + 1] != 0xae {
        return None;
    }
    let modrm = code[at + 2];
    let (mode, rm) = (modrm >> 6, modrm & 7);
    if mode == 3 || (modrm >> 3) & 7 != 6 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut len = at + 3;
    let mut base = rm;
    if rm == 4 {
        base = code[len] & 7;
        len += 1;
    }
    len += match mode {
        0 if rm == 5 || (rm == 4 && base == 5) => 4,
        1 => 1,
        2 => 4,
        _ => 0,
    };
    Some(len)
}

/// A `clwb` write-back loop as the title's compilers build it, one cache line a
/// pass (`base` and `limit` any registers):
///
/// ```text
/// top: clwb [base]
///      add  base, 0x40
///      cmp  base, limit
///      jbe  top
/// ```
///
/// An exception costs about a microsecond and the title writes back whole
/// buffers this way while it loads, so the loop is done in one: `clwb` has
/// nothing to do on the PC, `base` ends past `limit` as the last pass leaves it.
struct ClwbLoop {
    base: u8,
    limit: u8,
    /// Bytes from `clwb` to the instruction after `jbe`.
    len: usize,
}

fn clwb_loop(code: &[u8]) -> Option<ClwbLoop> {
    // clwb [base]: 66 [40|41] 0f ae, ModRM mod 00, reg 6, no SIB or displacement.
    let (rex, at) = match code.get(1)? {
        0x40 | 0x41 => (code[1], 2),
        _ => (0, 1),
    };
    if *code.first()? != 0x66 || code.get(at..at + 2)? != [0x0f, 0xae] {
        return None;
    }
    let modrm = *code.get(at + 2)?;
    let rm = modrm & 7;
    if modrm >> 6 != 0 || (modrm >> 3) & 7 != 6 || rm == 4 || rm == 5 {
        return None;
    }
    let base = rm | (rex & 1) << 3;
    // add base, 0x40: REX.W(+B) 83 /0 ib.
    let add = at + 3;
    if *code.get(add..add + 4)? != [0x48 | base >> 3, 0x83, 0xc0 | (base & 7), 0x40] {
        return None;
    }
    // cmp base, limit: REX.W 39 /r with base in r/m.
    let cmp = add + 4;
    let &[cmp_rex @ 0x48..=0x4f, 0x39, cmp_modrm] = code.get(cmp..cmp + 3)? else {
        return None;
    };
    if cmp_modrm >> 6 != 3 || (cmp_modrm & 7 | (cmp_rex & 1) << 3) != base {
        return None;
    }
    let limit = (cmp_modrm >> 3) & 7 | (cmp_rex & 4) << 1;
    // jbe top.
    let jump = cmp + 3;
    let len = jump + 2;
    if *code.get(jump)? != 0x76 || i64::from(*code.get(jump + 1)? as i8) != -(len as i64) {
        return None;
    }
    (limit != base).then_some(ClwbLoop { base, limit, len })
}

/// The general register numbered `n` as instructions encode it.
fn gpr(context: &mut CONTEXT, n: u8) -> &mut u64 {
    match n & 15 {
        0 => &mut context.Rax,
        1 => &mut context.Rcx,
        2 => &mut context.Rdx,
        3 => &mut context.Rbx,
        4 => &mut context.Rsp,
        5 => &mut context.Rbp,
        6 => &mut context.Rsi,
        7 => &mut context.Rdi,
        8 => &mut context.R8,
        9 => &mut context.R9,
        10 => &mut context.R10,
        11 => &mut context.R11,
        12 => &mut context.R12,
        13 => &mut context.R13,
        14 => &mut context.R14,
        _ => &mut context.R15,
    }
}

/// The status flags `cmp a, b` leaves (CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, OF) as `EFLAGS` bits.
fn cmp_flags(a: u64, b: u64) -> u32 {
    let r = a.wrapping_sub(b);
    u32::from(a < b)
        | u32::from((r as u8).count_ones().is_multiple_of(2)) << 2
        | (((a ^ b ^ r) >> 4) as u32 & 1) << 4
        | u32::from(r == 0) << 6
        | ((r >> 63) as u32) << 7
        | ((((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) >> 63) as u32) << 11
}
const CMP_FLAGS: u32 = 0x8d5;

/// SSE4a's `extrq`/`insertq` (register forms, the only ones there are) on
/// the saved XMM registers; returns the instruction's length.
unsafe fn sse4a(code: *const u8, xmm: &mut [M128A; 16]) -> Option<usize> {
    // SAFETY: the caller's code bytes are readable up to the instruction's end.
    let b = |i: usize| unsafe { code.add(i).read() };
    let prefix = b(0);
    let (rex, at) = if b(1) & 0xf0 == 0x40 {
        (b(1), 2)
    } else {
        (0, 1)
    };
    if !matches!(prefix, 0x66 | 0xf2) || b(at) != 0x0f || !matches!(b(at + 1), 0x78 | 0x79) {
        return None;
    }
    let modrm = b(at + 2);
    if modrm >> 6 != 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let dst = usize::from((modrm >> 3) & 7 | (rex & 4) << 1);
    let src = usize::from(modrm & 7 | (rex & 1) << 3);
    let immediate = b(at + 1) == 0x78;
    let (fields, len) = if immediate {
        ((b(at + 3), b(at + 4)), at + 5)
    } else {
        // extrq reads its fields from src's low half, insertq from its high.
        let f = if prefix == 0x66 { xmm[src].Low } else { xmm[src].High as u64 };
        ((f as u8, (f >> 8) as u8), at + 3)
    };
    let (n, at_bit) = (u32::from(fields.0 & 63), u32::from(fields.1 & 63));
    let bits = if n == 0 { 64 } else { n };
    let mask = if bits == 64 { u64::MAX } else { (1u64 << bits) - 1 };
    if prefix == 0x66 {
        // extrq: register form takes its fields from src, works on dst.
        if immediate && (modrm >> 3) & 7 != 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let target = if immediate { src } else { dst };
        xmm[target].Low = (xmm[target].Low >> at_bit) & mask;
    } else {
        let value = (xmm[src].Low & mask) << at_bit;
        xmm[dst].Low = xmm[dst].Low & !(mask << at_bit) | value;
    }
    Some(len)
}

unsafe extern "system" fn handler(info: *mut EXCEPTION_POINTERS) -> i32 {
    // an instruction of the console's CPU this one lacks: emulated, the title goes on
    // SAFETY: the system passes valid exception pointers.
    if unsafe { (*(*info).ExceptionRecord).ExceptionCode } == EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION {
        // SAFETY: the faulting thread's context, for the exception being dispatched.
        let r = unsafe { crate::console_insn::emulate(&mut *(*info).ContextRecord) };
        if r != 0 {
            return r;
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: the system passes valid exception pointers.
    if unsafe { emulate_amd_only(info) } {
        return -1; // EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION
    }
    // SAFETY: as above.
    if FATAL.contains(&unsafe { (*(*info).ExceptionRecord).ExceptionCode }) {
        // SAFETY: as above.
        unsafe { report("first-chance exception", info, false) };
    }
    EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH
}

/// For an unhandled-exception filter: reports the exception that is about
/// to end the process, and appends it to the crash log.
///
/// # Safety
/// `info` comes from the system, for an exception being dispatched.
pub unsafe fn report_unhandled(info: *const EXCEPTION_POINTERS) {
    // SAFETY: forwarded from the caller.
    unsafe { report("unhandled exception", info, true) };
}

/// The bytes at `at` as hex, as many as the longest x86 instruction (15),
/// but none past the end of `at`'s page: the next page may not be mapped.
/// For an instruction the CPU refused, they name it (`0f 01 fd` is
/// `rdpru`), which the address alone does not.
///
/// # Safety
/// `at`'s page is readable.
unsafe fn instruction_bytes(at: usize) -> String {
    let n = (0x1000 - (at & 0xfff)).min(15);
    // SAFETY: `n` bytes from `at` stay inside its page, which the caller
    // says is readable.
    let bytes = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(at as *const u8, n) };
    let hex: Vec<_> = bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect();
    hex.join(" ")
}

/// MSVC's code for a C++ `throw`, and its magic first parameter.
const CPP_EXCEPTION: i32 = 0xE06D_7363_u32 as i32;
const CPP_MAGIC: usize = 0x1993_0520;

/// What a C++ throw threw: the decorated name of its type, then its value
/// where that names the cause (an integer, e.g. an HRESULT; a standard
/// exception's message).
///
/// # Safety
/// `p` are the parameters of a live MSVC throw (`p[0]` the magic).
unsafe fn thrown(p: &[usize]) -> String {
    // SAFETY: the throw's ThrowInfo, its RVAs relative to `p[3]`: catchable
    // type array at +12 (count, then type RVAs), each type's descriptor at
    // +4, whose decorated name starts at +16; the object is at `p[1]`.
    unsafe {
        let rva = |at: usize| (at as *const u32).read_unaligned() as usize;
        let types = p[3] + rva(p[2] + 12);
        let name = |i: usize| {
            let descriptor = p[3] + rva(p[3] + rva(types + 4 + 4 * i) + 4);
            std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr((descriptor + 16) as *const std::ffi::c_char)
                .to_string_lossy()
        };
        let first = name(0);
        let value = match &*first {
            // int, unsigned, long (HRESULT), unsigned long
            ".H" | ".I" | ".J" | ".K" if p[1] != 0 => {
                format!(" = {:#010x}", (p[1] as *const u32).read_unaligned())
            }
            // std::exception keeps its message after the table pointer.
            _ if (0..rva(types)).any(|i| name(i) == ".?AVexception@std@@") => {
                let message = (p[1] as *const *const std::ffi::c_char).add(1).read();
                if message.is_null() {
                    String::new()
                } else {
                    format!(": {}", std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr(message).to_string_lossy())
                }
            }
            _ => String::new(),
        };
        format!("{first}{value}")
    }
}

/// # Safety
/// See [`report_unhandled`].
unsafe fn report(what: &str, info: *const EXCEPTION_POINTERS, to_file: bool) {
    // SAFETY: the system passes valid exception pointers.
    let (record, context) = unsafe { (&*(*info).ExceptionRecord, &*(*info).ContextRecord) };
    let code = record.ExceptionCode;
    let at = record.ExceptionAddress as usize;
    let p = record.ExceptionInformation;
    let detail = if code == EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION {
        let kind = match p[0] {
            0 => "read",
            1 => "write",
            _ => "execute",
        };
        format!(" ({kind} {:#x}: {})", p[1], memory_at(p[1]))
    } else if code == CPP_EXCEPTION && record.NumberParameters >= 4 && p[0] == CPP_MAGIC {
        // SAFETY: a live MSVC throw.
        format!(" (C++ {} thrown)", unsafe { thrown(&p) })
    } else if code == EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION || code == EXCEPTION_PRIV_INSTRUCTION {
        // SAFETY: the CPU refused the instruction at `at`, so it fetched it.
        format!(" (code {})", unsafe { instruction_bytes(at) })
    } else {
        String::new()
    };
    // Printed line by line (a fault while unwinding must not lose the
    // lines before it), and kept for the file.
    let mut text = String::new();
    let mut line = |l: String| {
        eprintln!("{l}");
        text.push_str(&l);
        text.push('\n');
    };
    line(format!(
        "VIctory: {what} {:#010x} at {}{detail}",
        code as u32,
        locate(at)
    ));
    line(format!(
        "  rax {:#x} rbx {:#x} rcx {:#x} rdx {:#x} rsi {:#x} rdi {:#x} rsp {:#x} rbp {:#x}",
        context.Rax,
        context.Rbx,
        context.Rcx,
        context.Rdx,
        context.Rsi,
        context.Rdi,
        context.Rsp,
        context.Rbp
    ));
    line(format!(
        "  r8 {:#x} r9 {:#x} r10 {:#x} r11 {:#x} r12 {:#x} r13 {:#x} r14 {:#x} r15 {:#x}",
        context.R8,
        context.R9,
        context.R10,
        context.R11,
        context.R12,
        context.R13,
        context.R14,
        context.R15
    ));
    for (i, pc) in unwind(*context).into_iter().enumerate() {
        line(format!("  #{i:<2} {}", locate(pc as usize)));
    }
    if to_file {
        let said = title_output();
        eprint!("{said}");
        text.push_str(&said);
        append_to_log(&text);
    }
    #[cfg(feature = "diagnostics")]
    for (address, len, file) in SAVE.get().into_iter().flatten() {
        // SAFETY: the caller of `save_on_crash` named readable memory.
        let bytes = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(*address as *const u8, *len) };
        let saved = std::fs::write(file, bytes);
        eprintln!(
            "  saved {address:#x}+{len:#x} to {} ({saved:?})",
            file.display()
        );
    }
}

/// Return addresses of the faulting thread's frames, from the faulting
/// instruction up, by the unwind data of each image (the Windows loader
/// registered it for title images too). Code without unwind data (our
/// thunks, leaf functions) is taken to have its return address at `rsp`.
fn unwind(context: CONTEXT) -> Vec<u64> {
    let (mut low, mut high) = (0, 0);
    // SAFETY: writes the current thread's stack bounds.
    unsafe { GetCurrentThreadStackLimits(&mut low, &mut high) };
    let mut frames = Vec::with_capacity(MAX_FRAMES);
    unwind_into(context, low, high, &mut frames);
    frames
}

/// A `CONTEXT` at the 16-byte alignment the unwind and capture functions need.
#[repr(C, align(16))]
pub(crate) struct Aligned16(pub(crate) CONTEXT);

/// [`unwind`] for any thread of the process, its stack being `low..high`;
/// pushes no more than `MAX_FRAMES`, so it does not allocate when `frames`
/// has that capacity (another thread may be suspended holding the heap).
pub(crate) fn unwind_into(context: CONTEXT, low: usize, high: usize, frames: &mut Vec<u64>) {
    // `RtlVirtualUnwind` writes the context with 16-byte aligned stores, and
    // windows-sys declares `CONTEXT` without that alignment: a by-value copy on
    // the stack can land 8 bytes off and fault (seen in a debug build).
    let mut aligned = Aligned16(context);
    let context = &mut aligned.0;
    frames.push(context.Rip);
    while frames.len() < MAX_FRAMES {
        // Stop where reading the stack would fault inside this handler.
        let rsp = context.Rsp as usize;
        if rsp < low || rsp + 8 > high {
            break;
        }
        let mut image = 0;
        // SAFETY: looks up the function table entry covering `Rip`, if any.
        let entry = unsafe { RtlLookupFunctionEntry(context.Rip, &mut image, null_mut()) };
        if entry.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: `rsp` is inside this thread's stack.
            context.Rip = unsafe { (rsp as *const u64).read() };
            context.Rsp += 8;
        } else {
            let (mut data, mut frame) = (null_mut(), 0);
            // SAFETY: `entry` belongs to `image`; the context is our copy.
            unsafe {
                RtlVirtualUnwind(
                    UNW_FLAG_NHANDLER,
                    image,
                    context.Rip,
                    entry,
                    context,
                    &mut data,
                    &mut frame,
                    null_mut(),
                )
            };
        }
        if context.Rip == 0 {
            break;
        }
        frames.push(context.Rip);
    }
}

/// `module+rva`, or the bare address.
pub fn locate(address: usize) -> String {
    module_of(address).unwrap_or_else(|| format!("{address:#x}"))
}

fn module_of(address: usize) -> Option<String> {
    let mut module: HMODULE = std::ptr::null_mut();
    // SAFETY: looks up the module containing `address`; no reference taken.
    let found = unsafe {
        GetModuleHandleExW(
            GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS | GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT,
            address as *const u16,
            &mut module,
        )
    };
    if found == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut path = [0u16; 260];
    // SAFETY: `module` is a loaded module; the buffer length is passed.
    let len = unsafe { GetModuleFileNameW(module, path.as_mut_ptr(), path.len() as u32) };
    let path = String::from_utf16_lossy(&path[..len as usize]);
    let name = path.rsplit('\\').next().unwrap_or(&path);
    Some(format!("{name}+{:#x}", address - module as usize))
}

/// What is at `address`, for an access violation there: nothing, memory
/// reserved but never committed, a guard page, or the protection the access
/// broke (with the module, for an image's pages). Each points at a different
/// cause: a wild pointer, an allocation whose commit failed, a stack
/// overrun, a write to code or constants.
fn memory_at(address: usize) -> String {
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
        MEM_FREE, MEM_IMAGE, MEM_RESERVE, MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION, PAGE_EXECUTE,
        PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, PAGE_EXECUTE_WRITECOPY, PAGE_GUARD,
        PAGE_NOACCESS, PAGE_READONLY, PAGE_READWRITE, PAGE_WRITECOPY, VirtualQuery,
    };
    // SAFETY: a zeroed MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION is valid.
    let mut info: MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    // SAFETY: reads the address space's bookkeeping, not `address` itself.
    let n = unsafe { VirtualQuery(address as *const _, &mut info, size_of_val(&info)) };
    if n == 0 {
        // Above the process's address space: Windows reports a
        // non-canonical address as all ones.
        return "outside the address space".into();
    }
    let protect = match info.State {
        MEM_FREE => return "nothing mapped there".into(),
        MEM_RESERVE => return "reserved, never committed".into(),
        _ if info.Protect & PAGE_GUARD != 0 => return "a guard page".into(),
        _ => match info.Protect & 0xff {
            PAGE_NOACCESS => "no access".into(),
            PAGE_READONLY => "read-only".into(),
            PAGE_READWRITE => "read-write".into(),
            PAGE_WRITECOPY => "copy-on-write".into(),
            PAGE_EXECUTE => "execute-only".into(),
            PAGE_EXECUTE_READ => "read-execute".into(),
            PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE => "read-write-execute".into(),
            PAGE_EXECUTE_WRITECOPY => "copy-on-write, executable".into(),
            _ => format!("protection {:#x}", info.Protect),
        },
    };
    match module_of(address) {
        Some(module) if info.Type == MEM_IMAGE => format!("{protect}, in {module}"),
        _ => protect,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::{
        EXCEPTION_RECORD, RtlCaptureContext, RtlCaptureStackBackTrace,
    };

    #[test]
    #[inline(never)]
    fn unwinds_like_the_system_walk() {
        // SAFETY: zeroed CONTEXT is valid; both calls write our buffers.
        let (frames, walked) = unsafe {
            // `RtlCaptureContext` wants it 16-byte aligned too.
            let mut context = Aligned16(std::mem::zeroed());
            RtlCaptureContext(&mut context.0);
            let mut walked = [null_mut(); 8];
            let n = RtlCaptureStackBackTrace(0, 8, walked.as_mut_ptr(), null_mut());
            (unwind(context.0), walked[..usize::from(n)].to_vec())
        };
        // Frame 0 differs (two call sites in this function); callers agree.
        assert!(walked.len() >= 4, "{walked:?}");
        let ours: Vec<_> = frames[1..walked.len()]
            .iter()
            .map(|&f| f as usize)
            .collect();
        let system: Vec<_> = walked[1..].iter().map(|&f| f as usize).collect();
        assert_eq!(ours, system);
    }

    #[test]
    fn memory_at_names_what_an_access_hit() {
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
            MEM_COMMIT, MEM_RELEASE, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_GUARD, PAGE_NOACCESS, PAGE_READONLY,
            PAGE_READWRITE, VirtualAlloc, VirtualFree,
        };
        // SAFETY: reserves four pages of ours and commits three of them;
        // nothing reads or writes them.
        let base = unsafe {
            let base = VirtualAlloc(std::ptr::null(), 0x4000, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_NOACCESS);
            assert!(!base.is_null());
            let page = |i: usize, protect| {
                let at = base.cast::<u8>().add(i * 0x1000).cast();
                assert!(!VirtualAlloc(at, 0x1000, MEM_COMMIT, protect).is_null());
            };
            page(1, PAGE_READONLY);
            page(2, PAGE_READWRITE | PAGE_GUARD);
            page(3, PAGE_NOACCESS);
            base as usize
        };
        assert_eq!(memory_at(base + 8), "reserved, never committed");
        assert_eq!(memory_at(base + 0x1008), "read-only");
        assert_eq!(memory_at(base + 0x2008), "a guard page");
        assert_eq!(memory_at(base + 0x3008), "no access");
        // SAFETY: releases the reservation made above.
        unsafe { VirtualFree(base as *mut _, 0, MEM_RELEASE) };
        assert_eq!(memory_at(base + 8), "nothing mapped there");
        assert_eq!(memory_at(0), "nothing mapped there");
        assert_eq!(memory_at(usize::MAX), "outside the address space");
        // This test's own code: an image page, named by its module.
        let code = memory_at(memory_at_names_what_an_access_hit as *const () as usize);
        let named = code.starts_with("read-execute, in victory_loader-");
        assert!(named, "{code}");
    }

    /// On an Intel CPU, the real instructions go through the vectored
    /// handler. On an AMD CPU they run natively, and the tests below test
    /// the emulation.
    #[test]
    fn clwb_loops() {
        // clwb [rcx]; add rcx, 0x40; cmp rcx, rax; jbe top
        let a = clwb_loop(&[
            0x66, 0x0f, 0xae, 0x31, 0x48, 0x83, 0xc1, 0x40, 0x48, 0x39, 0xc1, 0x76, 0xf3,
        ])
        .expect("rcx loop");
        assert_eq!((a.base, a.limit, a.len), (1, 0, 13));
        // clwb [r9]; add r9, 0x40; cmp r9, rax; jbe top
        let b = clwb_loop(&[
            0x66, 0x41, 0x0f, 0xae, 0x31, 0x49, 0x83, 0xc1, 0x40, 0x49, 0x39, 0xc1, 0x76, 0xf2,
        ])
        .expect("r9 loop");
        assert_eq!((b.base, b.limit, b.len), (9, 0, 14));
        // A different stride, a jump elsewhere, or a cut-off loop is not one.
        assert!(
            clwb_loop(&[
                0x66, 0x0f, 0xae, 0x31, 0x48, 0x83, 0xc1, 0x20, 0x48, 0x39, 0xc1, 0x76, 0xf3
            ])
            .is_none()
        );
        assert!(
            clwb_loop(&[
                0x66, 0x0f, 0xae, 0x31, 0x48, 0x83, 0xc1, 0x40, 0x48, 0x39, 0xc1, 0x76, 0xf0
            ])
            .is_none()
        );
        assert!(clwb_loop(&[0x66, 0x0f, 0xae, 0x31, 0x48, 0x83, 0xc1, 0x40]).is_none());
        // The flags the last cmp leaves: base just past limit.
        assert_eq!(cmp_flags(0x1040, 0x1000) & 0x41, 0); // CF and ZF clear: the loop ends
        assert_eq!(cmp_flags(0x1000, 0x1000) & 0x40, 0x40);
    }

    #[test]
    fn clwb_lengths() {
        let pad = |b: &[u8]| {
            let mut c = [0u8; 15];
            c[..b.len()].copy_from_slice(b);
            c
        };
        assert_eq!(clwb_len(pad(&[0x66, 0x41, 0x0f, 0xae, 0x31])), Some(5)); // clwb [r9]
        assert_eq!(clwb_len(pad(&[0x66, 0x0f, 0xae, 0x30])), Some(4)); // clwb [rax]
        assert_eq!(clwb_len(pad(&[0x66, 0x0f, 0xae, 0x70, 0x40])), Some(5)); // clwb [rax+0x40]
        assert_eq!(
            clwb_len(pad(&[0x66, 0x0f, 0xae, 0xb0, 0, 1, 0, 0])),
            Some(8)
        ); // [rax+disp32]
        assert_eq!(clwb_len(pad(&[0x66, 0x0f, 0xae, 0x34, 0x24])), Some(5)); // clwb [rsp]
        assert_eq!(
            clwb_len(pad(&[0x66, 0x0f, 0xae, 0x35, 0, 0, 0, 0])),
            Some(8)
        ); // [rip+disp32]
        assert_eq!(clwb_len(pad(&[0x66, 0x0f, 0xae, 0x38])), None); // clflushopt, /7
        assert_eq!(clwb_len(pad(&[0x0f, 0xae, 0x30])), None); // xsaveopt, no 66
        assert_eq!(clwb_len(pad(&[0x66, 0x0f, 0xae, 0xf0])), None); // register form
    }

    #[test]
    fn clzero_zeroes_its_line_on_any_cpu() {
        report_crashes();
        #[repr(align(64))]
        struct Line([u8; 128]);
        let mut line = Line([0xff; 128]);
        let at = line.0.as_mut_ptr().wrapping_add(5); // inside the first line
        // SAFETY: clzero writes only the 64-byte line holding `at`, ours.
        unsafe { std::arch::asm!(".byte 0x0f, 0x01, 0xfc", in("rax") at) };
        assert!(line.0[..64].iter().all(|&b| b == 0));
        assert!(line.0[64..].iter().all(|&b| b == 0xff));
        // insertq xmm0, xmm1, len 16, at 16; then extrq xmm0, len 8, at 20.
        let out: u64;
        // SAFETY: touches only the named registers.
        unsafe {
            std::arch::asm!(
                "movq xmm0, {a}", "movq xmm1, {b}",
                ".byte 0xf2, 0x0f, 0x78, 0xc1, 0x10, 0x10",
                "movq {a}, xmm0",
                ".byte 0x66, 0x0f, 0x78, 0xc0, 0x08, 0x14",
                "movq {b}, xmm0",
                a = inout(reg) 0x1111_2222_3333_4444u64 => _, b = inout(reg) 0xabcdu64 => out,
                out("xmm0") _, out("xmm1") _)
        };
        assert_eq!(out, 0xbc); // 0x1111_2222_abcd_4444 >> 20, 8 bits
        // SAFETY: monitorx/mwaitx are wait hints that write no memory.
        unsafe {
            std::arch::asm!(".byte 0x0f, 0x01, 0xfa", ".byte 0x0f, 0x01, 0xfb",
                in("rax") at, in("ecx") 0, in("edx") 0)
        };
    }

    fn reg(low: u64, high: u64) -> M128A {
        M128A {
            Low: low,
            High: high as i64,
        }
    }

    /// Gives `code` to the emulation as if it faulted with `exception` at
    /// its first byte, with `rax` and `xmm` as the saved registers. The
    /// emulation does not execute `code`, so this works on any CPU. Returns
    /// the number of bytes that the emulation skipped, or `None` if it did
    /// not emulate the instruction. `xmm` gets the saved registers after.
    fn emulate_as(exception: i32, code: &[u8], rax: u64, xmm: &mut [M128A; 16]) -> Option<u64> {
        // `int3` after the instruction, so that a decoder that reads too
        // far sees no valid bytes.
        let mut bytes = [0xcc_u8; 16];
        bytes[..code.len()].copy_from_slice(code);
        let start = bytes.as_ptr() as u64;
        // SAFETY: a zeroed record and context are valid; the emulation
        // reads only `bytes` and writes only `context` (and memory at
        // `rax` for clzero, which the caller owns).
        unsafe {
            let mut record: EXCEPTION_RECORD = std::mem::zeroed();
            record.ExceptionCode = exception;
            let mut context: CONTEXT = std::mem::zeroed();
            context.Rip = start;
            context.Rax = rax;
            context.Anonymous.FltSave.XmmRegisters = *xmm;
            let mut pointers = EXCEPTION_POINTERS {
                ExceptionRecord: &mut record,
                ContextRecord: &mut context,
            };
            let emulated = emulate_amd_only(&mut pointers);
            *xmm = context.Anonymous.FltSave.XmmRegisters;
            emulated.then(|| context.Rip - start)
        }
    }

    fn emulate(code: &[u8], rax: u64, xmm: &mut [M128A; 16]) -> Option<u64> {
        emulate_as(EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION, code, rax, xmm)
    }

    fn low(xmm: &[M128A; 16], i: usize) -> u64 {
        xmm[i].Low
    }

    #[test]
    fn emulated_clzero_zeroes_its_line() {
        #[repr(align(64))]
        struct Line([u8; 128]);
        let mut line = Line([0xff; 128]);
        let at = line.0.as_mut_ptr().wrapping_add(5) as u64; // inside the first line
        let mut xmm = [reg(0, 0); 16];
        assert_eq!(emulate(&[0x0f, 0x01, 0xfc], at, &mut xmm), Some(3));
        assert!(line.0[..64].iter().all(|&b| b == 0));
        assert!(line.0[64..].iter().all(|&b| b == 0xff));
    }

    #[test]
    fn emulated_monitorx_and_mwaitx_are_skipped() {
        let mut xmm = [reg(1, 2); 16];
        assert_eq!(emulate(&[0x0f, 0x01, 0xfa], 0, &mut xmm), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(emulate(&[0x0f, 0x01, 0xfb], 0, &mut xmm), Some(3));
        assert!(xmm.iter().all(|r| r.Low == 1 && r.High == 2));
    }

    #[test]
    fn emulated_insertq_and_extrq_with_immediates() {
        let mut xmm = [reg(0, 0); 16];
        xmm[0] = reg(0x1111_2222_3333_4444, 0x5555);
        xmm[1] = reg(0xabcd, 0x6666);
        // insertq xmm0, xmm1, length 16, index 16
        let insertq = [0xf2, 0x0f, 0x78, 0xc1, 0x10, 0x10];
        assert_eq!(emulate(&insertq, 0, &mut xmm), Some(6));
        assert_eq!(low(&xmm, 0), 0x1111_2222_abcd_4444);
        assert_eq!((low(&xmm, 1), xmm[1].High), (0xabcd, 0x6666));
        // extrq xmm0, length 8, index 20
        let extrq = [0x66, 0x0f, 0x78, 0xc0, 0x08, 0x14];
        assert_eq!(emulate(&extrq, 0, &mut xmm), Some(6));
        assert_eq!(low(&xmm, 0), 0xbc);
    }

    #[test]
    fn emulated_insertq_and_extrq_with_fields_in_a_register() {
        let mut xmm = [reg(0, 0); 16];
        // insertq xmm0, xmm1: length and index in xmm1's high half.
        xmm[0] = reg(0x1111_2222_3333_4444, 0);
        xmm[1] = reg(0xabcd, 0x10_10);
        assert_eq!(emulate(&[0xf2, 0x0f, 0x79, 0xc1], 0, &mut xmm), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(low(&xmm, 0), 0x1111_2222_abcd_4444);
        // extrq xmm0, xmm1: length and index in xmm1's low half.
        xmm[1] = reg(0x14_08, 0);
        assert_eq!(emulate(&[0x66, 0x0f, 0x79, 0xc1], 0, &mut xmm), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(low(&xmm, 0), 0xbc);
    }

    #[test]
    fn emulated_sse4a_reaches_xmm8_to_xmm15() {
        let mut xmm = [reg(0, 0); 16];
        xmm[8] = reg(0x1111_2222_3333_4444, 0);
        xmm[9] = reg(0xabcd, 0);
        // insertq xmm8, xmm9, length 16, index 16 (REX.R and REX.B)
        let insertq = [0xf2, 0x45, 0x0f, 0x78, 0xc1, 0x10, 0x10];
        assert_eq!(emulate(&insertq, 0, &mut xmm), Some(7));
        assert_eq!(low(&xmm, 8), 0x1111_2222_abcd_4444);
        assert_eq!((low(&xmm, 0), low(&xmm, 1)), (0, 0));
        // extrq xmm9, length 8, index 4 (REX.B)
        let extrq = [0x66, 0x41, 0x0f, 0x78, 0xc1, 0x08, 0x04];
        assert_eq!(emulate(&extrq, 0, &mut xmm), Some(7));
        assert_eq!(low(&xmm, 9), 0xbc);
        assert_eq!(low(&xmm, 1), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn emulated_sse4a_length_0_is_64_bits() {
        let mut xmm = [reg(0, 0); 16];
        xmm[0] = reg(0x1122_3344_5566_7788, 0);
        // extrq xmm0, length 0 (64), index 0. A non-zero index with
        // length 64 goes past bit 63, and AMD leaves that result undefined.
        assert_eq!(
            emulate(&[0x66, 0x0f, 0x78, 0xc0, 0x00, 0x00], 0, &mut xmm),
            Some(6)
        );
        assert_eq!(low(&xmm, 0), 0x1122_3344_5566_7788);
        // insertq xmm0, xmm1, length 0 (64), index 0
        xmm[1] = reg(0xdead_beef_cafe_f00d, 0);
        assert_eq!(
            emulate(&[0xf2, 0x0f, 0x78, 0xc1, 0x00, 0x00], 0, &mut xmm),
            Some(6)
        );
        assert_eq!(low(&xmm, 0), 0xdead_beef_cafe_f00d);
    }

    #[test]
    fn other_instructions_and_exceptions_are_not_emulated() {
        let mut xmm = [reg(0, 0); 16];
        assert_eq!(emulate(&[0x0f, 0x0b], 0, &mut xmm), None); // ud2
        // extrq with a memory operand, which does not exist
        assert_eq!(emulate(&[0x66, 0x0f, 0x79, 0x00], 0, &mut xmm), None);
        // extrq with immediates needs ModRM.reg 0
        let bad_extrq = [0x66, 0x0f, 0x78, 0xc8, 0x08, 0x14];
        assert_eq!(emulate(&bad_extrq, 0, &mut xmm), None);
        // a clzero that did not cause an illegal instruction
        let clzero = [0x0f, 0x01, 0xfc];
        assert_eq!(
            emulate_as(EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION, &clzero, 0, &mut xmm),
            None
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn instruction_bytes_stop_at_the_end_of_their_page() {
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
            MEM_COMMIT, MEM_RELEASE, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_NOACCESS, PAGE_READWRITE, VirtualAlloc,
            VirtualFree, VirtualProtect,
        };
        // rdpru, then the next instruction (mov rcx, rax) and padding.
        let mut code = [0x90_u8; 16];
        code[..6].copy_from_slice(&[0x0f, 0x01, 0xfd, 0x48, 0x89, 0xc1]);
        // SAFETY: two fresh pages of ours, the second made unreadable, so a
        // read past the end of the first faults.
        unsafe {
            let page = VirtualAlloc(
                std::ptr::null(),
                0x2000,
                MEM_RESERVE | MEM_COMMIT,
                PAGE_READWRITE,
            )
            .cast::<u8>();
            assert!(!page.is_null());
            let mut old = 0;
            let guard = page.add(0x1000).cast();
            assert_ne!(VirtualProtect(guard, 0x1000, PAGE_NOACCESS, &mut old), 0);
            page.copy_from_nonoverlapping(code.as_ptr(), code.len());
            let whole = "0f 01 fd 48 89 c1 90 90 90 90 90 90 90 90 90";
            assert_eq!(instruction_bytes(page as usize), whole);
            // The page's last three bytes: rdpru, and nothing read after it.
            let end = page.add(0x1000 - 3);
            end.copy_from_nonoverlapping(code.as_ptr(), 3);
            assert_eq!(instruction_bytes(end as usize), "0f 01 fd");
            VirtualFree(page.cast(), 0, MEM_RELEASE);
        }
    }
}

```

`crates/victory-loader/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Runs a title's original x86-64 code natively, inside our process.
//!
//! Xbox Series X|S executables are x86-64 PE32+ images built for a Zen 2
//! CPU, so the machine code needs no translation. What differs is the
//! platform underneath, so the loader's job is to:
//!
//! 1. [`prepare()`] a lightly patched copy of the image (pure, portable): mark
//!    it as a DLL, remove its entry point and import directory, and detach
//!    its TLS callbacks, so the Windows loader maps it, relocates it,
//!    allocates its static TLS and registers its unwind tables, but runs
//!    none of its code and resolves none of its imports;
//! 2. load that copy as a real module (debuggers, profilers, crash dumps
//!    and stack walks all see it); this step is Windows-only;
//! 3. map the DLLs the title ships beside it the same way
//!    (`load_title_dlls`);
//! 4. bind every import ourselves through an [`ImportResolver`], our
//!    runtime (`victory-hle`), the host or the title's DLLs, and route
//!    anything unresolved to a generated stub that reports exactly what
//!    was called;
//! 5. initialise the title's DLLs, then run TLS callbacks and the entry
//!    point on a thread with the stack size the image asks for; from then
//!    on, pass every thread start and end on to the attached images.

#[cfg(windows)]
mod console_insn;
mod crash;
pub mod prepare;
pub mod resolve;
#[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]
mod stacks;
#[cfg(windows)]
mod threads;
#[cfg(windows)]
mod thunks;
#[cfg(windows)]
mod tls;
#[cfg(windows)]
mod windows;

#[cfg(windows)]
pub use crash::{
    locate, log_crash, log_crashes_to, note_title_output, report_crashes, report_unhandled,
};
#[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]
pub use crash::save_on_crash;
pub use prepare::{PrepareError, PreparedImage, prepare};
pub use resolve::{ImportResolver, Provenance, Resolution};
#[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]
pub use stacks::{dump_stacks, dump_stacks_on_schedule};
#[cfg(windows)]
pub use threads::disable_thread_calls;
#[cfg(windows)]
pub use thunks::{UnimplementedPolicy, unimplemented_call_count};
#[cfg(windows)]
pub use windows::{
    BindReport, LoadedImage, MissingImport, WithTitleDlls, load, load_title_dll, load_title_dlls,
};

/// `DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH`, for TLS callbacks.
pub const DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH: u32 = 1;
/// `DLL_PROCESS_DETACH`.
pub const DLL_PROCESS_DETACH: u32 = 0;

`crates/victory-loader/src/prepare.rs`:

```rs
//! Turns a title's image into something the Windows loader maps but does
//! not run. Pure byte manipulation, so it is testable on any host.

use victory_pe::layout::{self, dir, dll_flags, file_flags};
use victory_pe::{ImageInfo, PeError};

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum PrepareError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    Pe(#[from] PeError),
    #[error("cannot patch image: {0}")]
    Patch(&'static str),
}

/// A patched copy of an image plus everything we need from the original.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PreparedImage {
    /// Parsed from the *original* bytes: imports, TLS callbacks and entry
    /// point as the title expects them.
    pub info: ImageInfo,
    /// The patched bytes to hand to the Windows loader.
    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
    /// BLAKE3 of the original bytes: identifies the exact build.
    pub original_hash: blake3::Hash,
}

impl PreparedImage {
    /// File name for the patched copy, unique per original build.
    pub fn file_name(&self) -> String {
        format!("victory-image-{}.dll", &self.original_hash.to_hex()[..16])
    }
}

/// Produces the patched copy. The changes are:
///
/// * `IMAGE_FILE_DLL` set, entry point cleared: the OS maps it like a DLL
///   and calls nothing;
/// * import directory points to its empty terminator and the bound-import
///   directory is cleared: we bind the original slots using `info.imports`;
/// * TLS callback pointer cleared: the OS still allocates static TLS for
///   the image, but callbacks only run when we call them (after binding);
///   its base relocation is made a no-op so the 0 survives a rebase;
/// * `FORCE_INTEGRITY` cleared, checksum zeroed: the copy is unsigned.
pub fn prepare(original: &[u8]) -> Result<PreparedImage, PrepareError> {
    let info = ImageInfo::parse(original)?;
    let mut bytes = original.to_vec();

    let fh = layout::file_header_offset(&bytes).ok_or(PrepareError::Patch("no file header"))?;
    let opt =
        layout::optional_header_offset(&bytes).ok_or(PrepareError::Patch("no optional header"))?;

    let characteristics = info.characteristics | file_flags::DLL;
    write_u16(
        &mut bytes,
        fh + layout::FILE_HEADER_CHARACTERISTICS,
        characteristics,
    )?;
    write_u32(&mut bytes, opt + layout::OPT_ADDRESS_OF_ENTRY_POINT, 0)?;
    write_u32(&mut bytes, opt + layout::OPT_CHECKSUM, 0)?;
    let dll_characteristics = info.dll_characteristics & !dll_flags::FORCE_INTEGRITY;
    write_u16(
        &mut bytes,
        opt + layout::OPT_DLL_CHARACTERISTICS,
        dll_characteristics,
    )?;

    // Windows 10 assigns static TLS to the prepared DLL when its empty
    // import table is present. The parser has already walked one descriptor
    // per module up to the null terminator, regardless of the recorded Size.
    if let Some(at) = layout::data_directory_offset(&bytes, dir::IMPORT) {
        let rva = layout::read_u32(&bytes, at).ok_or(PrepareError::Patch("no import RVA"))?;
        if rva != 0 {
            let terminator = u32::try_from(info.imports.len())
                .ok()
                .and_then(|count| count.checked_mul(IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR_SIZE))
                .and_then(|offset| rva.checked_add(offset))
                .ok_or(PrepareError::Patch("import terminator RVA overflow"))?;
            write_u32(&mut bytes, at, terminator)?;
            write_u32(&mut bytes, at + 4, IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR_SIZE)?;
        }
    }
    if let Some(at) = layout::data_directory_offset(&bytes, dir::BOUND_IMPORT) {
        write(&mut bytes, at, &[0; layout::DATA_DIRECTORY_SIZE])?;
    }

    if let Some(tls) = &info.tls
        && tls.callbacks_va != 0
    {
        let at = info
            .rva_to_file_offset(tls.directory_rva)
            .ok_or(PrepareError::Patch("TLS directory is not file-backed"))?;
        write_u64(
            &mut bytes,
            at as usize + layout::TLS64_ADDRESS_OF_CALLBACKS,
            0,
        )?;
        // The field's base relocation would turn the 0 into `delta` whenever
        // the loader maps the copy away from its preferred base (Wine always
        // does for DYNAMIC_BASE images), and the loader then reads callbacks
        // from there. Make that entry a no-op.
        let field_rva = tls.directory_rva + layout::TLS64_ADDRESS_OF_CALLBACKS as u32;
        for (entry, target) in dir64_relocations(&bytes, &info) {
            if target == field_rva {
                write_u16(&mut bytes, entry, 0)?; // IMAGE_REL_BASED_ABSOLUTE
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(PreparedImage {
        info,
        bytes,
        original_hash: blake3::hash(original),
    })
}

/// Size of an IMAGE_IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR in the PE file.
const IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR_SIZE: u32 = 20;

/// Every `IMAGE_REL_BASED_DIR64` base relocation: (file offset of its entry,
/// RVA it patches). Empty if the image has no readable relocation table.
fn dir64_relocations(bytes: &[u8], info: &ImageInfo) -> Vec<(usize, u32)> {
    const DIR64: u16 = 10;
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let Some(d) = layout::data_directory_offset(bytes, dir::BASERELOC) else {
        return out;
    };
    let (Some(rva), Some(size)) = (layout::read_u32(bytes, d), layout::read_u32(bytes, d + 4))
    else {
        return out;
    };
    let Some(start) = info.rva_to_file_offset(rva).filter(|_| size != 0) else {
        return out;
    };
    let (mut at, end) = (start as usize, start as usize + size as usize);
    while at + 8 <= end {
        let (Some(page), Some(block)) =
            (layout::read_u32(bytes, at), layout::read_u32(bytes, at + 4))
        else {
            break;
        };
        let block = block as usize;
        if block < 8 || at + block > end {
            break;
        }
        for entry in (at + 8..at + block).step_by(2) {
            let Some(e) = bytes.get(entry..entry + 2) else {
                break;
            };
            let e = u16::from_le_bytes([e[0], e[1]]);
            if e >> 12 == DIR64 {
                out.push((entry, page + u32::from(e & 0xFFF)));
            }
        }
        at += block;
    }
    out
}

fn write_u16(bytes: &mut [u8], at: usize, v: u16) -> Result<(), PrepareError> {
    write(bytes, at, &v.to_le_bytes())
}
fn write_u32(bytes: &mut [u8], at: usize, v: u32) -> Result<(), PrepareError> {
    write(bytes, at, &v.to_le_bytes())
}
fn write_u64(bytes: &mut [u8], at: usize, v: u64) -> Result<(), PrepareError> {
    write(bytes, at, &v.to_le_bytes())
}
fn write(bytes: &mut [u8], at: usize, v: &[u8]) -> Result<(), PrepareError> {
    bytes
        .get_mut(at..at + v.len())
        .ok_or(PrepareError::Patch("header field outside of file"))?
        .copy_from_slice(v);
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn patches_own_test_binary() {
        let original = std::fs::read(std::env::current_exe().unwrap()).unwrap();
        let prepared = prepare(&original).unwrap();
        assert!(!prepared.info.is_dll(), "info describes the original");
        assert!(prepared.info.import_count() > 0);

        let patched = ImageInfo::parse(&prepared.bytes).unwrap();
        assert!(patched.is_dll());
        assert_eq!(patched.entry_rva, 0);
        assert!(patched.imports.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(patched.dll_characteristics & dll_flags::FORCE_INTEGRITY, 0);
        if let Some(tls) = &patched.tls {
            assert_eq!(tls.callbacks_va, 0);
            let field = tls.directory_rva + layout::TLS64_ADDRESS_OF_CALLBACKS as u32;
            assert!(
                dir64_relocations(&prepared.bytes, &patched)
                    .iter()
                    .all(|&(_, target)| target != field),
                "the cleared callback pointer must not be relocated"
            );
        }
        // Nothing else moved: same sections, same size.
        assert_eq!(patched.sections.len(), prepared.info.sections.len());
        assert_eq!(prepared.bytes.len(), original.len());
    }

    #[test]
    fn keeps_iat_slots_when_import_size_excludes_the_terminator() {
        let mut original = std::fs::read(std::env::current_exe().unwrap()).unwrap();
        let info = ImageInfo::parse(&original).unwrap();
        let directory = layout::data_directory_offset(&original, dir::IMPORT).unwrap();
        // This linker layout counts the descriptors for real modules only.
        let descriptor_bytes = u32::try_from(info.imports.len()).unwrap() * IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR_SIZE;
        write_u32(&mut original, directory + 4, descriptor_bytes).unwrap();
        let prepared = prepare(&original).unwrap();
        let empty = layout::read_u32(&prepared.bytes, directory).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            empty,
            layout::read_u32(&original, directory).unwrap() + descriptor_bytes
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout::read_u32(&prepared.bytes, directory + 4),
            Some(IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR_SIZE)
        );
        let at = info.rva_to_file_offset(empty).unwrap() as usize;
        assert_eq!(
            &prepared.bytes[at..at + IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR_SIZE as usize],
            &[0; 20]
        );
        let iat = layout::data_directory_offset(&original, dir::IAT).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            &prepared.bytes[iat..iat + layout::DATA_DIRECTORY_SIZE],
            &original[iat..iat + layout::DATA_DIRECTORY_SIZE]
        );
        assert_eq!(prepared.info.import_count(), info.import_count());
        for module in &prepared.info.imports {
            for entry in &module.entries {
                let at = info.rva_to_file_offset(entry.iat_slot_rva).unwrap() as usize;
                assert_eq!(&prepared.bytes[at..at + 8], &original[at..at + 8]);
            }
        }
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn windows_assigns_static_tls_to_a_prepared_dll() {
        // Model a title DLL using our own linked image. Loading a DLL leaves
        // its assigned index intact; the executable-specific redirect resets it.
        let mut original = std::fs::read(std::env::current_exe().unwrap()).unwrap();
        let flags =
            layout::file_header_offset(&original).unwrap() + layout::FILE_HEADER_CHARACTERISTICS;
        let characteristics =
            ImageInfo::parse(&original).unwrap().characteristics | file_flags::DLL;
        write_u16(&mut original, flags, characteristics).unwrap();
        let prepared = prepare(&original).unwrap();
        let info = &prepared.info;
        let tls = info.tls.as_ref().expect("the test binary uses static TLS");
        let directory = info.rva_to_file_offset(tls.directory_rva).unwrap() as usize;
        let index_va = layout::read_u64(&original, directory + 16).unwrap();
        let index_rva = index_va.checked_sub(info.image_base).unwrap();
        assert!(index_rva + 4 <= u64::from(info.size_of_image));

        let folder = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let image = crate::load(&prepared, folder.path()).unwrap();
        // SAFETY: the mapped test image contains the checked DWORD above.
        let assigned =
            unsafe { ((image.base() + index_rva as usize) as *const u32).read_unaligned() };
        // SAFETY: the prepared DLL has never been attached or given to a caller.
        unsafe { image.unload() };
        assert_ne!(
            assigned, 0,
            "the process executable already owns TLS slot zero"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_name_is_stable_per_build() {
        let original = std::fs::read(std::env::current_exe().unwrap()).unwrap();
        let a = prepare(&original).unwrap();
        let b = prepare(&original).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.file_name(), b.file_name());
    }
}

`crates/victory-loader/src/stacks.rs`:

```rs
//! Where every thread is: `VICTORY_STACKS=<seconds>[,<seconds>...]` prints
//! each thread's unwound stack as `module+rva` that many seconds after
//! [`dump_stacks_on_schedule`], to find what a title waits on.

use std::ffi::c_void;

use windows_sys::Wdk::System::Threading::{
    NtQueryInformationThread, ThreadBasicInformation, ThreadQuerySetWin32StartAddress,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{CloseHandle, HANDLE, INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE, LocalFree};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::{
    CONTEXT, CONTEXT_FULL_AMD64, GetThreadContext,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::ToolHelp::{
    CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, THREADENTRY32, Thread32First, Thread32Next,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
    GetCurrentProcessId, GetCurrentThreadId, GetThreadDescription, OpenThread, ResumeThread,
    SuspendThread, THREAD_GET_CONTEXT, THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION, THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME,
};

use crate::crash::{MAX_FRAMES, locate, unwind_into};

/// Reads `VICTORY_STACKS` and, if set, starts a thread that prints every
/// thread's stack at each listed time (seconds from now).
pub fn dump_stacks_on_schedule() {
    let Ok(list) = std::env::var("VICTORY_STACKS") else {
        return;
    };
    let mut times: Vec<f64> = list
        .split(',')
        .filter_map(|t| t.trim().parse().ok())
        .collect();
    times.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);
    let start = std::time::Instant::now();
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        for t in times {
            let at = std::time::Duration::from_secs_f64(t.max(0.0));
            std::thread::sleep(at.saturating_sub(start.elapsed()));
            dump_stacks();
        }
    });
}

/// `THREAD_BASIC_INFORMATION` (ntddk).
#[repr(C)]
struct BasicInfo {
    exit_status: i32,
    teb: *const usize,
    client_id: [usize; 2],
    affinity: usize,
    priority: i32,
    base_priority: i32,
}

/// `GetThreadContext` wants a 16-byte aligned context.
#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct Aligned(CONTEXT);

/// Prints every other thread's stack to stderr. Each thread is suspended
/// only while its context is read and unwound into a buffer allocated
/// beforehand (it may hold the heap lock).
pub fn dump_stacks() {
    // SAFETY: plain queries and a snapshot of this process's threads.
    let (me, process, snapshot) = unsafe {
        (
            GetCurrentThreadId(),
            GetCurrentProcessId(),
            CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, 0),
        )
    };
    if snapshot == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE {
        return;
    }
    let mut ids = Vec::new();
    // SAFETY: zeroed is a valid THREADENTRY32; its size is set before use.
    let mut entry: THREADENTRY32 = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    entry.dwSize = size_of::<THREADENTRY32>() as u32;
    // SAFETY: `snapshot` is open; `entry` is sized.
    let mut more = unsafe { Thread32First(snapshot, &mut entry) } != 0;
    while more {
        if entry.th32OwnerProcessID == process && entry.th32ThreadID != me {
            ids.push(entry.th32ThreadID);
        }
        // SAFETY: as above.
        more = unsafe { Thread32Next(snapshot, &mut entry) } != 0;
    }
    // SAFETY: we opened it.
    unsafe { CloseHandle(snapshot) };
    eprintln!("VIctory: stacks of {} threads", ids.len());
    for id in ids {
        // SAFETY: opens a thread of our own process.
        let thread = unsafe {
            OpenThread(
                THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME | THREAD_GET_CONTEXT | THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION,
                0,
                id,
            )
        };
        if thread.is_null() {
            continue;
        }
        let (frames, (priority, base)) = frames_of(thread);
        eprintln!(
            "  thread {id} \"{}\" start {} priority {priority} (base {base})",
            name_of(thread),
            locate(start_of(thread))
        );
        for (i, pc) in frames.into_iter().enumerate() {
            eprintln!("    #{i:<2} {}", locate(pc as usize));
        }
        // SAFETY: we opened it.
        unsafe { CloseHandle(thread) };
    }
}

/// The thread's frames and its current and base scheduling priority (0-31).
fn frames_of(thread: HANDLE) -> (Vec<u64>, (i32, i32)) {
    let mut frames = Vec::with_capacity(MAX_FRAMES);
    let mut info: BasicInfo = BasicInfo {
        exit_status: 0,
        teb: std::ptr::null(),
        client_id: [0; 2],
        affinity: 0,
        priority: 0,
        base_priority: 0,
    };
    // SAFETY: writes `info`, whose layout and size are the system's.
    let status = unsafe {
        NtQueryInformationThread(
            thread,
            ThreadBasicInformation,
            (&raw mut info).cast(),
            size_of::<BasicInfo>() as u32,
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
        )
    };
    if status != 0 || info.teb.is_null() {
        return (frames, (0, 0));
    }
    // SAFETY: the TEB of a live thread of this process: its NT_TIB holds
    // the stack base at +8 and the stack limit at +0x10.
    let (high, low) = unsafe { (info.teb.add(1).read(), info.teb.add(2).read()) };
    // SAFETY: zeroed is a valid CONTEXT.
    let mut context = Aligned(unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() });
    context.0.ContextFlags = CONTEXT_FULL_AMD64;
    // SAFETY: suspends, reads and resumes a thread that is not this one;
    // nothing between suspend and resume allocates or takes a lock the
    // thread could hold besides the unwinder's own.
    unsafe {
        if SuspendThread(thread) == u32::MAX {
            return (frames, (info.priority, info.base_priority));
        }
        if GetThreadContext(thread, &mut context.0) != 0 {
            unwind_into(context.0, low, high, &mut frames);
        }
        ResumeThread(thread);
    }
    (frames, (info.priority, info.base_priority))
}

fn start_of(thread: HANDLE) -> usize {
    let mut start = 0usize;
    // SAFETY: writes one pointer-sized start address.
    unsafe {
        NtQueryInformationThread(
            thread,
            ThreadQuerySetWin32StartAddress,
            (&raw mut start).cast(),
            size_of::<usize>() as u32,
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
        )
    };
    start
}

fn name_of(thread: HANDLE) -> String {
    let mut name = std::ptr::null_mut();
    // SAFETY: the system allocates the string; we free it with LocalFree.
    unsafe {
        if GetThreadDescription(thread, &mut name) < 0 || name.is_null() {
            return String::new();
        }
        let len = (0..).take_while(|&i| *name.add(i) != 0).count();
        let text = String::from_utf16_lossy(std::slice::from_raw_parts(name, len));
        LocalFree(name.cast::<c_void>());
        text
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn another_threads_stack_unwinds_to_its_start() {
        let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
        let (stop_tx, stop_rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<()>();
        let parked = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            // SAFETY: plain query.
            tx.send(unsafe { GetCurrentThreadId() }).unwrap();
            stop_rx.recv().ok();
        });
        let id = rx.recv().unwrap();
        // SAFETY: a thread of this process.
        let thread = unsafe {
            OpenThread(
                THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME | THREAD_GET_CONTEXT | THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION,
                0,
                id,
            )
        };
        assert!(!thread.is_null());
        let (frames, _) = frames_of(thread);
        // Waiting in the kernel, several frames down from the thread start.
        assert!(frames.len() >= 3, "{frames:?}");
        assert!(start_of(thread) != 0);
        // SAFETY: opened above.
        unsafe { CloseHandle(thread) };
        dump_stacks();
        stop_tx.send(()).unwrap();
        parked.join().unwrap();
    }
}
