`crates/victory-loader/src/threads.rs`:

```rs
//! Thread notices for title images. The prepared copies have no entry point
//! and no TLS callbacks, so the Windows loader tells them nothing when a
//! thread starts or ends. Our own TLS callback, which Windows calls on every
//! thread of the process whoever created it (title, host CRT or our
//! runtime), passes each notice on to every attached image: its TLS
//! callbacks, then a DLL's `DllMain`.

use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU32, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use crate::{DLL_PROCESS_DETACH, LoadedImage};

const DLL_THREAD_ATTACH: u32 = 2;
const DLL_THREAD_DETACH: u32 = 3;

struct Mapped {
    image: Arc<LoadedImage>,
    /// Its `DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH` is done; only then does it get thread notices.
    attached: bool,
    /// `DisableThreadLibraryCalls`: no more `DllMain` thread notices.
    quiet: bool,
}

/// Every title image we mapped, in load order.
static IMAGES: Mutex<Vec<Mapped>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());

fn images() -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'static, Vec<Mapped>> {
    IMAGES.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

pub(crate) fn mapped(image: &LoadedImage) {
    // SAFETY: reads our own static, so the linker keeps it (and its section).
    unsafe { std::ptr::from_ref(&ON_THREAD).read_volatile() };
    let image = Arc::new(image.clone());
    let mut images = images();
    images.retain(|m| m.image.base() != image.base());
    images.push(Mapped {
        image,
        attached: false,
        quiet: false,
    });
}

/// Its `DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH` is done. The list keeps attach order, which is
/// the Windows loader's initialisation order.
pub(crate) fn attached(base: usize) {
    let mut images = images();
    if let Some(i) = images.iter().position(|m| m.image.base() == base) {
        let mut m = images.remove(i);
        m.attached = true;
        images.push(m);
    }
    static AT_EXIT: std::sync::Once = std::sync::Once::new();
    // Registered before the title's own exit functions, so it runs after
    // them, as `ExitProcess` follows `exit`'s functions on Windows.
    // SAFETY: registers a function with the host CRT's exit table.
    AT_EXIT.call_once(|| unsafe {
        atexit(detach_all);
    });
}

pub(crate) fn detached(base: usize) {
    if let Some(m) = images().iter_mut().find(|m| m.image.base() == base) {
        m.attached = false;
    }
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn atexit(f: extern "C" fn()) -> i32;
}

/// Set once the process is ending: no more thread notices.
static EXITING: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

/// How long title images may take to detach before the process ends anyway
/// (a thread ended while holding a lock their detach code wants).
const DETACH_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);

/// Process exit (the CRT's `exit`, which titles call), in `ExitProcess`'s
/// order: the title's exit functions have run; every other thread ends
/// (title threads and ours); every attached image gets
/// `DLL_PROCESS_DETACH`, DLLs in reverse initialisation order, then the
/// exe's TLS callbacks; then the CRT ends the process.
extern "C" fn detach_all() {
    let attached: Vec<_> = images()
        .iter_mut()
        .filter(|m| m.attached)
        .map(|m| {
            m.attached = false;
            m.image.clone()
        })
        .collect();
    let (dlls, exes): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) =
        attached.into_iter().rev().partition(|i| i.info().is_dll());
    tracing::info!(
        images = dlls.len() + exes.len(),
        "process exit: ending other threads, detaching title images"
    );
    EXITING.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
    // As on Windows, a lock a thread held when it ended stays taken; detach
    // code that waits for one would hang the exit. The watchdog runs before
    // the other threads end: a thread that ends can hold the heap lock or
    // the loader lock, and a new thread needs both to start. After the
    // deadline it only ends the process; it does not log, because logging
    // needs the heap and the log writer's lock.
    // Its thread id, set when it runs its own code; 0 until then.
    static WATCHDOG: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
    drop(std::thread::spawn(|| {
        // SAFETY: a plain query of the calling thread.
        let id = unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentThreadId() };
        WATCHDOG.store(id, Ordering::SeqCst);
        std::thread::sleep(DETACH_DEADLINE);
        end_process();
    }));
    // Its start (loader notices, Rust's thread set-up) is done only when
    // it runs its own code. The loader notices need the loader lock. This
    // thread can hold it, or a thread that waits for this thread can hold
    // it. Then the watchdog does not start, so this wait has the same
    // deadline.
    let waiting = Instant::now();
    let watchdog = loop {
        match WATCHDOG.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            0 if waiting.elapsed() >= DETACH_DEADLINE => end_process(),
            0 => std::thread::yield_now(),
            id => break id,
        }
    };
    end_other_threads(&[watchdog]);
    for image in dlls.iter().chain(&exes) {
        // SAFETY: attached images are bound. A non-null third argument
        // tells the entry points the process is ending.
        unsafe {
            image.notify(
                DLL_PROCESS_DETACH,
                true,
                std::ptr::without_provenance_mut(1),
            )
        };
    }
}

/// Ends this process when the title images do not detach in time. It does
/// not use the heap or any lock: a thread that ended can hold them.
fn end_process() {
    // SAFETY: ends this process, which is exiting anyway.
    unsafe {
        windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::TerminateProcess(
            windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcess(),
            1,
        )
    };
}

/// Ends every thread of the process but this one and those in `keep` (and
/// the ones started while doing so), as `ExitProcess` does first; except
/// the system's thread-pool workers, which `TerminateThread` refuses (the
/// process fails fast) and which run no title code (no title image uses
/// that pool).
fn end_other_threads(keep: &[u32]) {
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{CloseHandle, INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::ToolHelp::{
        CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, THREADENTRY32, Thread32First, Thread32Next,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
        GetCurrentProcessId, GetCurrentThreadId, OpenThread, THREAD_TERMINATE, TerminateThread,
        THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION,
    };
    // SAFETY: plain queries of the calling process and thread.
    let (process, me) = unsafe { (GetCurrentProcessId(), GetCurrentThreadId()) };
    let mut ended = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    loop {
        // SAFETY: a snapshot of every thread, walked with a sized entry.
        let others: Vec<u32> = unsafe {
            let snapshot = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, 0);
            if snapshot == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE {
                break;
            }
            let mut entry = THREADENTRY32 {
                dwSize: size_of::<THREADENTRY32>() as u32,
                ..std::mem::zeroed()
            };
            let mut ids = Vec::new();
            let mut more = Thread32First(snapshot, &mut entry) != 0;
            while more {
                if entry.th32OwnerProcessID == process
                    && entry.th32ThreadID != me
                    && !keep.contains(&entry.th32ThreadID)
                {
                    ids.push(entry.th32ThreadID);
                }
                more = Thread32Next(snapshot, &mut entry) != 0;
            }
            CloseHandle(snapshot);
            ids
        };
        let new: Vec<u32> = others.into_iter().filter(|id| ended.insert(*id)).collect();
        if new.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        for id in new {
            // SAFETY: a thread of this process, which is exiting.
            unsafe {
                let thread = OpenThread(THREAD_TERMINATE | THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION, 0, id);
                if !thread.is_null() {
                    if !starts_in(thread, c"ntdll.dll") {
                        TerminateThread(thread, 0);
                    }
                    CloseHandle(thread);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn unmapped(base: usize) {
    images().retain(|m| m.image.base() != base);
}

/// `DisableThreadLibraryCalls` for a title image; `None` if `base` is not
/// one. Fails, as on Windows, for an image with static TLS.
pub fn disable_thread_calls(base: usize) -> Option<bool> {
    let mut images = images();
    let m = images.iter_mut().find(|m| m.image.base() == base)?;
    if m.image.info().tls.is_some() {
        return Some(false);
    }
    m.quiet = true;
    Some(true)
}

/// Windows calls every pointer between the CRT's markers `.CRT$XLA` and
/// `.CRT$XLZ`; `XLAV` sorts ahead of the usual `XLB`, so ours runs before
/// any other callback linked into the exe.
#[used]
#[unsafe(link_section = ".CRT$XLAV")]
static ON_THREAD: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, u32, *mut c_void) = on_thread;

unsafe extern "system" fn on_thread(_: *mut c_void, reason: u32, _: *mut c_void) {
    if reason != DLL_THREAD_ATTACH && reason != DLL_THREAD_DETACH {
        return;
    }
    if EXITING.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
        return; // our exit watchdog, or threads ending with the process
    }
    // A snapshot: title code may map and attach another DLL from here.
    let notify: Vec<_> = images()
        .iter()
        .filter(|m| m.attached)
        .map(|m| (m.image.clone(), !m.quiet))
        .collect();
    if notify.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    // Rust's std sets its threads up after this callback and aborts the
    // process if their per-thread state was touched first (the current
    // thread's id, which our logging asks for when title code calls us).
    // That state is put back as the thread started.
    let saved = (reason == DLL_THREAD_ATTACH && started_by_rust()).then(OwnTls::save);
    // Starts in load order, ends in reverse, as the Windows loader does.
    let notify_one = |(image, dll_main): &(Arc<LoadedImage>, bool)| {
        // SAFETY: attached images have their imports bound.
        unsafe { image.notify(reason, *dll_main, std::ptr::null_mut()) };
    };
    if reason == DLL_THREAD_ATTACH {
        notify.iter().for_each(notify_one);
    } else {
        notify.iter().rev().for_each(notify_one);
    }
    if let Some(saved) = saved {
        saved.restore();
    }
}

/// Our own image's static TLS block on this thread (Rust's std keeps its
/// per-thread state there), as copied before title code ran.
struct OwnTls {
    block: *mut u8,
    saved: Vec<u8>,
}

/// The TLS directory the linker emits for our image (the CRT's symbol).
#[repr(C)]
struct TlsDirectory {
    start: usize,
    end: usize,
    index: *const u32,
    callbacks: usize,
    zero_fill: u32,
    characteristics: u32,
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    static _tls_used: TlsDirectory;
}

impl OwnTls {
    fn save() -> OwnTls {
        let array: *const *mut u8;
        // SAFETY: reads TEB.ThreadLocalStoragePointer; the directory is our
        // image's, and Windows set up its block on this thread before
        // calling TLS callbacks.
        let (block, len) = unsafe {
            std::arch::asm!("mov {}, gs:[0x58]", out(reg) array, options(nostack, readonly));
            let dir = &raw const _tls_used;
            let block = *array.add((*dir).index.read() as usize);
            (block, (*dir).end - (*dir).start + (*dir).zero_fill as usize)
        };
        // SAFETY: the block is `len` bytes, live for the thread's life.
        let saved = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(block, len) }.to_vec();
        OwnTls { block, saved }
    }

    fn restore(self) {
        // SAFETY: the same block on the same thread, no reference to it held.
        unsafe { std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(self.saved.as_ptr(), self.block, self.saved.len()) };
    }
}

/// Whether Rust's std started this thread (its start routine is in our
/// exe): the title's main thread and our runtime's workers, which run
/// title callbacks.
fn started_by_rust() -> bool {
    // SAFETY: the calling thread's pseudo handle.
    starts_in(unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentThread() }, c"")
}

/// Whether `thread`'s start routine lies in the module named `module`
/// (empty: our exe).
fn starts_in(thread: windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::HANDLE, module: &std::ffi::CStr) -> bool {
    use windows_sys::Wdk::System::Threading::{
        NtQueryInformationThread, ThreadQuerySetWin32StartAddress,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::{
        GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS, GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT,
        GetModuleHandleA, GetModuleHandleExW,
    };

    let mut start = 0usize;
    // SAFETY: writes one pointer-sized start address.
    let status = unsafe {
        NtQueryInformationThread(
            thread,
            ThreadQuerySetWin32StartAddress,
            (&raw mut start).cast(),
            size_of::<usize>() as u32,
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
        )
    };
    let mut found = std::ptr::null_mut();
    let name = if module.is_empty() {
        std::ptr::null()
    } else {
        module.as_ptr().cast()
    };
    // SAFETY: looks up the module containing an address, taking no reference.
    status == 0
        && unsafe {
            GetModuleHandleExW(
                GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS | GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT,
                start as *const u16,
                &mut found,
            )
        } != 0
        // SAFETY: a module handle by name (or our exe's); no reference taken.
        && found == unsafe { GetModuleHandleA(name) }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, AtomicU64, Ordering};
    use std::time::Duration;

    /// A thread that counts in `ticks` until it ends; returns its thread id
    /// when it has counted once.
    fn busy(ticks: &'static AtomicU64) -> u32 {
        static ID: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
        ID.store(0, Ordering::SeqCst);
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            // SAFETY: a plain query of the calling thread.
            let id = unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentThreadId() };
            ID.store(id, Ordering::SeqCst);
            loop {
                ticks.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                std::thread::yield_now();
            }
        });
        while ticks.load(Ordering::SeqCst) == 0 {
            std::thread::yield_now();
        }
        ID.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
    }

    /// Whether `ticks` stays the same for a short time.
    fn stopped(ticks: &AtomicU64) -> bool {
        let at = ticks.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
        ticks.load(Ordering::SeqCst) == at
    }

    /// In a child process of the next test: ends the other threads but one
    /// kept thread, and checks that a busy thread stopped and the kept one
    /// did not.
    #[test]
    fn exit_child() {
        if std::env::var_os("VICTORY_EXIT_CHILD").is_none() {
            return;
        }
        static ENDS: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
        static KEPT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
        busy(&ENDS);
        let kept = busy(&KEPT);
        super::end_other_threads(&[kept]);
        let ended = stopped(&ENDS);
        let still_running = !stopped(&KEPT);
        // The test harness's threads are gone too: leave at once.
        println!(
            "{} {}",
            if ended { "ENDED" } else { "STILL RUNNING" },
            if still_running { "KEPT" } else { "NOT KEPT" }
        );
        std::process::exit(0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn exit_ends_the_other_threads_first() {
        let out = std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
            .args(["--exact", "threads::tests::exit_child", "--nocapture"])
            .env("VICTORY_EXIT_CHILD", "1")
            .output()
            .unwrap();
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout);
        assert!(
            out.status.success() && text.contains("ENDED KEPT"),
            "{text}"
        );
    }
}

`crates/victory-loader/src/thunks.rs`:

```rs
//! Stubs for imports nobody implements yet.
//!
//! Each unresolved import gets 32 bytes of generated code:
//!
//! ```text
//! mov rcx, <&'static ImportSite>   ; 48 B9 imm64
//! mov rax, <unimplemented_import>  ; 48 B8 imm64
//! jmp rax                          ; FF E0
//! ```
//!
//! The jump keeps the title's return address on the stack, so the handler
//! returns straight to the caller. Bring-up then shows exactly which API to
//! implement next, rather than failing at load time.

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

use anyhow::{Result, bail};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::{
    DebugBreak, FlushInstructionCache, IsDebuggerPresent,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
    MEM_COMMIT, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, PAGE_READWRITE, VirtualAlloc, VirtualProtect,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcess;

/// What an unimplemented import does when called.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum UnimplementedPolicy {
    /// Log, break into an attached debugger, then abort. The default:
    /// silently continuing usually crashes later and further from the cause.
    #[default]
    Trap,
    /// Log once per import and return 0. Useful to push through bring-up.
    ReturnZero,
}

/// Identifies one unresolved import. Leaked: lives as long as the process.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ImportSite {
    pub dll: String,
    pub symbol: String,
    pub policy: UnimplementedPolicy,
    pub calls: AtomicU64,
}

static UNIMPLEMENTED_CALLS: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);

/// Total number of calls that reached an unimplemented-import stub.
pub fn unimplemented_call_count() -> u64 {
    UNIMPLEMENTED_CALLS.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

extern "system" fn unimplemented_import(site: &'static ImportSite) -> u64 {
    UNIMPLEMENTED_CALLS.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    let previous = site.calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    match site.policy {
        UnimplementedPolicy::ReturnZero => {
            if previous == 0 {
                tracing::warn!(dll = %site.dll, symbol = %site.symbol, "unimplemented import called, returning 0");
            }
            0
        }
        UnimplementedPolicy::Trap => {
            tracing::error!(dll = %site.dll, symbol = %site.symbol, "unimplemented import called");
            // Into the crash log too: `abort` ends the process without
            // running the handlers that write it.
            let (dll, symbol) = (&site.dll, &site.symbol);
            let text = format!("VIctory: unimplemented import {dll}!{symbol} called");
            crate::log_crash(&text);
            // SAFETY: plain Win32 calls without preconditions.
            unsafe {
                if IsDebuggerPresent() != 0 {
                    DebugBreak();
                }
            }
            std::process::abort();
        }
    }
}

const THUNK_SIZE: usize = 32;

/// Executable memory holding one stub per unresolved import.
pub(crate) struct ThunkBlock {
    base: *mut u8,
    len: usize,
    used: usize,
}

impl ThunkBlock {
    /// Reserves room for `count` stubs (writable until [`Self::seal`]).
    pub(crate) fn new(count: usize) -> Result<Self> {
        let len = (count.max(1) * THUNK_SIZE).next_multiple_of(4096);
        // SAFETY: fresh anonymous allocation; no existing memory is touched.
        let base = unsafe {
            VirtualAlloc(
                std::ptr::null(),
                len,
                MEM_COMMIT | MEM_RESERVE,
                PAGE_READWRITE,
            )
        } as *mut u8;
        if base.is_null() {
            bail!(
                "VirtualAlloc for import stubs failed: {}",
                std::io::Error::last_os_error()
            );
        }
        Ok(ThunkBlock { base, len, used: 0 })
    }

    /// Emits a stub for `site` and returns its address.
    pub(crate) fn emit(&mut self, site: &'static ImportSite) -> Result<usize> {
        if self.used + THUNK_SIZE > self.len {
            bail!("import stub block is full");
        }
        let mut code = [0xCC_u8; THUNK_SIZE]; // int3 padding
        code[0..2].copy_from_slice(&[0x48, 0xB9]);
        code[2..10].copy_from_slice(&(site as *const ImportSite as u64).to_le_bytes());
        code[10..12].copy_from_slice(&[0x48, 0xB8]);
        let handler = unimplemented_import as extern "system" fn(&'static ImportSite) -> u64;
        code[12..20].copy_from_slice(&(handler as *const () as u64).to_le_bytes());
        code[20..22].copy_from_slice(&[0xFF, 0xE0]);
        // SAFETY: `used + THUNK_SIZE <= len`, and the block is still writable.
        let at = unsafe {
            let at = self.base.add(self.used);
            std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(code.as_ptr(), at, THUNK_SIZE);
            at
        };
        self.used += THUNK_SIZE;
        Ok(at as usize)
    }

    /// Makes the block read+execute. The block is intentionally leaked:
    /// title code may hold these addresses for the life of the process.
    pub(crate) fn seal(self) -> Result<()> {
        let mut old = 0;
        // SAFETY: `base..base+len` is the allocation made in `new`.
        let ok = unsafe { VirtualProtect(self.base as _, self.len, PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, &mut old) };
        if ok == 0 {
            bail!(
                "VirtualProtect for import stubs failed: {}",
                std::io::Error::last_os_error()
            );
        }
        // SAFETY: flushing our own process's instruction cache for our own block.
        unsafe { FlushInstructionCache(GetCurrentProcess(), self.base as _, self.len) };
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// In a child process of the next test: calls an unimplemented import
    /// that traps, with the crash log where `VICTORY_TRAP_LOG` says.
    #[test]
    fn trap_child() {
        let Some(log) = std::env::var_os("VICTORY_TRAP_LOG") else {
            return;
        };
        crate::log_crashes_to(log.into());
        let site = Box::leak(Box::new(ImportSite {
            dll: "probe.dll".into(),
            symbol: "Missing".into(),
            policy: UnimplementedPolicy::Trap,
            calls: AtomicU64::new(0),
        }));
        unimplemented_import(site);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_trapped_import_is_in_the_crash_log() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let log = dir.path().join("crashes.log");
        let out = std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
            .args(["--exact", "thunks::tests::trap_child", "--nocapture"])
            .env("VICTORY_TRAP_LOG", &log)
            .output()
            .unwrap();
        assert!(!out.status.success(), "the trap ends the process");
        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&log).unwrap_or_default();
        let named = text.contains("VIctory: unimplemented import probe.dll!Missing called");
        assert!(named, "crash log: {text:?}");
    }
}

`crates/victory-loader/src/tls.rs`:

```rs
//! Static TLS of an executable mapped as a DLL.
//!
//! An exe always gets TLS index 0, so title code reaches its thread-local
//! block as `mov r64, gs:[0x58]` (the thread's TLS array) followed by
//! `[r64]`, without reading `_tls_index`. Mapped as a DLL, the image gets
//! another index. Every such load is turned into a call to a thunk that
//! yields `&array[index]` instead, and the image's `_tls_index` (which CRT
//! code does read, and adds to the array pointer) is set to 0.

use std::ffi::c_void;

use anyhow::{Result, bail};
use victory_pe::ImageInfo;
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::FlushInstructionCache;
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
    MEM_COMMIT, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, PAGE_READWRITE,
    VirtualAlloc, VirtualProtect,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcess;

const SCN_MEM_EXECUTE: u32 = 0x2000_0000;
const TLS64_ADDRESS_OF_INDEX: usize = 16;
/// `mov r64, gs:[0x58]` is `65 REX 8B ModRM 25 58 00 00 00`.
const LOAD_LEN: usize = 9;
const THUNK_SIZE: usize = 32;

/// Redirects the image's TLS-array loads if the OS gave it an index other
/// than 0. Returns the number of loads patched.
///
/// # Safety
/// `base` is the image `info` describes, mapped and not yet running.
pub(crate) unsafe fn redirect(base: usize, info: &ImageInfo) -> Result<usize> {
    let Some(tls) = &info.tls else { return Ok(0) };
    // SAFETY: the TLS directory and the index it points to are in the image;
    // the OS relocated the pointer and wrote the index.
    let index_at = unsafe {
        ((base + tls.directory_rva as usize + TLS64_ADDRESS_OF_INDEX) as *const usize).read()
    } as *mut u32;
    // SAFETY: as above.
    let index = unsafe { index_at.read() };
    if index == 0 {
        return Ok(0);
    }
    let thunks = thunks(near(base, info.size_of_image as usize)?, index)?;
    let mut patched = 0;
    for section in info
        .sections
        .iter()
        .filter(|s| s.characteristics & SCN_MEM_EXECUTE != 0)
    {
        let start = base + section.rva as usize;
        let len = section.virtual_size as usize;
        let mut old = 0;
        // SAFETY: the section is part of the mapped image.
        if unsafe { VirtualProtect(start as _, len, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, &mut old) } == 0 {
            bail!(
                "VirtualProtect(code) failed: {}",
                std::io::Error::last_os_error()
            );
        }
        // SAFETY: writable now, and no title code runs yet.
        let code = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(start as *mut u8, len) };
        patched += patch(code, start, thunks);
        // SAFETY: restoring the protection we changed; flushing our own code.
        unsafe {
            VirtualProtect(start as _, len, old, &mut old);
            FlushInstructionCache(GetCurrentProcess(), start as _, len);
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: see `index_at`; `.data` is writable.
    unsafe { index_at.write(0) };
    tracing::info!(index, patched, "static TLS redirected");
    Ok(patched)
}

/// Rewrites each `mov r64, gs:[0x58]` in `code` (at address `at`) as
/// `call thunks[r]; nop4`. `thunks` must be within 2 GiB of `code`.
fn patch(code: &mut [u8], at: usize, thunks: usize) -> usize {
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i + LOAD_LEN <= code.len() {
        let c = &code[i..i + LOAD_LEN];
        let rex = c[1];
        let reg = usize::from((c[3] >> 3) & 7) | if rex & 4 != 0 { 8 } else { 0 };
        // shortcut: a byte match, not a decode. In the title all
        // 53,246 hits are instruction starts and none is missed (checked
        // against a full disassembly); decode .text if a title shows one.
        if c[0] == 0x65
            && (rex == 0x48 || rex == 0x4C)
            && c[2] == 0x8B
            && c[3] & 0xC7 == 0x04
            && c[4..] == [0x25, 0x58, 0, 0, 0]
            && reg != 4
        {
            let rel = (thunks + reg * THUNK_SIZE) as i64 - (at + i + 5) as i64;
            code[i] = 0xE8;
            code[i + 1..i + 5].copy_from_slice(&(rel as i32).to_le_bytes());
            code[i + 5..i + 9].copy_from_slice(&[0x0F, 0x1F, 0x40, 0x00]);
            count += 1;
            i += LOAD_LEN;
        } else {
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    count
}

/// Fills `block` with one thunk per register: `mov r, gs:[0x58];
/// lea r, [r + index * 8]; ret` (flags untouched, like the load it replaces).
fn thunks(block: *mut u8, index: u32) -> Result<usize> {
    let disp = (index * 8).to_le_bytes();
    for reg in 0..16u8 {
        let (r, low) = (reg >> 3, reg & 7);
        let mut code = vec![0x65, 0x48 | r << 2, 0x8B, low << 3 | 4, 0x25, 0x58, 0, 0, 0];
        code.extend([0x48 | r << 2 | r, 0x8D, 0x80 | low << 3 | low]);
        if low == 4 {
            code.push(0x24); // SIB: [r12 + disp32]
        }
        code.extend(disp);
        code.push(0xC3);
        // SAFETY: `block` holds 16 thunks and is still writable.
        unsafe {
            std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(
                code.as_ptr(),
                block.add(usize::from(reg) * THUNK_SIZE),
                code.len(),
            )
        };
    }
    let mut old = 0;
    // SAFETY: `block` is our allocation of one page.
    if unsafe { VirtualProtect(block as _, 4096, PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, &mut old) } == 0 {
        bail!(
            "VirtualProtect(TLS thunks) failed: {}",
            std::io::Error::last_os_error()
        );
    }
    Ok(block as usize)
}

/// One writable page within `rel32` reach of `[base, base + size)`. Leaked:
/// title code calls into it for the life of the process.
fn near(base: usize, size: usize) -> Result<*mut u8> {
    const GRANULE: usize = 0x1_0000;
    // The search spans 1 GiB each side, so every call site stays in reach.
    if size >= 1 << 30 {
        bail!("image too large for TLS thunks within rel32 reach");
    }
    let above = (base + size).next_multiple_of(GRANULE);
    for k in 0..(1usize << 14) {
        for hint in [
            base.checked_sub((k + 1) * GRANULE),
            Some(above + k * GRANULE),
        ] {
            let Some(hint) = hint else { continue };
            // SAFETY: a fresh allocation at a free address, or null.
            let p = unsafe {
                VirtualAlloc(
                    hint as *const c_void,
                    4096,
                    MEM_COMMIT | MEM_RESERVE,
                    PAGE_READWRITE,
                )
            };
            if !p.is_null() {
                return Ok(p.cast());
            }
        }
    }
    bail!("no free page near the image for TLS thunks")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Reads the thread's TLS array pointer the way title code does.
    fn tls_array() -> usize {
        let array: usize;
        // SAFETY: reads TEB.ThreadLocalStoragePointer.
        unsafe { std::arch::asm!("mov {}, gs:[0x58]", out(reg) array) };
        array
    }

    #[test]
    fn loads_become_calls_that_yield_the_title_slot() {
        let page = near(tls_array as *const () as usize, 0).unwrap();
        let thunks = thunks(near(page as usize, 4096).unwrap(), 3).unwrap();
        // (before the load, REX, ModRM, after the load): each case returns
        // the loaded register in rax; r12 is saved, being callee-saved.
        let cases: [(&[u8], u8, u8, &[u8]); 3] = [
            (&[], 0x48, 0x04, &[0xC3]),                   // rax
            (&[], 0x4C, 0x04, &[0x4C, 0x89, 0xC0, 0xC3]), // r8
            (
                &[0x41, 0x54],
                0x4C,
                0x24,
                &[0x4C, 0x89, 0xE0, 0x41, 0x5C, 0xC3],
            ), // r12
        ];
        for (before, rex, modrm, after) in cases {
            let mut code = before.to_vec();
            code.extend([0x65, rex, 0x8B, modrm, 0x25, 0x58, 0, 0, 0]);
            code.extend(after);
            // SAFETY: the page is ours and writable.
            let bytes = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(page, code.len()) };
            bytes.copy_from_slice(&code);
            assert_eq!(patch(bytes, page as usize, thunks), 1);
            let mut old = 0;
            // SAFETY: our page, made executable to run the patched code.
            unsafe { VirtualProtect(page as _, 4096, PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, &mut old) };
            // SAFETY: the page holds the patched load and a return.
            let f: extern "system" fn() -> usize = unsafe { std::mem::transmute(page) };
            assert_eq!(f(), tls_array() + 3 * 8, "REX {rex:#x} ModRM {modrm:#x}");
            // SAFETY: our page again.
            unsafe { VirtualProtect(page as _, 4096, PAGE_READWRITE, &mut old) };
        }
    }
}

`crates/victory-loader/src/windows.rs`:

```rs
//! Loading a prepared image as a real Windows module and binding it.

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::ffi::{CString, c_void};
use std::os::windows::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64;

use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};
use victory_pe::{ImageInfo, ImportSymbol};
use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{FreeLibrary, HMODULE};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::{GetProcAddress, LoadLibraryExW};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{PAGE_READWRITE, VirtualProtect};

use crate::thunks::{ImportSite, ThunkBlock, UnimplementedPolicy};
use crate::{
    DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH, DLL_PROCESS_DETACH, ImportResolver, PreparedImage, Provenance, Resolution,
    prepare,
};

/// A title image mapped into this process. A clone names the same mapping
/// (no reference of its own): unload one copy only.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LoadedImage {
    module: HMODULE,
    path: PathBuf,
    info: ImageInfo,
}

// SAFETY: HMODULE is a process-wide handle (the base address); using it from
// any thread is fine.
unsafe impl Send for LoadedImage {}
// SAFETY: as above; `LoadedImage` has no interior mutability.
unsafe impl Sync for LoadedImage {}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MissingImport {
    pub dll: String,
    pub symbol: String,
}

/// Outcome of [`LoadedImage::bind_imports`].
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct BindReport {
    pub hle: usize,
    pub host: usize,
    pub title: usize,
    pub missing: Vec<MissingImport>,
}

/// Writes the prepared copy into `dir` and maps it with the Windows loader.
///
/// `dir` receives derived game data, so it must be outside the repository.
pub fn load(prepared: &PreparedImage, dir: &Path) -> Result<LoadedImage> {
    victory_core::ensure_outside_repo(dir)?;
    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).with_context(|| format!("creating {}", dir.display()))?;
    let path = dir.join(prepared.file_name());
    write_if_changed(&path, &prepared.bytes)?;

    let wide: Vec<u16> = path.as_os_str().encode_wide().chain(Some(0)).collect();
    // SAFETY: `wide` is a NUL-terminated path. The image has no entry point
    // and no imports, so loading it runs no title code.
    let module = unsafe { LoadLibraryExW(wide.as_ptr(), std::ptr::null_mut(), 0) };
    if module.is_null() {
        bail!(
            "LoadLibraryExW({}) failed: {}{}",
            path.display(),
            std::io::Error::last_os_error(),
            if prepared.info.has_relocations {
                ""
            } else {
                " (image has no relocations; its preferred base may be taken)"
            }
        );
    }
    let loaded = LoadedImage {
        module,
        path,
        info: prepared.info.clone(),
    };
    // A DLL indexes its TLS properly; only an exe assumes index 0.
    if !loaded.info.is_dll() {
        // SAFETY: just mapped, and no title code has run.
        unsafe { crate::tls::redirect(loaded.base(), &loaded.info) }?;
    }
    tracing::info!(
        base = format_args!("{:#x}", loaded.base()),
        preferred = format_args!("{:#x}", loaded.info.image_base),
        path = %loaded.path.display(),
        "image mapped"
    );
    crate::threads::mapped(&loaded);
    Ok(loaded)
}

/// Maps the DLLs the title ships in `title_dir` that `main` imports,
/// directly or through each other, in initialisation order (dependencies
/// first). Only DLL names `wanted` accepts are considered, so DLLs the host
/// or our runtime provide stay with them. Imports are not bound.
pub fn load_title_dlls(
    main: &ImageInfo,
    title_dir: &Path,
    cache_dir: &Path,
    wanted: &dyn Fn(&str) -> bool,
) -> Result<Vec<(String, LoadedImage)>> {
    let mut loaded = Vec::new();
    let dirs = (title_dir, cache_dir);
    map_imports(main, dirs, wanted, &mut HashSet::new(), &mut loaded)?;
    Ok(loaded)
}

/// Maps the DLL `name` from `title_dir` like [`load_title_dlls`] does, with
/// the title DLLs it imports (dependencies first, `name` last); empty if
/// `wanted` refuses it or the folder has no such file. For DLLs a title
/// loads itself; `wanted` must refuse those already mapped.
pub fn load_title_dll(
    name: &str,
    title_dir: &Path,
    cache_dir: &Path,
    wanted: &dyn Fn(&str) -> bool,
) -> Result<Vec<(String, LoadedImage)>> {
    let mut loaded = Vec::new();
    let dirs = (title_dir, cache_dir);
    map_dll(name, dirs, wanted, &mut HashSet::new(), &mut loaded)?;
    Ok(loaded)
}

fn map_imports(
    info: &ImageInfo,
    dirs: (&Path, &Path),
    wanted: &dyn Fn(&str) -> bool,
    seen: &mut HashSet<String>,
    loaded: &mut Vec<(String, LoadedImage)>,
) -> Result<()> {
    for module in info.imports.iter().chain(&info.delay_imports) {
        map_dll(&module.dll, dirs, wanted, seen, loaded)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn map_dll(
    name: &str,
    dirs: (&Path, &Path),
    wanted: &dyn Fn(&str) -> bool,
    seen: &mut HashSet<String>,
    loaded: &mut Vec<(String, LoadedImage)>,
) -> Result<()> {
    let name = name.to_ascii_lowercase();
    let path = dirs.0.join(&name);
    if !seen.insert(name.clone()) || !wanted(&name) || !path.is_file() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let original = std::fs::read(&path).with_context(|| format!("reading {}", path.display()))?;
    let prepared = prepare(&original).with_context(|| format!("preparing {}", path.display()))?;
    let image = load(&prepared, dirs.1).with_context(|| format!("loading {}", path.display()))?;
    map_imports(&image.info, dirs, wanted, seen, loaded)?;
    loaded.push((name, image));
    Ok(())
}

/// Resolves through `inner`, then through the exports of the title's DLLs.
pub struct WithTitleDlls<'a> {
    pub inner: &'a dyn ImportResolver,
    pub dlls: &'a [(String, LoadedImage)],
}

impl ImportResolver for WithTitleDlls<'_> {
    fn resolve(&self, dll: &str, symbol: &ImportSymbol) -> Resolution {
        let found = self.inner.resolve(dll, symbol);
        if found != Resolution::Missing {
            return found;
        }
        self.dlls
            .iter()
            .find(|(name, _)| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(dll))
            .and_then(|(_, image)| image.export_symbol(symbol))
            .map_or(Resolution::Missing, |address| Resolution::Found {
                address,
                provenance: Provenance::Title,
            })
    }
}

fn write_if_changed(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {
    if std::fs::read(path).is_ok_and(|existing| existing == bytes) {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let tmp = path.with_extension("tmp");
    std::fs::write(&tmp, bytes).with_context(|| format!("writing {}", tmp.display()))?;
    std::fs::rename(&tmp, path).with_context(|| format!("renaming to {}", path.display()))?;
    Ok(())
}

impl LoadedImage {
    pub fn base(&self) -> usize {
        self.module as usize
    }

    /// Parsed from the original image (imports, entry point, TLS callbacks).
    pub fn info(&self) -> &ImageInfo {
        &self.info
    }

    /// Address of an export of the image, if it has one by that name.
    pub fn export(&self, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        let name = CString::new(name).ok()?;
        // SAFETY: valid module handle and NUL-terminated name.
        unsafe { GetProcAddress(self.module, name.as_ptr().cast()) }
            .map(|f| f as *const () as usize)
    }

    /// Address of an export, by name or ordinal.
    pub fn export_symbol(&self, symbol: &ImportSymbol) -> Option<usize> {
        match symbol {
            ImportSymbol::Name { name, .. } => self.export(name),
            // SAFETY: MAKEINTRESOURCE-style ordinal lookup on a valid module.
            ImportSymbol::Ordinal(o) => unsafe { GetProcAddress(self.module, *o as usize as _) }
                .map(|f| f as *const () as usize),
        }
    }

    /// Fills every IAT slot of the image.
    ///
    /// Each import goes to `resolver`; whatever it cannot resolve gets an
    /// unimplemented-import stub that behaves according to `policy`.
    pub fn bind_imports(
        &self,
        resolver: &dyn ImportResolver,
        policy: UnimplementedPolicy,
    ) -> Result<BindReport> {
        let mut report = BindReport::default();
        let mut slots: Vec<(u32, usize)> = Vec::with_capacity(self.info.import_count());
        let mut unresolved: Vec<(u32, &str, &ImportSymbol)> = Vec::new();

        // Delay-load slots are bound eagerly too, so the title's own
        // delay-load helper (which would ask the host) never runs.
        for module in self.info.imports.iter().chain(&self.info.delay_imports) {
            for entry in &module.entries {
                match resolver.resolve(&module.dll, &entry.symbol) {
                    Resolution::Found {
                        address,
                        provenance,
                    } => {
                        match provenance {
                            Provenance::Hle => report.hle += 1,
                            Provenance::Host => report.host += 1,
                            Provenance::Title => report.title += 1,
                        }
                        slots.push((entry.iat_slot_rva, address));
                    }
                    Resolution::Missing => {
                        unresolved.push((entry.iat_slot_rva, &module.dll, &entry.symbol));
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        if !unresolved.is_empty() {
            let mut block = ThunkBlock::new(unresolved.len())?;
            for (slot, dll, symbol) in unresolved {
                let site: &'static ImportSite = Box::leak(Box::new(ImportSite {
                    dll: dll.to_owned(),
                    symbol: symbol.to_string(),
                    policy,
                    calls: AtomicU64::new(0),
                }));
                slots.push((slot, block.emit(site)?));
                report.missing.push(MissingImport {
                    dll: site.dll.clone(),
                    symbol: site.symbol.clone(),
                });
            }
            block.seal()?;
        }

        self.write_slots(&slots)?;
        tracing::info!(
            hle = report.hle,
            host = report.host,
            missing = report.missing.len(),
            "imports bound"
        );
        Ok(report)
    }

    /// Protects and restores each slot on its own: import tables can sit in
    /// sections with different protections (delay-load tables in `.didat`).
    fn write_slots(&self, slots: &[(u32, usize)]) -> Result<()> {
        for &(rva, address) in slots {
            let slot = (self.base() + rva as usize) as *mut u64;
            let mut old = 0;
            // SAFETY: the parser only yields slots inside the image.
            if unsafe { VirtualProtect(slot as *const c_void, 8, PAGE_READWRITE, &mut old) } == 0 {
                bail!(
                    "VirtualProtect(IAT slot {rva:#x}) failed: {}",
                    std::io::Error::last_os_error()
                );
            }
            // SAFETY: inside the image, now writable, 8-byte aligned by the PE format.
            unsafe { slot.write_volatile(address as u64) };
            let mut ignored = 0;
            // SAFETY: restoring the protection we just changed.
            unsafe { VirtualProtect(slot as *const c_void, 8, old, &mut ignored) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Calls the image's TLS callbacks with `reason` (e.g. `DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH`).
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// Runs title code. Imports must be bound first.
    pub unsafe fn run_tls_callbacks(&self, reason: u32) {
        // SAFETY: forwarded from the caller.
        unsafe { self.tls_callbacks(reason, std::ptr::null_mut()) }
    }

    /// # Safety
    /// See [`Self::run_tls_callbacks`].
    unsafe fn tls_callbacks(&self, reason: u32, reserved: *mut c_void) {
        let Some(tls) = &self.info.tls else { return };
        for &rva in &tls.callback_rvas {
            type TlsCallback = unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, u32, *mut c_void);
            // SAFETY: the RVA came from the image's own TLS directory.
            let callback: TlsCallback = unsafe { std::mem::transmute(self.base() + rva as usize) };
            // SAFETY: the caller guarantees imports are bound.
            unsafe { callback(self.module, reason, reserved) };
        }
    }

    /// Initialises a DLL as the Windows loader would: its TLS callbacks,
    /// then `DllMain(DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH)`. From then on it hears of every
    /// thread start and end (see `threads`).
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// Runs title code. Imports must be bound first, and the DLLs this one
    /// depends on attached.
    pub unsafe fn attach(&self) -> Result<()> {
        // SAFETY: forwarded from the caller.
        if unsafe { self.notify(DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH, true, std::ptr::null_mut()) } == Some(0) {
            bail!("DllMain returned FALSE");
        }
        crate::threads::attached(self.base());
        Ok(())
    }

    /// `DLL_PROCESS_DETACH` as `FreeLibrary` sends it (TLS callbacks, then
    /// `DllMain`); the image hears of no more threads.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// Runs title code. The image must have been attached (or its attach
    /// failed), and no other thread may be using it.
    pub unsafe fn detach(&self) {
        crate::threads::detached(self.base());
        // SAFETY: forwarded from the caller.
        unsafe { self.notify(DLL_PROCESS_DETACH, true, std::ptr::null_mut()) };
    }

    /// Runs the image's TLS callbacks with `reason`, then, if `dll_main` and
    /// the image is a DLL with an entry point, its `DllMain`, whose result
    /// is returned. `reserved` is the entry points' third argument.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// Runs title code. Imports must be bound first.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn notify(
        &self,
        reason: u32,
        dll_main: bool,
        reserved: *mut c_void,
    ) -> Option<i32> {
        // SAFETY: forwarded from the caller.
        unsafe { self.tls_callbacks(reason, reserved) };
        if !dll_main || !self.info.is_dll() || self.info.entry_rva == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        type DllMain = unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, u32, *mut c_void) -> i32;
        // SAFETY: the entry RVA came from the original image header.
        let main: DllMain =
            unsafe { std::mem::transmute(self.base() + self.info.entry_rva as usize) };
        // SAFETY: forwarded from the caller.
        Some(unsafe { main(self.module, reason, reserved) })
    }

    /// Starts the title: on a new thread with the stack size from the image
    /// header, attaches `dlls` in order (see [`Self::attach`]), runs the
    /// image's TLS callbacks (`DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH`), then its original entry
    /// point. Returns the thread so the caller can join it.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// Runs title code. Imports of the image and of `dlls` must be bound.
    pub unsafe fn spawn_main(
        self: Arc<Self>,
        dlls: Vec<(String, LoadedImage)>,
    ) -> Result<std::thread::JoinHandle<Result<u32>>> {
        if self.info.entry_rva == 0 {
            bail!("image has no entry point");
        }
        let stack = usize::try_from(self.info.stack_reserve)
            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX)
            .max(1 << 20);
        std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("title-main".into())
            .stack_size(stack)
            .spawn(move || {
                for (name, dll) in &dlls {
                    // SAFETY: forwarded from the caller of `spawn_main`.
                    unsafe { dll.attach() }.with_context(|| format!("attaching {name}"))?;
                }
                // SAFETY: forwarded from the caller of `spawn_main`.
                unsafe { self.run_tls_callbacks(DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH) };
                crate::threads::attached(self.base());
                type Entry = unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void) -> u32;
                // SAFETY: the entry RVA came from the original image header.
                let entry: Entry =
                    unsafe { std::mem::transmute(self.base() + self.info.entry_rva as usize) };
                // SAFETY: forwarded from the caller of `spawn_main`.
                Ok(unsafe { entry(std::ptr::null_mut()) })
            })
            .context("spawning title main thread")
    }

    /// Unmaps the image.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// No title code may be running or run later, and no pointer into the
    /// image may be used afterwards.
    pub unsafe fn unload(self) {
        crate::threads::unmapped(self.base());
        // SAFETY: guaranteed by the caller.
        unsafe { FreeLibrary(self.module) };
    }
}

`crates/victory-loader/tests/load_probe.rs`:

```rs
//! End-to-end: prepare, load, bind and call into a stand-in title
//! (tests/fixtures/hle-probe), without any game data.
#![cfg(windows)]

use std::ffi::CString;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::Command;

use victory_loader::{
    ImportResolver, Provenance, Resolution, UnimplementedPolicy, WithTitleDlls, prepare,
    unimplemented_call_count,
};
use victory_pe::ImportSymbol;
use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle;
use windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::{GetProcAddress, LoadLibraryA};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{CreateThread, INFINITE, WaitForSingleObject};

fn workspace_root() -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("..").join("..")
}

/// Builds the fixture into its own target dir (the outer cargo holds the
/// lock on the main one while tests run), in the outer one's scratch folder
/// for tests, so that it follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` like the rest of the
/// build.
fn build_probe() -> PathBuf {
    let manifest = workspace_root().join("tests/fixtures/hle-probe/Cargo.toml");
    let target = Path::new(env!("CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR")).join("hle-probe");
    let status = Command::new(env!("CARGO"))
        .args(["build", "--quiet", "--manifest-path"])
        .arg(&manifest)
        .arg("--target-dir")
        .arg(&target)
        .status()
        .expect("running cargo");
    assert!(status.success(), "building hle-probe failed");
    target.join("debug").join("hle_probe.dll")
}

extern "system" fn fake_xgameruntime_initialize() -> i32 {
    0x1234
}
/// Asks for the current thread, as our logging does: on a thread std is
/// still starting, that must not abort the process.
extern "system" fn fake_get_tick_count() -> u32 {
    let _ = std::thread::current().id();
    777
}
extern "system" fn fake_delayed() -> u32 {
    4242
}

struct TestResolver;

impl ImportResolver for TestResolver {
    fn resolve(&self, dll: &str, symbol: &ImportSymbol) -> Resolution {
        let dll = dll.to_ascii_lowercase();
        let ImportSymbol::Name { name, .. } = symbol else {
            return Resolution::Missing;
        };
        let hle = match (dll.as_str(), name.as_str()) {
            ("xgameruntime.dll", "XGameRuntimeInitialize") => {
                Some(fake_xgameruntime_initialize as *const () as usize)
            }
            ("kernel32.dll", "GetTickCount") => Some(fake_get_tick_count as *const () as usize),
            ("victory-probe-delayed.dll", "VIctoryProbeDelayed") => {
                Some(fake_delayed as *const () as usize)
            }
            _ => None,
        };
        if let Some(address) = hle {
            return Resolution::Found {
                address,
                provenance: Provenance::Hle,
            };
        }
        host(&dll, name)
            .map(|address| Resolution::Found {
                address,
                provenance: Provenance::Host,
            })
            .unwrap_or(Resolution::Missing)
    }
}

fn host(dll: &str, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    let dll = CString::new(dll).ok()?;
    let name = CString::new(name).ok()?;
    // SAFETY: NUL-terminated strings; loading system DLLs into the test process.
    unsafe {
        let module = LoadLibraryA(dll.as_ptr().cast());
        if module.is_null() {
            return None;
        }
        GetProcAddress(module, name.as_ptr().cast()).map(|f| f as *const () as usize)
    }
}

#[test]
fn loads_binds_and_calls_probe() {
    let dll = build_probe();
    let original = std::fs::read(&dll).unwrap();
    let prepared = prepare(&original).unwrap();

    let imports: Vec<_> = prepared
        .info
        .imports
        .iter()
        .map(|m| m.dll.to_ascii_lowercase())
        .collect();
    assert!(
        imports.contains(&"xgameruntime.dll".to_owned()),
        "{imports:?}"
    );
    assert!(
        imports.contains(&"victory-probe-missing.dll".to_owned()),
        "{imports:?}"
    );
    assert!(
        prepared
            .info
            .delay_imports
            .iter()
            .any(|m| m.dll.eq_ignore_ascii_case("victory-probe-delayed.dll")),
        "fixture must delay-load victory-probe-delayed.dll"
    );

    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let image = victory_loader::load(&prepared, dir.path()).unwrap();

    // The "title" ships victory-probe-title.dll: any real DLL will do.
    let title_dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    std::fs::copy(
        r"C:\Windows\System32\version.dll",
        title_dir.path().join("victory-probe-title.dll"),
    )
    .unwrap();
    let dlls =
        victory_loader::load_title_dlls(image.info(), title_dir.path(), dir.path(), &|_| true)
            .unwrap();
    let names: Vec<_> = dlls.iter().map(|(n, _)| n.as_str()).collect();
    assert_eq!(names, ["victory-probe-title.dll"]);
    let resolver = WithTitleDlls {
        inner: &TestResolver,
        dlls: &dlls,
    };
    for (_, dll) in &dlls {
        dll.bind_imports(&resolver, UnimplementedPolicy::ReturnZero)
            .unwrap();
        // SAFETY: its imports are bound, and it depends on no other title DLL.
        unsafe { dll.attach() }.unwrap();
    }
    let report = image
        .bind_imports(&resolver, UnimplementedPolicy::ReturnZero)
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(report.title, 1);

    assert_eq!(report.hle, 3);
    assert!(report.host > 0);
    assert_eq!(report.missing.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(report.missing[0].symbol, "VIctoryProbeNotImplemented");

    let call = |name: &str| -> usize { image.export(name).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{name}")) };
    // SAFETY: the exports have the signatures declared in the fixture and
    // every import they use has been bound.
    unsafe {
        let f: extern "system" fn() -> i32 = std::mem::transmute(call("probe_xgameruntime_init"));
        assert_eq!(f(), 0x1234, "console API must reach our implementation");

        let f: extern "system" fn() -> u32 = std::mem::transmute(call("probe_tick"));
        assert_eq!(f(), 777, "host API must be overridable");

        let f: extern "system" fn() -> u32 = std::mem::transmute(call("probe_pid"));
        assert_eq!(f(), std::process::id(), "host API must pass through");

        let f: extern "system" fn() -> u32 = std::mem::transmute(call("probe_title"));
        assert_ne!(f(), 0, "title DLL export must be bound");

        let f: extern "system" fn() -> u32 = std::mem::transmute(call("probe_delayed"));
        assert_eq!(f(), 4242, "delay-loaded API must be bound");

        let before = unimplemented_call_count();
        let f: extern "system" fn() -> u64 = std::mem::transmute(call("probe_missing"));
        assert_eq!(f(), 0);
        assert_eq!(unimplemented_call_count(), before + 1);

        // Once attached, every thread start reaches its TLS callback and
        // DllMain (other tests may start threads too, hence at least one).
        assert!(
            image
                .info()
                .tls
                .as_ref()
                .is_some_and(|t| !t.callback_rvas.is_empty())
        );
        image.attach().unwrap();
        let f: extern "system" fn() -> u64 = std::mem::transmute(call("probe_thread_starts"));
        let before = f();
        // A thread std starts, as our runtime's workers are: notified
        // before std sets it up, which must still find its state pristine.
        let worker = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("probe-worker".into())
            .spawn(|| std::thread::current().name().map(str::to_owned))
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(worker.join().unwrap().as_deref(), Some("probe-worker"));
        let mid = f();
        assert!(mid >> 32 > before >> 32 && mid as u32 > before as u32);
        let before = mid;
        // Starting in title code, as a title's threads do; the extra
        // argument is ignored.
        let start: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut std::ffi::c_void) -> u32 =
            std::mem::transmute(call("probe_pid"));
        let thread = CreateThread(
            std::ptr::null(),
            0,
            Some(start),
            std::ptr::null(),
            0,
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
        );
        assert!(!thread.is_null());
        WaitForSingleObject(thread, INFINITE);
        CloseHandle(thread);
        let after = f();
        assert!(
            after >> 32 > before >> 32,
            "TLS callback: {before:#x} → {after:#x}"
        );
        assert!(
            after as u32 > before as u32,
            "DllMain: {before:#x} → {after:#x}"
        );
        // It has static TLS, so Windows would refuse too.
        assert_eq!(
            victory_loader::disable_thread_calls(image.base()),
            Some(false)
        );
        assert_eq!(victory_loader::disable_thread_calls(1), None);

        // `FreeLibrary`'s notice, as a failed late load sends it.
        let f: extern "system" fn() -> u32 = std::mem::transmute(call("probe_detaches"));
        assert_eq!(f(), 0);
        image.detach();
        assert_eq!(f(), 1);
        image.unload();
    }
}

#[test]
fn maps_a_title_dll_the_title_loads_itself() {
    let title_dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let cache = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    // Any real DLL will do; it imports only host DLLs, which are not in the folder.
    std::fs::copy(
        r"C:\Windows\System32\version.dll",
        title_dir.path().join("Late.dll"),
    )
    .unwrap();
    let load = |name: &str, wanted: &dyn Fn(&str) -> bool| {
        victory_loader::load_title_dll(name, title_dir.path(), cache.path(), wanted).unwrap()
    };
    let dlls = load("LATE.DLL", &|_| true);
    let names: Vec<_> = dlls.iter().map(|(n, _)| n.as_str()).collect();
    assert_eq!(names, ["late.dll"]);
    assert!(dlls[0].1.export("GetFileVersionInfoW").is_some());
    assert!(load("absent.dll", &|_| true).is_empty());
    assert!(load("late.dll", &|_| false).is_empty());
}

`crates/victory-pe/src/image.rs`:

```rs
use object::LittleEndian as LE;
use object::Object;
use object::pe::{self, ImageNtHeaders64};
use object::read::pe::{
    ExportTarget, ImageNtHeaders, ImageOptionalHeader, Import, ImportTable, ImportThunkList,
    PeFile64,
};

use crate::layout::{self, dir};
use crate::{MACHINE_AMD64, PeError};

/// Everything we need to know about a PE32+ image, extracted in one pass.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ImageInfo {
    pub machine: u16,
    /// `IMAGE_FILE_HEADER::Characteristics`.
    pub characteristics: u16,
    pub timestamp: u32,
    pub subsystem: u16,
    /// `IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER64::DllCharacteristics`.
    pub dll_characteristics: u16,
    pub image_base: u64,
    pub size_of_image: u32,
    pub entry_rva: u32,
    pub stack_reserve: u64,
    pub stack_commit: u64,
    pub sections: Vec<SectionInfo>,
    pub imports: Vec<ImportModule>,
    pub delay_imports: Vec<ImportModule>,
    pub exports: Vec<ExportInfo>,
    pub tls: Option<TlsInfo>,
    pub has_relocations: bool,
    pub has_exception_table: bool,
    pub has_load_config: bool,
    pub codeview: Option<CodeViewInfo>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SectionInfo {
    pub name: String,
    pub rva: u32,
    pub virtual_size: u32,
    pub file_offset: u32,
    pub file_size: u32,
    pub characteristics: u32,
}

/// One imported DLL and the functions taken from it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ImportModule {
    /// DLL name exactly as written in the image (case preserved).
    pub dll: String,
    pub entries: Vec<ImportEntry>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ImportEntry {
    pub symbol: ImportSymbol,
    /// RVA of the 8-byte IAT slot the loader must fill in.
    pub iat_slot_rva: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum ImportSymbol {
    Name { hint: u16, name: String },
    Ordinal(u16),
}

impl std::fmt::Display for ImportSymbol {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            ImportSymbol::Name { name, .. } => f.write_str(name),
            ImportSymbol::Ordinal(o) => write!(f, "#{o}"),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ExportInfo {
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub ordinal: u16,
    /// `None` for forwarded exports.
    pub rva: Option<u32>,
    /// `"dll.name"` or `"dll.#ordinal"` for forwarded exports.
    pub forward: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TlsInfo {
    /// RVA of `IMAGE_TLS_DIRECTORY64`.
    pub directory_rva: u32,
    /// VA (at the preferred base) of the callback array, 0 if none.
    pub callbacks_va: u64,
    /// Callback RVAs, in call order.
    pub callback_rvas: Vec<u32>,
}

/// CodeView (RSDS) record: identifies the exact build that produced an image.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct CodeViewInfo {
    pub pdb_path: String,
    pub guid: [u8; 16],
    pub age: u32,
}

impl CodeViewInfo {
    /// The key symbol servers use: GUID (Windows byte order) + age.
    pub fn symbol_key(&self) -> String {
        let g = &self.guid;
        let d1 = u32::from_le_bytes([g[0], g[1], g[2], g[3]]);
        let d2 = u16::from_le_bytes([g[4], g[5]]);
        let d3 = u16::from_le_bytes([g[6], g[7]]);
        let mut s = format!("{d1:08X}{d2:04X}{d3:04X}");
        for b in &g[8..] {
            s.push_str(&format!("{b:02X}"));
        }
        s.push_str(&format!("{:X}", self.age));
        s
    }
}

/// Upper bound on TLS callbacks we are willing to walk (defends against garbage).
const MAX_TLS_CALLBACKS: usize = 1024;

impl ImageInfo {
    /// Parses a complete PE32+ x86-64 image from its file bytes.
    pub fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, PeError> {
        let kind = object::FileKind::parse(data)?;
        if kind != object::FileKind::Pe64 {
            return Err(PeError::Unsupported(format!(
                "expected PE32+, found {kind:?}"
            )));
        }
        let file = PeFile64::parse(data)?;
        let nt = file.nt_headers();
        let fh = nt.file_header();
        let opt = nt.optional_header();

        let machine = fh.machine.get(LE).0;
        if machine != MACHINE_AMD64 {
            return Err(PeError::Unsupported(format!(
                "machine 0x{machine:04x} is not AMD64"
            )));
        }

        let sections = file
            .section_table()
            .iter()
            .map(|s| SectionInfo {
                name: String::from_utf8_lossy(s.raw_name()).into_owned(),
                rva: s.virtual_address.get(LE),
                virtual_size: s.virtual_size.get(LE),
                file_offset: s.pointer_to_raw_data.get(LE),
                file_size: s.size_of_raw_data.get(LE),
                characteristics: s.characteristics.get(LE).0,
            })
            .collect();

        let dir_present = |index: usize| {
            file.data_directory(index)
                .is_some_and(|d| d.virtual_address.get(LE) != 0 && d.size.get(LE) != 0)
        };

        let imports = match file.import_table()? {
            Some(table) => parse_imports(&table, opt.size_of_image())?,
            None => Vec::new(),
        };
        let delay_imports = parse_delay_imports(&file, opt.size_of_image())?;
        let exports = parse_exports(&file)?;
        let tls = parse_tls(&file, data, opt.image_base())?;
        let codeview = file.pdb_info()?.map(|cv| CodeViewInfo {
            pdb_path: String::from_utf8_lossy(cv.path()).into_owned(),
            guid: cv.guid(),
            age: cv.age(),
        });

        Ok(ImageInfo {
            machine,
            characteristics: fh.characteristics.get(LE).0,
            timestamp: fh.time_date_stamp.get(LE),
            subsystem: opt.subsystem().0,
            dll_characteristics: opt.dll_characteristics().0,
            image_base: opt.image_base(),
            size_of_image: opt.size_of_image(),
            entry_rva: opt.address_of_entry_point(),
            stack_reserve: opt.size_of_stack_reserve(),
            stack_commit: opt.size_of_stack_commit(),
            sections,
            imports,
            delay_imports,
            exports,
            tls,
            has_relocations: dir_present(dir::BASERELOC)
                && !has_flag(
                    fh.characteristics.get(LE).0,
                    layout::file_flags::RELOCS_STRIPPED,
                ),
            has_exception_table: dir_present(dir::EXCEPTION),
            has_load_config: dir_present(dir::LOAD_CONFIG),
            codeview,
        })
    }

    pub fn is_dll(&self) -> bool {
        has_flag(self.characteristics, layout::file_flags::DLL)
    }

    /// Maps an RVA to an offset in the file, if it is backed by file data.
    pub fn rva_to_file_offset(&self, rva: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        self.sections.iter().find_map(|s| {
            let delta = rva.checked_sub(s.rva)?;
            // Raw data may be padded past the virtual size; that padding is
            // not part of the section in memory.
            let backed = match s.virtual_size {
                0 => s.file_size,
                vs => vs.min(s.file_size),
            };
            // Header values are untrusted: an offset near 4 GiB overflows.
            (delta < backed).then(|| s.file_offset.checked_add(delta))?
        })
    }

    pub fn import_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.imports.iter().map(|m| m.entries.len()).sum()
    }

    pub fn subsystem_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        use layout::subsystem::*;
        match self.subsystem {
            WINDOWS_GUI => "windows-gui",
            WINDOWS_CUI => "windows-cui",
            XBOX => "xbox",
            XBOX_CODE_CATALOG => "xbox-code-catalog",
            _ => "other",
        }
    }
}

fn has_flag(value: u16, flag: u16) -> bool {
    value & flag != 0
}

fn utf8(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).into_owned()
}

fn convert_import(import: Import<'_>) -> ImportSymbol {
    match import {
        Import::Ordinal(o) => ImportSymbol::Ordinal(o),
        Import::Name(hint, name) => ImportSymbol::Name {
            hint,
            name: utf8(name),
        },
    }
}

fn parse_imports(
    table: &ImportTable<'_>,
    size_of_image: u32,
) -> Result<Vec<ImportModule>, PeError> {
    let mut modules = Vec::new();
    let mut descriptors = table.descriptors()?;
    while let Some(desc) = descriptors.next()? {
        let iat_rva = desc.first_thunk.get(LE);
        // Prefer the unbound name table; fall back to the IAT for old linkers.
        let int_rva = match desc.original_first_thunk.get(LE) {
            0 => iat_rva,
            rva => rva,
        };
        modules.push(ImportModule {
            dll: utf8(table.name(desc.name.get(LE))?),
            entries: entries(table.thunks(int_rva)?, iat_rva, size_of_image, |t| {
                table.import::<ImageNtHeaders64>(t)
            })?,
        });
    }
    Ok(modules)
}

fn parse_delay_imports(
    file: &PeFile64<'_>,
    size_of_image: u32,
) -> Result<Vec<ImportModule>, PeError> {
    let Some(table) = file.delay_load_import_table()? else {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    };
    let mut modules = Vec::new();
    let mut descriptors = table.descriptors()?;
    while let Some(desc) = descriptors.next()? {
        modules.push(ImportModule {
            dll: utf8(table.name(desc.dll_name_rva.get(LE))?),
            entries: entries(
                table.thunks(desc.import_name_table_rva.get(LE))?,
                desc.import_address_table_rva.get(LE),
                size_of_image,
                |t| table.import::<ImageNtHeaders64>(t),
            )?,
        });
    }
    Ok(modules)
}

/// Pairs each name-table entry with its IAT slot. The IAT RVA is not checked
/// by `object`, so every slot is checked to lie inside the image here.
fn entries<'data>(
    mut thunks: ImportThunkList<'data>,
    iat_rva: u32,
    size_of_image: u32,
    import: impl Fn(pe::ImageThunkData64) -> object::read::Result<Import<'data>>,
) -> Result<Vec<ImportEntry>, PeError> {
    let mut entries = Vec::new();
    while let Some(thunk) = thunks.next::<ImageNtHeaders64>()? {
        let iat_slot_rva = u32::try_from(entries.len() * 8)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|offset| iat_rva.checked_add(offset))
            .filter(|&rva| rva.checked_add(8).is_some_and(|end| end <= size_of_image))
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                PeError::Malformed(format!("IAT at {iat_rva:#x} runs outside the image"))
            })?;
        entries.push(ImportEntry {
            symbol: convert_import(import(thunk)?),
            iat_slot_rva,
        });
    }
    Ok(entries)
}

fn parse_exports(file: &PeFile64<'_>) -> Result<Vec<ExportInfo>, PeError> {
    let Some(table) = file.export_table()? else {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    };
    Ok(table
        .exports()?
        .into_iter()
        // An address of 0 marks an unused slot in the address table (a gap
        // in the ordinals), not an export at the image base.
        .filter(|e| !matches!(e.target, ExportTarget::Address(0)))
        .map(|e| {
            let (rva, forward) = match e.target {
                ExportTarget::Address(rva) => (Some(rva), None),
                ExportTarget::ForwardByName(d, n) => {
                    (None, Some(format!("{}.{}", utf8(d), utf8(n))))
                }
                ExportTarget::ForwardByOrdinal(d, o) => {
                    (None, Some(format!("{}.#{}", utf8(d), o.0)))
                }
            };
            ExportInfo {
                name: e.name.map(utf8),
                ordinal: e.ordinal.0,
                rva,
                forward,
            }
        })
        .collect())
}

fn parse_tls(
    file: &PeFile64<'_>,
    data: &[u8],
    image_base: u64,
) -> Result<Option<TlsInfo>, PeError> {
    let Some(dd) = file.data_directory(pe::IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_TLS) else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    let directory_rva = dd.virtual_address.get(LE);
    if directory_rva == 0 {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let sections = file.section_table();
    let tls = sections
        .pe_data_at(data, directory_rva)
        .ok_or_else(|| PeError::Malformed("TLS directory outside of sections".into()))?;
    let callbacks_va = layout::read_u64(tls, layout::TLS64_ADDRESS_OF_CALLBACKS)
        .ok_or_else(|| PeError::Malformed("truncated TLS directory".into()))?;

    let mut callback_rvas = Vec::new();
    if callbacks_va != 0 {
        let array_rva = va_to_rva(callbacks_va, image_base)?;
        let array = sections
            .pe_data_at(data, array_rva)
            .ok_or_else(|| PeError::Malformed("TLS callback array outside of sections".into()))?;
        for slot in array.as_chunks::<8>().0.iter().take(MAX_TLS_CALLBACKS) {
            let va = u64::from_le_bytes(*slot);
            if va == 0 {
                break;
            }
            callback_rvas.push(va_to_rva(va, image_base)?);
        }
    }
    Ok(Some(TlsInfo {
        directory_rva,
        callbacks_va,
        callback_rvas,
    }))
}

fn va_to_rva(va: u64, image_base: u64) -> Result<u32, PeError> {
    va.checked_sub(image_base)
        .and_then(|rva| u32::try_from(rva).ok())
        .ok_or_else(|| PeError::Malformed(format!("VA 0x{va:x} is outside the image")))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// The test binary itself is a real MSVC-linked PE32+ image.
    fn own_image() -> Vec<u8> {
        std::fs::read(std::env::current_exe().unwrap()).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_own_test_binary() {
        let info = ImageInfo::parse(&own_image()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(info.machine, MACHINE_AMD64);
        assert!(!info.is_dll());
        assert!(info.entry_rva != 0);
        assert!(info.has_exception_table, "x64 images always carry .pdata");
        assert!(info.sections.iter().any(|s| s.name.starts_with(".text")));
        let kernel32 = info
            .imports
            .iter()
            .find(|m| m.dll.eq_ignore_ascii_case("kernel32.dll"))
            .expect("Rust std imports kernel32");
        assert!(kernel32.entries.iter().all(|e| e.iat_slot_rva != 0));
        // Rust std uses static TLS, so a TLS directory must be present (its
        // callback array may legitimately be empty).
        assert!(info.tls.is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rva_to_file_offset_maps_entry_point() {
        let data = own_image();
        let info = ImageInfo::parse(&data).unwrap();
        let off = info.rva_to_file_offset(info.entry_rva).unwrap() as usize;
        assert!(off < data.len());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rva_to_file_offset_rejects_offsets_past_4_gib() {
        let mut info = ImageInfo::parse(&own_image()).unwrap();
        let rva = info.sections[0].rva + 0x20;
        assert!(info.rva_to_file_offset(rva).is_some());
        // Used to overflow (a panic in debug builds, a wrong offset in
        // release ones).
        info.sections[0].file_offset = u32::MAX - 0x10;
        assert_eq!(info.rva_to_file_offset(rva), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_garbage_without_panicking() {
        assert!(ImageInfo::parse(b"").is_err());
        assert!(ImageInfo::parse(b"MZ not really").is_err());
        let mut truncated = own_image();
        truncated.truncate(0x200);
        assert!(ImageInfo::parse(&truncated).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_iat_outside_image() {
        let mut data = own_image();
        let dd = layout::data_directory_offset(&data, dir::IMPORT).unwrap();
        let import_rva = layout::read_u32(&data, dd).unwrap();
        let desc = ImageInfo::parse(&data)
            .unwrap()
            .rva_to_file_offset(import_rva)
            .unwrap() as usize;
        // First descriptor's FirstThunk, at the 4 GiB limit: used to overflow.
        data[desc + 16..desc + 20].copy_from_slice(&0xFFFF_FFF8u32.to_le_bytes());
        assert!(matches!(
            ImageInfo::parse(&data),
            Err(PeError::Malformed(_))
        ));
    }
    /// A minimal PE32+ image: one section at RVA 0x1000 holding `body`, with
    /// the export directory (RVA 0x1000, 0x80 bytes) pointing at it.
    fn synthetic_image(body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut d = vec![0u8; 0x200];
        d[0..2].copy_from_slice(b"MZ");
        d[0x3C..0x40].copy_from_slice(&0x40u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[0x40..0x44].copy_from_slice(b"PE\0\0");
        d[0x44..0x46].copy_from_slice(&MACHINE_AMD64.to_le_bytes());
        d[0x46..0x48].copy_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes()); // sections
        d[0x54..0x56].copy_from_slice(&240u16.to_le_bytes()); // optional header size
        d[0x56..0x58].copy_from_slice(&0x2022u16.to_le_bytes()); // DLL, large address aware
        let opt = 0x58;
        d[opt..opt + 2].copy_from_slice(&0x20Bu16.to_le_bytes());
        d[opt + 24..opt + 32].copy_from_slice(&0x1_8000_0000u64.to_le_bytes());
        d[opt + 32..opt + 36].copy_from_slice(&0x1000u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[opt + 36..opt + 40].copy_from_slice(&0x200u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[opt + 56..opt + 60].copy_from_slice(&0x2000u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[opt + 60..opt + 64].copy_from_slice(&0x200u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[opt + 108..opt + 112].copy_from_slice(&16u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[opt + 112..opt + 116].copy_from_slice(&0x1000u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[opt + 116..opt + 120].copy_from_slice(&0x80u32.to_le_bytes());
        let sec = opt + 240;
        d[sec..sec + 6].copy_from_slice(b".edata");
        d[sec + 8..sec + 12].copy_from_slice(&0x200u32.to_le_bytes()); // virtual size
        d[sec + 12..sec + 16].copy_from_slice(&0x1000u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[sec + 16..sec + 20].copy_from_slice(&0x200u32.to_le_bytes()); // raw size
        d[sec + 20..sec + 24].copy_from_slice(&0x200u32.to_le_bytes()); // raw offset
        d.extend_from_slice(body);
        d.resize(0x400, 0);
        d
    }

    #[test]
    fn unused_export_slots_are_not_exports() {
        // Ordinal base 1; three address slots: "alpha", an unused hole (0),
        // and "gamma". The Windows loader treats address 0 as "not exported".
        let mut body = vec![0u8; 0x100];
        let put32 =
            |b: &mut Vec<u8>, at: usize, v: u32| b[at..at + 4].copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
        put32(&mut body, 12, 0x1040); // name of the DLL
        put32(&mut body, 16, 1); // ordinal base
        put32(&mut body, 20, 3); // number of functions
        put32(&mut body, 24, 2); // number of names
        put32(&mut body, 28, 0x1028); // address table
        put32(&mut body, 32, 0x1034); // name pointer table
        put32(&mut body, 36, 0x103C); // name ordinal table
        put32(&mut body, 0x28, 0x1200);
        put32(&mut body, 0x2C, 0);
        put32(&mut body, 0x30, 0x1204);
        put32(&mut body, 0x34, 0x1044);
        put32(&mut body, 0x38, 0x104A);
        body[0x3C..0x3E].copy_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes());
        body[0x3E..0x40].copy_from_slice(&2u16.to_le_bytes());
        body[0x40..0x44].copy_from_slice(b"t.dl");
        body[0x44..0x4A].copy_from_slice(b"alpha\0");
        body[0x4A..0x50].copy_from_slice(b"gamma\0");

        let info = ImageInfo::parse(&synthetic_image(&body)).unwrap();
        let exports: Vec<_> = info
            .exports
            .iter()
            .map(|e| (e.name.as_deref(), e.ordinal, e.rva))
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(
            exports,
            [
                (Some("alpha"), 1, Some(0x1200)),
                (Some("gamma"), 3, Some(0x1204))
            ]
        );
    }
}
