`crates/victory-shader/src/emit/bitcode.rs`:

```rs
//! A DXIL module and its LLVM 3.7 bitcode, written with unabbreviated
//! records only (the format DXIL fixes; codes from LLVM's `LLVMBitCodes.h`).
//!
//! Values are symbolic while the module is built ([`V`]) and numbered when
//! it is written: functions, then constants (all at module level), then the
//! instructions of `main` in block order.

use std::collections::HashMap;

pub mod census;
pub mod opt;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub(crate) struct Ty(u32);

/// What the lowering made an instruction for, where it says so (counted by
/// [`census`], nothing else reads it).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Tag {
    /// The select that keeps a register's old value in lanes a guard masks.
    Guard,
    /// An index clamp the translation adds (the console has none).
    Clamp,
    /// The iteration counter and limit test the translation adds to a loop.
    Counter,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
enum TypeDef {
    Void,
    Int(u32),
    Float,
    Double,
    /// Pointee and address space.
    Ptr(Ty, u32),
    Struct(Option<String>, Vec<Ty>),
    Array(u32, Ty),
    Func(Ty, Vec<Ty>),
}

/// A value: a global variable, a function, a module constant, or an
/// instruction result.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub(crate) enum V {
    Global(u32),
    Func(u32),
    Const(u32),
    Inst(u32),
}

/// A global variable declaration (thread-group shared memory).
struct Global {
    name: String,
    ty: Ty,
    /// Its pointer type.
    ptr: Ty,
    space: u32,
    /// An internal constant with this initialiser (a constant table).
    init: Option<u32>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
enum Const {
    Int(i64),
    Float(u32),
    Undef,
    Aggregate(Vec<u32>),
}

/// LLVM binary opcodes (the same codes serve the float forms).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Bin {
    Add = 0,
    Sub = 1,
    Mul = 2,
    UDiv = 3,
    SDiv = 4,
    URem = 5,
    Shl = 7,
    LShr = 8,
    AShr = 9,
    And = 10,
    Or = 11,
    Xor = 12,
}

/// `atomicrmw` operations.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Rmw {
    Xchg = 0,
    Add = 1,
    Sub = 2,
    And = 3,
    Or = 5,
    Xor = 6,
    Max = 7,
    Min = 8,
    UMax = 9,
    UMin = 10,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Cast {
    Trunc = 0,
    ZExt = 1,
    SExt = 2,
    FpToUi = 3,
    FpToSi = 4,
    UiToFp = 5,
    SiToFp = 6,
    Bitcast = 11,
}

/// Compare predicates: floats 0-15, integers 32-41.
pub(crate) mod pred {
    pub const FALSE: u8 = 0;
    pub const OEQ: u8 = 1;
    pub const OGT: u8 = 2;
    pub const OGE: u8 = 3;
    pub const OLT: u8 = 4;
    pub const OLE: u8 = 5;
    // Not emitted: the AMD D3D12 driver treats it as UNE, so `v_cmp_lg`
    // lowers as OLT | OGT instead.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub const ONE: u8 = 6;
    pub const ORD: u8 = 7;
    pub const UNO: u8 = 8;
    pub const UEQ: u8 = 9;
    pub const UGT: u8 = 10;
    pub const UGE: u8 = 11;
    pub const ULT: u8 = 12;
    pub const ULE: u8 = 13;
    pub const UNE: u8 = 14;
    pub const TRUE: u8 = 15;
    pub const EQ: u8 = 32;
    pub const NE: u8 = 33;
    pub const IUGT: u8 = 34;
    pub const IUGE: u8 = 35;
    pub const IULT: u8 = 36;
    pub const IULE: u8 = 37;
    pub const SGT: u8 = 38;
    pub const SGE: u8 = 39;
    pub const SLT: u8 = 40;
    pub const SLE: u8 = 41;
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Op {
    Bin(Bin, V, V),
    Cast(Cast, V),
    Cmp(u8, V, V),
    Select(V, V, V),
    Extract(V, u32),
    Call(u32, Vec<V>),
    /// Filled in later: (value, block).
    Phi(Vec<(V, usize)>),
    /// `getelementptr` over the pointee type, from a pointer.
    Gep(Ty, V, Vec<V>),
    Load(V),
    /// Pointer, value.
    Store(V, V),
    AtomicRmw(Rmw, V, V),
    /// Pointer, expected, new; returns `{i32, i1}`.
    CmpXchg(V, V, V),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct Inst {
    ty: Ty,
    op: Op,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum Term {
    Br(usize),
    CondBr(V, usize, usize),
    Ret,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
struct Block {
    phis: Vec<u32>,
    body: Vec<u32>,
    term: Option<Term>,
}

/// Function attributes of a `dx.op` declaration.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Attr {
    ReadNone = 1,
    NoUnwind = 2,
    ReadOnly = 3,
    /// Barriers.
    NoDuplicate = 4,
}

struct Func {
    name: String,
    ty: Ty,
    attr: Option<Attr>,
    body: bool,
}

/// A metadata node operand.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct Md(u32);

enum MdDef {
    Str(String),
    Value(Ty, V),
    Node(Vec<Option<Md>>),
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Module {
    types: Vec<TypeDef>,
    type_ids: HashMap<TypeDef, u32>,
    consts: Vec<(Ty, Const)>,
    const_ids: HashMap<(Ty, Const), u32>,
    globals: Vec<Global>,
    funcs: Vec<Func>,
    func_ids: HashMap<String, u32>,
    insts: Vec<Inst>,
    blocks: Vec<Block>,
    mds: Vec<MdDef>,
    named: Vec<(String, Vec<Md>)>,
    /// See [`Tag`]: by instruction.
    tags: HashMap<u32, Tag>,
}

impl Module {
    fn ty(&mut self, def: TypeDef) -> Ty {
        if let Some(&t) = self.type_ids.get(&def) {
            return Ty(t);
        }
        let t = self.types.len() as u32;
        self.types.push(def.clone());
        self.type_ids.insert(def, t);
        Ty(t)
    }

    pub fn void(&mut self) -> Ty {
        self.ty(TypeDef::Void)
    }
    pub fn int(&mut self, bits: u32) -> Ty {
        self.ty(TypeDef::Int(bits))
    }
    pub fn float(&mut self) -> Ty {
        self.ty(TypeDef::Float)
    }
    pub fn double(&mut self) -> Ty {
        self.ty(TypeDef::Double)
    }
    pub fn ptr(&mut self, to: Ty) -> Ty {
        self.ty(TypeDef::Ptr(to, 0))
    }
    pub fn ptr_in(&mut self, to: Ty, space: u32) -> Ty {
        self.ty(TypeDef::Ptr(to, space))
    }
    pub fn array(&mut self, n: u32, of: Ty) -> Ty {
        self.ty(TypeDef::Array(n, of))
    }
    pub fn named_struct(&mut self, name: &str, fields: Vec<Ty>) -> Ty {
        self.ty(TypeDef::Struct(Some(name.into()), fields))
    }
    pub fn func_ty(&mut self, ret: Ty, params: Vec<Ty>) -> Ty {
        self.ty(TypeDef::Func(ret, params))
    }

    fn is_void(&self, t: Ty) -> bool {
        self.types[t.0 as usize] == TypeDef::Void
    }

    fn constant(&mut self, ty: Ty, c: Const) -> V {
        if let Some(&i) = self.const_ids.get(&(ty, c.clone())) {
            return V::Const(i);
        }
        let i = self.consts.len() as u32;
        self.consts.push((ty, c.clone()));
        self.const_ids.insert((ty, c), i);
        V::Const(i)
    }

    pub fn int_const(&mut self, ty: Ty, v: i64) -> V {
        self.constant(ty, Const::Int(v))
    }
    pub fn i32(&mut self, v: u32) -> V {
        let t = self.int(32);
        self.int_const(t, i64::from(v as i32))
    }
    pub fn i8(&mut self, v: u8) -> V {
        let t = self.int(8);
        self.int_const(t, i64::from(v as i8))
    }
    pub fn bool(&mut self, v: bool) -> V {
        let t = self.int(1);
        self.int_const(t, -i64::from(v))
    }
    pub fn f32(&mut self, bits: u32) -> V {
        let t = self.float();
        self.constant(t, Const::Float(bits))
    }
    pub fn undef(&mut self, ty: Ty) -> V {
        self.constant(ty, Const::Undef)
    }
    /// A constant struct or array of constants.
    pub fn aggregate(&mut self, ty: Ty, fields: &[V]) -> V {
        let ids = fields
            .iter()
            .map(|f| match f {
                V::Const(i) => *i,
                _ => panic!("aggregate of a non-constant"),
            })
            .collect();
        self.constant(ty, Const::Aggregate(ids))
    }

    /// The value of an integer constant; `None` for anything else.
    pub fn int_value(&self, v: V) -> Option<i64> {
        match v {
            V::Const(i) => match self.consts[i as usize].1 {
                Const::Int(x) => Some(x),
                _ => None,
            },
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Gives constant `old` the content of `new` (both stay valid).
    pub fn replace_const(&mut self, old: V, new: V) {
        if let (V::Const(o), V::Const(n)) = (old, new) {
            self.consts[o as usize] = self.consts[n as usize].clone();
        }
    }

    /// A function declaration (or `main` with `body`), found by name.
    pub fn function(&mut self, name: &str, ty: Ty, attr: Option<Attr>, body: bool) -> V {
        if let Some(&i) = self.func_ids.get(name) {
            return V::Func(i);
        }
        let i = self.funcs.len() as u32;
        self.funcs.push(Func {
            name: name.into(),
            ty,
            attr,
            body,
        });
        self.func_ids.insert(name.into(), i);
        V::Func(i)
    }

    /// An external global of type `ty` in address space `space` (DXIL
    /// declares thread-group shared memory this way).
    pub fn global(&mut self, name: &str, ty: Ty, space: u32) -> V {
        let ptr = self.ptr_in(ty, space);
        self.globals.push(Global {
            name: name.into(),
            ty,
            ptr,
            space,
            init: None,
        });
        V::Global(self.globals.len() as u32 - 1)
    }

    /// An internal constant global initialised with the constant `init`.
    pub fn constant_global(&mut self, name: &str, init: V) -> V {
        let V::Const(i) = init else {
            panic!("a global initialised with a non-constant")
        };
        let ty = self.consts[i as usize].0;
        let g = self.global(name, ty, 0);
        if let V::Global(n) = g {
            self.globals[n as usize].init = Some(i);
        }
        g
    }

    /// Notes what instruction `v` is for (see [`Tag`]); only when modules
    /// are counted.
    pub fn tag(&mut self, v: V, tag: Tag) {
        if let V::Inst(i) = v
            && census::enabled()
        {
            self.tags.insert(i, tag);
        }
    }

    pub fn new_block(&mut self) -> usize {
        self.blocks.push(Block::default());
        self.blocks.len() - 1
    }

    pub fn type_of(&self, v: V) -> Ty {
        match v {
            V::Global(i) => self.globals[i as usize].ptr,
            V::Const(i) => self.consts[i as usize].0,
            V::Inst(i) => self.insts[i as usize].ty,
            V::Func(i) => {
                let t = self.funcs[i as usize].ty;
                *self
                    .type_ids
                    .get(&TypeDef::Ptr(t, 0))
                    .map(|t| Ty(*t))
                    .as_ref()
                    .expect("function pointer type")
            }
        }
    }

    fn push(&mut self, block: usize, ty: Ty, op: Op) -> V {
        let i = self.insts.len() as u32;
        self.insts.push(Inst { ty, op });
        // Terminators are kept apart, so a block can still grow at its end.
        self.blocks[block].body.push(i);
        V::Inst(i)
    }

    pub fn bin(&mut self, block: usize, op: Bin, a: V, b: V) -> V {
        let ty = self.type_of(a);
        self.push(block, ty, Op::Bin(op, a, b))
    }
    pub fn cast(&mut self, block: usize, op: Cast, v: V, to: Ty) -> V {
        self.push(block, to, Op::Cast(op, v))
    }
    pub fn cmp(&mut self, block: usize, pred: u8, a: V, b: V) -> V {
        let t = self.int(1);
        self.push(block, t, Op::Cmp(pred, a, b))
    }
    pub fn select(&mut self, block: usize, c: V, t: V, f: V) -> V {
        let ty = self.type_of(t);
        self.push(block, ty, Op::Select(c, t, f))
    }
    pub fn extract(&mut self, block: usize, agg: V, index: u32) -> V {
        let ty = match &self.types[self.type_of(agg).0 as usize] {
            TypeDef::Struct(_, f) => f[index as usize],
            TypeDef::Array(_, t) => *t,
            t => panic!("extractvalue from {t:?}"),
        };
        self.push(block, ty, Op::Extract(agg, index))
    }
    pub fn call(&mut self, block: usize, f: V, args: Vec<V>) -> V {
        let V::Func(i) = f else {
            panic!("call of a non-function")
        };
        let TypeDef::Func(ret, _) = self.types[self.funcs[i as usize].ty.0 as usize] else {
            unreachable!()
        };
        self.push(block, ret, Op::Call(i, args))
    }
    /// A phi at the top of `block`; incoming values come with [`Module::set_phi`].
    pub fn phi(&mut self, block: usize, ty: Ty) -> V {
        let i = self.insts.len() as u32;
        self.insts.push(Inst {
            ty,
            op: Op::Phi(Vec::new()),
        });
        self.blocks[block].phis.push(i);
        V::Inst(i)
    }
    /// The address of element `index` of the array `ptr` points to.
    pub fn element(&mut self, block: usize, ptr: V, index: V) -> V {
        let TypeDef::Ptr(arr, space) = self.types[self.type_of(ptr).0 as usize] else {
            panic!("element of a non-pointer")
        };
        let TypeDef::Array(_, elem) = self.types[arr.0 as usize] else {
            panic!("element of a non-array")
        };
        let ty = self.ptr_in(elem, space);
        let zero = self.i32(0);
        self.push(block, ty, Op::Gep(arr, ptr, vec![zero, index]))
    }
    pub fn load(&mut self, block: usize, ptr: V) -> V {
        let TypeDef::Ptr(ty, _) = self.types[self.type_of(ptr).0 as usize] else {
            panic!("load from a non-pointer")
        };
        self.push(block, ty, Op::Load(ptr))
    }
    pub fn store(&mut self, block: usize, ptr: V, value: V) {
        let void = self.void();
        self.push(block, void, Op::Store(ptr, value));
    }
    pub fn atomic(&mut self, block: usize, op: Rmw, ptr: V, value: V) -> V {
        let ty = self.type_of(value);
        self.push(block, ty, Op::AtomicRmw(op, ptr, value))
    }
    /// The old value of a compare-exchange.
    pub fn cmpxchg(&mut self, block: usize, ptr: V, expected: V, new: V) -> V {
        let (i32t, i1) = (self.type_of(new), self.int(1));
        let pair = self.ty(TypeDef::Struct(None, vec![i32t, i1]));
        let r = self.push(block, pair, Op::CmpXchg(ptr, expected, new));
        self.extract(block, r, 0)
    }

    pub fn set_phi(&mut self, phi: V, incoming: Vec<(V, usize)>) {
        let V::Inst(i) = phi else { panic!() };
        self.insts[i as usize].op = Op::Phi(incoming);
    }
    pub fn terminate(&mut self, block: usize, t: Term) {
        self.blocks[block].term = Some(t);
    }

    pub fn md_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> Md {
        self.mds.push(MdDef::Str(s.into()));
        Md(self.mds.len() as u32 - 1)
    }
    pub fn md_value(&mut self, v: V) -> Md {
        let ty = self.type_of(v);
        self.mds.push(MdDef::Value(ty, v));
        Md(self.mds.len() as u32 - 1)
    }
    pub fn md_node(&mut self, ops: Vec<Option<Md>>) -> Md {
        self.mds.push(MdDef::Node(ops));
        Md(self.mds.len() as u32 - 1)
    }
    pub fn named_md(&mut self, name: &str, nodes: Vec<Md>) {
        self.named.push((name.into(), nodes));
    }

    /// The module as bitcode.
    /// Which instructions are written: every body instruction, the branch
    /// conditions, and whatever they read, transitively (a phi nothing reads
    /// is dropped). A worklist visits each instruction once, so a long chain
    /// of merges costs one pass, not one pass per merge.
    fn live(&self) -> Vec<bool> {
        let mut live = vec![false; self.insts.len()];
        let mut work: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
        let mark = |live: &mut [bool], work: &mut Vec<u32>, v: V| {
            if let V::Inst(i) = v
                && !live[i as usize]
            {
                live[i as usize] = true;
                work.push(i);
            }
        };
        for b in &self.blocks {
            for &i in &b.body {
                mark(&mut live, &mut work, V::Inst(i));
            }
            if let Some(Term::CondBr(c, ..)) = b.term {
                mark(&mut live, &mut work, c);
            }
        }
        while let Some(i) = work.pop() {
            for_each_operand(&self.insts[i as usize].op, |v| {
                mark(&mut live, &mut work, v)
            });
        }
        live
    }

    pub fn write(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut w = Writer::default();
        w.bytes(b"BC\xC0\xDE");
        w.enter(MODULE_BLOCK, 3);
        w.record(1, &[1]); // VERSION: relative value ids

        // Attribute groups 1-4 and one list per group.
        w.enter(PARAMATTR_GROUP_BLOCK, 3);
        for (id, kinds) in [
            (1, &[18u64, 20][..]),
            (2, &[18]),
            (3, &[18, 21]),
            (4, &[12, 18]),
        ] {
            let mut r = vec![id, 0xFFFF_FFFF];
            for &k in kinds {
                r.extend([0, k]);
            }
            w.record(3, &r);
        }
        w.exit();
        w.enter(PARAMATTR_BLOCK, 3);
        for id in 1..=4 {
            w.record(2, &[id]);
        }
        w.exit();

        w.enter(TYPE_BLOCK, 4);
        w.record(1, &[self.types.len() as u64]);
        for t in &self.types {
            match t {
                TypeDef::Void => w.record(2, &[]),
                TypeDef::Float => w.record(3, &[]),
                TypeDef::Double => w.record(4, &[]),
                TypeDef::Int(b) => w.record(7, &[u64::from(*b)]),
                TypeDef::Ptr(p, space) => w.record(8, &[u64::from(p.0), u64::from(*space)]),
                TypeDef::Array(n, e) => w.record(11, &[u64::from(*n), u64::from(e.0)]),
                TypeDef::Struct(name, fields) => {
                    let mut r = vec![0];
                    r.extend(fields.iter().map(|f| u64::from(f.0)));
                    match name {
                        Some(n) => {
                            w.record(19, &chars(n));
                            w.record(20, &r);
                        }
                        None => w.record(18, &r),
                    }
                }
                TypeDef::Func(ret, params) => {
                    let mut r = vec![0, u64::from(ret.0)];
                    r.extend(params.iter().map(|p| u64::from(p.0)));
                    w.record(21, &r);
                }
            }
        }
        w.exit();

        w.record(2, &chars("dxil-ms-dx"));
        w.record(
            3,
            &chars(
                "e-m:e-p:32:32-i1:32-i8:32-i16:32-i32:32-i64:64-f16:32-f32:32-f64:64-n8:16:32:64",
            ),
        );
        let first_const = (self.globals.len() + self.funcs.len()) as u64;
        for g in &self.globals {
            // [type, address space << 2 | explicit type | constant, init id
            // + 1, linkage (external 0, internal 3), log2 alignment + 1,
            // section]
            let (constant, init, linkage) = match g.init {
                Some(i) => (1, first_const + u64::from(i) + 1, 3),
                None => (0, 0, 0),
            };
            w.record(
                7,
                &[
                    u64::from(g.ty.0),
                    u64::from(g.space) << 2 | 2 | constant,
                    init,
                    linkage,
                    3,
                    0,
                ],
            );
        }
        for f in &self.funcs {
            // [type, cc, isproto, linkage, paramattr, align, section,
            // visibility, gc, unnamed_addr, prologue, dllstorage, comdat, prefix]
            let attr = f.attr.map_or(0, |a| a as u64);
            w.record(
                8,
                &[
                    u64::from(f.ty.0),
                    0,
                    u64::from(!f.body),
                    0,
                    attr,
                    0,
                    0,
                    0,
                    0,
                    0,
                    0,
                    0,
                    0,
                    0,
                ],
            );
        }

        // Value ids: globals, functions, constants, instructions.
        let globals = self.globals.len() as u32;
        let funcs = globals + self.funcs.len() as u32;
        let const_id = |i: u32| u64::from(funcs + i);
        w.enter(CONSTANTS_BLOCK, 4);
        let mut current = None;
        for (ty, c) in &self.consts {
            if current != Some(*ty) {
                w.record(1, &[u64::from(ty.0)]);
                current = Some(*ty);
            }
            match c {
                Const::Undef => w.record(3, &[]),
                Const::Int(v) => w.record(4, &[signed(*v)]),
                Const::Float(bits) => w.record(6, &[u64::from(*bits)]),
                Const::Aggregate(ids) => {
                    let r: Vec<u64> = ids.iter().map(|&i| const_id(i)).collect();
                    w.record(7, &r);
                }
            }
        }
        w.exit();

        // Phis nothing reads are left out (one register per phi makes many).
        let live = self.live();

        // Blocks are laid out in reverse postorder, so every block follows
        // its forward predecessors (drivers take a branch to an earlier
        // block for a loop's back edge).
        let succs = |b: usize| successors(self.blocks[b].term);
        let mut seen = vec![false; self.blocks.len()];
        let mut post = Vec::new();
        let mut stack = vec![(0usize, 0usize)];
        seen[0] = true;
        while let Some(top) = stack.last_mut() {
            let (b, k) = *top;
            top.1 += 1;
            match succs(b).get(k) {
                Some(&s) if !seen[s] => {
                    seen[s] = true;
                    stack.push((s, 0));
                }
                Some(_) => {}
                None => {
                    post.push(b);
                    stack.pop();
                }
            }
        }
        post.reverse();
        let mut pos = vec![u64::MAX; self.blocks.len()];
        for (n, &b) in post.iter().enumerate() {
            pos[b] = n as u64;
        }
        // An empty latch (only a branch back to its loop header) is folded
        // into its one predecessor, so the exiting block is the latch as in
        // DXC's loops; the AMD driver hangs on divergent loops otherwise.
        let mut preds = vec![Vec::new(); self.blocks.len()];
        for &b in &post {
            for &s in succs(b).iter() {
                preds[s].push(b);
            }
        }
        let mut fold = vec![None; self.blocks.len()];
        for &b in &post {
            let blk = &self.blocks[b];
            if let (Some(Term::Br(h)), true, [p]) = (
                blk.term,
                blk.phis.is_empty() && blk.body.is_empty(),
                &preds[b][..],
            ) && pos[h] < pos[b]
                && !succs(*p).contains(&h)
            {
                fold[b] = Some((*p, h));
            }
        }
        let layout: Vec<usize> = post.into_iter().filter(|&b| fold[b].is_none()).collect();
        let mut pos = vec![u64::MAX; self.blocks.len()];
        for (n, &b) in layout.iter().enumerate() {
            pos[b] = n as u64;
        }
        // Branch targets and phi blocks through folded latches.
        let target = |t: usize| fold[t].map_or(pos[t], |(_, h)| pos[h]);
        let from = |b: usize| fold[b].map_or(pos[b], |(p, _)| pos[p]);

        // Instruction value ids, in layout order.
        let base = funcs + self.consts.len() as u32;
        let mut ids = vec![u32::MAX; self.insts.len()];
        let mut next = base;
        for b in layout.iter().map(|&b| &self.blocks[b]) {
            for &i in b.phis.iter().filter(|&&i| live[i as usize]).chain(&b.body) {
                if !self.is_void(self.insts[i as usize].ty) {
                    ids[i as usize] = next;
                    next += 1;
                }
            }
        }
        let abs = |v: V| -> u32 {
            match v {
                V::Global(i) => i,
                V::Func(i) => globals + i,
                V::Const(i) => funcs + i,
                V::Inst(i) => {
                    let id = ids[i as usize];
                    assert_ne!(id, u32::MAX, "use of a void value");
                    id
                }
            }
        };

        w.enter(METADATA_BLOCK, 3);
        for m in &self.mds {
            match m {
                MdDef::Str(s) => w.record(1, &chars(s)),
                MdDef::Value(ty, v) => w.record(2, &[u64::from(ty.0), u64::from(abs(*v))]),
                MdDef::Node(ops) => {
                    let r: Vec<u64> = ops
                        .iter()
                        .map(|o| o.map_or(0, |m| u64::from(m.0) + 1))
                        .collect();
                    w.record(3, &r);
                }
            }
        }
        for (name, nodes) in &self.named {
            w.record(4, &chars(name));
            let r: Vec<u64> = nodes.iter().map(|m| u64::from(m.0)).collect();
            w.record(10, &r);
        }
        w.exit();
        // The metadata kinds an LLVM 3.7 module declares, as DXC writes them.
        w.enter(METADATA_BLOCK, 3);
        for (id, kind) in [
            "dbg",
            "tbaa",
            "prof",
            "fpmath",
            "range",
            "tbaa.struct",
            "invariant.load",
            "alias.scope",
            "noalias",
            "nontemporal",
            "llvm.mem.parallel_loop_access",
            "nonnull",
            "dereferenceable",
            "dereferenceable_or_null",
        ]
        .into_iter()
        .enumerate()
        {
            let mut r = vec![id as u64];
            r.extend(chars(kind));
            w.record(6, &r);
        }
        w.exit();

        w.enter(VALUE_SYMTAB_BLOCK, 4);
        let names = self.globals.iter().map(|g| &g.name);
        for (i, name) in names.chain(self.funcs.iter().map(|f| &f.name)).enumerate() {
            let mut r = vec![i as u64];
            r.extend(chars(name));
            w.record(1, &r);
        }
        w.exit();

        w.enter(FUNCTION_BLOCK, 4);
        w.record(1, &[layout.len() as u64]);
        let mut inst_id = base;
        // The operands of variable-length records, reused across them.
        let mut r: Vec<u64> = Vec::new();
        for b in layout.iter().map(|&b| &self.blocks[b]) {
            for &i in b.phis.iter().filter(|&&i| live[i as usize]).chain(&b.body) {
                let inst = &self.insts[i as usize];
                let rel = |v: V| {
                    let a = abs(v);
                    assert!(a < inst_id, "forward reference outside a phi");
                    u64::from(inst_id - a)
                };
                match &inst.op {
                    Op::Bin(op, a, b) => w.record(2, &[rel(*a), rel(*b), *op as u64]),
                    Op::Cast(op, v) => w.record(3, &[rel(*v), u64::from(inst.ty.0), *op as u64]),
                    Op::Cmp(p, a, b) => w.record(28, &[rel(*a), rel(*b), u64::from(*p)]),
                    Op::Select(c, t, f) => w.record(29, &[rel(*t), rel(*f), rel(*c)]),
                    Op::Extract(a, idx) => w.record(26, &[rel(*a), u64::from(*idx)]),
                    Op::Call(f, args) => {
                        r.clear();
                        r.extend([0, 1 << 15, u64::from(self.funcs[*f as usize].ty.0)]);
                        r.push(rel(V::Func(*f)));
                        r.extend(args.iter().map(|&a| rel(a)));
                        w.record(34, &r);
                    }
                    Op::Phi(incoming) => {
                        r.clear();
                        r.push(u64::from(inst.ty.0));
                        for &(v, b) in incoming {
                            r.push(signed(i64::from(inst_id) - i64::from(abs(v))));
                            r.push(from(b));
                        }
                        w.record(16, &r);
                    }
                    Op::Gep(ty, p, idx) => {
                        r.clear();
                        r.extend([0, u64::from(ty.0), rel(*p)]);
                        r.extend(idx.iter().map(|&i| rel(i)));
                        w.record(43, &r);
                    }
                    // Alignment 4 (log2 + 1), not volatile.
                    Op::Load(p) => w.record(20, &[rel(*p), u64::from(inst.ty.0), 3, 0]),
                    Op::Store(p, v) => w.record(44, &[rel(*p), rel(*v), 3, 0]),
                    // Sequentially consistent, across threads.
                    Op::AtomicRmw(op, p, v) => {
                        w.record(38, &[rel(*p), rel(*v), *op as u64, 0, 6, 1])
                    }
                    Op::CmpXchg(p, c, n) => {
                        w.record(46, &[rel(*p), rel(*c), rel(*n), 0, 6, 1, 6, 0]);
                    }
                }
                if !self.is_void(inst.ty) {
                    inst_id += 1;
                }
            }
            match b.term.expect("unterminated block") {
                Term::Ret => w.record(10, &[]),
                Term::Br(t) => w.record(11, &[target(t)]),
                Term::CondBr(c, t, f) => {
                    let a = abs(c);
                    assert!(a < inst_id);
                    w.record(11, &[target(t), target(f), u64::from(inst_id - a)]);
                }
            }
        }
        w.exit();
        w.exit();
        w.finish()
    }
}

const MODULE_BLOCK: u64 = 8;
const PARAMATTR_BLOCK: u64 = 9;
const PARAMATTR_GROUP_BLOCK: u64 = 10;
const CONSTANTS_BLOCK: u64 = 11;
const FUNCTION_BLOCK: u64 = 12;
const VALUE_SYMTAB_BLOCK: u64 = 14;
const METADATA_BLOCK: u64 = 15;
const TYPE_BLOCK: u64 = 17;

/// Calls `f` with every value `op` reads, in operand order.
fn for_each_operand(op: &Op, mut f: impl FnMut(V)) {
    match op {
        Op::Bin(_, a, b) | Op::Cmp(_, a, b) | Op::Store(a, b) | Op::AtomicRmw(_, a, b) => {
            f(*a);
            f(*b);
        }
        Op::Cast(_, v) | Op::Extract(v, _) | Op::Load(v) => f(*v),
        Op::Select(a, b, c) | Op::CmpXchg(a, b, c) => {
            f(*a);
            f(*b);
            f(*c);
        }
        Op::Call(_, args) => args.iter().copied().for_each(f),
        Op::Phi(inc) => inc.iter().for_each(|x| f(x.0)),
        Op::Gep(_, p, idx) => {
            f(*p);
            idx.iter().copied().for_each(f);
        }
    }
}

/// A block's successors (at most two), without allocating.
struct Succs {
    to: [usize; 2],
    len: usize,
}

impl std::ops::Deref for Succs {
    type Target = [usize];
    fn deref(&self) -> &[usize] {
        &self.to[..self.len]
    }
}

fn successors(term: Option<Term>) -> Succs {
    match term {
        Some(Term::Br(t)) => Succs { to: [t, 0], len: 1 },
        Some(Term::CondBr(_, t, f)) => Succs { to: [t, f], len: 2 },
        _ => Succs { to: [0, 0], len: 0 },
    }
}

fn chars(s: &str) -> Vec<u64> {
    s.bytes().map(u64::from).collect()
}

/// LLVM's signed VBR operand: magnitude shifted left, sign in bit 0.
fn signed(v: i64) -> u64 {
    if v >= 0 {
        (v as u64) << 1
    } else {
        (v.unsigned_abs() << 1) | 1
    }
}

/// The bitstream: little-endian 32-bit words filled from bit 0.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Writer {
    words: Vec<u32>,
    cur: u64,
    bits: u32,
    /// Per open block: abbreviation width, index of its length word.
    stack: Vec<(u32, usize)>,
}

impl Writer {
    fn width(&self) -> u32 {
        self.stack.last().map_or(2, |b| b.0)
    }

    fn emit(&mut self, v: u64, width: u32) {
        debug_assert!(width == 64 || v >> width == 0);
        self.cur |= v << self.bits;
        self.bits += width;
        while self.bits >= 32 {
            self.words.push(self.cur as u32);
            self.cur >>= 32;
            self.bits -= 32;
        }
    }

    fn vbr(&mut self, mut v: u64, width: u32) {
        let hi = 1u64 << (width - 1);
        while v >= hi {
            self.emit(v & (hi - 1) | hi, width);
            v >>= width - 1;
        }
        self.emit(v, width);
    }

    fn align(&mut self) {
        if self.bits > 0 {
            self.words.push(self.cur as u32);
            self.cur = 0;
            self.bits = 0;
        }
    }

    fn bytes(&mut self, b: &[u8]) {
        for &x in b {
            self.emit(u64::from(x), 8);
        }
    }

    fn enter(&mut self, id: u64, width: u32) {
        self.emit(1, self.width()); // ENTER_SUBBLOCK
        self.vbr(id, 8);
        self.vbr(u64::from(width), 4);
        self.align();
        self.words.push(0);
        self.stack.push((width, self.words.len()));
    }

    fn exit(&mut self) {
        self.emit(0, self.width()); // END_BLOCK
        self.align();
        let (_, start) = self.stack.pop().expect("open block");
        self.words[start - 1] = (self.words.len() - start) as u32;
    }

    /// An unabbreviated record.
    fn record(&mut self, code: u64, ops: &[u64]) {
        self.emit(3, self.width());
        self.vbr(code, 6);
        self.vbr(ops.len() as u64, 6);
        for &o in ops {
            self.vbr(o, 6);
        }
    }

    fn finish(mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.align();
        self.words.iter().flat_map(|w| w.to_le_bytes()).collect()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn vbr_and_blocks() {
        let mut w = Writer::default();
        w.vbr(5, 6);
        w.vbr(100, 6); // two chunks: 100 = 0b1100100 -> 0b100100 | 32, then 3
        assert_eq!(w.cur, 5 | (0b10_0100 << 6) | (3 << 12));
        let mut w = Writer::default();
        w.enter(8, 3);
        w.record(1, &[1]);
        w.exit();
        let bytes = w.finish();
        // header word, length word, one record word, end word.
        assert_eq!(bytes.len() % 4, 0);
        assert_eq!(u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[4..8].try_into().unwrap()), 1);
        assert_eq!(signed(-3), 7);
        assert_eq!(signed(2), 4);
    }

    /// A structured shader's shape: `stages` if/else diamonds in a row, each
    /// merge with one phi per register (as the lowering makes them), then a
    /// loop, and a tail that reads only the first `read` registers.
    fn synthetic(regs: usize, stages: usize, read: usize) -> Module {
        let mut m = Module::default();
        let i32t = m.int(32);
        let void = m.void();
        let fty = m.func_ty(i32t, vec![i32t, i32t]);
        let f = m.function("dx.op.synthetic", fty, Some(Attr::ReadNone), false);
        let main_ty = m.func_ty(void, vec![]);
        m.function("main", main_ty, None, true);
        let mut b = m.new_block();
        let mut cur: Vec<V> = (0..regs).map(|r| m.i32(r as u32)).collect();
        for s in 0..stages {
            let c = m.cmp(b, pred::EQ, cur[0], cur[s % regs]);
            let (t, e, j) = (m.new_block(), m.new_block(), m.new_block());
            m.terminate(b, Term::CondBr(c, t, e));
            let x = m.call(t, f, vec![cur[s % regs], cur[(s + 1) % regs]]);
            m.terminate(t, Term::Br(j));
            m.terminate(e, Term::Br(j));
            cur = (0..regs)
                .map(|r| {
                    let p = m.phi(j, i32t);
                    let tv = if r == s % regs { x } else { cur[r] };
                    m.set_phi(p, vec![(tv, t), (cur[r], e)]);
                    p
                })
                .collect();
            b = j;
        }
        // A loop: header phis fed back from an empty latch (which is folded).
        let (head, body, latch, exit) =
            (m.new_block(), m.new_block(), m.new_block(), m.new_block());
        m.terminate(b, Term::Br(head));
        let phis: Vec<V> = (0..regs).map(|_| m.phi(head, i32t)).collect();
        let one = m.i32(1);
        let stepped: Vec<V> = phis
            .iter()
            .map(|&p| m.bin(body, Bin::Add, p, one))
            .collect();
        let c = m.cmp(body, pred::IULT, stepped[0], cur[0]);
        m.terminate(head, Term::Br(body));
        m.terminate(body, Term::CondBr(c, latch, exit));
        m.terminate(latch, Term::Br(head));
        for r in 0..regs {
            m.set_phi(phis[r], vec![(cur[r], b), (stepped[r], latch)]);
        }
        let mut acc = stepped[0];
        for &v in &stepped[1..read.max(1)] {
            acc = m.bin(exit, Bin::Add, acc, v);
        }
        let _ = m.call(exit, f, vec![acc, cur[0]]);
        m.terminate(exit, Term::Ret);
        m
    }

    /// FNV-1a, to pin a written module's exact bytes.
    fn fnv(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
        bytes.iter().fold(0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325, |h, &b| {
            (h ^ u64::from(b)).wrapping_mul(0x0100_0000_01b3)
        })
    }

    /// Liveness as `write` computed it before the worklist: whole passes over
    /// the instructions until one changes nothing.
    fn live_by_passes(m: &Module) -> Vec<bool> {
        let mut live = vec![false; m.insts.len()];
        for b in &m.blocks {
            for &i in &b.body {
                live[i as usize] = true;
            }
            if let Some(Term::CondBr(V::Inst(c), ..)) = b.term {
                live[c as usize] = true;
            }
        }
        let mut changed = true;
        while changed {
            changed = false;
            for (i, inst) in m.insts.iter().enumerate() {
                if live[i] {
                    for_each_operand(&inst.op, |v| {
                        if let V::Inst(j) = v
                            && !live[j as usize]
                        {
                            live[j as usize] = true;
                            changed = true;
                        }
                    });
                }
            }
        }
        live
    }

    #[test]
    fn worklist_liveness_matches_passes() {
        for (regs, stages, read) in [(1, 0, 1), (1, 1, 1), (4, 3, 1), (8, 17, 3), (16, 40, 16)] {
            let m = synthetic(regs, stages, read);
            let live = m.live();
            assert_eq!(live, live_by_passes(&m), "{regs} regs x {stages} stages");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn unread_phis_are_dropped() {
        let mut m = Module::default();
        let i32t = m.int(32);
        let (entry, join) = (m.new_block(), m.new_block());
        let (a, b) = (m.i32(1), m.i32(2));
        m.terminate(entry, Term::Br(join));
        let read = m.phi(join, i32t);
        let unread = m.phi(join, i32t);
        // A cycle of phis that only feed each other stays dead.
        let cyc_a = m.phi(join, i32t);
        let cyc_b = m.phi(join, i32t);
        m.set_phi(read, vec![(a, entry)]);
        m.set_phi(unread, vec![(b, entry)]);
        m.set_phi(cyc_a, vec![(cyc_b, entry)]);
        m.set_phi(cyc_b, vec![(cyc_a, entry)]);
        let sum = m.bin(join, Bin::Add, read, b);
        m.terminate(join, Term::Ret);
        let ids = |v: V| match v {
            V::Inst(i) => i as usize,
            _ => unreachable!(),
        };
        let live = m.live();
        assert!(live[ids(read)] && live[ids(sum)]);
        assert!(!live[ids(unread)] && !live[ids(cyc_a)] && !live[ids(cyc_b)]);
        assert_eq!(live, live_by_passes(&m));
    }

    #[test]
    fn successors_of_each_terminator() {
        assert!(successors(None).is_empty());
        assert!(successors(Some(Term::Ret)).is_empty());
        assert_eq!(&*successors(Some(Term::Br(7))), &[7]);
        assert_eq!(&*successors(Some(Term::CondBr(V::Const(0), 3, 5))), &[3, 5]);
    }

    /// The written bytes are pinned to what the writer produced before the
    /// worklist and the reused record buffers.
    #[test]
    fn written_bytes_unchanged() {
        for ((regs, stages, read), len, hash) in [
            ((64, 64, 64), 38_916, 0x9586_730c_f953_4a45),
            ((128, 256, 32), 295_952, 0x89e5_de2d_64f0_8785),
        ] {
            let bytes = synthetic(regs, stages, read).write();
            assert_eq!((bytes.len(), fnv(&bytes)), (len, hash), "{regs}x{stages}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    #[ignore = "benchmark: cargo test --release -p victory-shader bitcode -- --ignored --nocapture"]
    fn bench_write() {
        for (regs, stages, read) in [(64, 64, 64), (128, 256, 32), (256, 512, 256)] {
            let m = synthetic(regs, stages, read);
            let bytes = m.write();
            let runs = 5;
            let t = std::time::Instant::now();
            for _ in 0..runs {
                std::hint::black_box(m.write());
            }
            let per = t.elapsed() / runs;
            println!(
                "write {regs} regs x {stages} stages ({} insts): {per:?}, {} bytes, fnv {:#018x}",
                m.insts.len(),
                bytes.len(),
                fnv(&bytes)
            );
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-shader/src/emit/bitcode/census.rs`:

```rs
//! Counts of a module's instructions by kind (a diagnostic): what a
//! translated program costs before the driver's compiler sees it.
//!
//! `VICTORY_SHADER_CENSUS` (any value) turns the counting on; the counts of
//! the module a thread wrote last are read with [`take`]. The `translate`
//! command writes them as a table (see `apps/victory/src/translate.rs`).

use super::{Cast, Module, Op, Tag, Term, V};
use std::cell::RefCell;

/// The kinds, in the order of [`Census::counts`].
pub const KINDS: [&str; 26] = [
    "total",
    "arith",
    "math_call",
    "bitcast",
    "cast",
    "select",
    "guard_select",
    "phi",
    "extract",
    "buffer_load",
    "cbuffer_load",
    "texture_read",
    "lds_load",
    "buffer_store",
    "lds_store",
    "atomic",
    "handle",
    "annotate",
    "dimensions",
    "barrier",
    "wave_op",
    "io_other",
    "gep",
    "clamp",
    "loop_counter",
    "blocks",
];

/// Instruction counts of one written module, by [`KINDS`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Census {
    pub counts: [u32; KINDS.len()],
}

thread_local! {
    /// The modules this thread wrote since the last [`take`]: the length and
    /// a hash of each one's bitcode, with its counts (a program may be
    /// emitted in several forms before one is kept).
    static WRITTEN: RefCell<Vec<(usize, u64, Census)>> = const { RefCell::new(Vec::new()) };
}

fn fnv(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    bytes.iter().fold(0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325, |h, &b| {
        (h ^ u64::from(b)).wrapping_mul(0x0100_0000_01b3)
    })
}

/// Whether modules are counted (`VICTORY_SHADER_CENSUS` set).
pub fn enabled() -> bool {
    static ON: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_SHADER_CENSUS").is_some())
}

/// The counts of the module whose bitcode the container `dxil` holds, if
/// this thread wrote it since the last call (which forgets the others).
pub fn take(dxil: &[u8]) -> Option<Census> {
    let written = WRITTEN.with(|l| std::mem::take(&mut *l.borrow_mut()));
    let at = dxil.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"BC\xC0\xDE")?;
    written
        .into_iter()
        .rev()
        .find(|(len, hash, _)| dxil.get(at..at + len).is_some_and(|b| fnv(b) == *hash))
        .map(|w| w.2)
}

/// Counts `m`, whose written form is `bitcode`, and keeps the result for
/// [`take`].
pub(crate) fn note(m: &Module, bitcode: &[u8]) {
    if !enabled() {
        return;
    }
    let c = m.census();
    WRITTEN.with(|l| l.borrow_mut().push((bitcode.len(), fnv(bitcode), c)));
}

fn kind(name: &str) -> usize {
    let n = name.strip_prefix("dx.op.").unwrap_or(name);
    let n = n.split('.').next().unwrap_or(n);
    let k = |s: &str| KINDS.iter().position(|k| *k == s).expect("kind");
    match n {
        "unary" | "binary" | "tertiary" | "unaryBits" | "legacyF16ToF32" | "legacyF32ToF16"
        | "isSpecialFloat" | "dot2" | "dot3" | "dot4" | "quaternary" => k("math_call"),
        "bufferLoad" | "rawBufferLoad" => k("buffer_load"),
        "cbufferLoadLegacy" | "cbufferLoad" => k("cbuffer_load"),
        "bufferStore" | "rawBufferStore" | "textureStore" => k("buffer_store"),
        "atomicBinOp" | "atomicCompareExchange" => k("atomic"),
        "createHandle" | "createHandleFromBinding" | "createHandleFromHeap" => k("handle"),
        "annotateHandle" => k("annotate"),
        "getDimensions" => k("dimensions"),
        "barrier" => k("barrier"),
        _ if n.starts_with("wave") || n.starts_with("quad") => k("wave_op"),
        _ if n.starts_with("textureLoad")
            || n.starts_with("sample")
            || n.starts_with("textureGather")
            || n.starts_with("calculateLOD") =>
        {
            k("texture_read")
        }
        _ => k("io_other"),
    }
}

impl Module {
    /// The instructions [`Module::write`] writes, by kind.
    pub(crate) fn census(&self) -> Census {
        let k = |s: &str| KINDS.iter().position(|k| *k == s).expect("kind");
        let call_kind: Vec<usize> = self.funcs.iter().map(|f| kind(&f.name)).collect();
        let live = self.live();
        // The blocks `write` lays out: those reached from the entry.
        let mut seen = vec![false; self.blocks.len()];
        let mut stack = vec![0usize];
        if !self.blocks.is_empty() {
            seen[0] = true;
        }
        while let Some(b) = stack.pop() {
            for &s in super::successors(self.blocks[b].term).iter() {
                if !seen[s] {
                    seen[s] = true;
                    stack.push(s);
                }
            }
        }
        let mut c = Census::default();
        for (b, blk) in self.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            if !seen[b] {
                continue;
            }
            c.counts[k("blocks")] += 1;
            let _: Option<Term> = blk.term;
            for &i in blk
                .phis
                .iter()
                .filter(|&&i| live[i as usize])
                .chain(&blk.body)
            {
                c.counts[0] += 1;
                let at = match &self.insts[i as usize].op {
                    Op::Bin(..) | Op::Cmp(..) => k("arith"),
                    Op::Cast(Cast::Bitcast, _) => k("bitcast"),
                    Op::Cast(..) => k("cast"),
                    Op::Select(..) => k("select"),
                    Op::Extract(..) => k("extract"),
                    Op::Phi(_) => k("phi"),
                    Op::Gep(..) => k("gep"),
                    Op::Load(_) => k("lds_load"),
                    Op::Store(..) => k("lds_store"),
                    Op::AtomicRmw(..) | Op::CmpXchg(..) => k("atomic"),
                    Op::Call(f, _) => call_kind[*f as usize],
                };
                c.counts[at] += 1;
                match self.tags.get(&i) {
                    Some(Tag::Guard) => c.counts[k("guard_select")] += 1,
                    Some(Tag::Clamp) => c.counts[k("clamp")] += 1,
                    Some(Tag::Counter) => c.counts[k("loop_counter")] += 1,
                    None => {}
                }
                let _ = V::Inst(i);
            }
        }
        c
    }
}

```

`crates/victory-shader/src/emit/bitcode/opt.rs`:

```rs
//! Clean-up of a finished module before it is written: the lowering emits
//! one instruction after another as the console code names them, and
//! nothing stands between it and the driver's compiler. Every pass here is
//! exact: the module computes the same values and has the same effects for
//! every input.
//!
//! - [`DEAD`]: instructions without an effect whose result nothing reads
//!   are left out (the lowering computes every dword of every register a
//!   console instruction writes; a guarded write reads the register's old
//!   value whether anything reads the new one or not).
//! - [`FOLD`]: integer arithmetic on constants is done here, and identities
//!   (`x + 0`, `x & -1`, a select between a value and itself, a cast there
//!   and back, a join of one value) give their operand. Float arithmetic is
//!   left alone: `x + 0.0` and `x * 1.0` are not `x` for every `x`.
//! - [`REUSE`]: an instruction without an effect whose operands are those
//!   of an earlier one that every path to it has run gives that one's
//!   result (a descriptor handle made again in each block, an index clamped
//!   again, a register read as a float again).
//! - [`FACTS`]: in the blocks only one side of a branch leads to, the
//!   branch's condition is that side's constant, and so is what the
//!   condition was made of (both terms of an `and` that held, the opposite
//!   comparison). The lowering branches on a lane's condition and then
//!   guards each instruction behind the branch with the same condition.
//! - [`LOADS`]: within a block, a read of the same place as an earlier read
//!   gives that one's result while no store, atomic, barrier or other call
//!   with an effect stands between them (another thread's unsynchronised
//!   store may fall between any two reads or before both: the title's code
//!   cannot tell which).
//!
//! Which passes run is `emit::shader_opt()` (`VICTORY_SHADER_OPT`), part of
//! the translation and so of the shader cache's key.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use super::{
    Attr, Bin, Cast, Const, Func, MdDef, Module, Op, Term, Ty, TypeDef, V, for_each_operand, pred,
    successors,
};

/// Dead-code elimination.
pub const DEAD: u32 = 1;
/// Constants folded, identities removed.
pub const FOLD: u32 = 2;
/// One instruction for one value.
pub const REUSE: u32 = 4;
/// What a branch taken says about its condition.
pub const FACTS: u32 = 8;
/// One read for one place within a block, while nothing is stored.
pub const LOADS: u32 = 16;
/// Not a pass over the module: the lowering of a first-lane read in a
/// wave64 program run as two host waves skips the exchange that asks which
/// half has a lane where every lane is in EXEC (`lower.rs`,
/// `v_readfirstlane_b32`).
pub const FIRST: u32 = 32;
/// Not a pass over the module either: the lowering reads the dwords of one
/// console load (`s_buffer_load_dwordx2` to `x16` from an SRV, a
/// `global_load_dwordx2` to `x4`) by one call for every four of them, not
/// by a call each (`lower.rs`, `raw_dwords`). The same bytes are read.
pub const WIDE: u32 = 64;
/// The passes over the module.
pub const MODULE: u32 = DEAD | FOLD | REUSE | FACTS | LOADS;
/// Every pass.
pub const ALL: u32 = MODULE | FIRST | WIDE;
/// The passes that run when nothing says which: every one but [`WIDE`],
/// which no card has shown a gain for yet (`VICTORY_SHADER_OPT=127` asks
/// for it).
pub const DEFAULT: u32 = ALL & !WIDE;

/// What the instructions a module writes use, of the features a shader
/// declares by flag (the validator's "flags must match usage").
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct Usage {
    /// A wave or quad operation.
    pub wave_ops: bool,
    /// A 64-bit integer, as a result or an operand.
    pub int64: bool,
    /// A typed load of several components from a UAV.
    pub typed_uav_loads: bool,
    /// A handle from the view heap.
    pub heap_views: bool,
    /// A handle from the sampler heap.
    pub heap_samplers: bool,
    /// A 64-bit atomic.
    pub atomic64: bool,
}

/// What makes two instructions without an effect the same value.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
enum Key {
    Bin(u8, V, V),
    Cast(u8, Ty, V),
    Cmp(u8, V, V),
    Select(V, V, V),
    Extract(V, u32),
    Call(u32, Vec<V>),
    Gep(Ty, V, Vec<V>),
    Load(V),
}

/// The blocks reached from the entry, each after the blocks that dominate
/// it, and each block's children in the dominator tree.
struct Tree {
    order: Vec<usize>,
    children: Vec<Vec<usize>>,
    /// Per block: the reached blocks that branch to it, once per edge.
    preds: Vec<Vec<usize>>,
}

/// The comparison that holds exactly when `p` does not (floats 0-15,
/// integers 32-41).
fn opposite(p: u8) -> u8 {
    match p {
        0..=15 => 15 - p,
        pred::EQ => pred::NE,
        pred::NE => pred::EQ,
        pred::IUGT => pred::IULE,
        pred::IULE => pred::IUGT,
        pred::IUGE => pred::IULT,
        pred::IULT => pred::IUGE,
        pred::SGT => pred::SLE,
        pred::SLE => pred::SGT,
        pred::SGE => pred::SLT,
        _ => pred::SGE,
    }
}

/// What holds in the block being walked: values that are a known bit there,
/// and comparisons (by their operands) with a known outcome.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Facts {
    bits: HashMap<V, bool>,
    compares: HashMap<(u8, V, V), bool>,
}

/// The facts a block added, to forget when its part of the tree is done.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Learned {
    bits: Vec<V>,
    compares: Vec<(u8, V, V)>,
}

fn mask(bits: u32) -> u64 {
    if bits >= 64 { !0 } else { (1 << bits) - 1 }
}

/// `x` of `bits` bits as a signed number.
fn signed(bits: u32, x: u64) -> i64 {
    if bits < 64 && x >> (bits - 1) & 1 != 0 {
        (x | !mask(bits)) as i64
    } else {
        x as i64
    }
}

/// What `v` stands for after the replacements so far.
fn resolve(repl: &[Option<V>], mut v: V) -> V {
    while let V::Inst(i) = v {
        match repl[i as usize] {
            Some(r) => v = r,
            None => break,
        }
    }
    v
}

/// Replaces every value `op` reads by `f` of it.
fn map_operands(op: &mut Op, mut f: impl FnMut(V) -> V) {
    match op {
        Op::Bin(_, a, b) | Op::Cmp(_, a, b) | Op::Store(a, b) | Op::AtomicRmw(_, a, b) => {
            *a = f(*a);
            *b = f(*b);
        }
        Op::Cast(_, v) | Op::Extract(v, _) | Op::Load(v) => *v = f(*v),
        Op::Select(a, b, c) | Op::CmpXchg(a, b, c) => {
            *a = f(*a);
            *b = f(*b);
            *c = f(*c);
        }
        Op::Call(_, args) => args.iter_mut().for_each(|a| *a = f(*a)),
        Op::Phi(inc) => inc.iter_mut().for_each(|x| x.0 = f(x.0)),
        Op::Gep(_, p, idx) => {
            *p = f(*p);
            idx.iter_mut().for_each(|i| *i = f(*i));
        }
    }
}

/// What a call does besides returning its result.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum Effect {
    /// Nothing, and the result depends on the arguments alone for the whole
    /// run of the shader (arithmetic, handles, inputs, constant buffers,
    /// resource sizes).
    Pure,
    /// Nothing, but the result depends on memory a store may change
    /// (buffer and texture reads).
    Reads,
    /// Nothing, but the result depends on which lanes run the instruction
    /// (wave and quad operations).
    Lanes,
    /// Stores, atomics, barriers, outputs, discards: always kept.
    Writes,
}

pub(super) fn effect(f: &Func) -> Effect {
    let name = f.name.strip_prefix("dx.op.").unwrap_or(&f.name);
    match f.attr {
        Some(Attr::ReadNone) => Effect::Pure,
        // A shader cannot write a constant buffer or resize a resource.
        Some(Attr::ReadOnly)
            if name.starts_with("cbufferLoadLegacy") || name.starts_with("getDimensions") =>
        {
            Effect::Pure
        }
        Some(Attr::ReadOnly) if name.starts_with("wave") => Effect::Lanes,
        Some(Attr::ReadOnly) => Effect::Reads,
        // Declared with the attribute of calls that have effects, and have
        // none: they read the other lanes' values.
        _ if name.starts_with("wave") || name.starts_with("quad") => Effect::Lanes,
        _ => Effect::Writes,
    }
}

impl Module {
    /// Runs the clean-up passes named in `passes` ([`ALL`]: every one).
    pub(crate) fn optimise(&mut self, passes: u32) {
        if passes & (FOLD | REUSE | FACTS | LOADS) != 0 {
            // Values merged in one round can make two joins the same in
            // the next (a loop's registers that only go round), and a
            // branch that goes one way leaves blocks with one way in.
            for _ in 0..4 {
                let mut changed = self.merge(passes);
                if passes & FOLD != 0 {
                    changed |= self.prune();
                }
                if !changed {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        if passes & DEAD != 0 {
            self.drop_dead();
        }
    }

    /// Per function: what a call of it does.
    pub(super) fn effects(&self) -> Vec<Effect> {
        self.funcs.iter().map(effect).collect()
    }

    /// The blocks reached from the entry.
    pub(super) fn reached(&self) -> Vec<bool> {
        let mut seen = vec![false; self.blocks.len()];
        if self.blocks.is_empty() {
            return seen;
        }
        let mut stack = vec![0usize];
        seen[0] = true;
        while let Some(b) = stack.pop() {
            for &s in successors(self.blocks[b].term).iter() {
                if !seen[s] {
                    seen[s] = true;
                    stack.push(s);
                }
            }
        }
        seen
    }

    fn dominator_tree(&self) -> Tree {
        let n = self.blocks.len();
        let succs = |b: usize| successors(self.blocks[b].term);
        // Reverse postorder, as `write` lays the blocks out.
        let mut seen = vec![false; n];
        let mut post = Vec::new();
        let mut stack = vec![(0usize, 0usize)];
        seen[0] = true;
        while let Some(top) = stack.last_mut() {
            let (b, k) = *top;
            top.1 += 1;
            match succs(b).get(k) {
                Some(&s) if !seen[s] => {
                    seen[s] = true;
                    stack.push((s, 0));
                }
                Some(_) => {}
                None => {
                    post.push(b);
                    stack.pop();
                }
            }
        }
        post.reverse();
        let order = post;
        let mut number = vec![usize::MAX; n];
        for (k, &b) in order.iter().enumerate() {
            number[b] = k;
        }
        let mut preds = vec![Vec::new(); n];
        for &b in &order {
            for &s in succs(b).iter() {
                preds[s].push(b);
            }
        }
        // Immediate dominators (Cooper, Harvey and Kennedy's iteration).
        let mut idom = vec![usize::MAX; n];
        idom[0] = 0;
        let mut changed = true;
        while changed {
            changed = false;
            for &b in &order[1..] {
                let mut new = usize::MAX;
                for &p in &preds[b] {
                    if idom[p] == usize::MAX {
                        continue;
                    }
                    if new == usize::MAX {
                        new = p;
                        continue;
                    }
                    let (mut x, mut y) = (p, new);
                    while x != y {
                        while number[x] > number[y] {
                            x = idom[x];
                        }
                        while number[y] > number[x] {
                            y = idom[y];
                        }
                    }
                    new = x;
                }
                if idom[b] != new {
                    idom[b] = new;
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
        }
        let mut children = vec![Vec::new(); n];
        for &b in &order[1..] {
            children[idom[b]].push(b);
        }
        Tree {
            order,
            children,
            preds,
        }
    }

    /// Notes that `v` (an i1) is `holds` in the block being walked, and what
    /// follows from it for the values `v` was made of.
    fn learn(&self, v: V, holds: bool, facts: &mut Facts, learned: &mut Learned, depth: u32) {
        let V::Inst(i) = v else { return };
        if facts.bits.contains_key(&v) {
            return;
        }
        facts.bits.insert(v, holds);
        learned.bits.push(v);
        if depth == 0 {
            return;
        }
        match self.insts[i as usize].op {
            // Both terms of an `and` that holds hold; neither of an `or`
            // that does not.
            Op::Bin(Bin::And, a, b) if holds => {
                self.learn(a, true, facts, learned, depth - 1);
                self.learn(b, true, facts, learned, depth - 1);
            }
            Op::Bin(Bin::Or, a, b) if !holds => {
                self.learn(a, false, facts, learned, depth - 1);
                self.learn(b, false, facts, learned, depth - 1);
            }
            Op::Bin(Bin::Xor, a, b) => {
                let (x, k) = match (self.int_k(a), self.int_k(b)) {
                    (None, Some((1, k))) => (a, k),
                    (Some((1, k)), None) => (b, k),
                    _ => return,
                };
                self.learn(x, holds != (k != 0), facts, learned, depth - 1);
            }
            // The opposite comparison of the same operands.
            Op::Cmp(p, a, b) => {
                let key = (opposite(p), a, b);
                if let std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Vacant(e) = facts.compares.entry(key) {
                    e.insert(!holds);
                    learned.compares.push(key);
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    fn int_bits(&self, ty: Ty) -> Option<u32> {
        match self.types[ty.0 as usize] {
            TypeDef::Int(bits) => Some(bits),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// An integer constant's width and value (the bits of that width).
    fn int_k(&self, v: V) -> Option<(u32, u64)> {
        let V::Const(i) = v else { return None };
        let (ty, Const::Int(x)) = &self.consts[i as usize] else {
            return None;
        };
        let bits = self.int_bits(*ty)?;
        Some((bits, *x as u64 & mask(bits)))
    }

    /// The constant `x` of the integer type `ty`, kept sign-extended as
    /// [`Module::i32`] and [`Module::bool`] keep theirs.
    fn k(&mut self, ty: Ty, bits: u32, x: u64) -> V {
        self.int_const(ty, signed(bits, x & mask(bits)))
    }

    /// The value instruction `i` is known to have without it, if any: a
    /// constant or an earlier value. May instead give `i` simpler operands
    /// (`changed` says so).
    fn simplify(&mut self, i: u32, changed: &mut bool) -> Option<V> {
        let ty = self.insts[i as usize].ty;
        match self.insts[i as usize].op {
            Op::Bin(op, a, b) => {
                // Floats: `x + 0.0`, `x * 1.0` and the like are not `x` for
                // every `x` (a negative zero, a signalling NaN).
                let bits = self.int_bits(ty)?;
                let (ka, kb) = (self.int_k(a).map(|k| k.1), self.int_k(b).map(|k| k.1));
                let all = mask(bits);
                if let (Some(x), Some(y)) = (ka, kb) {
                    // A shift by the width or more and a division by zero
                    // have no defined result: left as they are.
                    let amount = u32::try_from(y).ok().filter(|&y| y < bits);
                    let r = match op {
                        Bin::Add => x.wrapping_add(y),
                        Bin::Sub => x.wrapping_sub(y),
                        Bin::Mul => x.wrapping_mul(y),
                        Bin::And => x & y,
                        Bin::Or => x | y,
                        Bin::Xor => x ^ y,
                        Bin::Shl => x << amount?,
                        Bin::LShr => x >> amount?,
                        Bin::AShr => (signed(bits, x) >> amount?) as u64,
                        Bin::UDiv if y != 0 => x / y,
                        Bin::URem if y != 0 => x % y,
                        _ => return None,
                    };
                    return Some(self.k(ty, bits, r));
                }
                match (op, ka, kb) {
                    (
                        Bin::Add | Bin::Sub | Bin::Or | Bin::Xor | Bin::Shl | Bin::LShr | Bin::AShr,
                        _,
                        Some(0),
                    ) => Some(a),
                    (Bin::Add | Bin::Or | Bin::Xor, Some(0), _) => Some(b),
                    (Bin::Mul | Bin::UDiv, _, Some(1)) => Some(a),
                    (Bin::Mul, Some(1), _) => Some(b),
                    (Bin::Mul | Bin::And, _, Some(0)) => Some(b),
                    (Bin::Mul | Bin::And, Some(0), _) => Some(a),
                    (Bin::And, _, Some(m)) if m == all => Some(a),
                    (Bin::And, Some(m), _) if m == all => Some(b),
                    (Bin::Or, _, Some(m)) if m == all => Some(b),
                    (Bin::Or, Some(m), _) if m == all => Some(a),
                    (Bin::And | Bin::Or, _, _) if a == b => Some(a),
                    _ => None,
                }
            }
            Op::Cmp(p, a, b) if p <= pred::TRUE => {
                // Two float constants compare one way (`v_mul_legacy` asks
                // whether its constant factor is zero).
                let (V::Const(x), V::Const(y)) = (a, b) else {
                    return None;
                };
                let (Const::Float(x), Const::Float(y)) =
                    (&self.consts[x as usize].1, &self.consts[y as usize].1)
                else {
                    return None;
                };
                let (x, y) = (f32::from_bits(*x), f32::from_bits(*y));
                let unordered = x.is_nan() || y.is_nan();
                // Bits 0-2 of a predicate: equal, greater, less; bit 3:
                // or unordered.
                let holds = if unordered {
                    p & 8 != 0
                } else {
                    (p & 1 != 0 && x == y) || (p & 2 != 0 && x > y) || (p & 4 != 0 && x < y)
                };
                Some(self.bool(holds))
            }
            Op::Cmp(p, a, b) => {
                if !(pred::EQ..=pred::SLE).contains(&p) {
                    return None;
                }
                let holds = |x: u64, y: u64, bits: u32| {
                    let (sx, sy) = (signed(bits, x), signed(bits, y));
                    match p {
                        pred::EQ => x == y,
                        pred::NE => x != y,
                        pred::IUGT => x > y,
                        pred::IUGE => x >= y,
                        pred::IULT => x < y,
                        pred::IULE => x <= y,
                        pred::SGT => sx > sy,
                        pred::SGE => sx >= sy,
                        pred::SLT => sx < sy,
                        _ => sx <= sy,
                    }
                };
                if let (Some((bits, x)), Some((_, y))) = (self.int_k(a), self.int_k(b)) {
                    return Some(self.bool(holds(x, y, bits)));
                }
                if a == b {
                    return Some(self.bool(holds(0, 0, 32)));
                }
                // A bit widened and tested again is the bit.
                if p == pred::NE
                    && self.int_k(b).is_some_and(|k| k.1 == 0)
                    && let V::Inst(z) = a
                    && let Op::Cast(Cast::ZExt, x) = self.insts[z as usize].op
                    && self.type_of(x) == ty
                {
                    return Some(x);
                }
                None
            }
            Op::Select(c, mut t, mut f) => {
                if let Some((_, c)) = self.int_k(c) {
                    return Some(if c != 0 { t } else { f });
                }
                // Under the same condition an inner select is one of its
                // operands (two guarded writes of one register in a row).
                let mut inner = false;
                while let V::Inst(x) = t
                    && let Op::Select(c2, t2, _) = self.insts[x as usize].op
                    && c2 == c
                {
                    (t, inner) = (t2, true);
                }
                while let V::Inst(x) = f
                    && let Op::Select(c2, _, f2) = self.insts[x as usize].op
                    && c2 == c
                {
                    (f, inner) = (f2, true);
                }
                if t == f {
                    return Some(t);
                }
                if self.int_bits(ty) == Some(1)
                    && self.int_k(t).is_some_and(|k| k.1 == 1)
                    && self.int_k(f).is_some_and(|k| k.1 == 0)
                {
                    return Some(c);
                }
                if inner {
                    self.insts[i as usize].op = Op::Select(c, t, f);
                    *changed = true;
                }
                None
            }
            Op::Cast(op, x) => {
                let from = self.type_of(x);
                let through = match x {
                    V::Inst(y) => match self.insts[y as usize].op {
                        Op::Cast(op2, z) => Some((op2, z)),
                        _ => None,
                    },
                    _ => None,
                };
                match op {
                    Cast::Bitcast => {
                        if from == ty {
                            return Some(x);
                        }
                        // There and back: the bits are the same.
                        if let Some((Cast::Bitcast, z)) = through
                            && self.type_of(z) == ty
                        {
                            return Some(z);
                        }
                        let V::Const(c) = x else { return None };
                        let to_float = matches!(self.types[ty.0 as usize], TypeDef::Float);
                        match self.consts[c as usize].1 {
                            Const::Int(bits) if to_float && self.int_bits(from) == Some(32) => {
                                Some(self.f32(bits as u32))
                            }
                            Const::Float(bits) if self.int_bits(ty) == Some(32) => {
                                Some(self.int_const(ty, i64::from(bits as i32)))
                            }
                            _ => None,
                        }
                    }
                    Cast::ZExt | Cast::SExt | Cast::Trunc => {
                        let to = self.int_bits(ty)?;
                        if let Some((bits, k)) = self.int_k(x) {
                            let k = if op == Cast::SExt {
                                signed(bits, k) as u64
                            } else {
                                k
                            };
                            return Some(self.k(ty, to, k));
                        }
                        // Widened and narrowed again.
                        if op == Cast::Trunc
                            && let Some((Cast::ZExt | Cast::SExt, z)) = through
                            && self.type_of(z) == ty
                        {
                            return Some(z);
                        }
                        None
                    }
                    _ => None,
                }
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// What kind of instruction `i` is for merging.
    fn class(&self, effects: &[Effect], i: u32) -> Effect {
        match &self.insts[i as usize].op {
            Op::Bin(..)
            | Op::Cast(..)
            | Op::Cmp(..)
            | Op::Select(..)
            | Op::Extract(..)
            | Op::Gep(..) => Effect::Pure,
            Op::Load(p) => {
                // A constant table reads the same whatever is stored.
                let base = match *p {
                    V::Inst(g) => match &self.insts[g as usize].op {
                        Op::Gep(_, base, _) => *base,
                        _ => *p,
                    },
                    _ => *p,
                };
                match base {
                    V::Global(g) if self.globals[g as usize].init.is_some() => Effect::Pure,
                    _ => Effect::Reads,
                }
            }
            Op::Store(..) | Op::AtomicRmw(..) | Op::CmpXchg(..) => Effect::Writes,
            Op::Phi(_) => Effect::Lanes,
            Op::Call(f, _) => effects[*f as usize],
        }
    }

    fn key(&self, i: u32) -> Option<Key> {
        let inst = &self.insts[i as usize];
        Some(match &inst.op {
            Op::Bin(op, a, b) => {
                // Integer sums, products and bit operations whichever way
                // round; float ones as written (which NaN an operation of
                // two NaNs gives is the hardware's choice by operand).
                let commutes = matches!(op, Bin::Add | Bin::Mul | Bin::And | Bin::Or | Bin::Xor)
                    && self.int_bits(inst.ty).is_some();
                let (a, b) = if commutes && b < a {
                    (*b, *a)
                } else {
                    (*a, *b)
                };
                Key::Bin(*op as u8, a, b)
            }
            Op::Cast(op, v) => Key::Cast(*op as u8, inst.ty, *v),
            Op::Cmp(p, a, b) => Key::Cmp(*p, *a, *b),
            Op::Select(c, t, f) => Key::Select(*c, *t, *f),
            Op::Extract(a, n) => Key::Extract(*a, *n),
            Op::Call(f, args) => Key::Call(*f, args.clone()),
            Op::Gep(ty, p, idx) => Key::Gep(*ty, *p, idx.clone()),
            Op::Load(p) => Key::Load(*p),
            _ => return None,
        })
    }

    /// [`FOLD`], [`REUSE`], [`FACTS`] and [`LOADS`]: one walk over the
    /// dominator tree. Returns whether anything changed.
    fn merge(&mut self, passes: u32) -> bool {
        if self.blocks.is_empty() {
            return false;
        }
        let effects = self.effects();
        let tree = self.dominator_tree();
        let mut repl: Vec<Option<V>> = vec![None; self.insts.len()];
        let mut changed = false;
        // Joins of one value: until none is left (one gone can leave
        // another with one value).
        if passes & FOLD != 0 {
            let mut again = true;
            while again {
                again = false;
                for &b in &tree.order {
                    for &p in &self.blocks[b].phis {
                        if repl[p as usize].is_some() {
                            continue;
                        }
                        let Op::Phi(incoming) = &self.insts[p as usize].op else {
                            continue;
                        };
                        let mut one = None;
                        let mut same = true;
                        for &(v, _) in incoming {
                            let v = resolve(&repl, v);
                            if v == V::Inst(p) {
                                continue;
                            }
                            match one {
                                None => one = Some(v),
                                Some(o) if o == v => {}
                                Some(_) => same = false,
                            }
                        }
                        if let (true, Some(v)) = (same, one) {
                            repl[p as usize] = Some(v);
                            again = true;
                            changed = true;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // The values every path to the block being walked has computed
        // (those of the blocks above it in the tree, and its own so far).
        let mut known: HashMap<Key, V> = HashMap::new();
        // The reads of the block being walked since its last store.
        let mut read: HashMap<Key, V> = HashMap::new();
        let mut facts = Facts::default();
        let (yes, no) = (self.bool(true), self.bool(false));
        enum Step {
            Enter(usize),
            Leave(Vec<Key>, Learned),
        }
        let mut steps = vec![Step::Enter(0)];
        while let Some(step) = steps.pop() {
            let b = match step {
                Step::Enter(b) => b,
                Step::Leave(keys, learned) => {
                    for k in keys {
                        known.remove(&k);
                    }
                    for v in learned.bits {
                        facts.bits.remove(&v);
                    }
                    for k in learned.compares {
                        facts.compares.remove(&k);
                    }
                    continue;
                }
            };
            let mut added = Vec::new();
            // Reached from one block alone, by one side of its branch: the
            // condition is that side's, here and in every block below.
            let mut learned = Learned::default();
            if passes & FACTS != 0
                && let [p] = tree.preds[b][..]
                && let Some(Term::CondBr(c, t, f)) = self.blocks[p].term
                && t != f
            {
                self.learn(resolve(&repl, c), b == t, &mut facts, &mut learned, 8);
            }
            let known_bit = |facts: &Facts, v: V| match facts.bits.get(&v) {
                Some(true) => yes,
                Some(false) => no,
                None => v,
            };
            read.clear();
            // Two joins of the same values from the same blocks are one.
            if passes & REUSE != 0 && self.blocks[b].phis.len() > 1 {
                let mut joins: HashMap<Vec<(usize, V)>, V> = HashMap::new();
                for &p in &self.blocks[b].phis {
                    if repl[p as usize].is_some() {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let ty = self.insts[p as usize].ty;
                    let Op::Phi(incoming) = &self.insts[p as usize].op else {
                        continue;
                    };
                    let mut key: Vec<(usize, V)> = incoming
                        .iter()
                        .map(|&(v, from)| (from, resolve(&repl, v)))
                        .collect();
                    key.sort();
                    // The type too: an undefined value of one type is not
                    // that of another.
                    key.push((ty.0 as usize, V::Global(u32::MAX)));
                    match joins.get(&key) {
                        Some(&first) => {
                            repl[p as usize] = Some(first);
                            changed = true;
                        }
                        None => {
                            joins.insert(key, V::Inst(p));
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            let body = std::mem::take(&mut self.blocks[b].body);
            let mut kept = Vec::with_capacity(body.len());
            for i in body {
                map_operands(&mut self.insts[i as usize].op, |v| {
                    let v = resolve(&repl, v);
                    let bit = known_bit(&facts, v);
                    changed |= bit != v;
                    bit
                });
                if let Op::Cmp(p, x, y) = self.insts[i as usize].op
                    && let Some(&holds) = facts.compares.get(&(p, x, y))
                {
                    repl[i as usize] = Some(if holds { yes } else { no });
                    changed = true;
                    continue;
                }
                if passes & FOLD != 0
                    && let Some(v) = self.simplify(i, &mut changed)
                {
                    repl[i as usize] = Some(v);
                    changed = true;
                    continue;
                }
                let class = self.class(&effects, i);
                if passes & REUSE != 0
                    && class == Effect::Pure
                    && let Some(key) = self.key(i)
                {
                    if let Some(&first) = known.get(&key) {
                        repl[i as usize] = Some(first);
                        changed = true;
                        continue;
                    }
                    known.insert(key.clone(), V::Inst(i));
                    added.push(key);
                }
                // Reads of memory, and wave operations (the same lanes run
                // the whole block): the block's own earlier one.
                if passes & LOADS != 0
                    && matches!(class, Effect::Reads | Effect::Lanes)
                    && let Some(key) = self.key(i)
                {
                    if let Some(&first) = read.get(&key) {
                        repl[i as usize] = Some(first);
                        changed = true;
                        continue;
                    }
                    read.insert(key, V::Inst(i));
                }
```
