```rs
            let aligned = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Sub, byte, within);
            let shift = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Shl, within, k3);
            let four = self.s.m.i32(4);
            let next = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Add, aligned, four);
            let ones = self.s.m.i32(if bits == 8 { 0xff } else { 0xffff });
            let zero = self.s.m.i32(0);
            let k8 = self.s.m.i32(8);
            let straddles = self.s.m.cmp(c, pred::EQ, within, k3);
            if !store {
                let mask = self.s.m.i8(1);
                let align = self.s.m.i32(4);
                let dword = |l: &mut Self, at: V| {
                    let r = l.s.op(
                        c,
                        "rawBufferLoad.f32",
                        Attr::ReadOnly,
                        l.s.t.res_ret,
                        139,
                        &[h, at, iu, mask, align],
                    );
                    let f = l.s.m.extract(c, r, 0);
                    l.as_int(f)
                };
                let low = dword(self, aligned);
                let mut x = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::LShr, low, shift);
                if bits == 16 {
                    let high = dword(self, next);
                    let high = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Shl, high, k8);
                    let high = self.s.m.select(c, straddles, high, zero);
                    x = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Or, x, high);
                }
                x = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::And, x, ones);
                if signed {
                    let up = self.s.m.i32(32 - bits);
                    x = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Shl, x, up);
                    x = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::AShr, x, up);
                }
                let Some(Operand::Vector { reg, .. }) = *data else {
                    return Err("a buffer result");
                };
                self.write(inst, Reg::V(reg), x, guard);
                return Ok(());
            }
            let d = data.as_ref().ok_or("buffer store data")?;
            let v = self.vgprs(inst, d, 1)?[0];
            let v = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::And, v, ones);
            let all = self.s.m.i32(u32::MAX);
            let clear = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Shl, ones, shift);
            let keep = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Xor, clear, all);
            let set = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Shl, v, shift);
            let keep_next = self.s.m.i32(0xffff_ff00);
            let set_next = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::LShr, v, k8);
            let (and, or) = (self.s.m.i32(1), self.s.m.i32(2));
            let i32t = self.s.t.i32;
            let at = self.begin_guarded(guard);
            for (op, x) in [(and, keep), (or, set)] {
                let args = [h, op, aligned, iu, iu, x];
                self.s
                    .op(self.cur, "atomicBinOp.i32", Attr::NoUnwind, i32t, 78, &args);
            }
            if bits == 16 {
                let second = self.begin_guarded(Some(straddles));
                for (op, x) in [(and, keep_next), (or, set_next)] {
                    let args = [h, op, next, iu, iu, x];
                    self.s
                        .op(self.cur, "atomicBinOp.i32", Attr::NoUnwind, i32t, 78, &args);
                }
                self.end_guarded(second, &[]);
            }
            self.end_guarded(at, &[]);
            return Ok(());
        }
        if let Some(op) = atomic {
            let d = data.as_ref().ok_or("buffer atomic data")?;
            let vals = self.vgprs(inst, d, if op == u32::MAX { 2 } else { 1 })?;
            let (h, coords) = match index {
                // A raw buffer (stride 1) read by index: the index is the byte.
                Some(index) if used.is_some_and(|u| u.stride == 1) => {
                    let byte = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Add, index, off);
                    (self.handle(site, src, false, (11 | u, 0))?, [byte, iu, iu])
                }
                Some(index) => {
                    let stride = used.map_or(0, |u| u.stride);
                    if stride < 4 || !stride.is_multiple_of(4) {
                        return Err("a structured buffer of unknown stride");
                    }
                    let h = self.handle(site, src, false, (12 | u, stride))?;
                    (h, [index, off, iu])
                }
                None => (self.handle(site, src, false, (11 | u, 0))?, [off, iu, iu]),
            };
            let Operand::Vector { reg, .. } = *d else {
                return Err("buffer atomic data");
            };
            let returns = matches!(inst.fields, Fields::Buffer { cache, .. } if cache.glc);
            let old = match inst.read(Reg::V(reg)) {
                Some(v) if returns => self.i32_of(v)?,
                _ => self.s.m.i32(0),
            };
            let at = self.begin_guarded(guard);
            let i32t = self.s.t.i32;
            let r = if op == u32::MAX {
                // cmpswap: data is (new, compare).
                let mut args = vec![h];
                args.extend(coords);
                args.extend([vals[1], vals[0]]);
                self.s.op(
                    self.cur,
                    "atomicCompareExchange.i32",
                    Attr::NoUnwind,
                    i32t,
                    79,
                    &args,
                )
            } else {
                let mut args = vec![h, self.s.m.i32(op)];
                args.extend(coords);
                args.push(vals[0]);
                self.s
                    .op(self.cur, "atomicBinOp.i32", Attr::NoUnwind, i32t, 78, &args)
            };
            let r = self.end_guarded(at, &[(r, old)])[0];
            if returns {
                self.write(inst, Reg::V(reg), r, None);
            }
            return Ok(());
        }
        if store {
            let regs = if d16 { count.div_ceil(2) } else { count };
            let mut vals =
                self.vgprs(inst, data.as_ref().ok_or("buffer store data")?, regs as u8)?;
            if d16 {
                // shortcut: d16 data is taken as f16 (integer formats would
                // keep 16 bits), widened for the 32-bit float store.
                let mut wide = Vec::new();
                for k in 0..count {
                    let mut x = vals[(k / 2) as usize];
                    if k % 2 == 1 {
                        let k16 = self.s.m.i32(16);
                        x = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::LShr, x, k16);
                    }
                    let f32t = self.s.t.f32;
                    let f = self
                        .s
                        .op(c, "legacyF16ToF32", Attr::ReadNone, f32t, 131, &[x]);
                    wide.push(self.as_int(f));
                }
                vals = wide;
            }
            let mut args = Vec::new();
            let (op, name) = if typed {
                // shortcut: typed stores are taken to write all four channels
                // of a float format.
                if count != 4 || *offen || *offset != 0 {
                    return Err("a typed buffer store of some channels or at an offset");
                }
                args.push(self.handle(site, src, false, (10 | u, 0x409))?);
                args.extend([index.unwrap_or(self.s.m.i32(0)), iu]);
                for x in vals {
                    args.push(self.as_float(x));
                }
                (69, "bufferStore.f32")
            } else {
                match index {
                    // A raw buffer (stride 1) written by index: the index is the byte.
                    Some(index) if used.is_some_and(|u| u.stride == 1) => {
                        let byte = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Add, index, off);
                        args.push(self.handle(site, src, false, (11 | u, 0))?);
                        args.extend([byte, iu]);
                    }
                    Some(index) => {
                        let stride = used.map_or(0, |u| u.stride);
                        if stride < 4 || !stride.is_multiple_of(4) {
                            return Err("a structured buffer of unknown stride");
                        }
                        args.push(self.handle(site, src, false, (12 | u, stride))?);
                        args.extend([index, off]);
                    }
                    None => {
                        args.push(self.handle(site, src, false, (11 | u, 0))?);
                        args.extend([off, iu]);
                    }
                }
                args.extend(&vals);
                args.resize(3 + 4, iu);
                (140, "rawBufferStore.i32")
            };
            args.push(self.s.m.i8(if typed { 0xF } else { (1u8 << count) - 1 }));
            if !typed {
                args.push(self.s.m.i32(4));
            }
            let at = self.begin_guarded(guard);
            let void = self.s.t.void;
            self.s.op(self.cur, name, Attr::NoUnwind, void, op, &args);
            self.end_guarded(at, &[]);
            return Ok(());
        }
        if let Some(f) = *format {
            if index.is_some() {
                return Err("a typed-format load by index");
            }
            let h = self.handle(site, src, false, (11 | u, 0))?;
            let Some(Operand::Vector { reg, .. }) = *data else {
                return Err("a buffer result");
            };
            for (k, x) in self.format_load(h, off, f, count)?.into_iter().enumerate() {
                self.write(inst, Reg::V(reg + k as u8), x, guard);
            }
            return Ok(());
        }
        let r = if typed {
            if *offen || matches!(off, V::Inst(_)) || *offset != 0 {
                return Err("a typed buffer load at an offset");
            }
            if uav {
                self.s.flags |= flags::TYPED_UAV_LOADS;
            }
            let h = self.handle(site, src, false, (10 | u, 0x409))?;
            let index = index.unwrap_or(self.s.m.i32(0));
            self.s.op(
                c,
                "bufferLoad.f32",
                Attr::ReadOnly,
                self.s.t.res_ret,
                68,
                &[h, index, iu],
            )
        } else {
            let mask = self.s.m.i8((1u8 << count) - 1);
            let align = self.s.m.i32(4);
            match index {
                // A raw buffer (stride 1) read by index: the index is the byte.
                Some(index) if used.is_some_and(|u| u.stride == 1) => {
                    let byte = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Add, index, off);
                    let h = self.handle(site, src, false, (11 | u, 0))?;
                    self.s.op(
                        c,
                        "rawBufferLoad.f32",
                        Attr::ReadOnly,
                        self.s.t.res_ret,
                        139,
                        &[h, byte, iu, mask, align],
                    )
                }
                Some(index) => {
                    let stride = used.map_or(0, |u| u.stride);
                    if stride < 4 || !stride.is_multiple_of(4) {
                        return Err("a structured buffer of unknown stride");
                    }
                    let h = self.handle(site, src, false, (12 | u, stride))?;
                    self.s.op(
                        c,
                        "rawBufferLoad.f32",
                        Attr::ReadOnly,
                        self.s.t.res_ret,
                        139,
                        &[h, index, off, mask, align],
                    )
                }
                None => {
                    let h = self.handle(site, src, false, (11 | u, 0))?;
                    self.s.op(
                        c,
                        "rawBufferLoad.f32",
                        Attr::ReadOnly,
                        self.s.t.res_ret,
                        139,
                        &[h, off, iu, mask, align],
                    )
                }
            }
        };
        let Some(Operand::Vector { reg, .. }) = *data else {
            return Err("a buffer result");
        };
        if d16 {
            // Two f16 channels per VGPR (an odd last high half 0).
            let k16 = self.s.m.i32(16);
            let i32t = self.s.t.i32;
            for k in 0..count.div_ceil(2) {
                let mut x = None;
                for ch in (2 * k..(2 * k + 2).min(count)).rev() {
                    let f = self.s.m.extract(c, r, ch);
                    let h = self
                        .s
                        .op(c, "legacyF32ToF16", Attr::ReadNone, i32t, 130, &[f]);
                    x = Some(match x {
                        Some(hi) => {
                            let hi = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Shl, hi, k16);
                            self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Or, h, hi)
                        }
                        None => h,
                    });
                }
                self.write(inst, Reg::V(reg + k as u8), x.expect("a channel"), guard);
            }
            return Ok(());
        }
        for k in 0..count {
            let x = self.s.m.extract(c, r, k);
            let x = self.as_int(x);
            self.write(inst, Reg::V(reg + k as u8), x, guard);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn export(&mut self, b: usize, i: usize) -> Result<(), Why> {
        let e = *self
            .exports
            .get(&(b, i))
            .ok_or("an export I/O raising did not see")?;
        if e.compressed {
            return Err("a compressed export");
        }
        let guard = self.guard(b, i)?;
        let mesh = self.s.mesh.is_some();
        let c = self.cur;
        if let Some(g) = guard
            && !mesh
        {
            if !(e.done && self.s.pixel) {
                return Err("a conditional export");
            }
            let t = self.s.m.bool(true);
            let kill = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Xor, g, t);
            self.s
                .op(c, "discard", Attr::NoUnwind, self.s.t.void, 82, &[kill]);
        }
        if mesh && e.target == Target::Primitive {
            return self.emit_indices(e, guard);
        }
        let param_row = |usage: Usage, row: u8| match usage {
            // The 2020 compiler leaves a mesh program's first entry zeroed
            // (usage "position"): its row is the one no other entry names.
            Usage::Other(0) if mesh => self.unnamed_row(),
            _ => Some(row),
        };
        // (output element, channel) per exported channel; per-primitive
        // outputs are elements of `prims`.
        let mut stores = Vec::new();
        let primitive = matches!(e.target, Target::PrimitiveParam { .. });
        let outputs = if primitive {
            &self.s.prims
        } else {
            &self.s.outputs
        };
        let by_kind = |kind: u8| outputs.iter().position(|o| o.kind == kind);
        // 16-bit vertex outputs: the halves each dword carries, as (output
        // element, channel, high half) per channel.
        let halves = match e.target {
            Target::Param { usage, row } => {
                param_row(usage, row).and_then(|r| self.half_outputs.get(&r).map(|&h| (r, h)))
            }
            _ => None,
        };
        if let Some((row, (pack2, _))) = halves {
            let packs: Vec<(u8, Option<u8>)> = self
                .half_outputs
                .iter()
                .filter(|(_, h)| h.0)
                .map(|(&r, h)| (r, h.1))
                .collect();
            for ch in 0..4u8 {
                let Some(value) = e.values[usize::from(ch)] else {
                    continue;
                };
                for high in [false, true] {
                    let h = 2 * ch + u8::from(high);
                    let src = if pack2 {
                        packed_half(outputs, &packs, row, h)
                    } else {
                        (!high).then_some((row, ch))
                    };
                    let found = src.and_then(|(r, c)| {
                        outputs.iter().position(|o| {
                            o.row == Some(u32::from(r)) && c >= o.col && c < o.col + o.cols
                        })
                    });
                    if let Some(id) = found {
                        let col = src.expect("found").1 - outputs[id].col;
                        stores.push((id, col, value, Some(high)));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        for ch in 0..4u8 {
            let Some(value) = e.values[usize::from(ch)] else {
                continue;
            };
            if halves.is_some() {
                break;
            }
            let found = match e.target {
                Target::Color(n) => outputs
                    .iter()
                    .position(|o| o.kind == 16 && o.row == Some(u32::from(n)))
                    .map(|id| (id, ch)),
                Target::Position(0) => by_kind(3).map(|id| (id, ch)),
                Target::Depth => match ch {
                    0 => by_kind(17)
                        .or(by_kind(18))
                        .or(by_kind(19))
                        .map(|id| (id, 0)),
                    1 => by_kind(20).map(|id| (id, 0)),
                    2 => by_kind(14).map(|id| (id, 0)),
                    _ => None,
                },
                Target::Param { usage, row } | Target::PrimitiveParam { usage, row } => {
                    let row = param_row(usage, row);
                    outputs
                        .iter()
                        .position(|o| {
                            row.is_some_and(|r| o.row == Some(u32::from(r)))
                                && ch >= o.col
                                && ch < o.col + o.cols
                        })
                        .map(|id| (id, ch - outputs[id].col))
                }
                Target::Null | Target::Unread => None,
                Target::Position(n @ 1..=2) => {
                    // shortcut: without the misc vector (point size, render
                    // target or viewport index) pos1 and pos2 carry the clip
                    // then cull distances, in semantic order.
                    if outputs.iter().any(|o| matches!(o.kind, 4 | 5)) {
                        return Err("render-target or viewport index exports");
                    }
                    let mut dists: Vec<usize> = (0..outputs.len())
                        .filter(|&i| matches!(outputs[i].kind, 6 | 7))
                        .collect();
                    dists.sort_by_key(|&i| (outputs[i].kind, outputs[i].index));
                    let flat: Vec<(usize, u8)> = dists
                        .iter()
                        .flat_map(|&i| (0..outputs[i].cols).map(move |c| (i, c)))
                        .collect();
                    // Channels past the distances the signature declares are
                    // ones the clipper does not enable (`PA_CL_VS_OUT_CNTL`).
                    let k = usize::from(n - 1) * 4 + usize::from(ch);
                    flat.get(k).copied()
                }
                Target::Position(_) => return Err("clip, cull or point-size exports"),
                Target::Primitive => return Err("a primitive export"),
            };
            if let Some((id, col)) = found {
                stores.push((id, col, value, None));
            }
        }
        fn elements<'l>(l: &'l mut Lower, primitive: bool) -> &'l mut Vec<SigElement> {
            if primitive {
                &mut l.s.prims
            } else {
                &mut l.s.outputs
            }
        }
        if stores
            .iter()
            .any(|s| s.3.is_none() && elements(self, primitive)[s.0].half)
        {
            return Err("a 16-bit output the stage data does not mark");
        }
        // A mesh lane writes its own vertex or primitive, where it exports.
        let at = if mesh {
            let flat = self.mesh_thread();
            let limit = if let Some(m) = self.s.mesh {
                if primitive {
                    m.max_primitives
                } else {
                    m.max_vertices
                }
            } else {
                0
            };
            let threads = self.s.threads.map(|t| t[0]).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
            let mesh_guard = if limit > 0 && threads > limit {
                let lim = self.s.m.i32(limit);
                let in_bounds = self.s.m.cmp(self.cur, pred::IULT, flat, lim);
                match guard {
                    Some(g) => Some(self.s.m.bin(self.cur, Bin::And, g, in_bounds)),
                    None => Some(in_bounds),
                }
            } else {
                guard
            };
            self.begin_guarded(mesh_guard)
        } else {
            None
        };
        let (name, opcode) = match (mesh, primitive) {
            (false, _) => ("storeOutput", 5),
            (true, false) => ("storeVertexOutput", 171),
            (true, true) => ("storePrimitiveOutput", 172),
        };
        for (id, col, value, half) in stores {
            let mut x = self.i32_of(value)?;
            if let Some(high) = half {
                // An f16 half, declared a 32-bit float on the host.
                let c = self.cur;
                if high {
                    let k16 = self.s.m.i32(16);
                    x = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::LShr, x, k16);
                }
                let f32t = self.s.t.f32;
                let f = self
                    .s
                    .op(c, "legacyF16ToF32", Attr::ReadNone, f32t, 131, &[x]);
                x = self.as_int(f);
            }
            let el = &mut elements(self, primitive)[id];
            el.usage |= 1 << col;
            let (suffix, x) = match el.comp {
                9 if half.is_some() => (".f32", self.as_float(x)),
                9 => {
                    let f = match self.floats.get(&value) {
                        Some(&f) => f,
                        None => self.as_float(x),
                    };
                    (".f32", f)
                }
                _ => (".i32", x),
            };
            let mut args = vec![
                self.s.m.i32(id as u32),
                self.s.m.i32(0),
                self.s.m.i8(col),
                x,
            ];
            if mesh {
                args.push(self.mesh_thread());
            }
            let void = self.s.t.void;
            self.s.op(
                self.cur,
                &format!("{name}{suffix}"),
                Attr::NoUnwind,
                void,
                opcode,
                &args,
            );
        }
        self.end_guarded(at, &[]);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Mesh: `exp prim` as the lane's primitive. Bit 31 culls it (all
    /// indices 0: no area).
    fn emit_indices(&mut self, e: &Export, guard: Option<V>) -> Result<(), Why> {
        let v = e.values[0].ok_or("a primitive export without its indices")?;
        let x = self.i32_of(v)?;
        let flat = self.mesh_thread();
        let guard = if let Some(mesh) = self.s.mesh {
            let threads = self.s.threads.map(|t| t[0]).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
            if threads > mesh.max_primitives {
                let p = self.s.m.i32(mesh.max_primitives);
                let in_bounds = self.s.m.cmp(self.cur, pred::IULT, flat, p);
                match guard {
                    Some(g) => Some(self.s.m.bin(self.cur, Bin::And, g, in_bounds)),
                    None => Some(in_bounds),
                }
            } else {
                guard
            }
        } else {
            guard
        };
        let at = self.begin_guarded(guard);
        let c = self.cur;
        let z = self.s.m.i32(0);
        let mut culled = self.s.m.cmp(c, pred::SLT, x, z);
        // A primitive that names a vertex past the declared count, or one
        // no lane writes (lane n writes vertex n alone), is culled too: the
        // host would read a vertex nothing set, at any position.
        let written = self.s.mesh.map(|m| {
            m.max_vertices
                .min(self.s.threads.map_or(u32::MAX, |t| t[0]))
        });
        let mut indices = [z; 3];
        for (k, slot) in indices.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            let (shift, mask) = (self.s.m.i32(10 * k as u32), self.s.m.i32(0x3FF));
            let i = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::LShr, x, shift);
            let i = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::And, i, mask);
            if let Some(n) = written {
                let n = self.s.m.i32(n);
                let past = self.s.m.cmp(c, pred::IUGE, i, n);
                culled = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Or, culled, past);
            }
            *slot = i;
        }
        let mut args = vec![flat];
        for i in indices {
            args.push(self.s.m.select(c, culled, z, i));
        }
        let void = self.s.t.void;
        self.s
            .op(c, "emitIndices", Attr::NoUnwind, void, 169, &args);
        self.end_guarded(at, &[]);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The per-vertex arbitrary row no mesh output entry names but one
    /// (the 2020 compiler's zeroed entry).
    fn unnamed_row(&self) -> Option<u8> {
        let StageIo::Ms(ms) = &self.x.native.io else {
            return None;
        };
        let named = |r: u32| {
            ms.outputs
                .iter()
                .any(|o| o.param & 0x80 == 0 && o.usage != Usage::Other(0) && u32::from(o.row) == r)
        };
        let free: std::collections::BTreeSet<u32> = self
            .s
            .outputs
            .iter()
            .filter(|o| o.kind == 0)
            .filter_map(|o| o.row)
            .filter(|&r| !named(r))
            .collect();
        match free.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>()[..] {
            [r] => u8::try_from(r).ok(),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    fn exit(&mut self, b: usize) -> Result<(), Stop> {
        let offset = self.x.p.blocks[b]
            .insts
            .last()
            .map_or(self.x.p.blocks[b].offset, |i| i.machine.offset);
        let term = match self.x.st.exits[b] {
            LaneExit::Jump(t) if self.counters.contains_key(&t) && self.rpo[t] <= self.rpo[b] => {
                let ok = self.count_iteration(t, pred::IULT);
                let abort = self.abort_block();
                Term::CondBr(ok, self.block[t].expect("reachable"), abort)
            }
            LaneExit::Jump(t) => {
                self.enter_loop(b, t, self.cur);
                Term::Br(self.block[t].expect("reachable"))
            }
            LaneExit::Branch {
                when,
                taken,
                not_taken,
            } => {
                // A negated condition branches the other way round.
                let (cond, taken, not_taken) = match self.x.st.bools.node(when) {
                    _ if self.x.st.wide.contains(&b) => {
                        let c = self.wave_wide(b, when).map_err(|w| unsupported(offset, w))?;
                        (c, taken, not_taken)
                    }
                    Some((atom, Bool::TRUE, Bool::FALSE)) => {
                        let a = self
                            .atom(atom, self.cur)
                            .map_err(|w| unsupported(offset, w))?;
                        (a, not_taken, taken)
                    }
                    _ => {
                        let c = self
                            .boolean(when, self.cur)
                            .map_err(|w| unsupported(offset, w))?;
                        (c, taken, not_taken)
                    }
                };
                // A back edge is taken only below the iteration limit.
                let back =
                    |l: &Self, to: usize| l.counters.contains_key(&to) && l.rpo[to] <= l.rpo[b];
                // (No `xor` of a compare: a loop exit testing one hung the
                // AMD driver.)
                let cond = if back(self, taken) {
                    let ok = self.count_iteration(taken, pred::IULT);
                    self.s.m.bin(self.cur, Bin::And, cond, ok)
                } else if back(self, not_taken) {
                    let stop = self.count_iteration(not_taken, pred::IUGE);
                    self.s.m.bin(self.cur, Bin::Or, cond, stop)
                } else {
                    cond
                };
                // Critical edges get a block of their own, so loops have
                // dedicated exits and preheaders as DXC emits them.
                let (t, f) = (self.edge(b, taken), self.edge(b, not_taken));
                for (to, via) in [(taken, t), (not_taken, f)] {
                    if !back(self, to) {
                        // From an edge block, or from here.
                        let from = if Some(via) == self.block[to] {
                            self.cur
                        } else {
                            via
                        };
                        self.enter_loop(b, to, from);
                    }
                }
                Term::CondBr(cond, t, f)
            }
            LaneExit::End => {
                if self.s.pixel && !self.exported[b] && !self.has_done_export(b) {
                    // A lane leaving without its final export was killed.
                    let t = self.s.m.bool(true);
                    self.s
                        .op(self.cur, "discard", Attr::NoUnwind, self.s.t.void, 82, &[t]);
                }
                Term::Ret
            }
            LaneExit::Indirect => return Err(unsupported(offset, "an indirect jump")),
        };
        let _ = Exit::End;
        self.s.m.terminate(self.cur, term);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// A forward edge into loop header `to` (from DXIL block `via`) starts
    /// its count at 0.
    fn enter_loop(&mut self, _from: usize, to: usize, via: usize) {
        if let Some((_, incoming)) = self.counters.get_mut(&to) {
            let z = self.s.m.i32(0);
            incoming.push((z, via));
        }
    }

    /// A back edge to header `to` (a back edge keeps its block, no
    /// critical-edge block): the count goes up; the result compares it with
    /// [`LOOP_LIMIT`] by `p` (below: go on; at or above: stop).
    fn count_iteration(&mut self, to: usize, p: u8) -> V {
        let c = self.cur;
        let (phi, _) = self.counters[&to];
        let one = self.s.m.i32(1);
        let next = self.s.m.bin(c, Bin::Add, phi, one);
        self.s.m.tag(phi, Tag::Counter);
        self.s.m.tag(next, Tag::Counter);
        // Per stage unless the switch names one: a loop that never meets its
        // exit (a count read from a buffer the host has not got yet, say)
        // runs to the limit in every lane. A million iterations a pixel
        // hung the GPU for seconds a draw until Windows reset it
        // (PS_Textured_Eight, 2026-11-24, run 12).
        // shortcut: a pixel loop past 128 iterations, a vertex or mesh loop
        // past 256 or a compute loop past 4,096 is cut short. (They were
        // 1,024, 4,096 and 65,536: the opening cutscene then lost the card
        // 14-25 frames in, in a minimap or shadow mesh draw; with every
        // loop cut at 64 it ran 90 frames. Raise them again once shaders
        // stop reading data that is not there yet.)
        let limit = match super::loop_limit() {
            LOOP_LIMIT if self.s.pixel => 1 << 7,
            LOOP_LIMIT if self.s.mesh.is_some() || self.s.threads.is_none() => 1 << 8,
            LOOP_LIMIT => 1 << 12,
            named => named,
        };
        let limit = self.s.m.i32(limit);
        self.counters
            .get_mut(&to)
            .expect("header")
            .1
            .push((next, c));
        let over = self.s.m.cmp(c, p, next, limit);
        self.s.m.tag(over, Tag::Counter);
        over
    }

    /// The block a lane stopped by [`LOOP_LIMIT`] leaves through.
    fn abort_block(&mut self) -> usize {
        if let Some(a) = self.abort {
            return a;
        }
        let a = self.s.m.new_block();
        if self.s.pixel {
            let t = self.s.m.bool(true);
            self.s
                .op(a, "discard", Attr::NoUnwind, self.s.t.void, 82, &[t]);
        }
        self.s.m.terminate(a, Term::Ret);
        self.abort = Some(a);
        a
    }

    /// The DXIL block a branch from IR block `from` to `to` goes to.
    fn edge(&mut self, from: usize, to: usize) -> usize {
        let target = self.block[to].expect("reachable");
        let preds = self.x.p.blocks[to]
            .preds
            .iter()
            .filter(|&&q| self.block[q].is_some())
            .count();
        // Back edges stay as they are: the exiting block is the latch.
        if preds < 2 || self.rpo[to] <= self.rpo[from] {
            return target;
        }
        let e = self.s.m.new_block();
        self.s.m.terminate(e, Term::Br(target));
        self.edges.insert((from, to), e);
        e
    }

    fn fill_phis(&mut self) -> Result<(), Stop> {
        let p = self.x.p;
        // Lane-mask joins first (what an edge brings may ask for more joins,
        // of masks and of numbers): each edge's mask as the structure
        // tracked it, a constant or a scalar-built one included.
        let st = self.x.st;
        while let Some((v, b, i)) = self.pending_masks.pop() {
            let phi = &p.blocks[b].phis[i];
            let offset = p.blocks[b].offset;
            let args = st
                .phi_masks
                .get(&phi.value)
                .ok_or_else(|| unsupported(offset, "a lane-mask join of an untracked mask"))?;
            let mut incoming = Vec::new();
            for (n, &q) in p.blocks[b].preds.iter().enumerate() {
                let Some(qb) = self.tail[q] else { continue };
                let qb = self.edges.get(&(q, b)).copied().unwrap_or(qb);
                let x = self.boolean(args[n], qb).map_err(|w| unsupported(offset, w))?;
                incoming.push((x, qb));
            }
            self.s.m.set_phi(v, incoming);
        }
        // A join that only another join reads is read wherever that one is. Left
        // unmarked, a value without a DXIL form coming into it became zero without a
        // word (the looked-up tint of the material resolve programs, whose size
        // computation had no value, was zero in every lane that way).
        // shortcut: only with `VICTORY_STRICT_JOINS` set (the offline pack
        // listing sets it to count them): 40 programs that translate today
        // stop by name with it (vehicle paint pixel shaders at "the first
        // half of an interpolation", foliage mesh shaders); until those are
        // lowered they keep drawing with that zero.
        static STRICT: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
        let strict = *STRICT.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("VICTORY_STRICT_JOINS").is_some());
        let mut work: Vec<Value> = if strict {
            self.read_phis.iter().copied().collect()
        } else {
            Vec::new()
        };
        while let Some(v) = work.pop() {
            let Some(&(b, i)) = self.phi_at.get(&v) else {
                continue;
            };
            for &a in &p.blocks[b].phis[i].args {
                if self.phi_at.contains_key(&a) && self.read_phis.insert(a) {
                    work.push(a);
                }
            }
        }
        for (v, b, i) in std::mem::take(&mut self.data_phis) {
            let phi = &p.blocks[b].phis[i];
            let bit = phi.reg == Reg::Scc;
            // A join of numbers with dead registers (`dead`): the paths that bring those
            // never read the result, so they bring zero. Not for a join that is itself a
            // lane mask (a ballot gives that one as data).
            let st = self.x.st;
            let numbers = !bit
                && !st.masks.contains_key(&phi.value)
                && !st.highs.contains_key(&phi.value)
                && phi
                    .args
                    .iter()
                    .any(|a| matches!(self.vals.get(a), Some(Val::I32(_))));
            let mut incoming = Vec::new();
            for (n, &q) in p.blocks[b].preds.iter().enumerate() {
                let Some(qb) = self.tail[q] else { continue };
                let qb = self.edges.get(&(q, b)).copied().unwrap_or(qb);
                let arg = phi.args[n];
                if self.read_phis.contains(&phi.value) && !self.vals.contains_key(&arg) {
                    let _ = self.lazy_barycentric(arg);
                    // A root parameter nothing read before the join (user
                    // data is loaded on first use, in the entry block).
                    if !self.vals.contains_key(&arg)
                        && let Some(&(param, dword)) = self.params.get(&arg)
                    {
                        let val = self.user(param, dword);
                        self.vals.insert(arg, val);
                    }
                }
                let x = match (self.vals.get(&arg).copied(), bit) {
                    (Some(Val::I32(x)), false) | (Some(Val::Bit(x)), true) => x,
                    (Some(Val::Missing(_)) | None, false)
                        if numbers && self.dead(arg, &mut Vec::new()) =>
                    {
                        self.s.m.i32(0)
                    }
                    // A lane mask joined with numbers (a traversal that keeps its lanes' masks on
                    // a stack with its node numbers): the mask comes as the number it is, the
                    // ballot of its lanes where it is written.
                    (Some(Val::Missing(_)) | None, false)
                        if self.read_phis.contains(&phi.value)
                            && self.mask_data == MaskData::Console
                            && (st.masks.contains_key(&arg) || st.highs.contains_key(&arg)) =>
                    {
                        match self.mask_dword(arg) {
                            Ok(x) => x,
                            Err(why) => return Err(Stop::Retry(phi.value, why)),
                        }
                    }
                    // SCC of a mask operation ("some lane is left") joined with a scalar test:
                    // the compiler branches around code that sets SCC and tests SCC after it,
                    // the skip bringing "no lane" along. As data it is "some lane of the wave
                    // has the bit" - right only if the wave took that skip together, as the
                    // console does: a lane that skipped alone would bring "some lane" where the
                    // console has the skipped code's SCC. So the branch must be one the wave
                    // takes together; else its region is named for `emit`'s retry to widen it.
                    (Some(Val::Missing(_)) | None, true)
                        if self.read_phis.contains(&phi.value)
                            && self.mask_data == MaskData::Console
                            && st.scc_some.contains_key(&arg) =>
                    {
                        let per_lane = !st.wide.contains(&q)
                            && matches!(st.exits[q], LaneExit::Branch { when, .. }
                                if !st.bools.support(when).iter().all(|a| matches!(a, Atom::Uniform(_))));
                        if per_lane {
                            for &other in p.blocks[b].preds.iter().filter(|&&o| o != q) {
                                need(other);
                            }
                            return Err(Stop::Retry(phi.value, LANE_MASK));
                        }
                        match self.scc_some(arg) {
                            Ok(x) => x,
                            Err(why) => return Err(Stop::Retry(phi.value, why)),
                        }
                    }
                    (Some(Val::Bit(_)), false) if self.read_phis.contains(&phi.value) => {
                        return Err(Stop::Retry(phi.value, "an SCC joined with SGPR values"));
                    }
                    (Some(Val::Missing(why)), _) if self.read_phis.contains(&phi.value) => {
                        return Err(Stop::Retry(phi.value, why));
                    }
                    _ if self.read_phis.contains(&phi.value) => {
                        return Err(Stop::Retry(phi.value, "a join of mismatched values"));
                    }
                    _ if bit => self.s.m.bool(false),
                    _ => self.s.m.i32(0),
                };
                incoming.push((x, qb));
            }
            self.s.m.set_phi(v, incoming);
        }
        for (phi, incoming) in std::mem::take(&mut self.counters).into_values() {
            self.s.m.set_phi(phi, incoming);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The DXIL interpolation mode of a kind of barycentrics (none for the
/// pull model).
fn interp_mode(kind: Barycentric) -> Option<u8> {
    Some(match kind {
        Barycentric::PerspectiveCenter => 2,
        Barycentric::PerspectiveCentroid => 3,
        Barycentric::PerspectiveSample => 6,
        Barycentric::LinearCenter => 4,
        Barycentric::LinearCentroid => 5,
        Barycentric::LinearSample => 7,
        Barycentric::PerspectivePullModel => return None,
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{Lowered, Numeric, Parts, buffer_format, half_shift, lower};
    use crate::native::{
        ComputeIo, HwStage, NativeProgram, ResourceType, RootParam, RootType, StageIo, UsedResource,
    };
    use crate::{io, ir, resource, structure};

    const S_ENDPGM: u32 = 0xBF81_0000;

    #[test]
    fn packed_pixel_inputs_find_their_second_row() {
        use super::super::container::SigElement;
        use super::half_input_partners;
        use crate::native::{PsInput, Usage};
        let entry = |row, row2, pack2| PsInput {
            usage: Usage::Generic,
            row,
            mask: 0xF,
            attr: row,
            flat: false,
            fp16: true,
            pack2,
            row2,
        };
        let element = |row| SigElement {
            name: "TEXCOORD".into(),
            index: row,
            kind: 0,
            comp: 9,
            interp: 2,
            row: Some(row),
            col: 0,
            cols: 4,
            usage: 0,
            half: true,
        };
        // Rows 0 and 3 pack and leave their second row out; 5 names its
        // own (6). Unnamed 16-bit rows: 1, 4, 6, 7.
        let io = StageIo::Ps {
            inputs: vec![entry(0, 0, true), entry(3, 3, true), entry(5, 6, true)],
            input_addr: 0,
            db_shader_control: 0,
            patches: vec![],
        };
        let sig: Vec<_> = [0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7].map(element).into();
        let p = half_input_partners(&io, &sig);
        assert_eq!(p.get(&0), Some(&1));
        assert_eq!(p.get(&3), Some(&4));
        assert_eq!(p.get(&5), None);
    }

    /// The packed pedestrian layouts of the title: an element
    /// behind another one in its register follows in the first parameter
    /// with a dword left, and is not a half of its register's row.
    #[test]
    fn packed_elements_behind_another_take_the_first_free_dword() {
        use super::super::container::SigElement;
        use super::packed_half;
        let element = |index, row, col, cols| SigElement {
            name: "TEXCOORD".into(),
            index,
            kind: 0,
            comp: 9,
            interp: 2,
            row: Some(row),
            col,
            cols,
            usage: 0,
            half: true,
        };
        // MS_VS_PedTransformPreSkinD_Packed 005fe88ec1bdc0c7 and its pixel
        // shader 93667197d3d05e1c: TEXCOORD6 is one value at register 4
        // column 3; parameter 3 (rows 6 and 7) carries it in dword 3.
        let sig = vec![
            element(1, 2, 0, 4),
            element(2, 3, 0, 4),
            element(4, 4, 0, 3),
            element(6, 4, 3, 1),
            element(3, 5, 0, 4),
            element(5, 6, 0, 4),
            element(7, 7, 0, 2),
            element(9, 9, 0, 3),
            element(11, 10, 0, 3),
            element(15, 12, 0, 4),
        ];
        let packs = [
            (2, Some(3)),
            (4, Some(5)),
            (6, Some(7)),
            (9, Some(10)),
            (12, None),
        ];
        let at = |a, h| packed_half(&sig, &packs, a, h);
        // Parameter 2: TEXCOORD4's three values, a zero half, TEXCOORD3.
        assert_eq!(at(4, 2), Some((4, 2)));
        assert_eq!(at(4, 3), None);
        assert_eq!(at(4, 4), Some((5, 0)));
        assert_eq!(at(4, 7), Some((5, 3)));
        // Parameter 3: TEXCOORD5, TEXCOORD7, then TEXCOORD6 alone.
        assert_eq!(at(6, 3), Some((6, 3)));
        assert_eq!(at(6, 5), Some((7, 1)));
        assert_eq!(at(6, 6), Some((4, 3)));
        assert_eq!(at(6, 7), None);
        // Parameters without such an element are as before.
        assert_eq!(at(9, 3), None);
        assert_eq!(at(9, 4), Some((10, 0)));
        assert_eq!(at(12, 3), Some((12, 3)));
        assert_eq!(at(12, 4), None);
        // The common layout (29805d23a495cdf8): TEXCOORD7 is two values at
        // register 1 columns 2-3; parameter 0 is TEXCOORD0, TEXCOORD1,
        // TEXCOORD7.
        let sig = vec![
            element(0, 1, 0, 2),
            element(7, 1, 2, 2),
            element(1, 2, 0, 4),
            element(2, 3, 0, 4),
            element(4, 4, 0, 3),
        ];
        let packs = [(3, Some(4)), (1, Some(2))];
        let at = |a, h| packed_half(&sig, &packs, a, h);
        assert_eq!(at(1, 1), Some((1, 1)));
        assert_eq!(at(1, 2), Some((2, 0)));
        assert_eq!(at(1, 5), Some((2, 3)));
        assert_eq!(at(1, 6), Some((1, 2)));
        assert_eq!(at(1, 7), Some((1, 3)));
        assert_eq!(at(3, 6), Some((4, 2)));
        assert_eq!(at(3, 7), None);
        // A row no element holds gives nothing, as before.
        assert_eq!(packed_half(&sig, &[(8, None)], 8, 0), None);
    }

    /// Whether a synthetic compute program translates with these input registers.
    fn lowers(words: &[u32], rsrc2: u32) -> Result<(), crate::ShaderError> {
        let code: Vec<u8> = words.iter().flat_map(|w| w.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        let native = NativeProgram {
            stage: HwStage::Cs,
            wave64: false,
            vgprs: 256,
            layout: vec![],
            used: vec![],
            io: StageIo::Cs(ComputeIo {
                rsrc2,
                threads: [1, 1, 1],
            }),
            code,
        };
        let p = ir::build(&native.code, false, 256).unwrap();
        let st = structure::structure(&p).unwrap();
        let res = resource::track(&p, &native.layout, native.stage, Some(&st)).unwrap();
        let io = io::raise(&p, &native).unwrap();
        lower(&Parts {
            native: &native,
            p: &p,
            st: &st,
            io: &io,
            res: &res,
            inputs: vec![],
            outputs: vec![],
            prims: vec![],
            mesh_stride: 0,
        })
        .map(|_| ())
    }

    /// Lowers a compute program with the root parameters `layout` (in user
    /// SGPRs from s0 on) and the used resources `used`.
    fn lower_with(
        words: &[u32],
        layout: Vec<RootParam>,
        used: Vec<UsedResource>,
    ) -> Result<Lowered, crate::ShaderError> {
        lower_wave(words, layout, used, false)
    }

    /// [`lower_with`] in wave64 if `wave64`.
    fn lower_wave(
        words: &[u32],
        layout: Vec<RootParam>,
        used: Vec<UsedResource>,
        wave64: bool,
    ) -> Result<Lowered, crate::ShaderError> {
        let code: Vec<u8> = words.iter().flat_map(|w| w.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        let sgprs: u32 = layout.iter().map(|p| p.sgprs).sum();
        let native = NativeProgram {
            stage: HwStage::Cs,
            wave64,
            vgprs: 256,
            layout,
            used,
            io: StageIo::Cs(ComputeIo {
                // The layout's user SGPRs (at least two), 512 bytes of LDS.
                rsrc2: 1 << 15 | sgprs.max(2) << 1,
                threads: [1, 1, 1],
            }),
            code,
        };
        let p = ir::build(&native.code, wave64, 256).unwrap();
        let st = structure::structure(&p).unwrap();
        let res = resource::track(&p, &native.layout, native.stage, Some(&st))?;
        let io = io::raise(&p, &native).unwrap();
        lower(&Parts {
            native: &native,
            p: &p,
            st: &st,
            io: &io,
            res: &res,
            inputs: vec![],
            outputs: vec![],
            prims: vec![],
            mesh_stride: 0,
        })
    }

    /// Root parameter `slot` in user SGPRs from `user_data` on.
    fn root(root: RootType, user_data: u8, slot: u8) -> RootParam {
        RootParam {
            root,
            table_offset_dwords: 0,
            sgprs: if root == RootType::Descriptor { 2 } else { 1 },
            base_register: 0,
            user_data,
            slot,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn buffer_cache_invalidations_lower_as_no_ops() {
        // MUBUF opcode 0x071/0x072 with no data operand: the title asks the
        // host to invalidate its cached view of a buffer.
        assert!(lowers(&[0xE1C4_0000, 0, S_ENDPGM], 0).is_ok(), "buffer_gl0_inv");
        assert!(lowers(&[0xE1C8_0000, 0, S_ENDPGM], 0).is_ok(), "buffer_gl1_inv");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_scalar_carry_chain_reaches_the_select() {
        // The high dword of a 64-bit add or subtract, then a select on the
        // carry (borrow) the high half leaves in SCC, and a branch on it
        // (only code with an effect needs its operands).
        let add = [
            0xBE80_03C1, // s_mov_b32 s0, -1
            0xBE81_0380, // s_mov_b32 s1, 0
            0x8000_8100, // s_add_u32 s0, s0, 1
            0x8201_8001, // s_addc_u32 s1, s1, 0
            0x8502_0001, // s_cselect_b32 s2, s1, s0
            0xBF07_8002, // s_cmp_lg_u32 s2, 0
            0xBF85_0001, // s_cbranch_scc1 -> s_endpgm
            0xBE83_0380, // s_mov_b32 s3, 0
            S_ENDPGM,
        ];
        let sub = [
            0xBE80_0380, // s_mov_b32 s0, 0
            0xBE81_0380, // s_mov_b32 s1, 0
            0x8080_8100, // s_sub_u32 s0, s0, 1
            0x8281_8001, // s_subb_u32 s1, s1, 0
            0x8502_0001, // s_cselect_b32 s2, s1, s0
            0xBF07_8002, // s_cmp_lg_u32 s2, 0
            0xBF85_0001, // s_cbranch_scc1 -> s_endpgm
            0xBE83_0380, // s_mov_b32 s3, 0
            S_ENDPGM,
        ];

        for words in [add, sub] {
            lowers(&words, 0).unwrap();
        }
    }

    fn perm_features(selector: u32) -> u64 {
        // Synthetic compute shader:
        // v0 is the thread ID and can supply a dynamic selector.
        // Store the result in LDS to keep the permutation live.
        let words = [
            0x7E02_02FFu32,
            0x817F_34AB,
            0x7E04_02FF,
            0xFE01_56CD,
            0xD744_0003,
            257 | (258 << 9) | (selector << 18),
            0x3408_0082,
            0xD834_0000,
            0x0000_0304,
            S_ENDPGM,
        ];

        let code: Vec<u8> = words.iter()
            .flat_map(|w| w.to_le_bytes())
            .collect();

        let native = NativeProgram {
            stage: HwStage::Cs,
            wave64: false,
            vgprs: 256,
            layout: vec![],
            used: vec![],
            io: StageIo::Cs(ComputeIo {
                rsrc2: 1 << 15,
                threads: [64, 1, 1],
            }),
            code,
        };

        let p = ir::build(&native.code, false, 256).unwrap();

        assert!(p.blocks.iter()
            .flat_map(|b| &b.insts)
            .any(|i| i.name() == "v_perm_b32"));

        let st = structure::structure(&p).unwrap();
        let res = resource::track(&p, &native.layout, native.stage, Some(&st)).unwrap();

        let io = io::raise(&p, &native).unwrap();

        let emitted = lower(&Parts {
            native: &native,
            p: &p,
            st: &st,
            io: &io,
            res: &res,
            inputs: vec![],
            outputs: vec![],
            prims: vec![],
            mesh_stride: 0,
        }).unwrap();

        let container =
            crate::Container::parse(&emitted.dxil).unwrap();

        let features =
            container.part(crate::FourCC::SFI0).unwrap();

        u64::from_le_bytes(features.data.try_into().unwrap())
    }

    #[test]
    fn perm_constant_selector_needs_no_int64() {
        assert_eq!(perm_features(128) & 0x8000, 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn perm_dynamic_selector_needs_no_int64() {
        assert_eq!(
            perm_features(256) & 0x8000,
            0,
            "dynamic v_perm_b32 must not require INT64"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_descriptor_selected_by_scc_picks_its_heap_index() {
        // Two buffer descriptors loaded from the table at s0, one picked by
        // a root constant (s1) with s_cselect_b64 per half, and loaded
        // through by index and stored to LDS so the load is needed.
        let words = [
            0xBE84_0300, // s_mov_b32 s4, s0
            0xBE85_0380, // s_mov_b32 s5, 0
            0xF408_0202,
            0xFA00_0000, // s_load_dwordx4 s[8:11], s[4:5], null
            0xF408_0302,
            0xFA00_0010, // s_load_dwordx4 s[12:15], s[4:5], 0x10
            0xBF06_8001, // s_cmp_eq_u32 s1, 0
            0x8590_0C08, // s_cselect_b64 s[16:17], s[8:9], s[12:13]
            0x8592_0E0A, // s_cselect_b64 s[18:19], s[10:11], s[14:15]
            0xE030_2000,
            0x8004_0100, // buffer_load_dword v1, v0, s[16:19], 0 idxen
            0xD834_0000,
            0x0000_0100, // ds_write_b32 v0, v1
            S_ENDPGM,
        ];
        let layout = || vec![root(RootType::Table, 0, 0), root(RootType::Constants, 1, 1)];
        // Both are structured buffers of dwords in the table's range.
        let used = || {
            vec![UsedResource {
                kind: ResourceType::Srv,
                root: RootType::Table,
                table_offset_dwords: 0,
                lower_bound: 0,
                stride: 4,
                dwords: 4,
                user_data: 0,
                slot: 0,
            }]
        };
        lower_with(&words, layout(), used()).unwrap();
    }

    /// Tables of 2D textures at s0 and samplers at s1.
    fn texture_tables() -> (Vec<RootParam>, Vec<UsedResource>) {
        let range = |kind, user_data, slot| UsedResource {
            kind,
            root: RootType::Table,
            table_offset_dwords: 0,
            lower_bound: 0,
            stride: 0,
            dwords: if kind == ResourceType::Sampler { 4 } else { 8 },
            user_data,
            slot,
        };
        (
            vec![root(RootType::Table, 0, 0), root(RootType::Table, 1, 1)],
            vec![
                range(ResourceType::Srv, 0, 0),
                range(ResourceType::Sampler, 1, 1),
            ],
        )
    }

    #[test]
    fn waterfall_loops_over_per_lane_descriptors_sample_with_each_lanes_own() {
        use crate::resource::tests::{
            WATERFALL_FETCHED_WAVE32, WATERFALL_FETCHED_WAVE64, WATERFALL_PICKED_WAVE32,
        };
        for (words, wave64) in [
            (WATERFALL_FETCHED_WAVE32, false),
            (WATERFALL_FETCHED_WAVE64, true),
            (WATERFALL_PICKED_WAVE32, false),
        ] {
            let (layout, used) = texture_tables();
            let l = lower_wave(words, layout, used, wave64).unwrap();
            // The loop's reads of the first lane became each lane's own
            // dwords: no wave operation is left.
            assert_eq!(l.nonuniform_handles, 1);
            assert!(!l.wave_ops);
        }
    }

    /// [`texture_tables`] with a raw buffer UAV at dword 16 of the first.
    pub(crate) fn texture_and_uav_tables() -> (Vec<RootParam>, Vec<UsedResource>) {
        let (layout, mut used) = texture_tables();
        used.push(UsedResource {
            kind: ResourceType::Uav,
            root: RootType::Table,
            table_offset_dwords: 16,
            lower_bound: 0,
            stride: 0,
            dwords: 4,
            user_data: 0,
            slot: 0,
        });
        (layout, used)
    }

    #[test]
    fn waterfall_loops_over_descriptors_joined_per_lane_sample_with_each_lanes_own() {
        use crate::resource::tests::{WATERFALL_JOINED_MIXED_WAVE32, WATERFALL_JOINED_WAVE32};
        for words in [WATERFALL_JOINED_WAVE32, WATERFALL_JOINED_MIXED_WAVE32] {
            let (layout, used) = texture_and_uav_tables();
            let l = lower_wave(words, layout, used, false).unwrap();
            // One image handle, from the join's per-lane heap index.
            assert_eq!(l.nonuniform_handles, 1);
            assert!(!l.wave_ops);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn scalar_bit_tests_lower() {
        // Each tests one bit of a constant into SCC and branches on it (only
        // code with an effect needs its operands).
        let tail = [
            0xBF85_0001, // s_cbranch_scc1 -> s_endpgm
            0xBE84_0380, // s_mov_b32 s4, 0
            S_ENDPGM,
        ];
        let bit_tests: [&[u32]; 4] = [
            &[0xBE81_0387, 0xBF0C_8301], // s_mov_b32 s1, 7; s_bitcmp0_b32 s1, 3
            &[0xBE81_0387, 0xBF0D_8301], // s_mov_b32 s1, 7; s_bitcmp1_b32 s1, 3
            &[
                0xBE80_0387, // s_mov_b32 s0, 7
                0xBE81_0380, // s_mov_b32 s1, 0
                0xBF0E_8300, // s_bitcmp0_b64 s[0:1], 3
            ],
            &[
                0xBE80_0387, // s_mov_b32 s0, 7
                0xBE81_0380, // s_mov_b32 s1, 0
                0xBF0F_8300, // s_bitcmp1_b64 s[0:1], 3
            ],
        ];
        for head in bit_tests {
            let words: Vec<u32> = head.iter().chain(&tail).copied().collect();
            lowers(&words, 0).unwrap();
        }
    }

    #[test]
    #[ignore = "ours marks joins read through joins only with VICTORY_STRICT_JOINS (40 programs stop otherwise)"]
    fn a_missing_value_stays_missing_through_two_live_joins() {
        let mut words = [
            0xF490_0180,
            0,           // s_memtime s[6:7]
            0xBF06_8000, // s_cmp_eq_u32 s0, 0 (s0 = group id X)
            0xBF85_0001, // skip the first overwrite
            0xBE86_0380, // s_mov_b32 s6, 0
            0xBF06_8101, // s_cmp_eq_u32 s1, 1 (s1 = group id Y)
            0xBF85_0001, // skip the second overwrite
            0xBE86_0381, // s_mov_b32 s6, 1
            0xBF07_8006, // s_cmp_lg_u32 s6, 0
            0xBF85_0001, // use the result to branch
            0xBE83_0380,
            S_ENDPGM,
        ];
        let group_ids_xy = 3 << 7;
        // Compare to a direct read so future timestamp support works in both cases.
        let refusal = |code: &[u32]| match lowers(code, group_ids_xy) {
            Ok(()) => None,
            Err(crate::ShaderError::Unsupported { what, .. }) => Some(what),
            Err(error) => panic!("{error}"),
        };
        let direct = [&words[..2], &words[8..]].concat();
        assert_eq!(refusal(&words), refusal(&direct));
        words[8] = 0xBF07_8000; // read the group id instead; the timestamp is dead
        lowers(&words, group_ids_xy).expect("dead timestamp");
    }

    #[test]
    fn buffer_formats_by_number() {
        // The numbers the disassembler names 8_8_8_8_UNORM, 16_16_SNORM,
        // 2_10_10_10_UNORM, 16_FLOAT, 32_32_32_32_FLOAT.
        assert_eq!(buffer_format(56), Some((&[8, 8, 8, 8][..], Numeric::Unorm)));
        assert_eq!(buffer_format(24), Some((&[16, 16][..], Numeric::Snorm)));
        assert_eq!(
            buffer_format(50),
            Some((&[10, 10, 10, 2][..], Numeric::Unorm))
        );
        assert_eq!(buffer_format(13), Some((&[16][..], Numeric::Float)));
        assert_eq!(
            buffer_format(77),
            Some((&[32, 32, 32, 32][..], Numeric::Float))
        );
        // Invalid, past the table.
        assert_eq!(buffer_format(0), None);
        assert_eq!(buffer_format(78), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn packed_buffer_formats_by_number() {
        // LLVM's `UfmtGFX10`: 10_11_11 is 30-36, 11_11_10 37-43,
        // 10_10_10_2 44-49. Channels from the lowest bits: R11G11B10_FLOAT
        // is 10_11_11 (Mesa), 10_10_10_2 has the 2-bit channel first.
        assert_eq!(buffer_format(30), Some((&[11, 11, 10][..], Numeric::Unorm)));
        assert_eq!(buffer_format(36), Some((&[11, 11, 10][..], Numeric::Float)));
        assert_eq!(buffer_format(37), Some((&[10, 11, 11][..], Numeric::Unorm)));
        assert_eq!(buffer_format(43), Some((&[10, 11, 11][..], Numeric::Float)));
        assert_eq!(
            buffer_format(44),
            Some((&[2, 10, 10, 10][..], Numeric::Unorm))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            buffer_format(45),
            Some((&[2, 10, 10, 10][..], Numeric::Snorm))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            buffer_format(46),
            Some((&[2, 10, 10, 10][..], Numeric::Uscaled))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            buffer_format(47),
            Some((&[2, 10, 10, 10][..], Numeric::Sscaled))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            buffer_format(48),
            Some((&[2, 10, 10, 10][..], Numeric::Uint))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            buffer_format(49),
            Some((&[2, 10, 10, 10][..], Numeric::Sint))
        );
    }

    /// A half's value (sign, 5-bit exponent biased 15, 10-bit mantissa), as
    /// `legacyF16ToF32` widens it.
    fn half(h: u32) -> f32 {
        let (s, e, m) = ((h >> 15) & 1, (h >> 10) & 31, h & 1023);
        let v = match e {
            0 => m as f32 * 2f32.powi(-24),
            31 if m == 0 => f32::INFINITY,
            31 => f32::NAN,
            _ => (1024 + m) as f32 * 2f32.powi(e as i32 - 25),
        };
        if s == 1 { -v } else { v }
    }

    #[test]
    fn small_floats_widen_as_halves() {
        // Unsigned 11- and 10-bit floats: a 5-bit exponent biased 15 over a
        // 6- or 5-bit mantissa, no sign; values from the D3D/GL spec.
        let f11 = |x: u32| half(x << half_shift(11));
        let f10 = |x: u32| half(x << half_shift(10));
        assert_eq!(f11(0), 0.0);
        assert_eq!(f11(0x001), 2f32.powi(-20)); // smallest denormal
        assert_eq!(f11(0x03F), 63.0 * 2f32.powi(-20)); // largest denormal
        assert_eq!(f11(0x040), 2f32.powi(-14)); // smallest normal
        assert_eq!(f11(0x3C0), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(f11(0x3E0), 1.5);
        assert_eq!(f11(0x7BF), 65024.0); // largest
        assert_eq!(f11(0x7C0), f32::INFINITY);
        assert!(f11(0x7C1).is_nan());
        assert_eq!(f10(0x001), 2f32.powi(-19));
        assert_eq!(f10(0x020), 2f32.powi(-14));
        assert_eq!(f10(0x1E0), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(f10(0x3DF), 64512.0);
        assert_eq!(f10(0x3E0), f32::INFINITY);
        assert!(f10(0x3FF).is_nan());
        // A 16-bit float is a half already, sign included.
        assert_eq!(half(0xBC00 << half_shift(16)), -1.0);
    }
}

```

`crates/victory-shader/src/emit/mod.rs`:

```rs
//! DXIL emission (decision 0003, step 3): a console vertex, pixel, compute
//! or mesh shader as a PC DXIL container (SM 6.6) that host D3D12 accepts.
//! Compute shaders keep the console's thread-group size; one that depends
//! on the lane layout (cross-lane operations) declares the console's wave
//! size (`WaveSize`), so the host device must support it.
//!
//! What the host binds for a translated shader ([`HostShader`]):
//!
//! * **User data** at `b0, space 0` (32-bit root constants or a constant
//!   buffer, per stage): dword `index` holds a root parameter's value, as
//!   [`UserData`] lists. A root-constant dword is the constant. A
//!   descriptor table is the byte offset of its first descriptor in its
//!   heap: the descriptor index times 32 for CBV/SRV/UAV tables, times 16
//!   for sampler tables (the console's descriptor sizes; the code adds
//!   offsets in those units). The heap bases of dynamic resources are 0
//!   and not listed.
//! * **Descriptors** through SM 6.6 `ResourceDescriptorHeap[]` and
//!   `SamplerDescriptorHeap[]`, at the index the console address gives, so
//!   the host heaps keep the title's descriptor order. The root signature
//!   needs `CBV_SRV_UAV_HEAP_DIRECTLY_INDEXED` and
//!   `SAMPLER_HEAP_DIRECTLY_INDEXED`.
//! * **Immediate samplers** as static samplers `s<n>, space 0`, `n` the
//!   position in [`HostShader::samplers`] (the console sampler words) and
//!   [`HostShader::static_samplers`] (the same decoded into a D3D12 static
//!   sampler description). Comparison sampling (added 2026-11-23): an
//!   immediate sampler it uses has a comparison filter there (bit 0x80);
//!   a heap sampler it uses must be a comparison sampler on the host.
//! * **Root CBVs and root SRVs** (raw buffers) as root descriptors
//!   `b<i>` / `t<i>` in [`ROOT_CBV_SPACE`], `i` the title's root parameter
//!   index ([`HostShader::root_cbvs`], [`HostShader::root_srvs`]); the
//!   address the title sets is the buffer's.
//! * **Vertex fetch** (added 2026-11-23). The title's mesh and
//!   vertex programs fetch vertices themselves with typed-format loads
//!   (`tbuffer_load_format_*`): the format (8_8_8_8 unorm, 16_16 snorm,
//!   2_10_10_10 unorm, 8_8_8_8 and 16_16_16_16 uint...) is in the
//!   instruction, so the translation reads raw bytes and converts them
//!   itself. Their descriptors are built around a root SRV (stride 1, no
//!   record limit): the host binds the root SRV `t<slot>` above with the
//!   address the title sets, nothing more. The vertex index, the stride
//!   and the attribute offset are the shader's own arithmetic on data in
//!   that buffer (per-stream headers), not descriptor fields.
//! * **Buffer views in the heap** are declared by how the shader reads
//!   them: raw (ByteAddressBuffer) for dword loads and stores, atomics and
//!   typed-format loads without an index; structured with the used-resource
//!   entry's stride when indexed; typed with four 32-bit float channels for
//!   `buffer_load_format_*` and `buffer_store_format_*`. The host's view at
//!   that index must be of that kind and start at the console descriptor's
//!   base address (raw: `R32_TYPELESS` with the raw flag), whatever kind the
//!   title's view description says. Typed-format loads from heap
//!   descriptors (1,024 world compute programs, ray-tracing material
//!   resolves) read raw views this way.
//!
//! * **Texture atomics** use a scalar integer UAV. The host binds R32_UINT
//!   for 32-bit operations and R32G32_UINT for 64-bit operations. The latter
//!   require SM 6.6 atomic support on typed and descriptor-heap resources.
//!
//! Entry points: [`translate`] (container bytes as the title passes them
//! at pipeline creation → [`HostShader`]), [`emit`] (the same with the
//! earlier stages already run). The root constants of each stage must
//! cover [`HostShader::user_data_dwords`]. Stability: these types and the
//! binding scheme are what pipeline creation builds on; changes are
//! announced.
//! * **Signatures** as the console container has them (same semantics,
//!   registers and masks), so the input layout and stage linking are the
//!   title's; pixel outputs are plain 32-bit values.
//! * **Mesh shaders** ([`HwStage::Ms`], `ms_6_6`): user data and
//!   descriptors as above (the root constants visible to the mesh stage);
//!   the pipeline is a mesh pipeline (pipeline-state stream, no input
//!   layout) with the title's pixel shader. The thread group is the
//!   console's in lanes (`[numthreads]` in the DXIL), the vertex and
//!   primitive maxima its own, triangles only, no wave size required. The
//!   console numbers groups in x only: the draw path passes the title's
//!   count as `DispatchMesh(x, 1, 1)`. Per-primitive outputs (`PSG1`) are
//!   the console's, without `SV_PrimitiveID` and `SV_CullPrimitive` (the
//!   console never exports them).
//! * **Rectangle lists** ([`rect_list_gs`], `gs_6_6`): the console draws a
//!   rectangle from three vertices; the host has no such topology. A
//!   pipeline the title makes for rectangles (topology type 19) gets a
//!   geometry shader of ours between the translated vertex and pixel
//!   shaders and draws triangle lists with the title's own vertex counts.
//!   It binds nothing.

mod bitcode;
mod container;
#[cfg(all(test, windows))]
mod diff_tests;
#[cfg(all(test, windows))]
mod intersect_tests;
#[cfg(all(windows, any(test, feature = "host")))]
pub mod host;
mod lower;
mod own_bits;
mod rect;
mod sampler;
mod shader;
mod threading;
#[cfg(windows)]
pub mod validator;
#[cfg(all(test, windows))]
mod valu_tests;
#[cfg(all(test, windows))]
mod waterfall_tests;
#[cfg(all(test, windows))]
mod wave64_tests;
mod wave;

use crate::dxbc::{Container, FourCC};
use crate::native::{HwStage, NativeProgram, RootType};
use crate::{ShaderError, io, ir, resource, structure};

pub use bitcode::census;
pub use sampler::StaticSampler;
pub use lower::set_host_max_wave;
pub use rect::rect_list_gs;
pub use shader::{
    MEMORY_FAULTS, MEMORY_PAGES, ROOT_CBV_SPACE, SAMPLER_SPACE, SLOT_FAULTS, SLOT_MEMORY, SLOT_STRIDES,
    SLOT_STRIDES_COUNT, USER_DATA_SPACE, USER_MEMORY_BASE, USER_VIEW_ADDRESS, USER_VIEW_BIAS,
    set_view_heap_limit, view_heap_limit,
};

/// The loop limit without an override: 2^20.
pub const DEFAULT_LOOP_LIMIT: u32 = lower::LOOP_LIMIT;

/// The iteration count after which a translated loop is left, per lane and
/// per entry into the loop: [`DEFAULT_LOOP_LIMIT`].
///
/// With the `diagnostics` feature, `VICTORY_SHADER_LOOP_LIMIT` (decimal or
/// `0x` hex, at least 1) sets it instead. A loop that hits the limit in
/// every lane of a full-screen pass still runs for seconds (2^20 times a
/// 4K screen is about 10^13 iterations); a much lower limit shows whether
/// such loops are what makes a frame slow. The value is part of the
/// translation, so the shader cache must key on it (`victory-gpu`'s does).
pub fn loop_limit() -> u32 {
    static LIMIT: std::sync::OnceLock<u32> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *LIMIT.get_or_init(|| {
        if cfg!(feature = "diagnostics") {
            parse_loop_limit(std::env::var("VICTORY_SHADER_LOOP_LIMIT").ok().as_deref())
        } else {
            lower::LOOP_LIMIT
        }
    })
}

/// Which of a translated program's group barriers wait for the whole
/// group (`GroupMemoryBarrierWithGroupSync`); the others keep their memory
/// fence and lose the wait. A wait that some thread of the group never
/// reaches is undefined on the host, and NVIDIA's wait is for every
/// thread: the group stands until Windows resets the card. (The console's
/// barrier is the wave's, whatever lanes are live, and a wave that ended
/// is not waited for.) `VICTORY_GROUP_SYNC`:
/// - unset or `2`: every barrier waits, as before.
/// - `1`: the title's `s_barrier` waits only in a block every lane runs,
///   in a program no lane can be cut out of at the iteration limit.
/// - `0`: no barrier waits, neither the title's nor the ones the
///   translation adds (wave64 programs in two host waves exchange through
///   them, so such programs compute wrong values). For one run that tells
///   whether a barrier is what stops the card: with it no run can stand in
///   a barrier.
///
/// Part of the translation: the shader cache keys on it (`victory-gpu`'s
/// does).
pub fn group_sync() -> u8 {
    static MODE: std::sync::OnceLock<u8> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *MODE.get_or_init(|| match std::env::var("VICTORY_GROUP_SYNC").ok().as_deref().map(str::trim) {
        Some("0") => 0,
        Some("1") => 1,
        _ => 2,
    })
}

/// The clean-up passes that run over a translated program before it is
/// written (`bitcode::opt`): a set of that module's pass bits. Every pass
/// is exact, so the switch is for telling a translator fault from a
/// clean-up fault, and for measuring what the clean-up is worth.
/// `VICTORY_SHADER_OPT`:
/// - unset: every pass but the last one below (63).
/// - `0`: none (the module as the lowering made it).
/// - a number (decimal or `0x` hex): those passes; 1 dead code, 2 constants
///   and identities, 4 one instruction for one value, 8 what a branch taken
///   says about its condition, 16 one read for one place within a block,
///   32 a first-lane read of two host waves without the round that asks
///   which half has a lane (where every lane has one).
///   64 the dwords of one console load read by one call for every four
///   (not on unless asked: `127` is every pass with it).
///
/// Part of the translation: the shader cache keys on it (`victory-gpu`'s
/// does).
pub fn shader_opt() -> u32 {
    static PASSES: std::sync::OnceLock<u32> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *PASSES.get_or_init(|| parse_shader_opt(std::env::var("VICTORY_SHADER_OPT").ok().as_deref()))
}

/// Everything a translation depends on besides the container: the
/// translator's own source (hashed at build time), the value of every
/// `VICTORY_*` switch it reads, the host facts the device hands it (widest
/// wave, view heap limit) and the settings above. The shader cache keys on
/// this instead of on the whole executable, so a rebuild that leaves the
/// translator alone keeps its translations. Call it after the device is made.
pub fn translation_fingerprint() -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    out.extend_from_slice(env!("VICTORY_SHADER_SOURCE_HASH").as_bytes());
    out.push(u8::from(cfg!(feature = "diagnostics")));
    out.push(u8::from(cfg!(debug_assertions)));
    for name in env!("VICTORY_SHADER_SWITCHES").split(',').filter(|n| !n.is_empty()) {
        out.extend_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        out.push(b'=');
        if let Some(value) = std::env::var_os(name) {
            out.extend_from_slice(value.as_encoded_bytes());
        }
        out.push(0);
    }
    out.extend_from_slice(&lower::host_max_wave().to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&shader::view_heap_limit().to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&loop_limit().to_le_bytes());
    out.push(group_sync());
    out.extend_from_slice(&shader_opt().to_le_bytes());
    out
}

/// `VICTORY_SHADER_OPT`'s value; every pass when it is unset or
/// unreadable. Pure, for testing.
fn parse_shader_opt(value: Option<&str>) -> u32 {
    let parsed = value
        .map(str::trim)
        .and_then(|v| match v.strip_prefix("0x") {
            Some(hex) => u32::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok(),
            None => v.parse().ok(),
        });
    parsed.map_or(bitcode::opt::DEFAULT, |n| n & bitcode::opt::ALL)
}

/// `VICTORY_SHADER_LOOP_LIMIT`'s value; the default when it is unset,
/// unreadable or 0. Pure, for testing.
fn parse_loop_limit(value: Option<&str>) -> u32 {
    let parsed = value
        .map(str::trim)
        .and_then(|v| match v.strip_prefix("0x") {
            Some(hex) => u32::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok(),
            None => v.parse().ok(),
        });
    match parsed {
        Some(n) if n > 0 => n,
        _ => lower::LOOP_LIMIT,
    }
}

/// A translated shader and what the host binds for it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct HostShader {
    pub stage: HwStage,
    /// The DXIL container, hashed as D3D12 expects.
    pub dxil: Vec<u8>,
    /// The user-data dwords the shader reads.
    pub user_data: Vec<UserData>,
    /// Immediate samplers: the four sampler words of `s<n>`.
    pub samplers: Vec<[u32; 4]>,
    /// The same samplers decoded, `s<n>` at position n: the static sampler
    /// descriptions the host's root signature declares.
    pub static_samplers: Vec<StaticSampler>,
    /// Root CBVs the shader reads: root parameter indices, each bound as
    /// `b<index>` in [`ROOT_CBV_SPACE`].
    pub root_cbvs: Vec<u8>,
    /// Root SRVs (raw buffers) the shader reads: `t<index>` in
    /// [`ROOT_CBV_SPACE`].
    pub root_srvs: Vec<u8>,
    /// Root UAVs (raw buffers) the shader reads or writes: `u<index>` in
    /// [`ROOT_CBV_SPACE`].
    pub root_uavs: Vec<u8>,
    /// Heap descriptors that can be selected from root state at bind time.
    pub root_indexed_views: Vec<crate::resource::RootIndexedView>,
}

impl HostShader {
    /// Size of the user-data buffer the shader declares, in dwords (a
    /// multiple of 4; 0 when it reads none). Root constants must cover it.
    pub fn user_data_dwords(&self) -> u32 {
        let n = self
            .user_data
            .iter()
            .map(|u| u.index + 1)
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(0);
        n.next_multiple_of(4)
    }
}

/// One dword of user data and the root parameter that fills it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct UserData {
    /// Dword in the user-data buffer (the console's user-data index).
    pub index: u32,
    /// Root parameter index in the title's root signature.
    pub slot: u8,
    /// `Constants` or `Table` (see the module notes for the value).
    pub root: RootType,
    /// Dword within the parameter.
    pub dword: u32,
}

/// Translates the vertex, pixel, compute or mesh program of a console
/// shader container.
///
/// A program refused because the first half of an interpolation is read as
/// data is translated once more with first halves evaluated as the pair
/// they start (`lower::with_first_half_pairs`), and only such a program:
/// with that on for every program, 8,551 pixel programs of the title that
/// already translated came out changed (an extra evaluation in each), for
/// the sake of 9 that did not translate.
pub fn translate(container: &[u8]) -> Result<HostShader, ShaderError> {
    match translate_plain(container) {
        Err(ShaderError::Unsupported { what, .. }) if what == lower::FIRST_HALF => {
            lower::with_first_half_pairs(|| translate_plain(container))
        }
        other => other,
    }
}

fn translate_plain(container: &[u8]) -> Result<HostShader, ShaderError> {
    let c = Container::parse(container)?;
    let dxil = c
        .part(FourCC::DXIL)
        .ok_or(ShaderError::Malformed("no DXIL part"))?;
    let native = crate::native_programs(dxil.data)?
        .into_iter()
        .find(|p| {
            matches!(
                p.stage,
                HwStage::Vs | HwStage::Ps | HwStage::Cs | HwStage::Ms
            )
        })
        .ok_or(ShaderError::Unsupported {
            offset: 0,
            what: "a container without a vertex, pixel, compute or mesh program",
        })?;
    let p = crate::spill::build(&native)?;
    // Structurisation first: tracing per-lane descriptors needs it (its
    // failure is reported after the earlier stages').
    let st = structure::structure(&p);
    let res = resource::track(&p, &native.layout, native.stage, st.as_ref().ok())?;
    let io = io::raise(&p, &native)?;
    let st = st?;
    emit(&c, &native, &p, &st, &io, &res)
}

/// Emits a program whose earlier stages already ran.
pub fn emit(
    c: &Container,
    native: &NativeProgram,
    p: &ir::Program,
    st: &structure::Structured,
    io: &io::Io,
    res: &resource::Resources,
) -> Result<HostShader, ShaderError> {
    // (what an earlier program's lowering on this thread left behind)
    lower::take_needs();
    let original = emit_program(c, native, p, st, io, res);
    // A console wave64 compute program on a host of 32-lane waves that
    // still needs 64 lanes, or whose cross-lane code sits where not every
    // lane runs: once more with its early-outs left out
    // ([`ir::without_early_outs`]), which is what usually keeps the whole
    // body from being a block every lane runs.
    let stuck = match &original {
        Ok((_, wave)) => *wave == Some(64),
        Err(ShaderError::Unsupported { what, .. }) => lower::needs_every_lane(what),
        Err(_) => false,
    };
    // (a mask with lanes elsewhere is only helped by the exact forms: not by each half-wave
    // on its own)
```
