`crates/victory-shader/src/emit/threading.rs`:

```rs
//! Jump threading for uniform diamonds. One arm can set a flag that fixes
//! the join's next branch. Registers recycled on that arm then never reach
//! the other successor, even if an ordinary SSA phi joins their values.
use crate::gfx10::{Fields, Operand, Valu};
use crate::ir::{Exit, Program, Reg, Value};
use crate::structure::{Atom, Bool, LaneExit, Structured};
use std::collections::HashMap;

fn plain(v: &Valu) -> bool {
    v.abs == 0
        && v.neg == 0
        && v.opsel == 0
        && !v.clamp
        && v.omod == 0
        && v.sdwa.is_none()
        && v.dpp.is_none()
}

fn immediate(op: Operand) -> Option<u32> {
    match op {
        Operand::Const(c) => crate::resource::inline(c),
        Operand::Literal(n) => Some(n),
        _ => None,
    }
}

pub(super) fn constant_edges(p: &Program, st: &Structured) -> Vec<(usize, usize, usize)> {
    let mut constants = HashMap::new();
    for (b, block) in p.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        for (i, inst) in block.insts.iter().enumerate() {
            if inst.name() == "v_mov_b32"
                && st.guards[b][i].is_none()
                && let Fields::Valu(v) = &inst.fields
                && plain(v)
                && let [src] = v.src.as_slice()
                && let Some(word) = immediate(*src)
                && let [(_, dst)] = inst.writes.as_slice()
            {
                constants.insert(*dst, word);
            }
        }
    }
    let mut edges = Vec::new();
    for (join, block) in p.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        let LaneExit::Branch {
            when,
            taken,
            not_taken,
        } = st.exits[join]
        else {
            continue;
        };
        if when == Bool::TRUE || when == Bool::FALSE {
            continue;
        }
        // Keep memory accesses and wave operations at their original
        // reconvergence point. Only duplicate scalar ALU and comparisons.
        if !block.insts.iter().all(|i| match &i.fields {
            Fields::Sop { .. } => true,
            Fields::Sopp { .. } => i.name().starts_with("s_cbranch_"),
            Fields::Valu(_) => i.name().starts_with("v_cmp_"),
            _ => false,
        }) {
            continue;
        }
        let [a, b] = block.preds.as_slice() else {
            continue;
        };
        // A triangle has a direct edge from the fork to the join. A full
        // diamond has an unconditional jump at the end of each arm.
        let arm_from = |arm: usize| match p.blocks[arm].preds.as_slice() {
            &[fork] if p.blocks[arm].exit == Exit::Jump(join) => Some(fork),
            _ => None,
        };
        let fork = match (arm_from(*a), arm_from(*b)) {
            (Some(f), Some(g)) if f == g => f,
            (_, Some(f)) if f == *a => f,
            (Some(f), _) if f == *b => f,
            _ => continue,
        };
        if fork == join || a == b {
            continue;
        }
        let LaneExit::Branch { when: entry, .. } = st.exits[fork] else {
            continue;
        };
        if !st
            .bools
            .support(entry)
            .iter()
            .all(|a| matches!(a, Atom::Uniform(_)))
        {
            continue;
        }
        for (edge, &pred) in block.preds.iter().enumerate() {
            let value = |v: Value| {
                let input = block
                    .phis
                    .iter()
                    .find(|p| p.value == v)
                    .map_or(v, |p| p.args[edge]);
                constants.get(&input).copied()
            };
            // Restrict the branch's decision diagram to known comparisons.
            // Unknown tests stop the proof. Keep the original join for the
            // other arm, which may still go either way.
            let mut cond = when;
            while let Some((Atom::Lane(id), lo, hi)) = st.bools.node(cond) {
                let Some(inst) = block
                    .insts
                    .iter()
                    .find(|i| i.writes.iter().any(|&(_, v)| v == id))
                else {
                    break;
                };
                let Fields::Valu(v) = &inst.fields else { break };
                let [left, right] = v.src.as_slice() else {
                    break;
                };
                let operand = |op| match op {
                    Operand::Vector { reg, dwords: 1 } => value(inst.read(Reg::V(reg))?),
                    _ => immediate(op),
                };
                let (Some(x), Some(y)) = (operand(*left), operand(*right)) else {
                    break;
                };
                if !plain(v) {
                    break;
                }
                let yes = match inst.name() {
                    "v_cmp_eq_u32" | "v_cmp_eq_i32" => x == y,
                    "v_cmp_ne_u32" | "v_cmp_ne_i32" => x != y,
                    _ => break,
                };
                cond = if yes { hi } else { lo };
            }
            if cond == Bool::TRUE || cond == Bool::FALSE {
                edges.push((
                    pred,
                    join,
                    if cond == Bool::TRUE { taken } else { not_taken },
                ));
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    edges
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::ir;
    use crate::structure;

    // s8 initially holds a descriptor address. One arm overwrites it with
    // a buffer load and sets v1. Only that arm can use s8 as the stored value.
    const WORDS: [u32; 19] = [
        0xbe810380, // s1 = 0 (table address high)
        0xf4080200, 0xfa000000, // load SRV into s[8:11]
        0xf4080300, 0xfa000020, // load UAV into s[12:15]
        0x7e020280, // v1 = 0
        0xbf068002, 0xbf850003, // if s2 == 0, jump to join
        0xf4200204, 0xfa00000c, // s8 = buffer.Load(12)
        0x7e020281, // v1 = 1
        0x7d840280, 0xbf870002, // join: if v1 == 0, jump to constant
        0x7e060208, 0xbf820001, // v3 = s8, jump to store
        0x7e060293, // constant: v3 = 19
        0xe0700000, 0x80030300, // store v3 at byte 0
        0xbf810000, // end
    ];

    fn program(words: &[u32]) -> Program {
        ir::build(
            &words
                .iter()
                .flat_map(|w| w.to_le_bytes())
                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            false,
            4,
        )
        .unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn only_the_buffer_load_reaches_the_numeric_read() {
        let p = program(&WORDS);
        let st = structure::structure(&p).unwrap();
        let edges = constant_edges(&p, &st);
        assert_eq!(edges, [(0, 2, 4)]);
        let p = ir::thread_edges(&p, &edges).unwrap();
        let load = &p.blocks[1].insts[0];
        assert_eq!(p.blocks[3].insts[0].read(Reg::S(8)), load.write(Reg::S(8)));
        assert_eq!(
            p.blocks[0].exit,
            Exit::Branch {
                taken: 6,
                not_taken: 1
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(p.blocks[6].exit, Exit::Jump(4));
        assert_eq!(p.blocks[6].insts.len(), p.blocks[2].insts.len());
    }

    #[test]
    fn leaves_unknown_flags_and_divergent_forks_alone() {
        let mut words = WORDS;
        words[5] = 0x7e020202; // v1 = s2
        words[10] = 0x7e020203; // v1 = s3
        let p = program(&words);
        assert!(constant_edges(&p, &structure::structure(&p).unwrap()).is_empty());
        let mut words = WORDS;
        words[6] = 0x7d840080; // compare 0 with lane-dependent v0
        words[7] = 0xbf870003; // branch on VCC
        let p = program(&words);
        assert!(constant_edges(&p, &structure::structure(&p).unwrap()).is_empty());
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-shader/src/emit/validator.rs`:

```rs
//! The DXIL validator in `dxil.dll` (`IDxcValidator`), for tests and the
//! offline batch. Translated shaders do not need it: they carry the
//! container hash we compute (`container::hash`).
//!
//! The DLL is found at `VICTORY_DXIL` if set, else the newest Windows SDK's
//! `bin\<version>\x64\dxil.dll`, else wherever `LoadLibrary` finds it.

use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::path::PathBuf;

use windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::{GetProcAddress, LoadLibraryW};

type Hresult = i32;

#[repr(C)]
struct Guid(u32, u16, u16, [u8; 8]);

const CLSID_DXC_VALIDATOR: Guid = Guid(
    0x8ca3_e215,
    0xf728,
    0x4cf3,
    [0x8c, 0xdd, 0x88, 0xaf, 0x91, 0x75, 0x87, 0xa1],
);
const IID_IDXC_VALIDATOR: Guid = Guid(
    0xa6e8_2bd2,
    0x1fd7,
    0x4826,
    [0x98, 0x11, 0x28, 0x57, 0xe7, 0x97, 0xf4, 0x9a],
);
/// `DxcValidatorFlags_InPlaceEdit`: sign the container we pass.
const IN_PLACE_EDIT: u32 = 1;

type CreateInstance =
    unsafe extern "system" fn(*const Guid, *const Guid, *mut *mut c_void) -> Hresult;

/// COM object: a pointer to a table of method pointers.
type Object = *mut *const usize;

unsafe fn method<F: Copy>(obj: Object, slot: usize) -> F {
    // SAFETY: the caller names a slot of the object's interface.
    unsafe { std::mem::transmute_copy(&*(*obj).add(slot)) }
}

unsafe fn release(obj: Object) {
    if !obj.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: slot 2 of every COM interface is Release.
        unsafe { method::<unsafe extern "system" fn(Object) -> u32>(obj, 2)(obj) };
    }
}

/// An `IDxcBlob` over our bytes: QueryInterface, AddRef, Release,
/// GetBufferPointer, GetBufferSize. Lives on the caller's stack.
#[repr(C)]
struct Blob {
    vtable: *const BlobVtable,
    data: *mut u8,
    len: usize,
}

/// IUnknown and IDxcBlob, as raw GUID bytes.
const IUNKNOWN: [u8; 16] = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0xc0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x46];
const IDXC_BLOB: [u8; 16] = [
    0x08, 0xfb, 0xa5, 0x8b, 0x95, 0x51, 0xe2, 0x40, 0xac, 0x58, 0x0d, 0x98, 0x9c, 0x3a, 0x01, 0x02,
];

unsafe extern "system" fn blob_qi(
    this: *mut Blob,
    iid: *const [u8; 16],
    out: *mut *mut c_void,
) -> Hresult {
    // SAFETY: the validator passes valid pointers.
    unsafe {
        if *iid == IUNKNOWN || *iid == IDXC_BLOB {
            *out = this.cast();
            0
        } else {
            *out = std::ptr::null_mut();
            0x8000_4002_u32 as i32 // E_NOINTERFACE
        }
    }
}
unsafe extern "system" fn blob_ref(_: *mut Blob) -> u32 {
    1
}
unsafe extern "system" fn blob_ptr(this: *mut Blob) -> *mut u8 {
    // SAFETY: `this` is our blob.
    unsafe { (*this).data }
}
unsafe extern "system" fn blob_len(this: *mut Blob) -> usize {
    // SAFETY: `this` is our blob.
    unsafe { (*this).len }
}

#[repr(C)]
struct BlobVtable {
    qi: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut Blob, *const [u8; 16], *mut *mut c_void) -> Hresult,
    add_ref: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut Blob) -> u32,
    release: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut Blob) -> u32,
    ptr: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut Blob) -> *mut u8,
    len: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut Blob) -> usize,
}

static BLOB_VTABLE: BlobVtable = BlobVtable {
    qi: blob_qi,
    add_ref: blob_ref,
    release: blob_ref,
    ptr: blob_ptr,
    len: blob_len,
};

pub struct Validator {
    object: Object,
}

// SAFETY: the validator object is free-threaded (DXC's validator has no
// thread affinity); calls are serialised by `&mut self`.
unsafe impl Send for Validator {}

impl Validator {
    /// Where `dxil.dll` is looked for.
    pub fn default_path() -> Option<PathBuf> {
        if let Some(p) = std::env::var_os("VICTORY_DXIL") {
            return Some(p.into());
        }
        let kits = PathBuf::from(r"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\bin");
        let mut versions: Vec<PathBuf> = std::fs::read_dir(&kits)
            .ok()?
            .filter_map(Result::ok)
            .map(|e| e.path().join(r"x64\dxil.dll"))
            .filter(|p| p.exists())
            .collect();
        versions.sort();
        versions.pop()
    }

    /// Loads `path`'s validator (or `dxil.dll` from the DLL search path).
    pub fn load(path: Option<&std::path::Path>) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let name: Vec<u16> = path
            .map_or_else(|| "dxil.dll".into(), |p| p.as_os_str().to_owned())
            .to_string_lossy()
            .encode_utf16()
            .chain([0])
            .collect();
        // SAFETY: plain Win32 calls with a NUL-terminated name.
        unsafe {
            let module = LoadLibraryW(name.as_ptr());
            if module.is_null() {
                return Err(format!("cannot load {}", String::from_utf16_lossy(&name)));
            }
            let create = GetProcAddress(module, c"DxcCreateInstance".as_ptr().cast())
                .ok_or("dxil.dll lacks DxcCreateInstance")?;
            let create: CreateInstance = std::mem::transmute(create);
            let mut object = std::ptr::null_mut();
            let hr = create(&CLSID_DXC_VALIDATOR, &IID_IDXC_VALIDATOR, &mut object);
            if hr < 0 || object.is_null() {
                return Err(format!("DxcCreateInstance(validator) failed: {hr:#x}"));
            }
            Ok(Validator {
                object: object.cast(),
            })
        }
    }

    /// Validates `container` and signs it in place; the error text if it
    /// is rejected.
    pub fn validate(&mut self, container: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
        let mut blob = Blob {
            vtable: &BLOB_VTABLE,
            data: container.as_mut_ptr(),
            len: container.len(),
        };
        // SAFETY: IDxcValidator::Validate (slot 3) with our blob; then
        // IDxcOperationResult GetStatus (3) and GetErrorBuffer (5), and
        // IDxcBlob GetBufferPointer (3) / GetBufferSize (4).
        unsafe {
            let mut result: Object = std::ptr::null_mut();
            let validate: unsafe extern "system" fn(
                Object,
                *mut Blob,
                u32,
                *mut Object,
            ) -> Hresult = method(self.object, 3);
            let hr = validate(self.object, &mut blob, IN_PLACE_EDIT, &mut result);
            if hr < 0 || result.is_null() {
                return Err(format!("Validate failed: {hr:#x}"));
            }
            let mut status = 0;
            let get_status: unsafe extern "system" fn(Object, *mut Hresult) -> Hresult =
                method(result, 3);
            get_status(result, &mut status);
            let mut text = String::new();
            if status < 0 {
                let mut errors: Object = std::ptr::null_mut();
                let get_errors: unsafe extern "system" fn(Object, *mut Object) -> Hresult =
                    method(result, 5);
                if get_errors(result, &mut errors) >= 0 && !errors.is_null() {
                    let ptr: unsafe extern "system" fn(Object) -> *const u8 = method(errors, 3);
                    let len: unsafe extern "system" fn(Object) -> usize = method(errors, 4);
                    let bytes = std::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr(errors), len(errors));
                    text = String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes)
                        .trim_end_matches('\0')
                        .trim()
                        .into();
                    release(errors);
                }
                if text.is_empty() {
                    text = format!("rejected ({status:#x})");
                }
            }
            release(result);
            if status < 0 { Err(text) } else { Ok(()) }
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for Validator {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: we own one reference.
        unsafe { release(self.object) };
    }
}
```

`crates/victory-shader/src/emit/valu_tests.rs`:

```rs
//! End-to-end tests of synthetic GFX10 VALU shaders lowered to DXIL, validated
//! by `dxil.dll` when present, and executed on the host GPU and WARP.
//!
//! Covers RDNA2 hardware semantics that differ from naive DXIL lowering:
//! `v_med3_f32`/`v_med3_f16` with NaN operands, `v_fract_f32`/`v_fract_f16`
//! near `1.0`, turn-range reduction for `v_sin_*`/`v_cos_*`, and the LDS
//! float atomics `ds_min_f32`/`ds_max_f32`.

use super::host::{Dispatch, Host, Root, View};
use super::{HostShader, lower, validator};
use crate::native::{
    ComputeIo, HwStage, NativeProgram, ResourceType, RootParam, RootType, StageIo, UsedResource,
};
use crate::{io, ir, resource, structure};

const S_ENDPGM: u32 = 0xBF81_0000;

/// SOP1 `s_mov_b32 sdst, src0`.
const fn s_mov_b32(sdst: u8, src0: u8) -> u32 {
    0xBE80_0000 | (sdst as u32) << 16 | 0x03 << 8 | src0 as u32
}

/// SOP2 `op sdst, src0, src1`.
const fn sop2(op: u8, sdst: u8, src0: u8, src1: u8) -> u32 {
    0x8000_0000
        | (op as u32 & 0x7F) << 23
        | (sdst as u32 & 0x7F) << 16
        | (src1 as u32) << 8
        | src0 as u32
}

/// SMEM `s_load_dwordx4 s[dst:dst+3], s[base:base+1], 0` (soffset = null).
const fn s_load_dwordx4(dst: u8, base: u8) -> [u32; 2] {
    [
        0x3D << 26 | 0x02 << 18 | (dst as u32) << 6 | (base as u32 >> 1),
        125 << 25,
    ]
}

/// VOP1 `op vdst, src0` (`src0`: 0..105 = SGPR, 256..511 = VGPR).
const fn vop1(op: u16, vdst: u8, src0: u16) -> u32 {
    0x7E00_0000 | (vdst as u32) << 17 | (op as u32) << 9 | (src0 as u32 & 0x1FF)
}

/// VOP3 `op vdst, src0, src1, src2` (no modifiers).
const fn vop3(op: u16, vdst: u8, src0: u16, src1: u16, src2: u16) -> [u32; 2] {
    vop3_mod(op, vdst, src0, src1, src2, 0, 0, 0, false)
}

/// VOP3 `op vdst, src0, src1, src2` with explicit `abs`, `neg`, `omod`, `clamp`.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
const fn vop3_mod(
    op: u16,
    vdst: u8,
    src0: u16,
    src1: u16,
    src2: u16,
    abs: u8,
    neg: u8,
    omod: u8,
    clamp: bool,
) -> [u32; 2] {
    [
        0x35 << 26
            | (op as u32 & 0x3FF) << 16
            | (clamp as u32) << 15
            | (abs as u32 & 7) << 8
            | vdst as u32,
        (neg as u32 & 7) << 29
            | (omod as u32 & 3) << 27
            | (src0 as u32 & 0x1FF)
            | (src1 as u32 & 0x1FF) << 9
            | (src2 as u32 & 0x1FF) << 18,
    ]
}

/// MUBUF `buffer_store_dword vdata, off, s[srsrc:srsrc+3], 0 offset:byte_off`.
const fn buffer_store_dword(vdata: u8, srsrc: u8, byte_off: u16) -> [u32; 2] {
    [
        0x38 << 26 | 0x1C << 18 | (byte_off as u32 & 0xFFF),
        0x80 << 24 | ((srsrc as u32 >> 2) & 0x1F) << 16 | (vdata as u32) << 8,
    ]
}

const fn sgpr(n: u8) -> u16 {
    n as u16
}

const fn vgpr(n: u8) -> u16 {
    256 + n as u16
}

/// Builds and lowers a 1-thread synthetic RDNA2 compute shader that receives
/// 4 dwords of root constants in `s0..s3`, runs `body` (leaving its result in
/// `v0`), and stores `v0` to dword 0 of the raw UAV at heap index 0.
fn build_valu_cs(body: &[u32]) -> HostShader {
    build_cs(body, 1, 0)
}

/// [`build_valu_cs`] with `threads` threads in x (thread index in `v0`
/// on entry, before `body`) and `lds_bytes` of LDS (a multiple of 512).
fn build_cs(body: &[u32], threads: u32, lds_bytes: u32) -> HostShader {
    let mut words = Vec::new();
    // s[4:5] = descriptor table address (heap index 0 -> byte offset 0).
    words.push(s_mov_b32(5, 0x80)); // inline constant 0
    words.extend_from_slice(&s_load_dwordx4(8, 4));
    // Copy root constants s0..s3 into v1..v4 so VALU instructions operate on
    // VGPRs just as they do in real shaders.
    for i in 0..4u8 {
        words.push(vop1(0x001, i + 1, sgpr(i))); // v_mov_b32
    }
    words.extend_from_slice(body);
    words.extend_from_slice(&buffer_store_dword(0, 8, 0));
    words.push(S_ENDPGM);

    let code: Vec<u8> = words.iter().flat_map(|w| w.to_le_bytes()).collect();
    let native = NativeProgram {
        stage: HwStage::Cs,
        wave64: false,
        vgprs: 8,
        layout: vec![
            RootParam {
                root: RootType::Constants,
                table_offset_dwords: 0,
                sgprs: 4,
                base_register: 0,
                user_data: 0,
                slot: 0,
            },
            RootParam {
                root: RootType::Table,
                table_offset_dwords: 0,
                sgprs: 1,
                base_register: 0,
                user_data: 4,
                slot: 1,
            },
        ],
        used: vec![UsedResource {
            kind: ResourceType::Uav,
            root: RootType::Table,
            table_offset_dwords: 0,
            lower_bound: 0,
            stride: 0,
            dwords: 4,
            user_data: 4,
            slot: 1,
        }],
        io: StageIo::Cs(ComputeIo {
            rsrc2: (5 << 1) | ((lds_bytes / 512) << 15), // 5 user SGPRs: s0..s4
            threads: [threads, 1, 1],
        }),
        code,
    };

    let p = ir::build(&native.code, native.wave64, native.vgprs).expect("ir::build");
    let st = structure::structure(&p).expect("structure");
    let res =
        resource::track(&p, &native.layout, native.stage, Some(&st)).expect("resource::track");
    let io = io::raise(&p, &native).expect("io::raise");
    let lowered = lower::lower(&lower::Parts {
        native: &native,
        p: &p,
        st: &st,
        io: &io,
        res: &res,
        inputs: Vec::new(),
        outputs: Vec::new(),
        prims: Vec::new(),
        mesh_stride: 0,
    })
    .expect("lower");

    let shader = HostShader {
        stage: HwStage::Cs,
        dxil: lowered.dxil,
        user_data: lowered.user_data,
        samplers: lowered.samplers,
        static_samplers: Vec::new(),
        root_cbvs: lowered.root_cbvs,
        root_srvs: lowered.root_srvs,
        root_uavs: lowered.root_uavs,
        root_indexed_views: res.root_indexed_views,
    };

    if let Ok(mut v) = validator::Validator::load(validator::Validator::default_path().as_deref()) {
        let mut copy = shader.dxil.clone();
        let ours = copy[4..20].to_vec();
        v.validate(&mut copy).expect("DXIL validation failed");
        assert_eq!(copy[4..20], ours[..], "container hash mismatch");
    }

    shader
}

/// One GPU test at a time. With these tests on the hardware adapter and WARP
/// from several test threads at once, now and then none of their dispatches
/// ever completes and the test binary hangs; and two GPU tests at once on
/// WARP can end the test process with an access violation. Other GPU test
/// modules take this lock too.
pub(super) static ONE_AT_A_TIME: std::sync::Mutex<()> = std::sync::Mutex::new(());

/// Runs `shader` on every available SM 6.6 host (hardware GPU and WARP) for
/// each 4-dword input set and invokes `check(backend, case_index, inputs, result_dword)`.
fn run_cases(
    shader: &HostShader,
    cases: &[[u32; 4]],
    check: impl FnMut(&str, usize, [u32; 4], u32),
) {
    run_cases_on(shader, cases, &[("hardware", false), ("warp", true)], check);
}

fn run_cases_on(
    shader: &HostShader,
    cases: &[[u32; 4]],
    devices: &[(&str, bool)],
    mut check: impl FnMut(&str, usize, [u32; 4], u32),
) {
    let _one = ONE_AT_A_TIME.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    let mut ran = 0;
    for &(label, warp) in devices {
        let Ok(host) = Host::new(warp) else {
            eprintln!("no SM 6.6 {label} device; skipped");
            continue;
        };
        let (root, pso) = host
            .compute_pipeline(shader)
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{label}: compute_pipeline failed: {e}"));
        for (i, &inputs) in cases.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut ud = vec![0u32; shader.user_data_dwords().max(1) as usize];
            for u in &shader.user_data {
                ud[u.index as usize] = match (u.root, u.slot) {
                    (RootType::Constants, 0) => inputs[u.dword as usize],
                    (RootType::Table, 1) => 0,
                    other => panic!("unexpected user data {other:?}"),
                };
            }
            let out = host
                .dispatch(
                    &root,
                    &pso,
                    &Dispatch {
                        roots: vec![(0, Root::Constants(ud))],
                        views: &[View::RawUav(1)],
                        samplers: &[],
                        groups: [1, 1, 1],
                    },
                )
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{label}: dispatch failed: {e}"));
            check(label, i, inputs, out[0][0]);
        }
        ran += 1;
    }
    if ran == 0 && devices.iter().all(|&(_, warp)| !warp) {
        // A case for the hardware adapter alone, on a machine without one.
        eprintln!("no SM 6.6 hardware device; a hardware-only case not run");
        return;
    }
    assert!(ran > 0, "no SM 6.6 device available ({devices:?})");
}

fn is_f16_nan(bits: u16) -> bool {
    (bits & 0x7FFF) > 0x7C00
}

fn f16_to_f32(bits: u16) -> f32 {
    let sign = u32::from(bits >> 15) << 31;
    let exp = (bits >> 10) & 0x1F;
    let mant = bits & 0x3FF;
    let f32_bits = match exp {
        0 => {
            if mant == 0 {
                sign
            } else {
                let mut m = u32::from(mant);
                let mut e = 127 - 14;
                while (m & 0x400) == 0 {
                    m <<= 1;
                    e -= 1;
                }
                sign | (e << 23) | ((m & 0x3FF) << 13)
            }
        }
        0x1F => sign | (0xFF << 23) | (u32::from(mant) << 13),
        _ => sign | ((u32::from(exp) + 112) << 23) | (u32::from(mant) << 13),
    };
    f32::from_bits(f32_bits)
}

#[test]
fn packed_add_selects_halves_of_inline_constants() {
    // Add the inline constant 1/(2*pi) to v1 (zero) to read back its two halves.
    // The same GFX10 source field (248) has a different bit pattern for a
    // packed floating-point and a packed integer instruction.
    let cases = [
        // v_pk_add_f16 v0, 0x3118, v1
        ([0xcc0f4000, 0x1a0202f8], 0x0000_3118),
        // v_pk_add_f16 v0, 0x3118, v1 op_sel_hi:[0,1] (use low twice)
        ([0xcc0f4000, 0x120202f8], 0x3118_3118),
        // v_pk_add_u16 v0, 0x3e22f983, v1
        ([0xcc0a4000, 0x1a0202f8], 0x3e22_f983),
    ];
    for (words, expected) in cases {
        let shader = build_valu_cs(&words);
        run_cases(&shader, &[[0; 4]], |backend, _, _, got| {
            assert_eq!(got, expected, "{backend}: {words:08x?}");
        });
    }
}

/// The float `v_cvt_f32_f64` gives for `x`: Rust's rounding (to nearest
/// even), with results below the smallest normal float flushed to signed
/// zero as the console's default float mode does.
fn cvt_f32_f64_reference(x: f64) -> u32 {
    let r = x as f32;
    if r.is_subnormal() || (r == 0.0 && x != 0.0) {
        r.to_bits() & 0x8000_0000
    } else {
        r.to_bits()
    }
}

#[test]
#[ignore = "expects results below the smallest normal float flushed to zero; the IEEE lowering (v_cvt_f32_f64_matches_ieee754) is kept until the console's mode is checked"]
fn v_cvt_f32_f64_rounds_to_nearest_even() {
    // v_cvt_f32_f64 v0, v[1:2] (VOP1 opcode 0x0f)
    let shader = build_valu_cs(&[vop1(0x00f, 0, vgpr(1))]);
    let tie_even = 1.0f64 + f64::from(f32::EPSILON) / 2.0; // ties to 1.0
    let tie_odd = 1.0f64 + 1.5 * f64::from(f32::EPSILON); // ties up to 1 + 2 ulp
    let values = [
        0.0,
        -0.0,
        1.0,
        -2.5,
        std::f64::consts::PI,
        1.0e-3,
        123_456_789.123,
        tie_even,
        tie_odd,
        1.0 + f64::from(f32::EPSILON) * 0.75,
        f64::from(f32::MAX),
        f64::from(f32::MAX) * 1.000_000_1, // rounds to infinity
        1.0e300,
        -1.0e300,
        1.0e-40, // a float denormal: flushed
        -1.0e-300,
        f64::from(f32::MIN_POSITIVE),
        f64::INFINITY,
        f64::NEG_INFINITY,
        f64::NAN,
    ];
    let inputs: Vec<[u32; 4]> = values
        .iter()
        .map(|x| {
            let b = x.to_bits();
            [b as u32, (b >> 32) as u32, 0, 0]
        })
        .collect();
    run_cases(&shader, &inputs, |backend, i, _, got| {
        let x = values[i];
        if x.is_nan() {
            assert!(f32::from_bits(got).is_nan(), "{backend}: cvt({x}) = {got:#010x}, want NaN");
            return;
        }
        let want = cvt_f32_f64_reference(x);
        assert_eq!(got, want, "{backend}: cvt({x:e}) = {got:#010x}, want {want:#010x}");
    });
}

/// The lane `v_permlane16_b32` (`cross` false) or `v_permlanex16_b32` reads
/// for `lane`, with selector dwords `s1` (lanes 0-7 of a row) and `s2`.
fn permlane_source(lane: u32, s1: u32, s2: u32, cross: bool) -> u32 {
    let sel = u64::from(s1) | u64::from(s2) << 32;
    let pick = (sel >> (4 * (lane & 15)) & 15) as u32;
    let row = if cross {
        (lane & !31) | ((lane & 16) ^ 16)
    } else {
        lane & !15
    };
    row | pick
}

#[test]
fn v_permlane16_and_x16_read_the_lanes_their_selectors_pick() {
    // 32 lanes, each with its lane number in v0; v1 = permute(v0, s0, s1);
    // lane `read` of v1 into s12, then into v0 for the store.
    let selectors: [(u32, u32); 3] = [
        (0x7654_3210, 0xfedc_ba98), // identity within the row
        (0x89ab_cdef, 0x0123_4567), // reversed
        (0x1111_1111, 0xf0f0_f0f0), // repeats
    ];
    for (op, cross) in [(0x377u16, false), (0x378, true)] {
        for read in [0u8, 5, 15, 16, 22, 31] {
            let mut body = Vec::new();
            body.extend_from_slice(&vop3(op, 1, vgpr(0), sgpr(0), sgpr(1)));
            // v_readlane_b32 s12, v1, read (inline constant 128 + read)
            body.extend_from_slice(&vop3(0x360, 12, vgpr(1), 128 + u16::from(read), 0));
            body.push(vop1(0x001, 0, sgpr(12))); // v_mov_b32 v0, s12
            let shader = build_cs(&body, 32, 0);
            let inputs: Vec<[u32; 4]> = selectors.iter().map(|&(a, b)| [a, b, 0, 0]).collect();
            // Cross-lane code declares WaveSize(32), which WARP's pipeline
            // creation refuses: hardware only.
            run_cases_on(&shader, &inputs, &[("hardware", false)], |backend, i, inp, got| {
                let want = permlane_source(u32::from(read), inp[0], inp[1], cross);
                assert_eq!(
                    got, want,
                    "{backend}: op {op:#x} selectors {:08x?}, lane {read}",
                    selectors[i]
                );
            });
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn v_med3_f32_matches_rdna2_with_nan() {
    // v_med3_f32 v0, v1, v2, v3 (VOP3 opcode 0x157)
    let shader = build_valu_cs(&vop3(0x157, 0, vgpr(1), vgpr(2), vgpr(3)));
    let nan = f32::NAN.to_bits();
    let f = f32::to_bits;

    let cases: &[([u32; 4], Option<f32>)] = &[
        // Normal medians (all orderings).
        ([f(1.0), f(2.0), f(3.0), 0], Some(2.0)),
        ([f(3.0), f(1.0), f(2.0), 0], Some(2.0)),
        ([f(-5.0), f(0.0), f(5.0), 0], Some(0.0)),
        ([f(1.0), f(1.0), f(2.0), 0], Some(1.0)),
        // One NaN: RDNA2 returns min3 of the non-NaN operands.
        ([f(1.0), f(2.0), nan, 0], Some(1.0)),
        ([nan, f(1.0), f(0.0), 0], Some(0.0)),
        ([nan, f(0.0), f(1.0), 0], Some(0.0)),
        ([f(2.0), nan, f(1.0), 0], Some(1.0)),
        ([f(-3.0), nan, f(4.0), 0], Some(-3.0)),
        // Two NaNs: returns the sole non-NaN operand.
        ([nan, f(5.0), nan, 0], Some(5.0)),
        ([nan, nan, f(-2.0), 0], Some(-2.0)),
        ([f(7.0), nan, nan, 0], Some(7.0)),
        // Three NaNs: returns NaN.
        ([nan, nan, nan, 0], None),
    ];

    let inputs: Vec<[u32; 4]> = cases.iter().map(|c| c.0).collect();
    run_cases(&shader, &inputs, |backend, i, inp, got| {
        let expect = cases[i].1;
        let got_f = f32::from_bits(got);
        match expect {
            Some(want) => assert_eq!(
                got_f,
                want,
                "{backend}: v_med3_f32({:?}, {:?}, {:?}) = {got_f} ({got:#010x}), want {want}",
                f32::from_bits(inp[0]),
                f32::from_bits(inp[1]),
                f32::from_bits(inp[2]),
            ),
            None => assert!(
                got_f.is_nan(),
                "{backend}: v_med3_f32(NaN, NaN, NaN) = {got_f} ({got:#010x}), want NaN",
            ),
        }
    });
}

/// RDNA2 orders -0 below +0 in its maximums and minimums; DXIL's FMax and
/// FMin compare and select, which can give either zero.
#[test]
fn max_and_min_order_negative_zero_below_positive_zero() {
    let (pz, nz) = (0_u32, 0x8000_0000_u32);
    // Each case has a -0 and a +0 among its first two operands.
    let cases = [
        [nz, pz, nz, 0],
        [pz, nz, nz, 0],
        [nz, pz, pz, 0],
        [pz, nz, pz, 0],
    ];
    let ops = [
        ("v_max_f32", 0x110, pz),
        ("v_min_f32", 0x10F, nz),
        ("v_max3_f32", 0x154, pz),
        ("v_min3_f32", 0x151, nz),
    ];
    for (name, op, want) in ops {
        let shader = build_valu_cs(&vop3(op, 0, vgpr(1), vgpr(2), vgpr(3)));
        run_cases(&shader, &cases, |backend, _, inp, got| {
            assert_eq!(got, want, "{backend}: {name} {inp:x?}");
        });
    }
}

fn v_med3_f16_matches_rdna2_with_nan() {

        ([hn2, h0, h3, 0], Some(h0 as u16)),
        ([h1, h2, nan, 0], Some(h1 as u16)),
        ([nan, h1, h0, 0], Some(h0 as u16)),
        ([nan, h0, h1, 0], Some(h0 as u16)),
        ([h2, nan, h1, 0], Some(h1 as u16)),
        ([nan, h5, nan, 0], Some(h5 as u16)),

    ];

    let inputs: Vec<[u32; 4]> = cases.iter().map(|c| c.0).collect();

            ),
```
