`docs/architecture.md`:

```md
# Architecture

```
 user's files (outside repo)             VIctory
 ───────────────────────────             ─────────────────────────────────────────
 game assets ──────────────────────────► victory-pipeline + victory-game
                                         (victory-formats, victory-shader)
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                         cache_dir: converted data
                                                    │
 game executable ─► victory-loader ────► title code (native x86-64)
                    prepare, map, bind      │ imports
                                            ▼
                                         victory-hle ── host Windows (shared APIs)
                                            │ D3D12.X
                                            ▼
                                         victory-gpu ─► host D3D12
                                            │ shaders at pipeline creation
                                            ▼
                                         victory-shader ◄─► cache_dir
```

Shaders are translated when the title creates a pipeline, from the bytes it
passes, wherever it loaded them from (executable, archive, memory).
Converting them ahead of time from files is only a warm-up.

## Crates

| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `victory-core` | config, asset-policy guard, logging |
| `victory-pe` | read-only PE32+ and import-library analysis |
| `victory-loader` | prepare, map, bind and start the title image |
| `victory-hle` | console API implementations, host pass-through policy |
| `victory-gpu` | D3D12.X objects, command lists and GPU memory → host D3D12 |
| `victory-shader` | Xbox shader containers → host shaders |
| `victory-formats` | the GPU's texture layouts (sizes, tiling, detiling), audio codecs; planned: BCPack |
| `victory-pipeline` | converter trait, content-addressed cache |
| `victory-game` | the title-specific formats, build identities, hooks |
| `apps/victory` | command-line front end |
| `xtask` | asset-policy check, git hooks |
| `tests/fixtures/hle-probe` | a stand-in "title" (our own code) for loader tests |

Everything except `victory-game` is platform-level and can be tested with
any Xbox Series title.

## Import resolution

For every `dll!function` the title imports, in order:

1. our implementation in `victory-hle::modules` (always wins);
2. the host's own function, if `HostPolicy` allows that DLL;
3. an export of a DLL the title ships beside its executable, mapped like
   the executable (only DLLs neither of the above serves);
4. a generated stub that names the import when called (`--unimplemented
   trap` breaks into the debugger and aborts; `zero` logs once and returns 0).

`LoadLibrary*` of a console-only DLL we implement (e.g. `xgameruntime.dll`)
returns a pseudo handle; `GetProcAddress` on it finds our functions.
`LoadLibrary*` of a title DLL returns its mapped image, mapping it first if
nothing imports it. By name, as by import, a title gets only host DLLs
`HostPolicy` passes through, and `GetProcAddress` on one returns our
override where import binding would.
`QueryApiImpl` hands out our runtime objects by provider and interface id
(`victory-hle::modules::xgameruntime` lists the areas); online areas answer
as an offline console. Game saves are files under `VICTORY_DATA_DIR`.

Title storage is a drive on the console, and titles build paths on that.
`victory-hle::modules::files` binds every path-taking title import
(kernel32 and the C/C++ runtime) and rewrites paths on a virtual drive to
the host folder behind it; persistent local storage is one such drive over
a folder under `VICTORY_DATA_DIR`. Other paths reach the host unchanged.

An exe's code reaches its static TLS as slot 0; mapped as a DLL it gets
another slot, so the loader redirects those loads (`victory-loader::tls`).
`victory run --execute` installs a crash reporter that names faults as
`module+rva` and unwinds the faulting thread's stack
(`victory-loader::crash`).

`victory census` shows this classification without running anything (it
does not map title DLLs; `victory run` without `--execute` does).

## Shaders

`victory_shader::ir::build` turns a native program into SSA, one
instruction per machine instruction. `victory_shader::structure` then
removes EXEC: lane masks become per-lane booleans, wave-wide mask tests
become per-lane branches, and vector instructions keep a guard only where
a lane can reach them with its EXEC bit clear. `victory_shader::resource`
traces each descriptor and scalar memory address to the root parameter it
comes from (table, heap, root descriptor or constant). A descriptor a
waterfall loop reads from the first lane (`v_readfirstlane_b32`) is traced
to the per-lane load or choice that gives each lane its own (a mask's
`v_cndmask_b32`, or an if/else whose arms each set it: traced on the paths
the lanes take, from structurisation), and accessed with a non-uniform heap
index in one pass. `victory translate`
runs every shader it finds (containers, SGD5 files) through these and
lists what they cannot handle yet.

```

`docs/asset-policy.md`:

```md
# Asset policy (rule #1)

**Nothing from the game is ever stored in this repository.** Everything is
built on the user's machine from files the user supplies. The same applies
to other titles used for testing, and to any other proprietary material.

## Not allowed

In any form (files, string literals, fixtures, snapshots, docs):

* assets: models, textures, shaders, audio, video, text, archives;
* the executable or any part of it: data sections, strings, tables,
  resources, code beyond the signatures below;
* anything derived from those: converted assets, decompiled or
  disassembled code, shader dumps, extracted tables, screenshots.

## Allowed

* our own code that understands formats;
* build identities: BLAKE3 of an executable, CodeView GUID/age;
* per-build offsets of functions we hook, under names we choose;
* byte-pattern signatures that locate functions or data in the executable;
* small interoperability constants (magic numbers, enum values) we write;
* synthetic test data generated by our own code.

## The one exception

`crates/victory-formats/src/bcpack-tables.bin` (about 78 KB): the constant
tables of the BCPack format (entropy models, index rank tables, control
codes, per-format dictionaries). A BCPack stream cannot be decoded without
exactly these tables and they cannot be derived, so they ship with VIctory
by the project owner's decision (2026-11-23), entered as an exception in
`xtask/src/policy.rs`. They are part of the format, not our work, and the
repository's licence does not cover them. Nothing else of this kind is
accepted.

## Where data lives

Outside the repository, configured in `victory.toml`: `game_dir` (the
user's dump), `test_titles`, and `cache_dir` for everything derived
(default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\victory\cache`).

## Enforcement

1. `.gitignore` keeps common data types out of `git status`.
2. `cargo xtask policy` (run by the pre-commit hook; install with
   `cargo xtask install-hooks`) is an allowlist: files must have an allowed
   type, be under 512 KiB, contain no binary data or known binary
   signatures, and hold no long hex/base64 runs. Exceptions need an entry
   with a reason in `xtask/src/policy.rs`.
3. At runtime, everything that writes derived data calls
   `victory_core::ensure_outside_repo`.
4. Tests that need real files take their paths from environment variables
   and skip when unset. They assert on properties, never on snapshots.

## If something slips through

A follow-up commit is not enough. Rewrite history
(`git filter-repo --path <file> --invert-paths`), force-push, and have
everyone re-clone.

```

`docs/fork-ray-tracing.md`:

```md
# Ray tracing in this fork: what the title does and what has been built

Status, 2026-11-25: **nothing is lit by ray tracing yet.** Most of the
machinery translates and is unit-tested; it has not yet run end to end in the
game. Everything here is off by default.

## What the title does

The title's indirect light (probes, bounce, reflections) and the
shadows of its lamps and sun are ray traced. Without them, anything the sun
does not hit directly is black: interiors, the shadowed side of a face, rooms
lit only by lamps.

The title does not use a ray-tracing API:

- Traversal is ordinary compute-shader code: a per-thread stack in shared
  memory, and loads through raw 40-bit addresses of title memory.
- The static world's acceleration structures ship pre-built in the title's
  data, in the console GPU's native node format (64-byte nodes: box nodes with
  four children and 16-bit float bounds, 128-byte box nodes with 32-bit float
  bounds, triangle nodes, instance nodes). They are unpacked on the GPU.
- A set of builder programs (from the title's `XboxBvhBuilder.dll`, 52 compute
  programs) builds and refits the dynamic structures on the GPU every frame.
- Only the per-node test is hardware: the instructions
  `image_bvh64_intersect_ray` and `image_bvh_intersect_ray`. One call tests a
  ray against a box node's four children (returning the hit children, nearest
  first) or against a triangle node (returning the intersection's numerator,
  denominator and barycentric numerators).

So mapping this onto the host's own ray tracing (DXR) is not practical: the
layer would have to know the geometry behind structures the title never
describes to it, and the traversal loops live in 64 of the title's own
programs. This fork runs the title's builder and traversal as translated
shaders and emulates the one instruction.

## What this fork adds

1. **The builder programs translate** (49 of 52; all that the title creates in
   the scenes tested). They pass buffer addresses in a spilled parameter table
   rather than in descriptors. Added: the spilled user-data table, root
   unordered-access views (translator and host binding), byte and 16-bit buffer
   accesses, and several control-flow shapes.
2. **Title memory by raw address from shaders.** A directory with one entry per
   64 KiB of title address space leads a shader to the layer's host copy of
   that memory; loads, stores, atomic add/sub and float min/max go through it.
   Before a dispatch the host makes ready the memory its root views and root
   constants name.
3. **The ray test, emulated in DXIL.** Four slab tests and a sorting network
   for box nodes; a watertight ray/triangle test for triangle nodes; both forms
   of the instruction. A plain Rust reference lives in
   `crates/victory-shader/src/bvh.rs`; tests run the emitted DXIL on the GPU
   over 311 ray/node cases and compare with the reference bit for bit.
4. **The trace and shading programs translate** (59 of 64 trace programs, and
   the irradiance-cache shading program). This needed lane masks treated as
   plain numbers on some paths, and exact forms for programs written for
   64-lane waves running on a GPU with 32-lane waves.
5. **A safety rule on the host side.** The builder's stages run only while
   every builder pipeline the title has created has a host pipeline; otherwise
   none run (`VICTORY_BVH_BUILDER=1` asks for it; `VICTORY_BVH_QUARANTINE=1`
   also keeps the builder's stores out of title memory, for a first test). A
   partly working builder wrote garbage bounds into title memory and crashed
   the title.

## Known gaps

- With `VICTORY_BVH_BUILDER=1` the builder still stays off in a real run: a few
  of its pipelines are refused by the host (they still ask for 64-lane waves on
  a 32-lane GPU) or do not translate.
- Five shadow-mask trace programs do not translate yet.
- An access to a title page that has no host copy is lost (a read gives zero, a
  store is dropped).
- Not publicly documented, and assumed: the instruction's rounding, the order
  of two boxes entered at the same distance, and the result for a ray exactly
  through an edge.
- Cost on the GPU is unmeasured.

## Where to look

- `crates/victory-shader/src/bvh.rs`: the reference for the node test.
- `crates/victory-shader/src/emit/lower.rs`: the lowering of the two
  instructions and of memory by address (`Lower::memory`).
- `crates/victory-shader/src/resource.rs`: address tracking for descriptors
  and raw addresses.
- `crates/victory-gpu/src/pipeline.rs`, `draw.rs`: the builder rule and the
  host side of root views and title memory.

```

`tests/fixtures/hle-probe/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! A stand-in for a title, written by us. It imports from DLLs that do not
//! exist on a PC, which is exactly the situation victory-loader handles.
//! Loaded normally, this DLL would fail with "module not found".

use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};

const DLL_THREAD_ATTACH: u32 = 2;

#[link(name = "xgameruntime", kind = "raw-dylib")]
unsafe extern "system" {
    fn XGameRuntimeInitialize() -> i32;
}

#[link(name = "victory-probe-missing", kind = "raw-dylib")]
unsafe extern "system" {
    fn VIctoryProbeNotImplemented(x: u64) -> u64;
}

// A DLL the "title" ships; the test supplies a renamed copy of version.dll.
#[link(name = "victory-probe-title", kind = "raw-dylib")]
unsafe extern "system" {
    fn GetFileVersionInfoSizeW(path: *const u16, handle: *mut u32) -> u32;
}

// Delay-loaded (see build.rs): bound through the delay-load table.
#[link(name = "victory-probe-delayed", kind = "raw-dylib")]
unsafe extern "system" {
    fn VIctoryProbeDelayed() -> u32;
}

#[link(name = "kernel32")]
unsafe extern "system" {
    fn GetTickCount() -> u32;
    fn GetCurrentProcessId() -> u32;
}

/// Console-only API, answered by the resolver's HLE implementation.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "system" fn probe_xgameruntime_init() -> i32 {
    unsafe { XGameRuntimeInitialize() }
}

/// Exists on the host too, but the resolver overrides it.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "system" fn probe_tick() -> u32 {
    unsafe { GetTickCount() }
}

/// Exists on the host and is passed through to it.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "system" fn probe_pid() -> u32 {
    unsafe { GetCurrentProcessId() }
}

/// An export of a title-shipped DLL: the version-info size of kernel32.dll.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "system" fn probe_title() -> u32 {
    let path: Vec<u16> = r"C:\Windows\System32\kernel32.dll"
        .encode_utf16()
        .chain(Some(0))
        .collect();
    let mut handle = 0;
    unsafe { GetFileVersionInfoSizeW(path.as_ptr(), &mut handle) }
}

/// A delay-loaded console API.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "system" fn probe_delayed() -> u32 {
    unsafe { VIctoryProbeDelayed() }
}

/// Nobody implements this one: it must land in an unimplemented-import stub.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "system" fn probe_missing() -> u64 {
    unsafe { VIctoryProbeNotImplemented(42) }
}

static TLS_THREAD_STARTS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
static MAIN_THREAD_STARTS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);

/// A TLS callback, as titles have: counts thread starts.
unsafe extern "system" fn on_thread(_: *mut c_void, reason: u32, _: *mut c_void) {
    if reason == DLL_THREAD_ATTACH {
        TLS_THREAD_STARTS.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
}

#[used]
#[unsafe(link_section = ".CRT$XLB")]
static ON_THREAD: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, u32, *mut c_void) = on_thread;

/// Called by the CRT's DLL entry point: counts thread starts too, and calls
/// an import the resolver overrides, as title code calls our runtime.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "system" fn DllMain(_: *mut c_void, reason: u32, _: *mut c_void) -> i32 {
    if reason == DLL_THREAD_ATTACH {
        MAIN_THREAD_STARTS.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        unsafe { GetTickCount() };
    }
    if reason == DLL_PROCESS_DETACH {
        DETACHES.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
    1
}

const DLL_PROCESS_DETACH: u32 = 0;
static DETACHES: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);

/// `DLL_PROCESS_DETACH` notices seen by `DllMain`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "system" fn probe_detaches() -> u32 {
    DETACHES.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

/// Thread starts seen by the TLS callback (high half) and `DllMain` (low).
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "system" fn probe_thread_starts() -> u64 {
    // SAFETY: reading our own static keeps the linker from dropping it.
    unsafe { std::ptr::from_ref(&ON_THREAD).read_volatile() };
    u64::from(TLS_THREAD_STARTS.load(Ordering::Relaxed)) << 32
        | u64::from(MAIN_THREAD_STARTS.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
}
```

`xtask/src/main.rs`:

```rs
//! Repository maintenance. Run with `cargo xtask <command>`.

mod policy;

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::Command;

use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use clap::{Parser, Subcommand};

#[derive(Parser)]
#[command(name = "xtask")]
struct Cli {
    #[command(subcommand)]
    command: Cmd,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
enum Cmd {
    /// Enforce the asset policy: the repository holds only small text files
    /// we wrote. Checks tracked and untracked-but-not-ignored files.
    Policy {
        /// Check only what is staged for commit (used by the pre-commit hook).
        #[arg(long)]
        staged: bool,
    },
    /// Point git at .githooks/ so every commit runs the policy check.
    InstallHooks,
}

fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let root = workspace_root();
    match Cli::parse().command {
        Cmd::Policy { staged } => policy::run(&root, staged),
        Cmd::InstallHooks => {
            let status = Command::new("git")
                .args(["config", "core.hooksPath", ".githooks"])
                .current_dir(&root)
                .status()
                .context("running git")?;
            anyhow::ensure!(
                status.success(),
                "git config failed (is this a git repository?)"
            );
            println!("hooks installed: commits now run `cargo xtask policy --staged`");
            Ok(())
        }
    }
}

fn workspace_root() -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .parent()
        .expect("xtask lives in the workspace")
        .into()
}

```

`xtask/src/policy.rs`:

```rs
//! Rule #1, statically: the repository only ever contains small text files
//! that we wrote. See docs/asset-policy.md.
//!
//! This is an allowlist, not a blocklist: a file passes only if its name is
//! on the list, it is not too big, it is text, and it does not smuggle data
//! inside text (long hex/base64 runs).

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::Command;

use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};

const MAX_FILE_SIZE: usize = 512 * 1024;
const MAX_ENCODED_RUN: usize = 512;

const ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS: &[&str] = &[
    "rs", "toml", "md", "txt", "lock", "yml", "yaml", "json", "hlsl", "hlsli", "ps1", "cmd", "sh",
];
const ALLOWED_NAMES: &[&str] = &[
    ".gitignore",
    ".gitattributes",
    ".editorconfig",
    ".victory-root",
    "pre-commit",
    "LICENSE",
    "LICENSE-MIT",
    "LICENSE-APACHE",
];

/// Paths explicitly exempted, with a reason. Keep this empty if at all possible.
const EXCEPTIONS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[(
    "crates/victory-formats/src/bcpack-tables.bin",
    "the BCPack format's constant tables: nothing decodes without them and they cannot be derived (owner's decision, 2026-11-23; docs/asset-policy.md)",
)];

/// Signatures of formats that must never be committed.
const FORBIDDEN_MAGIC: &[(&[u8], &str)] = &[
    (b"MZ", "PE executable"),
    (b"DXBC", "shader container"),
    (b"DDS ", "DDS texture"),
    (b"RIFF", "RIFF (audio/video)"),
    (b"BC\xC0\xDE", "LLVM bitcode"),
    (b"Microsoft C/C++ MSF", "PDB"),
    (b"!<arch>", "library archive"),
    (b"PK\x03\x04", "zip"),
    (b"7z\xBC\xAF", "7-zip"),
    (b"MSCF", "cabinet"),
    (b"\xD0\xCF\x11\xE0", "MSI/OLE"),
];

pub fn run(root: &Path, staged: bool) -> Result<()> {
    let files = list_files(root, staged)?;
    let mut violations = Vec::new();
    for path in &files {
        if EXCEPTIONS.iter().any(|(p, _)| p == path) {
            continue;
        }
        let content = if staged {
            let out = Command::new("git")
                .args(["show", &format!(":{path}")])
                .current_dir(root)
                .output()?;
            if !out.status.success() {
                continue; // deleted in the index
            }
            out.stdout
        } else {
            match std::fs::read(root.join(path)) {
                Ok(c) => c,
                Err(_) => continue,
            }
        };
        for problem in check(path, &content) {
            violations.push(format!("{path}: {problem}"));
        }
    }
    if violations.is_empty() {
        println!("asset policy: {} files ok", files.len());
        return Ok(());
    }
    for v in &violations {
        eprintln!("POLICY: {v}");
    }
    bail!(
        "{} asset-policy violation(s). Nothing from the game may be committed; \
         see docs/asset-policy.md",
        violations.len()
    )
}

fn list_files(root: &Path, staged: bool) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
    let git = |args: &[&str]| -> Result<Option<Vec<String>>> {
        let out = Command::new("git")
            .args(args)
            .current_dir(root)
            .output()
            .context("running git")?;
        if !out.status.success() {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        Ok(Some(
            out.stdout
                .split(|&b| b == 0)
                .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
                .map(|s| String::from_utf8_lossy(s).replace('\\', "/"))
                .collect(),
        ))
    };
    if staged {
        return git(&[
            "diff",
            "--cached",
            "--name-only",
            "--diff-filter=ACMR",
            "-z",
        ])?
        .context("--staged needs a git repository");
    }
    if let Some(mut tracked) = git(&[
        "ls-files",
        "-z",
        "--cached",
        "--others",
        "--exclude-standard",
    ])? {
        tracked.sort();
        tracked.dedup();
        return Ok(tracked);
    }
    // Not a git repository: walk everything except build output.
    Ok(walkdir::WalkDir::new(root)
        .into_iter()
        .filter_entry(|e| !matches!(e.file_name().to_str(), Some("target" | ".git")))
        .filter_map(Result::ok)
        .filter(|e| e.file_type().is_file())
        .filter_map(|e| {
            e.path()
                .strip_prefix(root)
                .ok()
                .map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/"))
        })
        .collect())
}

/// All problems with one file. Pure, for testing.
pub fn check(path: &str, content: &[u8]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut problems = Vec::new();
    let name = path.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(path);
    let ext = name.rsplit_once('.').map(|(_, e)| e.to_ascii_lowercase());
    let allowed = ALLOWED_NAMES.contains(&name)
        || ext
            .as_deref()
            .is_some_and(|e| ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS.contains(&e));
    if !allowed {
        problems.push("file type not on the allowlist".to_owned());
    }
    if content.len() > MAX_FILE_SIZE {
        problems.push(format!(
            "{} bytes exceeds the {MAX_FILE_SIZE}-byte limit",
            content.len()
        ));
    }
    for (magic, what) in FORBIDDEN_MAGIC {
        if content.starts_with(magic) {
            problems.push(format!("looks like a {what}"));
        }
    }
    if content.contains(&0) {
        problems.push("binary content (NUL bytes)".to_owned());
    } else if let Some(run) = longest_encoded_run(content)
        && run > MAX_ENCODED_RUN
    {
        problems.push(format!("{run}-character hex/base64 run (embedded data?)"));
    }
    problems
}

/// Longest run of characters that could be hex or base64 payload.
fn longest_encoded_run(content: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    let is_payload = |b: &u8| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(b, b'+' | b'/' | b'=');
    content.split(|b| !is_payload(b)).map(<[u8]>::len).max()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::check;

    /// Enforces the policy wherever tests run, even in clones without the hook.
    #[test]
    fn repository_passes_policy() {
        super::run(&crate::workspace_root(), false).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_source() {
        assert!(check("crates/x/src/lib.rs", b"fn main() {}\n").is_empty());
        assert!(check(".gitignore", b"/target/\n").is_empty());
        assert!(check(".githooks/pre-commit", b"#!/bin/sh\n").is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_game_like_files() {
        assert!(!check("assets/tex.dds", b"DDS \x7c\0\0\0").is_empty());
        assert!(
            !check("notes.txt", b"MZ\x90\0").is_empty(),
            "magic wins over extension"
        );
        assert!(
            !check("data.bin", b"hello").is_empty(),
            "extension not allowed"
        );
        assert!(
            !check("a.rs", &vec![b'a'; 600 * 1024]).is_empty(),
            "too big"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_data_smuggled_into_text() {
        let blob = format!("const DATA: &str = \"{}\";", "A1".repeat(400));
        assert!(!check("src/blob.rs", blob.as_bytes()).is_empty());
    }
}
```
